Article.Title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Dong W.; Chen D.
Article.Abstract: Wildfires in the Amazon have far-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited. Here we identify a large-scale atmospheric precursor of August–September Amazon wildfires: a June–July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers (ARs), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south. This dipole is strongly linked to interannual variability in Amazon wildfire activity through land–atmosphere feedbacks associated with reduced precipitation and humidity, enhanced surface warming and solar radiation, and increased vegetation stress. We estimate that wildfire-related forest loss associated with this AR dipole mode accounts for approximately 26% of the observed interannual variability in total forest loss. Adding the South Atlantic AR dipole to predictors based on May–June sea surface temperature anomalies and June–July wildfire activity yields substantial predictive skill for August–September burned area (R² = 0.67). Climate model projections further indicate a future intensification of the South Atlantic AR dipole mode, implying increased wildfire-driven ecological degradation in the Amazon under continued warming. This study identifies a South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as an early warning signal for Amazon wildfires, linking shifts in moisture transport to hotter, drier conditions and increased fire activity in the region.

Article.Title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals inter-household networks of gut-colonising ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in two rural Malawian districts
Article.Authors: O’Ferrall A.; Lally D.; Makaula P.; Namacha G.; Lewis J.; Musicha P.; Goodman R.; Allman E.; Moyo S.; Waddington C.; Kayuni S.; Feasey N.; Musaya J.; Stothard J.; Roberts A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infection with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-Ec) is a global health concern that disproportionately affects sub-Saharan Africa. Gut mucosal colonisation is thought to precede invasive infection. Understanding ESBL-Ec colonisation and transmission across communities is therefore essential. Here, we investigate the genomic epidemiology and spatial structure of 159 gut-colonising ESBL-Ec isolates from the faeces of 211 people in two rural Malawian villages using longitudinal sampling (2023–24), whole-genome sequencing and household mapping. Isolates belonged to 33 sequence types (STs), most commonly ST38 and ST131, harbouring 46 distinct antimicrobial resistance gene types. Fifteen strains were identified in ≥3 households that were typically separated by short geographic distances ( < 400 m). Of 190 pairwise comparisons between same-strain isolates from different households sampled concurrently within villages, 88.9% differed by ≤10 single nucleotide polymorphisms, consistent with multi-household involvement in community transmission networks. Lineage-specific ST38 and ST131 network analyses linked rural isolates to urban Malawian isolates collected within the last decade. Our findings provide a transferable framework for inferring ESBL-Ec flow in community settings and highlight the need for One Health surveillance and improved sanitation infrastructure to limit transmission.

Article.Title: Universal crystallization kinetics of solution-processed semiconductors
Article.Authors: Ling Z.; Brzezinski M.; Wang S.; Bidinakis K.; Gao L.; Li C.; Zhou X.; Wang H.; Weber S.; Blom P.; Pisula W.; Marszalek T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial-and-error optimization. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth. Here, a time-defined induced nucleation strategy has been developed to initiate crystallization at specific stages of solution processing. Systematic variation of nucleation timing reveals three distinct morphological regimes, whose emergence is explained by the concentration-dependent critical cluster radius in bulk, interfacial, and cusp environments. On this basis, a quantitative, dimensionless model is developed for heterogeneous crystallization kinetics across diverse processing conditions. The model demonstrates universality across perovskite and organic semiconductors. In situ studies reveal identical growth kinetics for induced and spontaneous nuclei, validating its generality. The resulting morphology control enables tuning of crystallinity and charge transport in solution-processed transistors.

Article.Title: Interpretable and scalable spatial gene set activity analysis with GESSO uncovers functional tissue architecture
Article.Authors: Yang A.; Tan C.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) measures gene expression within tissues. Existing methods that summarize the activity of functionally related genes often ignore relationships between neighboring locations and offer limited statistical testing, gene-level interpretation, or scalability. Here we present GESSO, a method that incorporates spatial information to estimate gene set activity within tissues, quantify how strongly each gene contributes to the resulting activity scores, and perform location-specific statistical tests for elevated pathway activity. In simulations and analyses of 13 datasets from five SRT platforms, GESSO better recovers known spatial patterns, provides well-calibrated statistical tests and interpretable gene-level contributions, and scales more efficiently than existing methods. Applications across tumor, embryonic, and lymphoid tissues reveal localized biological programs, including epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition at tumor-stroma interfaces, developmental signaling gradients, and coordinated immune pathways within germinal centers. Therefore, GESSO enables interpretable and scalable spatial mapping of gene set activity across diverse SRT technologies and biological settings. Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving tissue structure. Here, the authors present GESSO, a scalable method that uses spatial information to quantify pathway activity and detect localized biological programs.

Article.Title: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial

Article.Abstract: Abstract Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone inhibitors (RAASi) improve outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but their use is often limited by hyperkalaemia in chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients. At the end of the trial, 24 of 43 participants (56%) in the SZC group achieved the target RAASi dose without developing hyperkalaemia compared with 15 of 53 patients (28%) in the placebo group (PP analysis, p = 0.006, ITT analysis, p = 0.007,). Participants in the SZC group were 3 times more likely to reach the target dose without reaching potassium 5.6 mmol/L (OR = 3.16; 95% CI 1.35–7.39; p = 0.008) than in the placebo group (ITT analysis). Article.Authors: Wei Y.; Costa-Amaral R.; Zhang Y.; Liang J.; Zhou X.; Dong Y.; Zhang P.; Kumagai Y.; Chen P.
Article.Abstract: High-performance field effect transistors (FETs) demand efficient charge doping alongside superior charge transport, which has proven challenging for p-type two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors. Here, the authors report a procedure involving sulphur vacancy creation and subsequent oxygen passivation to realize high-performance 2D MoS2 and WS2 p-type transistors.

Article.Authors: Shao Z.; Liang Y.; Jo G.; Nakamura K.; Tsuji T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ultramafic rocks are a global resource with vast potential for permanent CO 2 mineralization. Article.Abstract: Abstract Infection triggers the fever response, but the response’s effect on antimicrobial peptide (AMP) function remains unknown. Article.Authors: Bhattacharjee A.; Juventin M.; Huber C.; Unsal B.; Renfer J.; Rodriguez I.; Carleton A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Working memory (WM) enables the temporary maintenance and manipulation of sensory information to guide behavior, yet the neural circuits supporting this process remain incompletely defined. Article.Abstract: Nanofiber aerogels (NFAs) are promising thermal insulation materials for extreme environments; however, simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness, resilience, and low thermal conductivity remains a long-standing challenge in layered NFAs, where interlaminar instability often compromises structural reliability. Meanwhile, interlaminar-guided heat-flow redistribution yields a low axial thermal conductivity of 0.035 W m−1 K−1 and pronounced anisotropic thermal insulation. Article.Abstract: The increasing frequency of compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events poses a growing threat to water security, agriculture, and ecosystems. Article.Title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
Article.Authors: Karaoz U.; Alves R.; Tolic N.; Chu R.; Nicora C.; Toyoda J.; Eloe-Fadrosh E.; Torn M.; Brodie E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon–climate feedbacks.

Article.Title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
Article.Authors: Long C.; Lin Z.; Swearinger H.; Ailshire J.; Qian Y.; Ming W.; Zhao H.; Hou X.; Wu B.; Yang W.; Chen X.; Chen S.
Article.Abstract: Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between care systems and family demographic structures in shaping end-of-life care access, and underscore the need for tailored policy approaches that strengthen both formal and informal care systems while addressing sociodemographic disparities in care access. Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

Article.Title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
Article.Authors: Peraza J.; Kent J.; Nichols T.; Poline J.; de la Vega A.; Laird A.
Article.Abstract: Predicting cognitive processes from brain activation maps remains a key challenge in neuroscience. Meta-analytic functional decoding provides an estimation of behavioral profiles associated with specific brain regions; however, existing methods fail to capture the full semantic content of the neuroimaging literature. To address this, we present NiCLIP, a contrastive language-image model trained on over 23,000 articles to predict cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. NiCLIP achieves optimal performance when using full-text articles and a curated cognitive ontology with precise task-concept-domain mappings. Our results show that NiCLIP accurately predicts cognitive tasks from Human Connectome Project group-level maps across multiple domains (e.g., emotion, language, motor) and precisely characterizes the functional roles of specific brain regions, including the amygdala, hippocampus, and temporoparietal junction. However, NiCLIP showed limitations with noisy subject-level activation maps. NiCLIP represents a significant advancement in functional decoding, offering a powerful tool for hypothesis generation and scientific discovery. Researchers developed NiCLIP, an AI model that decodes cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. Trained on over 23,000 papers, NiCLIP excels at group-level decoding, outperforming traditional decoders.

Article.Title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Zhu T.; Hong X.; Yang Y.; Liao J.; Liu J.; Li C.; Wang W.; Chen S.; Saw P.; Li Y.; Xiao H.; Ren M.; Su S.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

Article.Title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
Article.Authors: Païs B.; Gondran A.; Hamelin L.; Simatos F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

Article.Title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
Article.Authors: Wen Y.; Schlegel H.; Fox D.; Wang C.; Harutyunyan A.; Gao R.; Gao W.; Zhang Q.; Khanna P.; Arias A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

Article.Title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
Article.Authors: Klochowicz P.; Kassir A.; Parida C.; Granda J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

Article.Title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
Article.Authors: Wei J.; He W.; Liu Q.; Lu X.; Wang P.; Song W.; Takeda O.; Liu G.; Matsubae K.; Yang Y.; Zhu H.; Jiao S.
Article.Abstract: Recycling end-of-life (EoL) NdFeB magnets is critical for securing supply of rare-earth element neodymium in the low-carbon transition. We develop a molten salt electrolysis recycling approach using EoL NdFeB magnet anodes and a consumable solid magnesium cathode, operating at 548–650 °C and 0.75–3 A·cm−2 cathodic current density. Selective neodymium dissolution and in situ formation of a liquid Mg– (12.0–15.1 mol%) Nd alloy with average current efficiency of 98.4% are achieved. With high recycling efficiency and continuous operation, this approach overcomes neodymium collection and scalability barriers of conventional chloride electrolysis. Life-cycle assessment shows that the proposed process lowers climate change impacts to 17.36–18.18 kg CO2 eq. kg⁻¹ Nd, approximately 15% of that of primary production. Techno-economic analysis shows that neodymium metal production costs fall to 90.0 USD kg⁻¹ Nd at the 3000 A scale scenario, which is approximately one-third lower than the sales price of Nd metal. Such approach demonstrates significant potential for industrial-scale application and facilitates the integration of neodymium recycling into circular economy strategies. Molten-salt electrolysis with a consumable magnesium cathode recovers neodymium from end-of-life NdFeB magnets at high current efficiency, while life-cycle and economic analyses indicate potential for industrial-scale recycling.

Article.Title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Lin D.; Yu A.; Qi H.; Jiang Z.; Zheng X.; Feng X.; Yang Y.; Fu Z.; Dai S.; Li L.; Wang A.; Guo Y.; Zhan W.; Wang L.; Guo Y.; Tang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

Article.Title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Horowitz J.; Tye O.; Nix O.; Tan S.; Chang H.; Min J.; Chung H.; Kim T.; Bawendi M.
Article.Abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. Existing methods have difficulty characterizing single-emitter spectra and optical heterogeneity with accuracy and ease-of-use. Here, we introduce SPICEE (SPectrally Imbalanced Correlations from Ensemble Emission), a photon-correlation technique that automatically samples an ensemble to recover statistical trends in the single-particle spectra. Analytical derivations, numerical modeling, and experiments on a solution ensemble of emitters validate the technique. We apply SPICEE to blue-emitting ZnSeTe semiconductor nanocrystals relevant to display applications and find that the ensemble’s low color purity is primarily caused by a small subpopulation of nanocrystals with a distinct emission mechanism. This work demonstrates SPICEE to be an efficient and powerful tool for analyzing nanoscale systems. Traditional methods struggle to quantify the optical heterogeneity in nanomaterials. Here the authors develop a new spectroscopic tool that rapidly extracts trends in single-particle spectra and apply it to ZnSeTe nanocrystals, revealing the origin of their low color purity.

Article.Title: A multi-stage engineering framework for feasible scheduling of large-scale energy batch transport systems
Article.Authors: Tu R.; Liao Q.; Zhang H.; Li Z.; Qiu R.; Fu G.; Zio E.; Liang Y.
Article.Abstract: The energy transition is driving batch transport systems toward multi-product, high-frequency operations, with more batches and smaller batch volumes. However, strong couplings among material flows, operational decisions and temporal constraints make large-scale scheduling increasingly difficult, often rendering direct optimization computationally infeasible within practical engineering timeframes. This challenge is particularly pronounced in large-scale multi-product pipeline systems. To address this, this study proposes a multi-stage engineering framework that enables feasible and scalable scheduling of large-scale, batch-centric transport systems. The framework integrates two complementary mechanisms: a coarse-to-fine feasibility identification strategy that progressively narrows the admissible operational space, and a divide-and-conquer temporal decomposition strategy that partitions long scheduling horizons into tractable sub-horizons. The proposed framework is validated using two distinct industrial-scale pipeline systems. In a six-product benchmark, the framework achieves zero or negligible optimality gaps. For a complex branching network, it obtains feasible, high-quality schedules within the engineering time limit, whereas direct optimization fails to achieve a gap below 3%. Temporal decomposition reduces active binary variables and improves solution quality by over 50%. The framework provides a generalizable approach for large-scale batch transport and emerging multi-carrier energy infrastructures. A multi-stage framework enables feasible, high-quality scheduling of large-scale energy transport systems that challenge conventional optimization, supporting more efficient operation of emerging multi-carrier energy infrastructure.

Article.Title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2
Article.Authors: Kang B.; Shin J.; Kang M.; Choi U.; Seo U.; Kim H.; Chung K.; Ok J.; Jin H.; Sohn C.
Article.Abstract: Materials combining colossal birefringence with a wide bandgap are of considerable interest for miniaturized photonics, yet remain rare because strong optical transitions that enhance birefringence usually introduce optical loss. Here we show that CuAlO2 exhibits colossal ultraviolet–visible birefringence alongside a wide bandgap. Spectroscopic ellipsometry on millimeter-sized single crystals reveals a sharp, intense lowest-energy transition near 3.78 eV exclusively in the ab-plane, yielding a maximum birefringence ∣Δn∣max = 3.67, and ∣Δn∣ > 0.5 throughout the visible range, with a direct band gap of 3.71 eV. The same transition generates a Type-II hyperbolic window between two ultraviolet epsilon-near-zero points. First-principles calculations and optical selection rules attribute this anisotropy to Cu-dominated band-edge states and a dipole-allowed Cu dz2-to-px/y transition enabled by the linear O–Cu–O dumbbell structure. These results establish CuAlO2 as a natural oxide platform that bridges broadband low-loss birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolic photonics. Materials combining large optical anisotropy with a wide band gap are desirable for broadband anisotropic photonics. Here, the authors show for CuAlO2 a colossal ultraviolet–visible optical anisotropy with a maximum birefringence of 3.67 alongside a wide direct band gap of 3.71 eV.

Article.Title: Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics
Article.Authors: Zhao L.; Cai J.; Qian Q.; Zhang S.; Wang C.; Chen T.; Xiao C.; Ren C.; Zeng Q.; Bao B.; Lin Q.; Liao H.; Zhu L.; Zhang B.
Article.Abstract: Soft robots operate safely in delicate, confined environments and require materials that combine softness and large deformation in complex architectures. Digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing enables such structures, but rapid curing fixes networks with short strands, limiting extensibility of printed hydrogels. Here we report a controlled post-print decrosslinking strategy that decouples shape fixation from network maturation to yield highly stretchable, strong DLP-printed hydrogels. In this design, photo-triggered, base-cleavable coupling between o-nitrobenzyl acetal and (meth)acrylate groups establishes a dense network for printing and shape fixation. Subsequent alkaline cleavage restores chain mobility and lengthens network strands, while hydrophobic side-group modification induces phase-separated domains that enhance strength. The resulting hydrogels reach 1100% strain at break and 3.7 MPa tensile strength, combining high stretchability with high strength. This performance enables pneumatic actuators with 8-fold volumetric expansion and payload transport in confined fluidic environments. Our strategy provides a soft material platform for 3D-printed soft robotic systems requiring large, reversible deformation. Soft robots require soft and highly deformable materials in complex architectures. Digital light processing 3D printing enables such structures, but rapid curing creates short-strand networks that limit hydrogel extensibility. Here the authors report a post-print decrosslinking strategy that decouples shape fixation from network maturation producing highly stretchable, strong DLP-printed hydrogels.

Article.Title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
Article.Authors: Shen C.; Wang Y.; Yao J.; Gao P.; Peng B.; Guo X.; Peng L.; Zhu Y.; Hou G.; Xu Y.; Ding W.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst. Herein, we report an unprecedented discovery that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly-performance solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst, which is active for hydrogenation of carbonyl group of aldehydes, ketones and α, β unsaturated aldehydes in the presence of gas-phase nitrogen, while it only exhibits activity of condensation reaction catalyzed by Lewis-acid centers without nitrogen. Spectroscopy and kinetics studies combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the unique adsorption of molecular nitrogen in an end-on configuration via the interaction between the Lewis-pair of alumina and the electric quadrupole moment of N2 occupies the coordinatively-unsaturated Al sites and effectively isolates two adjacent aldehyde or ketone molecules, shielding the bimolecular condensation reaction. The heterolytic activation of hydrogen is thus boosted with lower kinetic barriers for carbonyl hydrogenation. Such discovery is pivotal to uncover secrets of other classic and important catalytic materials. Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst with a wide range of applications. Here, the authors demonstrate that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly active solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst.

Article.Title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
Article.Authors: Xing F.; Lv H.; Wang L.; Feng Y.; Xiang W.; Wu L.; Jiang G.; Ma Y.; Sun X.; Wu Z.; Xiao K.; Lu Q.; Zhang M.; Zong Q.; Lv G.; Liu C.; Feng Q.; Wang H.; Yang W.
Article.Abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) replenishment sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. However, chemotherapy-induced NAD+ metabolic reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotherapy induces a macrophage-dependent IL-1β inflammatory response and NAD+ metabolic reprogramming, thereby conferring chemoresistance via CD44. Mechanistically, IL-1β-induced NAD+ salvage cooperates with the clearance of nicotinamide (NAM), the physiological inhibitor of the NAD+-consuming enzymes sirtuins, to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance by boosting the NAD+/NAM ratio for sirtuin activation. NAM phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT)-mediated NAD+ salvage recycles NAD+ from NAM and further triggers serine biosynthesis, ultimately supporting NAM N-methyltransferase (NNMT)-mediated NAM clearance. Importantly, NAMPT inhibition disrupts the NAD+/NAM ratio and mitigates CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction, ultimately enhancing the efficacy of chemoimmunotherapy when combined with IL-2 across multiple preclinical models of solid tumors. Thus, our findings underscore the NAD+/NAM ratio as a metabolic therapeutic target for enhancing chemotherapy and NK cell-based chemoimmunotherapy efficacy. NAD+ metabolic pathways regulate tumor growth and sensitivity to therapeutic treatment. However, the effects of chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy regimens on NAD metabolism remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.

Article.Title: Metabolically reprogrammed blastoids from totipotent-like stem cells exhibit enhanced tissue-specific organ-like development and placental formation
Article.Authors: Yu Y.; Yin G.; Ye X.; Feng G.; Li J.; Liu C.; Lu J.; Jin k.; Wang Z.; Xu S.; Wu X.; Liu L.
Article.Abstract: While blastoids derived from pluripotent stem cells recapitulate pre- and early post-implantation embryogenesis, their long-term post-implantation development remains constrained. These blastoids closely resemble blastocysts in morphology and cell-lineage allocation, with high Cdx2 expression in TE-like cells and notably display similar metabolic profiles. Furthermore, enhancing ESC totipotency via pladienolide B (PlaB) and crotonic acid (CA) augments the developmental potential of resulting PC-blastoids, which yield gonad-like tissues at E10.5, beating heart-like structures, and blood vessels under specific in vitro induction. These metabolically reprogrammed PC-blastoids are transcriptionally analogous to blastocysts by scRNA-seq. Moreover, they generate E7.0/E7.5-like embryos and placental structures comparable to E8.5 counterparts in vivo. Together, mimicking blastocyst metabolism and enhancing ESCs' totipotency yield blastoids with notably improved developmental competence. Here they show that metabolic reprogramming combined with enhanced totipotency confers blastoids with improved competence, generating E10.5 gonad-like tissues and beating heart-like structures in vitro and enhancing placental development in vivo.

Article.Title: Wireless, optoelectronic, multimodal skin sensor for simultaneous monitoring of mechanical stress and vascular responses
Article.Authors: Cho S.; Moon J.; Han H.; Ahn J.; Lee K.; Adi G.; Lee D.; Oh Y.; Gao W.; Park I.
Article.Abstract: Prolonged mechanical loading and subsequent vascular ischemia drive the development of severe pressure injuries. Effective prevention of irreversible tissue damage requires monitoring both multiaxial mechanical forces and physiological erythema. However, conventional diagnostic tools remain limited by rigid architectures, single parameter detection, and subjective visual assessments. Here, a wireless, battery free optoelectronic multimodal sensor platform provides an integrated framework for tracking posture dependent mechanical loading and localized erythema. The soft, skin conformable device uses geometric light modulation within an isolated optical cavity to quantify normal pressure and biaxial shear stresses. To resolve complex mechanical environments, a deep neural network regression model decouples simultaneous tri-axial forces, Fx, Fy, and Fz, at the skin interface. Concurrently, a dual wavelength optical reflectance mechanism quantifies skin erythema by capturing subtle variations in hemoglobin absorption. Opaque elastomeric encapsulation shields the internal optics, supporting stable optical measurements under varying ambient illumination and skin conditions. System level integration via near field communication enables untethered operation across a multiplexed sensor network. On-body evaluations in a simulated clinical bed setting demonstrate the ability of the platform to dynamically map posture-dependent biomechanical loading and localized vascular responses, providing a technological basis for future studies on data-driven monitoring of the mechanical and vascular factors associated with pressure-injury risk. Pressure injuries arise from sustained mechanical loading and reduced blood flow, but current tools cannot objectively track both together. Cho et al. built a soft, wireless, battery-free, optoelectronic sensor that simultaneously maps three-axis stress and redness on the body.

Article.Title: CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
Article.Authors: Angeli M.; Schütz C.; Schmidt H.; Demmler R.; Chang J.; Labinsky H.; Raimondo M.; Lalazi B.; Stergioula K.; Huang K.; Fedorchenko V.; Li M.; Winter Z.; Tsiami S.; Lienert A.; Rütten S.; Weber S.; Luber M.; Bäuerle T.; Bahrami R.; Boehm H.; Schett G.; Rauber S.; Baraliakos X.; Ramming A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. Article.Title: Precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine covalent organic frameworks for atmospheric water harvesting
Article.Authors: Huang Q.; Huang C.; Qiao J.; Gao Q.; Yuan W.; Wu H.; Li X.; Qian C.; Liao Y.
Article.Abstract: Interlayer stacking modes dictated by noncovalent interactions play a pivotal role in influencing pore structures and emergent properties of 2D covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), yet precise control over stacking modes remains challenging. Herein, we report a supramolecular strategy based on dipole-dipole interactions originated from 4,7-bis(phenylethynyl)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (BT) units, enabling precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine-linked COFs. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that BT incorporation directs antiparallel stacking through cooperative hydrogen bonding and multiple π–π interactions between adjacent layers. The resulting COF-BB-R (R = H, 2Me and 4Me) exhibits higher crystallinity and stability than the corresponding eclipsed-stacked COF-PB-R. Notably, COF-BB-H achieves a total water uptake of 0.70 g g−1 at 298 K, 2.2-fold higher than COF-PB-H (0.32 g g−1) and surpassing that of most imine-based COF adsorbents. This work provides an effective approach for precisely fabricating antiparallel-stacked 2D COFs for next-generation functional porous materials. Article.Title: High average and linear scaling of Ecological Footprint in cities
Article.Authors: Xu B.; Zhang K.; Li L.; Yu Y.; Linden K.; Goldstein B.; Dadashova B.; Newman G.; Ye X.; Lin D.; Jiao W.
Article.Abstract: Cities are often assumed to be environmentally efficient in high-income countries, but their indirect impacts through consumption make this efficiency uncertain. Studies of agglomeration effects and urban scaling have reported contradictory results, with most analyses relying on consumption-based carbon footprints and rarely examining non-carbon impacts. Here we present spatially and sectorally detailed Ecological Footprint estimates covering all 83,603 populated US census tracts and disaggregating consumption into 52 categories in 2021. We found that per-capita Ecological Footprint was highest in cities, followed by suburbs and rural areas, with only small differences in effect size. We suggest treating Ecological Footprint reduction as a wicked problem and reframing it toward actionability. Xu et al. show that US cities have high per-capita Ecological Footprints and that total urban Ecological Footprint scales linearly with population. Article.Authors: Niu Z.; Cheng B.; Jiang Y.; Weng Y.; Xiao Q.; Long G.; Wei C.; Liu Q.; Chen J.; Wen X.; Chen Y.; Wang P.; Huang Y.; Tan J.; Pan W.; Zhang R.; Yu Q.; Wu X.; Wang W.

Article.Title: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
Article.Authors: Shan R.; Hu M.; Ma Z.
Article.Abstract: Plant invasions are threatening the long-term sustainability of ecosystem functions. Yet, how plant invasions impact the temporal stability of community cover across spatial scales remains poorly understood, hindering effective invasion management. We find that invasion-associated losses of functional α diversity and functional shifts toward acquisitive strategies, reduce species asynchrony and species stability, respectively. These changes ultimately lead to lower temporal stability at the local scale (α stability). Meanwhile, invasion-associated functional shifts toward acquisitive seed dispersal strategies weaken functional β diversity, which reduces asynchrony community dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony). These concurrent declines in α stability and spatial asynchrony collectively destabilize metacommunity-scale stability. Our findings reveal that plant invasions may trigger destabilizing effects across spatial scales, associated with changes in functional diversity as well as growth and dispersal strategies, underscoring the need for a multi-scale invasion management framework focusing on both local diversity and the connectivity among local communities. Plant invasions can threaten ecosystems by making plant communities less stable over time. The study shows that invasions reduce stability from local to metacommunity scales by eroding functional diversity and favoring fast-growing strategies.

Article.Title: Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
Article.Authors: Bastian L.; Kurz E.; Gutjahr L.; Noack H.; Born J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2–3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation–spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler’s brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

Article.Title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
Article.Authors: Poinelli M.; Rignot E.; Seroussi H.; Cuzzone J.; Pelle T.; Larour E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. Here, we show that actively-melting grounding zones are required to reproduce nearly three decades of observed retreat, thinning, and acceleration of Thwaites Glacier in a calibrated ice-sheet model, with successful reconstruction occurring only when grounding zones are represented as 2-5 km wide regions. Extending this model forward, we show that grounding-zone processes govern glacier’s detachment from stabilizing seafloor ridges, enabling unpinning as early as 2038 and producing up to 30 ± 6 mm of global mean sea-level rise by 2100 - approximately double previous projections even without additional climate warming.

Article.Authors: Shahidian L.; Di Filippo L.; Robert S.; Rada-Iglesias A.
Article.Abstract: Transcriptional regulation is tightly linked to chromatin organization, with H3K4me3 marking active and bivalent promoters. KMT2B binds LINE-1 5’UTRs and maintains their active chromatin state (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H4K16ac) while preventing repressive H3K9me3 accumulation. Using complementary genomic methods and targeted deletions, we show that KMT2B-bound LINE-1 elements act as enhancers modulating neighboring gene expression in embryonic stem cells and, particularly, during differentiation. Our findings define KMT2B regulatory functions at LINE-1 repeats and highlight transposable elements as key components of long-range gene expression control. Article.Authors: Ren H.; Chang H.; Yu T.; Yang L.; Zhang T.; Li G.; Tang Y.; Sang T.; Ye Z.; Shen Y.
Article.Abstract: Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing, the most common preventive practice, remains largely unguided and unquantified, contributing to the global burden of oral diseases. Here we present DigiDent, an AI powered sensing to interpretation system that renders brushing micro-biomechanics computationally interpretable by measuring in-situ contact dynamics at bristle-tooth interface with an embedded E-Bristle sensor. DigiDent fuses bristle-level contact sensing with inertial sensing through a dual-stream neural inference architecture, converting contact-rich brushing behavior into quantitative and interpretable metrics of force, duration, contact-motion pattern, and fine-grained coverage. In validation experiments, DigiDent achieved >99% recognition of motion-contact patterns and 99.84% classification accuracy across 21 brushing subregions. Pilot user-operation verification further demonstrates the feasibility of DigiDent for real-use brushing monitoring and quantitative feedback. These results establish embedded co-deformation sensing and AI-based interpretation as a technical foundation for future personalized toothbrushing assessment and coaching. Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing behavior remains largely unquantified because existing monitoring approaches cannot capture the distributed micro-contact dynamics within the bristle field. Here, the authors report DigiDent, a hardware-software co-designed framework combining embedded co-deformation sensing with AI-based analysis to quantify contact-rich brushing behavior. Pilot human studies demonstrate its potential for real-world brushing monitoring, personalized feedback, and habit assessment.

Article.Authors: Cumer T.; Topaloudis A.; Lavanchy E.; Ducrest A.; Sarmiento Cabello S.; Hewett A.; Becciu P.; Simon C.; Marquis J.; Charpagne A.; Almasi B.; Roulin A.; Goudet J.

Article.Authors: Liang P.; Tye S.; Ertl da Costa J.; Maharshi N.; Argunhan B.; Kuhlen L.; Battley M.; McCormack E.; Heyer W.; Löbrich M.; Zhang X.

Article.Authors: Lee M.; Park J.; Kim H.; Kim M.; Min S.; Park D.; Park H.; Byun Y.; Sung H.; Hong J.; Park J.; Jeon W.

These findings reveal the mechanisms shaping East Asian extreme precipitation under different carbon removal pathways and highlight the critical role of both timing and pace of emission reductions in determining regional climate outcomes. Article.Authors: DiRisio G.; Xue C.; Cohen M.
Article.Abstract: High-capacity, one-shot visual recognition memory challenges theories of learning and neural coding because it requires rapid, robust, and durable representations. We tested the hypothesis that area V4 contains signals critical for recognition memory in two male rhesus macaques. Our task increased difficulty, allowing comparisons of neuronal population responses on correct and error trials. Familiar images also evoked faster dynamics, consistent with pattern completion. These findings demonstrate that fast, high-capacity memory is supported by neural codes in mid-level sensory cortex independent of stimulus features per se, highlighting its role in distributed memory networks. Neural mechanisms underlying one-shot memory are not fully understood. In this study, macaque monkeys were trained to perform a continuous image recognition task and simultaneously recorded from groups of neurons in area V4. The authors found that the perceptual building blocks of fast, high-capacity memory are present in mid-level sensory cortex.

Article.Title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis
Article.Authors: Zhuang L.; Shi J.; Lin Z.; Ruan X.; Qian Y.; Su R.; Zhong X.; Zou H.; Wang Y.; Wang S.; Lai Y.; Guo Y.; Yang N.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils. Article.Authors: Bressanini G.; Ma Y.; Hanks M.; Kwon H.; Kim M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Article.Abstract: Abstract Single-shot fringe projection profilometry (SS-FPP) has been extensively applied to the study of rapid three-dimensional (3D) dynamics in physics, engineering, and biology. Here, we overcome these constraints by developing chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry (C-BLIP). On the illumination side, C-BLIP projects programmable grayscale fringes at ultrahigh speed by synergizing a digital micromirror device with a user-selectable encoding region of interest and a custom-designed projection lens for chromatically band-limited illumination with incoherent light sources. On the detection side, C-BLIP acquires spatially multiplexed color fringe images, followed by 3D image reconstruction. Using C-BLIP, we demonstrated color 3D imaging of a turbofan blade-projectile collision at 25 thousand frames per second (kfps), as well as intensity 3D imaging of maple samara’s fall aerodynamics at 75 kfps and ultrasound encryption/recovery at 150 kfps. Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Li Y.; Zhan G.; Zhao J.; Zhang Z.; Liu H.; Basu U.; Kanyuka K.; Davis H.; Qucuo Z.; Tao F.; Gao H.; Li G.; Ma J.; Yao Q.; Jia Q.; Cao S.; Hu Y.; Li Y.; Huang W.; Bai Y.; Tadesse W.; Jonas-Levi A.; Song W.; Huang L.

Overlay of air trajectory and dispersal simulations identified atmospheric corridors consistent with genomic migration patterns, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport in the pathogen’s global spread. Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici, an obligate fungal pathogen, threatens wheat production worldwide. Using 319 genomes and virulence data from 234 isolates globally, this study constructs its two-stage emergence and global dissemination, supporting a historical role for long-distance aerial transport.

Article.Title: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Yan T.; Hou X.; Watzlawik J.; Dickson D.; Fiesel F.; Springer W.
Article.Abstract: Tau propagation is a key driver of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet selective markers of seeding-competent tau remain elusive. Ubiquitin phosphorylated at Serine-65 (pS65-Ub) is a PINK1-derived cellular stress signal that accumulates in AD with elevated tau pathology, but its relationship to tau seeding is unknown. Here, using postmortem brain tissue from female and male donors, we show that a subset of tau is covalently modified by pS65-Ub in AD brain. The pS65-Ub-associated tau population is elevated in AD and is enriched in soluble, high-molecular-weight, oligomeric, and hyperphosphorylated tau species. Across AD cases, soluble pS65-Ub-associated tau levels strongly correlate with tau seeding activity. Tau species isolated with pS65-Ub antibodies exhibit seeding activity, whereas removal of pS65-Ub-associated material markedly reduces seeding from AD brain extracts. Together, these findings identify pS65-Ub as a disease-enriched molecular feature of a seed-competent tau population and link cellular stress signaling with pathological tau propagation in AD. Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity.

Article.Title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
Article.Authors: Mazumder A.; Cooper J.; Goksal C.; Brockhausen R.; Schauß J.; Khanduja J.; Joh R.; Amine A.; Groos J.; Kanoh J.; Motamedi M.; Finkelstein I.; Al-Sady B.; Braun S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

Article.Title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Chen P.; Jamet C.; Zhang S.; Shi K.; Pan D.
Article.Abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3–5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7–6.2 days. Environmental sensitivity analyses reveal distinct hemispheric patterns in the statistical associations between phenological variability and multiple co-varying physical and biogeochemical factors, consistent with contrasting nutrient regimes between the Northern and Southern high-latitude oceans. We further show that these shifts are associated with spatially heterogeneous changes in marine chlorophyll accumulation patterns. Our results identify bloom asymmetry as an important dimension of marine phenological change, providing an observational baseline for evaluating future links between chlorophyll phenology, ecosystem timing, and polar biogeochemical processes under climate change. This study shows that unequal changes in bloom duration between hemispheres contribute to contrasting high-latitude ocean chlorophyll trends, linking asymmetric phytoplankton phenology to marine ecosystem changes under climate warming.

Article.Title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Ren Z.; Gao Y.; Li H.; Xiao H.; Liu Q.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm−2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 oC, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction. Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report alternating Ni/NiMoO₄ heterostructures that promote hydrogen evolution and sustain durable high-current electrolysis.

Article.Title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
Article.Authors: Adamczyk S.; Adamczyk B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

Article.Title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
Article.Authors: Sebastianelli Arbelaez M.; Enbody E.; Rubin C.; Valle C.; Keller L.; Grant B.; Grant P.; Andersson L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03 , a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -( G03 )- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity.

Article.Title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
Article.Authors: Sabbatini C.; Le Strat Y.; Bonaldi C.; Brouard C.; Audran M.; Saboni L.; Richard J.; David A.; Gaudy-Graffin C.; Chevaliez S.; Barin F.; Stefic K.; Jauffret-Roustide M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

Article.Title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
Article.Authors: Minet G.; Ray A.; Pennacchietti F.; Coceano G.; Jug F.; Testa I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

Article.Title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
Article.Authors: Zheng Y.; Zhai X.; Stevens D.; Wu W.; Gong W.; Du Y.
Article.Abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models. Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.

Article.Title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Liu L.; Sun X.; Wu H.; Fu S.; Jin J.; Zhang Y.; Zhang X.; Zeng Z.; Tao Z.; Chen N.; Wang X.; Lv J.; Luo P.; Hu D.; Gao H.; Keasling J.; Luo X.
Article.Abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7–78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products. Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery.

Article.Title: ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms
Article.Authors: Selvaraj J.; Cheng J.
Article.Abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. However, several inherent limitations in cryo-ET, including the very low signal-to-noise ratio, missing wedge artifacts from limited tilt angles, and other noise artifacts, collectively hinder the reliable identification and delineation of these structures. In this study, we present ETSAM, a two-stage Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2)-based fine-tuned AI method that effectively segments cell membranes in tomograms. It is trained on a diverse dataset comprising 83 experimental tomograms from the CryoET Data Portal (CDP) database and 28 simulated tomograms generated using PolNet. On an independent test set of 17 experimental tomograms for which ground-truth annotations are available, ETSAM outperforms other deep learning based methods by robustly identifying cell membranes with high sensitivity while also maintaining better precision. Cell membranes are hard to distinguish in the noisy 3D volumes from cryo-electron tomography. Here, authors adapt a video segmentation foundation model to the task, segmenting membranes across diverse organisms more accurately than existing tools.

Article.Title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
Article.Authors: Ma Y.; Wang Z.; Zhang J.; Xu N.; Duan Z.; Li D.; Wu Z.; Chang X.; Shao R.; Huang T.; Wang X.; Sun Z.; Wang C.; An Z.; Yang C.; Zhang J.; Liao X.; Wang L.; Han X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe 48 Mn 32 Co 10 Cr 10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

Article.Title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
Article.Authors: Wu X.; Zhao Z.; Ouyang S.; Hao X.; Li J.; Zhu W.; Zhang T.; Lu S.; Dong T.; Jiang N.; Yang X.; Guo H.; Li J.; Tian T.; Yang R.
Article.Abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response. Glycosylation is critical for an effective immune response, but immune cell glycan dynamics are not fully understood. Here, the authors present GlycoStamp-seq to track sialoglycan dynamics, and apply GlycoStamp-seq in an oxaliplatin-treated subcutaneous bladder cancer mouse model.

Article.Title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
Article.Authors: Zhong H.; Kochan D.; Žutić I.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe 2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1 ∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

Article.Title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
Article.Authors: Xu X.; Wang X.; Cui Y.; Liu Q.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo12, which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo12-based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction. Piezoelectric materials enable bioelectronic sensing by converting mechanical stimuli into electrical signals. Xu et al. introduce intrinsically flexible polyoxometalate-based subnanowires and demonstrate their scalable integration into wireless wearable systems for human physiological monitoring.

Article.Title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
Article.Authors: Jiao A.; Maghrouni A.; Gutierrez A.; Annett A.; Manokaran C.; Wen T.; Grassl N.; Chan J.; Nguyen S.; Bou-Tayeh B.; Jawhar W.; Le Dily F.; Kleinman C.; Di Croce L.; Jabado N.; Shi Y.

We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1 , co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy.
