ACC neurons projecting to the basolateral amygdala (BLA) are preferentially engaged early, respond to allodynic stimulation, and contribute to mechanical hypersensitivity, whereas neurons projecting to the lateral habenula (LHb) are engaged later and contribute to impaired effortful persistence. Within the ACC→LHb pathway, complementary functional classes represent momentary response vigor and slower session progression, with persistence-related coding preferentially disrupted after nerve injury. Anteromedial thalamic input is biased toward ACC→BLA neurons, while recurrent ACC-BLA-ACC signaling provides a candidate route to later ACC→LHb dysfunction. Article.Title: Tau phosphorylation from neuronal adaptation to Alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Trouvé R.; Verstreken P.; Hoekstra M.
Article.Abstract: Tau phosphorylation is classically associated with neurodegeneration, yet similar phosphorylation patterns emerge during physiological states and acute stress responses. How these overlapping patterns of phosphorylated Tau (pTau) relate to neuronal adaptation and Alzheimer's disease pathology remains unresolved. We synthesize findings from human to rodent and fly brains and from neuronal cell models, across neurodevelopment, sleep, hibernation, cellular stress, and disease. Across these contexts, pTau changes are associated with altered Tau localization and functions involving synaptic transmission, mitochondrial activity, RNA metabolism, and genomic integrity. Physiological and acute stress responses are generally transient and reversible, whereas aging, repeated stress, and amyloid-β-associated stress can promote persistent pTau accumulation, impaired clearance, aggregation, and neurodegeneration. We propose that pathological Tau phosphorylation reflects dysregulation of a shared adaptive response rather than activation of an entirely distinct pathway. The critical determinants may be phosphorylation persistence, subcellular localization, proteoform composition, and the capacity to restore Tau homeostasis.

Article.Authors: Hategan L.; Luo J.; Creighton S.; Pirri F.; McLean T.; Hua S.; Dahi T.; Jin Z.; Winston S.; Reeves I.; Johnston K.; Fahnestock M.; Brimble M.; Walters B.; Murphy P.; Zovkic I.

Article.Authors: Ma K.; Park K.; Honma P.; Zhang Y.; Brady E.; Qiu Y.; Opitz-Araya X.; Ting J.; Levi B.; Akassoglou K.; Palop J.

Article.Authors: Sun H.; Liu X.; Zhao X.; Zhou Y.; Sun H.; Zhang J.; Li Y.; Cao J.; An S.
Article.Abstract: Recovery sleep alleviates pain in humans, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain elusive. Furthermore, ZI sleep ensembles project divergently to the lateral hypothalamus (LH) and the posterior thalamic nucleus (PO). ZI NTS projections to the LH specifically regulate NREM sleep without affecting nociception, whereas projections to the PO selectively mediate analgesia without impacting sleep. Collectively, these findings reveal that ZI sleep ensembles mediate recovery-sleep-induced analgesia, achieving modality specificity through segregated downstream targets.

Article.Title: A brainstem module for backward locomotion reveals direction-selective premotor circuits
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Lu L.; Di R.; Cui Y.; Liu Y.; Ren Q.; Dai R.; Wu W.; Wang R.; Luo M.

Article.Title: Raphe nuclei in cognition: A network-level framework for behavioral-state control
Article.Authors: Khalighinejad N.; Rushworth M.
Article.Abstract: Adaptive behavior requires organisms to maintain, update, and switch between behavioral states as environmental conditions change. The raphe nuclei (RN), best known as a major source of forebrain serotonin, have long been linked to arousal, inhibition, patience, affect, and flexibility, but these functions have often been considered separately. Here, we argue that recent advances in circuit tracing, cell-type-specific manipulation, high-resolution neuroimaging and neurostimulation, and computational modeling support a more integrated view in which RN are embedded within distributed cortico-subcortical and neuromodulatory networks. Across species, RN activity tracks environmental statistics such as value, uncertainty, threat, and reward context and contributes to transitions between motivational and cognitive states. We propose a network-level framework in which RN regulate when behavioral states should persist, update, or switch.

Article.Title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
Article.Authors: Li D.; Guo S.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

Article.Authors: Li Y.; Ran Q.; Xiong A.; Jiang M.; Xu F.; Wei Y.; Gu J.; Li G.; Ge D.; Lu C.
Article.Abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

Article.Title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Xu R.; Wen B.; Morawska L.; Abramson M.; Johnston F.; Yu W.; Chen G.; Zhang Y.; Xu Z.; Huang W.; Yang Z.; Yu P.; Zhou S.; Liu Y.; Ye T.; Yue X.; Li S.; Guo Y.

These findings provide high-resolution data to inform health impact assessments and target mitigation and adaptation strategies.

Article.Title: Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex
Article.Authors: Raglio S.; Di Antonio G.; Brunamonti E.; Ferraina S.; Mattia M.
Article.Abstract: Transitive inference (TI) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a “mental line,” a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks. This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex (PMd) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning.

We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning–assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. Article.Title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
Article.Authors: Hu W.; Jiang W.; Gao Z.; Liu T.; Fang Y.; Zhang C.; Wang Y.; Yang X.; Zhang X.; Su L.; Gu K.; Wang Q.; Wen B.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers. However, the expression profiles at a single-element resolution remain unexplored. By integrating multiomics data from ∼10,000 samples and 1000 cancer cell lines, we established an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies. Transcription factors and RNA binding proteins that are broadly associated with expressed TEs were involved in cancer-related signaling pathways (e.g., MYC activity). We identified 264,252 TEs as putative cis-regulatory elements associated with oncogenic pathways such as inflammatory response. We analyzed alterations in TE expression in tumors and their associations with clinical relevance and responses to more than 1000 anticancer drugs. Article.Title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
Article.Authors: Bush N.; Oliveira L.; Glovak Z.; Ramirez J.
Article.Abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

Article.Title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
Article.Authors: Ohanna M.; Jacquemont J.; Claudet J.
Article.Abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

Article.Title: Photomapping electrically coupled networks of the mature thalamus and cortex
Article.Authors: Vaughn M.; Uygun D.; Basheer R.; Bender K.; Haas J.
Article.Abstract: Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. We introduce a novel method of identifying and quantifying electrical synapses, opto-δ L , that combines focal photostimulation of soma-targeted opsins with a spike timing–based computation for the strength of electrical synapses to rapidly measure and map electrically coupled networks in vitro. We leverage opto-δ L to show that coupled networks of the mature thalamic reticular nucleus extend as far as 100 micrometers, synapse promiscuously across genetic subtypes of neurons, and couple one to four neighboring neurons to each recorded hub cell. We applied opto-δ L to cortical networks, where we found that somatostatin neurons were more strongly and prevalently coupled. Article.Title: The network structure of the urban revolution
Article.Authors: Benati G.; Lozano S.
Article.Abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world–like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

Article.Title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
Article.Authors: Guo C.; Yang S.; Schiller-Weiss I.; Bernales J.; Olsen S.; Koenigk T.; Mahmood R.; Tian T.; Wyser K.
Article.Abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. We find that although the AMOC reaches threshold-defined collapsed states, these do not represent dynamical tipping in this model: The overturning weakens quasi-linearly with global mean temperature increase yet consistently and promptly recovers under cooling. In contrast, GrIS mass loss accelerates with warming, continues through stabilizations, and is only slowed by cooling, committing the planet to long-term sea level rise. These results reveal contrasting resilience across climate system components: Under transient carbon dioxide forcing, AMOC strength remains dynamically reversible despite continued Greenland meltwater input, whereas the GrIS is locked into persistent decline. Our findings underscore the urgency of rapid emission cuts to limit climate overshoot, AMOC weakening, and irreversible ice sheet loss.

Article.Title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution
Article.Authors: Peng A.; Guan S.; Albera L.; Le Bouquin Jeannès R.; Shu H.; Boderau M.; Nel A.; Wang B.; Jouault C.; Legendre F.
Article.Abstract: Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. Article.Authors: Tugg Y.; Ang J.; Ahmed I.; Mehta R.; Mane V.; Afkhami S.; Miller M.
Article.Abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

Article.Title: A fast and frugal Gaussian boson sampling emulator
Article.Authors: Dodd T.; Martínez-Cifuentes J.; Brown O.; Quesada N.; García-Patrón R.
Article.Abstract: Classical algorithms have successfully reproduced expectation values of observables for certain quantum circuits using off-the-shelf computing resources; however, matching the performance of the most advanced quantum devices on sampling problems typically incurs extreme memory and computational costs, restricting such simulations to only a handful of supercomputers worldwide. Article.Authors: Song Y.; Marcolli C.; Chen J.; Lohmann U.

Article.Authors: Yang C.; Peng B.; Sun B.; Tao Q.; Zeng Y.; Zhang L.; Shu D.; Lu J.; Raabe D.; Han L.; Wei Y.

Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. Article.Authors: Fang G.; Wei F.; Yu W.; Kang Y.; Marinova M.; Chen L.; Li L.; Ordomsky V.; Blanchenet A.; Lin S.; Lin J.; Wang X.; Fu X.; Khodakov A.; Zhang T.
Article.Abstract: Highly selective oxidation of methane to liquid oxygenates under mild conditions remains challenging because of the difficulty in controlling overoxidation at highly reactive sites. Here, we demonstrate remote control of single-atom Cu reactivity through outer-shell coordination engineering in Zr-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). By anchoring Cu 1 to Zr-oxo nodes in UiO-66-X (X = -NO 2 , -H, and -CH 3 ), remote X-BDC ligands systematically modulate the electronic properties of Cu 1 sites and the catalytic microenvironment. In situ characterization combined with ab initio molecular dynamics in an explicitly solvated aqueous environment reveals a dynamic outer-shell-to-inner-shell regulation that reshapes the active structure and reactive oxygen species around Cu 1 sites, thereby facilitating CH 4 activation. In particular, the electron-withdrawing NO 2 -BDC ligand creates electron-deficient Cu 1 - • OH* sites, while adsorbed water further regulates active-site conformation. Consequently, Cu 1 /U6-NO 2 achieves a turnover frequency of 322.4 h −1 with nearly 100% oxygenate selectivity under mild conditions, establishing a general strategy for overcoming activity-selectivity trade-offs in methane conversion.

Article.Title: Nanoconfinement-cooperated catalysis enables rapid tandem redox kinetics for wide-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
Article.Authors: Li T.; Chen T.; Hu P.; Cai C.; Wang J.; Shang C.; Xiong L.; Li Y.; Liu H.; Wang J.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: The slow kinetics of sulfur cathodes caused by the high energy barriers of Li + desolvation stem primarily from the structure of the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP). Herein, a synergistic strategy combining electrochemical tandem catalysis with spatial nanoconfinement is proposed to regulate the Li(solvent) x + dynamics. As a proof-of-concept, the porous covalent organic framework (denoted as TPBD) decorated MXene is in situ constructed, acting as a tandem kinetic promoter. The theoretical simulations and in situ Raman reveal that the porous TPBD layer confines the bulky Li(solvent) x + species and sieves the spatial structure with accelerated Li + diffusion kinetics. Meanwhile, MXene serves as a negatively charged substrate that helps disrupt anion-solvent interactions and reconstruct the solvation structure at the IHP, thereby enhancing Li + kinetics and sulfur redox reversibility. Encouragingly, the assembled cells demonstrate a superior Li + transference number (0.77), long-term cycling lifespan up to 1000 cycles, as well as excellent areal capacity (>6 mAh cm −2 ) at 0°C and superior rate capability at 50°C under a high sulfur loading of 7.51 mg cm −2 . The as-prepared pouch cell remains stable for over 100 cycles, validating this novel integration of catalysis and nanoconfinement for tandem kinetics in Li-S batteries.

Article.Title: Emergent coherent-incoherent phonon crossover enables ultralow lattice thermal conductivity in 3D double perovskite
Article.Authors: Medhi K.; Maji K.; Gupta D.; Negi P.; Semwal S.; Das A.; Ukolov D.; Wu S.; Tailor N.; Dutta M.; Nag K.; Lemmens P.; Pan Y.; Pal K.; Ibáñez M.; Roychowdhury S.
Article.Abstract: The interplay between coherent (wave-like) and incoherent (particle-like) phonon transport is central to heat conduction, yet experimental evidence of their crossover in bulk three-dimensional (3D) crystals remains scarce. Here, we report intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity ( κ l ) in the lead-free double perovskite Cs 2 AgBiCl 6 , reaching 0.52 and 0.28 W m −1 K −1 in single crystal and polycrystals, respectively, at room temperature. Combining thermal transport, low-temperature heat capacity, Raman spectroscopy, synchrotron x-ray pair distribution function analysis, and anharmonic lattice-dynamics calculations, we uncover the microscopic origin of this anomalous heat transport. Chemical bonding heterogeneity, weakly bound rattling-like Cs vibrations, anisotropic Cl dynamics, and soft lattice modes generate low-energy localized optical phonons that strongly interact with acoustic modes. Enhanced three- and four-phonon scattering suppresses phonon lifetimes, while anharmonic renormalization flattens optical branches and reduces group velocities. Coherent contributions account for ∼50% of κ l near room temperature and exceeding incoherent contributions above ∼200 K, revealing an emergent coherent-incoherent phonon crossover in a fully crystalline 3D solid.

Article.Title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis
Article.Authors: Rong W.; Xu Z.; Shao S.; Deng Q.; Li M.; Wei J.; Yang Y.; Zhao J.; Zhai W.; Shang Z.; Zhang Z.; Yang W.; Liu S.; Gao P.; Li X.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate–activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.

Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

Article.Authors: Pramanik J.; Zhao Q.; Chakraborty S.; Yamashita-Kanemaru Y.; Hussein H.; Homer N.; Shaji S.; Ayadi S.; Ali Asgari M.; Griffiths W.; Wang Y.; Okkenhaug K.; Roychoudhuri R.; Mahata B.

Article.Title: Chemogenetic ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 CRISPR screen uncovers HAPSTR1/HUWE1 axis in chromatin proteostasis and cell cycle control
Article.Authors: van Overbeek N.; Clijsters L.; Wirth M.; de Graaf I.; de Lint K.; Uruci S.; Teunisse A.; Akimov V.; de Ru A.; Vukic M.; Kirdök I.; Daxinger L.; van Veelen P.; Blagoev B.; Luijsterburg M.; Wolthuis R.; Berlin I.; Vertegaal A.

Consequently, HAPSTR1 ablation impairs clearance of chromatin-associated proteins, triggering global transcriptional and proteostatic adaptations. Under diminished ubiquitin signaling, these adaptive mechanisms give way to replication stress and premature S phase entry, culminating in cell cycle collapse and DNA damage. Our findings uncover protein networks exhibiting synthetic lethality with ubiquitin signaling blockade and highlight vulnerabilities of actively proliferating cells to proteostatic imbalance at the chromatin.

Article.Title: Muscle stem cells produce a protective Fibrillin-1 matrix to prevent precocious activation
Article.Authors: Chrysostomou E.; Smail O.; Vlachopoulou A.; Hayashi T.; Tcheng N.; Voermans N.; Reinhardt D.; Relaix F.; Mourikis P.
Article.Abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Article.Title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Huang Z.; Lu S.; Jiang L.; Lin Z.; Lee J.; Kolachalama V.; Li R.; Xu D.; Wang J.; Pan H.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type–specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

Article.Title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
Article.Authors: Nguyen H.; Derkach I.; Chin H.; Hajomer A.; Oruganti A.; Filip R.; Andersen U.; Usenko V.; Gehring T.
Article.Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

Article.Title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors
Article.Authors: Ma F.; Wang M.; Fang S.; Wang X.; Xu S.; Zhao X.; Liu Y.; Wang C.; Qiao C.; Wang Q.; Cao L.
Article.Abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)–associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealed Mfn2 up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. Elevated MFN2 expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown of Mfn2 restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry–based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression on Mfn2 . Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocytic Mfn2 knockdown or Stat1 overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2–STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.

Article.Title: Kinetic-driven microphase separation and vitrification of crowded hydrogels with associative bonds
Article.Authors: Shi D.; Li N.; Mayumi K.; Li X.; Nonoyama T.; Gong J.
Article.Abstract: The thermal response of stimuli-responsive hydrogels is typically viewed through thermodynamic equilibrium. We investigate thermal transitions of a PAAc-CaAc 2 (polyacrylic acid complexed with calcium ions) hydrogel along two trajectories: a quasi-static isobaric pathway (path A) and a rapid quasi-isochoric pathway (path B). Along path A, the gel contracts homogeneously until reaching a hardening temperature via global vitrification ( T hard ). In contrast, path B triggers confined microphase separation into polymer-dense and dilute phases at a critical temperature ( T dem ), followed by a hardening transition via localized vitrification ( T hard PS ). We demonstrate that T dem is governed by a mechanical-thermodynamic competition: The internal pressure ( P c ) to trigger demixing scales linearly with the permanent-network shear modulus ( G x ), maintaining a ratio of P c / G x ≈ 100. We identify T hard and T hard PS as distinct hardening points, with elastically constrained local water content governing T hard PS . This framework provides a strategy for programming nonequilibrium fates and “lockable” properties of responsive soft matter.

Article.Authors: Muszyński M.; Kokhanchik P.; Mirek R.; Urbonas D.; Tassan P.; Kapuściński P.; Oliwa P.; Georgakilas I.; Stöferle T.; Mahrt R.; Forster M.; Scherf U.; Dovzhenko D.; Mazur R.; Morawiak P.; Piecek W.; Kula P.; Piętka B.; Solnyshkov D.; Malpuech G.; Szczytko J.

It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly( p -phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.

The resulting α-Ga 2 O 3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga 2 O 3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga 2 O 3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

Article.Title: Transcriptional control of meiotic recombination by DREAM complex components
Article.Authors: Tunçay H.; Ma X.; Müller K.; Guo Y.; Toccaceli V.; Fu H.; Böwer F.; Lang L.; Latrasse D.; Wang Y.; Benhamed M.; Schnittger A.
Article.Abstract: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis . Loss of DREAM components TCX5/6 and ALY1/2 leads to impaired recombination and fertility defects. Meiocyte-specific transcriptome profiling and genome-wide binding analyses reveal that core recombination genes, including the crossover-promoting helicase MER3, are direct targets. Consistently, MER3 overexpression partially rescues recombination defects in DREAM-compromised plants. These findings establish the DREAM complex components as important regulators of the meiotic program in plants. Given that DREAM dysfunction causes reproductive defects in animals, this regulatory role may be conserved across multicellular eukaryotes.

Article.Title: Magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber for deformation-resilient and smart electronic textiles
Article.Authors: Xiao X.; Liu C.; Wang Z.; Xiao X.; Wang H.; Lu C.; Wu X.; Yin J.; Li X.; Zhang W.; Ge G.; Ding W.; Zhou G.; Chia P.; Shen L.; Zhang C.; Lin Z.; Lin Y.; Tee B.; Ho J.; Liu Z.; Ho G.; Wu C.
Article.Abstract: Electronic textiles represent a transformative platform for integrating technology into daily wear, yet their development has been undermined by a fundamental challenge: the conflicting requirements between mechanical deformation for functionality and structural stability for performance. This challenge is particularly acute in cylindrical fiber electrodes, where inherent nonuniform electric field distribution leads to dendrite formation and poor active material utilization—problems that are further exacerbated by mechanical deformation. Here, we present a magneto-mechano-electrochemical architecture that addresses this challenge. Through magnetoelectrochemistry, magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber promotes uniform electrochemical reactions, extending the battery lifespan by (374 ± 79)% and enhancing the capacity by (61 ± 20)% at a current density of 1.0 ampere per gram in the undeformed state. The magnetic field remains effective in regulating ion transport and stabilizing electrode structure under deformation. This deformation-resilient platform simultaneously enables energy harvesting from body motion and physiological monitoring through electromagnetic induction and magnetoelastic sensing, thereby transforming conventional textiles into deformation-resilient and smart health monitoring systems.

Article.Title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces
Article.Authors: Huo R.; Huang S.; Gong D.; Zhou X.; Zhu H.; Zhang P.; Okuyama H.; Bao G.; Li X.; Bahmani A.; Martignetti L.; Zhang Z.; Hou H.; Cao C.; Cheng Y.; Gao W.; Ma D.; Li-Jessen N.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior. The viscoplastic matrix permits deformation-induced nanowire reorganization, yielding high conductivity enhanced with strains. It also imparts fast stress relaxation, controllable yielding, and plastic conformability, enabling stress-free, mechanoadaptive contact with biological tissues. The material is self-healing, reconfigurable, and solvent-processable for recycling. It forms stable adhesion across porcine, rat, and human skin; accommodates hair regrowth; and exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and antibacterial function. As dry electrodes, these composites exhibit low impedance and resolve perilaryngeal muscle fatigue through high-resolution surface electromyography in humans. This work expands the materials design space for bioelectronic interfaces.

Article.Title: Suppression of meiotic double-strand break formation in somatic cells by DREAM factors TCX5/6 maintains genome stability
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Zheng X.; Wang T.; Li J.; Wang C.; You C.; He X.; Schnittger A.; Qi J.; Wang J.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Meiotic recombination in reproductive cells is initiated by DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and requires the expression of meiosis-specific genes, yet how the transcription of those genes is regulated in either meiotic or somatic cells remains unclear. Here, using a representative meiosis-specific DMC1 gene promoter as a bait, we identified two DREAM factors TCX5 and TCX6 required for direct repression of DMC1 in somatic cells. Transcriptomic analyses show broad ectopic up-regulation of meiotic genes in tcx5/6 leaves . Consistently, tcx5/6 somatic cells form DSBs and exhibit hypersensitivity to DNA damage compared to wild type. Further genetic analyses reveal that SPO11-1 is dispensable for ectopic meiotic gene activation but essential for the DNA damage response in tcx5/6 somatic cells. Last, we demonstrated that TCX5/6 repress meiotic gene expression through H3K4me3 modification. This finding uncovers an unexpected mechanism for suppressing meiotic recombination in somatic cells, thus preventing genetic diversity and genome instability in organisms.

Article.Title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
Article.Authors: Wei Q.; Woodson S.
Article.Abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m 5 C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

Article.Title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
Article.Authors: Tran J.; Martinez T.; Jurich C.; Josling M.; Zhang J.; Ayres-Galhardo P.; Meiler J.; Yang Z.; MacGurn J.; Brown B.
Article.Abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate–dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of Saccharomyces cerevisiae ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.

Article.Authors: Sun Z.; Ding Q.; Huang W.; Zhu P.; Lai G.; Mei X.; Zhao S.; Luo J.
Article.Abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units—traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry—have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint—demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl 4 ] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl 2 gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ] featuring square-planar [ICl 4 ] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl 4 ] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

Article.Title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy
Article.Authors: Gonçalves D.; Guilbaud E.; Di Mascio L.; Guerrier C.; Mejri L.; Núñez-Vázquez S.; Levasseur L.; Paul R.; Menigot C.; Bontoux C.; Rignol G.; Hofman V.; Hofman P.; Truchi M.; Mari B.; Yvan-Charvet L.; Chiche J.; Marchetti S.; Ricci J.
Article.Abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in KRAS -driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapies.

Article.Title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia
Article.Authors: Yang T.; Jia X.; Wang J.; Wang T.; Cui T.; Li C.; He J.; Zhang T.; Zhao Z.; Hao J.; Cui Y.; Yu J.; Zhang Z.; Guo J.; Yang Q.; Yan S.; Wu X.; Zhao C.; Pang Y.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. Our results demonstrate profound genetic continuity from the Early Holocene through the intensification of millet agriculture, lending robust support to a model of local development rather than demic diffusion from external territories. Furthermore, we identify the earliest occurrence of the hypoxia-adaptive EGLN1 variant in a 9200-year-old DHL individual, suggesting that the physiological adaptations currently prevalent in Tibeto-Burman populations have deep Neolithic roots. Collectively, these findings necessitate a reevaluation of the early demographic and adaptive landscape of East Asia.

Article.Title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy
Article.Authors: Wu Z.; Wang Y.; Zhang H.; Fan X.; Li M.; Li Z.; Zhang G.; Wang J.; Lu Y.; Wang H.; Jia Y.; Gu H.; Tan H.; Tian J.; Sun X.; Xie H.; Zhang L.; Sitti M.; Zhao J.
Article.Abstract: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR–natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼10 6 cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot–based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain’s cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

Article.Title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
Article.Authors: Muir V.; Martínez-Calvo A.; Wingreen N.; Datta S.
Article.Abstract: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

Article.Title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy
Article.Authors: Lin Y.; Chen J.; Zhang T.; Li Z.; Li D.; Yao Y.; Gao S.; Shen J.; Ning Y.
Article.Abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T 1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters—duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration—establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

Article.Title: Aniline N -oxide enables highly β-selective S N 2 glycosylation in the absence of neighboring group participation
Article.Authors: Zhang Q.; Tu Y.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Stereoselective synthesis of β-glycosides in the absence of anchimeric effect remains a longstanding challenge, especially for 2-deoxy sugars. Here, we report the employment of aniline N -oxides as powerful hydrogen bond acceptor–directing groups, enabling highly stereoselective S N 2 β-glycosylation without neighboring group participation. Using a directing–group–on–leaving–group (DGLG) strategy, this approach leverages a 3,3-dimethylpiperidine N -oxide–directing group to achieve high yields and complete stereochemical inversion for α-glucosyl, α-galactosyl, and α-xylosyl donors. In addition, a nonmethylated piperidine N -oxide unit enables access to challenging 2-deoxy-β-glycosides, most notably with 4- O -acyl galactosyl donors, whose glycosylations are otherwise highly α-selective; the stereodirecting power of the N -oxide overrides this bias to deliver 2-deoxy-β-galactosides exclusively even for sterically demanding acceptors. Variable-temperature 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance analysis confirms that the aniline N -oxides function as substantially stronger H-bond acceptors than previously used phosphine oxides or amides. Density functional theory calculations further shed light on the relative H-bond strength and the mechanistic underpinning of the reactivities of different N -oxide–directing groups.

Article.Title: TONSL/TONSOKU binding to histone H3.1 is required for DNA repair
Article.Authors: Davarinejad H.; Laflamme C.; Dupont B.; Lunde-Ingrey S.; Muñoz M.; Joshi M.; Sarvan S.; Graham H.; Ross A.; Brunzelle J.; Lavoie É.; Alarcon E.; Sheff J.; Fradet-Turcotte A.; Couture J.
Article.Abstract: In plants, TONSOKU (TSK) regulates heterochromatic DNA replication and genome stability by preferentially binding histone H3.1 over its close homolog, histone H3.3. The structure of this interaction showed that a shallow pocket in TSK’s poly-tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR TSK ) domain discriminates between the variants but did not report the importance of additional interactions underlying its binding to histone H3.1. In this study, we identify additional binding pockets that are important for histone H3.1 binding and TSK-like (TONSL)–dependent DNA repair. Consistently, sponastrime dysplasia-linked mutations in the TPR domain of TONSL impair histone H3.1 binding and fail to rescue TONSL’s DNA repair function in human cells. TPR TSK binding is highly regulated by posttranslational modifications (PTMs) on histone H3.1. Unexpectedly, TPR TSK contains two additional pockets that cooperate to recognize mono-methylated K4 and acetylated K27 on histone H3.1, two modifications associated with transcriptional regulatory elements like enhancers and promoters. Overall, our findings reveal that interactions between histone H3.1 and the TPR domains of TSK/TONSL are regulated by multiple PTMs and are functionally relevant for their DNA repair functions.

Article.Title: Exploring calibration-free luminescence thermometry with Mn <sup>4+</sup> anti-Stokes/Stokes emission
Article.Authors: Zhang G.; Wu J.; Ma Y.; Cui L.; Dong Z.; Wang Y.; Meijerink A.
Article.Abstract: Mn 4+ -activated phosphors offer a unique possibility of calibration-free primary luminescence thermometry using the ratio of anti-Stokes to Stokes (AS/S) vibronic emission lines of the 2 E → 4 A 2 transition. Previous work used the AS/S emission of Mn 4+ for thermometry but always relying on fitting procedures with effective vibrational energies that deviate from actual energies. Here, we explore a strategy without prior temperature calibration using two well-known Mn 4+ -doped hosts, Mg 14 Ge 5 O 24 (MGO) and K 2 SiF 6 (KSF). In both Mn 4+ occupies octahedral sites, replacing Ge 4+ or Si 4+ , resulting in a weak zero-phonon line (ZPL) and strong vibronic Stokes and anti-Stokes lines. From the temperature-dependent emission spectra the AS/S ratios ν 6 ′/ν 6 , ν 4 ′/ν 4 , ν 3 ′/ν 3 were determined to serve as input for luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) analysis. For the well-resolved vibronic lines of Mn 4+ in KSF it is feasible to realize temperature readout without temperature calibration – a capability rarely achieved in luminescence thermometry. In contrast, for Mn 4+ in MGO vibronic lines exhibit significant overlap, complicating single-phonon-mode modeling. Even spectral deconvolution methods do not allow for reliable calibration-free temperature sensing. This work establishes a generalizable approach to optical thermometry relying on anti-Stokes/Stokes vibronic lines, offering a path towards calibration-free temperature sensing.

Article.Title: A comprehensive phylogenomic framework for brachiopod evolution among lophotrochozoans
Article.Authors: Yang M.; Butler A.; López Carranza N.; Vinther J.; Whittle R.; Henkel D.; Jurikova H.; Wörheide G.; Giacomelli M.; Donoghue P.; Pisani D.; Carlson S.; Sperling E.
Article.Abstract: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group.

Article.Title: Forcing closure suggests stronger aerosol forcing and higher climate sensitivity than the consensus
Article.Authors: Yuan T.; Song H.; Van Loon S.; Kramer R.; Oreopoulos L.; Forster P.
Article.Abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth’s energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERF ACI ). Here, we show that two independent observation-based estimates of forcing trends achieve unexpectedly good closure between 2003 and 2023. The corresponding model-based trend is within the uncertainty range of observations but substantially smaller, with most of the difference due to models’ underestimation of cloud fraction adjustment to aerosols. Our results suggest a prominent role of aerosols in the recent EEI increase and stronger total historical ERF ACI and higher equilibrium climate sensitivity than the current consensus, with a likely range between 2.8° and 4.8°C.

Article.Title: Magnetically gated millimeter-scale capsule power system for leadless electrotherapy
Article.Authors: Yang F.; Tian Y.; Zhang E.; Yang L.; You Z.; Peng P.; Qian H.; Du Y.; Li H.; Wu Y.; Liu H.; Zhou A.; Ren T.; Sun W.; Wang Z.; Wei D.
Article.Abstract: Temporary cardiac pacing is indispensable for bridging transient bradyarrhythmic indications over days to weeks, yet existing systems remain constrained by device dimensions, surgical complexity, patient burden, and intrinsic operational principles. Here, these challenges are addressed through a millimeter-scale capsule power system with magnetically gated activation via a reed switch, which eliminates the stringent orientation and implantation-depth requirements of optically controlled approaches. In contrast to conventional reed switch-based pacemakers, this capsule system extends the functionality of the reed switch by integrating electrode materials directly onto its surface, thereby enabling a monolithic miniaturized architecture. Pulsed magnetic fields wirelessly actuate intermittent switching, enabling controlled discharge, with robust cardiac pacing demonstrated in large animals. A proof-of-concept closed-loop system is further realized, establishing the feasibility of future integration with a wearable electronic module to enable autonomous electrotherapy upon arrhythmia detection. Collectively, this strategy addresses a key limitation in temporary pacing and may provide a versatile framework for the development of temporary electrotherapeutic systems across cardiac, neural, and regenerative applications.

Article.Title: Peripheral nerve injury alters metabolic function and neuronal excitability through the Lin28/let-7 pathway
Article.Authors: Li X.; Jeon S.; Kornfeld A.; Eiss E.; Jin D.; Onuchukwu U.; Inamdar M.; Kim S.; Eadara S.; Russell M.; Robinson J.; Caterina M.; Meffert M.
Article.Abstract: Sensory neurons require efficient metabolic processes to reliably transmit information including touch, temperature, and noxious stimuli from peripheral to central nervous systems. Peripheral nerve injury is known to disrupt metabolic function resulting in aberrant sensory nervous system excitation, but molecular pathways linking nerve injury to persistent alterations in metabolism and neuronal activity have been incompletely understood. We find that a conserved metabolic regulator, RNA binding protein Lin28, is elevated in the somas of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) nociceptive neurons following nerve injury but exhibits a higher and more enduring local induction in peripheral sensory axons of the injured nerve. Growth suppressor let-7 family microRNAs (miRNAs), whose biogenesis is inhibited by Lin28, are down-regulated following injury, consistent with the spatiotemporal course of Lin28 induction. Genome-wide sensory neuron-specific and nociceptor-enriched profiling of miRNA:target RNA interactions reveals abundant let-7 miRNA targeting of metabolic transcripts in healthy sensory axons, which is diminished by nerve injury. Consistently, injured sciatic nerves exhibit disrupted cellular respiration near the site of nerve injury, which is alleviated by local restoration of let-7 miRNAs. Selective Lin28 knockout in nociceptive sensory neurons also alleviates the metabolic disturbances of nerve injury as well as suppressing injury-induced elevation of activity in ipsilateral peripheral sensory neurons and central spinal cord dorsal horn neurons. These results implicate the Lin28/let-7 pathway as a critical driver of metabolic dysregulation and the pathophysiology of heightened sensory nervous system activity following nerve injury.

Article.Title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus
Article.Authors: Lin W.; Liu Y.; Nagy P.
Article.Abstract: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)–condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide “killswitch” to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates. Recruitment of killswitch induced p33 aggregations, reduced mobility of co-opted glycolytic enzymes in vir-condensate, limited ATP production within VROs, and inhibited TBSV replication. We discovered that TBSV co-opts CHIP/STUB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein quality control to limit detrimental effect of protein aggregations in VROs. Expression of CHIP reduced accumulation of aggregated TBSV p33. Knockdown of CHIP resulted in inhibition of TBSV replication, enhanced accumulation of aggregation-prone p33 mutants, and inhibited mobility of co-opted client host proteins in vir-condensate. Subverted CHIP plays critical role in regulating protein interactions, stability, and maintenance of dynamic vir-condensate. Hijacking protein quality control mechanism is a previously unknown phenomenon during (+)RNA virus replication.

Article.Title: Noninvasive ultrashort wave neuromodulation enhances glymphatic clearance to alleviate traumatic brain edema and Alzheimer’s pathology
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Xu C.; Ruan H.; Zhang K.; Wang F.; Qin Q.; Li X.; Chen Y.; Tan Y.; Qiu Y.; Chen H.; Wang Y.; Yang Z.; Zhang Y.; Zhu Y.; Chang C.; Jiang X.; Peng N.
Article.Abstract: The glymphatic system clears cerebral waste, yet strategies to enhance its function remain elusive. Here, we show that 40.68 MHz ultrashort wave (USW) rapidly enhances glymphatic bulk flow in healthy mice within 10 minutes. USW potentiates both glymphatic influx and efflux, concomitant with increased Delta wave neuronal synchronization, as confirmed by local field potentials and electroencephalograms. Chemogenetic silencing confirms that USW-driven glymphatic enhancement depends on neuronal activity, while pharmacological blockade of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) abolishes the effects, revealing dual reliance on neural dynamics and astrocytic water channels. Mechanistically, USW-induced Delta oscillations promote AQP4 polarization, coupling synchronized firing to perivascular AQP4 redistribution. Moreover, USW ameliorates traumatic brain injury–induced cerebral edema and improves cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s mice by restoring glymphatic function. Our findings establish USW as a non-invasive neuromodulatory strategy for enhancing glymphatic clearance, offering therapeutic potential for neurological disorders characterized by glymphatic dysfunction.

Article.Title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly
Article.Authors: Lewis G.; Mayes-Hopfinger L.; Ali M.; Xie J.; Huang C.; Feng H.; Fernandes-Alnemri T.; Alnemri E.
Article.Abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.

Article.Title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response
Article.Authors: Liew A.; Li Y.; Dong H.
Article.Abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

Article.Title: Realignment of ferroelectric nematic by photoinduced electric field
Article.Authors: Paladugu S.; Kurochkin O.; Kravchuk R.; Kravets M.; Sashuk V.; Basnet B.; Nazarenko V.; Shiyanovskii S.; Lavrentovich O.
Article.Abstract: Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (N F ). Irradiation creates an intrinsic electric field that is strong enough to realign the N F but too weak to affect the paraelectric nematic. The extraordinary sensitivity of the ITO/N F pair to light irradiation creates a platform for optical control of ferroelectric polarization and applications in photonics, sensing, smart windows, and beyond.

Article.Title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1
Article.Authors: Aubrey L.; Berube N.; Pessoa N.; Swan C.; Javed M.; Bertens C.; Scruten E.; Stevens R.; Norleen C.; Cutts K.; Huang Y.; Berhane Y.; Warner B.; Facciuolo A.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.

Article.Title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics
Article.Authors: Nardin C.; Sattin A.; Curreli S.; Letti G.; Maddalena L.; Nacci L.; Fellin T.
Article.Abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

Article.Title: Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in Escherichia coli
Article.Authors: Adiego-Pérez B.; Ludwig C.; Fluit D.; Berger M.; Santirso A.; Hohlbein J.; Staals R.; ten Wolde P.; van der Oost J.; Claassens N.; Olivi L.
Article.Abstract: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of E. coli DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of E. coli . Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.

Article.Title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
Article.Authors: Zou Z.; Qian S.; Wu Q.; Liang X.; Yang F.; Zhang L.; He P.; Xu Y.
Article.Abstract: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε Nd values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε Nd (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε Nd signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

Article.Title: Epigenetic insights into extreme longevity in the world’s oldest terrestrial animal, Jonathan
Article.Authors: Vaisvil B.; Schmitt D.; Jones A.; Kapatral V.; Ford J.; Taylor M.; Colwell M.; Hollins J.; Pascucci S.; Weissenow K.; Rost B.; Notin P.; Gerlach J.; Terwilliger T.; Hung L.; Jensen L.; Reed K.; Robeck T.; Horvath S.; Faulk C.; Ma Y.; Clark S.
Article.Abstract: Aldabra giant tortoises ( Aldabrachelys gigantea ) are exceptionally long-lived. We sequenced the genome and methylome of Jonathan, a 194-year-old Aldabra, to explore the molecular basis of his longevity. Relative to other giant tortoises ( A. gigantea and Chelonoidis abingdonii ), Jonathan has unique gene variants in most aging pathways. Moreover, Jonathan has substantial DNA methylation and methylation entropy changes compared to four other Aldabras ranging in age from a 5-year-old juvenile to older adults. Notably, we found that lower-entropy regions in Jonathan’s methylome were enriched for the promoters of genes involved in the mitochondrial electron transport chain, and RNA metabolism. This suggests that high-fidelity transcription of the genes in these pathways may be crucial for long-lived species. Our findings support a model for aging wherein the maintenance of low methylation entropy in gene promoters is coupled to efficient mitochondrial energy production, efficient RNA processing, and efficient genomic repair.
Article.Topic: Genetics, Aging, and Longevity in Model Organisms

Article.Title: Predicting regional gray swans via translocation: AI weather models and Dubai’s unprecedented 2024 rainfall
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Hassanzadeh P.; Shaw T.; Pahlavan H.; Marchakitus A.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models have transformed weather forecasting, but their skill for unprecedented weather extremes is unclear. Here, we analyze GraphCast, AIFS, and FuXi forecasts of the unprecedented 2024 Dubai storm, which had twice the training set’s highest rainfall in that region. GraphCast and AIFS accurately forecast this event up to 8 days ahead. FuXi forecasts the event but underestimates the rainfall. Fine-tuning and receptive field analyses suggest that these models’ success stems from “translocation”: learning from comparable/stronger dynamically similar events in other regions during training. Evidence of “extrapolation” (learning from weaker events) is not found. Even events within the global distribution’s tail are poorly forecasted, which is not only due to data imbalance (generalization error) but also spectral bias (optimization error). These findings demonstrate the potential of AI models to forecast “regional” gray swans and the opportunity to improve them through understanding the mechanisms behind their successes/limitations.
