Article.Title: Context shapes action understanding in social interactions
Article.Authors: Keck J.; Sato K.; Cañal-Bruland R.
Article.Abstract: In social interactions, individuals anticipate what others are about to do next, enabling smooth social interactions and coexistence in daily life. Here, we examined how kinematic and contextual cues are weighted and integrated to predict an interactor's actions during dynamic, real-time competitive interactions. We analyzed 76 participants (38 dyads) freely playing 300 games of rock-paper-scissors each while tracking their kinematics using motion capture. Although movement kinematics consistently conveyed intention-related information, successful action selection depended primarily on how this information influenced predictions. Reinforcement-learning based contextual inference emerged as the strongest predictor of single-trial success and modulated the degree to which movement-derived predictions guided behavior. When contextual and movement-derived information afforded different actions, prioritizing contextual inference consistently outperformed movement-derived predictions. Thus, successful social action understanding depends not on maximizing sensitivity to movement cues, but on adaptively arbitrating between movement-derived and outcome-based contextual information during ongoing social interaction.

Article.Title: Large cranial windows distort auditory cortical maps and degrade feature integration in secondary auditory cortex
Article.Authors: Kline A.; Tsukano H.; Mehra M.; Schneider G.; Garcia M.; Kato H.
Article.Abstract: Understanding how sensory information is transformed along cortical hierarchies requires reliable measurement of sensory representations across areas. In vivo two-photon calcium imaging through chronic cranial windows has become an essential approach for characterizing cortical sensory representations with cellular resolution and spatial registration across experiments. However, cortical computations, particularly in higher-order cortices, depend on intricate intracortical circuitry and can be sensitive to subtle tissue perturbations introduced during surgical preparation. By comparing sensory maps in the mouse auditory cortex before and after window implantation, we show that commonly used large cranial windows mechanically compress the intrinsically curved cortical surface, producing systematic map distortion away from the window center. Macroscopic and cellular-level analyses further reveal deterioration of feature-selective responses in the secondary auditory cortex following such distortion. Together, these findings identify an overlooked but controllable surgical factor that can bias measurements of sensory representations and highlight an important consideration for reproducibility across studies.

Article.Title: Lipid metabolism remodeling in human cardiomyocyte differentiation and maturation
Article.Authors: Tang H.; Liu R.; Xiong Z.; He Q.; Lu G.; Chan W.; Wang W.
Article.Abstract: Cardiac development involves extensive metabolic remodeling, yet dynamic changes of endogenous lipid species during human cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation remain poorly characterized. MYL2 expression confirmed ventricular lineage specification in late-stage CMs. Ceramide levels peaked at the cardiac progenitor cell (CPC) stage, suggesting a stage-specific association with the mesendoderm (MES)-to-CPC transition. Meanwhile, lipid categories such as monosialodihexosylganglioside, phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophosphatidylcholine, and lysophosphatidic acid were markedly elevated in mature CMs. Integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility analyses further delineated the temporal regulatory landscape underlying stage-dependent lipid remodeling during cardiogenic differentiation. Functional assays revealed that PC promotes the expression of mature CM marker genes and improves CM viability. Collectively, these findings establish a comprehensive, high-resolution dynamic lipidomic atlas of in vitro hESC-derived CM differentiation, providing a valuable resource for understanding lipid-associated mechanisms in heart development.

Article.Title: Gamma irradiation shapes high value metabolite responses across microbes microalgae and plants
Article.Authors: Ebadi A.; Neissi A.; Ebadi M.; Nasiri J.; Kordrostami M.
Article.Abstract: Gamma irradiation can function either as an acute physical elicitor that alters redox and metabolic regulation or as a mutagen that generates selectable genetic variation. We compared evidence from bacteria, fungi, microalgae, plants, and plant cell systems using a common framework that links absorbed dose and exposure context to response mode, evidence strength, phenotype stability, and productivity. Across these systems, irradiation can increase metabolite accumulation or support recovery of improved strains and lines, but responses remain strongly dependent on biological material, dosimetry, selection, and cultivation conditions. Heterogeneous dose reporting, inconsistent productivity denominators, limited causal validation, and scarce scale-up data prevent definition of a universal effective dose or mechanism. We therefore distinguish concentration from total yield and volumetric productivity and propose a stage-gated workflow integrating dosimetry, molecular characterization, stability testing, bioprocess evaluation, and safety and economic assessment to support defensible translation.

Article.Authors: Antonosyan M.; Hovhannisyan A.; Roberts P.; Cassidy L.; Mkrtchyan S.; Simonyan H.; Bobokhyan A.; Aghikyan L.; Piliposyan A.; Badalyan R.; Yeranyan N.; Gnuni A.; Avetisyan H.; Badalyan M.; Gabrielyan A.; Sarkisian N.; Grigoryan A.; Simonyan H.; Safaryan M.; Vardanyan B.; Martirosyan-Olshansky K.; Jackson I.; Breslin E.; Gyonjyan A.; Khachatryan Z.

Article.Title: L-Histidine alleviates tacrolimus-induced islet dysfunction via the gut-pancreas axis
Article.Authors: Geng Z.; Li Q.; Wang D.; Yang H.; Wang H.; Bao J.; Wang Y.; Wei L.
Article.Abstract: Tacrolimus is widely used after organ transplantation but can impair pancreatic β-cell function and glucose homeostasis. Microbiota depletion attenuated several protective effects of L-histidine, supporting a contribution of the gut microbiota to this response. These findings connect a microbiota-associated amino acid with tacrolimus-related β-cell dysfunction and provide a framework for investigating microbiota-metabolite contributions to metabolic complications of immunosuppression.

Article.Title: Dissociable pupil-linked arousal during overt and inner speech
Article.Authors: Kuwamizu R.; Watanabe R.; Yamamoto N.; Otani K.; Moriguchi Y.
Article.Abstract: Inner (covert) speech, the silent production of language in one's mind, plays a central role in human cognition and engages speech-related cortical networks partly overlapping with those for overt speech. Because cortical language processing unfolds within arousal states set by the ascending systems, we asked whether inner and overt speech are accompanied by similar pupil-linked arousal patterns. Using pupillometry across three counting-task experiments, we found a dissociation between inner and overt speech. While overt speech consistently elicited pupil dilation across conditions, inner speech produced a variable dilation profile relative to baseline: pupil constriction (simple counting), no deviation (noun-phrase counting), and clear dilation (step counting; high cognitive load). Importantly, pupil size during inner speech remained smaller than that during overt speech despite task-dependent dynamics. These findings suggest that task-elicited inner speech is accompanied by lower pupil-linked arousal than overt speech, adding a state-level physiological dimension to cortical accounts of verbal processing.

Article.Authors: Xie X.; Yan B.; Wang T.; Han C.; Wei C.; Zhai Y.; Lv J.; Zhang M.
Article.Abstract: Groundwater-level prediction supports water-resource management in overexploited aquifers, yet conventional data-driven models often struggle to represent pumping disturbances and contrasting shallow- and deep-aquifer responses. Article.Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) distributions provide a foundation for understanding upper-ocean ecosystem dynamics and biogeochemical variability. The framework first learns large-scale spatiotemporal vertical representations from long-term CMIP6 simulations and then adapts them using reconstructed fields constrained by BioGeoChemical-Argo (BGC-Argo) observations, reducing simulation biases while preserving regional variability. This framework demonstrates how transferable knowledge from climate simulations can be combined with autonomous observations to generate continuous 3D Chl-a fields, enabling large-scale investigations of subsurface marine ecosystems and biogeochemical change.

Article.Title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies
Article.Authors: Farhadzadeh F.; Borji A.; Aram C.; Alishvandi A.; Kamali M.; Rahimi M.
Article.Abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities—absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift—that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

Here, we applied state-of-the-art computational modeling to >50 million single cells from diagnostic bone marrow aspirates of 502 AML patients. Jointly modeling leukemic and non-malignant cells, we identified seven patient clusters with distinct immunophenotypic signatures. These clusters showed strong concordance with recurrent mutations, including NPM1 , IDH1/IDH2 , CEBPA , and t(8;21)(q22;q22); RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusions, and enabled accurate prediction of genomic subgroups. In addition, we identified an immunophenotypic patient cluster comprising ∼11% of patients characterized by significant bone marrow lymphocyte enrichment where outcomes diverged depending on genetic risk. Article.Title: Mechano-electric response of tribopositive, fluoropolymer-free polyvinyl acetate nanogenerators in multiple contact electrification
Article.Authors: Slobodian P.; Riha P.; Hausnerova B.
Article.Abstract: Polyvinyl acetate (PVAc) is a highly polar, fluorine-free polymeric adhesive that combines strong interfacial adhesion with good processability. Despite this, PVAc has rarely been investigated as an active layer in mechano-electric nanogenerators, even though its strong adhesion facilitates effective interfacial contact, thereby eliminating the need for auxiliary conductive layers. Electrical measurements revealed that the electrical output of PVAc arises from the interplay of triboelectric charge transfer, electrostatic induction driven by residual polarization, and deformation-induced interfacial polarization. Article.Title: Climate change and sexual and reproductive health: A mixed methods scoping review of possible mechanisms
Article.Authors: Vahedi L.; Pradhan S.; Zaidi S.; Brizuela V.; Rashid S.; El Adawy M.; Hajjeh R.; Gaffey M.; Bhutta Z.
Article.Abstract: Summary: This scoping review synthesized empirical evidence on the relationships and possible pathways through which climate change could impact sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Five mediator domains were identified: (1) systems and infrastructure, (2) demographic shifts, (3) socioeconomic resources, and (4) behavioral and (5) biological. Article.Abstract: Bone organoids offer three-dimensional systems for studying skeletal development, disease, and regeneration. Article.Authors: Castaldi E.; Anobile G.; Marazzi M.; Federici S.; Angelelli P.; Turi M.

Article.Authors: Tang X.; Xu H.; Liu X.; Yang Y.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic disease affecting the entire joint, influenced by a combination of inflammatory, metabolic, immune, and environmental factors. Article.Abstract: Biomolecular condensates can age into gel-like or solid-like states, and their interfaces can promote amyloid fibril formation. Article.Title: Short-term indoor fine particulate matter exposure impedes cognitive performance and autonomic nervous system in adults
Article.Authors: Zhou J.; Huebner G.; Liu K.; Ucci M.
Article.Abstract: Evidence suggests short-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) air pollution can impact health, yet its wider cognitive effects and underlying mechanisms are unknown. In this randomized single-blind crossover lab-based study, 90 working-age adults were exposed to two stable indoor PM2.5 conditions generated by candle-burning: low concentration (1.70 μg/m 3 , representing clean air) achieved via an air purifier, and high concentration (31.22 μg/m 3 , representing global average exposure) using a sham filter in the purifier. Participants' cognitive performance across various domains was assessed, alongside heart rate variability (HRV) and electrodermal activity (EDA) to appraise potential mediating mechanisms of autonomic nervous activity on cognition. Higher PM2.5 exposure resulted in lower HRV and poorer cognitive performance in attention and memory, but not in coordination or reasoning. Decreased HRV partly mediated declines in some cognitive functions. The findings could have broader implications for workforce productivity beyond direct effects on ill health.

Article.Title: Core needle biopsy-derived breast cancer microtumors enable functional drug-response testing for precision oncology
Article.Authors: Plikomol M.; Laohawiriyakamol S.; Wangkulangkul P.; Thongsuksai P.; Khirilak P.; Nontikarn R.; Phanthuvet O.; Ulhaka K.; Khongkow P.
Article.Abstract: To predict neoadjuvant chemotherapeutic outcomes, breast cancer organoids have been developed. However, low yields from small tissue specimens and the high cost of niche factor-enriched medium remain barriers to clinical translation. Here, breast cancer patient-derived microtumors (PDMs) from core needle biopsies and small tissue specimens were established using a modified culture protocol and an optimized fetal bovine serum (FBS)-based culture medium, achieving a 75% success rate (6 of 8 cases). PDM characteristics mostly agreed with the tissue origins, according to growth evaluation, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and genetic profiling. As a proof of concept, PDMs were tested with neoadjuvant chemotherapy alongside the patients' treatment. Notably, the PDM results were positively correlated with the patient outcomes and were obtained within a clinically relevant time frame (∼2–3 weeks). Collectively, our protocol and FBS-based medium efficiently generate breast cancer PDMs from core needle biopsies and small tissue specimens, with promising potential to guide neoadjuvant chemotherapy decisions.

Article.Title: Automated evaluation of basketball skills using multimodal data fusion for improving shooting training efficiency
Article.Authors: Sun P.
Article.Abstract: Reliable basketball shooting assessment requires integration of complementary movement signals and actionable feedback. This study developed the multimodal shooting evaluation and efficiency model (MSEEM) and evaluated it in 156 players assigned to MSEEM feedback or standard coaching. RGB video, pose, inertial measurement unit signals, ball trajectories, and shot outcomes were fused to estimate rubric-based total and component scores. MSEEM achieved lower mean absolute error (4.82 ± 0.31) and stronger rank agreement ( ρ = 0.824) than SlowFast (6.24 ± 0.41; ρ = 0.702). MSEEM feedback also produced steeper training improvement and higher 14-day retention ( d = 0.68), supporting standardized component-targeted feedback.

Article.Title: Design and validation of a GMP-compliant manufacturing platform of extracellular vesicles from mesenchymal stromal cells
Article.Authors: Courageux Y.; Monguió-Tortajada M.; López-Fernández A.; Schoch L.; Poblador F.; Morini S.; Prat-Vidal C.; Rodriguez L.; Torrents S.; Aran G.; Codinach M.; Gálvez-Montón C.; Bayes-Genis A.; Vives J.; Querol S.; Roura S.
Article.Abstract: There is growing interest in mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) as key components in the development of next-generation regenerative cell-free therapies; however, their clinical translation remains limited by a lack of validated clinical-grade manufacturing platforms. Thus, we have established a good manufacturing practice (GMP)-compliant, semi-automated, mid-scale manufacturing workflow that couples the single-use stirred-tank bioreactor expansion of Wharton's jelly-derived MSCs with tangential flow filtration and automated size-exclusion chromatography, featuring in-line monitoring of critical process parameters. The MSC-EV-based product meets pre-specified critical quality attributes (CQAs), co-expresses parental-cell- and EV-specific markers, and complies with standardized quality and safety regulations. Moreover, the final product CQAs—including CD73-associated immunomodulatory activity—remained within acceptable limits for 12 months of storage in PlasmaLyte 148 at −80°C. Overall, our integrated platform yields MSC-EVs with high batch-to-batch reproducibility, in alignment with current GMP and regulatory standards, thereby providing a robust foundation supporting their potential clinical applicability.

Article.Title: An experimental study on HRM combined with multiplex PCR for the identification of single and mixed diatom species
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Liu Y.; Cong B.; Chen J.; Deng J.
Article.Abstract: Diatoms are research subjects in both ecological environments and forensic science. The identification of mixed diatom samples has always been a challenging issue. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction-high-resolution melting (PCR-HRM) provides a potential solution, but the effectiveness of this method in analyzing single and mixed diatom samples remains unclear. This study focuses on eight species of marine diatoms, identifying and designing corresponding primers to preliminarily explore the HRM technique combined with multiplex PCR for species identification of marine diatoms. By using two primer combinations, we achieved rapid identification of single diatoms. The experiments revealed that the HRM technique showed reduced identification capability for mixed diatom samples, whereas the multiplex PCR-HRM technique could enhance the identification accuracy for mixed diatom samples. By using a mixture of three primers, we identified four species of diatoms in mixed samples. This method can improve the identification capability of mixed diatom samples and provides a new approach for diatom species identification.

Article.Title: Migraine burden inequities and 2050 projections in Africa based on global burden of disease 2023
Article.Authors: Lu G.; Wang Y.; Xiao S.; Yu M.; Guan X.; Zhang X.; He J.; Wang Y.; Wang X.; Liu R.; Yang W.
Article.Abstract: This study analyzes migraine burden and health inequalities across 53 African Union countries from 1990 to 2023 using Global Burden of Disease data, with projections to 2050. Inequality was quantified via the slope index of inequality, health system efficiency via stochastic frontier analysis, and future trends via Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average modeling. In 2023, prevalent cases reached 180.4 million (95% uncertainty interval [UI]: 152.2–211.3), disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) 6.1 million (95% UI: 4.1–8.5), with an age-standardized prevalence rate of 13,385.8 per 100,000. From 1990 to 2023, rates increased steadily (estimated annual percentage change: 0.16 for prevalence; 0.18 for DALYs). The burden peaks in young adults and women, with widening regional disparities. Cases are projected to nearly to 375.7 million by 2050. These findings establish migraine as an escalating public health priority in Africa, underscoring the urgent need for targeted policy interventions and health system strengthening across the continent.

Article.Title: Intestinal microbiota-associated LysoPC(16:0) promotes endometriosis via PPARγ-mediated M2 macrophage polarization and IL-10 secretion
Article.Authors: Li N.; Yuan M.; Jin X.; Jiao X.; Wang S.; Zhong Z.; Guan H.; Le X.; Ren Q.; Liu Y.; Dong X.; Li Q.; Wang M.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: Both gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered pelvic immune microenvironment have been linked to endometriosis (EM), but the metabolites connecting the two remain undefined. Combining 16S rDNA sequencing with non-targeted metabolomics in a murine EM model, we found altered gut microbiota composition alongside a marked rise in peritoneal lysophosphatidylcholine (LysoPC(16:0)), linked to the microbiota shift by correlation analysis and fecal transplantation. LysoPC(16:0) promoted M2 macrophage polarization through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ), an effect observed in two mouse strains. Clodronate-mediated macrophage depletion blocked LysoPC(16:0)-driven lesion growth. LysoPC(16:0) further induced PPARγ-dependent IL-10 transcription, and IL-10 neutralization in vivo reduced lesion weight. Conditioned medium from LysoPC(16:0)-stimulated THP-1 macrophages promoted migration of primary endometrial stromal cells from patients with EM, an effect reversed by GW9662 or IL-10 neutralization. Together, these results outline a gut microbiota-LysoPC(16:0)-PPARγ-M2–IL-10 axis in EM pathogenesis, a mechanistic and therapeutic target for future clinical study.

Article.Title: NOSE-OE: A molecular signaling map of the olfactory epithelium
Article.Authors: Gupta S.; Genovese F.; Singh K.; Nicoli A.; Ferri F.; Kogut-Günthel M.; Fastus D.; Gupta S.; Van Welzen M.; Wolkenhauer O.; Di Pizio A.
Article.Abstract: The olfactory epithelium (OE) is a dynamic and complex sensory tissue in which continuous regeneration, neuronal differentiation, and tissue maintenance depend on coordinated molecular and cellular signaling. We developed NOSE-OE (Network of Signaling Events in the Olfactory Epithelium), an open-access knowledge resource that integrates mechanistic evidence from more than 300 publications into a standardized, computer-readable signaling network. NOSE-OE comprises over 500 molecular elements and 1,000 curated interactions and is implemented within the MINERVA platform for interactive exploration and network analysis. By connecting fragmented experimental evidence within a unified molecular framework, NOSE-OE enables the systematic investigation of signaling processes governing OE homeostasis and responses to perturbation. The resource provides a foundation for hypothesis generation and systems-level investigation of olfactory epithelial biology across physiological and disease contexts.

Article.Title: Proteomic and extracellular particle changes in preterm neonates with suspected late-onset sepsis
Article.Authors: O’Reilly D.; Murphy L.; Fouhy E.; Ryan L.; Murphy C.; O’Loughlin J.; Áinle F.; Gormley I.; Wynne K.; Inzitari R.; Doran P.; Drew R.; Morrell C.; Moore C.; Curley A.; McCallion N.; Maguire P.
Article.Abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality in neonates. In this prospective, multisite observational study, proteomics and extracellular particle analysis were performed on platelet-poor plasma from neonates at the point of clinical suspicion for sepsis ( n = 110). Neonates were then classified by their clinical teams into three groups: culture-proven sepsis, culture-negative sepsis, or non-sepsis. Neonates with culture-proven sepsis demonstrated statistically significant differences in their analyzed proteome compared to neonates deemed to have non-sepsis, while those with culture-negative sepsis did not. Extracellular particle concentration and type, as determined by flow cytometry, did not differ between the three groups. This study provides further evidence that culture-proven sepsis and culture-negative sepsis are not equivalent diagnoses in the neonatal population without a consensus definition for sepsis. The proteins identified in the culture-positive group may be of utility in determining neonatal sepsis endotypes, but this would require further validation.

Article.Title: Effect of the end-of-life care education program on improving oncology nurses’ knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors: A quasi-experimental study
Article.Authors: Yu W.; Hou X.; Guo R.; Wang Y.; Ma X.; Pang D.; Lu Y.
Article.Abstract: Education can strengthen nurses' capabilities in end-of-life care. Existing training programs have shortcomings such as monotonous content, unsatisfactory intervention effects, and limitations in research design. This single-center, quasi-experimental study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of an educational program based on the supportive care strategy list for end-of-life cancer patients in improving oncology nurses' knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors. Participants from a tertiary cancer hospital in Beijing were allocated into a training group and a non-training group (N1 = N2=27) using matched-pair sampling. The non-training group received no intervention, while the training group underwent an 18-class (45–60 min per class), 7-week education. At the 8-month follow-up, post-intervention assessments showed that the training group demonstrated significantly better knowledge and attitudes than the non-training group ( p < 0.05). Intra-group comparisons showed the training group exhibited superior knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors than at baseline ( p < 0.05). The end-of-life care education program effectively enhanced oncology nurses' knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors.

Article.Title: Epidemiological modeling of African swine fever in wild boars—A systematic review
Article.Authors: Hirwa F.; Tanveer M.; Ntakiyisumba E.; Won G.
Article.Abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a viral disease that poses a major threat to swine production, with wild boars contributing to virus persistence and transmission. We systematically reviewed global epidemiological modeling studies published from 2014 to 2024 to assess modeling approaches, transmission pathways, methodological patterns, and factors associated with ASF occurrence and spread in wild boar populations. Fifty-four studies from twenty-nine countries were grouped into five categories based on research objectives. Risk-factor and spatiotemporal analyses were the most common approaches, supporting targeted surveillance and risk mapping. Carcass-mediated transmission, wild boar density, movement, habitat conditions, and seasonal variation were important factors influencing ASF occurrence and spread. As modeling approaches differ in their assumptions, data requirements, and applicability, we developed a framework linking model choice to surveillance capacity, outbreak stage, data availability, and management objectives. This framework provides a structured basis for selecting appropriate approaches to strengthen ASF surveillance and control strategies.

Article.Title: Senescence and tumor immunology: A multifaceted interplay of influence
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Zhang J.; Wang S.; Rao D.; Zhang J.; Ao Y.
Article.Abstract: Medical advances and global population aging have propelled aging and cancer research into a new period of discovery. Senescent cells, which exert context-dependent tumor-suppressive and tumor-promoting effects, are central to this progress and engage in complex crosstalk with tumor proliferation. This review critically examines the multidimensional interplay between aging and cancer by synthesizing genetic, cytokine signaling, and tissue microenvironment evidence. We discuss how senescent cells influence immune surveillance, therapy response, tumor progression, metastasis, and age-related cancer risk, while cellular diversity, molecular complexity, immune balance, tumor heterogeneity, treatment resistance, and individual aging variability further complicate this relationship. We conclude that aging and cancer are intertwined through dynamic, context-specific mechanisms. By integrating these insights, this review aims to inspire novel research directions and transformative advances in cancer therapy and healthy longevity.

Article.Title: Longitudinal associations of screen time with brain development and expressive language skills in early childhood
Article.Authors: Choi E.; Nichols E.; Tomfohr-Madsen L.; Giesbrecht G.; Manning K.; Lebel C.; Duerden E.
Article.Abstract: Screen-based media may reduce reciprocal social interactions that support expressive language development, but little is known about how early language abilities, later screen use, and brain structure are related during toddlerhood. We examined 70 toddlers with structural magnetic resonance imaging and standardized developmental assessments at age 2, along with parent-reported screen time at ages 2 and 3. Greater weekday and weekend screen time at age 2 were associated with poorer concurrent expressive language skills. Right pars triangularis volume did not explain additional variance in these cross-sectional associations. Longitudinally, right pars triangularis volume moderated the association between expressive language skills at age 2 and screen time at age 3. Among toddlers with relatively smaller right pars triangularis volumes, poorer expressive language skills were associated with greater subsequent weekday and weekend screen time. These findings support guidance to limit screen use during toddlerhood, a sensitive window for language and brain development.

Article.Title: Paleogenomics reveals leprosy at the late antique burial site of Fallward in northern Germany
Article.Authors: Myburgh D.; da Silva N.; Romeyer-Dherbey J.; Grefen-Peters S.; Jöns H.; Peek C.; Nebel A.; Krause-Kyora B.
Article.Abstract: The coastal settlement of Fallward in northwestern Germany (3 rd –5 th century CE) is renowned for exceptionally preserved wooden and textile grave goods, yet the genetic and pathogen landscape of its inhabitants has remained unstudied. We conducted metagenomic analyses on skeletal samples from 11 individuals to investigate their genetic affinities and infectious disease history. Three individuals yielded sufficient data for population genetic analysis: two clustered with northwestern European Iron Age and Anglo-Saxon groups, while one adult male might have originated from a Roman frontier population. This man was also infected with a strain of Mycobacterium leprae belonging to phylogenetic branch 4 and was buried in a boat accompanied by Roman-influenced grave goods, including carved furniture and a military belt. Together, these findings point to possible long-distance connections linking remote communities, such as Fallward, to the wider Roman world during Late Antiquity.

Article.Title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence
Article.Authors: Paraskevopoulos E.; Bamidis P.
Article.Abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Here, we propose a hierarchical framework that reconceptualizes multisensory processing as a continuum of representational emergence across three distinct levels: level I (multimodal binding), where features are integrated via probabilistic causal inference; level II (supramodal representation), where recurrent co-activation and value-guided selection establish consolidated, perceptual-semantic engrams that act as emergent modalities; and level III (amodal concepts), where meaning becomes increasingly detached from sensory form and is represented within transmodal semantic networks. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Finally, we delineate an empirical roadmap and outline implications for supramodal AI, toward architectures capable of more autonomous semantic representation and generation.

Article.Title: Evidence for climate-mediated range expansion of hybrid wood ants
Article.Authors: Krapf P.; Heidbreder P.; Bruijning M.; Meirmans P.; Stankowski S.; Kulmuni J.
Article.Abstract: Climate change challenges many species. To persist, species can shift ranges, respond plastically, and adapt, which all require variation. Hybridization can quickly increase genetic variation, potentially facilitating climate adaptation; however, it is unclear how hybrids respond to climatic changes. Here, we combine whole-genome, life-history, acute heat-shock, and climatic data of 69 wood ant populations across Finland to assess whether F. aquilonia × F. polyctena hybrids outperform their cold-adapted parent F. aquilonia in warming climates. Compared to F. aquilonia , hybrids are active and their offspring emerge earlier in spring, and they withstand acute temperatures relevant in nature better. Further, the hybrids' border has shifted 200 km northwards, coinciding with the expansion of climatic conditions suitable for hybrids. Our results provide evidence that hybrids have an adaptive advantage over F. aquilonia due to their admixed ancestry, and recent climatic changes can lead to range expansion of hybrids.

Article.Authors: Espino-Payá A.; Prantner S.; Chalas N.; Wollbrink A.; Gross J.; Pastor M.; Fuentes-Sánchez N.; Junghöfer M.
Article.Abstract: Music has a powerful capacity to evoke emotional responses. This study explored the neural and subjective correlates of pleasant and unpleasant emotions elicited by music. 30 volunteers (15 women) listened to 60 film musical excerpts (30 unpleasant and 30 pleasant) from the Film Music Stimulus Set (FMSS) while their neural activity was recorded using magnetoencephalography (MEG). Participants gave self-reports of hedonic valence, emotional arousal, happiness, fear, and musical preference on nine-point Likert scales. These findings enhance understanding of music-induced emotions and suggest potential clinical applications for treating mood disorders and emotional dysregulation.

Article.Abstract: Leishmaniasis lacks an effective vaccine. Dual single-cell RNA sequencing detected parasitized bone marrow cells 28 days after intradermal inoculation with either virulent LmWT or attenuated LmCen −/− . Flow cytometry showed increased myelopoiesis following LmCen −/− immunization compared with LmWT infection. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated enhanced granulin-Sort3 signaling as a potential driver of this response. Bone marrow monocytes from LmCen −/− -immunized mice efficiently cleared virulent LmWT parasites in co-culture, consistent with the induction of trained innate immunity. These findings identify the bone marrow as an active site of anti- Leishmania immune programming and suggest that LmCen −/− vaccination promotes durable protection through coordinated adaptive and innate mechanisms.

Article.Title: Single-cell-resolved dynamic immune remodeling following Omicron infection and recovery in vaccinated individuals
Article.Authors: Khare K.; Kumar S.; Chattopadhyay P.; Halder S.; Bano M.; Gupta A.; Patel A.; Soni J.; Tarai B.; Budhiraja S.; Pandey R.
Article.Abstract: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infections occur despite vaccination, yet post-infection immune recovery remains incompletely understood. Chemokine surges ( CXCL1 , CXCL5 , and CXCL8 ) resolved during convalescence, whereas selective cytokines ( CCL5 and CCL8 ) and interleukins ( IL-6 , IL-18 , and IL-24 ) persisted. Trajectory analysis revealed non-uniform remodeling of T cell states with persistent differentiation signatures across naive, effector, and memory compartments. Overall, vaccination tempered early immune collapse and accelerated innate rebound, highlighting interleukin-linked checkpoints and metabolic regulation underlying post-vaccination immune resilience.

Article.Title: Avoiding spiders: Affective context shapes tactile sensitivity during movement
Article.Authors: Arikan B.; McManus M.; Fiehler K.
Article.Abstract: Tactile sensitivity is typically reduced during voluntary movements, a phenomenon known as tactile suppression. While affective context is known to modulate tactile processing, it remains unclear how it influences tactile suppression. In a virtual reality (VR) environment, we investigated tactile sensitivity during movements to avoid threatening (spider) or approach non-threatening (rabbit) stimulus, involving arm flexion or extension and during the limb at rest (baseline). Tactile sensitivity was measured using brief vibrations delivered through the VR controller. Detection thresholds were higher during movement than at baseline, confirming tactile suppression. Both affective context and movement type modulated suppression: avoiding threatening stimulus and extending the arm, each increased suppression. A control experiment using neutral, geometric objects showed similar tactile sensitivity for arm extension and flexion. These findings demonstrate that affective context shapes tactile suppression during movement.

Article.Abstract: Dual-task performance requires coordination between cognitive control and motor systems. Article.Abstract: Gastric cancer-related long non-coding RNA1 ( GClnc1 ) is an emerging oncogenic regulator in multiple malignancies, including gastric, colorectal, ovarian, and bladder cancers, as well as osteosarcoma. Article.Authors: Tomita K.; Nakano T.; Morozumi S.; Okahashi N.; Arita M.

Article.Title: Linking nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal microbiota to immune responses during influenza-like illness in an aging population
Article.Authors: Kool J.; Konstanti P.; van Dijken H.; Chu M.; Nanlohy N.; Bijvank E.; van Woudenbergh E.; van Beek J.; van Baarle D.; Fuentes S.
Article.Abstract: Older adults are vulnerable to influenza-like illness (ILI). Immune activation was strong in the NP but limited in the OP, and stayed above healthy levels at follow-up, suggesting incomplete recovery. NP composition was also associated with symptom burden, viral and bacterial co-detection and smoking status. These site-specific microbiota-immune relationships identify the nasopharynx as the primary site of immune modulation during ILI in older adults.

Article.Title: Similar degenerative patterns of olfactory receptor genes in the giant panda and marine carnivores
Article.Authors: Kang L.; Chen J.; Hong M.; Wei W.; Xiang Z.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Olfactory receptor (OR) genes constitute the largest mammalian gene family and are critical for olfactory perception and ecological adaptation. These findings reveal convergent OR functional decay under aquatic adaptation and extreme dietary specialization, illustrating complex links between lifestyle and chemosensory genome evolution in mammals.

Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Luo L.; Zhang F.; Jiang B.; Jaroniec M.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Absorption spectroscopy of solids is hindered by strong scattering, which violates assumptions underlying the Beer-Lambert (BL) law. In contrast, KMF increases linearly with mass fraction within a low-loading regime, and the relation persists across distinct morphologies. This work underscores a simple, rapid, and non-destructive calibration strategy for scattering semiconductors that uses KMF as a linear axis for composition.

Article.Authors: Zheng W.; Geng D.

Article.Authors: Hilt P.; Gueugneau N.; Demougeot L.; Fadiga L.; Pozzo T.; Papaxanthis C.
Article.Abstract: The mirror neuron network is activated during both execution and observation of the same action, enabling visual-to-motor transformation. Two main hypotheses account for this process: the direct matching hypothesis proposes a direct link between visual cues and the observer's motor representations, whereas the predictive hypothesis suggests that motor predictions are generated and compared with visual information. Article.Title: Heavy metal contamination, source apportionment and health risk in soil-crop systems of high-geochemical-background Pb-Zn mining area
Article.Authors: Duan Z.; Chen J.; Xu Y.; Wang S.; Li T.
Article.Abstract: Mining and smelting, combined with high-geochemical-backgrounds, cause heavy metal accumulation in soil-crop systems, endangering food-chain health. Topsoil (0-20 cm) and three local crops were sampled from Yunnan's Huize lead-zinc mining area. Pb, Zn, Cu, Cd contamination, spatial patterns, source contributions and risks were assessed via ArcGIS interpolation, PN, RI, APCS-MLR, PMF, and USEPA health risk models. All soils exceeded Yunnan background values (100% exceedance), presenting extreme ecological risks mainly driven by Cd (92.94%). Cd has the highest bioavailability, while Pb existed mostly potentially bioavailable. Leafy crops show 100% over-standard rates for Pb and Cd, maize exceeds Pb limits. Four pollution sources were identified. Ingestion was the primary exposure pathway. Children suffered prominent non-carcinogenic Pb risks, while all populations encountered unacceptable Cd carcinogenic risks. Mismatches between soil metal contents and crop safety reveals uniform soil-standard limitations, offering references for pollution control, crop-layout optimization and differentiated risk management in analogous mining areas.

Article.Title: A synthesis of recorded fine-scale threats to imperiled species in the United States
Article.Authors: Niederman T.; Nunes L.; Dreiss L.; Gainsbury A.
Article.Abstract: Biodiversity in the United States faces mounting anthropogenic pressures, with an increasing number of species at risk of extinction. We present the most extensive synthesis of recorded threats confronting U.S. imperiled species to date, considering species assessments from NatureServe and the IUCN Red List for over 16,000 species. Our results demonstrate the value of identifying fine-scale threats species face. Species occupying multiple ecosystems tend to see more recorded threats on average, and threat prevalence differs by ecosystem. Certain taxa (particularly corals, reptiles, amphibians, bivalves, and mammals) face disproportionately high recorded threat numbers. Climate change is both the fastest-growing recorded threat and the most ubiquitous IUCN threat category among species with up-to-date assessments. This analysis also highlights significant data gaps, revealing that most imperiled species have outdated or incomplete threat assessments, and over half lack even an initial evaluation. Gaps are disproportionately found among invertebrates, plants, and fungi.

Article.Title: Retrospective attention reveals a decaying theta rhythm in conscious access to a preceding stimulus
Article.Authors: Yun S.; Kim Y.; Jeong J.; Kim Y.
Article.Abstract: Conscious perception is often presumed to arise immediately upon external stimulation. However, retroperception-conscious access to a stimulus after it has disappeared-challenges this perspective by demonstrating temporally flexible awareness. The fine-grained temporal dynamics governing retroperception, however, remain unknown. Here, we tested three competing models for the temporal architecture of retroperception: a monotonic decay, a sustained oscillation, and a damped oscillation. We implemented a retro-cue paradigm and densely sampled behavioral reports. Through spectral analysis and computational modeling, we found that both behavioral accuracy and subjective visibility exhibited theta-band fluctuations, with model comparison modestly favoring a damped oscillatory profile over sustained oscillatory or non-oscillatory alternatives. Furthermore, we found that oscillations in accuracy and visibility were temporally aligned, suggesting temporal coordination between attention and perception during post-stimulus access. These findings suggest that conscious access to recent sensory information may be rhythmically structured and temporally limited, placing computational constraints on models of retroperception.

Article.Title: AI-assisted metabolomic profiling identifies candidate metabolites associated with diabetic kidney disease staging in a Korean cohort
Article.Authors: Jung I.; Park S.; Ji M.; Park S.; Lee D.; Yu J.; Seo J.; Paik M.; Park H.; Kwon S.; Lee D.; Kim N.
Article.Abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is commonly staged using albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), yet complementary molecular markers are needed. We profiled urine and serum metabolites from 92 Korean participants (72 with type 2 diabetes and 20 healthy controls) using gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (GC-MS/MS) and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). An exploratory restricted Boltzmann machine framework compared five DKD staging criteria and prioritized candidate metabolites; robustness was assessed against LASSO, linear support vector machine (SVM), and random forest using nested cross-validation. ACR-based staging showed the highest metabolomic discrimination. Urinary adenosine and 5'-methylthioadenosine decreased, whereas serum N2,N2-dimethylguanosine and cis-aconitic acid increased across ACR stages. Integration with a public renal tubular microarray dataset suggested NT5E as a cross-study network hub. These cross-sectional findings define candidate metabolite signatures associated with DKD severity and require external longitudinal validation before clinical translation.

Article.Title: Tailoring electric arc furnace steelmaking expansion pathways based on regional scrap and energy availability in China
Article.Authors: Shen J.; Tian S.; Zhang Z.; Li Z.; Lu H.; Wang P.; Sun L.; Wei L.; Xie S.; Zhang Q.
Article.Abstract: Electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking underpins China's low-carbon steel transition, while uneven regional resources and energy conditions greatly constrain its low-carbon development. This study adopts a province-level material flow analysis-capacity integration framework with multi-scenario modeling to explore targeted regional decarbonization pathways. Although national scrap supply generally meets domestic EAF demand, severe provincial mismatches occur: major producers, including Hebei (36.3 Mt) and Guangdong (32.0 Mt), heavily rely on interprovincial scrap transfers. Low-carbon electricity-rich regions are spatially separated from core EAF hubs, driving large disparities in provincial electricity carbon intensity (0.101-0.171 kg CO2 kWh-1 by 2060) and heterogeneous EAF emissions ranging from 69.6 to 92.7 Mt across scenarios. This study highlights dynamic scrap circulation, renewable energy matching, and differentiated provincial policies to coordinate national steel decarbonization.

Article.Title: Multiscale damage evolution and chemo-mechanical constitutive modeling of acid-corroded sandstone
Article.Authors: Hao L.; Yifan Z.; Qiang W.; Yifan C.; Donghui Y.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated time-dependent chemo-mechanical deterioration of fine-grained sandstone exposed to dilute sulfuric acid representing the proton-sulfate component of acid mine drainage. Specimens were corroded for 0-20 days and examined by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, endpoint solution chemistry, and triaxial compression at 20, 30, and 40 MPa. Results showed cumulative carbonate dissolution, cement degradation, microstructural deterioration, and mechanical weakening. After 20 days, Ca2+ and Mg2+ concentrations reached 156 and 25.3 mg/L, while peak strength decreased by 33.3%, 26.6%, and 29.9%, respectively. A nested Mohr-Coulomb comparison yielded F(4,5) = 1.284 and p = 0.388, supporting downward envelope translation but not statistically detectable slope variation. A time-dependent damage model reproduced pre-peak responses across all 15 conditions, with R 2 = 0.767-0.961. The framework links mineral alteration and microstructural damage to mechanical degradation but requires further validation for multicomponent field acid mine drainage and long-term engineering service.

Article.Title: The mechanism of vascular injury caused by polystyrene microplastics: Involving ferroptosis and metabolomics
Article.Authors: Zhu D.; Liang X.; Huang Q.; Wu Y.; Wei Z.; Cai S.; Feng Q.; Ma P.; Yang X.; Bao C.; Bao X.
Article.Abstract: Polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) are environmental pollutants linked to cardiovascular diseases. This study investigated PS-MP-induced vascular toxicity mechanisms in mice. Article.Authors: Hyun J.; Jung S.; Noh Y.; Cho Y.; Saido T.; Nah J.; Kim K.; Jung Y.
Article.Abstract: Amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation and neuroinflammation are central features of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the molecular link connecting inflammatory signaling to γ-secretase activation remains poorly understood. Article.Title: Dopamine modulation of motor and implicit learning contributions to auditory temporal attention
Article.Authors: Zalta A.; Spitz L.; Schnitzler A.; Morillon B.; Florin E.
Article.Abstract: Auditory periodic temporal attention operates optimally around 1.5 Hz when temporal structure is judged explicitly. Synchronized rhythmic movements further enhance its efficacy, an effect thought to depend on basal ganglia dopamine, crucial for both motor and temporal processing. However, whether dopamine underpins the relationship between auditory temporal attention and motor activity remains unclear. Using an auditory temporal attention task in Parkinson's disease (PD) patients ON versus OFF the dopaminergic medication L-DOPA, alongside healthy controls, we found no evidence that dopamine modulates the ∼1.5 Hz optimal sampling rate of auditory temporal attention. However, dopamine enables motor synchronization to the auditory stream and is hence crucial for the motor benefits of auditory temporal attention. Performing the first session ON L-DOPA also improved performance in the following session. These findings underscore a selective role for dopamine in audio-motor interaction, with no evidence that the intrinsic rhythm of auditory attention depends on dopamine.

Article.Title: Carbon- and boron-based nano-inclusions for thermoelectric nanocomposites: Matrix matching and interface design
Article.Authors: Ahmed A.; Lu Y.; Yang G.; Wang X.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Nanocomposite engineering offers a route to improve thermoelectric (TE) performance by modifying the coupled transport of charge carriers and phonons. This review examines carbon- and boron-based nanoinclusions across bismuth chalcogenides, Cu2Se, oxide matrices, and flexible polymer- and film-based thermoelectrics, with emphasis on inclusion chemistry, dimensionality, loading, processing route, and interface engineering. Bismuth chalcogenides generally require a narrow loading window because additional interfaces can degrade carrier mobility, whereas Cu2Se more readily accommodates such interfaces and has high zT values > 2. In oxides, improved electrical transport is often insufficient to offset high lattice thermal conductivity, while flexible systems require consideration of power factor, mechanical durability, and device output. Cross-system comparison shows that effective nanoinclusion design depends on balancing phonon suppression with carrier transport and interfacial stability, providing practical guidance for thermoelectric materials and device development.

Article.Authors: Uthicke S.; Cabrera M.; Byrne M.; Purcell S.
Article.Abstract: Coral reef sea cucumbers are heavily exploited despite the precarious conservation status of many species, yet limited life-history knowledge constrains effective management. The O2 environment strongly induces activation of the CHCl˙- anion, while COS exhibits minimal reactivity. Bond activation occurs across O-O, C-O, C-S, N-O, N-N, and S-O linkages, with binding strengths following O2 > NO2 > SO2 > CO. Although CO2, NO, and N2O interactions are thermodynamically limited at room temperature, they become accessible upon heating. These results demonstrate that anion-molecule reactivity emerges from coupled mass transport, electrostatic compatibility, and bond lability, thereby advancing predictive frameworks for radical-mediated chemistry.

Article.Title: Quantitative measurement of anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies for routine laboratory implementation

Article.Title: Recurrent power outages and the mental health burden of grid reliability in Maryland

Article.Title: Substrate-dependent performance patterns in nanocoatings across interior materials
Article.Authors: Boostani H.; Altan H.
Article.Abstract: Nanostructured coatings are widely used to enhance surface durability while preserving visual appearance, yet it remains unclear whether performance is primarily governed by coating chemistry or by the underlying substrate. Here, we address this question through a structured scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) of 80 eligible empirical studies spanning seven material classes relevant to interior environments. Across 311 standardized observations, we find that substrate class emerged as the strongest observed association with simultaneous functional and optical performance. This pattern is consistent with interfacial film formation mechanisms, including capillary depletion, hygroscopic stress, and surface heterogeneity. Exploratory study-level logistic regression (N = 80) supports this trend, with highly porous substrates showing substantially reduced odds of dual-axis success (odds ratio (OR) = 0.24; adjusted confidence interval (CI): 0.11-0.52). Coating chemistry, deposition conditions, and interfacial interactions further influence performance within these substrate-dependent trends: TiO2-based systems enhance antimicrobial efficacy but incur greater optical degradation relative to SiO2-based formulations. These findings support the interpretation of nanocoating performance as strongly influenced by substrate-dependent interfacial phenomena rather than a formulation-driven outcome alone. More broadly, they suggest that thin-film performance in complex environments is constrained by substrate-controlled transport and stress regimes, with implications for material selection and surface engineering beyond coating systems. As a synthesis based on proxy classification, these results are hypothesis-generating and highlight the need for controlled experiments directly testing substrate-controlled thin-film performance.

Article.Title: Systematic image perturbations reveal persistent gaps between human and machine vision
Article.Authors: Kato M.; He B.
Article.Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are promising computational models for understanding visual object recognition. Article.Title: Metabolic reprogramming in diabetic panvascular disease: Molecular mechanism and therapeutic strategies
Article.Authors: Bai Y.; Bai Y.; Liu S.
Article.Abstract: Diabetes mellitus substantially increases the risk of cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, retinal and peripheral vascular complications. These are collectively referred to as diabetic panvascular disease. A traditional approach that treats each complication separately is no longer sufficient. An emerging framework places metabolic reprogramming at its center. This review examines how the diabetic environment, including hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia, rewires core metabolic pathways in vascular cells. Major changes include the diversion of glucose through the polyol, hexosamine and AGE-PKC axes, lipotoxicity resulting from excessive fatty acids, disruption of amino acid networks such as BCAA and one-carbon metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction with increased mtROS production, and epigenetic modifications that drive metabolic memory. These interconnected abnormalities promote oxidative stress and chronic inflammation, which in turn lead to endothelial dysfunction, atherosclerosis, microvascular rarefaction, and end-organ damage in the heart, brain, kidney, retina, and peripheral nerves. We also describe the current therapeutic landscape, ranging from established agents such as metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, RAAS blockers, and anti-VEGF therapies to emerging mechanism-based strategies including aldose reductase inhibitors, glucokinase activators, PKC, RAGE, NOX, and NLRP3 inhibitors, miRNA modulators, and exosome therapy. Finally, we highlight unmet needs and future directions. These may include multi-omics guided precision phenotyping, cross-organ causal inference, single-cell metabolic flux technologies, and adaptive clinical trial designs. By shifting from a glucose-centric to a metabolic reprogramming-centric paradigm, this review aims to provide a roadmap for developing more targeted therapies for diabetic panvascular disease.

Article.Title: Evidence for early and late prediction error-associated ERP responses during probabilistic cueing
Article.Authors: Schlossmacher I.; Schlotmann A.; Schindler S.; Moeck R.; Straube T.
Article.Abstract: Probabilistic relationships are omnipresent in our sensory environment. According to some predictive coding models, the processing of deviations from expectation should be accompanied by enhanced neuronal responses, reflecting a prediction error, while expected stimuli should lead to suppression of brain responses. However, probabilistic cueing designs show no clear picture regarding prediction error and expectation suppression. Here, we measured event-related potentials (ERPs) while participants were presented with a probabilistic cueing procedure with low, high, or equal-probable stimuli, while the task relevance of the probabilistic relations was varied. Our data show enhanced ERPs to infrequent stimuli in early (increased negative amplitudes over posterior electrodes) and late (increased positive amplitudes over central electrodes) time windows, driven by a prediction error and not by expectation suppression. Article.Title: Scalable piezoelectrochemical energy harvesting via Li-ion battery-based DEECs with laser-patterned electrodes
Article.Authors: Aziz M.; Khan A.; Karan N.; Kang S.
Article.Abstract: Piezoelectrochemical energy harvesting converts mechanical compression into electrical output through stress-coupled electrochemistry in lithium-ion systems. Here, we study lithium-ion battery-based distributed embedded energy converters (DEECs) as unit cells in DEEC-Tec metamaterials and examine how interconnection topology and electrode microarchitecture affect performance under 10 MPa loading. For commercial pouch cells, harvested energy increased from 153 to 395 μJ/cycle in series and from 101 to 204 μJ/cycle in parallel as the number of units increased from one to four, while a hybrid series-parallel network delivered the best performance (501 μJ/cycle; 16.73 nW/Ah). For laboratory-fabricated cells, laser-patterned electrodes improved harvested energy and capacity-normalized output by 84.5% despite an 18%-19% capacity loss. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy showed 89.8% lower solid-electrolyte interphase resistance, 18.1% lower charge-transfer resistance, and 77.7% lower total resistance. These results show that topology and electrode microstructure can jointly improve scalable low-frequency piezoelectrochemical energy harvesting.

Article.Title: Ga(III) ion release from gallium-based liquid metals: The trade-off between efficacy and safety
Article.Authors: Wang D.; He S.; Wei Z.; Tan H.; Wang Y.; Lan J.; Pan W.
Article.Abstract: Due to unique pharmacological activities and distinctive physicochemical properties, gallium-based liquid metals (LMs) have attracted tremendous attention in therapeutics. As biodegradable metallic materials, gallium-based LMs can predominantly release Ga(III) ions under physiological conditions, which represents a double-edged sword for clinical translation. On the one hand, the Ga(III) ions act as redox-inert Fe(III) competitive inhibitors and may provide therapeutic effects for broad-spectrum therapeutic applications. On the other hand, upon nonspecific biodistribution or uncontrolled Ga(III) release, substitution of Fe(III) by Ga(III) may disturb iron metabolism in normal cells and subsequently induce toxicological outcomes. Therefore, understanding and managing the trade-off between efficacy and safety is a key prerequisite for the clinical translation of gallium-based LMs. This review aims to systematically summarize the therapeutic activities and toxicological characteristics of gallium-based LMs. Meaningfully, the unresolved challenges and future perspectives regarding the balance between efficacy and safety are outlined to inspire future academic explorations and clinical translation.

Article.Title: Two-photon light-sheet microscopy with isotropic near-diffraction-limited resolution in three dimensions
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Yang L.; Wang W.; Zhang J.; Qu R.; Liang S.; Zhang H.; Zhang Y.; Xu W.; Li Z.; Wang R.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Achieving isotropic high-resolution three-dimensional imaging across a large field of view (FOV) remains a key challenge in two-photon light-sheet microscopy (TPLSM). To address this limitation, we developed a TPLSM system that stitches multiple short Bessel beams into a large, ultrathin illumination light sheet and employs a dedicated control protocol to suppress stray light. The system delivers isotropic near-diffraction-limited resolution across a 332.8 μm FOV, enabling uniform visualization of fine structural details in biological samples and avoiding morphological misinterpretation. In vivo imaging of zebrafish embryos validates the system's performance, confirming its utility for high-fidelity biological observation. Furthermore, the proposed approach is broadly applicable to other microscope modalities using Bessel-beam illumination, extending its utility well beyond TPLSM.

Article.Title: Chased and displaced: Impact of anthropogenic disturbance on habitat use and movement patterns of Asian elephants in South West Bengal, India
Article.Authors: Singh A.; Kumara H.
Article.Abstract: Managing large mammals sustaining on crops in human-dominated landscapes is challenging, and the most common mitigation strategy is "driving". In South Bengal, elephants are driven away by locals or organized "hula" teams. Over 223 monitored days in 2017-18 (56 no drive, 97 local, and 70 hula drives), we collected data on elephant movement, habitat use, costs, and community responses. Mean monthly movement type differed significantly, with local drive being highest (0.43 km ± 0.10 SD), followed by hula (0.31 km ± 0.11 SD) and no drive (0.26 km ± 0.12 SD). Mean daily path length differed too, hula drives being highest (9.43 km ± 4.24), while local drives were lowest (5.20 km ± 2.34). Expenditure on hula drives correlated positively with hula size (5.86 ± 2.00 SD). Drives were mainly triggered by grievances (54%) and crop damage (24%). Local communities interfered in 55.71% of drives. Hula drives are reactive, socially mediated, energy-intensive interventions offering only short-term relief, not a long-term mitigative measure.

Article.Title: Excessive activation of the RAS/MAPK pathway triggers adult-onset motor axonal degeneration
Article.Authors: Been M.; Lambert E.; Serna A.; Balvert A.; Heisinger S.; Kreshpani M.; te Dorsthorst-Maas C.; Paškevičiūtė P.; Rodríguez Arias H.; Beijer D.; Astuti G.; Kenna K.; van Reijmersdal B.; Gloudemans S.; van Lith P.; Sijlmans C.; Verstreken P.; Veldink J.; Züchner S.; Gilissen C.; Schenck A.; Storkebaum E.
Article.Abstract: Axonal and synaptic degeneration are key hallmarks of neurodegenerative diseases, but the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we performed an unbiased forward genetic mosaic screen in Drosophila to identify genes required for maintenance of adult motor axons and neuromuscular junctions (NMJs). We identified 49 mutations in 30 genes, including 8 causing adult-onset progressive degeneration. Loss of pebbled (peb), the Drosophila RAS- responsive element binding protein 1 (RREB1) ortholog, causes adult-onset motor axonal and NMJ degeneration and age-dependent motor deficits. peb encodes a C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor that negatively regulates transcription of RAS/MAPK pathway target genes, and its loss resulted in RAS/MAPK pathway overactivation. Loss of other RAS/MAPK pathway negative regulators also induced adult-onset progressive NMJ degeneration and motor deficits. Importantly, treatment of adult flies with the MEK1/2 inhibitor mirdametinib induced a dosage-dependent rescue of peb mutant motor neurodegenerative phenotypes. Thus, RAS/MAPK pathway overactivation triggers adult-onset progressive neurodegeneration, which can be prevented by RAS/MAPK pathway inhibition.

Article.Title: Macrophages promote collagen deposition through circadian regulation of fibroblasts
Article.Authors: Lowles K.; Zhang X.; Yao X.; Cutiongco M.; Hughes J.; Li S.; Knox J.; Coy M.; Lin W.; MacDonald A.; Kadler K.; Meng Q.; Hussell T.; Chang J.
Article.Abstract: Fibroblast collagen deposition is regulated by macrophages and the circadian rhythm; understanding how these processes interact provides insights to collagenous tissue homeostasis. Here, we reveal that macrophage-fibroblast interaction enhances collagen deposition and requires a functional circadian rhythm. Macrophage polarization status determines how fibroblast responses were elicited, where naive and pro-inflammatory macrophages require direct cell-cell contact, and anti-inflammatory macrophages secrete soluble factors. One key secreted factor identified by mass spectrometry proteomics analysis is PDGFA. Crucially, macrophages lacking PDGFA, or treatment with PDGFRa inhibitor, showed diminished ability to modulate fibroblast circadian rhythms and collagen production. Impaired circadian rhythms in either cell type also led to a reduced collagen fibrillogenesis response. These results confirmed that the collagen deposition pathway is under circadian clock control in lung fibroblasts, and demonstrated that macrophages can re-synchronize fibroblast circadian rhythms to promote collagen deposition and extracellular remodeling, which are implicated in processes such as wound healing responses.

Article.Title: Non-canonical cleavage of GPR125/ADGRA3 releases extracellular receptor fragments detectable in cerebrospinal fluid
Article.Authors: Walser A.; Larsen O.; Stüdle C.; Thorsen N.; Seufert F.; Drzazga A.; Mężyk-Kopeć R.; Raj I.; Qvist F.; Bagger S.; Hjortø G.; Toft-Bertelsen T.; Slowikowski E.; Bergt S.; Ganseman E.; Goth C.; Lokau J.; Garbers C.; Ishikawa H.; Schroten H.; Proost P.; Simonsen A.; Taylor N.; Bereta J.; MacAulay N.
Article.Abstract: Adhesion G protein-coupled receptors (aGPCRs) are crucial for barrier tissues and typically autoproteolytically cleaved into N- and C-terminal fragments (NTF and CTF) that remain non-covalently associated until separation is triggered. Here, we show that human GPR125 (ADGRA3), expressed in choroid plexus epithelium, is not cleaved at the GPCR autoproteolysis site (GPS), consistent with its divergent SLS motif. Instead, it undergoes non-canonical proteolytic processing that generates and releases atypical, non-canonical N-terminal fragments (ncNTFs), a process further enhanced by insulin. Using mutational analyses, metalloprotease inhibition, and ADAM10/17-deficient cells, we find that multiple proteases likely participate in cleavage. Mass spectrometry reveals one specific cleavage site, and real-time imaging uncovers GPR125's intracellular trafficking and shedding dynamics. Changing the GPS destabilizes the ncNTF-ncCTF association and increases ncNTF release, thereby promoting cell viability. Finally, detection of multiple GPR125-derived peptides in human cerebrospinal fluid suggests ncNTF shedding in vivo and possible biological relevance.

Article.Title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls
Article.Authors: De Smedt M.; Cuypers W.; Hudda N.; Delputte P.
Article.Abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens. Untargeted shotgun metagenomic sequencing offers a broader, unbiased view of the wastewater virome, although its performance is challenged by low human viral abundance, complex background signals, and genome assembly challenges. We also discuss key challenges complicating bioinformatic analysis, including limited human viral sequences, co-circulating viral lineages, viral dark matter, reference database limitations, large data volumes, and methodological biases, as well as emerging computational approaches aimed at improving wastewater sequencing analysis and interpretation.

Article.Title: Data-driven burst shape analysis for functional phenotyping of neuronal cultures
Article.Authors: Schäfer T.; Giannakakis E.; Schmidt-Barbo P.; Levina A.; Vinogradov O.
Article.Abstract: Cultures of neurons in vitro are instrumental for studying network dynamics under normal and pathological conditions. Mature networks typically exhibit network bursting activity, traditionally quantified by simplified features such as inter-burst intervals and burst durations. These features have advanced our understanding of development, disease phenotypes, and drug effects. However, they overlook the temporal structure within bursts, which is highly sensitive to network changes and can thus reveal additional physiological or pathological effects. Here, we developed a comprehensive framework to quantify burst shapes, the time-course of network firing during bursts. On four datasets, including rodent- and human pluripotent stem cell-derived cultures, we show that burst shapes contain rich information about the underlying network dynamics. We quantify this information by classifying conditions (genetic disorders, pharmacological agents) using traditional and burst-shape features, and find that including shape features significantly improves accuracy. We provide an open pipeline for burst shape characterization, introducing burst shape as a complementary functional phenotyping feature that expands the analytical toolkit for disease modeling and drug screening.

Article.Title: Assessing machine learning prediction of recycled aggregate concrete strength with a tabular foundation model
Article.Authors: Fan J.; Bharati R.; Zhang G.; Zhang H.; Zhang N.; Zhang Y.; Liang A.; Pokhrel M.
Article.Abstract: Recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) supports more sustainable construction, but recycled concrete aggregate (RCA)'s heterogeneity complicates compressive-strength prediction. This study evaluates the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) against nine conventional machine-learning models using a standardized literature-derived database of 833 RAC mixtures. Cube strengths were converted to equivalent cylinder strengths, with conversion sensitivity also assessed. Among conventional models, CatBoost achieved the highest accuracy (R2 = 0.843), whereas TabPFN achieved R2 = 0.870, mean absolute error (MAE) = 3.924 MPa, and root mean squared error (RMSE) = 5.551 MPa. TabPFN also produced a lower RMSE than CatBoost across all four RCA replacement intervals without extensive task-specific hyperparameter tuning. Feature importance and Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analyses identified effective water-to-cement ratio, aggregate-to-cement ratio, RCA density, and RCA absorption as key predictors, while RCA replacement level alone had limited influence. The moderate improvement over CatBoost indicates that further gains depend on improved RCA characterization.

Article.Title: IL-4 and arginine synergy accelerates early bone regeneration via enhanced efferocytosis and ameliorated microenvironment
Article.Authors: Meng L.; Liu R.; Wang S.; Wang J.; Vinnikov I.; Yang R.; Song X.; Zhang H.; Wang J.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: Host bone microenvironment is a critical factor for successful bone regeneration during implantation. In this work, we identified a spatiotemporal mismatch at drilling-induced injury sites where initial apoptosis outpaces macrophage recruitment, leading to apoptotic cell accumulation and oxidative stress that impairs osteogenic differentiation. To mitigate this phenomenon, we developed a synergistic strategy co-delivering interleukin 4 (IL-4) and arginine (Arg) to reprogram the microenvironment. Mechanistically, IL-4 recruits and polarizes macrophages toward a pro-reparative M2 phenotype, while Arg fuels the arginase-1 metabolic pathway to sustain continual efferocytosis and secretion of pro-regenerative cytokines. In a mouse bone injury model, transcriptomic and histological analyses confirmed that this strategy accelerates apoptotic clearance and establishes an M2-dominant environment, significantly enhancing early bone regeneration. Altogether, this work proposes a novel therapeutic paradigm targeting macrophage efferocytosis to resolve early microenvironmental imbalances, providing a promising therapeutic approach to promote bone defect healing and offering novel insights into optimizing host microenvironments for osseointegration following implantation.

Article.Title: PXT3003: Lessons for therapeutic development in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A and related neuropathies
Article.Authors: Burns J.
Article.Abstract: Most drug development stories end predictably: promising compounds either succeed or fail. Occasionally, however, a therapy repeatedly returns from apparent extinction. PXT3003 for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A (CMT1A) represents one such example. More than a decade after early promise, the program has survived formulation instability, interrupted clinical development, regulatory uncertainty, and controversy surrounding efficacy before re-emerging with renewed evidence of clinical benefit. Yet, as with many therapeutic development programs, interpretation of the available evidence is influenced by the extent to which findings are publicly accessible. In a recent issue of iScience, a phase 3 clinical trial evaluated PXT3003, a combination of baclofen, naltrexone, and D-sorbitol, versus placebo over 15 months in participants aged 16-65 years with mild-to-moderate CMT1A across 25 sites in China. PXT3003 is not simply the story of one drug; it highlights the scientific, methodological, operational, and reporting challenges of developing disease-modifying therapies for slowly progressive inherited neuropathies.

Article.Title: Monotropein mitigates atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability through circ_0140736/miR-495/SIRPα-mediated efferocytosis
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Wu Z.; Huang B.; Ye W.; Xu S.; He W.; Lan Y.; Xiao C.; Qin C.; Gao W.; Ye Z.
Article.Abstract: Efferocytosis is a biological process in which phagocytic cells engulf and degrade senescent, damaged, or dead cells to prevent secondary necrosis and inflammation. This process is implicated in various diseases, including atherosclerosis (AS). Enhancing efferocytosis efficiency may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for managing AS. Consequently, increasing attention is being paid to pharmacological agents that can promote efferocytosis. Monotropein (MON), the predominant iridoid glycoside in Morinda officinalis, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties in previous studies. However, its role in regulating atherosclerotic plaque stability remains unclear. In this study, we show that MON enhances plaque stability in AS. The expression of circ_0140736 was found to be elevated in unstable atherosclerotic plaques. MON suppressed circ_0140736 expression and alleviated miR-495 sequestration via a competing endogenous RNA mechanism, thereby increasing miR-495 levels and downregulating signal regulatory protein α (SIRPɑ) expression. In conclusion, MON exerts its anti-atherosclerotic effects by promoting efferocytosis through the circ_0140736/miR-495/SIRPɑ axis, suggesting its potential as a promising therapeutic candidate for AS.

Article.Title: Development of proteome-derived cyclic peptide libraries via ortho-phthalaldehyde-assisted cyclization
Article.Authors: Wei Y.; Feng K.; Hou W.; Tian X.; Xue Y.; Zhang W.; Deng H.
Article.Abstract: Cyclic peptides possess unique structural features and binding capabilities that make them attractive scaffolds for molecular recognition. However, strategies for generating functionally diverse libraries directly from natural proteomes remain comparatively underdeveloped. Here, we present a proteome-informed approach for constructing cyclic peptide libraries by integrating cysteine-enrichment protocols with ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA)-mediated macrocyclization. This method enables direct library generation from proteome digests and is compatible with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based annotation and downstream functional screening. We systematically identify key parameters governing OPA-mediated cyclization topology and develop a rule-based pipeline for automated library annotation of OPA-cyclized peptides. Applying this strategy, we generate a library of over 15,000 unique cyclic peptides and perform target-specific screening against human IgG. This yielded cyclic peptide binder candidates, including one lead peptide showing cyclization-dependent IgG-binding potential. Our study establishes an OPA-enabled, proteome-informed workflow for cyclic peptide library construction and annotation.
