Article.Title: Stress induced hyperphagia in C. elegans as a genetic model for binge eating disorders
Article.Authors: Pucci M.; Cifani C.; D’Addario C.; Swoboda P.
Article.Abstract: Binge eating (BE) is often triggered by stress, dieting, and adverse environmental factors, and represents a common precursor to eating disorders such as anorexia, bulimia, and BE disorder. Stress-induced hyperphagia captures core features of binge-like feeding and shares neurobiological substrates will BE disorder, making it a useful behavioral readout for dissecting underlying mechanisms. We used the genetically tractable worm Caenorhabditis elegans to examine how starvation and stress interact to drive feeding, quantifying pharyngeal pumping as a measure of food intake. Combined starvation and heat stress increased feeding beyond starvation alone, with effects shaped by stress timing, food quality, and sex. Feeding phenotypes were separable from locomotor and feeding-capacity defects. Mutations in evolutionarily conserved homeostatic and hedonic feeding-pathway genes showed distinct hyperphagic responses, implicating that conserved neuronal circuits govern stress-induced feeding across species. This model offers a platform for genetic screening and drug testing to accelerate discovery of therapeutics for binge-like feeding disorders.

Article.Title: Pharmacological protection from a sugar-rich diet through inhibition of Ras/MAPK signaling
Article.Authors: Laskovs M.; Cook J.; Pitt A.; Spickett C.; Slack C.
Article.Abstract: Consumption of sugar-rich diets adversely affects health and reduces life expectancy through the excessive production and storage of triacylglycerides (TAGs), leading to metabolic dysfunction. Here, we show that in Drosophila, pharmacological inhibition of Ras/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling using the highly specific MEK inhibitor, trametinib, mitigates several of the detrimental effects of a high-sugar diet by reducing TAG accumulation, restoring TAG composition, and increasing survival. Notably, Ras/MAPK activity is required for the transcriptional response to elevated sugar intake, including expression of the glucagon-like hormone, Akh. We further demonstrate that adipokinetic hormone (AKH) is essential for the protective effects of trametinib under high-sugar conditions. Together, our findings support Ras/MAPK signaling as an important link between dietary sugar and metabolic dysfunction and show that its pharmacological inhibition can uncouple excess sugar intake from adverse metabolic outcomes.

Article.Title: Contrasting fate and GHG emissions of algal vs. manure DOM under light and microbes in lakes
Article.Authors: Tao Y.; Wang Q.; Bao M.; Tian Y.; Lu L.
Article.Abstract: The escalating dissolved organic matter (DOM) inputs from algal (ADOM) and livestock manure (MDOM) sources are altering lake ecosystems, yet their fate under light and microbes in steppe lakes is unclear. Using microcosms, we found that photodegradation suppressed ADOM bioavailability by 4.8% via substrate competition and reactive oxygen species (ROS) inhibition (especially singlet oxygen), while light enhanced MDOM bioavailability by 5.4%. ADOM mineralization released 1.6× more CO2 than MDOM. Multi-group structural equation modeling (SEM) indicated that efficient ADOM microbial transformation drove higher CO2 emissions, whereas light-induced ROS shifted microbial communities and transformation pathways. ADOM and MDOM inputs predominantly enhanced CO2 emissions and water browning, respectively. These processes are interconnected-exogenous MDOM can promote algal blooms and subsequent greenhouse gas release. For eutrophic steppe lakes, integrated management combining exogenous load reduction and endogenous bloom suppression is critical to mitigate ecological risks and greenhouse effects.

Article.Title: Boid inclusion body disease in Boa constrictor: Unraveling the myth of immunosuppression
Article.Authors: Dervas E.; Czirják G.; Michalopoulou E.; Liesegang A.; Novacco M.; Schwarzenberger F.; Hetzel U.; Hepojoki J.; Baggio F.; Kipar A.
Article.Abstract: Boid inclusion body disease (BIBD) is an infectious disease of captive boid snakes of major relevance since the 1970s. It is caused by reptarenaviruses and characterized by intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies in most cell types. Affected snakes frequently develop secondary bacterial infections, suggesting virus-associated immunosuppression. To investigate this, we analyzed peripheral blood from 48 Boa constrictor with confirmed BIBD, three infected snakes without disease, and 84 reptarenavirus-negative snakes, assessing hematology, biochemistry, stress parameters, and immune function. A functional phagocytosis assay on peripheral blood revealed a significantly reduced proportion of phagocytic cells (Iba1+ monocytes/azurophils) in BIBD-positive and reptarenavirus-infected snakes compared to uninfected animals, indicating impaired phagocytic capacity. In addition, BIBD-positive snakes showed reduced cholesterol and total immunoglobulin concentrations, while virus-specific IgY and IgM levels were elevated. These findings indicate selective impairment of innate and humoral immune components, providing mechanistic evidence for increased susceptibility to secondary bacterial infections in BIBD.

Article.Title: Inhibitory receptor profiles for joint prediction of benefit and toxicity in immune checkpoint blockade
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Xiong D.; Duan B.; Ding G.; Huang Y.; Wang Q.
Article.Abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has transformed cancer therapy, but durable benefit is limited to a subset of patients and can be accompanied by immune-related adverse events. This Review evaluates inhibitory receptor profiles as candidate biomarkers for predicting both antitumor benefit and immune toxicity. We examine how receptor abundance, co-expression, cellular lineage, clonality, spatial context, and treatment-induced dynamics shape interpretation across tissue imaging, cytometry, bulk transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, and spatial profiling, with particular attention to organ-specific toxicity and time-dependent analytical bias. Current evidence supports context-dependent associations, especially for multi-receptor T-cell states and early on-treatment changes, but not universal thresholds or stand-alone clinical use. Because benefit and toxicity share pathways yet arise from partly distinct biological determinants, they should remain separate model outputs. We propose a staged path from mechanistic discovery to a locked minimal assay, external validation, and prospective evaluation of clinical utility.

Article.Title: Endometriosis and chronic pain syndrome: The role of stress mechanisms
Article.Authors: Reis F.; Vannuccini S.; De Logu F.; Pisani I.; Nassini R.; Petraglia F.
Article.Abstract: Patients with endometriosis report increased levels of perceived stress, which correlates with disease severity and pain intensity, creating feedback loops that perpetuate the cycle of endometriosis inflammation, chronic pain syndrome, and pathological stress response. Stress and chronic pain form an integrated biopsychosocial system in which neuroendocrine dysregulation, central sensitization, neuroinflammation, large-scale network reorganization, and maladaptive threat learning mutually reinforce each other. Sex differences, developmental experiences, and resilience factors modulate this interaction. Chronic pain in endometriosis emerges as the result of a progressive integration of peripheral inflammation and central nervous system plasticity. Thus, mechanism-based therapeutic strategies for endometriosis-associated pain should address both peripheral drivers and central amplification processes. Further research is needed to better understand whether chronic stress is a contributing cause for the onset of endometriosis and whether there is an opportunity to modify this risk factor before endometriosis is fully established.

Article.Authors: Kelbessa B.; Ghosh S.; Ghadamgahi F.; Catara V.; Whisson S.; Ortiz R.; Vetukuri R.
Article.Abstract: Late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans remains a major challenge to sustainable potato production. Genome sequencing of the two potato-associated strains, AV10 and S. rubidaea EV23, revealed biosynthetic clusters and genes potentially linked to antimicrobial activity, siderophore production, biofilm formation, nutrient acquisition, and plant growth promotion. Bacterial treatment also influenced the expression of potato genes associated with jasmonic acid, ethylene, salicylic acid-related defense, and auxin-linked growth response. Article.Title: Climate vulnerability and governance impact the payoff of policy drivers for SDG 7 outcomes in BRICS countries
Article.Authors: Sinha A.; Jindal A.; Abbas S.
Article.Abstract: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 7 (SDG 7) in large emerging economies requires energy policies that operate under diverse institutional and climatic conditions. We examine BRICS countries over 2000-2022 to assess how climate vulnerability and governance quality condition the estimated marginal effects of environmental policy stringency, innovation, financial development, inequality, and demographic structure on energy access, renewable energy, and energy efficiency. A two-stage empirical framework combines moderated GLS estimation with post-estimation evaluation of marginal-effect surfaces across contrasting governance-vulnerability regimes and country-specific conditions. The results show that stronger governance and lower climate vulnerability are generally associated with more favorable estimated effects of finance, innovation, and policy stringency, while weak governance and high vulnerability can weaken or reverse these relationships. Policy priorities also differ across SDG 7 subgoals and BRICS economies. These findings support context-specific energy policies that align institutional strengthening and climate resilience with SDG 7 implementation.

Article.Abstract: Rising outdoor activities have created major challenges for managing protected natural areas due to uncertain ecological effects. Early short-term impacts and subsequent recovery were monitored over a year using biotic and abiotic indicators: soil compaction, vegetation (total cover, Simpson's diversity index, and composition), bacterial colony-forming units, and edaphic microfauna. Article.Abstract: Oxytocin neurons in the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVHOxt) regulate feeding, anxiety, and social behaviors. Article.Authors: Nägele N.; Suppli M.; Gilliam-Vigh H.; Petersen N.; Hartmann B.; Knop F.; Lund A.; Jensen B.

Article.Authors: Kidtiwong A.; Arteaga M.; Tarasova K.; Gültekin S.; Rothbauer M.; Gerner I.; Jenner F.

Article.Title: Low-frequency non-destructive adaptive fastest pulse preheating for lithium-ion batteries
Article.Authors: Li C.; Mao S.; Gao M.; He M.; Sun Y.; Wang D.; Han X.; Xia C.; Wang X.; Lu Y.; Gao W.
Article.Abstract: Low-temperature polarization sharply reduces lithium-ion battery capacity and power, limiting electric vehicles and energy storage systems in cold regions. Bidirectional pulsed current (BPC) self-heating exploits increased internal resistance to enable efficient, rapid, and uniform heating, but high-rate pulses may induce lithium plating. Although high-frequency (>100 Hz) BPC suppresses plating, it requires additional power components. Here, we propose an adaptive, non-destructive BPC heating strategy that adjusts pulse current with temperature and state of charge (SOC), enabling the fastest heating within the lithium-plating-free boundary at low frequencies (<1 Hz). Using parameters optimized with three-electrode cells, lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) batteries were heated from -15°C to 10°C while maintaining the negative electrode potential above 0 V (vs. Li/Li+). After 100 heating cycles, neither chemistry showed capacity degradation, and post-heating analysis revealed no lithium plating, confirming safe and non-destructive low-temperature heating without compromising battery performance or requiring high-frequency auxiliary power electronics.

Article.Title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction
Article.Authors: Wang B.; Xie X.; Zou H.; Peng S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from multiple pretrained protein language models, aligns graph-based structural features with pretrained semantic embeddings for drugs under subspace constraints, and progressively refines drug-protein interaction representations through cascaded cross-modal signal propagation. Experiments on six benchmark datasets under standard, cold-start, and cross-domain settings demonstrate that SF-DTI achieves competitive performance relative to seven state-of-the-art baselines across evaluation scenarios. These results suggest that SF-DTI is a promising framework for DTI prediction and may support virtual screening, drug repositioning, and drug discovery.

Article.Abstract: Polymeric materials have become increasingly important in transportation and aerospace due to their low weight, processability, and ability to provide tailored functional properties. Article.Authors: Zhang P.; Chen Y.; Shi Y.; Zhao R.; Guo T.; Guo H.; Chen L.; Yu P.

Article.Title: The effectiveness of sound-based interventions on promoting sleep quality in hospitalized patients: A systematic review

Article.Abstract: Sleep quality strongly affects hospitalized patients' recovery, yet pain, anxiety, and environmental factors such as noise and light frequently disrupt it. Article.Abstract: Subclass cell types are strongly conserved across mammalian brains, making the systemic absence of a caudal ganglionic eminence (CGE) Pax6 interneuron subclass in mouse transcriptional atlases unexpected. Article.Title: Oscillatory dynamics within fronto-insular-parietal networks integrate thermosensory signals into body ownership
Article.Authors: Mattavelli G.; Crottini F.; Gorrino I.; Arrigoni E.; Maiocchi C.; Pisoni A.; Bottini G.; Salvato G.
Article.Abstract: Cutaneous thermosensory signals are linked to survival and homeostatic regulation, yet their relationship with higher order cognitive functions remains poorly understood. Moreover, the strength of a functional connectivity network spanning bilateral frontoparietal areas, including the insula, was associated with temperature changes coupled with ownership modulation. Article.Authors: Huang X.; Zhang Z.; Zhong Z.; Weng Z.; Xu Y.; Zhong G.; Li W.; Wang Q.; Du B.; Peng M.; Ma C.

Article.Title: Response speed is modulated by respiratory phase
Article.Authors: Yamazaki E.; Paller K.
Article.Abstract: Mere milliseconds can determine whether a sprinter or swimmer wins or places second. Would it help to intentionally control breathing while awaiting the starting signal? Article.Authors: Donaka R.; Awad K.; Khrystoforova I.; Hezkial B.; Brotto M.; Karasik D.

Article.Abstract: The COVID-19 crisis is now over, but additional viral strains of SARS-CoV-2 that evade immunity are continuously emerging. Article.Title: FGFR kinase isoform and activation state modulate ATPase activity
Article.Authors: Besch A.; Lamon G.; Zhang Y.; Traaseth N.
Article.Abstract: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) binding to FGF receptor (FGFR) induces trans-autophosphorylation of activation loop tyrosine residues within the receptor's intracellular kinase domain, thereby activating the receptor and promoting downstream substrate phosphorylation. Article.Title: Neutrophil swarm formation on large targets
Article.Authors: Wine C.; Apostolopoulou A.; Lin C.; Sevenler D.; Mansour M.; Irimia D.
Article.Abstract: Neutrophils are smaller in size than most fungal hyphae. Neutrophils from immunocompromised patients after liver transplant or hematopoietic stem cell transplant produce swarms that grow slowly and end up smaller compared with those from healthy donors. Article.Authors: Kavanagh R.; Bertola L.; Nielsen S.; Hua Zhu H.; Heller R.; Bhatt S.; Duchêne D.

Article.Title: Multitasking boosts human muscular endurance task performance due to elevated arousal
Article.Authors: Nagisa S.; Oblak E.; Shimojo S.; Shibata K.
Article.Abstract: Multitasking is generally thought to impair performance because of the interference between tasks arising from the limited processing capacity. Contrary to this view, we show that multitasking can also facilitate performance when interference between tasks is minimal. A similar effect was observed when monetary reward was offered for the cognitive task. These facilitation effects were associated with greater pupil dilation elicited by the cognitive task. These results suggest that a concurrent cognitive task can elevate a pupil-linked arousal state that facilitates endurance performance under the task conditions examined here, potentially by increasing the overall processing capacity. Article.Title: Non-volatile memristors as prospective radio frequency switches for 6G communications - A review
Article.Authors: Keat Seow E.; Toh R.; Ang D.
Article.Abstract: As communication technologies continue to improve to the 6G standard, highly performing radio frequency (RF) switches that have short switching times, high energy efficiency, high cutoff frequencies, capabilities of operating beyond 100 GHz while maintaining reasonable RF performance, and high data transmission rates of 100 Gbit s-1 are needed. Existing RF switches based on solid-state and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technologies fall short of meeting these requirements because of their volatility and parasitic inductive effects that lead to undesirably high insertion losses at high frequencies. Non-volatile memristors are emerging as likely candidates to replace traditional switches. They offer numerous benefits, including virtually zero static energy consumption, fast switching speeds, and excellent scalability. This review will provide an overview of the progress and challenges associated with implementing four types of non-volatile memristive technologies as RF switches: Resistive random access memory (ReRAM), conductive bridge random access memory (CBRAM), phase change memory (PCM), and memory based on two-dimensional (2D) materials, specifically molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The performance of these prospective switches is compared against one another and subsequently benchmarked against existing switch technologies. The review will provide an objective critique of the future readiness for 6G for the four main types of memristive switch technologies based on factors such as RF performance, CMOS compatibility, and fabrication maturity. Special attention is paid to 2D material-based memristors involving MoS2 and hBN, which have attracted significant research interest for multiple benefits that are claimed to be distinctive. Finally, it will also propose research directions to further the progress of future memristive RF switches.

Article.Authors: Li Y.; Wang Y.; Jin Z.; Tang C.; Xia X.; Gong Y.; Du Q.; Huang L.; Li Z.; Liao Y.; He S.; Wang B.; Liu Y.; Zheng Z.
Article.Abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HSCR) is characterized by distal intestinal aganglionosis and persistent dysfunction of the enteric nervous system after surgical treatment. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomics, network-based virtual perturbation analysis, proteomics, human tissue validation, enteric glial cell assays, neuron-glia co-culture systems, and an Ednrb conditional knockout (cKO) mouse model to investigate TXNRD1-dependent enteric glial remodeling in HSCR. We found that thioredoxin reductase 1 (TXNRD1) enrichment was associated with expansion of an SPP1-high/CXCL9-low enteric glial state and selective ERK/MAPK activation. TXNRD1 overexpression increased oxidative stress, impaired enteric glial migration and neurotrophic support, and induced neuronal dysfunction through suppression of GDNF/GFRα1/RET signaling. TXNRD1 inhibition alleviated HSCR-like phenotypes in Ednrb cKO mice. These findings identify TXNRD1-driven redox-dependent enteric glial remodeling as a mechanism contributing to neuronal dysfunction and HSCR progression.

Article.Title: An ultrasound-switchable hydrogel enables sequential antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy for infected diabetic wounds
Article.Authors: Zhu J.; Zhang C.; Zhang Q.; Xu F.; Wen B.; Xu Y.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Traditional dressings often fail to address the dynamic progression of infected diabetic wounds, which requires early bacterial elimination followed by timely control of oxidative stress and inflammation. Here, we developed an ultrasound-switchable Ce6/celastrol hydrogel for sequential antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy. Chlorin e6 (Ce6) and celastrol were co-encapsulated in a gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) hydrogel. Upon ultrasound irradiation, Ce6 generated singlet oxygen to reduce methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Escherichia coli (E. coli) in vitro. After ultrasound cessation, celastrol scavenged residual reactive oxygen species and suppressed inflammation. In an MRSA-infected diabetic wound model, the hydrogel with ultrasound reduced bacterial burden, alleviated inflammation, promoted collagen deposition, and accelerated wound closure. This strategy provides temporally regulated antibacterial and anti-inflammatory therapy for infected diabetic wounds.

Article.Title: Decoding how RNase E membrane targeting controls RNA degradosome activity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Article.Authors: Geslain S.; Allen G.; Geiser J.; Redder P.; Valentini M.
Article.Abstract: In many Proteobacterial species, transcription and RNA degradation are physically separated through segregation of the main ribonucleolytic machinery-the RNA degradosome-into RNase E-driven membrane-anchored assemblies that form discrete foci. Despite widespread conservation of the amphipathic membrane-targeting sequence (MTS) in RNase E, its function and biological importance remain poorly understood. Here, we have investigated how the MTS contributes to bacterial virulence or stress response in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. We show that membrane anchoring is dispensable for formation of RNA degradosome foci, but required for their proper morphology, dynamics, and localization, whereas the MTS sequence modulates foci behavior. Transcriptomic and mRNA spatial organization analyses further reveal specific stabilization of localized transcripts encoding membrane proteins in the MTS mutant, together with abnormal operon processing. Altogether, our study reveals the elegant MTS-mediated control of RNA degradosome spatial organization and target selection, shaping the transcriptome and bacterial stress responses.

Article.Title: Baseline techno-economic and life cycle assessment of black mass production
Article.Authors: Yingnakorn T.; Kansomket C.; Longbutsri C.; Scott S.; Patcharawit T.; Yang J.; Abbott A.; Khumkoa S.
Article.Abstract: Recycling lithium-ion batteries hinges on economically producing black mass-the electrode powder concentrate that feeds downstream metal recovery-yet public baselines pairing real process economics with environmental impacts remain scarce. Here we show that a purely mechanical flowsheet-shredding, zigzag air classification, and circular screen vibration-applied identically to two structurally distinct feedstocks recovers black mass at 93.28 wt % separation efficiency from electric-vehicle modules and 75.77 wt % from mobile phone cells. Built on measured pilot data, loaded processing costs of $0.31-0.73/kg yield net profits of $4.39-5.53/kg under realistic feedstock purchase prices, with a probability of unprofitability below 0.2% across simulated market scenarios. Life cycle assessment attributes most impacts to grid electricity, with a global warming potential of 0.210-0.241 kg CO2 eq./kg input; a low-carbon grid cuts this by 62.8%. This paired baseline enables benchmarking of emerging recycling routes and supports circular battery supply chains.

Article.Title: Genomic structural variations distinguishing archaic and modern humans are associated with neurodevelopment
Article.Authors: Zha S.; Li C.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: Understanding the divergence in neurodevelopment between extinct archaic hominins and modern humans is a central goal in evolutionary biology. Structural variants (SVs) are key genomic drivers of phenotypic change. Here, we identified a set of SVs present in archaic humans by screening fixed SV events from diverse non-human primate (NHP) lineages, termed archaic hominin structural variants (AHSVs). AHSVs are significantly enriched in genes governing brain development and function, many of which are implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders. We found that several AHSVs overlap with brain cis-regulatory elements (CREs). Furthermore, in three neural-related genes (PDE10A, RAPGEF4, and DCTN4), modern human-specific chromatin loop anchors coincide with deletions shared by archaic hominins, suggesting that AHSVs may have influenced three-dimensional chromatin architecture. Overall, this study expands our understanding of the adaptive evolution of the modern human brain.

Article.Title: Domain-autonomous MKLP1 modules divergently regulate mitotic fidelity and polyploidy in a holocentric system
Article.Authors: Zhang B.; Liu X.; Song M.; Qin M.; Tian S.; Lin Y.; Li D.; Yao L.; Ayra-Pardo C.; Kan Y.
Article.Abstract: While the kinesin MKLP1 is a well-established regulator of cytokinesis, whether its individual domains possess autonomous functions has remained unexplored. Here, using the holocentric Bombyx mori BmN4 system, we show that isolated head, stalk, and tail domains of MKLP1 exhibit distinct subcellular localization patterns and exert divergent control over mitosis. These domains differentially regulate cell-cycle progression, with the head and stalk inducing G2/M arrest, whereas the tail, and to a lesser extent the head, promotes polyploidization. Despite these divergent outcomes, all three domains converge on a shared pathological activity, aberrantly recruiting γ-tubulin, disrupting spindle organization, and compromising chromosome segregation. The domains also exert opposing effects on EdU incorporation, with the head suppressing EdU labeling and the stalk and tail enhancing it. Together, our findings redefine MKLP1 as a composite platform of regulatory modules, whose uncoupling reveals a principle of kinesin organization with broad implications for mitotic robustness and genomic stability.

Article.Title: Materials design strategies for green thermoelectric generators enabling sustainable and scalable energy harvesting
Article.Authors: Sabran N.; Fadzallah I.; Van Toan N.; Ono T.; Mohd Sabri M.; Jun H.
Article.Abstract: Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) harvest low-grade heat without moving parts and can be integrated into compact, flexible, or distributed systems. Progress in this field is typically measured through figure of merit, ZT, and the power factor, yet materials with high ZT often depend on scarce elements, toxic precursors, high-temperature processing, or difficult end-of-life recovery-considerations that matter for technologies intended to support sustainable energy systems. This perspective examines green thermoelectric design as a coupled materials, process, device, and life cycle problem, considering how aqueous processing, bio-assisted synthesis, hydrothermal methods, electrochemical deposition, and printable processing shape microstructure, defect chemistry, and charge-heat transport in conductive polymers, carbon nanotube hybrids, biomass-derived carbons, recycled inorganic compounds, and ionic thermoelectric systems. We propose a design framework that combines material abundance, process energy, solvent and waste burden, device lifetime, manufacturability, and circularity, and identify where environmentally responsible TEGs can deliver useful power with lower total burden.

Article.Title: Microenvironment shapes Staphylococcus aureus phenotypes in children with cystic fibrosis over time
Article.Authors: Robaldi S.; Pereda R.; Pautasso M.; Blasko E.; Fretes A.; Jaureguialzo T.; Diaz Appella M.; Galeano M.; Rial M.; Smith S.; Ginestet E.; Gonzalez N.; González J.; Smania A.; Vila A.; Sola C.; Cassanelli P.; Tribelli P.

Article.Title: Choroid plexus remodeling associated with inflammatory CSF exposure in preterm acquired hydrocephalus
Article.Authors: Jison G.; Ramos N.; Cotrim-Gomes F.; Lee S.; Hanak B.; Muhonen M.; Castañeyra-Ruiz L.
Article.Abstract: Acquired hydrocephalus in preterm infants follows intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) or central nervous system infection and is associated with inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles. Article.Title: Comparing soil-health- and species-based sensitivity distributions for metal risk assessment in Tianjin soils
Article.Authors: Xu Q.; Shi Y.; Xiong X.; Qian L.; Fang L.; Zhou X.; Shao X.
Article.Abstract: Soil contamination threatens ecosystem functioning, while conventional ecological risk assessment (ERA) based on single-species toxicity may not capture system-level responses. Observed SHSDs were also shifted rightward relative to additive, non-interactive predictions, indicating lower apparent sensitivity of the integrated microcosm. These findings support SHSD as a higher tier, function-oriented complement to conventional SSDs, while emphasizing the need for independent field validation before regulatory application.

Article.Title: An unexploited almond biodiversity in central Italy: Genetic characterization and conservation strategies using molecular markers
Article.Authors: Savoia M.; Sgaramella N.; Micheletti A.; Staffolani P.; Gaeta L.; Venerito P.; Miazzi M.; Fanelli V.; Montemurro C.
Article.Abstract: Almond is one of the most important nut crops worldwide. In Italy, 96% of the national almond production is covered by the Southern regions. However, small resources of cultivated and wild trees are also found in central Italian regions like Abruzzo, Sardinia, and Marche. Exploratory missions throughout the Marche region revealed the presence of many local and uncharacterized almond genotypes. The aim of this study was to recover this germplasm and characterize it using molecular markers. The genetic analysis revealed a high genetic variation in Marche almond genotypes, which showed them to be genetically distinct from the Italian and international varieties. A great richness in private alleles was found in the Marche almond collection, supporting the uniqueness of this germplasm and the importance of this resource of genetic diversity for the development of conservation programs and the implementation of almond breeding activities.

Article.Title: Nonpharmacological interventions for frailty and sarcopenia in older adults with gastrointestinal cancers: A Bayesian network meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Hui X.; Fu Z.; Guo Y.; Duan L.; Shi W.; Dong Q.; Xu Q.; Xu X.
Article.Abstract: To compare the effects of nonpharmacological interventions on frailty, sarcopenia, and related physical-function outcomes in older adults with gastrointestinal cancers, we conducted a Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of 21 randomized controlled trials from 10 countries. Most interventions did not show clear benefits for frailty, sarcopenia, gait speed, Timed Up and Go performance, sit-to-stand performance, skeletal muscle index, or 6-min walk distance. Prehabilitation exercise showed a low-certainty benefit for handgrip strength, whereas enhanced nutritional support and intensive physiotherapy showed limited benefits for patient-reported physical function. However, these findings were based on small, sparsely connected networks, and the certainty of evidence was generally low or very low. No single intervention was consistently effective across outcomes. These results highlight the need for larger, cancer-specific trials using standardized outcome definitions and clearer reporting of intervention intensity, adherence, safety, and feasibility.

Article.Title: Host-response biomarker panels for distinguishing selected acute respiratory viral-bacterial co-infections from mono-infections
Article.Authors: Nahid-Samiei R.; Ebrahimi D.; Samiei M.; Nahand J.; Donyavi T.; Bokharaei-Salim F.
Article.Abstract: Acute respiratory viral-bacterial co-infections complicate antimicrobial decisions because pathogen detection may not establish whether both organisms are clinically contributing to disease. Conventional C-reactive protein and procalcitonin were most useful as supportive or rule-out markers of bacterial involvement, but lacked sufficient specificity when used alone. These findings support prospective validation of integrated host-response panels as rapid decision-support tools for antimicrobial stewardship and clinically meaningful co-infection diagnosis.

Article.Title: Ectopic overproduction of cell wall glucan through membrane perturbation by an antifungal peptide theonellamide A in fission yeast
Article.Authors: Nakao K.; Carvalho V.; Suganaga A.; Osumi M.; Tokukura M.; Kakeya H.; Matsuyama A.; Yashiroda Y.; Matsunaga S.; Cortés J.; Yoshida M.; Ribas J.; Nishimura S.

Article.Title: Development of CNN and LSTM fusion model for early fault warning in hydro turbine units
Article.Authors: Zhu Y.; Chen Y.; Xiang X.; Wang J.; Wang S.; Jiang X.; Lu Y.
Article.Abstract: Early fault detection is important for the safe and stable operation of large hydro turbine units under complex and variable operating conditions. The CNN LSTM model captures local correlations and temporal evolution, achieving R2 values of 0.947, 0.955, 0.848, 0.701, 0.687, and 0.853 for SPCA1 to SPCA6. The framework provides a practical approach for condition monitoring and hierarchical early warning of large hydro turbine units.

Article.Title: Trait anxiety selectively amplifies reward learning under uncertainty, while N3 sleep attenuates it
Article.Authors: Deshmukh R.; Ramakrishnan A.
Article.Abstract: Adaptive learning under uncertainty requires distinguishing random variability (stochasticity) from true environmental change (volatility), yet how trait anxiety and sleep together influence it remains unclear. Hierarchical Bayesian modeling showed that in stable but noisy environments, individuals with higher trait anxiety appeared to treat stochastic fluctuations as indicators of genuine change, resulting in over updating and lower evidence accumulation, while preserving normative trends in volatile environments. In a second experiment combining task performance with overnight sleep electroencephalography, greater N3 sleep was associated with reduced updating and higher evidence accumulation in stable environments among individuals with higher trait anxiety. These findings suggest that trait anxiety selectively alters how uncertainty is computationally represented, while N3 sleep appears to attenuate it. Together, these findings provide a computational framework linking anxiety, sleep, and adaptive learning under uncertainty.

Article.Title: Bidirectional metabolic-vascular feedback loops in heart failure: From myocardial energetics to multisystem cardiometabolic crosstalk
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Li Y.; Qin C.; Chen X.; Wang K.; Zhang M.; Cheng W.
Article.Abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a multisystem syndrome in which myocardial dysfunction is shaped by metabolic, vascular, and extracardiac abnormalities. We also examine how adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, liver, and kidney amplify these circuits. Together, this framework links myocardial energetic dysfunction with systemic vascular-metabolic stress and highlights circuit-directed opportunities for phenotype-informed HF therapy.

Article.Title: Urban habitats offer buffered environmental conditions for city-dwelling bats
Article.Authors: Ding J.; Boonman A.; Eitan O.; Werber Y.; Troupin D.; Sapir N.; Yovel Y.
Article.Abstract: Urbanization reshapes local climates, potentially altering how animals respond to environmental variation. We used continuous acoustic monitoring at 12 urban and 15 rural sites across a steep aridity gradient in Israel, recording bats for 2.5 months from midsummer to autumn. Across 1,151 site-nights, we detected 95,473 encounters from 11 species. Rural bat activity was strongly associated with temperature, humidity, wind speed, and illumination, whereas urban activity was less sensitive to these environmental factors and to building height and density. Rural specialists avoided cities and were active within relatively narrow environmental ranges, while generalists occurred in both habitats and used broader activity conditions in cities. Urban bat activity also remained comparatively stable as rural activity declined seasonally. These findings show that cities may buffer environmental variability, allowing bats to forage across broader weather and potentially remain active later in the year.

Article.Title: Evolution of lake microbial structure and function under climatic and anthropogenic forcings: Insights from sedimentary ancient DNA
Article.Authors: Shi X.; Xu H.; Li W.; Wang J.; Song Y.; Yang M.; Wang B.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Structure and function of lake microorganisms are sensitive to environmental disturbances; yet their differential responses to climatic and anthropogenic forcings over centennial scales remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed a sediment core from Lake Daihai in northern China, combining metagenomics and stable isotope analyses. Our results revealed that microbial community assembly was dominated by deterministic processes, whereas stochasticity increased notably after 1850, coinciding with the termination of the Little Ice Age and intensified human impacts. This decoupling was mediated by functional redundancy associated with bacterial keystone taxa, ultimately resulting in more negative sedimentary carbon and nitrogen isotopic compositions nearly a century later. Gene-level functional redundancy further buffered ecosystem function variability across biological scales. Collectively, our findings integrate omics and geochemical approaches to advance the understanding of lake ecological evolution under complex multi-forcing regimes.

Article.Title: An atlas of sarbecovirus infectivity across diverse ACE2 orthologs
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Cheng Z.; Wu X.; Liu K.; Wang L.; Yang D.; Huang W.; Nie J.
Article.Abstract: Sarbecoviruses pose a substantial zoonotic threat, yet the determinants governing their host range remain incompletely defined. To systematically investigate host entry mechanisms, we generated a panel of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudoviruses representing 46 sarbecoviruses and assessed their infectivity across 66 angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) orthologs. Together, these findings define host entry constraints relevant to receptor-based risk assessment and inform surveillance and pandemic preparedness.

Article.Abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) is extensively employed in high-voltage electrical equipment due to its exceptional dielectric properties, yet its potent greenhouse effect and extreme chemical inertness demand efficient abatement strategies. Article.Authors: Gao H.; Fang Y.; Tian Z.; Guo C.; Wang P.; Liu T.; Sun Y.; Zhang P.; Qian Q.
Article.Abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy provides substantial clinical benefits in hematologic malignancies. Article.Title: Sulfonylurea receptor 1 deficiency alleviates acute lung injury by activating PARP1 in epithelial cells
Article.Authors: Yin X.; Zhu Q.; Zhao L.; Ma W.; Wang L.; Li H.; Wang C.; Wang Y.; Xu L.; Zhang H.; Wang X.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a critical disease with high mortality, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Article.Title: Recent advances in medical hemostatic materials: Mechanisms, evaluation, and clinical perspectives

Article.Abstract: Uncontrolled hemorrhage remains a major cause of preventable death in trauma and surgery, yet the performance of hemostatic materials varies markedly with wound geometry, blood flow, coagulation status, and tissue sensitivity. This review critically examines natural polymer-based, synthetic polymer-based, inorganic, and composite hemostats by linking material structure to six principal mechanisms: fluid absorption and surface adsorption, coagulation activation, bioactive-factor delivery, photothermal assistance, adhesive sealing, and microstructural regulation. Beyond cataloging materials, we compare class-specific advantages, failure modes, and safety constraints, and analyze how hemodilution, hypothermia, acidosis, anticoagulation, infection, and high-flow bleeding reshape material performance. We further integrate clinically used products, scenario-based material selection, and a staged evaluation framework spanning mechanistic assays, hostile-condition testing, translational bleeding models, rebleeding assessment, and post-hemostasis safety. Finally, we outline stage-matched pathways for responsive and multifunctional systems. Article.Abstract: Induction of gastric ulcer by ethanol is associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired gastric mucosal defense. Article.Abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are fundamental to vast biological processes. Article.Abstract: Cats are among the world's most popular companion animals. Owner-pet hormonal synchrony is documented in dogs but untested in cats. Article.Abstract: Early initiation of alcohol use is a risk factor for developing alcohol use disorder (AUD) later in life, yet the long-term neuronal consequences of adolescent drinking remain poorly understood. Collectively, our data reveal that AIE produced a long-lasting reduction in adult CeA inhibitory tone, and this change is likely independent of the noradrenergic system. This developmental-specific shift in CeA activity reflects the heightened vulnerability of the adolescent brain to ethanol-induced neuroadaptation and may represent a neural substrate underlying the increased risk of AUD following adolescent alcohol use.

Article.Authors: Jabłońska J.; Orzoł D.; Ciurko D.; Wiera G.; Mozrzymas J.

However, when CHX was restricted to the recorded postsynaptic neuron, the initial phase of iLTP proceeded normally, but GABAergic currents gradually returned to baseline levels, indicating intact induction but impaired maintenance. Here, we compared subcutaneous nicotine injection and nicotine aerosol inhalation in male mice across behavioral, dopaminergic, and transcriptomic domains. Nicotine aerosol inhalation produced concentration-dependent modulation of conditioned place preference, accompanied by rapid nicotine absorption and delayed cotinine accumulation. Fiber photometry recordings in the nucleus accumbens revealed distinct dopamine dynamics during nicotine-associated contextual processing, with nicotine-paired contexts eliciting shorter time-to-peak but reduced amplitude and area under the curve. High-dimensional behavioral tracking under mecamylamine-precipitated withdrawal conditions demonstrated that nicotine exposure conditions reshaped behavioral organization rather than producing generalized hyperlocomotion. Subcutaneous nicotine and aerosol exposure produced partially overlapping but compositionally distinct behavioral profiles influenced by nicotine exposure, delivery paradigm, and aerosol formulation. Transcriptomic analyses further revealed region-specific molecular signatures, including metabolic pathways in the ventral tegmental area and synaptic/neuroimmune-related pathways in the nucleus accumbens after aerosol exposure. Together, these findings demonstrate that nicotine delivery paradigms shape distinct neurobehavioral and molecular responses, emphasizing the importance of inhalation-based models in preclinical nicotine research.

Article.Title: Effects of metabotropic 2/3-glutamate receptor agonism and antagonism on activity-based anorexia model in mice
Article.Authors: Varjelus T.; Oksanen A.; Kaljala L.; Ryazantseva M.; Aitta-aho T.
Article.Abstract: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder disproportionately found in female teens and young adults. It is often resistant to treatment, has a significant chance of relapse and is more lethal than other eating disorders, such as bulimia nervosa or Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID). There is no specific medication for the treatment of anorexia nervosa. Treatment consists of psychosocial means, psychotherapy, psychoeducation, and nutritional counseling. Medication is usually used for treating comorbidities such as anxiety or to decrease obsessive-compulsive tendencies. These medications cannot help the patient regain weight or treat core symptoms. Metabotropic 2/3-glutamate (mGluR2/3) receptor agonist (LY379268) and antagonist (LY341495) are promising pharmacological agents to treat psychiatric disorders. Both have been reported to be anxiolytic, while antagonists have shown antidepressant-like effects in preclinical studies. The activity-based anorexia (ABA) paradigm is used to study mechanisms related to anorexia nervosa. It consists of giving mice access to a running wheel and restricting their feeding time. This causes mice to exercise more than mice without feeding time restriction and to eat less than mice without access to a moving running wheel. In this study, we subcutaneously injected female ABA model mice with a metabotropic 2/3-glutamate receptor agonist (LY379268) and antagonist (LY341495) in two experiments. Both compounds exacerbated weight loss by decreasing food intake as well as increasing physical activity. It can be concluded that the pharmacological manipulation of mGluR2/3 receptors is detrimental for the female ABA model and, therefore, might be potentially harmful for anorexia nervosa as well.

Article.Title: Altered hsa_circ_0005567 expression in schizophrenia: exploratory clinical associations and cellular evidence involving RPL7A
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhong Q.; Long J.; Lu R.; Lv M.; Huang X.; Zhong Z.; Lan W.; Liao F.; Su L.
Article.Abstract: Background: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a chronic mental disorder with unknown etiology and complex pathophysiology. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as important regulators in neuropsychiatric disorders. This study investigated the clinical relevance, functional role, and potential mechanism of hsa_circ_0005567 in SCZ. Methods: hsa_circ_0005567 expression was measured by qRT-PCR in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 160 patients with SCZ and 160 healthy controls. Associations with clinical symptoms and laboratory parameters were explored. Functional studies were conducted in MK-801-treated SH-SY5Y cells after hsa_circ_0005567 knockdown or overexpression. Cell viability, apoptosis, and inflammatory cytokines were assessed. Candidate hsa_circ_0005567-interacting proteins were explored using chromatin isolation by RNA purification (CHIRP), mass spectrometry, RNA immunoprecipitation, and Western blotting. Results: hsa_circ_0005567 expression was significantly increased in PBMCs from patients with SCZ (P < 0.001) and in SH-SY5Y cells following MK-801 treatment (P = 0.026). Higher hsa_circ_0005567 expression remained associated with SCZ status after adjustment for age and sex. Exploratory analyses of PANSS scores and laboratory parameters showed only nominal associations, none of which remained significant after FDR correction. In vitro, hsa_circ_0005567 manipulation affected cell viability, apoptosis, and TNF-α expression in MK-801-treated SH-SY5Y cells. RPL7A was identified as a candidate hsa_circ_0005567-interacting protein, and its protein expression was altered following hsa_circ_0005567 knockdown or overexpression. Conclusions: hsa_circ_0005567 is upregulated in PBMCs from patients with SCZ and is independently associated with SCZ status. Functional experiments suggest that hsa_circ_0005567 may participate in cellular responses under MK-801-induced stress conditions, while RPL7A represents a candidate interacting protein. Further clinical and mechanistic validation is needed.

Article.Title: Suppression of ER stress underlies Montelukast's neuroprotective actions in D-gal/AlCl3-induced Alzheimer's disease in rats
Article.Authors: Mahmoud A.; Ibrahim S.; El-Yamany M.; Gowifel A.; Mohammed R.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative ailment characterized by neuronal and cognitive dysfunctions. Notably, cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 1 (CysLT1R) overexpression was detected in various AD models. It was closely associated with other hallmarks of AD, including increased oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, amyloid beta (Aβ) deposition, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Montelukast (MTK), a CysLT1R antagonist, is an anti-asthmatic drug possessing antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Consequently, this study aimed to mechanistically investigate MTK's neuroprotective potential on D-galactose/Aluminum Chloride (D-gal/AlCl3)-induced AD in rats. This was accomplished by allocating thirty-six adult male Wistar rats into four equal groups as follows: Group I served as the control group, and Group II was orally treated daily with MTK (10 mg/kg) for eight weeks. At the same time, groups III and IV were administered D-gal (65 mg/kg/day, SC) and AlCl3 (200 mg/kg/day, p.o.), starting from week 3 until the end of the experiment, for the remaining six consecutive weeks, to induce AD. Group IV received MTK orally daily for eight weeks. The findings showed that dampening CysLT1R expression by MTK ameliorated D-gal/AlCl3-induced amyloidopathy. MTK rectified the behavioral outcomes, as evidenced by the improved parameters in the novel object recognition, Y-maze, and Morris water maze tests. MTK hampered oxidative stress (MDA and GSH), inflammatory (NF-κB and TNF-α), glial activation (GFAP and Iba1), apoptotic (Caspase-3), ER stress, and Aβ biomarkers. Additionally, MTK, as a CysLT1R antagonist, exerted these favorable actions via adjustment of PERK/IRE1-α/CHOP, NF-κB, mTOR, and apoptotic axes. In conclusion, this study underscored the use of MTK as a promising neuroprotective approach for mitigating AD via modulation of ER stress, neuroinflammatory, and apoptotic trajectories.

Article.Title: Adult-administered chronic nicotine remodels nigral dopaminergic and pedunculopontine cholinergic physiology
Article.Authors: Chen R.; Hosseini H.; Hall S.; Zhang S.; Evans R.
Article.Abstract: Nicotine is linked to neuroprotection and has been proposed as a potential preventative treatment for Parkinson's disease (PD). Because PD is an aging disorder, such a treatment would necessarily be administered to adults. However, previous studies examining the effects of chronic nicotine in neurons vulnerable to PD have primarily been conducted in juvenile animals. Here we administer chronic nicotine to adult mice of both sexes. We examine nicotine-induced functional adaptations in two brain structures vulnerable to PD, the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) and the pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN). Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology and two-photon calcium imaging, we observed changes in cellular properties that potentially contribute to reduced risk of PD associated with nicotine exposure. Chronic nicotine decreased pacemaking frequency, burst propensity, and rebound firing in SNc dopaminergic neurons, while decoupling tonic firing rate from dendritic calcium levels. These changes in the SNc occurred without altering L-type channel contributions, dendritic arborization, or excitatory synaptic drive. Although the PPN degenerates in PD and is the primary cholinergic input to the SNc, no previous studies have evaluated the effects of chronic nicotine on this structure. We find that chronic nicotine induced subregion-specific plasticity in the PPN. Rostral PPN neurons showed depolarized membrane potentials, broadened action potentials, and dendritic pruning, whereas caudal PPN neurons showed reduced spike frequency adaptation and accelerated excitatory postsynaptic current kinetics. While these PPN alterations do not have a previously established link with cellular vulnerability, synaptic and physiological changes in this region may have unexpected contributions to PD progression. In addition, these findings reveal novel mechanisms that could underlie nicotine's modulation of brainstem circuitry controlling arousal, sensory gating, and drug dependence.

Article.Title: 4-methyl-3-aminopyridine: A novel active blocker of voltage-gated potassium ion channels in the central nervous system
Article.Authors: Rodríguez-Rangel S.; Coronado O.; Ortega B.; Sun Y.; El-Saadi S.; Brugarolas P.; Sánchez-Rodríguez J.
Article.Abstract: Aminopyridines, including 4-aminopyridine (4AP), 3,4-diaminopyridine, and [18F]3-fluoro-4-aminopyridine, are voltage-gated potassium (KV) channel blockers used clinically to enhance conduction in neurological disorders and to image demyelination by positron emission tomography (PET). Here, we characterized the physicochemical properties (pKa, logD), KV channel-blocking activity, toxicity (LD50), and pharmacokinetics of a novel compound, 4-methyl-3-aminopyridine (4Me3AP). 4Me3AP was less basic and more lipophilic than 4AP and showed greater blocking potency across multiple KV channels expressed in Xenopus oocytes. In mice, 4Me3AP exhibited lower acute toxicity (LD50 = 29.3 mg/kg) than 4AP (LD50 = 12.7 mg/kg) and a longer plasma half-life. These findings indicate that 4Me3AP is a potent KV channel blocker with favorable pharmacological properties, supporting its potential for symptomatic treatment of demyelinating diseases.

Article.Title: Molecular pathways implicated in antidepressant actions exhibits diurnal fluctuations in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus of adult male and female mice
Article.Authors: González-Hernández G.; Rozov S.; Berrocoso E.; Rantamäki T.
Article.Abstract: Epidemiological and experimental studies have demonstrated a bidirectional relationship between mood disorders and the circadian system, with disrupted circadian rhythms contributing to depressive states, and their restoration playing a key role in antidepressants effects. In this context, we sought to examine whether selected molecular pathways implicated in antidepressant responses exhibit diurnal regulatory patterns. Naïve adult male and female C57BL/6 mice were euthanized at 3-h intervals beginning at Zeitgeber Time 0 (ZT0), and hippocampal (HC) and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) tissues were collected for RT-qPCR and Western blot analyses. We observed statistically significant diurnal rhythmicity in all analyzed transcripts (cFos, Arc, Nr4a1, Dusp1, Dusp5, and Dusp6) in both HC and mPFC samples, with peak expression occurring during the dark (active) phase (ZT15-18). Phosphorylation levels of TrkBY816 (tropomyosin-related kinase) and GSK3βS9 (glycogen synthase kinase 3β) also showed patterns suggestive of temporal rhythmicity, peaking during the light (inactive) phase. Levels of p-ERK2T185/Y187 (extracellular-signal regulated kinase) did not display rhythmic fluctuations, but peaked during the light phase in the HC, especially in males. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that antidepressant-related signaling is subject to diurnal regulation, highlighting the importance of integrating circadian biology and time-of-day as relevant variables in the development of translationally relevant antidepressant research.

Article.Title: Structure-activity relationships of BnOCPA derivatives at native pre- and postsynaptic adenosine A1Rs
Article.Authors: la Mache C.; Preti B.; Wani M.; Lochner M.; Frenguelli B.; Wall M.
Article.Abstract: The addition of a benzyloxy group to the adenosine A1R agonist cyclopentyladenosine (CPA) produces a compound (BnOCPA) that selectivity activates A1R signalling via the G protein alpha subunit Gob. In rat hippocampus, BnOCPA inhibits CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission (IC50 65 nM) likely via Gob, with no effect on Goa-mediated postsynaptic membrane electrophysiology at concentrations up to 1 μM. We have investigated how modifications of the benzyloxy group of BnOCPA affects signalling: addition of methoxy group, MBnOCPA, substituting a phenoxy group, PhOCPA; and addition of bromide to the phenoxy group, BPhOCPA. These derivatives, previously shown to be selective A1R agonists, were assessed through inhibition of hippocampal CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission and postsynaptic effects on CA1 pyramidal neurons. All compounds inhibited synaptic transmission and increased paired-pulse facilitation, indicative of presynaptic actions. At a concentration that inhibited synaptic transmission (>75 %), none of the compounds hyperpolarised the resting membrane potential and thus retained the pre-vs postsynaptic selectivity of BnOCPA. Increasing their concentration allowed a measure of the selectivity range. BnOCPA hyperpolarised ∼40 % of neurons at 3 μM (∼50x the IC50 for synaptic inhibition). For PhOCPA and MBnOCPA, hyperpolarisation, occurred for some neurons, at 1 μM. For BPhOCPA, no hyperpolarisation occurred at concentrations up to 10 μM. Pre-application of the derivatives (at 300 nM) reduced adenosine-mediated hyperpolarisation, showing they bind but do not activate postsynaptic A1Rs. This data shows that modifying the structure of BnOCPA changes the discrimination between different native A1Rs, likely based upon selective activation of G-protein coupling.

Article.Title: Psychoneuroimmunology of glioblastoma: How emotional states shape tumor biology
Article.Authors: de Melo M.; Bezerra T.; de Souza P.; Sales V.; da Rosa M.
Article.Abstract: Psychological states profoundly influence physiological processes, with growing evidence linking emotional dysregulation to cancer progression. Within the framework of psychoneuroimmunology, recent findings have shown that chronic stress, depression and anxiety disrupt immune surveillance and promote a pro-inflammatory environment that favors tumor growth. Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the most aggressive brain tumor, appears particularly sensitive to these neuroimmune influences. Some stress mediators and neurotransmitters-such as glucocorticoids and catecholamines- modulate the GBM microenvironment, fostering tumor-supportive pathways and epigenetic changes. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence connecting emotional disturbances and glioma biology, highlighting shared neuroimmune mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that integrating psychosocial and neuropharmacological strategies into GBM care could improve patients outcomes by targeting both tumor biology and emotional well-being.

Article.Title: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone increases dorsal premammillary nucleus neuron activity and darting behavior
Article.Authors: Coletta C.; Laing B.
Article.Abstract: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) is classically recognized for its role in regulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis; however, it also functions as a central neuromodulator influencing arousal, locomotion, and autonomic processes. Despite these established roles, the circuit-level mechanisms through which TRH modulates behavior remain poorly defined. The dorsal premammillary nucleus (PMd) is a hypothalamic structure implicated in high-imminence defensive states, yet whether TRH directly engages PMd circuits is unknown. Here, we assessed the role of TRH as a modulator of PMd neuronal activity and behavioral output using in situ hybridization, electrophysiology, calcium imaging, and behavioral assays in male and female mice. TRHR mRNA was co-localized with a subset of PMd CCK-positive neurons. TRH increased firing rate in a subset of PMd neurons in brain slices, revealing functional activation of a subset of the population. This finding was corroborated by calcium imaging that showed increased activity following TRH exposure. In vivo, intrahypothalamic administration of TRH produced darting and behavioral effects. Together, these findings identify a subpopulation of PMd neurons that serve as a functional hypothalamic target of TRH signaling associated with rapid locomotor behavioral output.

Article.Title: Deficiency of synaptotagmin 9 in the hippocampal region induces synaptic damage and cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease mice via BDNF/TrkB signaling
Article.Authors: Xu N.; Du C.; Li Y.; Yang W.; Li W.; Perez R.; Yu S.; Lou H.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive impairment is a prominent non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD) that severely affects patients' quality of life, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of hippocampal Synaptotagmin 9 (Syt9) in PD-related cognitive deficits. We found that Syt9 expression was significantly downregulated in the hippocampus of both MPTP-induced subacute PD mice and A53T α-synuclein transgenic mice, concomitant with cognitive impairment and synaptic damage. To determine causality, we performed hippocampal Syt9 knockdown and overexpression using AAV-mediated gene delivery. Syt9 knockdown exacerbated, while Syt9 overexpression alleviated, cognitive deficits and synaptic structural abnormalities in PD mice. Proteomic sequencing and pharmacological manipulations revealed that Syt9 may regulate the BDNF/TrkB signaling pathway at the protein level, likely by influencing BDNF vesicular transport, release, or stability. Intra-hippocampal BDNF supplementation rescued synaptic damage and cognitive impairment, whereas the TrkB antagonist ANA-12 reversed the protective effects of Syt9 overexpression. Collectively, our findings identify the Syt9/BDNF/TrkB axis as a key mechanism in PD-related cognitive impairment and suggest that targeting this pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for PD.

Article.Title: Gallic acid attenuates PTSD-like behavioral and hippocampal neuroplasticity deficits induced by single prolonged stress in male rats
Article.Authors: Meamar M.; Mohamadi Yarijani Z.; Parsaei H.; Vafaei A.; Rashidy-Pour A.; Raise-Abdullahi P.
Article.Abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with persistent cognitive and emotional disturbances linked to hippocampal dysfunction, oxidative stress, and impaired neuroplasticity. Gallic acid, a naturally occurring polyphenol, possesses antioxidant and neuroprotective properties, but its effects in trauma-related disorders remain incompletely understood. Male Wistar rats were subjected to single prolonged stress (SPS) to induce PTSD-like phenotypes and, beginning 24 h after SPS, received gallic acid (10 or 100 mg/kg) or saline for 14 days. SPS exposure induced anxiety-like behavior, impaired fear extinction, and deficits in spatial learning and memory, accompanied by increased lipid peroxidation, reduced antioxidant capacity, decreased hippocampal BDNF expression, and CA3 dendritic atrophy. Early post-stress gallic acid administration attenuated these behavioral alterations and was accompanied by improvements in hippocampal oxidative status, BDNF expression, and CA3 dendritic morphology, without detectable effects on locomotor activity or relative adrenal gland weight. Collectively, these findings indicate that early post-stress gallic acid administration attenuates SPS-associated behavioral and hippocampal abnormalities and that these effects are associated with antioxidant and neuroplasticity-related changes rather than establishing a causal mechanism. Further studies using delayed treatment paradigms and pathway-specific approaches are needed to determine the efficacy of gallic acid after establishment of the PTSD-like phenotype and to clarify the mechanisms underlying its effects.

Article.Title: zDHHC11 is a common palmitoyltransferase regulating microglia-mediated neuroinflammation across neurodegenerative diseases
Article.Authors: Luo H.; Jiang D.; Hao Z.; Bu J.; Wang J.; Xu N.; Nie X.; Zhang Y.; Yin Q.; Zhuang P.
Article.Abstract: Purpose: Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is a shared feature across Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and diabetic cognitive impairment (DCI), but the convergent molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether protein S-palmitoylation serves as a common regulator of microglial neuroinflammation across distinct neurodegenerative diseases etiologies and aimed to identify the key palmitoyltransferase involved. Methods: In vivo ND models (APP/PS1 for AD, MPTP for PD, STZ/high-fat diet for DCI) and in vitro BV2 microglial models stimulated with amyloid-β (Aβ), lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or high glucose (HG) were established. Microglial morphology, inflammatory responses, and the TLR4/MyD88 pathway were assessed by immunofluorescence, RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. Protein palmitoylation levels were evaluated using 2-BP and ABE assays. Palmitoyltransferase expression profiling was performed, and protein-level validation was conducted both in vitro and in vivo. Subsequently, the identified common enzyme, zDHHC11, was knocked down by siRNA to determine its functional role. Results: All three ND models showed robust microglial activation with a pro-inflammatory amoeboid morphology. Aβ, LPS, and HG each upregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines and activated the TLR4/MyD88 pathway in BV2 cells. Palmitoylation inhibition with 2-BP attenuated cytokine production, and all three stimuli increased total protein palmitoylation. Among all palmitoyltransferases screened, zDHHC11 was uniquely and consistently upregulated by all three stimuli. This upregulation was further corroborated at the protein level, with elevated zDHHC11 expression observed both in cultured cells and in brain tissue sections. Knockdown of Zdhhc11 suppressed cytokine expression/secretion and reduced TLR4/MyD88 levels, indicating that zDHHC11 acts upstream of this common pathway. Conclusion: Protein S-palmitoylation mediated by zDHHC11 is a convergent mechanism driving microglial pro-inflammatory activation across distinct ND etiologies. zDHHC11 represents a common regulator of TLR4/MyD88-dependent neuroinflammation and a potential therapeutic target for multiple NDs.

Article.Authors: Ceglarek V.; Czarnabay D.; Fontes G.; Sagae S.; Baldo G.; Blandina P.; Passani M.; Provensi G.; Benetti F.
Article.Abstract: Fear memory can become maladaptive, leading to stress disorders, which represent a significant global health challenge that requires alternative treatment approaches. Oleoylethanolamide (OEA), an endogenous lipid mediator, has demonstrated anxiolytic and pro-cognitive properties to address these conditions. This study investigated the role of OEA in fear memory attenuation and its interaction with hippocampal protein synthesis pathways during memory reconsolidation. Male Wistar rats were trained in a contextual fear conditioning paradigm. Twenty-four hours post-training, memory reactivation was induced through a 10-min context re-exposure, immediately followed by systemic intraperitoneal administration of OEA (1, 5, or 10 mg/kg) or saline. To examine downstream mechanisms, the protein synthesis inhibitor anisomycin or the mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) inhibitor rapamycin was microinfused into the CA1 region of the hippocampus. Freezing behavior was assessed during a retention test conducted 3 h or 24 h later. Systemic OEA at 10 mg/kg facilitated the attenuation of fear memory 24 h post-reactivation, an effect that was dependent on memory reactivation. Intra-CA1 microinfusion of anisomycin blocked the behavioral effects of OEA, while rapamycin did not reliably prevent the behavioral effects of OEA under the present conditions. These results indicate that OEA-mediated memory attenuation requires de novo protein synthesis within the hippocampus, but that the precise involvement of mTORC1 remains unresolved, implicating alternative downstream cascades. Our findings highlight the potential of OEA as a therapeutic target for fear-related disorders and emphasize the need for further research to delineate the specific neural pathways involved.

Article.Title: Dual hypocretin receptor antagonism reduces oxycodone seeking and attenuates aberrant dopamine transporter function during abstinence
Article.Authors: Samson K.; Bashford A.; España R.
Article.Abstract: A major barrier in the treatment of opioid use disorder is persistent drug craving during abstinence. While opioid-based medications have been used to treat opioid use disorder for decades, there is an urgent need for novel, non-opioid-based pharmacotherapies. The hypocretin/orexin (hypocretin) system is a promising target for treating opioid use disorder due to its influence on motivation for drugs of abuse through actions on dopamine transmission. We recently showed that intermittent access to oxycodone promoted sustained oxycodone seeking and alterations in dopamine transmission during abstinence. In the current studies, we investigated to what extent suvorexant, an FDA-approved dual hypocretin receptor antagonist, reduces oxycodone seeking and restores dopamine function during abstinence in female and male Long Evans rats. Treatment with suvorexant 24 h prior to a cue-induced seeking test significantly reduced oxycodone seeking and attenuated aberrant dopamine uptake. These findings suggest that targeting hypocretin receptors could be a promising strategy for reducing opioid craving and associated neuroadaptations, thus lowering the risk of relapse.

Article.Title: Cued unpredictable intermittent access exacerbates loss of control over ethanol drinking
Article.Authors: Mitten E.; Caldwell J.; Zambrano G.; Arce Soto N.; Glover E.
Article.Abstract: Background: Loss of control over drinking is a hallmark feature of alcohol use disorder (AUD) that is modeled preclinically through escalation of ethanol consumption and aversion-resistant drinking. Prior work with other reinforcers suggests that within-session unpredictable, intermittent access (uIntA) promotes these phenotypes. However, the effect of uIntA on voluntary ethanol consumption is unknown. Methods: Male and female Long-Evans rats (n = 9-10/group) underwent seven weeks of daily voluntary ethanol (20% v/v) drinking sessions under either a continuous access (ContA) or uIntA schedule. Following four weeks of baseline, rats were rendered dependent using a two-week chronic intermittent ethanol vapor exposure procedure. Daily testing was maintained through one week into withdrawal from vapor exposure. On the final day of testing, ethanol was adulterated with quinine (30 mg/L) to assess aversion-resistant drinking. Results: Rats drinking under ContA and uIntA exhibited similar levels of average daily ethanol consumption at baseline. However, uIntA elicited a more robust dependence-induced escalation of ethanol consumption compared to ContA, with uIntA sustaining escalation through early withdrawal. Additionally, while rats with ContA to ethanol remained sensitive to quinine even after chronic ethanol vapor exposure, uIntA promoted aversion-resistant drinking in ethanol dependent rats. Conclusions: These results demonstrate that, compared to ContA, uIntA maintains ethanol drinking and exacerbates dependence-induced escalation and aversion-resistant ethanol consumption. This work positions uIntA as a powerful tool to assess psychological and neurobiological factors that may underlie loss of control over drinking.

Article.Title: Activation and increased hippocampal GPR55 prevents cognitive deficits in male APP/PS1 mice
Article.Authors: Liang Y.; Zhi T.; Fan B.; Wu Y.; Wu L.; Xie Z.; YanYang N/A.; Mu R.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive memory loss and cognitive decline. G protein-coupled receptor 55 (GPR55) has been linked to cognitive regulation, yet its precise role in AD pathogenesis remains unclear. Objectives: Here, we investigated the role of GPR55 in AD and its molecular mechanism. Methods: This study utilized APP/PS1 and GPR55 knockout (GPR55KO) mice to investigate the role and possible mechanism of GPR55 in AD. Results: We observed progressive reduction of GPR55 levels in the hippocampus of aging APP/PS1 mice. Conversely, hippocampal GPR55 overexpression rescued cognitive deficits, neuroinflammation, and impairment of synaptic plasticity in APP/PS1 mice. Moreover, GPR55 activation reduced neuronal death and memory impairments in APP/PS1 mice. In addition, aged GPR55KO mice showed cognitive deficits, but hippocampal GPR55 reexpression improved cognition. We also demonstrated that GPR55 activation mitigates Aβ1-42-induced synaptic damage and apoptosis in HT22 cells. Further studies revealed that in both animal and cell models, the levels of P-AKT/AKT and P-GSK3β/GSK3β were significantly decreased, and the level of P-ERK/ERK was markedly increased, while upregulation of GPR55 reversed this trend. Conclusions: These results indicate that hippocampal GPR55 may improve cognitive dysfunction by regulating the AKT/GSK3β and ERK signaling pathways, highlighting its crucial role in AD.

Article.Title: Sex-specific differences in endocannabinoid regulation of cocaine-evoked dopamine in the medial nucleus accumbens shell
Article.Authors: Gaulden A.; Chase K.; McReynolds J.
Article.Abstract: Endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling is a key regulator of reward-related dopaminergic signaling, particularly in response to drugs of abuse, such as cocaine. To date, our understanding of this mechanism has primarily been limited to male subjects. Prior work establishes that female cocaine users have more adverse outcomes, and female rats show greater sensitivity to cannabinoid type 1 receptor (CB1R) regulation of cocaine self-administration. Therefore, we hypothesize that female rats exhibit enhanced eCB regulation of cocaine-evoked dopamine (DA). We used in vivo fiber photometry recording of the dopamine biosensor, dLight 1.3b, in the nucleus accumbens medial shell (NAcms) in response to cocaine in male and female rats. Rats were pretreated with cannabinoid-targeting drugs to investigate the effects of CB1R inactivation or augmentation of the eCB 2-AG on cocaine-evoked DA. Our results revealed that CB1R inactivation attenuates cocaine-evoked DA in male and female rats, but females showed enhanced sensitivity for CB1R regulation of cocaine-evoked DA. Cocaine-evoked DA was enhanced by augmenting 2-AG levels, and females again showed increased sensitivity to this manipulation. Finally, females show greater cocaine-evoked DA when in a non-estrous cycle compared to estrous, reinforcing that estrous cycle is a determinant of cocaine-evoked DA. These data indicate that females show enhanced eCB regulation of cocaine-evoked DA signaling, underscoring the importance of sex as a biological variable in our understanding of endocannabinoid regulation of drug reward.

Article.Title: Inferior olive-selective amplitude suppression and progressive dentato-cortical decoupling during haloperidol-induced parkinsonism: a longitudinal multi-unit activity study
Article.Authors: Zarate-Calderon C.; Chi-Castañeda D.; López-Meraz M.; Beltrán-Parrazal L.; Morgado-Valle C.; García L.
Article.Abstract: Drug-induced parkinsonism (DIP) arises from competitive D2 receptor blockade, yet its cerebellar circuit-level dynamics remain poorly characterized. We recorded multi-unit activity simultaneously from four cerebellar structures (dentate nucleus, Crus II, inferior olive, and lobulus Sim B) across three weekly sessions in male Wistar rats receiving chronic haloperidol (1.5 mg/kg/day, subcutaneous) to characterize structure-specific and longitudinally evolving cerebellar population dynamics. Resting-state discharge amplitude was suppressed only in the inferior olive after FDR correction, where all six amplitude features fell sharply (d = -6, pFDR < 0.001); reductions in the same direction in Sim B were smaller and non-significant (d = -1.24 to -1.38), as was a concurrent increase in discharge rate (Hedges' g = +1.15, 95% CI [-0.07, 2.37]). During spontaneous tremor, all four structures showed elevated population amplitude alongside reduced discharge rate and irregularity, identifying temporally concentrated synchronized discharge rather than generalized hyperactivation as the mesoscopic tremor correlate. Phase coupling diverged anatomically: dentate-Crus II synchronization declined progressively across weeks (slope = -0.024 per week, p = 0.0006, Rm2 = 0.36) while olivocerebellar coupling remained robust and static. Week-1 Crus II activity alone predicted week-3 tremor burden in this single cohort with cross-validated accuracy (rLOO = 0.993, RLOO2 = 0.901, pFDR = 9.0×10-4), and unsupervised clustering revealed progressive neural state reorganization across all structures without behavioral escalation. These findings establish DIP as a longitudinally evolving cerebellar network state driven by pharmacodynamic changes beyond acute D2 occupancy, identifying the inferior olive, the dentate-Crus II axis, and Crus II as mechanistically and anatomically distinct nodes for future pharmacological and translational investigation.

Article.Title: M3 muscarinic receptor antagonism attenuates cocaine-induced hippocampal oligodendroglial changes and relapse-like behavior in male mice
Article.Authors: Yamada J.; Maeda S.; Okamura A.; Iinuma K.; Jinno S.
Article.Abstract: Acetylcholine (ACh) signaling regulates oligodendrocyte lineage progression via muscarinic ACh receptors (mAChRs), yet its role in cocaine-induced myelin-associated and relapse-like changes remains unexplored. Here, we examined whether hippocampal cholinergic and oligodendroglial alterations were associated with cocaine-related outcomes and pharmacologically sensitive to M3-preferential antagonism. Adult male C57BL/6J mice were subjected to cocaine-conditioned place preference (CPP), extinction, and cocaine-primed reinstatement, and treated with benztropine (BZT), the M1-selective mAChR antagonist VU0255035, or the M3-preferential mAChR antagonist solifenacin (SOL). Cocaine conditioning increased dorsal hippocampal ACh levels and reduced the expression of selected myelin-related genes and oligodendroglial transcription factors, including Mbp, Plp, Olig2, and Olig1, predominantly in the dorsal hippocampus. These changes were accompanied by reduced myelin basic protein (MBP) immunoreactivity, increased cholinergic terminal apposition to oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, and upregulation of Chrm3 in O4-sorted hippocampal oligodendrocytes. BZT reduced cocaine-primed reinstatement and increased Mbp and Plp expression and MBP immunoreactivity in several hippocampal layers. BZT also normalized cocaine-induced changes in Fosb, ΔFosb, Creb, and Slc6a3 in the dorsal hippocampus, whereas dorsal Bdnf remained different from vehicle-treated controls. SOL reduced reinstatement relative to both cocaine-conditioned and VU0255035-treated mice. SOL also increased open-arm time and entry ratio in the elevated plus maze test relative to cocaine-conditioned mice. In CD140a-sorted oligodendrocyte precursor cell-derived cultures, SOL increased MBP-positive oligodendrocyte volume relative to cocaine alone; however, the lack of a SOL-VU0255035 difference precluded conclusions about subtype specificity. These findings provide evidence consistent with a contribution of M3-sensitive muscarinic mechanisms to cocaine-associated oligodendroglial and behavioral alterations.
