Article.Title: Individualized Theta Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation Modulates Mnemonic Discrimination and ERP Responses to Positive Information in Individuals With Elevated Depressive Symptoms
Article.Authors: Huang X.; Zhou M.; Wang C.; Huang Y.; Wang W.; Shao J.; Mao J.; Li J.; Zhang L.; Ye R.; Zhu C.; Tian Y.; He K.; Yu F.; Wang K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Individuals with elevated depressive symptoms often show impairments in positive memory processing. This randomized, double-blind study investigated whether individualized theta-frequency transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) using an OFC-oriented montage modulates mnemonic discrimination and ERP responses to positive information. Sixty-one individuals with elevated depressive symptoms received either real or sham stimulation before completing an emotional mnemonic discrimination task. Behavioral results showed that lure discrimination increased following real stimulation but not sham stimulation. EEG results showed that real stimulation modulated ERP responses during positive memory encoding and retrieval, as reflected by increased late positive potential (LPP) amplitudes during encoding and altered early retrieval-related ERP amplitudes. These findings suggest that individualized theta-tACS may influence both mnemonic discrimination performance and neural responses to positive information.

Article.Title: Impaired Neural Pattern Separation During Implicit Emotion Regulation in PTSD: An MVPA fMRI Study
Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Zhang Y.; Poletti S.; Zhang Z.; Liu S.; Hu J.; Xiong Q.; Yu P.; Ren Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Implicit emotion regulation (IER) operates automatically and supports adaptive social–affective functioning. Although PTSD involves marked IER disturbances, the large-scale functional connectivity architecture supporting implicit emotional processing remains unclear. The Shifted Attention Emotion Appraisal Task (SEAT) offers an ecologically relevant framework for probing these processes. One hundred twenty-three adults (PTSD: n = 78; trauma-exposed controls: n = 45) completed fMRI during SEAT. Whole-brain functional connectivity multivariate pattern analysis (fc-MVPA) identified data-driven, condition-specific connectivity patterns distinguishing groups. MVPA-derived clusters were further assessed using seed-based and ROI-to-ROI analyses. fc-MVPA revealed three frontal-anchored connectivity patterns spanning frontoparietal, salience, and executive networks. Seed-based analyses centered on the right frontal pole showed increased coupling with posterior default mode and visual regions and reduced connectivity with frontal control systems. Dysconnectivity varied across regulatory stages, including frontal–occipital hyperconnectivity during threat-related attention shifts and frontal–midline hypoconnectivity during neutral appraisal. Greater re-experiencing severity was nominally associated with reduced multivariate network strength during implicit processing and appraisal; however, these associations did not survive correction for multiple comparisons and should be considered exploratory. Implicit regulation deficits in PTSD reflect distributed network dysfunction rather than localized abnormalities. Disrupted coordination among control, perceptual, and self-referential systems may limit flexible emotional responses. Integrating SEAT with fc-MVPA identifies connectivity patterns relevant to maladaptive emotional processing and advances network-level models of dysregulation in PTSD.

Article.Title: The gentle grip of beauty: Neural bases of motor inhibition during aesthetic appreciation
Article.Authors: Barbieri P.; Frascaroli J.; Varesio G.; Piovesan F.; Bechis L.; Sarasso P.; Ronga I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A century-old tradition characterizes aesthetic experiences as intense contemplative moments in which we suspend practical concerns and devote our full attention to the object at hand. In line with this tradition, recent theories suggest that aesthetic experiences involve heightened sensory processing accompanied by a suppression of motor activity. Yet, while the link between aesthetic appreciation and perceptual enhancement has received considerable attention, the role of motor inhibition remains largely unexplored. The present study addressed this gap by investigating whether the aesthetic appreciation of images can modulate behavioral and electrophysiological markers of motor inhibition. In Experiment 1, significantly slower reaction times following the observation of preferred images were found. In Experiment 2, EEG responses associated with motor preparation and execution were significantly reduced in trials involving preferred compared with non-preferred images. Time-frequency analysis revealed significantly decreased alpha power (associated with attentional engagement toward visual perception) and increased beta power (associated with inhibited motor preparation) for preferred than non-preferred images. Overall, our results provide new evidence for the existence of a relationship between aesthetic appreciation and motor inhibition and position aesthetic experience as a valuable case study for exploring the adaptive coordination of sensory and motor systems in response to environmental demands.

Article.Title: Positive interactions and active mentalizing facilitate inter-brain synchronization in couples
Article.Authors: Schneider I.; Moreau Q.; Neudecker D.; Herpertz S.; Dumas G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-quality interactions rely on socio-cognitive abilities, which help partners understand and respond to one another. Hyperscanning, which measures brain activity in multiple individuals simultaneously, can examine inter-brain synchronization as a possible signature of social coordination. In this study, we explore this synchronization during natural, everyday interactions in romantic couples. Forty-two dyads participated in a naturalistic behavioral paradigm while EEG was recorded. We measured behavioral dyadic reciprocity and negative states, and computed inter-brain synchronization using the circular correlation coefficient (CCorr) across multiple frequency bands (Theta [4-8 Hz], Alpha [8-13 Hz], and Beta [14-31 Hz]). Positive interactions elicited greater dyadic reciprocity and fewer negative states compared to negative interactions. At the neural level, inter-brain synchronization in the beta band was significantly higher during positive compared to negative interactions. Mentalizing compared to counting elicited increased inter-brain synchronization in both alpha and beta bands, indicating that active sociocognitive processing enhances neural alignment between partners. These findings demonstrate that inter-brain dynamics provide a neural signature of both interaction valence and mentalizing engagement during real-world social interactions, putting forward inter-brain synchronization as a sensitive marker of sociocognitive coordination.

Article.Title: Prevalence of 406 rare diseases by ethnicity and recorded COVID-19 infection rates among 62.5 million people in England
Article.Authors: Gu Q.; Hasheminasab S.; Pineda-Moncusí M.; Chilala C.; Thygesen J.; Wu H.; Khalid S.; N/A N/A.; Coombe A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rare diseases (RD) are individually uncommon but collectively affect millions of people. Yet national estimates of their prevalence, especially across ethnic groups, are limited, and how the COVID-19 pandemic affected people with RD across ethnic groups is unknown. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of 406 RD by ethnicity, and to describe recorded COVID-19 infection across these RD and ethnic groups, in England. We conducted a cross-sectional study within the National Health Service (NHS) England Secure Data Environment, accessed via the British Heart Foundation (BHF) Data Science Centre’s CVD-COVID-UK/COVID-IMPACT Consortium, linking primary care, hospital, and mortality records for individuals alive on 31 July 2023. We calculated age- and sex-standardised prevalence for 406 RD, and recorded COVID-19 infection rates for the overall group, for each RD, and across the six-group Office for National Statistics (ONS) and 19-group NHS ethnicity classifications. Of 62.5 million people, 1.05 million (1.7%) had at least one of the 406 RD. Recorded COVID-19 infection was higher in the RD group than in the non-RD population (32.8% vs. 29.0%). Within the RD group, infection rates varied by ethnicity (e.g. 27.7% in the Pakistani and 23.8% in the Black African groups, versus 33.7% in the White British group) and by specific RD (24.6–41.2% among the 25 most common). Age- and sex-standardised prevalence also varied widely across ethnic groups, with substantial heterogeneity emerging only when broad categories were disaggregated into the more granular NHS classifications (for example, markedly elevated discoid lupus erythematosus prevalence in Black Caribbean but not Black African individuals, obscured within the aggregate “Black” category). This national, ethnicity-resolved map shows that rare-disease prevalence varies substantially across ethnic groups, with differences largely hidden within broad categories, and that recorded COVID-19 infection among people with RD varied across ethnic groups, with the highest rates observed in the ONS White and NHS White British groups. These findings provide a baseline to support earlier, fairer diagnosis and more targeted care.

Article.Title: Adaptive entropy-guided access point selection for robust multi-floor Wi-Fi fingerprinting
Article.Authors: Bahy El-Din A.; Nafea H.; Samra A.; Abozied M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wi-Fi fingerprinting is widely used for indoor localization. Although a large number of observable access points (APs) can provide richer spatial information, retaining all APs introduces significant computational overhead, increased scanning latency, and reduced generalization under heterogeneity across floors, devices, and contexts. This paper presents an entropy-guided dimensionality reduction framework that selects the most informative APs while preserving localization accuracy. First, each AP is ranked using Shannon entropy computed from its empirical RSSI distribution. The approach is evaluated on the multi-floor JUIndoorLoc dataset (172 AP features, three floors, four devices, and multiple contextual conditions) using a Random Forest classifier with stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and robustness is further assessed under additive RSSI noise and random AP dropouts. Across floors, the proposed adaptive entropy selection achieves substantial dimensionality reduction with negligible accuracy loss: it selects 17 APs on F3 ( $$\approx $$ 90.11% reduction) with only $$-0.41\%$$ accuracy change, 8 APs on F4 ( $$\approx $$ 95.34% reduction) with $$-0.51\%$$ change, and 26 APs on F5 ( $$\approx $$ 84.88% reduction) with $$-0.42\%$$ accuracy loss compared to the baseline configuration using all APs. Robustness experiments show that entropy-based selection can improve resilience under measurement noise on certain floors (e.g., on F5, at $$\sigma $$ =1–3 dB the selected subset achieves 0.8472/0.7748/0.7070 versus 0.7674/0.7084/0.6659 for using all APs), while also revealing floor-dependent trade-offs where extremely compact subsets may become more noise-sensitive under strong perturbations. Overall, the proposed adaptive entropy framework provides a lightweight, floor-aware AP selection mechanism that reduces inference cost and scanning burden while maintaining competitive accuracy and improving robustness in realistic degradation scenarios. The generalizability of these findings to more complex and dynamic real-world environments warrants further investigation.

Article.Title: Psychological (in)flexibility as a mediator between resilience and psychological outcomes in patients with cancer
Article.Authors: Sauer C.; Sajjad T.; Zinndorf L.; Weißflog G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Resilience and psychological flexibility are protective factors for mental health and well-being in the general population as well as in patients with cancer. Additionally, psychological inflexibility is a risk factor for poor wellbeing and psychopathology. Research suggests that psychological flexibility constitutes a resilience factor and mediates the association between resilience and psychological outcomes across various contexts. However, there is only sparse evidence regarding the mediating role of psychological inflexibility and flexibility processes in the relationship between resilience and psychological outcomes in patients with a chronic health condition. This study examined psychological inflexibility and flexibility processes as mediators of the relationship between resilience and psychological outcomes in patients with cancer. A total of N = 222 patients completed an online survey assessing resilience (Resilience Scale-11), psychological inflexibility (Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-2), distress (National Cancer Center Network distress thermometer), depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-8), anxiety (General Anxiety Disorder-7), and mental health-related quality of life (Short Form Health Survey-12). Across all bootstrapped mediation models, psychological inflexibility mediated the relationship between resilience and all psychological outcomes. Secondary analyses of acceptance of versus struggle with illness and value-based living versus obstruction showed partial mediation, with distinct patterns of association for each process. Our findings highlight psychological (in)flexibility as a key mediator between resilience and psychological outcomes in cancer patients. Obstruction showed the strongest association, suggesting that ACT-based interventions targeting psychological barriers may be particularly effective in enhancing resilience and mental health.

Article.Title: An innovative framework for student adaptability prediction using discriminant-based classification, feature selection, and sensitivity analysis
Article.Authors: Mao L.; Alkayid K.; Shreenidhi H.; Mostafa S.; MGM J.; Parhi M.; Wasson V.; Mohammed M.; Ansari G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurately predicting student adaptability is essential for enhancing academic performance and personal development. The present study presents a classification-based approach utilizing Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) to predict student adaptability. To enhance model performance, the Turbulent Flow of Water-based Optimization (TFWO) and Giant Armadillo Optimization (GAO) algorithms are employed. The dataset, consisting of 1,205 student records with demographic, educational, and socio-economic attributes, is split into training and test sets. The two best-performing hybrid models undergo a sensitivity analysis using the FAST approach. Experimental results demonstrate that the QDA model optimized with GAO (QDGO) achieves the highest classification accuracy of 0.975, outperforming other model configurations. These findings underscore the potential of optimized classification models in student adaptability prediction, providing valuable insights for educational institutions. Future studies can explore additional hybrid models and larger datasets to further refine predictive accuracy.

Article.Title: Computational DFT and docking investigation of isoproterenol delivery using Al₁₂N₁₂ and Al₁₂O₁₂ inorganic nanocarriers
Article.Authors: Al Omari R.; saraswat S.; Abosaoda M.; Rekha M.; Ray S.; Chennakesavulu K.; Sharma R.; Kashyap A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The development of efficient nanocarriers for catecholamine drugs remains a critical challenge in cardiovascular therapeutics. This study presents the first comprehensive computational investigation of aluminum-based nanoclusters (Al₁₂N₁₂ and Al₁₂O₁₂) as drug delivery vehicles for Isoproterenol, a synthetic catecholamine used in managing bradycardia, heart block, and cardiac arrest. Using density functional theory (DFT) at the B3LYP/6-311 + G(d) level, the adsorption of Isoproterenol onto these nanoclusters was systematically evaluated through geometric, electronic, and spectroscopic analyses. The calculated binding energies ranged from ‒29 to ‒33 kcal/mol for Isoproterenol/Al₁₂N₁₂ complexes and from ‒61 to ‒88 kcal/mol for Isoproterenol/Al₁₂O₁₂ complexes in gas phase, and ranged from ‒25 to ‒28 kcal/mol for Isoproterenol/Al₁₂N₁₂ complexes and from ‒54 to ‒75 kcal/mol for Isoproterenol/Al₁₂O₁₂ complexes in water phase, suggesting favorable adsorption interactions, with Al₁₂O₁₂ exhibiting stronger interactions due to the higher electronegativity of oxygen. A substantial increase in dipole moment upon complexation suggests which may contribute to improved aqueous solubility and potentially facilitate cellular uptake, favorable attributes for drug delivery applications. Molecular docking against the β₁-adrenergic receptor (β₁AR) revealed that the Isoproterenol/nanocluster complexes achieved docking scores of‒15.98 and ‒16.56 kcal/mol for Al₁₂N₁₂ and Al₁₂O₁₂ complexes, respectively, markedly superior to free Isoproterenol (‒7.41 kcal/mol). Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations at 300 K further supported the thermal and structural stability of the most stable Isoproterenol/Al₁₂N₁₂ and Isoproterenol/Al₁₂O₁₂ complexes under the simulated conditions, with no apparent dissociation or major structural distortion during the 10 ps trajectories. These findings suggest Al₁₂N₁₂ and Al₁₂O₁₂ nanoclusters as promising, previously unexplored carriers for Isoproterenol, offering a foundation for experimental validation and future development of inorganic nanocarrier-based delivery systems for cardiovascular drugs.

Article.Title: Interfacial control and evaporation pinning of nanocapillary filling from ambient to serpentinization temperatures
Article.Authors: Cihan A.; Gilbert B.; Bhuvankar P.; Hu M.; Steefel C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fluid transport in nanometer-scale channels underlies nanofluidic technologies and geological systems, yet measured capillary filling rates in hydrophilic channels are often far slower than classical theory predicts. Here we show, using a coupled flow model based on classical density functional theory combining hydrodynamics, electrokinetics and capillarity, that electrokinetic resistance and locally elevated viscosity near the channel walls jointly suppress flow, capturing the measured slowdown across independent experiments. At higher temperatures relevant to serpentinization (around 200 degrees Celsius), the model predicts a regime of evaporation-driven pinning: once relative humidity falls below saturation, classical capillary scaling breaks down and evaporation, orders of magnitude faster than at ambient conditions, balances capillary inflow and pins the meniscus inside the channel. Depending on wettability, humidity and channel length, transport may continue through thin liquid films and vapor migration. These predictions await experimental testing but identify a high-temperature flow regime, to our knowledge not previously described in nanochannels, relevant to nanodevice design, subsurface fluid modeling, and geologic hydrogen generation.

Article.Title: Occupational anxiety, workplace risk attitudes, and clinical learning safety climate among nursing students: a path analysis
Article.Authors: Kızıltan B.; Ağar A.; Berşe S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Occupational anxiety may influence nursing students’ engagement with workplace risks and shape how they perceive safety within clinical learning environments. Understanding these relationships may help inform curricular and placement-based strategies that support both student learning and patient safety. This analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 591 undergraduate nursing students at Gaziantep University, Türkiye, between April and June 2025. Data were collected using the occupational anxiety scale for healthcare students (OAS-HS), the nurses’ attitudes toward workplace risks scale (NATWRS), and the safety climate questionnaire (SCQ). Internal consistency was high for the three total scales (Cronbach’s α = 0.94–0.97). Independent-samples t tests and one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni correction were used to examine group differences (Welch and Games–Howell procedures where variances were heterogeneous). Path analysis was performed using AMOS 29.0 to model associations among occupational anxiety, attitudes toward workplace risks, and perceptions of the clinical learning safety climate. Participants reported moderate-to-high occupational anxiety (69.6 ± 17.3), generally positive attitudes toward workplace risks (144.5 ± 22.5), and moderately favorable perceptions of the clinical learning safety climate (71.9 ± 11.3). Occupational anxiety was significantly higher among female students, Turkish students, and those with a grade point average of 2.00 or above (all p < 0.001). More positive attitudes toward workplace risks were observed among male students and international students ( p = 0.029 and p = 0.011, respectively). Students who reported no trust in healthcare institutions or inadequate knowledge of occupational risks had higher anxiety and less favorable safety climate perceptions ( p < 0.001). In the path model, more positive attitudes toward workplace risks were associated with more favorable safety climate perceptions (standardized β = 0.52, p < 0.001), explaining 27% of the variance. Occupational anxiety was not significantly associated with safety climate perceptions, either directly (β < 0.001, p = 0.997) or indirectly through attitudes toward workplace risks. Nursing students’ perceptions of safety in clinical learning environments appear to be more closely related to their attitudes toward workplace risks than to their occupational anxiety. Educational strategies that strengthen risk management content, improve the quality and psychological safety of clinical placements, and support professional motivation may help foster a more positive safety climate. Additional support may be warranted for student subgroups reporting higher anxiety or less favorable risk attitudes.

Article.Title: Hydrogel application as a soil amendment to mitigate water deficiency effects on flaxseed cultivars grown in sandy soils
Article.Authors: Bakry A.; Abdelaal H.; Nowar M.; Sadak M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water scarcity is a major constraint for flax production in Egypt’s sandy soils. This research aims to investigate the use of hydrogels, as water-absorbing polymers can enhance soil moisture retention and improve crop performance under water deficit conditions, thereby increasing flax yield and seed quality. Two field experiments were conducted during the 2022/2023 and 2023/2024 winter seasons at the National Research Centre, Al Nubaria, Egypt, to evaluate the effects of hydrogel (0 and 80 kg/ha) on three flax cultivars (Giza-11, Giza-12, Sakha-3) under full water irrigation quantity (100%WIQ) and deficit water irrigation quantity (75%WIQ). Showed that Giza-12 variety outperformed the other varieties in growth, yield, and seed quality under all conditions. On the other hand, water deficit significantly reduced growth, photosynthetic pigments, indole acetic acid, yield, and seed nutritional components (oil, protein, carbohydrates). While hydrogel application mitigated these effects, enhancing growth, yield, compatible solutes (proline, soluble sugars, soluble nitrogen), and leaf phenolics. Specifically, full irrigation using hydrogel application, increased seed yield and oil yield by 45.0% and 59.5% for Giza-11, and 8.8% and 12.8% for Sakha-3. Under water stress using hydrogel application, the respective increases were 44.0% and 42.9%, 28.2% and 36.7%, and 37.0% and 42.9%. These findings indicate that hydrogel application is a practical strategy to enhance flax productivity and seed quality under water deficit conditions.

Article.Title: A transformer-enhanced U-Net with FiLM-driven clinical conditioning for multi-task breast ultrasound lesion analysis
Article.Authors: James B.; Krishnamoorthy N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Early and accurate detection of breast lesions using non-invasive imaging techniques is crucial for improving timely diagnosis, treatment outcomes, and patient prognosis. This study aims to develop and evaluate hybrid deep learning models for breast-lesion segmentation and classification in ultrasound images using patient-level cross-validation. Challenges such as low contrast, imaging artifacts, and irregular lesion morphology can limit accurate diagnosis, highlighting the need for advanced deep learning approaches for reliable breast-lesion analysis. Recent developments in deep learning, particularly hybrid architectures that combine convolutional and transformer representations, have shown promise in addressing these constraints. We present three Hybrid Deep Learning (HDL) models. Three complementary deep learning models were evaluated for breast lesion classification and segmentation using the Breast-Lesions-USG dataset. Model 1 employed DoubleHeadUNet with a ResNet-34 backbone, Model 2 combined a Swin V2 Transformer with a U-Net decoder, and Model 3 integrated a Hybrid Transformer-FiLM U-Net to incorporate clinical metadata. Patient-level five-fold cross-validation with strict patient separation and nested hyperparameter selection was employed. Model 1 achieved the highest accuracy (82.94%) and AUC (87.70%), while Model 3 demonstrated the highest malignant recall (81.63%) and strongest segmentation performance (Dice: 0.901; IoU: 0.825). Model 2 achieved an accuracy of 79.76% and an AUC of 87.54%. Statistical analysis indicated that most accuracy differences were not significant, supporting the complementary strengths of the three models rather than identifying a universally superior approach. Comparisons with previous studies were considered indicative due to differences in datasets and evaluation protocols.

Article.Title: Architecture diverse TabNet ensemble for crop type classification using harmonized multisource soil data
Article.Authors: Buriboev A.; Abror A.; Narzullo M.; Fayzullo N.; Yusuf Y.; Buriboyev S.; Bazarbaev M.; Abduvaytov A.; Achilov G.; Kuvandikov J.; Indiaminov R.; Jeon H.; Lee C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate analysis of heterogeneous soil records can support data-driven agricultural planning, but integrating datasets from different laboratories and public repositories introduces challenges related to inconsistent units, source-dependent distributions, missing values, duplicate observations, and potential information leakage. This study proposes ADWTabNet, an architecture-diverse TabNet ensemble for multiclass crop-type classification using harmonized multi-source soil data. The integrated dataset contained 18,237 observations representing seven crop classes and a broad set of chemical, physical, microbiological, and categorical soil properties. The proposed framework combines unit standardization, duplicate control, source-distribution harmonization, separate categorical and numerical imputation, tree-structured Parzen estimator-based hyperparameter optimization, structurally diverse TabNet models, probability-level ensemble fusion, calibration assessment, and attention-based interpretation. Under the evaluated stratified holdout protocol, XGBoost achieved a test accuracy of 0.8724 and a macro F1-score of 0.8670. Baseline TabNet improved these values to 0.8863 and 0.8822, respectively, while the TPE-optimized TabNet reached an accuracy of 0.8951 and reduced log loss from 0.3325 to 0.2566. The proposed ADWTabNet ensemble obtained the best reported performance, with a test accuracy of 0.9053, macro F1-score of 0.9025, weighted F1-score of 0.9050, macro ROC–AUC of 0.9930, and normalized multiclass Brier score of 0.0193. Repeated-run evaluation confirmed a stable advantage over the optimized individual TabNet, whereas the difference between validation-weighted and equal architecture-diverse averaging was not statistically significant. Aggregated TabNet attention ranked humus, phosphorus, electrical conductivity, nitrogen, and pH among the leading predictors, and this ranking was independently supported by permutation-importance analysis. These findings demonstrate improved crop-type classification within the evaluated integrated multi-source dataset. However, external validation using previously unseen laboratories and geographic regions is required before broader transferability can be established.

Article.Title: Investigation of the dosimetric characteristics of real-time silicone/Bi2O3 nanocomposites for the diagnostic level X-rays
Article.Authors: Keyvani F.; Gholamzadeh L.; Malekie S.; Kashian S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents the development of high-sensitivity real-time X-ray dosimeters based on room-temperature-vulcanized (RTV-2) silicone nanocomposites incorporating 0–60 wt% Bi 2 O 3 nanoparticles, fabricated via solution casting. Structural and morphological characterization using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) with elemental mapping, and elemental analysis confirmed the uniform dispersion of monoclinic Bi 2 O 3 nanorods within the amorphous RTV-2 matrix. Complementary Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) validated the chemical integrity, thermal stability, and mechanical robustness of the resulting nanocomposites. Dosimetric performance was investigated under diagnostic-range X-ray exposure using a COMET MXR 320/26 source (dose rates: 2.8–12 mGy/min). The I-V characteristics at 4.8 mGy/min exhibited a highly linear response over ± 400 V. At 400 V, the photocurrent increased from ~ 0.56 nA (pure RTV-2) to ~ 1.66 nA (60 wt% Bi 2 O 3 ), corresponding to a ~ 3-fold enhancement in photocurrent. The devices demonstrated good short-term repeatability (standard deviation of 2.3% over ten consecutive measurements) and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of up to ~ 1900 at 400 V. Compared with reported values for commercial MOSFET dosimeters (~ 0.1–1 nA/mGy) and previously reported Bi 2 O 3 -polymer systems, the developed nanocomposites exhibit a higher competitive normalized sensitivity (~ 0.35 nA/(mGy/min), or 878 nC·mGy⁻ 1 ·cm⁻ 3 on a volumetric basis), demonstrating their suitability as lead-free alternatives for low-dose, real-time diagnostic X-ray dosimetry; further evaluation of long-term stability and mechanical durability is needed to establish clinical applicability.

Article.Title: Age modifies the association between body composition and S1P levels in the study of health in pomerania
Article.Authors: Bibi S.; Naeem M.; Bahls M.; Groß S.; Dörr M.; Friedrich N.; Nauck M.; Lieb W.; Schwedhelm E.; Oetjen E.; Rauch B.; Gräler M.; Wielpütz M.; Völzke H.; Markus M.; Ittermann T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate whether age modifies the associations between body composition markers and sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) levels in the Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP) cohort. Among 4,080 participants (2,275 women, 51.4%), we examined age-specific associations of anthropometric (BMI, waist circumference, waist-to-height ratio) and MRI-derived (visceral and subcutaneous adipose tissue, liver fat) body-composition markers with S1P. Sex-stratified linear regression models, including interaction terms with age, were used. Overall, no significant body composition–S1P associations were found without accounting for age interactions. However, age significantly modified these associations: all body composition markers were positively associated with S1P at younger ages (20–30 years), weakened, became non-significant around midlife (35–50 years), and reversed in older adults (≥ 55 years). For example, at younger ages, BMI was positively associated with S1P—men: β = 0.029 (95% CI: 0.008 to 0.050); women: β = 0.025 (95% CI: 0.008 to 0.042), but negatively associated at older ages—men: β = −0.037 (95% CI: −0.056 to − 0.018); women: β = −0.022 (95% CI: −0.037 to − 0.006). Similar age-dependent patterns were observed for others markers. Our findings highlight that age substantially modifies the associations between body composition markers and S1P, underlining the importance of considering age in understanding metabolic risk.

Article.Title: Chemical profiling and multitarget computational screening reveal bioactive phytochemical scaffolds from Echiochilon pauciflorum stocks ex wight
Article.Authors: Nandaniya N.; Mehta D.; Dudhagara D.; Gamit S.; Pandya H.; Parmar R.; Thakar M.; Chaun D.; Naghera N.; Sindhav G.; Kapuriya N.; Ambasana M.; Vyas S.
Article.Abstract: Echiochilon pauciflorum (Boraginaceae) is an underexplored coastal medicinal plant. We combined GC–MS profiling, multitarget docking, ADMET prediction and cytotoxicity testing to prioritize its constituents. GC–MS analysis of aqueous, methanolic and ethanolic extracts and a hexane-trapped volatile fraction gave 271 peaks; after contaminant screening and grading of library matches, 44 compounds were tentatively identified as plausible plant metabolites, dominated by lupane- and oleanane-type triterpenoids, C13-norisoprenoids, phytosterols and Boraginaceae-type pyrrolizidine alkaloids. These compounds, together with those attributed to the species in the BIMP database (185 ligands in total), were docked against estrogen receptor α, progesterone receptor, EGFR, ALK and PARP1, and scores were ranked within each target. Four ligands, sitogluside, β-sitosterol and two spiro-bisnaphthalenes, ranked within the top 10% at two or more targets. In MTT assays (24 h), both extracts were weakly cytotoxic to A549 lung cancer cells (IC₅₀ > 1000 and 699 µg/mL), whereas HEK293 cells were more sensitive (IC₅₀ 48.1 and 36.4 µg/mL); the crude extracts were therefore not cancer-selective. The study provides a tentative chemical profile of E. pauciflorum and prioritized scaffolds for isolation and target-based testing.

Article.Title: F2D-RetinaNet: a feature-to-decision dual-path network with fractional operators for retinal disease detection and grading
Article.Authors: Delu M.; Harjule P.; Kumar R.; Gajjar K.; Nkomozepi P.
Article.Abstract: Visible pathological abnormalities and vascular integrity help diagnose retinal diseases. This paper introduces a unified feature-to-decision framework that first extracts vasculature and enhances lesions. First, this study proposes the fractional anisotropic diffusion–based hybrid enhancement (FADHE) method that selectively amplifies lesion contrast and vessel visibility in the green channel using long-memory fractional diffusion dynamics. Second, this study introduces a fractional Hessian-based attention U-Net (FHAU-Net), a multi-scale vessel segmentation model that leverages fractional Hessian responses across eight fractional orders and attention-guided skip connections to capture fine vessel structures. Finally, this work designs a dual-branch disease grading model, F2D-RetinaNet, which jointly processes the enhanced image and vessel map to learn lesion-related and vascular feature representations for the recognition and grading of retinal diseases. The FHAU-Net model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.8987, a sensitivity of 0.9084, an accuracy of 0.9804, and a specificity of 0.9876 across the unified test set, which contains variations in resolution, acquisition site, camera type, and imaging conditions. The F2D-RetinaNet is evaluated for Diabetic retinopathy (DR) detection, DR grading, and multiclass retinal disease classification tasks. Extensive testing and comparisons to the baseline procedures support the reliability of the proposed methodology on the datasets evaluated here.

Article.Title: A quantitative geophysical–geotechnical framework for slope stability analysis using electrical resistivity tomography
Article.Authors: Widodo N/A.; Panjaya H.; Prassetyo S.; Simangunsong G.; Wattimena R.; Widayat A.; Fatkhan N/A.; Nur T.; Fonna S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Slope instability constitutes a major constraint on infrastructure development in geologically complex and rapidly urbanizing regions such as West Java, Indonesia. Reliable slope stability analysis requires spatial characterization of subsurface mechanical parameters, including cohesion, internal friction angle, and bulk density. Conventional geotechnical investigations provide accurate point-scale data but are often constrained by high cost, limited spatial coverage, and logistical challenges. This study presents an integrated geoelectrical–geotechnical framework enabling the quantitative use of electrical resistivity for slope stability assessment. The investigation was conducted in the Padalarang District, West Bandung Regency, an area dominated by volcanic lithologies. Electrical Resistivity Tomography and Vertical Electrical Sounding were integrated with borehole logs, Standard Penetration Test data, and laboratory measurements to derive empirical correlations between resistivity and key geotechnical parameters. The results indicate a very strong correlation between electrical resistivity (ρ) and cohesion (R 2 = 0.8270), a strong correlation with bulk density (ρᵦ) (R 2 = 0.6860), and a weak correlation with internal friction angle (R 2 = 0.1780). The resistivity-derived parameters were incorporated into limit-equilibrium slope stability analysis under the specified groundwater condition. The representative resistivity-derived parameter model produced a Factor of Safety (FoS) of 2.60, while the final spatially integrated slope model yielded a minimum FoS of 1.23. These results demonstrate that electrical resistivity can provide spatially continuous, site-specific geotechnical information for preliminary slope stability assessment when calibrated and constrained by borehole and laboratory data.

Article.Title: Adaptive storage optimization for deep learning workloads in converged HPC-cloud environments: a reinforcement learning approach
Article.Authors: Baghdasaryan H.; Astsatryan H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Storage systems remain a significant bottleneck in large-scale deep learning training. Most evaluation studies rely on synthetic benchmarks that do not capture the I/O heterogeneity present in real training pipelines. Automated configuration methods often treat parameter selection as stateless, overlooking the temporal structure of recurring training phases. These challenges are addressed using a converged HPC-cloud platform that integrates Lustre with S3-compatible object storage. Three workloads with distinct I/O characteristics were evaluated: ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1K, 3D U-Net on the Medical Segmentation Decathlon, and Whisper Large on LibriSpeech. Time-to-convergence was used as the primary metric. We introduced a deep reinforcement learning framework that combines Proximal Policy Optimization and Soft Actor-Critic with a Transformer-based state encoder to predict workload phase transitions rather than merely respond to them. The learned policies reduced checkpoint write latency by up to 74.6% and improved GPU utilization across all three workloads. The approach generalizes across heterogeneous I/O profiles without per-workload reconfiguration. The results indicate that temporally aware storage control can improve the efficiency of distributed training pipelines in heterogeneous HPC-cloud environments.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Advanced Data Storage Technologies; Computer Science > Information Systems > Cloud Computing and Resource Management; Computer Science > Hardware and Architecture > Parallel Computing and Optimization Techniques

Article.Title: Food insecurity and its associated factors among lactating mothers in Ankesha Guagusa Woreda, Northwest Ethiopia: a community-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Wondale M.; Tiruneh B.; Mekonen H.; Aniley Z.; Negesse A.
Article.Abstract: Food insecurity is defined as the limited or uncertain availability of nutritious, adequate, and safe food, as well as a constrained potential to obtain suitable foods in socially acceptable manners. Food insecurity leads to both macro/micronutrient deficiency, making lactating women more vulnerable to inadequate human milk production and malnutrition during their optimal lactation period. However, data on the prevalence and associated factors that contribute to food insecurity are sparse within this specific population, where food insecurity might also be worsened in relatively highland areas. Thus, this study aimed to assess the prevalence of food insecurity and its associated factors among lactating mothers in Ankesha Guagusa Woreda, Awi Zone, Northwest Ethiopia. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted from July 1 to August 30, 2025, in Ankesha Guagusa Woreda. The data were collected by a pretested structured questionnaire. The single-population proportion formula was used to estimate sample size. The final sample size was 464. To assess the food insecurity status of mothers, an eight-item Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES) was considered. Data were cleaned, coded and entered into EpiData version 4.6 and then exported to SPSS Version 25 for analysis. Both bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify associated factors of food insecurity. The prevalence of food insecurity among lactating mothers was 70.9%. Mothers residing in rural areas (AOR = 1.97; 95% CI 1.2, 3.2), mothers experiencing an illness (AOR = 1.72; 95% CI 1.11, 2.68) and mothers who did not consume Vitamin A-rich vegetables, roots, or tubers (AOR = 1.99; 95% CI 1.06, 3.73) had higher odds of food insecurity. Conversely, meal frequency (> 3 meals) (AOR = 0.34, 95% CI 0.14, 0.76) and consuming milk and milk products (AOR = 0.5, 95% CI 0.3, 0.9) were inversely associated with food insecurity. The prevalence of food insecurity among lactating mothers was high in the study area. Therefore, to optimize food security, resources must prioritize remote rural kebeles during lean cycles while health extension workers screen for maternal illnesses during postnatal visits. Additionally, establishing community-based dairy cooperatives and supporting Vitamin A-rich home gardens will directly enhance nutrition and lower food access barriers for vulnerable, lactating households.
Article.Topic: Food Security and Health in Diverse Populations

Article.Title: Antimicrobial resistance profiles and antibiotic resistance gene detection in environmental isolates from urban streams in Ilorin, Nigeria: a One Health cross-sectional assessment
Article.Authors: Kolawole O.; Jimoh A.; Olayemi D.; Jimoh A.; Okunola A.; Aderibigbe J.; Oluwasegun F.; Olagunju A.; Oluwapelumi B.; Saliu F.; Abdullateef O.; Ahuoiza D.; Onifade A.; Olanrewaju F.; Aboyeji A.; Oloruntoba F.
Article.Abstract: Urban streams in sub-Saharan Africa receive continuous inputs of untreated wastewater and solid waste, potentially promoting accumulation of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) and resistance genes (ARGs). Data linking community sanitation to environmental antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in West African cities remain sparse. We assessed physicochemical quality, bacteriological contamination, antibiotic susceptibility, ARG prevalence, and sanitation practices across six urban streams in Ilorin, Nigeria. Three weeks of sampling yielded 247 isolates tested against six antibiotics; 98 multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative isolates were PCR-screened for five ARGs; seven isolates were 16S rRNA-sequenced; 180 households were surveyed to compute a Composite Sanitation Score (CSS) per catchment. All streams deviated from WHO/NSDWQ reference values. Ampicillin resistance was 64–89% per site; MDR prevalence was 43–68%. bla TEM was most prevalent (58–82%), followed by tet A (46–74%) and int I1 (39–61%). CSS correlated strongly negatively with all five AMR indicators (ρ = − 1.00; exact permutation p = 0.003; Bonferroni α = 0.01). With only six catchments, these are exploratory ecological associations, not causal evidence. Sanitation quality is associated with environmental AMR burden in Ilorin streams, supporting WASH investment within One Health AMR strategies, subject to confirmation in larger multi-site studies.

Article.Title: Exports of technologically related environmental goods are associated with higher environmental performance in OECD countries
Article.Authors: Toktaş Y.; Temiz D.; Şeker H.; Altıner A.
Article.Abstract: In this study, the impact of trade in technologically related environmental goods on environmental quality in OECD countries is examined for the period 2000–2023 using the MMQR method. To further address potential reverse causality concerns, the empirical analysis is complemented by the Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel Granger causality test. The study highlights how trade in these goods promotes the diffusion of environmentally friendly technologies, thereby supporting sustainable energy transitions and improvements in environmental performance. Empirical findings show that exports of technologically related environmental goods have a positive and significant impact across all quantiles, indicating that exports contribute consistently to technology diffusion. In contrast, the effect of imports becomes significant only in countries with relatively high environmental performance levels. The Dumitrescu–Hurlin test results further indicate a unidirectional predictive relationship running from both exports and imports of technologically related environmental goods to environmental performance, while no statistically significant feedback from environmental performance to trade variables is detected. The results further reveal that economic growth initially harms environmental quality, but as development progresses, its effect turns positive, confirming the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. Renewable energy consumption provides limited short-term support for environmental performance, whereas urbanization generally exerts positive effects. Overall, the findings suggest that sustainable development policies should be tailored to country-specific structural characteristics. To maximize the benefits of trade in technologically related environmental goods, it is recommended that countries prioritize tax incentives encouraging the export of environmentally friendly products and invest in infrastructure that facilitates the effective domestic use of imported environmental technologies.
