Article.Title: Globally guided multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled critics for cooperative UAV path planning
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Liu Q.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cooperative path planning for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires the simultaneous achievement of target navigation, collision avoidance, and formation coordination in complex obstacle environments. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods often suffer from sparse rewards, local deadlocks, and conflicts between formation maintenance and obstacle avoidance, which can destabilize policy learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Globally Guided Decoupled-Critic Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic algorithm (GDC-MASAC). RRT $$^*$$ -based global guidance provides reference waypoints for the leader UAV, reducing inefficient exploration and local deadlocks. Three decoupled Critic branches separately evaluate target navigation, formation maintenance, and safety objectives, while an environment-aware formation reward adjustment relaxes formation tracking near obstacles according to the distance to obstacle boundaries. Experiments under different obstacle densities and swarm sizes show that GDC-MASAC improves mission completion, collision avoidance, and formation coordination. In a scenario with 12 obstacles and 3 UAVs, GDC-MASAC achieves a mission success rate of 86%, whereas the baseline methods achieve success rates below 50%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of GDC-MASAC for cooperative multi-UAV path planning in cluttered environments.

Article.Title: Combining ability and gene action studies for different horticultural traits in pink brinjal (Solanum melongena L.)
Article.Authors: Sharma S.; Bhushan A.; Kumar S.; Kumar B.; Sharma M.; Vaid A.; Chopra S.; Kumar V.; Mehta A.
Article.Abstract: Pink brinjal ( Solanum melongena L.) is a highly preferred and extensively cultivated vegetable crop in Jammu and Kashmir, yet its genetic improvement has been constrained by the limited availability of high-yielding cultivars and the paucity of genetic information for parental selection. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of combining ability and gene action in elite pink brinjal germplasm, generating a strategic framework for hybrid breeding in the specialized market segment. An 8 × 8 half-diallel mating design involving eight elite pink brinjal parental lines produced 28 cross combinations, which along with their parents, were evaluated for twenty horticultural traits in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with three replications. Combining ability was estimated using Griffing’s Method II, Model I. Significant mean squares due to GCA and SCA revealed the simultaneous contribution of additive and non-additive genetic components in trait inheritance. Among the parental lines, Ganderbal Local Selection (P 3 ) and SJPB-22-12 (P 6 ) were identified as good general combiners for the majority of the yield-contributing traits, while Long Kashmiri × Kashmiri Long (P 4 × P 5 ) and SJPB-22-12 × Pink Long (P 6 × P 8 ) exhibited higher per se performance and significant positive SCA effectsfor yield related traits. In contrast, SJPB-22-08 × Pink Long (P 7 × P 8 ) exhibited good specific combining ability effects for quality traits. Beyond identifying promising parental lines and cross combinations, this study establishes a valuable genetic resource for the rational exploitation of heterosis and provides valuable evidence-based breeding strategies for developing high-yielding, good quality pink brinjal hybrids adapted to regional production systems.

Article.Title: Dual-band single negative metamaterial-based MIMO antenna with enhanced performance
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Kumar S.; Pathi S.; Shukla M.; Vimal V.; Kumar G.; Srivastava K.; Soliman N.
Article.Abstract: This work presents a single-layer metasurface characterization and analysis for converting a linearly polarised narrowband antenna to a wideband circularly polarised antenna and its multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) implementation. The single-layer metasurface is supported by grounded dielectric substrate, which is considered wave-guided metamaterial to retrieve the effective refractive index along the propagation direction. The proposed metasurface shows dual-band single negative (SNG) properties, with the first band (3 to 5.9 GHz) having negative permittivity and the second band (5.9 to 9 GHz) having negative permeability, which increases the effective propagation constant and thus allows antenna miniaturisation. The metasurface-integrated MIMO antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth of 3.11 GHz (4.3–7.41 GHz), an axial ratio bandwidth of 1.6 GHz (4.7–6.3 GHz), and the antenna gain ranges from 4.8 to 7.8 dB across the impedance bandwidth.

Article.Title: Nonlinear dynamic analysis of a variable angle tow composite diving board
Article.Authors: Heidarpour B.; Rahi A.
Article.Abstract: This paper investigates the nonlinear dynamic response and energy transfer mechanisms of a Variable Angle Tow (VAT) composite springboard featuring an intermediate unilateral support. While conventional straight-fiber composites are limited by their constant stiffness profiles, VAT composites enable spatial stiffness tailoring to optimize kinematic performance. A fully coupled nonlinear mathematical model is developed utilizing the Timoshenko beam theory and von Kármán geometric nonlinearities to account for large deformations. The governing equations are derived via Hamilton’s principle, discretized using the Galerkin method, and integrated numerically with a penalty approach modeling the unilateral contact. A comparative dynamic analysis between a tailored VAT (45 ∘ -90 ∘ ) and a straight-fiber composite springboard demonstrates that the VAT configuration significantly reduces the fundamental natural frequency while amplifying the maximum tip vertical velocity by over 145% (reaching 2.7 m/s). The results reveal that the variable fiber orientation induces a strong bend-twist coupling ( \(\:{D}_{16}\) ), triggering pronounced torsional oscillations and activating dominant geometric nonlinearities, which are evidenced by asymmetric phase portraits and higher-order harmonics in the frequency spectrum. Furthermore, energy analysis confirms that the VAT springboard possesses a vastly superior mechanical energy capacity, storing approximately 380 J of strain energy and releasing over 300 J of kinetic energy, compared to just 125 J and 50 J in the straight-fiber counterpart. These findings indicate that VAT composites provide substantial dynamic tailorability, alongside enhanced mechanical energy storage and energy return capacity for high-performance diving structures.

Article.Title: Iron oxide nanoparticle-mediated elicitation enhances secondary metabolite production, antioxidant activity, and gene expression in Melia azedarach L
Article.Authors: Rabbani V.; Garoosi G.; Haddad R.; Farjaminezhad R.; Japelaghi R.
Article.Abstract: Melia azedarach L. is an important medicinal plant with various biological activities, such as antidiabetic, antibacterial, antifungal, analgesic, and anticancer. The effect of iron oxide nanoparticles on the contents of azadirachtin, lupeol, stigmasterol, mevalonic acid, and squalene metabolites, expression of genes involved in their synthesis pathway, and the activity of some antioxidants in M. azedarach cell suspension culture has not been extensively studied. The impact of iron oxide nanoparticles at different concentrations (0, 20, 40, and 60 mg/L) and sampling times (3, 6, and 9 days) on cell suspension growth, production, and accumulation of the metabolites, expression of MOF1 and SQS1 genes, and antioxidant enzyme activity was investigated. Also, response surface methodology was used to optimize the applied treatment to achieve maximum accumulation of the secondary metabolites. The results of the RSM showed that the optimal conditions for achieving maximum accumulation of azidarichtin and squalene were a concentration of 20 mg/L of iron oxide nanoparticles on days 8.1 and 5.6 of sampling, respectively, and for lupeol, the optimal conditions were 39.2 mg/L of iron oxide nanoparticles and a sampling time of 4.5 days. The results showed that the highest expression levels of Mof1 and SQS1 genes, with an increase of 30.83 and 10.25-fold compared to the control, were observed under the treatment where squalene accumulation reached its highest level. In addition, the highest proline content, total flavonoid content, and phenol content were found for the 60 mg/L iron oxide nanoparticles and 6 days of sampling, 20 mg/L iron oxide nanoparticles and 9 days of sampling, and 40 mg/L iron oxide nanoparticles and 3 days of sampling, respectively. The catalase and superoxide dismutase enzymes showed the maximum activity in the 20 mg/L iron oxide nanoparticle and 6 days of sampling. The results suggest that optimized iron oxide nanoparticle treatments are associated with enhanced growth, metabolite accumulation, antioxidant activity, and expression of selected biosynthetic genes.

Article.Title: Particle swarm optimization-based type-2 fuzzy modeling for ECG signal prediction
Article.Authors: Pashikanti R.; Rathod V.; Raut A.; Dhotre V.; Tikore S.; Paithankar V.; Admasu D.
Article.Abstract: A hybrid prediction framework based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Inference System (IT2FIS) is proposed in this paper. The major contribution is a systematic methodology for calculating the ideal parameter vector to tune the membership functions of a type-2 fuzzy controller. In contrast to type-1 fuzzy controllers, the interval type-2 formulation provides better robustness in uncertain operating conditions by explicitly modelling uncertainty through a Footprint of Uncertainty (FOU) bounded by upper and lower membership functions. Four performance indices mean square error (MSE), root mean square error (RMSE), error mean, and error standard deviation were used to assess the suggested IT2FIS-PSO framework on typical ECG arrhythmia signal data. The baseline IT2FIS produced an RMSE of 0.1198. This improved to 0.0429, a reduction of almost 75.98%, after PSO-based optimization of both membership function bounds. Experimental data show that the proposed optimization technique significantly improves ECG prediction accuracy relative to the unoptimized baseline, and simulation results confirm that PSO consistently finds the optimal parameters for a type-2 fuzzy controller.

Article.Title: Multistep synthesis of novel indole–benzimidazole hydrazone hybrids as xanthine oxidase inhibitors: In-Vitro evaluation, molecular docking, MD simulations and DFT studies
Article.Authors: Ammara N/A.; Latif A.; Ali M.; Khushal A.; Khan S.; Mammadova K.; Duran S.; Halim S.; Abdellattif M.; Khan A.; Al-Harrasi A.
Article.Abstract: This work reports the synthesis of a focused library of indole-benzimidazole hydrazone hybrids ( 17 - 35 ) via a multistep procedure involving thiolation, hydrazination, and Schiff base condensation. The final structures were confirmed using 1 H-NMR, 13 C-NMR, and FT-IR spectroscopy by observing diagnostic NH, azomethine, and carbonyl peaks consistent with the proposed frameworks. All of the synthesized compounds were evaluated for in vitro xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibition, where only eight compounds possessed significant activity (IC₅₀ = 26.8–91.5 µM). Amongst the active molecules, compound 18 emerged as the most potent inhibitor (IC₅₀ ≈ 26–27 µM), followed by 20 , 17 , and 33 , with several analogues outperforming allopurinol (IC₅₀ = 78.5 ± 1.34 µM), indicating promising lead potential. The structure-activity (SAR) analysis highlights that small, single electron-donating substituents at ortho/meta positions increased XO potency, whereas multiple, bulky, or strongly electron-withdrawing groups created steric clashes, hence reduced activity. Conceptual DFT results supported the biological trends, showing lower HOMO-LUMO gaps (3.75–4.37 eV) and reduced hardness relative to allopurinol, consistent with higher electronic softness and improved target interaction in active compounds. Molecular docking was performed against bovine XO (PDB: 3NRZ), which displayed strong binding of the active compounds ( 18 , 20 , 17 , and 33 ) via cooperative H-bonding (Ser876), π–π stacking with phenylalanine residues, and π-cation/π-sulfur interactions (Lys771, Met770), rationalizing their inhibitory mechanisms. Furthermore, MD simulations were applied to compound 18 , allopurinol as a standard, and APO, and the results reveal that after ligand binding, the protein was stabilized. The ligand-binding complex of compound 18 was found to be more stable than the allopurinol complex. The binding energy was calculated by MMPBSA; compound 18 has -28.839 ± 4.59 kcal/mol, and the allopurinol complex has -7.746 ± 2.53 kcal/mol. This interactive experimental-computational work identifies the indole-benzimidazole hydrazone scaffold, specifically compound 18 , as a viable platform for producing next-generation XO inhibitors for the management of hyperuricemia and gout.

Article.Title: Externally validated machine learning models for prediction of treatment selection and clinical outcomes in posterior communicating artery aneurysms
Article.Authors: Sanker V.; Register E.; Eberle A.; Javed S.; Paul B.; Chang C.; Jensen K.; Kasem R.; Almosawi M.; Scherschinski L.; Catapano J.; Benet A.; Rahmani R.; Lawton M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Posterior communicating artery (PCOM) aneurysms account for approximately 25% of intracranial aneurysms and present clinical challenges regarding optimal treatment selection. This study developed and validated machine learning models to predict treatment modality, complications, and functional outcomes in PCOM aneurysm management using a comprehensive institutional database of 75 patients treated between 2002 and 2023. Five machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and XGBoost—were systematically compared across 7 outcome variables: treatment type (open vs. endovascular), specific open surgical treatment, specific endovascular treatment, intraoperative rupture, complications, angiographic obliteration, and discharge modified Rankin Scale score. Models were developed using preoperative patient-specific (age, sex, family history) and aneurysm-specific (size, presentation, morphology, location) parameters, with rigorous preprocessing that included class-balancing strategies, feature engineering, and regularization to minimize overfitting. Cross-validation performance demonstrated high accuracy for treatment prediction (78.7% Random Forest), complications (94.7% Random Forest; however, sensitivity of 0% indicates that this accuracy should not be interpreted as clinically useful event detection), intraoperative rupture (92.0% Random Forest), and angiographic obliteration (87.3% Random Forest). External validation on an independent cohort from the University of Louisville (n=20–28; n=20 most complete cases for the primary external cohort, with up to n=28 for selected endpoints with available labels) revealed variable generalizability: treatment prediction maintained 78.1% accuracy, and complication prediction showed reduced external performance (70.3%), highlighting institution-specific factors. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses demonstrated that class balancing significantly improved minority class recall (0.0% → 52.2%–86.3%) for rare outcomes. Feature importance analyses identified age, aneurysm size, admission modified Rankin Scale score, and Hunt-Hess grade as the most influential predictors across multiple outcomes. This study represents the first externally validated, multioutcome machine learning framework for PCOM aneurysm management, providing quantitative risk estimates and evidence-based decision support for treatment selection and outcome prediction.

Article.Title: Multi-level malware subfamily attribution from RGB executable images using attention-augmented deep learning
Article.Authors: Saxena M.; Das T.
Article.Abstract: Malware analysis in modern cybersecurity increasingly requires decisions at multiple levels of granularity, including maliciousness detection, malware family identification, and fine-grained subfamily attribution. While image-based malware classification has demonstrated promising performance for binary detection and family-level recognition, the application of RGB executable image representations to hierarchical malware subfamily attribution remains largely unexplored. This study presents a unified hierarchical deep learning framework for malware classification using RGB representations of Windows Portable Executable (PE) files, enabling simultaneous malware detection, family classification, and 33-subfamily attribution within a multi-output architecture. Four attention-augmented transfer learning models ResNet50V2-CBAM, DenseNet169-CBAM, Xception-NonLocal, and VGG19-Triplet Attention were evaluated under identical datasets, taxonomy, preprocessing, and training conditions to ensure fair comparison. Experimental results achieved 99% binary classification accuracy, 96–97% family-level accuracy, and 91–95% subfamily-level accuracy, with macro F1-scores up to 0.89 for fine-grained attribution. A comprehensive experimental evaluation using per-class precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion-matrix analysis showed closely comparable performance among the three strongest attention-based models, with the fully fine-tuned VGG19 variant trailing on the most difficult variants. A protocol-matched comparison with our previously published grayscale framework further showed that RGB executable images provide competitive hierarchical performance while enabling direct compatibility with modern three-channel transfer learning architectures. This study represents one of the first systematic evaluations of RGB executable image representations for hierarchical malware subfamily attribution across a 33-subfamily taxonomy. The proposed framework provides an effective and computationally efficient approach for fine-grained malware attribution, supporting practical applications in digital forensics, cyber threat intelligence, and security operation centers.

Article.Title: Agreement between initial in-person and follow-up telemedicine assessment in patients presenting with first-time headache
Article.Authors: Sarıdaş F.; Oguz-Akarsu E.; Mercan Kara M.; Ur Özçelik E.; Köse N.; Cerrahoğlu Şirin T.; Huseynli Z.; Kocasoy Orhan E.; Gökçay F.; Öztürk V.; Karlı H.
Article.Abstract: Remote healthcare services have markedly increased in recent years. Telemedicine is increasingly considered a practical alternative to in-person evaluations of chronic neurological disorders, including primary headache syndromes. However, prospective data examining its reliability during first-time consultation are limited. This study assessed the consistency between initial in-person examination and subsequent telemedicine follow-up in patients presenting with headache for the first time, and compared costs, time burden, loss of work capacity, and patient and physician satisfaction. Sixty patients (49 women and 11 men) aged 20–40 years who presented with headaches for the first time to six specialized headache clinics were enrolled in this study. Each patient underwent an initial in-person examination, followed by a video-based telemedicine consultation at the same center 45 days later. Demographic data, clinical characteristics, and diagnoses were recorded during interviews. Patients completed cost and burden assessment questionnaires, and both groups completed satisfaction questionnaires. Analyses examined the concordance between the two examination methods and factors influencing them. Headache history showed excellent agreement between in-person and telemedicine assessments (ICC = 0.928, 95% CI 0.882–0.956), while headache frequency and duration demonstrated moderate agreement. Localization and lateralization were consistent in more than 80% of cases, headache intensity in 77.8%, and overall diagnostic concordance reached 95%, with the highest agreement observed for migraine with and without aura. In-person outpatient examinations resulted in a mean time loss of 208.05 ± 119.78 min, whereas telemedicine reduced work-capacity time loss by 87.4%. Patient satisfaction with telemedicine was high (86.2% very satisfied), and physicians rated the overall telemedicine consultation favorably (69% excellent). Patients also expressed greater willingness than physicians to use telemedicine for future follow-up visits (60% vs. 39.7%). Telemedicine shows high consistency with in-person assessments, particularly for migraine patients, and has reduced time, cost, and work loss. These findings support telemedicine as a reliable follow-up approach after an initial face-to-face assessment, particularly for patients with primary headache disorders requiring limited physical examination.

Article.Title: Pain self-efficacy mediates the relationship between illness perceptions and health-related quality of life in women with endometriosis
Article.Authors: Motakef H.; Bani Hani S.; Basyouni N.; Alshahithy Y.; Abu Aqoulah E.; Salem Alshammari L.; Mazied Alshammari S.; Kamel Mosbah Mahmoud S.; Galal Abd Elrazik Siam B.; Aljabbab L.; Ali Marzouk S.
Article.Abstract: Endometriosis is a major health problem affecting about 190 million reproductive-aged women. There is no definite cure for endometriosis; however, there are many medical and surgical options for relieving the severity of the disease and improving the quality of life for these women. This study aims to examine the relationship between illness perception and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among women who have been diagnosed with endometriosis, as well as examining the role of pain self-efficacy as a mediator between these two variables. A cross-sectional design was employed with 300 participants. Data were collected using a structured, self-administered questionnaire that included sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire, the Pain Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, and the Health-Related Quality of Life: Endometriosis Health Profile-30 (EHP-30). Data were analyzed using. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27 and SmartPLS 4.0. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was also conducted to test both direct and mediating effects. Statistical significance was set at p < .05. The mean age of participants was 30.0 ± 5.5 years. The majority were predominantly married and attained a bachelor’s education, with a marked symptom burden. Two-thirds of participants were overweight and obese. It was found that 28.7% had Stage III endometriosis, and over 80% reported moderate-to-severe pelvic pain. Both Illness perceptions and pain self-efficacy were at moderate levels, while HRQoL impairment was substantial, especially in pain and emotional domains as well. More negative illness perceptions were significantly associated with worse HRQoL (r = 0.458, p < .001) and lower pain self-efficacy (r = − 0.474, p < .001), whereas higher pain self-efficacy was associated with better HRQoL (r = − 0.542, p < .001). In regression analysis, illness perceptions and pain self-efficacy together explained 34.6% of the variance in HRQoL, with pain self-efficacy demonstrating the stronger independent association. This study demonstrated that illness perceptions and pain self-efficacy are related factors that influence HRQoL in endometriosis patients. Negative illness perceptions were found to be associated with HRQoL, and increased levels of pain self-efficacy were found to be related to HRQoL. Pain self-efficacy also partially mediated the relationship between illness perceptions and HRQoL.

Article.Title: Improved Swin Transformer-based fine-grained human motion understanding approach driven by simulation-based augmentation for intangible cultural heritage in sports
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Huang X.; Yu L.; Dai B.
Article.Abstract: Fine-grained human motion understanding for Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) in sports faces challenges such as high similarity in posture between motion categories and significant differences in temporal rhythms within categories. Existing spatiotemporal motion models suffer from insufficient feature discrimination under small sample conditions and severe degradation in generalization ability when migrating from the simulation domain to the real domain. This paper proposes an improved Swin Transformer-based fine-grained human motion understanding method driven by simulation-based data augmentation for ICH. The method reconstructs the 3D skeleton of ICH motions using the Unity3D simulation engine combined with the OptiTrack motion capture system, and generates multimodal simulation samples by applying random perturbations to lighting, viewpoint, and body shape parameters. Addressing the limitation of the original Swin Transformer window self-attention mechanism lacking inter-frame temporal awareness, a Temporal Difference Attention (TDA) module is embedded after each Stage attention layer. This module explicitly models the rhythmic motion changes of ICH motions through the differential response of feature maps from adjacent frames. A cross-domain alignment loss, \(\:{\text{L}}_{\text{MMD}}\) , based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), is introduced at the top of the feature pyramid to force the convergence of high-level semantic feature distributions between the simulation and real domains, enabling cross-domain transferability of spatiotemporal representations. The overall framework is jointly trained end-to-end to complete closed-loop modeling from simulation generation to real-world action classification and stage localization. Experiments are conducted on the public datasets NTU RGB + D 120 (hereinafter referred to as “NTU”) and Kinetics-400 for system validation. The accuracy rates for fine-grained human action recognition reach 88.6% and 79.3%, respectively. The mean average precision (mAP) in cross-domain scenarios reaches 81.2%; the MMD distance converges to 0.038; the temporal intersection over union (tIoU) for action stage localization reaches 0.76. Further generalization analysis is conducted on the SICHA-Derived sports ICH action test dataset (covering 8 categories of traditional actions such as Tai Chi and martial arts routines, totaling 1,240 annotated videos) derived from NTU. The proposed method achieves a Top-1 accuracy of 82.4%, a 10.6% point improvement over the strongest baseline, validating the framework’s practicality in the sports ICH scenario. Notably, under extreme small-sample conditions with only a single real sample per class, the framework achieves 71.6% accuracy, substantially exceeding both the simulation-only variant at 52.4% and real-data-only fine-tuning at 18.3%, demonstrating the practical value of the simulation-based augmentation and cross-domain alignment mechanisms for real-world sports ICH scenarios where annotations are inherently scarce.

Article.Title: A reliability-oriented multimodal ensemble framework for fake news detection in armed conflict crisis situations
Article.Authors: Muhammad F.; Al-Ahmadi S.; Saeed F.; Hussain N.
Article.Abstract: Social media platforms where people can post fake news threaten public trust, social stability, and the informed nature of people’s choices because of the rapid growth of fake news. Multimedia content is widely accessible today and has added to the complication of misinformation through the use of multimedia (including images, audio, video) in combination with textual information, which often contain emotional language to create narratives that deceive consumers of information. There has been much research over the last few years that has explored ways to detect fake news on multiple platforms, and while this research has resulted in the development of many multimodal fake news detection systems, the majority of these current methods rely on single-classifier architectures and fairly simple fusion strategies that do not provide much in terms of robustness, generalization, or reliability in terms of detection under noisy and ambiguous conditions. To address these limitations, this study presents a novel multimodal fake news detection framework that incorporates both textual and visual representation learning based on transformer models, affective feature modeling, and a stacked ensemble decision-fusion approach. The textual representation learning module in the proposed framework makes use of the XLM-R model, whereas the visual representation learning module uses the ViT-B/16 model. Finally, the affective modeling module utilizes pretrained sentiment and emotion models for capturing and distinguishing the affective signals. The predictions made by the multimodal representations are combined through the meta-classifier to generate the final classification result. In this regard, the proposed architecture enables robust cross-modal reasoning and probabilistic calibration. In what follows, we discuss the empirical results of extensive experiments conducted using four large-scale benchmark datasets (Fakeddit, Ukraine-GitHub, Weibo, and MediaEval), which show that the proposed multimodal detection architecture always outperforms the state-of-the-art multimodal detection approaches proposed recently. The proposed framework performs competitively on four benchmark datasets and achieves the accuracy of 94.66%, 98.23%, 98.12%, and 97.98% on Fakeddit, Ukraine-GitHub, Weibo, and MediaEval, respectively. Evaluations and ablation studies confirm the efficacy of the proposed multimodal ensemble approach under the given experimental settings.

Article.Title: IL-6R blockade with tocilizumab disrupts pericyte– and tumor cell–driven IL-6/STAT3 signaling, enhancing docetaxel efficacy in ER+ breast cancer
Article.Authors: Przanowska R.; Gomez-Villa J.; Liu V.; Antonides-Jensen N.; Visvabharathy L.; Alverdy J.; Hernandez S.; Yee S.
Article.Abstract: Metastatic breast cancer is a global health concern with a persistently low five-year survival rate. Taxane microtubule stabilizers, including docetaxel (DTX), are the standard of care, with a majority of estrogen receptor-postive (ER+) breast cancer patients ultimately developing cancer relapse and progression. Pericytes, vascular cells within the tumor microenvironment, and their role in promoting pro-survival remain understudied. Inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin 6 (IL-6) are known to drive and contribute to drug resistance via activation of the pro-survival JAK/STAT pathway. We found that DTX induced IL-6 secretion of pericytes by at least two-fold compared to vehicle-treated controls in vitro . All tested breast cancer cell lines expressed subunits of the IL-6 receptor (IL-6R) complex, indicating their capacity to respond to JAK/STAT signaling. Conditioned media from DTX-treated pericytes activated STAT3 in ER+ breast cancer cells to levels comparable to recombinant IL-6. Pharmacologic blockade of IL-6 signaling with the IL-6R inhibitor, tocilizumab, reduced DTX-induced STAT3 activation in vitro. Combined treatment with tocilizumab and DTX synergistically suppressed the growth of zero-passage patient-derived ER+ breast cancer organoids expressing intact IL-6 signaling. Together, our findings suggest that combining DTX with tocilizumab may revert DTX-induced pro-survival in ER+ breast cancer patients by inhibiting IL-6-mediated activation of the STAT3 pathway.

Article.Title: Adherence to treatment recommendations and quality of life among patients with cardiovascular disease
Article.Authors: Jurczak A.; Młyńska K.; Krężel P.; Piątak M.; Michniewicz B.; Sobczyńska K.; Napieracz-Trzosek I.; Seretna P.; Wieder-Huszla S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases are a common and serious health problem. Patients are often unaware of the severity of their condition, fail to undergo appropriate diagnostic tests and don’t follow the recommended treatment. The aim of the study was to assess the lifestyle and adherence to therapeutic recommendations of cardiac patients. The study was conducted among 465 patients in the cardiology clinic in Gryfice, Poland from June to October 2023. A self-designed questionnaire and standardized tools were used: World Health Organization Quality of Life (WHOQOL-BREF), Adherence to Refills and Medications Scale (ARMS), A dherence in Chronic Diseases Scale (ACDS) and The Satisfaction with Life Scale (SWLS). Treatment reported by the participants mainly involved pharmacotherapy (90.8%) and 35.1% of the respondents took medication strictly as prescribed. Higher medication adherence (lower ARMS scores) was significantly correlated with better quality of life in the Psychological (r = − 0.18, p < 0.001) and Environment (r = − 0.13, p = 0.007) domains, and this association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, comorbidity burden, and socioeconomic factors. A weak positive correlation was also found between medication adherence and life satisfaction ( p = 0.003). Cardiac patients were characterised by poor to average adherence to treatment recommendations. Medication adherence appears to be associated with the quality of life of cardiac patients.

Article.Title: A geospatial and community perception analysis of the impacts of land use and land cover change on ecosystem service values
Article.Authors: Islam M.; Yeasmin T.; Hasan I.; Hasan Munna M.; Parvez A.
Article.Abstract: Rapid urbanization in developing countries is causing significant changes in land use and land cover (LULC), which affect ecosystem service values (ESVs). This study investigates the impacts of LULC changes on ESV in the Gazipur city area of Bangladesh over a 30-years from 1991 to 2021. The analysis was conducted using satellite imagery from Landsat-5 TM (1991 and 2006) and Landsat-8 OLI-TIRS (2021), with a supervised classification approach to prepare LULC maps and the Benefit Transfer Method for ESV evaluation. We used the global coefficient values proposed by Costanza et al. 1 and the updated coefficients from Costanza et al. 2 , along with the local coefficient values modified by Hoque et al. 3 for ESV estimation. The results show significant LULC changes, particularly the rapid expansion of built-up areas, increasing from 3.70% in 1991 to 44.95% in 2021. Due to this expansion, vegetation cover and agricultural land decreased by 39% and 55%, respectively. The expansion of urban areas was the main reason for the 40% decrease in water bodies. These changes show that the study area is rapidly urbanizing and industrializing due to population growth and rising economic activity. The total ESV demonstrated a declining trend from 1991 to 2021, with overall reductions of 40.3%, 46.5%, and 40.9% estimated under all coefficient sets. The study found that waterbodies and agricultural land were mostly lost in terms of ESV which accounted for over 60% of the total ESV reduction. The coefficient of sensitivity (CS) was applied to address uncertainties in the valuation process and the results found the assessment to be robust based on all three coefficient sets. Community perception of Ecosystem Services (ES) by LULC category in the study area was measured using a four-point Likert scale method, and data were collected through direct field surveys using a structured questionnaire, focus group discussions, and key informant interviews. This approach provides an important community-based assessment that complements the biophysical ESV outcomes and helps contextualize changes in ES from the community’s perspectives. This study provides a robust framework to evaluate ES dynamics and support evidence-driven urban environmental management in rapidly urbanizing cities by integrating long-term LULC investigation, spatial ESV analysis, multiple valuation coefficient sets and local perceptions.

Article.Title: Pelvic magnetic stimulation added to pelvic-floor muscle training for female vaginal laxity: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Shi R.; Ye X.; Tan Y.; Shi R.; Du X.; Zhou R.; Hong X.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the short-term efficacy of pelvic magnetic stimulation combined with pelvic floor rehabilitation training (Intervention) versus isolated pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) among women diagnosed with vaginal laxity (Population). The Vaginal Laxity Questionnaire (VLQ) total score assessed at 8 weeks of treatment was predefined as the primary outcome (Outcome), and multiple subjective and objective indicators were adopted as secondary outcomes to comprehensively reflect pelvic floor function recovery. A total of 147 patients diagnosed with vaginal laxity at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Qinghai Red Cross Hospital—either during outpatient visits or hospitalization—from March 2025 to October 2025 and meeting the inclusion criteria were enrolled. After providing informed consent, all participants were randomly assigned using a random number table into two groups: the control group (n = 73) receiving PFMT alone, and the combined-intervention group (n = 74) receiving the combined intervention. Both groups underwent an 8-week treatment regimen, with a treatment log established for each participant. Assessments were conducted at three predefined time points, evaluating the following eight outcome measures: VLQ, female sexual function, degree of vaginal laxity, vaginal health index score(VHIS), pelvic floor type I and type II muscle fibers, surface electromyography (sEMG) of the pelvic floor muscles, three-dimensional ultrasound parameters, and mean vaginal pressure. The primary outcome (8-week VLQ total score) was significantly higher in the combined-intervention group compared with the control group at both 4-week and 8-week follow-ups (both P < 0.001). However, although the primary analysis employed cross-sectional between-group comparisons at each timepoint rather than a formal group × time interaction test, a supplementary linear mixed-effects model with group × time interaction was performed as a sensitivity analysis and confirmed significant differential change trajectories between groups (Group × Time interaction: F = 29.587, P < 0.001 for VLQ; F = 495.662, P < 0.001 for FSFI total score). All secondary subjective indicators including total Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) and its six subdomains, vaginal laxity finger grading, type I/II pelvic floor muscle fiber strength and fatigue resistance showed significantly superior improvements in the combined-intervention group ( P < 0.05). For objective imaging and functional metrics, most 3D pelvic floor ultrasound parameters and vaginal resting/cough/defecation pressure values were significantly better in the combined-intervention group at week 8 ( P < 0.05). No intergroup statistical differences were detected in vaginal health index (VHIS) total score, post-contraction resting-phase sEMG value, resting bladder neck initial position and levator-urethra gap(LUG) at either follow-up time point ( P > 0.05). These preliminary findings suggest that combined pelvic magnetic stimulation and PFMT may improve vaginal laxity and sexual function compared with PFMT alone. Results require confirmation in multicenter, sham-controlled trials with longer follow-up. Trial registration : Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600122143); registered on April 9, 2026.

Article.Title: Anthill clay–supported TiO₂/Fe3O₄/ZnO nanocomposite for green remediation of petrochemical wastewater: simultaneous removal of COD, BOD, sulphate, and chloride
Article.Authors: Otaru A.; Awe O.; Baba I.; Albin Zaid Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The design of sustainable multifunctional nanoadsorbents capable of addressing highly polluted petrochemical wastewaters is still a formidable environmental task. In this research, TiO₂/Fe₃O₄/ZnO ternary nanocomposites immobilized on anthill clay with different ratios of oxides (1:1:1, 1:2:1, 1:1:2 and 2:1:1) have been successfully prepared using a green impregnation technique in conjunction with Daniellia oliveri leaf extract and assessed for the adsorptive elimination of chemical oxygen demand (COD), biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), sulphate and chloride ions. The success of nanocomposite preparation was confirmed by structural analysis techniques that showed average hydrodynamic particle sizes within the range of 37.80 to 68.25 nm, while nitrogen adsorption studies revealed the mesoporous nature of the samples with BET surface areas between 190.81 and 264.42 m² g⁻¹; the 1:1:1 nanocomposite sample gave the highest BET surface area (264.42 m² g⁻¹) and pore volume (0.0248 cm³ g⁻¹). Successful immobilization of the nanoparticles TiO₂, Fe₃O₄ and ZnO onto the anthill clay was verified through XRD, FTIR, SEM, EDX and TGA techniques that gave excellent thermal stability below 5% weight loss above 500 °C. Batch adsorption studies gave very good efficiency for all the pollutants, with the nanocomposite having the highest ZnO content (1:1:2 ratio), giving removal efficiencies of 99.51%, 98.03% for COD, 93.95% for sulphate, and 96.62% for chloride at an adsorbent dosage of 0.40 g. Initial characteristics of petrochemical effluent included BOD of 56.30 mg L⁻¹, COD of 119.94 mg L⁻¹, sulphate of 297.65 mg L⁻¹, and chloride of 351.63 mg L⁻¹, which were above permissible limits. In the performance evaluation based on compositional variations, nanocomposites that were either balanced or rich in ZnO showed better pore accessibility and adsorption efficiency than those with more Fe₃O₄. Adsorption kinetics were best modeled using the pseudo-second-order kinetic model, which indicates that chemisorption is the prevalent mode of adsorption. This study reveals that the use of TiO₂/Fe₃O₄/ZnO nanocomposites derived from anthill clay is a safe, cost-effective, and efficient solution to petrochemical wastewater treatment problems.

Article.Title: Offspring prematurity, family socioeconomic status, and parental investment: the bavarian longitudinal study
Article.Authors: Wong M.; Copeland W.; Wolke D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evolutionary models of parental investment propose that parental investment may vary with child characteristics relevant to reproductive value, parental resources (i.e., socioeconomic status; SES), or their interaction. The relative importance of these factors in high-income societies remains unclear. Using preterm birth as a proxy of variation in early-life biological characteristics, we analyzed data from 607 preterm and 859 full-term children in the Bavarian Longitudinal Study. Participants were born between January 1985 and March 1986 in Bavaria, Germany, and comprised neonatal at-risk infants requiring admission to a children’s hospital within 10 days of birth and healthy term-born controls. Parental investment across seven domains was assessed during the first 9 years of life. Linear mixed models examined hypotheses derived from reproductive value-based allocation (H1), resource-based allocation (H2), and contingent parental investment models (H3). Results strongly supported H2: high-SES parents invested more than low-SES parents across most domains after accounting for prematurity. Prematurity was additively associated with lower parental investment in some domains, providing partial support for H1. No clear evidence supported the interaction predicted by H3. Overall, parental investment was more consistently associated with family SES than with prematurity, whereas associations with prematurity were more domain specific. These findings inform evolutionary models of parental investment while highlighting policy implications for reducing social inequities.

Article.Title: Nutritional assessment and dietary intake patterns in early-stage chronic kidney disease: a hospital-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Ghosh A.; Badikol V.; Muley A.
Article.Abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) presents a rapidly growing public health challenge in India, with early stages offering a critical window for nutritional intervention. This hospital-based cross-sectional study assesses nutritional intake, anthropometric measurements, biochemical markers, and appetite status among adults with CKD stages 1–3 (n = 184) attending outpatient nephrology departments of two tertiary care hospitals in Hyderabad, India. Assessment tools include a Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ), 24-h dietary recall, Subjective Global Assessment (SGA), and the Council on Nutrition Appetite Questionnaire (CNAQ). Mean age is 47.6 ± 12.1 years; 59.8% are male. Stage distribution is: Stage 1 (10.9%), Stage 2 (25.5%), Stage 3a (34.2%), and Stage 3b (29.3%). Mean protein intake is 0.82 ± 0.21 g/kg/day; based on single 24-hour dietary recall estimates, a substantial proportion appeared to exceed recommended sodium (approximately 64%) and potassium (approximately 58%) thresholds, representing directional trends rather than precise habitual intake values; 34.2% are malnourished by SGA.Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) category correlates negatively with haemoglobin (r = − 0.350, p < 0.001) and positively with urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR; r = + 0.350, p < 0.001), and negatively with CNAQ score (r = − 0.244, p = 0.001), indicating that lower appetite co-varies with more advanced CKD stages. In a multivariable linear regression modelling eGFR as a continuous outcome, older age (β = −0.65, p < 0.001), male sex (β = +7.48, p = 0.014), and higher BMI (β = +0.70, p = 0.044) were independently associated with eGFR (adjusted R² = 0.16); haemoglobin and CNAQ score were independently not associated with eGFR after adjustment. Older age, male sex, and higher BMI were independently associated with eGFR in this cross-sectional cohort, while dietary patterns, appetite (CNAQ), and haemoglobin showed significant bivariate associations with CKD stage that were not retained in the adjusted model. Systematic nutritional assessment and individualised dietary counselling nonetheless remain clinically relevant given the high observed burden of suboptimal dietary patterns and reduced appetite in this population.

Article.Title: Aspiration-line pressure stability in Venturi and peristaltic pump configurations during phacoemulsification: an in vitro study
Article.Authors: Kunishige T.; Suzuki H.; Okamoto F.
Article.Abstract: This in vitro study descriptively evaluated aspiration-line pressure waveforms between Venturi and peristaltic pump configurations and their associated tubing systems using two Stellaris systems and a KITARO artificial anterior chamber model. VAC200 and VAC400 represented 200- and 400-mm Hg vacuum settings in the Venturi configuration and vacuum limits in the peristaltic configuration, with peristaltic flow settings of 20 and 35 mL/min, respectively. Pressure was recorded at 0.1-s intervals and analyzed during the stable 30- to 50-s period after activation. Only one continuous run was performed per condition. Reported standard deviations (SDs) represent within-run temporal fluctuation, not between-run variability. Mean pressure, SD, and transient fluctuations of 10 mm Hg or greater were evaluated. At VAC200, mean pressure was − 10.40 ± 0.53 mm Hg in the Venturi configuration and 11.02 ± 2.99 mm Hg in the peristaltic configuration. At VAC400, values were − 70.90 ± 1.06 and − 50.97 ± 2.54 mm Hg, respectively. Descriptive analysis suggested greater pressure fluctuation in the peristaltic configuration at both settings. Intermittent transient fluctuations of 10 mm Hg or greater occurred only in P-VAC400. These findings describe aspiration-line pressure waveforms under the tested in vitro conditions.

Article.Title: Management of skeletal anterior open bite using zygomatic miniplates: a prospective interventional study
Article.Authors: Alanazi F.; Alanazi A.; Shah S.; AlRwuili M.; Shah K.; Khan T.; Albilasi R.; Alenzi N.; Khan Z.
Article.Abstract: Apertognathia (anterior open bite) is among the most challenging skeletal discrepancies in adult orthodontics, where growth modification is no longer feasible. Orthognathic surgery is effective but invasive, whereas conventional incisor extrusion increases lower facial height and is prone to relapse. This study evaluated the clinical and cephalometric outcomes of managing anterior open bite using a zygomatic miniplate skeletal anchorage system combined with fixed orthodontic appliances. This single-arm prospective interventional study (case series) was conducted at the Gurayat Specialist Dental Center and Gurayat General Hospital, Al-Qurayyat, Saudi Arabia, from February 2023 to January 2024. Twenty consecutively enrolled adult patients (12 females, 8 males; mean age 20.85 ± 3.18 years; range 16–28 years) with skeletal anterior open bite were treated. Inclusion criteria were an open bite of − 4 mm to − 8 mm, maxillary posterior vertical dento-alveolar excess, acceptable incisor-lip relations, and a Frankfort-Mandibular plane angle (FMA°) greater than 29°. Skeletal maturity was confirmed using the cervical vertebral maturation (CVM) method (stage CS5–CS6) prior to inclusion. All patients underwent bilateral zygomatic miniplate placement under local anaesthesia, followed by fixed orthodontic treatment with a modified Erverdi appliance. Maxillary molar intrusion was performed with nickel-titanium coil springs delivering 150–200 g of force per side. Cephalometric variables (overbite, overjet, FMA°, and true molar intrusion) were recorded at pretreatment (T1), 6 months (T2), and 12 months (T3). Because the Shapiro–Wilk test indicated non-normal distributions for several variables, non-parametric tests (Wilcoxon Signed-Ranks and Kruskal–Wallis) were used throughout, with Spearman correlation; significance was set at p < 0.05. Significant improvements were observed across all parameters. Mean overbite improved from − 6.0 ± 1.48 mm (T1) to 2.80 ± 0.78 mm (T3) (correction 8.80 ± 1.26 mm; 95% CI 8.21–9.39 mm). Overjet decreased from 6.05 ± 1.08 mm to 2.67 ± 0.63 mm (reduction 3.37 ± 0.8 mm). True intrusion of the maxillary first molars averaged − 3.0 ± 0.86 mm relative to the palatal plane, with a mean FMA° reduction of − 2.8 ± 0.89° (from 31.95 ± 1.81° to 29.12 ± 1.71°). A strong correlation was found between molar intrusion and overbite correction (ρ = 0.85) and a moderate correlation with FMA° reduction (ρ = 0.72). No plate loosening, infection, or relapse was observed during follow-up. Within the limitations of a small, single-arm sample and a 12-month follow-up, zygomatic miniplate anchorage combined with fixed appliances appears to be an effective, minimally invasive option for correcting skeletal anterior open bite in adults. The approach induces counterclockwise mandibular autorotation and improves overbite, overjet, and FMA° without orthognathic surgery. Longer-term, controlled studies are required to confirm stability and to compare miniplates with alternative anchorage devices.

Article.Title: Mast cells may promote myeloma engraftment in the NSG-hIL6 patient derived xenograft model
Article.Authors: Hasanali Z.; Garfall A.; Vogl D.; Cohen A.; Waxman A.; Susanibar-Adaniya S.; Kapur S.; Stadtmauer E.; Cipriano C.; Weber K.; Allman D.
Article.Abstract: Multiple myeloma remains a fatal, incurable disease. Most therapies are targeted to the cancer cell or T cell engagement. Little is known about the supporting myeloma microenvironment and its contribution to tumor fitness. Here, we expand upon the observation of human mast cells in the NSG-hIL6 myeloma patient derived xenograft mouse model to correlate mast cells to decreased engraftment time and increased overall myeloma engraftment. Mast cells may also correlate to worsened bone disease. We identify 10 mast cell secreted factors that together improve the survival of patient myeloma cells in vitro. Our findings demonstrate the utility of the NSG hIL6 model for studying human bone marrow–myeloma crosstalk, including mast cells.

Article.Title: Transfer learning improves the prediction of ligand binding sites at protein–membrane interfaces
Article.Authors: Pliushcheuskaya P.; Künze G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Membrane-exposed ligand binding sites in membrane proteins are emerging as important modulatory targets in drug discovery, however, their prediction remains challenging due to limited structural data. Here, we present DeepPocket-Mem, a deep learning-based approach that applies transfer learning to a convolutional neural network originally developed for soluble protein binding sites. A curated dataset comprising 605 protein–ligand complexes was used to fine-tune the components responsible for ranking candidate binding sites and predicting their shapes, followed by validation using measures of binding-site localization and spatial overlap. While transfer learning of the classification module alone did not improve discrimination between binding and non-binding sites, fine-tuning of the segmentation module enhanced pocket localization and increased the number of correctly identified sites among top-ranked predictions, as reflected by improved success rates based on distance center-to-center (DCC) and discretized volume overlap (DVO). Further improvements were achieved by restricting training to drug-like ligands with confirmed biological activity, underscoring the importance of biologically relevant data for model performance. Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of transfer learning for binding site prediction under data-limited conditions and establish DeepPocket-Mem as a useful tool for identifying membrane-embedded binding sites. Concurrently, they highlight the need for expanded structural datasets to further improve prediction accuracy.

Article.Title: Improving allergic rhinitis symptoms through nutrition as an adjunct: a systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of dietary supplements
Article.Authors: Lim J.; Lee Y.; Wong Q.; Chew F.
Article.Abstract: Dietary supplements are increasingly explored as adjunctive strategies for allergic rhinitis (AR). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of dietary supplementation in improving AR symptoms and explored potential underlying mechanisms. A systematic PubMed search was conducted through May 2026 following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Trials evaluating dietary interventions in AR were included. Meta-analyses were performed using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models for studies reporting changes in Total Nasal Symptom Score (TNSS). Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB2 tool while publication bias was assessed using Egger’s test, and heterogeneity was quantified with the I 2 statistic. Ninety-three studies were included, with 26 eligible for meta-analysis. Interventions were classified into plant-based compounds, probiotics, vitamins, fatty acids, and other supplements. Most studies were assessed as low risk of bias (91.4%), with a small proportion (8.6%) raising some concerns. Significant reductions in TNSS were observed for probiotics (Standardized Mean Difference (SMD) = − 1.63, 95% CI − 2.59, − 0.66), plant-based compounds (SMD = − 1.24, 95% CI − 2.12, − 0.36), and vitamin D supplementation (SMD = − 2.79, 95% CI − 3.33, − 2.24). However, substantial heterogeneity existed across intervention types, formulations, and study methodologies. Mechanistic findings suggested potential roles in immune modulation, anti-inflammatory activity, and gut microbiota regulation, although these remain hypothesis-generating. Plant-based compounds, probiotics, and vitamin D may provide adjunctive benefits for improving AR symptoms. Nevertheless, findings should be interpreted cautiously given substantial heterogeneity, reliance on subjective outcomes, and potential small-study effects.

Article.Title: Residual-gated generative additive joint-bias identification and uncertainty-weighted fault compensation for quadruped robots with scarce data
Article.Authors: Wu L.; Zhang M.; Li D.; Cao Y.
Article.Abstract: Repeated actuator-fault injection on a physical quadruped is costly and can damage motors or gearboxes, which makes continuous fault-value identification difficult when only scarce sequences are available. This study targets command-equivalent additive joint bias. A temporal generator is trained with adversarial and temporal objectives, while an acceptance gate screens synthetic windows using an aggregate score of attitude-integration, first-order joint-kinematic, torque-limit, and command-limit residuals. A heteroscedastic identifier combines dense feature reuse, temporal convolution, bidirectional recurrent features, and cross-attention fusion to estimate the bias and predictive variance. The resulting estimate is converted into an uncertainty-weighted compensation command, with amplitude and rate constraints enforced by final-output projection over their feasible intersection. Controller-level simulations include four additive-bias profiles at the 12 actuated joints and representative same-leg and diagonal two-joint cases. In the reference sinusoidal single-calf-joint evaluation, the method reduces identification RMSE from 0.1404 rad for deterministic DGTNet to 0.1180 rad and reports an interval calibration error of 0.031. With matched controller protections, uncertainty weighting reduces mean recovery time from 0.764 to 0.743 s and RMS command variation from 0.00671 to 0.00651 rad. Across the four single-joint profile groups, the proposed RMSE ranges from 0.1194 to 0.1428 rad, compared with 0.1421 to 0.1696 rad for DGTNet. Same-leg and diagonal paired faults yield RMSE values of 0.1584 and 0.1510 rad and attitude-recovery rates of 74.6% and 77.4%, respectively. Outdoor physical-robot tests with eight runs per configuration show a 54.8% reduction in mean RMS attitude error relative to uncompensated faulty walking, with similar outcomes for constant and uncertainty-weighted confidence.

Article.Title: Spintronic and thermoelectric functionalities in transition-metal-based K₂MCl₆ double perovskites (M = Mn, Mo, Ta, Tc)
Article.Authors: El Goutni M.; Abdalla S.; Batouche M.; Dhaou M.; Alsawi A.; Ferjani H.; Alharbi S.
Article.Abstract: The vacancy-ordered double perovskites K₂MCl₆ (M = Mn, Mo, Ta, Tc) were systematically investigated using first-principles calculations to explore their structural, electronic, magnetic, and thermoelectric properties. Calculations based on the FP-LAPW + lo method within the WIEN2k framework, supported by phonon dispersion and AIMD analyses, confirm the thermodynamic and dynamical stability of all compounds in the cubic Fm-3 m phase. The transition-metal substitution strongly influences lattice parameters, elastic behavior, and electronic characteristics. Magnetic calculations reveal stable ferromagnetic ground states for all systems. K₂MnCl₆, K₂TaCl₆, and K₂TcCl₆ exhibit half-metallic behavior with complete spin polarization, whereas K₂MoCl₆ behaves as a spin-polarized semiconductor. Strong exchange interactions and spin–orbit coupling effects significantly govern the electronic structure. Thermoelectric analysis demonstrates remarkable performance, including Seebeck coefficients up to − 1150 µV/K and electronic figures of merit approaching unity over 300–1000 K, highlighting K₂MCl₆ compounds as promising materials for spintronic and thermoelectric energy applications.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic insights into hydrostatic-pressure-induced triploidy in large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) across developmental stages
Article.Authors: Ke Q.; Wang Y.; Qiao G.; Liu S.; Wang X.; Zheng W.; Peng S.
Article.Abstract: Induced triploidy is used in aquaculture to generate functionally sterile stocks and may alter the allocation of resources among growth, maintenance, and reproduction. However, the molecular responses associated with hydrostatic-pressure induction and triploidy remain poorly characterized in large yellow croaker ( Larimichthys crocea ). In this study, fertilized eggs assigned to the induction group were exposed to 7000 PSI hydrostatic pressure for 3 min at 2 min 30 s post-fertilization. Ploidy analysis confirmed triploid status in the pressure-induced groups and diploid status in the controls. RNA sequencing was performed on whole-body samples from 5-day-old larvae and dorsal fin tissue from 8-month-old fish, with three biological replicates for each treatment group and sampling context. A total of 1,194 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were detected in larvae, including 859 upregulated and 335 downregulated genes in triploids, whereas 3,174 DEGs were identified in 8-month-old fish, including 1,497 upregulated and 1,677 downregulated genes. Larval DEGs were enriched in cell-cell adhesion, epithelial polarity, tight junction, protein digestion and absorption, and innate immune-related pathways. The larval protein-protein interaction network highlighted claudin-family genes and digestive proteases, with most hub genes showing higher expression in triploids, although CLDN15 and CLDN18 displayed the opposite pattern. In 8-month-old fish, DEGs were dominated by ribosome biogenesis, rRNA processing, spliceosome, RNA degradation, mitochondrial translation, glutathione metabolism, and amino acid and steroid metabolism. Hub genes involved in ribonucleoprotein assembly and mitochondrial ribosomes were consistently lower in triploid dorsal fin. These findings reveal stage- and tissue-context-dependent transcriptomic responses to triploidy and identify candidate molecular modules for subsequent validation of epithelial, translational, metabolic, and immune phenotypes in triploid large yellow croaker.

Article.Title: Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of structural steel and reinforced-concrete frames in residential buildings
Article.Authors: Heidarian S.; Partonia P.; Heidarian P.; Dezvareh G.; Darban A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Selecting structural materials is critical to reducing the environmental burdens associated with building construction. This study comparatively evaluates structural steel versus reinforced-concrete framing systems in two functionally equivalent three-story residential buildings utilizing identical waffle slab floor configurations in Ahvaz, Iran. The assessment was conducted in SimaPro using the ReCiPe 2016 Endpoint (H) method and was defined as a cradle-to-gate assessment supplemented with end-of-life considerations. The modeled stages encompassed raw-material extraction, material production, transportation, construction-related material flows, and end-of-life treatment and recycling scenarios. To strictly isolate and benchmark the cradle-to-gate and end-of-life embodied impacts of the structural frames independent of envelope physics and operational dynamics, the operational use phase (modules B1–B7) was deliberately excluded from the system boundary. Although the high thermal inertia of concrete relative to steel can significantly influence cooling loads in extreme climates like Ahvaz, dynamic operational simulation (module B6) was defined as beyond the current scope and recognized as a key limitation for future whole-building assessments. The results reveal important environmental trade-offs between the alternatives. The steel-framed building generated a higher total single score than the reinforced-concrete frame building, with scores of 53.59 kPt and 32.61 kPt, respectively, representing a difference of 20.99 kPt. Human health was the dominant damage category in both alternatives. The steel frame recorded 50.83 kPt for human-health damage, compared with 29.87 kPt for the reinforced-concrete frame; calculated relative to the steel alternative, this indicates that the reinforced-concrete alternative had approximately 41% lower human-health damage under the modeled conditions. At the midpoint level, however, the reinforced-concrete building showed an approximately two-fold higher global-warming impact than the steel building, highlighting a significant climate-change trade-off. Regarding the resource-related endpoint, the reinforced-concrete alternative showed a slightly higher score (0.06 kPt) compared to the steel alternative (0.03 kPt), although this difference accounts for only 0.06% of the total score. Crucially, the apparent advantage of the steel alternative in mineral resource conservation is highly conditional, relying on an idealized best-case recycling scenario that presupposes an efficient recovery infrastructure. The difference in ecosystem-quality damage was limited. Furthermore, while the single-score metric indicated an overall higher integrated burden for the steel frame, such aggregated scores carry inherent weighting subjectivity and should not be interpreted as absolute superiority. The findings demonstrate that structural material selection involves multi-dimensional trade-offs that are strongly dependent on local supply chains, operational dynamics, and real-world recycling efficiency.

Article.Title: CST1 stabilizes GPX4 to suppress ferroptosis and promote bladder cancer progression
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Ni X.; Guo A.; Wang L.; Lu Q.; Dong S.; Liu X.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Cystatin SN (CST1), a cysteine protease inhibitor, participates in various cancers, yet its function and mechanism in bladder cancer (BCa) are unclear. Public databases, BCa cells and clinical samples were used to analyze CST1 expression profiles. Functional experiments detected cell proliferation, migration and invasion. Intracellular iron, ROS, MDA, GSH and mitochondrial morphology reflected ferroptosis. Co-IP assays verified the intracellular interaction between CST1 and GPX4, and ubiquitination assays clarified GPX4 stabilization via suppressed proteasomal degradation. Xenograft and rescue assays validated the CST1-GPX4 axis. The expression of CST1 is markedly higher in bladder cancer cells than in normal urothelial cells. CST1 knockdown inhibits malignant phenotypes and induces ferroptosis. CST1 binds GPX4 to block its ubiquitination and post-translationally elevate GPX4 protein without altering its transcription. GPX4 overexpression rescues CST1 silencing-induced ferroptosis and growth defects. In vivo CST1 facilitates tumor growth and GPX4 upregulation. CST1 interacts with GPX4 to inhibit its ubiquitin-dependent degradation, suppress ferroptosis and promote BCa progression, and may serve as a potential therapeutic target for bladder cancer.

Article.Title: Role of problematic use of social networks and self-consciousness in the association between adverse childhood experiences and well-being among young Indian adults
Article.Authors: Jadhav B.; Abdul Azeez E.; Kariveliparambil A.; Mathew M.; Kannah T.
Article.Abstract: The prevalence of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and problematic use of social networks (PUS) among the young adults prompted the current study. In understanding how ACEs are associated with well-being, the current study examined the mediating role of PUS and the moderating role of self-consciousness. This cross-sectional study employed self-report measures to collect data from 671 young adults (382 males, 287 females, 2 non-binary; Mean age = 20.85 years) across India. The data were analyzed using concurrent moderation and mediation model (Hayes PROCESS macro model 5) in SPSS. The findings revealed a negative association between ACEs and well-being. This relationship was partially and significantly mediated by PUS. The simultaneous analysis of the moderation and mediation model showed overall significance. The direct path between ACEs and well-being was moderated by self-consciousness and mediated by PUS. The results of conditional effects indicated that as self-consciousness increased, the negative association between ACEs and well-being became stronger . Hence, individuals did not benefit from greater self-consciousness as they intensified the emotional cost of early adversity, leading to reduced overall well-being. Developing evidence-based interventions to prevent ACEs and address negative health behaviors (such as PUS) in this population will be beneficial. A policy intervention to regulate excessive use of social networking sites should be introduced.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic insights into developmental and nutritional shifts in Huhu (Prionoplus reticularis) grub larval stages
Article.Authors: Henzeler B.; Kavle R.; Faya N.; Giehr P.; Bekhit A.; Carne A.; Kersten C.; Schneider S.; Agyei D.
Article.Abstract: The Huhu grub ( Prionoplus reticularis ; Order: Coleoptera, Family: Cerambycidae, Subfamily: Prioninae - hereafter referred to as P. reticularis ) is an edible beetle larva endemic to Aotearoa New Zealand and has long been part of Māori food traditions. Despite its cultural and nutritional relevance, molecular information for this species remains scarce. In this study, we present the first de novo transcriptome assembly for P. reticularis and examine stage‑associated transcriptional differences between small and large feeding larvae using whole‑larva RNA sequencing. Distinct expression patterns were observed between the two larval size classes. Larger larvae showed increased expression of genes involved in protein synthesis, mitochondrial activity, and central metabolic processes, consistent with elevated biosynthetic demand during growth. Enrichment analyses identified over‑representation of functions related to ribosome biogenesis, oxidoreductase activity, and ATP binding, alongside conserved metabolic pathways such as glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and amino‑acid biosynthesis. Differences were also observed in transcripts associated with membrane transport and structural components, suggesting broader physiological shifts accompanying larval growth. Because RNA was extracted from whole larvae, these results represent organism‑level transcriptional differences and do not resolve tissue‑specific regulation. Functional and nutritional interpretations should therefore be viewed as hypothesis‑generating rather than definitive. Nevertheless, this work provides a foundational transcriptomic resource for P. reticularis and offers initial molecular insight into physiological differences within the edible larval phase. The dataset establishes a basis for future tissue‑resolved transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic studies aimed at assessing nutritional properties, bioactive potential, and allergenic considerations of Huhu grub proteins.

Article.Title: Impact of skin-to-skin contact during postnatal transport in a low-resource setting: a prospective, observational study in Mozambique
Article.Authors: Frison M.; Cavallin F.; Avagnina I.; Ye L.; Magul S.; Manuel H.; Assane S.; Antonia L.; Mazzotta M.; Putoto G.; Trevisanuto D.
Article.Abstract: Postnatal transport may exacerbate thermal loss in low-resource settings. This study investigated the impact of skin-to-skin contact (SSC) on temperature, heart rate and oxygen saturation during postnatal transport in a low-resource setting. This is a prospective, observational study on SSC during postnatal transport by ambulance to Beira Central Hospital (Mozambique) between July and November 2024. Neonates were usually transferred in parents’ arms and SSC was offered to the parents. The outcome measures were neonatal temperature, normothermia, heart rate and oxygen saturation at admission. In 238 neonates, mean travel time was 18 min (SD 10) and SSC was performed in 30.7% of cases. At arrival, mean temperature was 35.9 °C (SD 1.3) with a normothermia rate of 27.3%. Adjusting for clinically relevant confounders, SSC was not associated with admission temperature (MD 0.19 °C, 95% CI -0.12 to 0.49 °C) or normothermia (OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.11). Adjusting for clinically relevant confounders, SSC was not associated with heart rate (MD 2.13 bpm, 95% CI -3.76 to 8.03 bpm) or oxygen saturation (MD 0.30, 95% CI -3.15 to 3.75) at admission. Compared to being carried in parent’s arms, SSC was not associated to improved thermal control, heart rate and oxygenation stability in newborns needing postnatal transport in a low-resource setting under the condition studied. Future investigations may explore the role of SSC in longer postnatal transports and further efforts should focus on improving neonatal thermal care in peripheral health facilities and during postnatal transport.

Article.Title: Helium migration patterns in the ultra-deep reservoirs of the Anyue gas field
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Qin S.; Zhao F.; Gao H.; Ou H.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: The Sinian–Cambrian reservoirs in the Anyue gas field contain over one trillion cubic meters of natural gas. These reservoirs are close to basement helium sources and have well-developed ancient formation water as a potential carrier. However, despite these favorable conditions, helium concentrations remain abnormally low. Traditional studies have not quantitatively constrained helium migration pathways. This hampers the evaluation of helium enrichment potential in ultra-deep strata. To address this, we analyzed noble gas isotopes (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe) and elemental ratios in 23 reservoir samples, aiming to trace helium sources and identify migration mechanisms. The results suggest that: (1) Helium in the Anyue gas field is mainly crustal-derived. The Sinian reservoir exhibits higher R / R a ratios (0.008–0.062) and a greater crustal helium proportion than the Cambrian reservoir (0.003–0.019). (2)The 20 Ne/ 36 Ar, 84 Kr/ 36 Ar, 132 Xe/ 36 Ar ratios consistently indicate open-system behavior in the Sinian and Cambrian strata. The Sinian shows a stronger He–N₂ correlation ( R 2 = 0.82) and contains more atmospheric noble gases, indicating more intense basement groundwater circulation. (3) Helium in the Sinian reservoir is primarily derived from exsolution of water-soluble helium from basement formation water. Correspondingly, helium in the Cambrian reservoir mainly originates from the Qiongzhusi source rocks, with minor exogenous contribution. (4) Poor fault connectivity and overpressure in the Cambrian (pressure coefficient 1.51–1.70) have contributed to inefficient helium migration pathways. This study establishes a quantitative model for helium differential enrichment controlled by the activity of formation water. It provides a testable theoretical framework for integrated helium concentration in basement groundwater circulation.

Article.Title: Modeling the heterogeneity of cognitive dysfunction in Parkinson’s disease using partially ordered set models
Article.Authors: Zweber C.; Jaeger J.; Zabetian C.; Miller R.; Iyer V.; Hiller A.; Sahoo S.; Cholerton B.; Ryan A.; Tatsuoka C.; Gupta D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional binary classifications of Parkinson’s disease (PD) cognitive dysfunction fail to capture its inherent heterogeneity. This study introduces the Partially Ordered Set (POSET) model, a Bayesian framework, to analyze cognitive heterogeneity using Parkinson’s Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI) data. Five cognitive domains: Attention, Visuospatial Judgement, Executive Functioning, Working Memory, and Episodic Memory, were mapped onto nine neuropsychological measures to calculate Cognitive Performance Scores (CPS). Of 264 participants without baseline cognitive dysfunction, 21.2% developed dysfunction by Year 3. After demographic adjustment and Bonferroni correction, cognitive dysfunction at Year 3 was inversely associated with median CPS values for: Attention (across all visits); Executive Functioning and Working Memory (Year 1 onward); and Visuospatial Judgement (baseline only). In multivariable logistic regression, both baseline Attention and Visuospatial Judgement CPS were significant predictors of future impairment without adjustment for baseline disease duration, however, only Visuospatial Judgement CPS remained a significant predictor after the adjustment. POSET modeling provides a sophisticated approach to characterizing PD cognitive decline, offering greater granularity than conventional schemes. Further large-cohort studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Article.Title: Dietary nanoencapsulated A-Ghrelin improves growth performance and health status in juvenile Siberian sturgeon
Article.Authors: Ahmadpour M.; Heidari B.; Valipour A.; Hadavi M.; Asghari S.; Khorshidi A.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated a novel multi-functional feed supplement for juvenile Siberian sturgeon ( Acipenser baerii ), combining an acetylated ghrelin analog (A-Ghrelin) with a chitosan-alginate-iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) nanoparticle delivery system. Over 60 days, 240 fish (initial weight: 8.5 ± 0.9 g) were assigned to eight diets ( n = 3 tanks/treatment). The complete supplement (nanoencapsulated A-Ghrelin + 1 mg/kg nano-Fe₂O₃) yielded the best outcomes: weight gain increased 75.5% (73.9 vs. 42.1 g in control), feed conversion ratio improved from 4.1 to 1.8, and reduced ALT/AST. Modulation of humoral immune parameters was observed, including increased complement activity and immunoglobulins. The number of intestinal fold and villi density increased by 39.7% and 28.2%, respectively. Gene expression showed upregulation of igf-1 (2.4-fold) in A-Ghrelin group and NpY (7.3-fold) in the Nano Fe + Al-Cs group. The encapsulation system achieved 73.8% efficiency for A-Ghrelin with a pH dependent sustained release profile under simulated gastrointestinal conditions in vitro. This formulation represents a promising precision nutrition strategy for sturgeon aquaculture.
