Article.Title: Multi-class Alzheimer’s disease classification using VGG19 transfer learning with hybrid Harris Hawks Optimization and random forest
Article.Authors: Anbu Selvi G.; Karthick T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate cognition-state classification of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), and Cognitively Normal (CN) is essential for early evaluation of the disease. Existing deep-learning approaches often retain redundant features, depend on dataset-specific configurations, and provide limited methodological optimization. This study proposes a transfer-learning-based MRI classification framework integrating spatial and intensity normalization, histogram equalization, double bilateral filtering, VGG19-based deep feature extraction, Harris Hawks Optimization with Simulated Annealing (HHO-SA) for feature selection, and Random Forest (RF) classification. The framework was implemented using Python and PyTorch and evaluated on the ADNI1 Complete 1Yr 1.5T dataset, containing 2,294 MRI observations from 639 subjects. Subject-level partitioning was employed to minimize data leakage. The proposed framework achieved 98.70% accuracy, 98.55% macro-precision, 98.93% macro-recall, 99.28% macro-specificity, 98.73% macro-F1, and 99.40% macro-ROC-AUC. Compared with the strongest reported benchmark accuracy of 98.20%, this study developed into 0.50%. The findings demonstrate effective retrospective three-class MRI classification and provide a reproducible computational framework for AD research.

Article.Title: Heterogeneous graph transformer with slot-based message passing for node classification
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Zheng W.; Ming Y.; Lin K.; Xiong B.
Article.Abstract: As a widely utilized data structure, heterogeneous graphs can accurately model complex structures and multi-typed relationships, finding extensive applications in social network analysis, recommendation systems, knowledge graphs, and biomedical analysis. Node classification supports these applications by identifying entity categories or functional roles. However, during the message-passing process, mapping different types of nodes into a unified representation space often leads to cross-type feature confusion, resulting in the loss of type-specific semantic information. To address this issue, this paper proposes the HGT-Slot model. First, the model employs a type-aware Slot initialization to construct type-specific representation spaces for different node types, preserving their unique semantic attributes. Subsequently, a Slot attention mechanism is employed during the message-passing phase to preserve heterogeneous semantic information through different Slot channels. Meanwhile, the Transformer architecture is leveraged to enhance interactions among node representations, thereby improving the representation capability of the model. Finally, a Slot aggregation mechanism integrates the Slot representations for local prediction, which is fused with the global prediction from the Transformer branch for classification. Experiments on three datasets show that HGT-Slot achieves the best mean Macro-F1 and Micro-F1 scores among the compared methods for node classification.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: graph transformer; node classification; heterogeneous graphs; graph neural networks

Article.Title: Dynamic fusion and robust downsampling for remote sensing object detection
Article.Authors: Hong Y.; Lian J.; Wan Z.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: In remote sensing imagery, complex backgrounds and scale variation make small objects difficult to detect. To address this issue, we propose an SRFD-CAFM (Shallow Robust Feature Downsampling - Convolution and Attention Fusion Module) framework, which is an improved RT-DETR (Real-Time Detection Transformer). It integrates CNN and Transformer to balance local and global information. A dynamic weight allocation (DWA) module adaptively regulates feature contributions, while the Shallow Robust Feature Downsampling (SRFD) module preserves fine-grained shallow information to mitigate small-object feature loss. Experiments on multiple datasets show a 1.6-point mAP50–95 improvement over the baseline, confirming the model’s capability in complex scenes and small object detection.

Article.Title: An automata-machine learning integrated framework for intelligent mental health diagnostics
Article.Authors: Pawar L.; Bajaj R.; Mengist Y.; Kumar N.; Pant R.; Kumar A.; Pandey P.
Article.Abstract: Depression among the students has critical impact on student’s life and it needs to be predicted at an early stage. The unstructured nature of self-emotions are going to undetected and emerged as a critical mental health concern. Integration of machine learning (ML) with behavioural modelling address the concern and connects with student emotional state and helps to predict the depression among students at early stage. An automata-machine learning integrated approaches including ensemble of lazy and eager classifiers, behavioural modelling, minimization of finite automata are evaluated and compared in three scenarios where in the first case predictive performance on original dataset is evaluated. The second case in sighting the real life scenario student specific emotions are extracted with automata-based behavioural states to generate meaningful patterns and feature vectors for each student and these automata generated features are statistically tested and signified then embed with original dataset. Further the ML feature selection Gini index applied on automata integrated dataset to select the prominent features to enhance the predictive performance. In the third case automata based feature merging is applied which maintain the credibility of each feature and merged systematically with related features and preserve the equivalence and reduce the feature redundancy. Unlike the traditional ML based feature selection, Automata based feature merging retains the interpretability and behavioural traceability of all features. Lastly, eager learning (random forest) and lazy Learning (kstar) are ensemble and deployed to take advantage of the automata based optimized feature sets. The automata assisted scenario performs well and improves the accuracy with 14.86% where the baseline accuracy is 82.02% evaluated with random forest classifier and the accuracy with automata based behavioural modelling is recorded 96.88% and shows proposed framework is an interpretable, dynamic solution for mental health interventions in educational settings. The main contributions of the proposed framework is to extract automata based features that behaviourally connects to student emotions and mental state. The minimization of finite automata reduces the redundant factors and maintained the credibility of each feature. Further multi-metric statistical validation determines the applicability of automata extracted features.

Article.Title: Knowledge, practice patterns and preventive counseling regarding peripartum pelvic floor disorders among Swiss healthcare professionals
Article.Authors: Keller N.; Mogy C.; Lange S.; Zachariah R.; Witzel I.; Betschart C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pregnancy and childbirth are partly modifiable risk factors for pelvic floor disorders (PFD). Many women are neither aware nor informed about possible sequelae of childbirth. For higher awareness of this public health issue, the Swiss Society of Gynecology and Obstetrics published an information brochure with a focus on written health information and preventive strategies. Together with the launch of the brochure, an online survey was conducted to study the level of awareness of PFD (i) and to describe the current practice patterns and preventive measures among different health professionals (ii). From December 2022 to April 2023, an online survey in French, German and Italian was created and sent by the Swiss Society of Gynecology and Obstetrics, the Swiss Association of Midwives and the Association of Swiss Pelvic Floor Physiotherapists (pelvisuisse) to their members. The descriptive, cross-sectional survey consisted of 22 questions designed to assess the awareness, practice patterns, and preventive strategies towards educational resources. 211 professionals responded to the survey: 100 gynecologists, 75 midwives and 36 physiotherapists from all regions of Switzerland. Regarding awareness (i) respondents discuss in 68% possible consequences of pregnancy and childbirth on the pelvic floor with their patients. 20% discuss PFD only in case of risk factors or symptoms. Information on urinary incontinence (UI) is given by 44%, on pelvic organ prolapse (POP) by 33% and on fecal incontinence (FI) by 26%. For the practice patterns and prevention of PFD peripartum (ii) most participants recommend perineal massage (77%) and one in five pelvic floor physiotherapy. The mode of delivery regarding possible birth injuries is rarely discussed, unless the pregnant women ask for it (32%), whereas the consequences of Caesarean section (CS) are a frequent topic in the consultations (58%). To raise awareness of PFD during pregnancy and the postpartum period, a professional brochure represents an initial step toward offering appropriate support for healthcare providers. Integrating information about FI into counseling poses greater challenges compared to UI. This survey underscores the considerable potential for healthcare providers to enhance the frequency and scope of information and prevention efforts addressing PFD in peripartum women.

Article.Title: Novel comprehensive characterization of PELLAMAR sapropelic extract and implications for therapeutic applications
Article.Authors: Iacob M.; Bălan A.; Nichita C.; Nedelcu E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The therapeutic value of natural sapropels from Romanian lakes has been known since Dacian-Roman times, and they have been used to treat a variety of disorders. Although PELLAMAR products are rooted in medical therapeutic tradition and have been used in balneotherapy for decades, the therapeutic mud extract has never been characterized by modern techniques. This novel study aimed to provide a comprehensive characterization of the PELLAMAR therapeutic mud extract. Core analytical and physicochemical methods used for characterization of PELLAMAR sapropelic mud extract were performed using Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR) and Raman Spectroscopy (RS) for molecular composition, and Thermogravimetric Analysis, Derivative Thermogravimetry, Differential Scanning Calorimetry (TGA/DTG/DSC) for thermal stability. These methods provide a comprehensive multi-modal assessment of sapropelic muds. FT-IR analysis demonstrates a mineral-dominated composition characterized by a broad envelope near 1090 cm⁻¹ arising from overlapping Si–O stretching of quartz and sulfate ν₃ stretching of gypsum, carbonate bands (~ 1317 cm⁻¹) consistent with calcite, and sulfate ν₁ stretching (~ 990 cm⁻¹) together with ν₄ bending (~ 611 cm⁻¹) confirming the presence of gypsum (CaSO₄·2 H₂O). Broad O–H stretching bands (3857–3473 cm⁻¹) and H–O–H bending (~ 1657 cm⁻¹) reflect significant hydration and a colloidal matrix. Minor contributions from organic functional groups suggest the presence of humic substances, supporting a mixed organic–mineral structure typical of sapropelic materials. Raman spectra indicate that the sapropelic mud extract contains a heterogeneous organic–mineral matrix, characterized by strong silicate, sulfate, and carbonate bands, with a smaller but detectable organic contribution reflected in O–H/H₂O and aliphatic C–H-associated features. Strong bands in the 2900–3000 cm⁻¹ region indicate abundant aliphatic C–H groups consistent with lipid-rich organic matter, whereas the 3634–3706 cm⁻¹ bands are consistent with hydroxylated humic structures. In addition, carotenoids, aromatic carbon structures, kerogen-like material, and alkynes or related unsaturated compounds are found. TGA/DTG/DSC analysis is consistent with the presence of a rich mineral phase that confers heat retention and thermal stability. This study, to our knowledge, provides the first modern multimodal spectroscopic and thermal characterization of the PELLAMAR sapropelic mud extract. The findings support a hydrated, mineral-dominated organo-mineral matrix with preserved organic signatures and provide a physicochemical basis for further investigation of its potential pelotherapeutic and cosmeceutical applications. Quantitative mineralogical, thermophysical, chemical, safety, and clinical studies are required to establish specific functional and therapeutic performance.

Article.Title: Sensitivity of synovial fluid analysis in hematogenous native joint septic arthritis – overall accuracy and pathogen-specific differences
Article.Authors: Alexandersson H.; Tillander J.; Dehlin M.; Jin T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate the sensitivity of synovial fluid (SF) white blood cell count (SF-WBC), SF polymorphonuclear neutrophil percentage (PMN%), and the SF/serum glucose ratio in a study population with a definitive diagnosis of hematogenous native joint septic arthritis (SA) and explore factors influencing their performance, including the causative pathogen. We conducted a retrospective register and medical record study of 57 patients with culture-verified hematogenous native joint SA identified through ICD-codes between 2016 and 2019 in western Sweden. All patients included had documented SF-WBC analysis. Clinical data and SF analyses were compared between patients above and below cutoffs for SF-WBC (50,000 cells/mm 3 ) and SF/serum glucose ratio of 0.5. SF findings were also compared between S. aureus and other pathogens. The sensitivity of SF-WBC ≥ 50,000 cells/mm 3 was 51%, SF/serum glucose ratio < 0.5 was 57% and PMN% ≥ 70 was 95%. Patients with SF-WBC ≥ 50,000 cells/mm 3 were significantly older. SA caused by S. aureus were associated with lower PMN% and higher SF/serum glucose ratio compared to other organisms. While PMN ≥ 70% had a high sensitivity for native joint SA, the conventional cutoffs for SF-WBC and SF/serum glucose ratio showed poor sensitivity. SA caused by S. aureus may be associated with a less pronounced inflammatory response compared with other pathogens, a finding that warrants further investigation.

Article.Title: BMP4 and WIF1 expression in mother–child pairs in relation to anorectal malformations and maternal reproductive history
Article.Authors: Asim M.; Rahim A.; Fiaz M.; Javed A.; Awan W.
Article.Abstract: Anorectal malformations (ARM) result from disrupted embryonic hindgut development, with both genetic and environmental factors contributing to disease pathogenesis. However, the relationships among maternal molecular alterations, reproductive history, and offspring gene expression remain poorly understood. This hospital-based case–control study evaluated BMP4 and WIF1 expression in peripheral blood from 182 biological mother–child pairs, comprising 83 children with ARM and 99 controls. Gene expression was quantified by quantitative real-time PCR and expressed as ΔCt, with 2⁻ΔΔCt used to describe relative expression. Consanguineous marriage was more frequent among mothers of children with ARM than controls (67.5% vs. 40.4%; odds ratio 3.06, 95% CI 1.66–5.63) and was included as a covariate in adjusted analyses. Children with ARM showed markedly reduced BMP4 expression compared with controls (0.44-fold, 95% CI 0.33–0.59), a difference unaffected by adjustment for consanguinity; BMP4 expression was similarly, though more modestly, reduced in their mothers (0.77-fold, 95% CI 0.63–0.95). Child WIF1 expression did not differ between groups, and evidence for altered maternal WIF1 expression was inconclusive. In multivariable regression, ARM status was the only independent predictor of child BMP4 ΔCt (B = 1.24, 95% CI 0.77–1.72, P < 0.001). Maternal miscarriage history significantly moderated the association between ARM status and child WIF1 ΔCt (FDR-adjusted P = 0.001 for miscarriage group; P = 0.004 for recurrent miscarriage). These findings support an association between reduced BMP4 expression and ARM in both children and their mothers and suggest that maternal reproductive history may modify child WIF1 expression. Prospective and functional studies are warranted to clarify the biological significance of these associations.

Article.Title: Handgrip strength as a moderating variable in the relationship between motor self-efficacy and perceived physical literacy in school physical education
Article.Authors: Castillo-Paredes A.; Galán-Arroyo C.; Rojo-Ramos J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Handgrip strength is an objective measure of muscular strength, while motor self-efficacy is associated with motor performance. Both constructs are conceptually related to perceived physical literacy, which reflects children’s self-perceptions in domains connected to participation in physical activity. To analyze the moderating role of handgrip strength between motor self-efficacy and perceived physical literacy in children and adolescents. A quantitative, correlational, cross-sectional design was used. Participants aged 10–17 years ( N = 1054) were recruited through non-probabilistic convenience sampling. Handgrip strength was assessed using hand-held dynamometry, motor self-efficacy was measured using the Motor Self-Efficacy Scale, and perceived physical literacy was evaluated using the Spanish Perceived Physical Literacy Instrument for Adolescents (S-PPLI). Group differences were tested using Mann–Whitney U and mediation and moderation models were estimated using nonparametric bootstrapping (5,000 resamples). Boys showed significantly higher scores than girls in handgrip strength, motor self-efficacy, and all dimensions of perceived physical literacy. Secondary students also presented higher handgrip strength than primary students. Moderation analyses revealed that the interaction term (motor self-efficacy × handgrip strength) was significant across all dimensions ( p < .001). The association between motor self-efficacy and perceived physical literacy was stronger at higher levels of handgrip strength. Handgrip strength acts as a moderating factor that strengthens the relationship between motor self-efficacy and perceived physical literacy, suggesting that objective measures of muscular strength may provide complementary information when examining perceived physical literacy in educational contexts.

Article.Title: Perceived academic stress, emotion regulation, academic buoyancy, and psychological well-being: a control-value theory-informed analysis
Article.Authors: Ismail S.; Akdemir A.; Khasawneh M.; Ibrahim K.; AlRashidi A.
Article.Abstract: Using Control-Value Theory (CVT) as an interpretive framework, this study examined the statistical associations of perceived academic stress, emotion regulation, and academic buoyancy with psychological well-being among Saudi EFL learners. Rather than testing the appraisal-emotion structure of CVT, the study estimated the relationships among these learner constructs within a single partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) model and used CVT to inform their theoretical interpretation. Data were collected from 250 intermediate-level EFL learners enrolled in institutionally based English programs in Saudi Arabia using the Perception of Academic Stress Scale (PASS), the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire, an adapted Academic Buoyancy Scale, and an adapted Psychological Well-Being Scale. SmartPLS 4 was used to evaluate the measurement and structural models. The measurement results indicated acceptable internal consistency and convergent validity, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.858 to 0.943 and AVE values exceeding 0.50. The specified model accounted for 31.2% of the observed variance in psychological well-being. Emotion regulation yielded the largest observed standardized coefficient in its association with psychological well-being (β = 0.316, p < .001), followed descriptively by perceived academic stress (β = 0.193, p = .014) and academic buoyancy (β = 0.145, p = .026). Because the differences among these coefficients were not tested directly, their ordering is descriptive and cannot be taken as evidence of statistically significant differences in association magnitude. Moreover, because perceived control, task value, and achievement emotions were not directly operationalized, the observed associations do not constitute evidence for the appraisal-emotion processes specified by CVT. Likewise, the positive stress-well-being coefficient provides no basis for concluding that learners made challenge appraisals, experienced eustress, or benefited from academic stress. The observed relationships provide a basis for future longitudinal and intervention studies examining whether changes in these constructs are accompanied by subsequent changes in learner well-being.

Article.Title: Characterization and efficacy of green-synthesized silver nanoparticles against Puccinia species - in vitro
Article.Authors: Sharma V.; Thakur S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Puccinia species cause substantial losses in wheat production and productivity across the globe, creating a serious challenge to food security. The environmental and health risks associated with conventional fungicides necessitate sustainable alternatives. The present study examines the eco-friendly synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) employing Eucalyptus globulus leaf extract through a biological reduction approach and evaluates antifungal efficacy against wheat rust pathogens. GC-MS identified bioactive compounds in the phytoextract, primarily alkaloids and flavonoids. UV-visible spectroscopy confirmed AgNPs formation. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, Scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, dynamic light scattering, and zeta potential analysis established their functional groups, surface morphology and size (22–50 nm), crystalline nature, and colloidal stability. In vitro antifungal activity against P. graminis , P. triticina , and P. striiformis was evaluated by cavity slide method. AgNPs exhibited dose-dependent inhibition of uredospore germination, achieving 98.49 ± 0.3% suppression of P. graminis , 98.38 ± 0.3% of P. striiformis , and 99.71 ± 0.2% of P. triticina at 40 ppm. The use of a single green-synthesized AgNP system against all three major wheat rust pathogens highlights its potential as a broad-spectrum approach for wheat rust management. These findings highlight the potential of Eucalyptus -derived AgNPs as an eco-friendly alternative for the management of wheat rust pathogens under in vitro conditions. However, further greenhouse and field studies are required to validate their efficacy, phytotoxicity, and environmental safety before agricultural application.

Article.Title: Effect of in-situ mechanochemical activation on the macroscopic properties and microstructure of graphite tailings-based autoclaved aerated concrete
Article.Authors: Yang P.; Sun K.
Article.Abstract: Graphite tailings (GTs) are hindered from direct AAC application by inherently poor hydrothermal reactivity. This study introduces an alkali-mechanical synergistic, in-situ mechanochemical activation strategy whereby GTs are co-ground with NaOH to boost reactivity for AAC synthesis. Systematic investigation reveals that within a reasonable activation time range, this strategy optimizes pore architecture, and concurrently enhances compressive strength while reducing bulk density. The 30 min co-ground specimen (A30) delivered optimal properties: 3.89 MPa compressive strength and 626 kg/m³ bulk density, fully complying with the A3.5 B06 grade criteria of GB/T 11,968–2020. Microstructural analyses verify that the activation accelerates silicon dissolution and intensifies hydrothermal reactions, augmenting tobermorite abundance and crystallinity while fostering a morphological evolution from acicular and fibrous crystals toward plate-like structures. These findings establish a transferable paradigm for GTs valorization and furnish critical theoretical underpinnings for scaling comparable siliceous wastes in sustainable construction materials.

Article.Title: The impact of achieving poverty eradication SDG1 on AIDS incidence in Latin America by 2030: a multi-country mathematical modeling analysis
Article.Authors: Bertoni A.; Rubio F.; Ordoñez J.; Anderle R.; Pinto P.; Chivardi C.; Moncayo A.; de Souza L.; Macinko J.; Dourado I.; Rasellaf D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The global polycrisis has intensified poverty and social inequalities, increasing the vulnerability of disadvantaged populations to HIV infection and progression to AIDS. Our study examined how ending poverty by 2030, the sustainable development goal 1 (SDG1) could influence AIDS incidence in seven Latin American countries. Utilizing country-specific compartmental models, we projected trends of AIDS incidence from 2020 to 2030. We integrated poverty trends into the models across three potential scenarios: increasing poverty due to economic downturns, a baseline (steady-state trend), and one where poverty decreases until eradication by 2030. Our study analyzed Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, and Peru, that represents 76.3% of the LA population. Under a scenario of gradually increasing poverty, our estimates indicate a rise in AIDS incidence from 6.13% (95% CI: 5.96–6.21) in Argentina to 13.87% (95% CI: 13.53–14.12) in Ecuador, compared to the baseline scenario. In the SDG1 scenario, AIDS incidence would decrease in all countries, with reductions ranging from 3.75% (95% CI: 3.65–3.74) in Chile to 14.15% (95% CI: 14.01–14.34) in Colombia. Our analysis indicates that poverty eradication (SDG 1) may help reduce the HIV/AIDS burden in Latin America, with potential relevance for other low- and middle-income countries, supportin progress toward SDG 3.3 related to HIV/AIDS.

Article.Authors: Ceylan İ.; Dalakçı M.; Canlı M.; Kürtüncüoğlu B.; Ilgar M.; Aydın B.; Alkan H.; Canlı İ.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the validity and test–retest reliability of the One-Minute Sit-to-Stand Test (1STS) in individuals with Parkinson’s disease (PD). Concurrent validity was examined using correlations with the 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT) and the Hoehn and Yahr (H&Y) stage. Test–retest reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). The 1STS showed a strong positive correlation with the 2MWT ( r = 0.69, p < 0.01) and a moderate negative correlation with the H&Y stage ( r = − 0.58, p < 0.01). Test–retest reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.86–0.97). The 1STS is a reliable and potentially valid measure of functional performance in individuals with PD. Article.Title: TransVJ2-MCA: power line defect recognition integrating video world model priors and cross-attention
Article.Authors: Xu L.; Wu X.; Liu Y.; Peng Y.
Article.Abstract: To address the dual challenges of scarce defect samples in power line component images and fine-grained defects being easily overwhelmed in complex backgrounds, this paper proposes a video world model prior-driven component defect recognition framework, TransVJ2-MCA. First, a cross-modal temporal reconstruction (CMTR) mechanism is designed to adapt to the input constraints of the video self-supervised pre-trained backbone network (V-JEPA v2). By replicating single-frame power line component images along the temporal dimension and converting them into stationary pseudo-video sequences, static images are aligned with the V-JEPA v2 encoder in both input form and feature distribution. A parameter-freezing strategy is then adopted to reuse the large-scale spatio-temporal structural priors embedded in the model, mitigating the limitation imposed by scarce defect samples on model training. Finally, a multi-scale cross-attention (MCA) module is constructed, which uses deep semantic features as guidance to selectively aggregate key discriminative information from shallow features, enabling effective selection and adaptive fusion of cross-level features, suppressing complex background interference, and enhancing fine-grained defect recognition capability. Experimental validation is conducted on five independent power line component classification tasks of the InsPLAD-Fault dataset. The results show that TransVJ2-MCA achieves an average balanced accuracy of 98.2% and a macro-average F1 score of 97.1%, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method under complex backgrounds and scarce defect samples, as well as its cross-modal transfer capability. This study provides a referential adaptation paradigm for transferring video pre-trained large models to static industrial visual inspection.

Article.Title: A non-compensatory screening framework for environmental, cost, and supply-risk trade-offs across China-relevant hydrogen production pathway archetypes
Article.Authors: Yuan C.; Tan Y.; Yuan X.; Tan Q.
Article.Abstract: Hydrogen can reduce emissions in hard-to-abate sectors, yet low-carbon production technologies introduce material, trade, and institutional dependencies that conventional life-cycle studies may not capture. This study develops a literature-calibrated, non-compensatory screening framework for three regionally framed, China-relevant pathway archetypes: Xinjiang-framed photovoltaic-powered proton-exchange-membrane electrolysis (green H 2 ), Shanxi-framed coal gasification with carbon capture, utilization and storage (blue H 2 ), and eastern-China-framed natural-gas steam-methane reforming (grey H 2 ). Environmental benchmarks, cost references, selected social questions, and an author-constructed illustrative supply-exposure score are reported separately. The adopted greenhouse-gas benchmarks are 2.5, 11.8, and 13.9 kg CO 2 -eq kg H 2 −1 , respectively; they are non-harmonized literature benchmarks rather than recalculated or site-specific estimates. The solar-electricity case has the lowest adopted benchmark, while the PV–PEM archetype has the highest illustrative supply-exposure score (GPRI 0.74). Under material-supply stress, its LCOH rises from 18.5 to 19.9 CNY kg H 2 −1 , whereas the technology-advance case lowers it to 15.0. Under Combined Adverse Conditions, LCOH rises to 21.7, 15.7, and 14.2 CNY kg H 2 −1 for the green, blue, and grey archetypes. These conditional results identify project-level questions and do not establish a national pathway ranking.

Article.Title: Hydrogen sulfide attenuates post-myocardial infarction cardiac fibrosis by modulating SENP1-dependent TEAD1 SUMOylation
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Li W.; Dai W.; Chen C.; Tan W.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Cardiac fibrosis (CF) after myocardial infarction (MI) is characterized by excessive collagen deposition and adverse ventricular remodeling, which contribute to impaired cardiac function. Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S), an endogenous gasotransmitter, has shown anti-fibrotic potential, but its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In vitro, NaHS reduced Ang II-induced HCF viability, migration, fibrosis-related protein expression, and TEAD1-YAP co-localization. SENP1 knockdown or TEAD1 overexpression partially reversed the protective effects of NaHS in Ang II-treated HCFs. Mechanistically, NaHS increased SENP1 S-sulfhydration and reduced TEAD1-associated SUMO1/SUMO2/3 signals detected by endogenous TEAD1 immunoprecipitation, while SENP1 knockdown weakened the inhibitory effect of NaHS on TEAD1 SUMOylation. These findings suggest that H₂S attenuates post-MI cardiac fibrosis, at least in part, by modulating SENP1-associated regulation of TEAD1 SUMOylation and TEAD1/YAP signaling. This study provides preclinical evidence for a potential anti-fibrotic mechanism of H₂S in post-MI cardiac remodeling.

Longitudinal studies and methodological validation are required before considering prognostic or intervention applications.

Article.Title: Feasibility of diffuse reflectance spectroscopy for tumor border detection in colorectal cancer surgery
Article.Authors: Hepkema J.; Boeije I.; Aalbers A.; Grotenhuis B.; Westerterp M.; Geldof F.; Dashtbozorg B.; Ruers T.
Article.Abstract: Adequate distal resection margins (DRM) in colorectal cancer surgery are critical for oncological safety while preserving sphincter function. In this study, continuous measurements were performed on freshly excised colorectal specimens using a broadband DRS system (400–1600 nm). A binary classification approach was applied to discriminate between non-tumor and tumor locations. Multiple feature extraction strategies were evaluated in combination with different classifiers and hyperparameter tuning was performed. A total of 39,741 spectra (22,451 non-tumor, 17,290 tumor) from 86 patients were included. Using the first derivative of the spectra paired with a radial basis function (RBF) support vector machine achieved good results, reaching a mean Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.76 ± 0.27 across patients. Sensitivity and specificity were 0.93 ± 0.13 and 0.88 ± 0.17, respectively. This study demonstrates the feasibility of using DRS combined with machine learning to distinguish tumor from non-tumor regions in colorectal cancer surgery. Future work should focus on prospective validation of distal margin assessment and exploring probe designs with deeper penetration to enhance intra-operative applicability.

These findings indicate that the selected isolates possess multifunctional in vitro properties that are relevant to both probiotic and biological control applications. Article.Title: Comprehensive analysis of chromosomal and plasmid-borne AMR determinants in Campylobacter coli Italian isolates from broilers
Article.Authors: Smedile D.; di Matteo P.; Iurescia M.; Dell’Aira E.; Buccella C.; Sorbara L.; Donati V.; Franco A.; Battisti A.; Alba P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Campylobacter coli is a key zoonotic pathogen and, owing to its close phylogenetic relationship and shared ecological niches with Campylobacter jejuni , an important reservoir of antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) determinants that can be horizontally transferred between these two species. Here, we provide a genomic overview of Italian C. coli isolates collected from broilers during the 2022 EU harmonised monitoring program, with a specific focus on the contribution of plasmids and other mobile genetic elements to the maintenance and spread of acquired AMR. Eight isolates were additionally sequenced with Oxford Nanopore long reads and reconstructed via hybrid assembly (Unicycler v0.4.9 and v0.5.1; Plassembler v1.6.2) to resolve chromosomal and plasmid structures and to obtain a complete genomic characterization. AMR determinants were widespread, including high prevalence of tet O (92%, 48/52), bla OXA genes (71%, 37/52), and the fluoroquinolone-associated gyr A T86I substitution (88%, 46/52). Hybrid assemblies showed that, despite the canonical association of acquired AMR with plasmids, most resistance determinants were located on the chromosome, usually in contexts suggestive of transformation or transposition (e.g., IS-associated arrangements), while plasmid-borne ARGs were unequivocally identified only in a subset of isolates. Furthermore, a custom cgMLST scheme has been created as a highly sensitive and discriminatory tool for comparison of genomically homogeneous Campylobacter populations.

Article.Title: A calculation model for the loess collapse coefficient considering progressive wetting dry density and applied vertical pressure
Article.Authors: Zhang A.; Du J.; Liang Z.
Article.Abstract: Predicting wetting-induced collapse of loess requires accounting for the coupled effects of applied pressure, moisture state, and pore structure. The main contribution is a continuous parameterization that allows the collapse coefficient to be calculated across the investigated soil states without independently refitting each water-content–dry-density combination. The model describes the nonlinear pressure-dependent response and incorporates moisture and pore-structure effects through saturation- and void-ratio-dependent parameters. Evaluation against the laboratory data yielded an overall coefficient of determination of R 2 = 0.783. A dimensionless wetting parameter was introduced to evaluate changes in remaining collapse potential across independently prepared moisture states within the tested range. An engineering-scale application to a 30 m loess profile predicted a self-weight collapse settlement of 3330.71 mm, compared with a reported field measurement of 3520 mm, corresponding to a relative error of 5.38%. Because some field conditions exceeded the laboratory calibration range, this comparison indicates application potential rather than general validation. The proposed formulation links routinely measured soil properties with collapse-coefficient estimation and layerwise settlement assessment.

Article.Title: Oscillometry-defined small airway dysfunction as a predictor of moderate-to-severe exacerbations in COPD: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Mari P.; Carriera L.; Ielo S.; Coppola A.; Siciliano M.; Ojetti V.; Baglioni S.; Scala R.; Ricci A.
Article.Abstract: Small airway dysfunction (SAD) is a pivotal feature of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), yet spirometry has limited sensitivity for peripheral airway impairment. Oscillometry offers effort-independent assessment of respiratory mechanics during tidal breathing. We systematically reviewed longitudinal studies reporting the association between baseline oscillometry and subsequent moderate-to-severe acute exacerbations (AE) in COPD. Ratio estimates (OR, HR, IRR) were pooled using a DerSimonian–Laird random-effects model, with sensitivity analyses for effect metric, follow-up, study quality and estimate selection. Six studies (1,317 unique patients; follow-up 1–5 years) met inclusion criteria, and four independent cohorts ( n = 1,236) contributed to the meta-analysis. Oscillometry-defined SAD was associated with a higher risk of moderate-to-severe AE (pooled estimate 2.28, 95% CI 1.77–2.94; I² = 0%; 95% prediction interval 1.31–3.98). The association persisted when restricted to hazard and rate ratios (2.23, 95% CI 1.67–2.98) and when the lowest available estimate from each study was pooled (1.60, 95% CI 1.16–2.22). Evidence on discrimination relative to FEV₁ was limited to a single cohort, in which R5–R20 and FEV₁ performed similarly (AUC 0.775 vs. 0.777). Within this small evidence base, oscillometry-defined SAD was associated with exacerbation risk; larger cohorts should define outcome-anchored thresholds and incremental value over spirometry.

Article.Title: Association of physical activity with all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality among adults with diabetes: Mexico City Prospective Study
Article.Authors: de Victo E.; Rezende L.; de Almeida-Pititto B.; Wahrhaftig J.; da Silva W.; Christofaro D.; Marques A.; Peralta M.; Wang Y.; Barahona-Fuentes G.; Ferrari G.
Article.Abstract: This study examined the association between physical activity (PA) and all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality among adults with diabetes. A total of 28,573 individuals aged ≥ 35 years from the Mexico City Prospective Study were included. PA was self-reported and categorized by frequency (< 1, 1–2, or ≥ 3 times/week), duration (< 30, 30–60, or > 60 min/session), and volume (combination of frequency and duration). Mean follow-up was 15.2 ± 5.7 years. For all-cause mortality, high PA frequency was associated with lower risk compared with low frequency (HR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.84–0.94). High PA duration and volume were also associated with lower risk compared with low (HR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.76–0.91 and HR: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.80–0.91, respectively); high volume was also associated with lower risk compared with medium volume (HR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.81–0.98). For cardiovascular mortality, high PA frequency, duration and volume were associated with lower risk compared with low levels (HR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.81–0.99; HR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.71–0.97; and HR: 0.82; 95% CI: 0.73–0.92, respectively). PA was not associated with cancer mortality.

Article.Title: Complementary and alternative medicine use for self-care of minor wounds and injuries among a convenience sample of palestinian adults
Article.Authors: Nori S.; Bdair M.; Sobeih A.; Mahmoud S.; Theeb S.; zaqah L.; Malhis L.
Article.Abstract: Complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) is used for self-care of minor wounds and injuries, but evidence on these practices in Palestine is limited. This cross-sectional electronic survey assessed CAM use and associated factors among 441 Palestinian adults recruited through convenience sampling between February and May 2026; the sample was predominantly young, female, and university-educated. CAM use was defined as self-reported use of any natural, traditional, or non-conventional remedy for a minor wound during the previous year. Overall, 235 participants (53.3%) reported CAM use. Among users answering the consultation item, 71.6% reported no consultation with a specialist, 42.3% reported antibiotic co-use (prescription status, route, and clinical indication were not assessed), 22.2% self-reported complications, and 31.1% reported needing a later physician visit. In multivariable analysis, CAM use was associated with age ≥ 46 years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 9.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.36–62.45; P = 0.023), government employment versus student status (aOR 3.62, 95% CI 1.20–10.89; P = 0.022), awareness of traditional or natural wound remedies (aOR 2.45, 95% CI 1.21–4.96; P = 0.013), and perceiving CAM as safe for minor wounds (aOR 2.82, 95% CI 1.53–5.23; P < 0.001); the wide confidence interval for the age ≥ 46 years association indicates imprecision. These findings demonstrate frequent CAM use for minor wound self-care in this convenience sample, but the electronic convenience sampling and demographic composition limit generalizability to the broader Palestinian adult population, and the observed 53.3% prevalence should not be interpreted as representative of Palestinian adults nationally.

Article.Title: Point-of-care hearing screening using consumer wireless earbuds in patients with USH2A-associated retinal disease: a prospective pilot feasibility study
Article.Authors: Huang A.; Tang R.; George L.; Ong C.; Sun C.; Ibrahim F.; Chan H.; Wirayasaputra S.; Mathur R.; Chan C.; Yeo I.; Tan B.; Tan A.; Cheung C.; Fenner B.
Article.Abstract: Usher syndrome type 2 (USH2) may be under-recognized in ophthalmology practice due to variable hearing loss severity and limited point-of-care audiometry. In this prospective pilot study at the Singapore National Eye Centre (November 2024 to February 2025) we evaluated a consumer earbud hearing test in patients with USH2A-associated retinal disease and explored cross-sectional relationships between hearing and visual measures. Thirteen patients with biallelic USH2A pathogenic variants (median age 45 years, range 29-81) and thirteen age- and sex-matched comparison participants underwent supervised air-conduction threshold estimation using AirPods Pro 2. All participants completed testing without failure, repetition or technical error. Among patients, median test duration was 4.5 minutes (range 3.6–5.1), and three required physical guidance. These feasibility outcomes are reported descriptively and post hoc. Right-ear pure-tone average (PTA4-R) ranged from 13.00 to 84.25 dB HL (median 48.25 dB HL) and ellipsoid zone (EZ) width ranged from 0 to 7,972 μm (median 1,037 μm). After adjustment for age, higher PTA4-R showed a negative association estimate with EZ width (β = −57.36 μm/dB, 95% CI −117.56 to 2.83; nominal p = 0.0597) and a positive association estimate with best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) in logMAR units (β = 0.02793 logMAR/dB, 95% CI 0.00429 to 0.05156; nominal p = 0.0251). Neither met the Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold (adjusted p = 0.1194 and 0.0501, respectively). Earbud-derived threshold configurations resembled previously described USH2A-associated patterns, but agreement with calibrated clinical audiometry was not assessed. Formal audiological evaluation remains necessary for diagnosis and management.

Article.Title: Parents’ perceptions of high-quality nursing care for children with cancer: a qualitative descriptive study
Article.Authors: Sheikhzakaryaee N.; Azami G.; Seidi J.
Article.Abstract: Parents remain closely involved in caring for children hospitalized with cancer, yet nursing quality extends beyond clinical task performance. Although previous studies have identified important aspects of pediatric oncology nursing care, less is known about how parents integrate these dimensions when evaluating overall care quality. To describe parents’ perceptions of high-quality nursing care for children hospitalized with cancer and explore how these dimensions shape parental confidence in care reliability. A qualitative descriptive study was conducted in a pediatric oncology ward in Sanandaj, Iran. Sixteen parents (14 mothers and two fathers) participated in semi-structured interviews, and seven completed follow-up interviews, resulting in 23 interview encounters. Data were analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis. Reflexive notes, field notes, an audit trail, collaborative analytic review, and participant follow-up supported trustworthiness. Five interconnected categories were identified: building a respectful and responsive care relationship; demonstrating clinical vigilance and technical competence; providing emotional security and child-centered support; enabling parental caregiving through practical education; and organizational conditions constraining reliable care. Parents evaluated nursing quality through the interaction of these dimensions. Parental confidence emerged as an integrated interpretation reflecting perceptions of care as safe, responsive, individualized, and dependable. Confidence was challenged when parents perceived workload pressures, overcrowding, staffing concerns, or variability in expertise as affecting care consistency. Parent-perceived nursing quality in pediatric oncology was described as multidimensional, reflecting parents’ perceptions of interactions between nursing practices and contextual conditions. Future quality-improvement efforts may consider communication, competence, emotional support, education, and organizational factors that parents perceive as influencing reliable care delivery.

Article.Title: Activation of the Hippo pathway by the MIAT/miR-877-5p/UBN2 axis contributes to keloid formation
Article.Authors: Zhou X.; Lin X.; Pan M.; Xie R.; Xie L.; Huang Y.; Yang J.; Hong T.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: Keloid is a prevalent fibroproliferative condition characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation and presents a significant clinical challenge. Despite the recognized association of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) with keloid pathogenesis, their specific roles remain undefined. Here, we identified the lncRNA MIAT as markedly upregulated in keloid tissues and human keloid fibroblasts (HKFs) through bioinformatics analysis of GEO datasets (GSE182192) and experimental validation. Functional assays showed that MIAT silencing in HKFs suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, ECM deposition (α-SMA, COL1, COL2), and promoted apoptosis. MIAT localized in the cytoplasm and acted as a molecular sponge for miR-877-5p, relieving inhibition of UBN2 and promoting its expression. The MIAT/miR-877-5p/UBN2 axis was confirmed by dual-luciferase reporter and RIP assays. Rescue assays demonstrated that miR-877-5p inhibition counteracted the phenotypic changes induced by MIAT knockdown. UBN2 promoted Hippo pathway transcription by binding TEAD2 and facilitating its nuclear translocation, upregulating CTGF and CYR61. Crucially, in a keloid xenograft model, MIAT knockdown suppressed keloid growth, reversed by simultaneous miR-877-5p inhibition, with altered UBN2 protein levels. Collectively, our findings preliminarily indicate that the MIAT/miR-877-5p/UBN2 axis promotes keloid progression partly through Hippo activation, providing new molecular clues for understanding keloid pathogenesis.

Article.Title: Lightweight hierarchical composite aerogel for ultrawideband microwave absorption
Article.Authors: Dehghani-Dashtabi M.; Hekmatara H.; Mohebbi M.
Article.Abstract: Lightweight aerogel absorbers, especially with polymer, carbon and mineral structures, are considered to be the most efficient materials for microwave absorption. Here, montmorillonite (MMT) nanosheets were decorated by MoSe 2 and activated carbon (AC) nanoparticles to form MoSe₂/AC/MMT composite. Then, MoSe₂/AC/MMT was loaded into the chitosan matrix as filler, with different weight percentage of 35, 50, and 75 to produce MoSe₂/AC/MMT–Chitosan aerogels named as Ch2-Ch4, and a sample without AC, named as Ch1. The results showed that, Ch3 was the optimal sample with the highest minimum reflection loss (-88 dB) at a thickness of 2.6 mm. All samples had broad absorption bands covering the entire X and Ku bands. Covering a spherical perfect electric conductor (PEC) with each aerogel reduces the radar cross section (RCS) and scattered far field by 30–60 dB and 30–33 dB, respectively Therefore, the MoSe 2 /AC/MMT–Chitosan aerogel demonstrates promising potential for lightweight microwave absorption applications.

Article.Title: Unsupervised learning on advanced diffusion MRI metrics for clinical characterization of migraine
Article.Authors: Gallo A.; Tristán-Vega A.; Guerrero Á.; García-Azorín D.; Aja-Fernández S.; de Luis-García R.; Planchuelo-Gómez Á.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Current migraine classification does not fully capture its clinical heterogeneity, and no objective biomarkers are available for diagnosis or progression. Neuroimaging, especially Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), offers promising biomarkers; however, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) oversimplifies diffusion properties, motivating the development of advanced approaches compatible with clinical routine. We applied unsupervised machine learning to diffusion MRI data to explore patient stratification and evaluate whether sophisticated diffusion techniques, such as AMURA, provide information complementary to DTI. A total of 107 patients with migraine (56 chronic [CM], 51 episodic [EM]) were included. Diffusion metrics from 48 white matter regions were extracted using standard DTI parameters and advanced AMURA descriptors, alone or combined with DTI. After dimensionality reduction and feature selection, unsupervised clustering was performed using K-means, Agglomerative, and Spectral algorithms. Two clusters consistently emerged, each characterized by distinct clinical features. DTI mainly separated patients based on chronicity-related features, particularly time since onset of CM, and showed an incremental longitudinal association with topiramate response. AMURA-based clusters were associated with migraine frequency, disease duration, and medication overuse headache. These results position the combination of advanced diffusion descriptors and unsupervised learning as an exploratory framework for migraine characterization requiring independent validation.

Article.Title: Integrated haematological, inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers in steady-state and vaso-occlusive crisis of sickle cell disease: a case-control study in Benin City
Article.Authors: Adejumo B.; Udemezue N.; Adebowale M.; Abdukaldir U.; Aiyesoro O.; Olise N.; Adegboye A.; Obiajunwa A.; Abolarin O.; Drisu U.; Ilekuba K.; Ebhohimhen B.; Kamdem A.; Dasari P.; Aliu A.
Article.Abstract: Integrated evidence on haematological, inflammatory, and endothelial biomarker profiles across clinically distinct sickle cell disease (SCD) states remains limited in African populations. This study evaluated these biomarkers among individuals with steady-state SCD, vaso-occlusive crisis (VOC), and healthy controls in Benin City, Nigeria. This case-control study included 89 participants: 20 with steady-state SCD, 32 presenting with VOC, and 37 healthy controls. Haematological parameters, complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices, C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and soluble vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (sVCAM-1) were assessed. Between-group differences and the within-cohort discrimination of VOC from steady-state SCD were evaluated using conventional and exploratory multivariable approaches. Participants with VOC showed greater haematological abnormalities and inflammatory and endothelial activation than those in steady state. Among individual markers, NLR, CRP, IL-6, and sVCAM-1 showed comparatively strong within-cohort discrimination of VOC status, with AUCs of 0.816, 0.857, 0.882, and 0.901, respectively. An integrated biomarker model yielded an AUC of 0.938, although performance was estimated within the same modest SCD cohort. Inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers differed across SCD clinical states and showed potential as adjunctive markers of disease activity. Larger prospective studies accounting for treatment exposure and providing independent validation are required before clinical application.

Article.Title: Vapor-based sequential deposition of CsSnI3: analysis of phase evolution with in situ X-ray diffraction
Article.Authors: Lin J.; Scheer R.; Pistor P.
Article.Abstract: All-inorganic CsSnI 3 is a lead-free halide perovskite with promising applications, which has been successfully synthesized by a variety of methods. Although industrially attractive, its sequential vacuum-based synthesis through deposition and annealing is challenging, because precursor conversion and thermal degradation occur in adjacent temperature ranges. In this work, CsSnI 3 films are prepared by deposition of CsI and SnI 2 precursor layers by sequential evaporation, followed by a thermal annealing process. We monitor the evolution of different crystalline phases and their conversion and degradation by in situ X-ray diffraction (ISXRD) throughout the complete deposition-conversion-degradation sequence. Room-temperature deposition produces a crystalline precursor stack composed of CsI and strongly textured β-SnI 2 , with no apparent initial CsSnI 3 formation. Upon thermal processing with a temperature ramp, we observe phase transitions of the precursor phases, before a cubic α-CsSnI 3 perovskite phase is formed. At even higher temperatures, we track the intermediate phases and the full decomposition of the film. This ramp experiment allows us to identify an apparent process window for suitable processing temperatures for the successful synthesis of photoactive, black α-CsSnI 3 perovskite thin films under the presented conditions. Finally, we demonstrate the successful synthesis of black α-CsSnI 3 thin films upon isothermal annealing at 160 °C. SEM images reveal compact polycrystalline films, and EDX shows an I/Sn ratio close to the nominal value of 3.

Article.Title: Association and diagnostic value of maternal plasma and placental ghrelin levels in predicting early preterm birth: a case–control study
Article.Authors: Gül C.; Uçkan K.; Başkıran Y.; Taşdemir E.; Çeleğen İ.
Article.Abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide. While inflammation is a known trigger, the role of metabolic-endocrine mediators like ghrelin in the pathogenesis of prematurity remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic potential of maternal plasma and placental ghrelin levels in predicting early preterm birth and their relationship with systemic inflammatory markers. A total of 60 pregnant women were enrolled and categorized into three groups: Early Preterm (n = 19; < 34 weeks), Late Preterm (n = 17; 34–37 weeks), and Term Control (n = 24; 37–42 weeks). Maternal plasma and placental tissue ghrelin concentrations were quantified using ELISA. Systemic inflammation was assessed via the Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR) and total leukocyte counts. Statistical analysis included ROC curve and univariate logistic regression to determine predictive performance. Both maternal plasma and placental ghrelin levels were significantly higher in the early preterm group compared to late preterm and term cohorts ( p < 0.001). A strong positive correlation was observed between plasma and placental ghrelin concentrations (r = 0.54, p < 0.001). ROC analysis revealed that maternal plasma ghrelin shows high diagnostic performance in this cohort for predicting early PTB, with an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.982 (95% CI: 0.961–1.000) and a cut-off value of > 2797 pg/mL (Sensitivity: 92.0%, Specificity: 100.0%). Univariate logistic regression identified ghrelin as a significant risk factor for early delivery (OR: 1.011, p = 0.014). Notably, no significant correlation was found between ghrelin levels and inflammatory markers (NLR/WBC), suggesting a metabolic signaling pathway independent of generalized systemic inflammation. Elevated maternal plasma and placental ghrelin levels are closely associated with early preterm birth. Given its high diagnostic accuracy and independence from systemic inflammatory markers, maternal ghrelin may serve as a promising predictive biomarker for identifying pregnancies at risk for early spontaneous preterm labor.

Article.Title: Influence of extraction techniques on the chemical composition, antioxidant, and enzyme inhibitory activities of cumin (Cuminum cyminum L.) essential oils
Article.Authors: El-Din M.; Korany D.; Zengin G.; Eldahshan O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cuminum cyminum L. is an aromatic spice valued for its essential oil and associated biological activities. This study investigated the impact of extraction technique on the yield, chemical composition, antioxidant activity, enzyme inhibition, and in silico biological potential of cumin essential oil, providing the first direct comparison of hydro-distillation, steam distillation, and microwave-assisted extraction under comparable conditions. Essential oil yields ranged from 0.8% to 1.4% (v/w), with hydro-distillation producing significantly the highest yield ( p < 0.05). GC–MS analysis identified 27 volatile compounds (> 97% of the total composition), with cuminaldehyde as the major constituent across all methods. Antioxidant assays showed comparable radical-scavenging activities, with the microwave-assisted oil exhibiting slightly higher DPPH and ABTS activities, whereas the hydro-distilled oil demonstrated superior reducing power in the CUPRAC and FRAP assays. The microwave-assisted extract showed the strongest acetylcholinesterase inhibition, whereas the hydro-distilled oil displayed higher inhibition of butyrylcholinesterase, α-amylase, and α-glucosidase. In silico ADME analysis indicated favorable drug-likeness and pharmacokinetic properties for all identified compounds, and molecular docking revealed acceptable binding affinities toward key metabolic and neurodegenerative enzymes, highlighting γ-muurolene, caryophyllene, and carotol as promising bioactive constituents. Overall, the findings emphasize the importance of the extraction technique in modulating the bioactivity of cumin essential oil.

Article.Title: Challenging a role for ceramide channels and microdomains in apoptosis induction using a bottom-up approach
Article.Authors: Wessing M.; Webersinn P.; Klaßen S.; Fiedler B.; Cosentino K.; Holthuis J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ceramides are essential but potentially toxic intermediates of sphingolipid metabolism that can act directly on mitochondria to trigger apoptotic cell death, but the underlying mechanism is unclear. While one model postulates that ceramides form stable channels in the outer mitochondrial membrane that induce cell death through direct release of cytochrome c, an alternative view is that ceramides self-assemble into microdomains that facilitate membrane insertion and oligomerization of the pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 protein Bax into cytochrome c -conducting pores. To challenge these models, we here analyzed the influence of ceramides in combination with recombinant Bax on the leakiness of model membranes. We show that ceramides on their own are unable to support membrane passage of even the smallest fluorescence markers. Moreover, we find that ceramides cannot substitute for cardiolipin in facilitating membrane recruitment of Bax and its subsequent assembly into functional pores. Our data argue against a direct role of ceramides in apoptotic pore formation and indicate that the mechanism by which ceramides initiate permeabilization of the outer mitochondrial membrane is independent of ceramide channels or ceramide acting autonomously as translocation platform for Bax.

Article.Title: The impact of ionic liquid formation on the activity, solubility and pharmacokinetics of rifampicin
Article.Authors: Rasmy H.; Ramadan Y.; Mousa H.; Hetta H.; Ibrahim E.; Abouelmagd S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rifampicin (RIF) is a key first-line antitubercular agent. However, its clinical utility is hindered by poor solubility and suboptimal oral absorption. When paired with oppositely charged citric acid (CA) at 1:5 molar ratio, the interaction yields an active pharmaceutical ingredient ionic liquid (API-IL); RIF-CA IL. This transformation resulted in a new liquid form that modulated RIF’s physicochemical properties. This study explores the pharmaceutical and biological properties of a RIF-CA IL, 1:5. The conditions of the solvent-evaporation method were found to be critical for its stability and antimicrobial activity. Spectroscopic analyses confirmed IL formation and significant intermolecular interactions. RIF-CA IL exhibited improved wettability and hydrophilicity, resulting in a 20-fold increase in RIF saturation solubility. The IL had comparable cytotoxicity and cellular uptake to RIF in A549 lung cells. A Novel greenness-assisted HPLC method was developed to precisely and selectively determine rifampicin levels in serum. An in-vivo pharmacokinetic study in rabbits demonstrated a more than 2.2-fold increase in oral bioavailability compared to native RIF. Notably, these enhancements were not observed with a physical mixture of RIF and CA at the same molar ratio. These results suggest RIF-CA IL is a promising alternative to conventional RIF form with comparable bioactivity, yet superior bioavailability.

Article.Title: Exonuclease 1 drives immune escape in lung adenocarcinoma by regulating the HIF-1α/PD-L1 axis
Article.Authors: Gao C.; Zhang L.; Gao B.; Fan J.; Kong D.
Article.Abstract: Lung Adenocarcinoma (LUAD) represents the most prevalent subtype of lung cancer and additionally possesses the highest potential for lethality. EXO1 is overexpressed in multiple cancers and linked to poor prognosis, but its role in LUAD immune regulation remains unclear. Immunosuppression can be stimulated by HIF-1α, with the underlying mechanism being the upregulation of PD-L1. Our hypothesis is that EXO1 facilitates immune evasion in LUAD by influencing the HIF-1α-PD-L1 axis. Bioinformatic analysis of TCGA data and clinical samples validated EXO1 expression and prognosis correlation. In vitro and in vivo models including EXO1 knockdown/overexpression in LUAD cell lines were established. Functional assays (CCK-8, Transwell, wound healing, colony formation) and xenograft models assessed proliferation, migration, invasion and tumor growth. Immune interactions were evaluated via co-culture systems with T cells, flow cytometry, western blot and immunofluorescence. HIF-1α inhibitor PX-478 was used in rescue experiments. EXO1 was significantly overexpressed in LUAD tissues and cell lines, correlating with advanced tumor stage, poor survival, and reduced CD4+ /CD8+ T-cell infiltration. EXO1 knockdown suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion and tumor growth in mice, while overexpression promoted these malignant phenotypes. EXO1 upregulated PD-L1 expression, inhibited T-cell cytotoxicity (reduced granzyme B and perforin), and enhanced resistance to T-cell-induced apoptosis. EXO1 facilitated HIF-1α nuclear translocation; HIF-1α inhibition reversed EXO1-driven PD-L1 upregulation and restored T-cell infiltration, while partially attenuating the anti-apoptotic effects mediated by EXO1 in vivo. EXO1 drives LUAD progression and immune escape by regulating the HIF-1α-PD-L1 axis. It serves as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target, with HIF-1α inhibition offering a promising strategy to counteract EXO1-mediated immunosuppression in LUAD.

Article.Title: A RAG-enhanced multi-agent LLM/VLM framework for auditable and region-aware structural health monitoring of a historic masonry structure
Article.Authors: Hacıefendioğlu K.; Kahya V.; Aslan T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Historic masonry structures require monitoring workflows that are non-destructive, interpretable, and robust to field variability. This paper presents a proof-of-concept, RAG-enhanced structural health monitoring (SHM) workflow demonstrated on a single historic masonry minaret case study, in which a manager–orchestrator coordinates signal analysis, visual analysis, and cross-modal fusion. Vibration data from four sensors installed on this minaret are processed through a reproducible pipeline that includes data cleaning, PSD-based baseline characterisation, adaptive windowing, robust normalisation, and anomaly screening with a 1D convolutional autoencoder trained on healthy reference data (Measurements 1–12), followed by evaluation on Measurements 13–20. Localisation is strengthened through relation-based autoencoders on sensor pairs and sensor-to-zone damage mapping. In parallel, a VLM analyses sensor-linked inspection images from the same case study, while a curated retrieval-augmented structural memory package for the monitored minaret (geometry, materials, baseline dynamics, FE notes, and inspection playbook) supports context-aware interpretation. A three-agent decision layer (Agent A: LLM+RAG, Agent B: VLM+RAG, Agent C: fusion + RAG) reconciles agreements and conflicts between signal- and image-derived evidence to produce case-specific global and zone-level risk assessments. The study compares with-RAG and without-RAG analysis modes within this single deployment and reports structured, traceable outputs, including JSON artefacts, per-image findings, per-sensor summaries, narrative reports, and final risk maps. Its main contribution is to demonstrate how signal-derived anomalies, image-derived evidence, and retrieval-grounded structural memory can be combined within a traceable multi-agent SHM workflow for one monitored historic masonry minaret.

Article.Title: Systematic validation of zucker diabetic-sprague dawley male rats as a model for type 2 diabetes-associated diabetic retinopathy
Article.Authors: Zhang G.; Shi W.; Zhang S.; Xu W.; Liu X.; Pan L.; Pang L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Zucker Diabetic Sprague-Dawley (ZDSD) rat is an emerging model for type 2 diabetes, but its suitability for diabetic retinopathy (DR) research remains unvalidated. This study aimed to perform a systematic, multimodal characterization of DR in the ZDSD rats to assess its translational relevance. Male ZDSD rats were fed a high-fat diet to induce diabetes, forming Diabetic and Normoglycemic Control groups ( n = 8 per group), alongside healthy Sprague-Dawley control ( n = 8). Metabolic parameters were monitored from 27 to 36 weeks. Retinal assessment combined in vivo imaging (OCTA, FFA, OCT), histology (H&E staining), and molecular biology (qRT-PCR, Western blot, IHC, ELISA) to quantify key DR mediators: inflammatory factors (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), VEGF, and Caspase-3. Diabetic ZDSD rats exhibited severe hyperglycemia, polydipsia, and weight loss. Retinal imaging revealed significant pathology, including progressive reduction in vascular density (OCTA), retinal thinning (OCT), and microvascular leakage (FFA). Histology confirmed structural disorganization and reduced retinal ganglion cell and photoreceptor density. Molecular analyses demonstrated significant upregulation of retinal inflammatory cytokines, elevated VEGF expression in retinal tissue and aqueous humor, and increased Caspase-3, indicating enhanced apoptosis. The ZDSD rat model reproduces several key metabolic, microvascular, structural, and molecular hallmarks of human non-proliferative DR. These findings support its potential utility as a relevant platform for investigating NPDR pathogenesis and evaluating early-stage therapeutics.

Article.Title: Interpretable water and agricultural land cover in urban landscapes using CNN–ViT framework with Grad-CAM for agricultural sustainability
Article.Authors: Addeen H.; Senan E.; Aklan F.; Alwazer S.; Alshari E.; Khan M.; Ahmed I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate land-use and land-cover classification in hyper-arid environments is challenging because several surface types can exhibit overlapping spectral and spatial characteristics in Landsat imagery. These surfaces include water, irrigated agriculture, moist soil, barren land, and built-up areas. This study proposes an interpretable hybrid framework for classifying six land-use and land-cover classes in Najran, Saudi Arabia, using seven-band Landsat 8 imagery. The framework integrates MobileNetV2, ResNet152, and ViT-B/16 to combine efficient local feature extraction, deep hierarchical representation learning, and global contextual modeling. This combination was selected to address the heterogeneous landscape patterns and mixed spectral responses that characterize the study area. Controlled ablation experiments showed progressive performance gains from the standalone CNN models to the CNN–ViT configurations and the complete three-branch framework. Overall accuracy increased from 86.73% to 88.23% for MobileNetV2 and ResNet152 to 94.98% and 95.68% for their respective CNN–ViT configurations. The complete framework achieved the highest overall accuracy of 98.70%, with a Kappa coefficient of 0.9827, on a geographically separate assessment partition. The F1-scores were 99.02% for Water Area, 98.38% for Agriculture, 98.64% for Built-up Area, and 99.16% for Barren Land. Other Land and Unclassified achieved F1-scores of 96.03% and 91.60%, respectively. Grad-CAM produced spatially coherent activation patterns over mapped water and cultivated surfaces. These patterns provided qualitative evidence that the model relied on landscape structures relevant to the predicted classes. The findings demonstrate that combining complementary local, hierarchical, and global representations improves both classification accuracy and model interpretability. The proposed framework therefore provides a reliable basis for land-use and land-cover monitoring in Najran and for further validation in other hyper-arid environments.

Article.Title: Measurement of contextual factors in clinical practice and research: development of an expert-informed toolkit
Article.Authors: Bent J.; Cook C.; Bailliard A.; Bialosky J.; Bishop F.; Carlino E.; Colloca L.; Esteves J.; Garcia A.; McDevitt A.; Napadow V.; Newell D.; Palese A.; Reed W.; Rossettini G.
Article.Abstract: Contextual factors (CFs) can influence therapeutic encounters and clinical outcomes, yet their measurement remains fragmented, lacking a unified framework to guide tool selection. To identify, appraise, and synthesize CF measurement instruments into an expert-informed clinical toolkit and identify current measurement gaps. An international panel of 15 experts evaluated 227 instruments across five domains (patient/practitioner characteristics, relational dynamics, environment, and treatment) using a hybrid COSMIN-informed appraisal design. Instruments were screened for content validity and psychometric robustness. Twenty instruments were selected for inclusion in the toolkit. Despite identifying high-quality instruments for stable traits, our analysis revealed critical measurement gaps in dynamic, state-responsive processes. Specifically, there is an absence of validated, clinically feasible tools for capturing real-time clinician affective states, non-verbal synchrony, therapeutic touch, and moment-to-moment environmental or procedural interactions. This study provides the first expert-informed framework for assessing CFs. Future research should prioritize developing state-responsive instruments capable of capturing these dynamic elements as they unfold in real-world settings to better understand the contextual drivers of recovery.

Article.Title: Joint molecular optimization for efficient virtual screening via machine learning
Article.Authors: Jain N.
Article.Abstract: Joint molecular optimization serves as the central focus of this research, which explores the synergistic integration of machine learning (ML) and virtual screening (VS) for drug discovery. This study addresses these limitations by integrating molecular docking and ML to predict and balance multiple molecular properties concurrently. Traditional VS methods often fall short by primarily targeting single molecular properties, such as binding affinity, overlooking the necessity of simultaneously optimizing multiple crucial parameters like ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) profiles. Key objectives include developing and evaluating multi-objective optimization strategies and employing ML models (e.g., logistic regression, SVM, neural networks) to enhance predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. This research balances efficacy and safety metrics to refine VS and demonstrates the effect of combining these strategies on benchmark data. This work contributes a controlled, reproducible framework and an explicitly defined multi-objective prioritization procedure intended to support more efficient and transparent virtual screening, offering valuable insights for researchers in drug discovery, computational chemistry, and ML. Claims of reduced clinical attrition or improved clinical success would require prospective experimental validation and lie beyond the scope of this computational study.

Article.Title: Shear strength behavior of frozen unsaturated sands under thermal loads
Article.Authors: Abhinav A.; Baser T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the mechanical behavior of frozen unsaturated sand under thermal gradients is crucial for the design and maintenance of infrastructure in permafrost regions. In this study the shear strength of Ottawa sand under varying temperatures, degrees of saturation, and loading conditions is investigated. A series of laboratory experiments were performed to measure the shear strength of Ottawa sand using direct simple shear equipment placed in a temperature controlled environmental chamber. During the experiments, soil temperatures and stress–strain curves were recorded, and they were analyzed to determine the strength behavior. Results show that shear strength increases with decreasing temperature, increasing ice content, strain rate, and normal stress. A significant increase in strength was observed with increasing initial degree of saturation, attributed to higher ice content acting as a cementing agent within the soil matrix. A modified Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion was developed by integrating soil freezing curves to account for the effects of ice content on both cohesion and friction angle. The model exhibited strong predictive capability (R 2 = 0.98) for shear strength under thermal loads. These findings provide a robust framework for assessing the stability of geotechnical structures in cold regions and highlight the critical role of ice content in frozen soil behavior.

Article.Title: Machine learning reduces questionnaire items while maintaining reliability and validity
Article.Authors: Li X.; Zhai Y.; Li Y.; Hon C.
Article.Abstract: Traditional long questionnaires often suffer from respondent fatigue, leading to decreased completion rates and compromised data quality. This study introduces a novel algorithmic item-reduction methodology, named NNAQ, designed to streamline high-dimensional survey instruments while strictly preserving both downstream classification capabilities and psychometric construct validity. Operating as a structured case study, the proposed multi-tiered framework strategically orchestrates linear filters, non-linear tree-embedded layers, and information-theoretic criteria. This hybrid architecture allows different mathematical paradigms to cross-validate and error-correct each other, successfully overcoming the limitations of traditional single-stage dimension reduction methods. This study evaluated the framework empirically using an expanded field dataset collected from 1,022 citizens. The experimental results demonstrate that the original 96-item questionnaire can be reduced to a parsimonious 34-item instrument, representing a 64.58% reduction in questionnaire length. Downstream evaluation via machine learning classifiers indicates that the predictive accuracy loss is kept under 5 percent, while comprehensive confirmatory factor analysis confirms that the shortened scale yields superior parsimonious fit indices and stable internal reliability. Furthermore, rigorous bootstrapping resampling and benchmarking experiments against alternative reduction methods validate the exceptional structural stability and empirical superiority of our pipeline. Overall, this research provides a robust, data-efficient, and scalability-tested framework for human-centered digital assessment, effectively mitigating respondent fatigue while securing high-fidelity data quality.

Article.Title: Are intellectual and developmental disabilities and mental illnesses associated with poorer educational outcomes? Evidence from India’s National Sample Survey
Article.Authors: Shah F.; Husain Z.; Datta S.; Ghosh A.; Dutta M.
Article.Abstract: Globally, one in eight people experiences mental illness, yet its intersection with education remains under-explored in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This study uses nationally representative data from the 76th round of the National Sample Survey (2018) for India to examine how intellectual and developmental (IDD) disability and mental illness—treated as distinct categories—are associated with low educational attainments. Employing a generalised ordered logit model, we found that IDDs were associated with a 71.3% probability of receiving no formal education, while the corresponding risk for respondents with mental illness was 48.3%. Females with mental illness were 18.7% points more likely than males to receive no formal education among mentally ill respondents. Economic affluence reduces the gender gap, but it persists even in the richest quintile among mentally ill respondents. These findings highlight that income-based solutions are insufficient and underscore the need for gender-sensitive mental health and education policies in LMICs to attain Sustainable Development Goals related to mental health, education, gender, and income inequality.
