Article.Title: The association between short-term nitrogen dioxide (NO2) exposure and ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attacks (TIA): a national study in Israel
Article.Authors: Fernando P.; Krasnov H.; Kloog I.; He M.; Ifergane G.; Zucker I.; Novack V.; Libruder C.; Yitshak-Sade M.
Article.Abstract: Air pollution is an environmental risk factor for stroke, but most studies have focused on fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), and fewer have investigated the independent association with exposure to nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ). We conducted a nationwide case-crossover study including all ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) reported in the Israeli National Stroke Registry from 2014 to 2018. We obtained daily NO 2 levels from high-resolution geospatial models and linked them to residential addresses. We used distributed lag nonlinear models to assess the cumulative association of NO 2 exposure over 0–5 lag days, adjusting for PM 2.5 and temperature. We further evaluated the modification of the associations by age, sex, urbanicity, and comorbidities (ischemic heart disease, hypertension, and diabetes). We included 85,162 cases, about 54% were males, and the mean age was 71.8. Cumulative NO 2 exposure was associated with increased odds of ischemic stroke or TIA (odds ratio – OR and 95% confidence interval − 1.057 [1.034–1.081]), with the strongest effects 3–5 days before the event. The associations were more pronounced in urban areas (1.064 [1.032;1.097]) compared to suburban areas (1.045 [1.012;1.080]). Although the overall association was similar across ages and sexes, the lag-specific associations on lag days 3–5 were more pronounced in younger adults and women. Short-term exposure to NO 2 is associated with an increased risk of ischemic stroke and TIA, with differential associations across urbanicity, sex, and age groups. These results underscore the urgent need for public health initiatives to reduce NO 2 emissions.

Article.Title: Imaging-based biological age estimation predicts competing mortality risk in lung cancer screening
Article.Authors: Cheng D.; McCabe J.; Patrick T.; Chapman R.; Wang S.; Yang T.; Szmul A.; Azimbagirad M.; Aslani S.; Mullin M.; Naidu S.; Khaw C.; So A.; N/A N/A.; Samson A.; Olabode A.; Villanueva A.; Mohammed A.; Cotton A.; Crossingham A.; Perugia A.; Ketkar A.; Sikorska A.; Edey A.; Andrews A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lung cancer screening (LCS) participants have a high competing risk of non-lung cancer related death, which limits screening benefit. We hypothesized that imaging-based biological age can identify individuals at higher risk of non-lung cancer mortality. Low dose computed tomography scans from a large LCS trial were retrospectively analyzed. Bone density loss, muscular fat infiltration, vascular calcification, and visceral fat mass were calculated using segmentations from a nnU-Net based deep learning segmentation model. Each participant’s age gap, defined as the difference between their estimated biological age and chronological age, was estimated with disease course mapping using a Bayesian mixed-effects model. Disease course map construction used all available longitudinal scan data, whilst individual biological age prediction used baseline scan data only. The performance of age gap as a parameter in competing risk models for non-lung cancer related death versus lung cancer diagnosis was evaluated, following the TRIPOD + AI reporting guideline. We included 29,745 scans from 12,478 participants in the final analysis. Median follow-up was 5 years, representing 58,284 person-years at risk. Multivariable survival models of competing risks were constructed, including the estimated age gap. The subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) for each decade of age gap for non-lung cancer related death was higher (sHR = 2.0, 95% CI 1.8–2.3), compared to lung cancer diagnosis (sHR = 1.3, 95% CI 1.2–1.5). Addition of age gap improved model concordance of non-lung cancer death compared to a model with clinical variables alone (pooled C-index = 0.69 vs 0.73, difference + 0.04, 95% CI 0.03–0.04, p < 0.001). Biological age estimation using an imaging-based disease progression model improves prediction of non-lung cancer related death in lung cancer screening.

Article.Title: Isolating the exposomic impact of acute war and displacement within chronic crisis using multimodal, AI-enabled phenotyping
Article.Authors: Fares M.; Al Kai N.; Zahran F.; Khalil J.; Brunato D.; Allé M.; Boulos L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wars often unfold within contexts of prolonged instability, yet little is known about how acute conflicts interact with cumulative exposomic adversity to shape mental health processes. Here we studied clinical and subclinical symptoms in a Lebanese sample across three groups—one assessed before the 2024 war and two assessed after, with or without displacement—within a shared background of chronic crises. Using a multimodal, AI-enabled approach combining clinical assessments, narrative coding, and large-scale linguistic and emotional profiling of life stories, we show that mental health burden does not scale linearly with acute war or displacement. Despite higher cumulative exposure, war-time groups did not exhibit higher PTSD or depression than pre-war participants, and resilience was lowest among non-displaced individuals. In contrast, narrative organization showed non-linear reconfiguration: displacement was associated with enhanced temporal structuring but reduced global causal coherence, whereas acute war exposure without displacement amplified autobiographical reasoning and explicit self-change. AI-based analyses further revealed emotional blunting rather than emotional overload, alongside increased linguistic complexity decoupled from symptom severity. By enabling scalable analysis of life narratives, this approach isolates acute vs chronic effects and reveals sub-clinical adaptations not captured by symptom measures alone, that can inform healthcare and policy in conflict-affected regions.

Article.Title: Comparison of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease awareness across two cross-sectional surveys in Southeastern China from 2019 to 2025
Article.Authors: Xi L.; Wenling Z.; Tiehui C.; Xiuquan L.; Jingyu C.
Article.Abstract: This study analyzed differences in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) knowledge awareness among Fujian residents aged 40 years and older, to provide scientific evidence to improve COPD prevention and management. We used data from two independent cross-sectional surveys from the China COPD Surveillance Program conducted in 2019–2020 and 2024–2025, respectively. A total of 5,482 participants were recruited in 2019–2020 and 5,438 in 2024–2025. Participants’ awareness rates of COPD knowledge categories, including the disease name, pulmonary function tests, and other COPD-related knowledge, significantly increased over the 5-year period, rising from 8.1% to 16.9%, 21.3% to 35.3%, and 5.4% to 12.9%, respectively (all P < 0.05). Primary channels for learning about COPD were hospitals and physicians, relatives and friends, and, increasingly, the Internet. Dyspnea had the highest awareness rate among COPD symptoms at both time points, while risk factors with the greatest awareness were smoking in 2019–2020 and severe outdoor air pollution in 2024–2025. Awareness of the name of COPD, pulmonary function testing, and other COPD-related knowledge all increased significantly. COPD prevention and health education should continue to be strengthened among the target population.

Article.Title: Multiregional single cell profiling reveals LGALS9 and CD44 mediated niche remodeling crosstalk in metastatic breast cancer
Article.Authors: Tang X.; Jiang N.; Cui Y.; Shen J.; Lu H.; Yan F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The transition from intraductal to invasive Breast cancer (BC) is driven by complex interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), a key stromal component, critically influence extracellular matrix remodeling, immune modulation, and metastatic dissemination. However, the spatially resolved cellular mechanisms through which malignant epithelial subpopulations reprogram fibroblasts to promote metastasis remain incompletely understood. We performed multiregional single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics on breast cancer specimens representing the tumor core, tumor border, and adjacent normal tissue. Malignant mammary luminal (ML) subtypes were identified through Large-scale chromosomal copy number variation (CNV) profiling. Fibroblast sub-clustering, pseudotime trajectory reconstruction, and cell–cell communication analysis (Cell Chat) were integrated with in vitro functional assays using primary fibroblasts and breast cancer cell lines to delineate key signaling interactions. Five ML clusters were identified, among which ML4—enriched at tumor borders—displayed transcriptional programs linked to ribosome activation, hypoxia, and hyper-inflammatory, and was associated with high recurrence and metastasis in TCGA-BC. Fibroblasts were classified into three spatially distinct subtypes: myofibroblasts (myoFIB), inflammatory fibroblasts (iFIB), and APOD⁺PTGDS⁺ fibroblasts, with iFIB predominantly localized to tumor borders. Cell–cell interaction analysis revealed hyperactivation of the LGALS9 (tumor)–CD44 (fibroblast) signaling associated pathway in the border regions. Functional validation confirmed that LGALS9-expressing BC cells promote migration and activation of primary fibroblasts, whereas activated fibroblasts enhance epithelial–mesenchymal transition and migration of BC cells, potentially involving via Smad2/3 signaling. We identify a spatially restricted malignant luminal subtype, ML4, which is associated with fibroblast activation through LGALS9–CD44 signaling, suggesting bidirectional crosstalk between breast cancer cells and fibroblasts within the TME. This niche remodeling holds prognostic relevance and may contribute to metastatic progression, representing a potentially targetable pathway requiring further validation in aggressive breast cancer.

Article.Title: Surrogate-assisted machine learning framework for performance enhancement of Rb2CuSbF6 perovskite LEDs with MoO3/WO3 charge transport layers
Article.Authors: Nagar M.; Agrawal N.; Sazid M.; Gautam A.; Gupta N.
Article.Abstract: Machine learning has become an impressive method to speed up the design and performance prediction of optoelectronic devices, by making the exploration of efficient high-dimensional and highly nonlinear parameter spaces. This is done by physics-based simulations of devices to undertake a systematic parametric sweep of fourteen important material and device parameters producing over 11,000 samples and provides the variation in four important performance measures indicating electrical and optical efficiency. Several machine learning regression models are developed and tested to build a good surrogate model that is sufficiently accurate to predict the nonlinear interactions among all input parameters and the performance of the device. The trained surrogate model is subsequently used for rapid prediction and design-space screening across the multidimensional parameter space, enabling identification of high-performing combinations of transport-layer properties at substantially lower computational cost than repeated physics-based simulations. The suggested framework has a strong predictive potential and rapid prediction action plan in the design and development of perovskite LEDs. This paper shows how surrogate-assisted machine learning solutions can be an efficient and scaled route to creating high-efficiency, environmentally common-place lead-free perovskite light-emitting devices.

Article.Title: Early deep-to-light sedation versus a sustained light-or-awake strategy in mechanically ventilated adults: a target trial emulation
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Han M.; Liu X.; Chen G.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Observational studies comparing sedation depth strategies in mechanically ventilated patients have relied on observed consciousness levels alone to define exposure, potentially conflating intentional drug-induced sedation with low arousal caused by residual medications, other agents, or underlying illness. Using MIMIC-IV (2008–2022), we identified 5,086 adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation for ≥ 48 h. Each patient was cloned to both strategies. During the primary 144-hour adherence window, inverse probability weights accounted for measured predictors of artificial censoring. The primary outcome was 28-day ventilator-free days (VFDs); successful extubation was analysed with death as a competing event. VFD outcomes were observed before artificial censoring in 1,481 sustained-light-or-awake and 622 DTLS clones. Weighted mean VFDs were 17.72 days for DTLS versus 17.76 days for sustained light-or-awake, a difference of − 0.04 days (95% CI, − 1.32–1.29). The cause-specific extubation HR was 0.97 (95% CI, 0.84–1.11). A sensitivity cohort without future minimum ventilation or ICU-duration requirements ( n = 15,842) showed fewer VFDs with DTLS (difference, − 1.03 days; 95% CI, − 1.47 to − 0.61). These findings do not establish a DTLS benefit; duration-based selection, residual confounding, and limited late-window support constrain interpretation.

Article.Title: Feasibility and safety of early bedside personalized rehabilitation in acute decompensated heart failure: a pilot randomized trial
Article.Authors: Zhang P.; Luo X.; Li N.; Huang W.; Jiang Z.; Zhu H.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: The initiation of individualized bedside rehabilitation during the acute phase of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF), particularly among elderly patients, remains insufficiently understood. A total of 58 patients were enrolled. The predefined AHF-CR intervention was successfully delivered in all patients allocated to the intervention group (29/29, 100%), and no rehabilitation-related adverse events were observed. Exploratory analyses showed higher SPPB scores in the intervention group at discharge. Early individualized bedside rehabilitation appears to be feasible and safe for elderly patients with ADHF. Preliminary exploratory differences in discharge SPPB and ERCS scores were observed between groups, warranting confirmation in larger adequately powered trials.

Article.Title: Mindfulness meditation does not make people more present-biased
Article.Authors: Gisbert J.; Navarro-Martinez D.; Martín-Asuero A.; Quoidbach J.
Article.Abstract: One essential aspect of mindfulness practice is to help people focus on the present moment. Although this present-focused attention has been linked to several positive outcomes, it also raises the possibility that mindfulness could increase present bias, with potentially negative consequences for decision-making. Across three laboratory studies and one longitudinal field study, we examined whether mindfulness meditation affects intertemporal choice. In the laboratory studies, participants completed brief guided mindfulness exercises before making economic decisions involving trade-offs between smaller immediate rewards and larger delayed rewards. In our field study, participants completed an eight-week mindfulness course offered by an established mindfulness institute, and they made intertemporal choices before and after their training. Across all four studies, mindfulness did not increase present bias or meaningfully alter intertemporal decisions.

Article.Title: Predicting pathogen-positive blood culture episodes at two hours using electronic health record data
Article.Authors: Grovu R.; Soomro H.; Gelinas N.; Rossi M.; Monaghan S.
Article.Abstract: Most blood cultures obtained early in hospitalization do not yield a pathogen. We evaluated prediction 2 h after the first blood-culture record using MIMIC-IV. Adults with an initial routine culture record within 24 h of hospital presentation were eligible if alive and still receiving care at prediction. The cohort included 145,914 encounters, 99.3% eventually admitted, and 6,404 pathogen-positive episodes (4.39%). Comparisons at 2, 4 and 6 h supported the earliest tested prediction time because later gains were small and uncertain. The primary XGBoost model was evaluated in 11,523 test encounters; 242 episodes were positive (2.10%). AUROC was 0.819 (95% CI 0.792–0.844), average precision 0.124 (0.096–0.167), and Brier score 0.0201. The top 5% of predicted risk contained 81 positives among 577 encounters, giving 14.0% positivity and 6.68-fold enrichment. Laboratory values, particularly lymphocyte percentage, contributed most to prediction. Secondary analyses assessed the added value of previous culture results. Mean predicted risk was 3.78%, compared with 2.10% observed. This 2-h model was able to concentrate pathogen-positive episodes in higher-risk groups, but calibration and transportability require further validation before clinical use.

Article.Title: Evaluating the role of non-HIV antigens in the initiation of QA013.2 HIV bnAb lineage
Article.Authors: Depierreux D.; Sung K.; Bergan L.; Shipley M.; Zhang Y.; Matsen IV F.; Lampe P.; Overbaugh J.
Article.Abstract: Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) are a major goal of HIV vaccine design because they neutralize diverse viral strains. Breadth is typically achieved via affinity maturation and accumulated somatic mutations. However, the inferred naïve precursors of some bnAbs fail to bind the HIV epitopes targeted by their mature counterparts. Consequently, the initiating antigens remain elusive, complicating vaccine design. Building on our previous identification of the HIV bnAb QA013.2 and evidence that its lineage acquired somatic mutations prior to HIV seroconversion, we explored the hypothesis that QA013.2 maturation may be initiated by non-HIV antigens. We screened the inferred naïve precursor and a pre-HIV mutated intermediate of this lineage against > 114.000 antigens, including microbial and parasite glycans, the human proteome and peptides from the human virome. Although human proteome profiling yielded reproducible signals for seven candidates, these interactions lacked a defining structural motif or clear context for B cell priming. Across all platforms, no definitive initiating antigen was identified under the conditions tested, suggesting that if early maturation is indeed driven by non-HIV exposure, the required antigen may involve low-affinity interactions or complex conformational features or glycosylation patterns that remain challenging to detect in standard high-throughput screens.

Article.Title: The analysis of genetic variants in nine patients with nemaline myopathy: implications for diagnosis and genetic counseling
Article.Authors: Zhou B.; Zhang C.; Lin X.; Ma P.; Wang Y.; Zheng L.; Hao S.; Hui L.; Bai Y.
Article.Abstract: Nemaline myopathy (NM) is a rare and hereditary myopathy caused by the fact that several related genes have been identified, thus exhibiting significant clinical and genetic heterogeneity. This study retrospectively analyzed 9 patients with NM. We utilized WES testing and bioinformatics analysis was performed on 9 families. Normal Mode Analysis (NMA) was used to evaluate the impact of missense variants in the NEB gene on the thermodynamic stability of the nebulin protein. The WES results revealed 17 variants in the TPM3 , NEB , and ACTA1 genes in the 9 patients. According to the variant classification criteria published by the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG), approximately two-thirds of the variants were classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic, while the remaining variants were classified as of uncertain significance. Meanwhile, our coarse-grained network meta-analysis of missense variants in the NEB gene showed that, compared with the other two missense variants, the c.9146T > G (p. Ile3049Ser) variant exhibited a significantly higher entropy value within the protein’s thermodynamic range, which may lead to protein instability. This study provides valuable insights and approaches for the diagnosis, prognosis, and genetic counseling of NM. By reviewing these cases, we hope to enrich the existing NM knowledge base.

Article.Title: Visualization and quantification of phage-induced bacterial lysis by phosphotungstic acid-based SEM imaging
Article.Authors: Hisada A.; Miwa T.; Ominami Y.; Hamazato F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Phage biocontrol, which employs bacteriophages for medical and industrial applications, has attracted increasing attention as an alternative to conventional antimicrobial strategies. However, rapid screening and quantitative evaluation of lytic phages remain major challenges for practical implementation. We propose a method based on phosphotungstic acid (PTA)-derived image contrast in scanning electron microscopy (SEM). This approach enables direct visualization of phage-induced bacterial lysis at the single-cell level and quantitative evaluation of cell damage associated with lysis using tabletop SEM. When Escherichia coli was mixed with T4 phage at a phage-to-bacterium ratio of 10:1 (MOI = 10), high-brightness cells indicative of cell damage became detectable within 30 min. Because PTA-stained cells exhibited increased brightness in images, the image-based damaged cell index was quantified as the proportion of high-brightness bacterial area within the total bacterial area, and used as an indicator of cell damage. Across MOIs ranging from 0.01 to 10, the index increased with increasing MOI, and the resulting growth inhibition was consistent with turbidity-based growth curves. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed intracellular PTA redistribution during lysis progression, along with progeny phage particles in pre-lysis cells. These results demonstrate the utility of this method for rapid detection of phage-induced lysis and evaluation of lytic activity.

Article.Title: Markerless pose-derived movement quality assessment in physical education: a multi-task student performance analysis
Article.Authors: Cui L.; Xuan H.; Zhan W.
Article.Abstract: Markerless motion capture offers a practical opportunity to support objective movement assessment in physical education, but its use for student performance evaluation remains limited by concerns about landmark reliability, task variability, camera-view effects, and insufficient validation. This study developed and internally validated a markerless pose-derived framework for evaluating student movement quality across common physical-education tasks. A publicly available synchronized marker-based and markerless motion-capture dataset was analyzed. The final analytical dataset included 21 male physical-education students, seven tasks, two camera views, and 294 eligible task-view trials. Markerless keypoints following the COCO-17 anatomical landmark convention were reconstructed into frame-level skeletons, cleaned using confidence-based filtering, interpolated for short gaps, smoothed, and normalized by body scale. Trial-level features were extracted to quantify movement amplitude, symmetry, smoothness, rhythm, postural control, and detection reliability. A Markerless Movement Quality Score was generated using equal-weighted, expert-weighted, and PCA-derived scoring strategies. Trials were stratified into low, moderate, and high pose-derived movement-quality groups within each task-view combination. Internal validation used grouped 5-fold, leave-one-subject-out, final subject holdout, leave-one-task-out, and leave-one-view-out strategies. The pipeline reconstructed 951,067 frame-level skeletons and more than 16 million keypoint observations. Trunk and lower-limb landmarks showed high reliability, with hips, knees, ankles, and shoulders demonstrating near-complete tracking availability, whereas facial landmarks were less stable. Task-level features captured distinct movement signatures across walking, jogging, high knees, jumping jacks, lunges, and squats. The scoring methods showed strong agreement, including Spearman correlations of 0.97 between equal-weighted and expert-weighted scores, 0.96 between equal-weighted and final scores, and 0.94 between PCA-derived and final scores. The PCA performance landscape showed partial separation of low, moderate, and high movement-quality groups. Machine-learning validation was modest, with the best grouped 5-fold Macro-F1 reaching approximately 0.39, and weaker cross-view generalization. The confusion matrix showed better recognition of low-quality trials than moderate or high-quality trials. Markerless pose-derived features can provide interpretable trial-level descriptors of movement quality across physical-education tasks, particularly when based on reliably detected trunk and lower-limb landmarks. However, predictive validation was modest, with limited discrimination between adjacent movement-quality groups and weak generalization across some task and camera-view conditions. The internally derived MMQS groups were not independently expert-rated, and the present results therefore support feasibility and internal methodological validation rather than reliable automated grading or generalizable performance prediction. External validation against expert assessments, marker-based trajectories, larger cohorts, and real classroom conditions is required before practical educational deployment.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: markerless motion capture; physical education; movement quality assessment; lunge; student assessment; pose estimation; postural control
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Human Pose and Action Recognition; Health Professions > Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation > Physical Education and Training Studies; Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Human Motion and Animation

Article.Title: Seroprevalence of 17 pathogens from an integrated national serosurvey in Niue
Article.Authors: Lawford H.; Mokoia G.; Tatui P.; Nicolas M.; Manu A.; Murphy A.; Marquardt T.; Robinson L.; Angrisano F.; Lau C.; Craig A.
Article.Abstract: Integrated serosurveillance (ISS), using multiplex bead assays to measure antibodies to multiple pathogens, can provide insights into population immunity and pathogen exposure. We estimated seroprevalence for neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), arboviruses, vaccine-preventable diseases, and enteric protozoa in Niue through a cross-sectional survey embedded within a World Health Organization (WHO) STEPwise survey from 24 February to 4 April 2025. Dried blood spots from participants aged ≥ 3 years were tested for 26 pathogen-specific antibodies. Among 750 participants (median age 37 years; range 3–93; 53% female), NTD seroprevalence was low (0% for yaws [among 165 participants aged ≤ 14 years] to 2.7% for cysticercosis). Arbovirus seroprevalence ranged from 3.1% (Zika) to 35.1% (dengue serotype 4). Dengue seropositivity increased with age ( p < 0.05). Measles and rubella seroprevalence exceeded 98%, while diphtheria and tetanus seropositivity was lower in older age groups ( p ≤ 0.03). Cryptosporidium seroprevalence (68.7%) increased with age ( p < 0.001), while Giardia seroprevalence was low (4.1%). Findings demonstrate the utility of ISS to generate policy-relevant surveillance data, although interpretation is limited by the cross-sectional design and non-probability sampling.

Article.Title: A blockchain-enhanced CNN architecture for robust anomaly detection in industrial and IoT cyber-physical systems
Article.Authors: Anwar R.; Abrar M.; Salam A.; Ullah F.
Article.Abstract: Cyber–physical and network attacks are becoming commonplace in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments, with the potential to disrupt operations, compromise safety, and potentially impact the reliability of security evidence. In this study, a modified CNN (mCNN) framework is proposed to detect anomalies with robust, auditable capabilities by incorporating blockchain technology. The detector is based on the following building blocks: dilated convolutions to capture temporal dependencies in industrial process data, multi-branch feature extraction, dataset-adaptive input structuring, and a compact classifier to model heterogeneous patterns in IoT traffic. Anomalies detected are turned into signed and hashed event records and sent to a permissioned Hyperledger Fabric workflow. They test the framework on SWaT and N-BaIoT and validate their results with three baselines: Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and LSTM, and compare them with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC. The proposed CNN is designed under the adopted protocol, and the F1-scores obtained on SWaT and N-BaIoT are 0.977 and 0.951, respectively. An incremental ablation study quantifies the contributions of dilation, multi-branch fusion, windowing, and structured input representation. The findings advocate for the use of customized CNN models for anomaly detection in heterogeneous IIoT applications, and blockchain stress testing, adversarial robustness, constrained-device profiling, and model-specific explainability are key aspects that need to be assessed in the future.

Article.Title: Machine learning–driven strength prediction and optimal waste glass powder dosage for concrete exposed to high temperatures
Article.Authors: Özkılıç Y.; Umiye O.; Alomayri T.; Yılmaz F.; Yildizel S.; Çelik A.
Article.Abstract: This study explores the synergistic effects of the addition of waste glass powder (WGP) and elevated temperatures on the mechanical behavior of concrete, and proposes a machine-learning-based framework for mixture design optimization. Six concrete mixtures containing 0–50% WGP were tested for compressive, flexural, and splitting tensile strengths over the temperature range 24–600 °C, and the results consistently showed an optimal WGP dosage of 10–20% at room temperature and a pronounced degradation in these strengths above 400 °C. To model the strength evolution across the entire WGP-temperature space, a physics-aware data augmentation method and a multi-output Random Forest surrogate model are developed and validated using mixture-wise three-fold cross-validation, parity plots, Y-randomization tests, SHAP-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification. The validated surrogate is then combined with NSGA-II to determine WGP dosages that simultaneously maximize room-temperature strength, high-temperature residual capacity, and material efficiency. Both prospective within-domain experimental validation showed close agreement between the surrogate predictions and independently measured responses. Contour maps and optimization results also consistently show that the 10–20% WGP dosage offers the best trade-off between initial strength and thermal resilience. The results demonstrate the two-fold role of WGP as a micro-filler in improving ambient performance and as a thermally sensitive phase governing degradation mechanisms at elevated temperatures. Therefore, this work presents a validated ML-based framework and practical design charts for optimizing WGP-modified concrete for fire-exposed or high-temperature applications. SEM analyses of the glass powder-reinforced concrete sample exposed to 600 °C showed an increase in cracks and voids in the microstructure; EDX results indicated Ca enrichment with the dominance of O (51.49%), Ca (20.78%), and Si (8.17%); FT-IR spectrum showed the disappearance of the ~ 3400 and ~ 1650 cm⁻¹ bands and the weakening of the ~ 950–1000 cm⁻¹ band, confirming C–S–H degradation; and XRD analysis revealed a decrease in amorphous humps and the prominence of crystalline peaks, indicating that the structure became more crystalline and brittle at high temperature. TGA results indicated that room-temperature-cured samples exhibited higher mass loss and progressive degradation at low temperatures, whereas samples pre-exposed to 600 °C exhibited reduced mass loss and enhanced thermal stability, owing to prior dehydration and microstructural reorganization.

Article.Title: Explainable deep graph attention learning with enhanced residual SwinV2 transformer for interpretable facial paralysis severity assessment
Article.Authors: Sripada R.; Giridhar K.; Marapelli B.; Raju G.; Dash B.; Mohanty S.; Rout S.
Article.Abstract: Facial paralysis is a severely disabling disorder that causes weakness or damage to facial muscles, thus leading to abnormal or asymmetric facial movements. Timely and precise detection and grading of facial paralysis is more essential for appropriate treatments and rehabilitations. Conventionally, facial image analysis was a manual process relying on expert proficiency. Recently, deep learning (DL) techniques have revolutionized the field, especially in the context of facial and clinical image analyses. While DL enables automatic, accurate facial recognition, its black-box nature restricts its use in healthcare. Therefore, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is integrated to enhance transparency that provides visual evidence for medical decision-making. This study introduces an Explainable Deep Graph Attention Learning Framework for Facial Paralysis Identification (XDGAL-FPI). The proposed model is designed to automatically identify the severity of facial paralysis using facial image data. Initially, the input images are preprocessed, including face detection and alignment, color space conversion and contrast enhancement, noise reduction, normalization, and data augmentation to improve the quality and consistency of the input data. Besides, deep feature representations are extracted using an Enhanced Residual SwinV2 Transformer. The extracted features are then provided to a Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network that models the relational dependencies between multiple facial regions, such as the eyes, eyebrows, and mouth, for precise severity classification. Additionally, to improve the training efficiency and convergence behavior of the model, the Ranger optimizer is employed. Furthermore, the GradCAM + + technique is integrated to improve model interpretability by highlighting the important facial regions that contribute to the model’s prediction. The effectiveness of the proposed model is assessed using YouTube Facial Paralysis (YFP) Updated Dataset, which contains 14, 389 images categorized into four severity levels across different facial regions. The experimental results indicate that the proposed XDGAL-FPI model achieves improved performance compared with existing approaches across various evaluation metrics. Thus, the proposed XDGAL-FPI model can serve as a reliable and interpretable tool for automated facial paralysis severity assessment. The source code of this study is available at https://github.com/researcher010-debug/XDGAL-FPI .

Article.Title: Predicting nitrogen dioxide column density from the International Wealth Index with a convolutional neural network in Africa
Article.Authors: Grieco F.; Kakooei M.; Daoud A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the pursuit of improving socioeconomic living conditions of their populations, many nations struggle to meet their nationally determined contributions (NDCs) under the Paris agreement, and that shortfall makes accountability for emissions reductions critical. The long atmospheric lifetimes of key gases such as carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) hinder traditional greenhouse gas (GHG) monitoring, because what any one place emits adds only a small excess to a large, well-mixed background. Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) behaves differently: it is short-lived and highly variable in space and time, so satellite instruments resolve its patterns close to source regions. Across the African continent, mapped temporal correlations between NO 2 and CO 2 are moderate in magnitude but spatially structured and consistently positive. Although we do not use that association to mechanically convert NO 2 observations into CO 2 , we report it as contextual evidence towards NDCs. Given this context, this study asks the following question: to what extent can socioeconomic development at the neighbourhood scale predict NO 2 column densities (the amount of NO 2 in the air column above that neighbourhood) across Africa? We apply a convolutional neural network (CNN) to gridded International Wealth Index (IWI) estimates and to NO 2 observations from the tropospheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI), and obtain an average predictive accuracy of $$R^2$$ = 0.56 across the African continent. Because IWI can be projected forward, we also present an illustrative 2030 scenario as a methodological demonstration of the relationship between socioeconomic development and NO 2 trajectories. These findings indicate that gridded wealth estimates carry predictive information about NO 2 column density in Africa. Such estimates offer a lightweight and scalable screening tool that complements process-based atmospheric monitoring rather than replacing it.

Article.Title: A compact dual-mode single-resonator DGS microwave sensor for self-referenced permittivity characterization
Article.Authors: Bijari A.; Nooki S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents a compact microwave sensor for permittivity characterization based on a single defected ground structure (DGS) resonator with an intrinsic dual-mode response. Unlike conventional differential sensors that require two physically separated resonators, the proposed design exploits two resonant modes intrinsically generated by a stub-loaded double split-ring resonator to enable internal referencing within a single compact structure, thereby eliminating inter-resonator mismatch issues and reducing the sensor footprint. The lower-frequency mode exhibits weaker interaction with the sample under test than the sensing mode and acts as a common-mode reference, whereas the higher-frequency mode shows strong electric-field confinement in the sensing region and is used for permittivity sensing. A prototype was fabricated on a Rogers RO4003 substrate and experimentally validated using several solid dielectric samples. The measured results show a normalized sensitivity of 1.41% and a coefficient of determination of R 2 = 0.9814, in good agreement with full-wave simulations. Owing to its compact size, single-resonator implementation, and self-referenced operation, the proposed sensor is suitable for non-destructive dielectric characterization.

Article.Title: Co-pyrolysis characteristics of vacuum residue and pretreated woody biomass-derived pyrolysis oils under simulated delayed coking temperature and pressure
Article.Authors: Kusumawati M.; Kumagai S.; Suzuki T.; Nakai Y.; Satoh T.; Borjigin S.; Phanthong P.; Saito Y.; Yoshioka T.
Article.Abstract: Integrating renewable carbon into existing petroleum refinery infrastructure is a promising strategy for the energy transition. This study investigates how bio-oil pretreatment and heating mode govern the co-pyrolysis of vacuum residue (VR) with commercial woody biomass pyrolysis oil (WBPO), dehydrated WBPO (dWBPO), and hydrotreated WBPO (hWBPO) under simulated delayed coking conditions. Under slow heating, co-pyrolysis of VR with 10 wt% dWBPO shifted condensable products toward heavy oil, reaching 136% of the additive prediction with only a slight increase in coke formation, whereas hWBPO favored hydrocarbon-rich light products. Direct-injection co-pyrolysis of VR/dWBPO increased light oil to 120% and reduced heavy oil to 50% of the predicted values. Petroleomics showed increased polar species with higher aromaticity and trace toluene-insoluble products during slow VR/dWBPO co-pyrolysis, although physical precipitation of heavy polar components cannot be excluded. High-temperature electron spin resonance showed radical concentrations close to additive predictions and slightly higher g -values, indicating a greater contribution from oxygen-containing radical environments without identifying specific radicals. These results demonstrate that WBPO pretreatment governs the chemical nature of interacting species, while heating history influences redistribution between light and heavy condensable fractions. These findings provide support evaluation of WBPO pretreatment and operating conditions for integration into delayed coking processes.

Article.Title: Real-time visualisation of brain drainage to the deep cervical lymph nodes following intraventricular indocyanine green administration in fresh human donors
Article.Authors: Del Rio M.; Garces Jimeno B.; Xarrie J.; Bonilla A.; Garcia-Garcia S.; Carrasco Lopez C.; Garnica J.; Cortes Rivera M.; Sosa Echeverría M.; Menéndez Albarracín A.; Videla S.; Higueras C.
Article.Abstract: To the best of our knowledge, no study has directly and dynamically demonstrated lymphatic drainage from the intracranial compartment to the cervical lymph nodes in humans, nor identified the specific nodal stations involved. The aim of this study was to provide evidence of real-time visualisation of cervical fluorescence following intraventricular administration of indocyanine green (ICG) and to propose a model for the observed pattern of cervical drainage. This was a prospective, anatomical and descriptive study in potential organ donor participants. Indocyanine green fluorescence imaging was used to evaluate lymphatic drainage from the intracranial compartment to the deep cervical lymph nodes. During standard organ procurement procedures, cervical exploration and intracranial indocyanine green injection was performed prior to tissue extraction. Near-infrared fluorescence imaging was then used to assess migration of indocyanine green into the cervical lymphatic system. A descriptive analysis was performed. Five potential organ donor participants were studied. Cervical lymph node fluorescence following intraventricular ICG administration was observed in 4 of 5 participants. In all four participants, cervical level IIA was the first nodal level in which fluorescence was detected within the exposed cervical field. Our findings provide real-time visualisation of cervical tracer uptake following intraventricular ICG administration in fresh human donors, where level IIA was the first nodal level in which fluorescence was detected within the exposed cervical field.

Article.Title: Combined foliar application of urea and potassium humate on nursery performance of guava cv. Sardar (L-49)
Article.Authors: Kaur K.; Singh H.; Gupta A.; Kaur G.
Article.Abstract: The production of vigorous and healthy nursery plants is fundamental for successful guava cultivation, as seedling quality directly influences field establishment, early growth and long-term orchard productivity. This study assessed the impact of foliar application of urea (1.0% and 1.5%) and potassium humate (1.0% and 2.0%), both applied separately and in combination, on the growth, root development, physiological characteristics, nutrient absorption and nursery performance of guava cv. Sardar (L-49) for two consecutive years. The experiment included eight treatments along with a control, organized in a Randomized Block Design with three replications and the effects of the treatments were evaluated using analysis of variance. The significant treatment effects were observed for all evaluated parameters. Among the treatments, the combined application of 1.5% urea + 2.0% potassium humate (KHm) consistently produced the best nursery performance, recording the highest plant height (51.90 cm), stem girth (1.10 cm), leaf area (25.15 cm 2 ), number of leaves (26.12), shoot number (5.42), root number (22.35), root length (9.87 cm), root volume (3.87 cm 2 ), root fresh weight (1.45 g) and root dry weight (0.41 g). The same treatment also resulted in the highest chlorophyll ( a , b and total chlorophyll) and leaf nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium contents, leading to maximum seedling survival (88.70%) and buddable seedlings (85.03%). Multivariate analyses, including principal component analysis, hierarchical clustering, correlation and regression, revealed strong positive associations among growth, root, physiological, nutrient and nursery performance traits, with the combined treatments clearly separated from the individual applications and untreated control. Overall, the integrated foliar application of 1.5% urea and 2.0% potassium humate (KHm) proved to be the most effective strategy for improving seedling vigour, root development and production of high-quality buddable nursery plants, providing a practical nutrient management approach for commercial guava nursery production.

Article.Title: An explainable two stage framework for spatial temporal traffic accident prediction and injury severity classification
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; He Y.; Liang Z.; Tian P.
Article.Abstract: Traffic accidents pose severe risks to public safety, yet existing injury severity prediction models often overlook spatial-temporal dynamics. This study proposes a two-stage framework integrating spatial-temporal analysis with machine learning to enhance prediction accuracy and interpretability. In the first stage, a Graph Convolution Network-Long Short-Term Memory (GCN-LSTM) model predicts daily accident counts across administrative regions, incorporating the predictions normalized as relative frequencies as features for injury severity classification. The second stage, which classifies the injury severity of accidents that have occurred, employs a stacking ensemble model with four tree-based classifiers, selecting the best-performing configuration based on performance metrics. Experimental results on a real-world dataset demonstrate the framework’s superiority over traditional methods. The GCN-LSTM model reduces mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE) by 18.4% and 3.6%, respectively, compared to the state-of-the-art Spectral Temporal Graph Neural Network (StemGNN). The stacking model with Random Forest as the meta-learner achieves an 87% accuracy in severity prediction. SHAP-based interpretability analysis reveals key factors influencing injury severity, providing actionable insights for traffic safety management. This study offers an interpretable approach to injury severity prediction, supporting data-driven decision-making in accident prevention and emergency response.

Article.Title: Asymptotic mixed graph convolutional with trend-aware self-attention networks for traffic flow forecasting
Article.Authors: Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Accurate traffic flow forecasting plays a critical role in enhancing the efficiency and safety of transportation systems. Nevertheless, this task remains challenging due to the complex spatio-temporal correlations embedded in traffic data. Existing adaptive-graph-based methods usually learn graph structures during training, making them insufficiently responsive to testing-phase traffic states. Consequently, their forecasting performance may deteriorate under unexpected fluctuations and irregular traffic variations. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a novel Asymptotic Mixed Graph Convolutional with Trend-Aware Self-Attention Network (AMG-TSA). By learning trend similarities among traffic nodes, AMG-TSA constructs an asymptotic adjacency matrix to support both asymptotic structure-aware graph convolution and asymptotic dynamic graph convolution, enabling synchronized modeling of dynamic spatial dependencies. Meanwhile, a trend-aware self-attention module is introduced to capture local contextual patterns and nonlinear temporal dependencies, while dilated causal convolution enlarges the temporal receptive field and supports long-range temporal dependency modeling. Experiments on two real-world traffic datasets show that AMG-TSA consistently outperforms representative baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness in traffic flow forecasting.

Article.Title: Design and development of a photochromic material based on spiropyran for Bisphenol A removal
Article.Authors: Maftei A.; Ignat M.; Dobromir M.; Neamţu M.
Article.Abstract: A photochromic material including spiropyran (SP) and multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) was designed and evaluated as a catalyst for the removal of Bisphenol A (BPA) in aqueous solution. All photodegradation processes followed pseudo-first-order kinetics, with calculated rate constants (k) ranging from 0.0013 min − 1 in the absence of the catalyst to 0.0251 min − 1 in the presence of 1.00 g/L of the catalyst under simulated solar irradiation. The recycling experiments showed a gradual decrease in photocatalytic performance over four consecutive reaction cycles, suggesting a slight loss of catalyst activity during repeated use. XRD analysis showed that the overall crystalline structure of the catalyst remained essentially unchanged after four cycles compared with the fresh material. The photochromic properties of spiropyrans make them highly efficient molecules that are capable of producing Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS). The Electron Spin Resonance (ESR) experiments pointed to the efficient formation of 1 O 2 by the studied catalyst in aqueous suspension. The radical scavenging experiments indicated that both singlet oxygen ( 1 O₂) and hydroxyl radicals (•OH) play an important role in the BPA degradation process. In addition, the MCF-7 cell viability tests showed that the aqueous samples became less cytotoxic after photocatalytic treatment. Thus, it was demonstrated that the developed catalyst shows potential as a photocatalyst, particularly for the removal of micropollutants such as BPA from contaminated water.

Article.Title: Distributed nested bi-layer pricing for wireless charging service operators in power-transportation coupled networks
Article.Authors: Huang L.; Su Y.; Jia Y.; Han X.; Jing X.
Article.Abstract: The development of electric vehicles (EVs) and wireless charging technology promotes the interconnections among transportation networks (TN), power distribution network (PDN) and wireless charging station (WCS). However, the coordinated operation of these systems is challenged by information barriers among independently operated entities and the complex coupling among charging prices, EV routing decisions, WCS loads, and PDN operating conditions. Considering the information barrier between different entities, a distributed nested bi-layer pricing strategy for charging service operator (CSO) is developed in this paper where the distribution network operator only interacts with CSO for information exchange, while CSO interacts with EV drivers. In the outer layer, a second-order cone alternating current optimal power flow model in PDN is established to determine the distribution locational marginal price. A bi-layer pricing model of CSO is established to maximize profits by adjusting the charging price in the inner layer. And in the inner lower layer, EV driver optimizes their charging and routing decisions to minimize travel cost according to charging price, thereby affecting the WCS’s load profile. Furthermore, the existence of CSO’s optimal pricing strategy is analyzed according to the fixed-point theory, and an alternating direction method of multipliers nested with genetic algorithm (GA) is proposed. The numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed improved ADMM algorithm, and analyze the effect of the pricing strategy for CSO on the CSO, PDN and TN.

Article.Title: Electrochemical fingerprints of sequential double-regenerative enzymatic mechanisms in protein-film voltammetry
Article.Authors: Janeva M.; Kokoskarova P.; Gulaboski R.
Article.Abstract: Electrochemical transformations of many lipophilic redox proteins and enzymes proceed through sequential two-step electron-transfer pathways that are frequently coupled with regenerative catalytic reactions accompanying both electron-transfer steps. Although protein-film voltammetry (PFV) provides a powerful experimental platform for direct investigation of such systems, theoretical descriptions of surface-confined double-regenerative mechanisms remain largely unexplored. In this work, we present, for the first time, a comprehensive theoretical framework describing a two-step surface-confined double-regenerative mechanism under square-wave protein-film voltammetry conditions. Systematic theoretical analysis demonstrates how the interplay between heterogeneous electron-transfer kinetics and successive regenerative catalytic reactions governs the shape, position, intensity, and kinetic characteristics of the corresponding square-wave voltammetric responses. Simulations reveal a broad spectrum of characteristic electrochemical fingerprints that can be directly associated with variations in the intrinsic kinetic parameters of both electron-transfer and catalytic steps. The developed framework provides a robust basis for mechanistic interpretation of experimentally recorded protein-film voltammograms and establishes practical diagnostic criteria for distinguishing different kinetic regimes. Furthermore, the proposed approach offers a reliable platform for developing experimental protocols aimed at quantitative extraction of electron-transfer and catalytic rate constants, thereby enabling evaluation of enzymatic activity and reaction pathways of various redox proteins and enzymes. The presented model considerably expands the theoretical foundation of protein-film square-wave voltammetry applied to surface-confined redox proteins and enzymes.

Article.Title: One-step anodization versus chronoamperometric electrodeposition for the fabrication of gold nanoparticle–TiO₂ nanotube nanocomposites for biosensing applications
Article.Authors: Paradowska E.; Arkusz K.; Pijanowska D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) modified with gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) are attractive materials for electrochemical sensing owing to their high surface area and enhanced electron-transfer properties. In this study, AuNP/TNT nanocomposites were fabricated using two different approaches: one-step anodization and chronoamperometric electrodeposition. In the first approach, AuNPs were generated directly during TNTs anodization by introducing HAuCl₄ into the electrolyte at final concentrations of 1, 5, and 10 mM. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report describing the fabrication of AuNPs/TNTs through the direct incorporation of HAuCl₄ into the anodization electrolyte. In the second, AuNPs were deposited onto annealed TNTs (TNTs-A) by chronoamperometry at − 0.3, − 0.9, and − 1.2 V. The obtained materials were characterized using scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, contact angle measurements, open-circuit potential measurements, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Among the investigated samples, the nanocomposite fabricated by one-step anodization in the presence of 1 mM HAuCl₄ and subsequently annealed in argon atmosphere at 450 °C for 2 h exhibited a well-dispersed AuNPs distribution (25.97 ± 2.84 nm) and 30% and 34% reductions in impedance modulus and real impedance, respectively, compared with TNTs-A. Furthermore, this platform showed an enhanced electrochemical response toward hydrogen peroxide (0.1–0.5 mM) in the presence of thionine and horseradish peroxidase, exhibiting higher sensitivity and a lower detection limit (0.001 mM) than TNTs-A (0.003 mM).

Article.Title: Freeze-thaw model for compressive strength of flowable solidified soil based on machine learning
Article.Authors: Wang B.; Shao J.; Huang Y.; Li C.; Han T.; Fan B.
Article.Abstract: Freeze-thaw cycling is a critical factor triggering durability degradation of flowable solidified soil in cold-region engineering, and its damage evolution process is affected by multi-factor coupling with obvious nonlinear characteristics. Based on experimental compressive strength data of flowable solidified soil under freeze-thaw cycles, four influencing factors, namely solidifier dosage (SD), admixture dosage (AD), water-solid ratio (WS) and freeze-thaw cycle number (F-T), are selected as input variables. Four machine learning algorithms including Decision Tree (DT), BP Neural Network (BP), Support Vector Regression (SVR) and XGBoost are adopted to establish freeze-thaw damage prediction models for the compressive strength of flowable solidified soil. The SHAP interpretable framework is further employed for feature sensitivity analysis to quantify the contribution and nonlinear effect of each input factor on prediction results. The results reveal that the DT model suffers severe overfitting with drastic error fluctuations on the test set; BP and SVR achieve a high test‑set R 2 yet show noticeable prediction deviations; the ensemble tree model XGBoost presents well‑balanced fitting capacity and satisfactory overall prediction stability with low error dispersion. SHAP analysis indicates the feature importance ranking: F-T > SD > AD > WS. Freeze-thaw cycle number (F-T) acts as the dominant control factor, and high/low values of each factor impose distinct positive and negative effects on model outputs. The proposed modeling and interpretive analysis method can provide technical references for rapid prediction of mechanical indices of similar flowable solidified soil specimens and identification of primary influencing factors.

Article.Title: Data-driven discrete geofence design using binary quadratic programming
Article.Authors: Otaki K.; Okada A.; Matsumori T.; Yoshida H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Geofences have attracted significant attention in the design of spatial and virtual regions for managing and triggering spatiotemporal events; for example, content providers can trigger spatiotemporal events through mobile devices. Traditionally, geofences were hand-crafted by providers. In addition to the hand-crafted approach, recent advances in collecting human mobility data through mobile devices can accelerate the automated, data-driven design of geofences, also known as the geofence design problem. Previous approaches assume circular shapes; thus, their flexibility is insufficient, and they are mainly suited to geofence-based applications over large areas at coarse resolutions. A challenge with using circular geofences in urban and high-resolution areas is that they often overlap and fail to align with political district boundaries and road segments, such as one-way streets and median barriers. This study proposes a discrete geofence design formulation that represents a geofence as selected spatial cells and optimizes the selection by binary quadratic programming. Although binary quadratic programming problems are computationally hard, modern optimization solvers can often find practical solutions. Furthermore, expressing the model in a quadratic binary form provides a computational interface to specialized quadratic and heuristic solvers, including annealing-based approaches. We then develop and compare different formulation methods to extract discrete geofences. In our numerical evaluation, we validate the formulation using a real-world GeoLife case study and synthetic multiple-POI scenarios, and compare it with circular geofences and density-based top- k , connected top- k , and DBSCAN + alpha-shape baselines. The evaluation uses user-level coverage ratio, user-point-level coverage ratio, shape connectivity, POI-aware separation, and runtime and scalability. The results show that the proposed formulation can generate area-controlled, non-circular geofences that better reflect mobility patterns than circular baselines, while the computational cost and the choice of discretization level remain important practical limitations.

Article.Title: Synchronous recovery of multiple valuable metals from municipal solid waste incineration fly ash and red mud via co-reduction technology
Article.Authors: Geng C.; Chang J.; Li Q.; Shi X.; Heng Y.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (FA) and red mud (RM) are hazardous industrial solid wastes that pose potential environmental and safety risks if improperly stored or disposed of. Based on the physical and chemical properties of FA and RM, this study employs co-reduction technology to recover valuable metals while integrating a real-time GIS framework for spatial monitoring and disaster risk management. Under the optimal reduction conditions, the recovery rates of Fe, Ni, Cu, and Cr reach 76.55%, 84.89%, 73.95%, and 58.87%, respectively, with corresponding grades of 94.40%, 0.45%, 0.77%, and 0.42%. The FA content strongly affects the co-reduction process: insufficient FA (< 30%) limits carbon availability, while excessive FA (> 40%) increases calcium content and raises the system’s melting point by forming gehlenite. An appropriate FA/RM ratio effectively lowers the melting point and achieves the simultaneous formation of ferroalloy and glass structures. Under optimized conditions, the tailings consist mainly of amorphous SiO 2 –Al 2 O 3 –CaO–FeO glass phases, with leaching toxicity meeting environmental standards. By coupling co-reduction recovery with real-time GIS-based risk mapping and monitoring, this study establishes a sustainable route for metal recovery from hazardous wastes while enhancing disaster prevention and environmental management.

Article.Title: Prevalence and associated factors of type 2 diabetes among HIV-infected patients at Arsi University Teaching and Referral Hospital, Southeast Ethiopia, 2023
Article.Authors: Tilahun B.; Teferi G.
Article.Abstract: The utilization of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) significantly extends the lifespan of People Living With Human Immunodeficiency Virus (PLWHIV) and markedly reduces HIV-related morbidity and mortality. On a global scale, non-communicable diseases associated with HIV, such as diabetes, are emerging as significant public health concerns. The prolonged use of HAART, coupled with the increasing burden of chronic comorbidities resulting from longer life expectancy, has become a substantial contributor to morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of diabetes mellitus and associated factors among adult HIV patients at Asella Teaching and Referral Hospitals. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from November 1, to December 30, 2023, among selected HIV patients at Asella Teaching and Referral Hospital. The data were collected using a structured interviewer administered questionnaire adapted from the STEP wise approach of the World Health Organization. The collected data were analysed using SPSS 26. Descriptive analysis such as frequency and mean was used to represent the characteristic of the study population and the prevalence of diabetes among the study participants. Bi-variable logistic regression analysis was used to identify candidate variables at p < 0.2, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was employed to identify significant factors associated with prevalence of diabetes among HIV patients at a p value < 0.05 and 95% confidence interval. A total of 159 responses were received, yielding a response rate of 100%. The prevalence of diabetes among people living with HIV (PLWHIV) receiving HAART was 10.7% (95% CI: 6.35–16.57), while 5.0% of the study participants had pre-diabetes. Multivariable logistic regression result revealed that being physically inactive (AOR = 3.82, 95% CI = 3.82(2.1–14.0), having hypertension (AOR = 6.2, 95% CI = 2.5–23.1) and LDL-C ≥ 130 mg/dl (AOR = 4.5, 95% CI = 1.13–18.30) were found to be associated factors with diabetes mellitus in PLWHIV. Among people living with HIV, physical inactivity, elevated blood pressure, and elevated LDL cholesterol were significantly associated with type 2 diabetes. These findings underscore the importance of promoting regular physical activity and routine screening for blood pressure and lipid profiles as part of comprehensive HIV care to facilitate the early identification and management of diabetes.

Article.Title: Radiogenic isotope variability in contemporary mineral dust across the intermountain west of the United States
Article.Authors: Munroe J.; Santis A.; Hulbert J.; Norris E.; Olson P.; Tappa M.; Bauer A.
Article.Abstract: Mineral dust is a highly mobile component of Earth’s Critical Zone that influences ecosystem function, soil development, biogeochemical cycling, and environmental archives. Radiogenic isotopes provide a powerful means of characterizing dust because isotope ratios largely preserve source signatures during atmospheric transport. Here we present a dataset of 100 modern dust samples analyzed for 87 Sr/ 86 Sr and ε Nd from a network of 20 passive dust collectors distributed across the Intermountain West of the United States, including sites in the Uinta Mountains, Wasatch Mountains, Great Basin ranges of Nevada, southern Utah, southern Idaho, and urban environments. Pb isotope compositions were determined for samples from 8 of these collectors. Consideration of collector position, grain-size distribution, and local geology identifies a limited number of samples influenced by locally derived material, but most measurements provide a robust characterization of the isotope fingerprint of contemporary dust deposition. Distinct geographic patterns are evident, with dust from Nevada exhibiting lower 87 Sr/ 86 Sr ratios and higher ε Nd values than dust collected in Utah mountain environments, whereas samples from southern Utah, Idaho, and urban locations occupy intermediate but distinguishable isotopic fields. These isotope fingerprints can be provisionally linked with potential source areas upwind. In concert with Sr and Nd, Pb isotope ratios provide additional discriminatory power. Repeated sampling demonstrates that individual sites exhibit modest year-to-year variability, yet temporal variation is generally smaller than spatial differences among regions. The resulting geographic clustering indicates that dust deposited across the Intermountain West is not isotopically homogeneous, but instead exhibits persistent regional differences reflecting varying source landscapes and transport pathways. These results highlight the value of distributed monitoring networks for characterizing dust variability across broad regions and provide a foundation for future investigations of dust transport, landscape connectivity, and Critical Zone processes in western North America.

Article.Title: Effects of angiotensin (1–7) producing Lactobacillus paracasei and palmitoleic acid on angiotensin converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) expression and gut microbiota in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats
Article.Authors: Ucar M.; Celebi D.; Celebi O.; Baser S.; Guler M.; Tanyeli A.; Dabanlıoglu B.; Kılıclıoglu M.; Gultekın Ucar A.; Yıldırım S.
Article.Abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disease characterized by hyperglycemia due to defects in insulin secretion or action. This study aimed to investigate the effects of angiotensin (1–7) producing Lactobacillus paracasei (LP) and palmitoleic acid (PA) on ACE2 expression and gut microbiota in a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rat model. A total of 42 male Wistar rats were divided into 7 groups: Control, STZ, LP, PA, STZ, STZ + LP, STZ + PA and STZ + LP+PA. Blood glucose level, ACE2 expression level by Western blot analysis, microbiota analysis and histopathologic examination were performed between the groups. Blood glucose levels were significantly elevated in STZ (60 mg/kg) treated groups (428.67 ± 18.44 vs. control 76.00 ± 4.52), whereas the combination of LP and PA brought blood glucose levels closer to control (103.00 ± 7.48). In Western blot analysis, ACE2 expression decreased in the STZ group, whereas LP and PA treatments increased this expression. The most significant increase was observed in the STZ + LP+PA group. Microbiota analysis showed that LP and PA increased intestinal diversity (Shannon index: 4.774) and decreased pathogenic species. Histopathologic examinations revealed severe degeneration and Nuclear Factor Kappa B (NF-κB) expression in the liver, intestine, and spleen in the STZ group, whereas the combination treatment attenuated this damage. In immunofluorescence analysis, Caspase-3 and Toll-Like Receptor 4 (TLR4) expression was significantly reduced in the STZ + LP+PA group. LP and PA has therapeutic potential in reducing diabetes-induced microbiota dysbiosis and inflammation by regulating the ACE2 pathway.

Article.Title: School connectedness and adverse childhood experiences in relation to suicidal behaviors among nationally representative adolescents
Article.Authors: Bin Radhyan F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are strongly associated with adolescent suicidality. Since these exposures have already occurred, prevention depends on identifying modifiable protective factors. School connectedness is a theoretically grounded candidate, yet its role in the context of cumulative childhood adversity has not been examined in nationally representative data. We analysed 10,605 U.S. high-school students from the 2023 national Youth Risk Behavior Survey, the first cycle to include a dedicated ACE module. Survey-weighted modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) for associations of cumulative ACEs and school connectedness with past-year suicidal ideation and suicide attempt, adjusting for sex, grade, and race/ethnicity. Cumulative ACEs showed a strong dose-response association with both outcomes (four or more ACEs: ideation PR = 11.49, 95% CI 8.83 to 14.95; attempt PR = 14.80, 95% CI 9.32 to 23.52). School connectedness was independently associated with lower prevalence of ideation (PR = 0.68, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.76) and attempt (PR = 0.75, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.87), and this association persisted after adjustment for a cumulative adverse-school-experience index. Interaction analyses showed no consistent buffering; connectedness was protective across all adversity levels. School connectedness is a broadly relevant, modifiable target for adolescent suicide prevention.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a minimum data set for a male sexual health assessment registry system
Article.Authors: Shafiee M.; Baghrobehbahani A.; Tahery N.; Varzaneh Z.; Kazemi-Arpanahi H.
Article.Abstract: Men’s sexual health is an important aspect of public health that requires focused attention and thorough analysis. A comprehensive evaluation must consider various health issues from multiple perspectives. Clinical registries are vital for tracking male sexual health and follow-up data; however, the absence of a standardized data collection tool hinders the systematic documentation of male sexual health from an information management standpoint. As a result, the data collected often lacks comparability, which limits the generalizability of the findings. This study aims to develop a minimum data set (MDS) as an initial step toward creating a male sexual health registry. This study was conducted from January 8, 2024, to March 20, 2025, using a multi-phased approach. We began by compiling a list of potential data items through a search of scientific databases, a review of grey literature, and an examination of existing information systems, forms, and websites related to male sexual health. Next, we applied a modified Delphi technique, which involved a two-round survey with a panel of 27 experts in clinical practice and research focused on male sexual health. These experts rated the importance of each candidate data item for inclusion in the MDS using afour-point Likert scale. Items that received an agreement level of 80% or higher were accepted for inclusion in the final MDS. Finally, we evaluated the content validity of the developed MDS using the content validity ratio (CVR) and the content validity index (CVI) criteria. The finalized MDS for male sexual health assessment comprises 105 items, organized into six distinct categories, including sociodemographic factors, relationship status, sexual behaviors and functions, awareness of sexual self-examination, sexual protective behaviors, and clinical history. This MDS is developed to assist registry designers and administrators in selecting the necessary data items for a male sexual health assessment registry system. Its purpose is to facilitate the design and implementation of a standardized registry and support the systematic collection of high-quality data. The MDS may also provide a useful foundation for improving the availability and consistency of information relevant to male sexual health care. However, further research is needed to evaluate its implementation, feasibility, and potential impact on clinical decision-making and quality of care.

Article.Title: Fabrication of a paper-based microextraction tool for monitoring volatile emission associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Article.Authors: M K A.; Mandal D.; Selvamuthukumar K.; Mazumder N.; Ghosh C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ), an opportunistic bacterial pathogen, causes severe respiratory infections. Rapid detection of bacterial species is important for switching from broad-spectrum to narrow-spectrum antibiotics when antimicrobial resistance is present. Here, we designed paper-based hydrophilic-lipophilic balance/divinylbenzene/polydimethylsiloxane polymer-coated TF-SPME patches and integrated them into a bacterial culture to extract volatile emissions associated with the P. aeruginosa (ATCC 27853) strain. The metabolites were analyzed using triple quadrupole mass spectrometry. The sampling patches captured 48 metabolites, including hydrocarbons, alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, acids, esters, and heteroatom-containing metabolites, from the logarithmic phase of P. aeruginosa , with alkanes and terpenes as the predominant classes. The technique requires minimal solvent, and the method’s greenness was validated using the AGREE, GAPI, BAGI, CACI, and CaFRI assessment tools. Therefore, this technique may offer a rapid, eco-friendly alternative for the fast detection of P. aeruginosa . This sampling tool may help to improve clinical decision-making in cases of respiratory infection caused by P. aeruginosa .

Article.Title: Gait freezing onset and termination prediction in Parkinson disease using shank sensor acceleration data
Article.Authors: Khera P.; Kumar A.; Kapila R.
Article.Abstract: Motor impairment Freezing-of-Gait (FoG) is associated with reduced mobility leading to falls usually occurring in advancing Parkinson’s disease (PD). Cueing techniques have been successfully used to alleviate the event. Although, FoG prediction is extensively studied but only paucity of work includes event termination detection. Together with freezing, unfreeze event prediction is advantageous to reduce long-term cueing effects. The focus of carried work is to propose a machine-learning based framework for prediction of freeze and unfreeze events. Based on the Freeze Index (FI), a relabelling scheme is developed to represent four gait states, that are, no-FoG, pre-FoG, FoG, and pre no-FoG using publicly available Daphnet dataset, comprising of 10PD patients. Using nine extracted features from the shank sensor, Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of 95.5% using segmentation window of 2s. While episode-independent GroupKFold (5-fold) and subject-independent evaluation reported accuracy of (91.2 ± 0.9)% and (86.2 ± 4.0)% respectively representing more stricter independence constraints to generalize across episodes and, unseen subjects. Following feature selection, a reduced set of five shank features are obtained using 2s segmentation window and accuracy of 96.2% is achieved. At event level, 197 of 237 annotated FoG episodes are successfully identified at onset, corresponding to per-episode sensitivity of 83.12%. The predicted termination transitions achieved 63.6% cue-deactivation accuracy. These results demonstrate that single shank sensor can provide information for both FoG onset and termination with relatively low sensing and feature-processing requirements. However, framework requires clinical validation and its effectiveness for real-time cueing following prospective validation on larger and more diverse PD population.

Article.Title: Suture-Anchor Broström–Gould repair with fibular periosteal flap augmentation for chronic lateral ankle instability: a North African experience
Article.Authors: Fatih T.; Khalifa A.; Karam-Allah I.; Masoud M.; Fadle A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ankle sprains are a common musculoskeletal injury, accounting for up to 20%. Although most of these injuries are initially treated nonoperatively, a subset of patients develops chronic lateral ankle instability (CLAI) over time, which, if symptomatic, will require operative intervention. To report our early results from a specialized North African sports medicine surgery unit after performing a modified Broström–Gould procedure using a suture anchor and augmenting the repair using a distally based fibular periosteal flap. Twenty-two patients, with a mean age of 33.48 ± 8.23 years, including 10 (45.45%) males and 12 (54.55%) females, presented with CLAI and were treated with the modified Broström–Gould procedure. The mean follow up was 29.3 ± 7.18 months, and the clinical assessment included the American Orthopedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle and hindfoot score and visual analog scale (VAS) for pain. Any complications were reported. The mean operative time was 61.3 ± 11.15 min. Two (9.1%) patients had complications: one with a superficial surgical site infection and the other with superficial peroneal nerve neuropraxia; both were treated conservatively. The AOFAS improved significantly at the last follow up compared to the preoperative scores, 83.9 ± 10.73 vs. 57.1 ± 14.78, respectively (p < 0.01). The VAS score improved significantly from a preoperative median of 7 to a last follow up median of 2 (p < 0.01). The patients returned to their activities of daily living after a mean of 13.30 ± 2.38 weeks. The majority of patients (95.5%) were either very satisfied or satisfied with the outcomes. None of the patients had instability recurrence or required secondary surgical intervention. Using suture anchors for ligament reattachment and augmenting the repair with a distally based fibular periosteal flap as a modification to the Broström–Gould procedure for managing CLAI demonstrated efficacy and acceptable clinical and patient satisfaction outcomes. Furthermore, despite a relatively high complication rate, it was consistent with the literature. However, future comparative studies are warranted to validate the obtained results.
