Article.Title: Contemporary cardiometabolic and inflammation targeting therapies reduce residual cardiovascular risk in an endpoint harmonized meta analysis
Article.Authors: Bashir M.; Chen C.; Mohammad A.; Ahmed R.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Residual cardiovascular risk remains substantial despite contemporary preventive therapy. Multiple pharmacological strategies targeting metabolic, lipid-related, cardiorenal, and inflammatory pathways have shown cardiovascular benefit in randomized trials, but differences in endpoint definitions and composite outcome structures complicate cross-trial interpretation. We aimed to evaluate whether contemporary cardiometabolic and anti-inflammatory therapies are associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular event risk using an endpoint-harmonized framework. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors, omega-3 fatty acid-based therapies, and anti-inflammatory agents. Databases were searched from inception through February 2026. The primary outcome was endpoint-harmonized major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the trial-reported cardiovascular composite endpoint judged most comparable across studies according to prespecified harmonization rules. A prespecified sensitivity analysis was restricted to strict 3-point MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled on the log scale using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung–Knapp adjustment. Seventeen randomized trials involving 157,278 participants and 15,815 events contributed to the primary endpoint-harmonized analysis. Active therapy was associated with a lower risk of MACE than control (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.79–0.88; I²=51%). In the sensitivity analysis restricted to strict 3-point MACE, 10 trials involving 98,973 participants and 9,067 events yielded a consistent pooled estimate with no observed heterogeneity (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.80–0.86; I²=0%). Directionally consistent benefit was observed for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, and anti-inflammatory therapies. Estimates for proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors and omega-3 fatty acid-based therapies were based on limited trials and should be interpreted cautiously. No statistically significant effect modification by therapeutic class was detected, although the analysis was not designed to establish comparative equivalence across classes. Across randomized trials, contemporary cardiometabolic and anti-inflammatory therapies were associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular event risk. The consistency of findings in the strict 3-point MACE sensitivity analysis supports the robustness of the overall association. However, differences in heterogeneity and precision across therapeutic classes suggest that these therapies should not be assumed to be clinically interchangeable.

Article.Title: Physics-guided residual inverse-transition modeling for continuum robots with simulation and ordered experimental evaluation
Article.Authors: Morakchi M.; Talhi A.; Ghoul A.; Djeffal S.; Bendriss B.; Latreche A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study distinguishes two levels that were conflated in the original submission: a tendon-driven mechanical dynamics model used only in simulation, and an ordered one-step inverse-transition estimator used for the recorded experiment. The experimental estimator does not identify force-level inverse dynamics because the supplied dataset contains no verified sampling interval, velocity, acceleration, tendon tension, actuator torque, pneumatic pressure, or contact-force channel. Instead, it predicts the next measured six-channel length-state increment from the present Cartesian state, desired Cartesian increment, and a structured representation of the measured length state. The first-order prior is a global empirical differential map, $$\widehat{{\bf J}}\in \mathbb {R}^{3\times 6}$$ , estimated only from the training block; it has rank 3, condition number 3.49, and singular values 1.425, 1.317, and 0.409. Reviewer-driven ablation further showed that the Clarke-like $$3\times 3$$ transform is a full-rank coordinate change rather than a dimensionality reduction, that appending both raw channels and deterministic modes reweights Gaussian-kernel distances, and that the one-step history term does not improve the held-out experimental prediction. The revised experimental instantiation therefore retains only the four bending coordinates $$(q_{\alpha ,1},q_{\beta ,1},q_{\alpha ,2},q_{\beta ,2})$$ in the nonlinear residual learner and excludes both the common mode and duplicated raw/mode features. On the chronologically held-out 39-transition test block, this bending-mode residual KRR obtains a task-space RMSE of 0.365 mm and a cable/length-state RMSE of 0.745 mm, compared with 0.469 mm for a validation-tuned direct KRR, 0.596 mm for ridge regression, 0.654 mm for the NARX-feature model, and 0.795 mm for the global empirical prior. A four-sample moving-block bootstrap gives a within-trajectory 95% interval of approximately 0.282–0.437 mm for the revised task-space RMSE. A paired sign-randomization test against direct KRR gives $$p\approx 0.060$$ , so the small test block does not justify a claim of statistically conclusive superiority over that strongest nonlinear baseline. The independently learned forward evaluator has a test component RMSE of 0.139 mm and vector RMSE of 0.240 mm, but its larger validation error also reveals chronological distribution shift. Accordingly, the revised claims are restricted to free-space, one-step inverse-transition prediction on the recorded trajectory family; no cross-speed, cross-platform, force/contact, or closed-loop hardware generalization is claimed.

Article.Title: Musculoskeletal pain, functional impact, and associations with recorded sex in an adult sample from Mashhad, Iran: a cross-sectional secondary analysis
Article.Authors: Nazary-Moghadam S.; Ziaee A.; Mirinezhad S.; Jafarzadeh S.
Article.Abstract: We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of musculoskeletal data collected within a parent survey in Mashhad, Iran, between May 2024 and March 2025. Descriptive analyses included all 1,074 participants with musculoskeletal data; recorded-sex comparisons included 1,049 participants (624 men and 425 women), and age-adjusted models included 1,037. A study-specific Persian questionnaire recorded pain in nine anatomical regions during the previous 12 months and 7 days, difficulty with normal activities, and physician consultation. In a post hoc exploratory analysis, multisite pain (at least two regions) affected 78.8% over 12 months and 62.3% over 7 days. Twelve-month knee and lower-back pain were reported by 65.5% and 57.8%, respectively. In exploratory age-adjusted analyses, women had lower prevalence than men of knee pain (prevalence ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.64–0.78; marginal prevalence difference −22.1 percentage points, −28.2 to −16.1) and lower-back pain (0.69, 0.61–0.78; −20.1 percentage points, −26.4 to −13.8). The direction of all 36 regional associations persisted after adjustment for available covariates. Estimates were unweighted and not adjusted for the intended sampling design. These findings describe the analyzed subset; selective participation, residual confounding, and sparse representation of younger and oldest adults restrict generalizability.

Article.Title: RBM39 regulates malignant progression in lung adenocarcinoma cells through alternative splicing of NRG1-206
Article.Authors: Li S.; Li Y.; Tursun I.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the function of RBM39 in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), with a particular focus on its regulatory effect on the alternative splicing of NRG1-206 and its role in tumor progression. Differential expression analysis of RNA binding proteins (RBPs) in LUAD samples was performed using TCGA datasets. RBM39 expression levels were validated by RT-qPCR and western blot. Functional assays, including cell proliferation, apoptosis, invasion, and migration were conducted using A549 cells with RBM39 or NRG1-206 overexpression. RNA-seq was employed to explore RBM39-mediated gene expression and alternative splicing regulation, and iRIP-seq combined with bioinformatics tools was used to identify binding motifs and downstream targets. Our results indicated that RBM39 expression was significantly downregulated in LUAD tissues and was associated with poor prognosis. Overexpression of RBM39 in A549 cells significantly inhibited proliferation and invasion while promoting apoptosis (all p < 0.05). Transcriptomic profiling revealed that RBM39 regulated gene expression and alternative splicing, with enrichment in immune and transcriptional pathways. iRIP-seq confirmed direct binding of RBM39 to pre-mRNAs including NRG1. Notably, RBM39 modulated the alternative splicing of NRG1, particularly suppressing the oncogenic NRG1-206 isoform. Functional rescue experiments showed that overexpression of NRG1-206 reversed the tumor-suppressive effects of RBM39. Overall, RBM39 exerts an antitumor effect in A549 cells by regulating gene expression and alternative splicing, largely by inhibiting the generation of the oncogenic NRG1-206 isoform to suppress malignant progression, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for LUAD.

Article.Title: Sustainable signal-processing spectrophotometric approaches for synchronous analysis of novel antiallergic combination: evaluation via multi-metric sustainability indices
Article.Authors: Abd El-Hadi H.; Fawzy M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents the development and validation of six sustainable signal-processing spectrophotometric approaches designed for the synchronous analysis of a novel antiallergic combination: Doxylamine succinate (DOX) and Phenylephrine hydrochloride (PHE). To resolve spectral overlap without chemical separation, various mathematical frameworks were employed, including: dual wavelength (DW), fourier self-deconvolution (FSD), first derivative (D 1 ), derivative ratio (DD 1 ), amplitude modulation (AM), and the amplitude summation (A-sum) method. The analytical procedures were conducted within linear ranges of 8.0–56.0 µg/mL for DOX and 20.0–180.0 µg/mL for PHE. Several processing parameters and wavelengths selection were optimized for each approach. DW approach is utilized ΔA 263.0–284.0 for DOX and ΔA 274.0–254.0 for PHE. The FSD method is applied at 286.0 for DOX and 278.0 nm for PHE. While D 1 amplitude is measured at 273.0 and 263.0 nm for DOX and PHE, respectively. The DD 1 approach utilized 237.0 nm for DOX and 287.0 nm for PHE. AM method was carried out at 277.0 nm while, A- sum method was applied at 288.0 nm for estimation of both DOX and PHE. All six methodologies showed excellent accuracy and precision according to ICH guidelines. Statistical comparison with established reference methods revealed no significant differences in performance. The environmental and practical impact of the methods was evaluated via multi-metric sustainability modern tools. The analytical greenness metric for sample preparation, the spider method, the green solvent selection too, Blue Applicability Grade Index, Click Analytical Chemistry Index, and Violet Innovation Grade Index were among the twelve newly created assessment metrics. Additionally, the Carbon Footprint Reduction Index, the Analytical Green Star Area, the Sustainability of Analytical Methods Index, the Modified GAPI, the Whiteness Evaluation for Chemical Analysis, and the Analytical Method Reliability Index. The results demonstrate that these signal-processing approaches offer a highly efficient, eco-friendly, and cost-effective alternative for the quality control of DOX and PHE in both raw materials and commercial tablets.

Article.Title: Characteristics of permeability variation in water well fracturing-flooding reconstruction and its numerical simulation representation
Article.Authors: Guo J.; Sun D.; Xu S.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Hydraulic fracturing flooding technology can effectively increase reservoir pressure and improve water injection capacity by injecting a large amount of fluid into the formation in a short time, which is especially suitable for low permeability, ultra-low permeability and tight sandstone reservoirs. In this paper, the study of water well fracturing flooding is carried out in the low permeability block of Jiangsu Oilfield. The relationship between permeability and effective stress is established by core fracturing flooding experiment, and the constitutive equation describing the change of reservoir physical properties after fracturing flooding is constructed. The method is applied to simulate the physical response of the reservoir near the wellbore during the fracturing flooding process. It is clear that there are two stages of permeability change before and after fracture, which meet the exponential relationship respectively. The constitutive equation is introduced into numerical simulation, and combined with the fracture propagation module, the dynamic characterization of reservoir physical property changes in the fracturing flooding transformation area is realized. The simulation results show that the proposed method can reasonably reflect the change of injection pressure in the process of fracturing flooding, improve the distribution of permeability field, and effectively evaluate the effect of fracturing flooding on the improvement of water injection capacity, average pressure near the wellbore and oil well production. The research provides theoretical basis and technical support for the optimization and effect evaluation of water well fracturing flooding parameters in low permeability reservoirs.

Article.Title: Dynamic allocation of post-earthquake emergency housing: a physically constrained lexicographic model
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Following major earthquakes, emergency housing allocation becomes a critical humanitarian logistics problem because shelter demand rises rapidly while transport networks may experience severe disruption. Unlike immediately consumable relief supplies, emergency housing provides effective shelter service only after transportation and post-arrival deployment have been completed. To address these challenges, this study develops a Physically Constrained Lexicographic Dynamic Allocation (PCLDA) model for post-earthquake emergency housing over a 72-h scenario-based acute allocation horizon following rapid assessment and initial route-serviceability assessment. The model integrates demand urgency, milestone-based minimum service protection, route availability, degraded travel time, period-specific dispatch capacity, vehicle loading capacity, and deployment delay, while distinguishing physical arrival from effective occupancy. A two-stage customized simulated annealing algorithm first maximizes 72-h effective coverage and then minimizes urgency-weighted cumulative unmet demand while preserving the best-found coverage. The model is evaluated using a Wenchuan-based scenario rather than an exact reconstruction of the historical relief process. Under the baseline setting, the best-found schedule provides 18,768 effectively occupiable housing units, corresponding to 90.746% of total demand, while satisfying the prescribed 5%, 30%, and 60% site-level service floors at 24, 48, and 72 h. Benchmark analysis shows that terminal-only protection can preserve final coverage while allowing substantial early service deprivation, whereas neglecting deployment delay can overestimate actual shelter availability. Route-disruption analysis further shows that moderate disruption reduces 72-h effective coverage to 87.612%, while under severe disruption no schedule satisfying all milestone requirements was identified. Sensitivity and housing-type analyses confirm that loading capacity and deployment delay materially affect short-horizon effective occupancy. The proposed PCLDA framework provides a physically grounded decision-support approach for emergency housing allocation over assessed and partially serviceable post-earthquake transport networks.

Article.Title: High prevalence and diversity of mesophilic bacteria detected in pre-enrichment raw milk from Ecuador using two multiplex TaqMan qPCR assays
Article.Authors: Loor-Giler A.; Muslin C.; Puga-Torres B.; Santander-Parra S.; Núñez L.
Article.Abstract: The consumption of raw cow’s milk remains common and traditional in Ecuador, especially due to its sale in informal markets, despite its recognized potential to act as a vehicle for multiple zoonotic pathogens and chemical substances. This study aimed to validate a multiplex quantitative PCR (qPCR) assay for the simultaneous detection and semi-quantitative assessment of eight mesophilic bacteria of food and public health relevance [ Listeria monocytogenes , Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) , Salmonella spp., Campylobacter spp., group B Streptococcus , Escherichia coli ( E. coli ), Shigella spp. and E. coli O157:H7], and to apply this tool to characterize their prevalence and distribution in raw milk from different production contexts in Ecuador. A total of 450 milk samples were analyzed, including 400 raw milk samples from cows without clinical mastitis, 40 samples from cows with confirmed mastitis, and 10 milk samples treated with ultra-high temperature (UHT) as negative controls. The multiplex assays showed amplification efficiencies between 95 and 105%, correlation coefficients ≥ 0.99 and limits of detection and quantification of 1 genomic copy/µL, with high analytical specificity and repeatability. In raw milk, at least one target bacterium was detected in almost all samples, with the highest prevalences observed for S. aureus (90.5%), E. coli (81.8%) and E. coli O157:H7 (70.8%), followed by Campylobacter spp. (46.3%), L. monocytogenes (34.0%), Salmonella spp. (28.8%), Shigella spp. (5.8%) and group B Streptococcus (1.8%). Mastitis milk showed 100% positivity for E. coli , high frequencies of S. aureus and group B Streptococcus , as well as absence of Salmonella spp. and L. monocytogenes , whereas all UHT samples were negative. Quantitative analysis revealed high bacterial loads for several pathogens, and the stratified evaluation showed significant differences in contamination patterns across provinces and producer size, although no significant seasonal (climatic) effect was observed. Overall, the findings confirm a substantial microbiological risk associated with raw milk consumption and support the use of multiplex qPCR as a robust tool for surveillance and risk-based control in dairy production systems. The consumption of raw milk poses a risk to public health, and given the results obtained here which indicate that there is little oversight in the region the public is urged to consume only pasteurized milk.
Article.Topic: Milk Quality and Mastitis in Dairy Cows

Article.Title: Estimated glucose disposal rate is associated with continuous glucose monitoring metrics in type 1 diabetes
Article.Authors: Herascu A.; Avram V.; Gaita L.; Braha A.; Cipu A.; Timar B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) is a composite surrogate of insulin sensitivity in type 1 diabetes (T1D) that incorporates HbA1c, creating potential construct overlap when associations with continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived metrics are examined. In this cross-sectional study of 64 adults with T1D, we evaluated eGDR–CGM associations and the contribution of the HbA1c component, using component-wise analysis as the primary interpretive approach. In conventional models adjusted for age, diabetes duration, and insulin delivery method, higher eGDR was associated with higher time in range (TIR), lower time above range (TAR), lower mean glucose, and lower glucose standard deviation (SD) and coefficient of variation (CV). However, after additional adjustment for HbA1c, eGDR was no longer associated with TIR, TAR, or mean glucose. Nominal associations remained with CV (β=−0.86% points, p = 0.043) and SD (β=−1.85 mg/dL, p = 0.031), but neither survived false-discovery-rate correction. In exploratory HbA1c-independent sensitivity analyses, higher CACTI estimated insulin sensitivity (eIS) was nominally associated with lower CV (β=−1.06% points, 95% CI − 1.97 to − 0.16; p = 0.0217; FDR q = 0.065) and lower SD (β=−2.72 mg/dL, 95% CI − 4.79 to − 0.65; p = 0.0109; q = 0.065); neither association survived FDR correction. Adjustment of the eGDR–SD model for mean glucose attenuated but did not eliminate the association, whereas simultaneous adjustment for HbA1c rendered it non-significant (β=−1.38 mg/dL, 95% CI − 2.79 to 0.02; p = 0.054). No association with TBR was observed (Spearman ρ=−0.056, p = 0.661). TIR > 70% was achieved by 24/64 participants. eGDR showed modest within-sample discrimination (AUC 0.704, 95% CI 0.562–0.829), whereas HbA1c alone had an AUC of 0.865 (95% CI 0.769–0.939). The associations with TIR, TAR, and mean glucose were largely attributable to shared HbA1c. The nominal variability associations did not survive FDR correction and remain exploratory.

Article.Title: Physics-guided explainable machine learning for predicting temporal scour evolution around hybrid spur dikes under unsteady flood hydrographs
Article.Authors: Daryaee M.; Hafshejani L.; Kashefipour S.; Shahriari A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of local scour around river-training structures during flood events remains a major challenge because scour evolution is governed by highly nonlinear interactions among hydraulic conditions, structural permeability, sediment transport, and time-dependent bed morphology. Although machine learning has recently improved scour prediction, existing studies have primarily focused on equilibrium scour under steady flow conditions and have largely treated predictive models as black boxes, limiting physical interpretation. This study develops an explainable physics-guided machine learning framework for predicting the temporal evolution of normalized scour depth around hybrid spur dikes (Bandal-like) under unsteady flood hydrographs. A laboratory dataset comprising 1,308 observations collected under nine hydrograph scenarios with different peak discharges, hydrograph durations, and permeability ratios was used to train and evaluate four regression algorithms, including Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Regression, and CatBoost. Hyperparameters were optimized using GridSearchCV with five-fold cross-validation, and a physics-guided cumulative-maximum constraint was incorporated to maintain temporal consistency of the predicted cumulative scour envelope by preventing nonphysical decreases. Among the investigated models, CatBoost achieved the highest predictive performance on the independent testing dataset, with \({R}^{2}=0.9110\) , RMSE = 0.0504, and MAE = 0.0343, and successfully reproduced the principal characteristics of temporal scour evolution across the investigated flood hydrographs. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses using CatBoost Feature Importance, Permutation Feature Importance, and SHAP consistently identified relative time ( \(t/{T}_{b}\) ) as the dominant predictor, followed by structural permeability ( \({R}_{a}\) ), while SHAP interaction analysis revealed nonlinear and condition-dependent relationships among hydrograph position, relative discharge, flow depth, and structural permeability. In particular, the predictive contribution of relative discharge became more pronounced near peak-flow conditions, while the influence of permeability varied with hydraulic loading and hydrograph stage. The proposed framework combines predictive performance with interpretable model-based insights and physics-guided temporal consistency, providing a complementary approach to conventional scour assessment within the investigated experimental domain.

Article.Title: Telomere length in midlife is associated with age, central adiposity, and perceived stress rather than habitual sauna exposure
Article.Authors: Skurvydas A.; Dadeliene R.; Aukstikalnis T.; Istomina N.; Strazdaite E.; Predkeliene A.; Baranauskiene N.; Valanciene D.; Majauskiene D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Regular sauna bathing has been linked to cardiovascular health and longevity benefits; however, the relationship between long-term sauna use and telomere biology, as well as its impact on biological aging, remains largely unexplored. In this cross-sectional study, we investigated the relationship between regular sauna use and telomere biomarkers in 84 adults aged 40 to 64 years. Telomere length was measured using high-throughput quantitative fluorescence in situ hybridization (HT Q-FISH), which allowed us to characterize the median, average, and short telomeres. Participants were divided into two groups: regular sauna users ( n = 42) and low-exposure controls ( n = 42). We assessed the associations between sauna use and telomere biomarkers using multivariable regression models. Telomere biomarkers did not show significant differences between the sauna groups, nor was sauna exposure independently linked to any telomere outcomes. The most consistent factor correlated with telomere length was chronological age; older individuals tended to have shorter telomeres and greater levels of biological aging derived from telomeres. Additionally, a higher waist-to-hip ratio and perceived stress were uniquely associated with shorter telomeres, and perceived stress was also connected to increased biological aging. There were no consistent associations found between physical activity, cardiorespiratory fitness, and telomere biomarkers, even in complementary quartile analyses. Regular sauna use did not show an independent link to peripheral blood telomere biomarkers in middle-aged adults. Instead, variations in telomere length were more consistently related to factors such as chronological age, central body fat, and perceived stress. This suggests that telomere length may better reflect the cumulative biological and psychosocial burdens a person has experienced, rather than their current lifestyle or functional abilities.

Article.Title: High-accuracy crude oil purity detection using a non-invasive microwave sensor with proximity-coupled patch antennas
Article.Authors: Zarghami S.; Roshani A.; Chayjan P.; Ali P.; Roshani G.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a non-invasive microwave-based sensor for high-precision purity detection of crude oil based on the proximity-coupled rectangular microstrip patch antennas. The sensor employs mutual electromagnetic coupling between two closely placed slotted rectangular-shaped antennas in order to extract dielectric metrics from oil-water mixtures. This design contrasts with more traditional single-antenna sensors, which rely entirely on S 11 or return loss, as our design utilizes additional scattering parameters (S 21 , S 22 ) for improved sensitivity and selectivity when characterizing oil purity. This antenna system operates in two primary frequency bands, specifically 6.9–7.6 GHz for detecting dielectric-based bandwidth variation and 1.6 GHz for characterizing signal transmission. The sensor is fabricated on the FR4 substrate and experimentally validates its capabilities with a wide range of water-oil mixtures. The results showed good agreement with simulated and measured data, and validated the high accuracy of the proposed sensor. To improve sensing precision and decrease nonlinearity due to operation at higher frequencies, artificial neural networks (ANN) models are used in the data processing step. Altogether, the ANN model increased prediction accuracy and model reliability for oil clarity classifications. Measured results indicate an S11 < − 10 dB in the 6.9–7.6 GHz with peak gain of 7.6 dBi, and the ANN regression yielded R²=0.995 with low prediction error, confirming enhanced detection accuracy.

Article.Title: A preclinical field-free line magnetic particle imaging system for molecular applications
Article.Authors: Aderhold E.; Schumacher J.; Stagge P.; Ahlborg M.; Scheel J.; Volpert T.; Graeser M.; Buzug T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Magnetic Particle Imaging offers unique features for molecular imaging. Its broader use in preclinical research is limited by the accessibility of suitable scanners. To aid in this, a scanner with a mechanically rotated permanent-magnet selection field with a gradient of 2.42 Tm $$^{-1}$$ is presented. It is paired with a modular transmit/receive chain, while feedthrough suppression is provided by a tunable second-order gradiometric receive coil and differential filtering, enabling operation in unshielded environments. The field-generation subsystem requires 413 W, considerably reducing infrastructure demands and permitting long measurements. Within a 40 mm diameter bore, system-matrix reconstruction yields sub-millimeter resolution of $$\le {0.36}$$ mm within a phantom filled with undiluted Perimag plain and a detection limit $$\le$$ 64.4 ng iron in 2D imaging at 1s $$^{-1}$$ rotation. The open software stack and modular hardware facilitate adaptation and scaling. Currently providing 2D images, the platform is poised for 3D through axial translation and algorithmic extensions, offering an accessible, cost-effective route to high-sensitivity preclinical molecular imaging.

Article.Title: Dynamic path reasoning with large language models for interpretable knowledge graph question answering
Article.Authors: Yuan L.; Wu B.; Yang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) aims to answer natural language questions by grounding them in structured knowledge graphs (KGs). Current KGQA systems still face three linked challenges: representing complex and compositional questions, providing transparent multi-hop reasoning traces, and using complete path-level evidence rather than only local triples. We propose SK-DRP ( S yntax- K nowledge enhanced D ynamic R easoning with P rompt learning), a modular KGQA framework that combines syntax-aware representation, state-adaptive path reasoning, and LLM-assisted answer selection. The syntax- and knowledge-enhanced encoder is an auxiliary representation enhancement that uses dependency information and knowledge-augmented pre-training to align questions with KG entities and relations. Here, dynamic denotes hop-wise recomputation of the question-focus indicator, score-qualified frontier expansion, and hop-weighted answer aggregation within a fixed dataset-level maximum hop budget; it does not denote automatic per-question depth selection. Candidate global paths are then compressed and transformed into natural-language auxiliary evidence for candidate-set-guided LLM answer selection. Experiments on MetaQA, WebQSP, and CWQ show that SK-DRP improves over several path-based and retrieval-based baselines on WebQSP and CWQ, while remaining competitive on MetaQA. Ablation, error, and interpretability analyses clarify how the syntax encoder, dynamic reasoning module, and LLM-assisted answer selection contribute to the final results, as well as the scope and limitations of the approach.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: knowledge graph question answering; large language models; dependency parsing; multi-hop reasoning; frontier expansion

Article.Title: HERO: a hierarchical attention and multi-feature fusion framework for automated English essay scoring
Article.Authors: Gou X.
Article.Abstract: Automated essay scoring (AES) has emerged as a crucial task in educational technology, aiming to replicate human evaluation of writing with speed, fairness, and accuracy. This study proposes an advanced deep learning framework, HERO (Hierarchical Essay Representation Optimizer), that uses hierarchical attention mechanisms and multi-feature fusion for holistic and grammar-based essay scoring. The proposed model employs a two-level bidirectional LSTM with attention to capture contextual information at both word and sentence levels, while integrating auxiliary metadata features such as prompt ID, gender, and grade level to enhance prediction performance. Experiments are conducted on the ASAP 2.0 dataset containing nearly 12,000 human-scored essays. The proposed framework demonstrates superior performance over baseline models, including MLP, KNN, and XGBoost, achieving a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.92, MAE of 0.019, and CCC of 0.91. Comprehensive evaluation using error metrics, correlation measures, and statistical validation confirms the robustness and reliability of the model. The findings indicate that the integration of hierarchical representation learning with feature-level fusion significantly enhances essay scoring accuracy while supporting interpretability. However, the fairness analysis was limited to aggregate evaluation on the available dataset, and subgroup-level calibration was not comprehensively validated.

Article.Title: Performance analysis of structural lightweight aggregate concrete modified with a combination of nano-silica and forta polymer fibers
Article.Authors: Tabari M.; Ahangari E.; Seidi E.; Rezaei S.; Nematzadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Recently, Structural Lightweight Aggregate Concrete (SLWAC) has gained significant attention as a viable solution for reducing structural dead weight and mitigating seismic structural demands in earthquake-prone regions. However, its widespread application has been hindered by its diminished strength and durability compared to normal-weight concrete. This study aims to investigate the synergistic effects of Nano-Silica (NS) and Forta polymer fibers on the mechanical and physical properties of SLWAC. Unlike prior works focused on isolated additives or normal-weight concretes, this study provides a comprehensive experimental evaluation of combining varying Forta fiber contents with NS in Lightweight Expanded Clay Aggregate (LECA)-based SLWAC, concurrently addressing compressive, tensile, flexural, and water absorption properties to determine an optimal balance between strength and durability. Accordingly, lightweight concrete was developed using LECA modified with NS at 3 wt% of cement, and Forta polymer fibers at volume fractions of 0%, 0.45%, 0.68%, and 0.9%. A total of 144 cubic, cylindrical, and flexural beam specimens were cast and tested. Compressive strength was evaluated at 7, 14, and 28 days, while tensile strength, flexural strength, and water absorption were determined at the 28-day mark. The results indicated that the combination of NS and Forta fibers significantly enhanced the performance, with increases in compressive, tensile, and flexural strengths by up to 44%, 77%, and 101%, respectively. Furthermore, water absorption of concrete was reduced by up to 42% through the inclusion of these two additives. Radar chart analysis identified the mix design containing 3 wt% NS and 0.68 vol% Forta fibers as the optimal proportion, providing an ideal balance between strength and durability. The findings of this research recommend the integrated use of NS and Forta polymer fibers as an effective strategy for upgrading the performance of SLWAC in structural engineering applications.

Article.Title: Surgical amputation and psychosocial adaptation with a focus on body image and phantom limb pain
Article.Authors: Yıldırım G.; Sarı B.; Keskin G.; Kılınç Ö.
Article.Abstract: Major earthquakes often result in severe injuries, including limb amputations, with long-lasting physical and psychosocial consequences. The February 6, 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes in Türkiye caused a substantial number of amputations. While surgical management and rehabilitation have been documented, limited research has explored the combined impact of phantom pain, body image changes, and psychosocial adaptation from the patient’s perspective. This study explores the lived experiences of amputees after the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes, focusing on phantom pain, body image changes, and psychosocial adaptation. A qualitative phenomenological approach was employed. Fifteen participants who underwent upper or lower limb amputations due to earthquake-related injuries were recruited via purposive and snowball sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth online interviews conducted between December 2024 and March 2025. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and thematically analyzed using manual coding in MAXQDA20.4.0 qualitative data analysis software. Trustworthiness was enhanced by member checking and peer debriefing. Five major themes were identified: (1) Communication patterns surrounding the amputation decision; (2) psychosocial reactions to amputation; (3) altered body image and role limitation; (4) phantom limb–related experiences; and (5) prosthesis-related issues. Participants reported limited communication during the amputation decision, intense emotional reactions following limb loss, altered body image and role limitations, persistent phantom limb pain, and challenges in adapting to prosthesis use. Post-disaster amputation is not only a physical loss but also a profound psychosocial experience, where phantom pain and body image changes play a central role in adaptation. Incorporating patient-centred, multidisciplinary, and culturally sensitive approaches into post-disaster healthcare frameworks is essential to support both physical recovery and psychosocial well-being.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: body image; phantom limb pain; psychosocial adjustment; amputation; amputees

Article.Title: Platelet trajectory subphenotypes in intensive care patients with sepsis-induced coagulopathy
Article.Authors: Wei E.; Zhao F.; Li F.; Lu W.
Article.Abstract: We aimed to identify early platelet trajectory-based subphenotypes in sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC), assess their prognostic value, explore whether glucocorticoid-related mortality associations differed across trajectory groups given within 24 h of ICU admission, and develop an early prediction model for trajectory membership. We retrospectively analyzed 6151 SIC patients from MIMIC-IV and externally validated the findings in 1305 patients from eICU. Platelet trajectories during the first 96 h were identified using group-based trajectory modeling among patients with sufficient platelet monitoring. The primary outcome was 28-day all-cause mortality after ICU admission. Multivariable Cox regression was used to evaluate associations between trajectory groups and outcome. An exploratory analysis assessed possible heterogeneity in the association between early systemic glucocorticoid exposure and mortality. A four-class prediction model was developed from first-day variables using XGBoost and externally validated. Four platelet trajectory groups were identified in MIMIC-IV, accounting for 23.3%, 35.3%, 32.4%, and 9.0% of patients. In the fully adjusted model, Groups 1, 2, and 3 had higher 28-day all-cause mortality risk than Group 4, with Group 1 showing the highest risk. The adjusted HRs for Groups 1, 2, and 3 versus Group 4 were 2.53, 1.73, and 1.39 in MIMIC-IV, and 5.78, 3.37, and 2.49 in eICU, respectively. The exploratory glucocorticoid analysis suggested possible heterogeneity in glucocorticoid-related mortality estimates across trajectory groups. The 24 h prediction model showed good multiclass performance in both internal and external validation, with macro-AUCs of 0.873 in MIMIC-IV and 0.884 in eICU. Among SIC patients with sufficient platelet monitoring, early platelet trajectories identified prognostically distinct subphenotypes. The observed differences in glucocorticoid-related mortality associations should be interpreted cautiously as hypothesis-generating. The 24 h prediction model may support early risk stratification.

Article.Title: Apigenin restores apoptotic pathways and induces G2/M arrest via modulation of DNA methylation and expression of pro and anti-apoptotic genes in HeLa cells
Article.Authors: Bhagavatula D.; Alagal R.; AlMousa L.; Behl S.; Zvereff V.; Bava P.; Raina R.; Faheem S.; Hasan T.; Hussain A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Apoptosis resistance is a characteristic of cervical cancer advancement, caused by the loss of tumor suppressor activity and continuous activation of pro-survival pathways. This study examines apigenin, a dietary flavonoid, as a regulator of proliferation and apoptotic signaling in HeLa cervical cancer cells. in silico analysis reported that Apigenin had a robust binding affinity for CDK1, CDK2, XIAP, and cIAP, indicating competitive suppression of their natural ligand interactions. In vitro studies revealed that treatment of HeLa cells with Apigenin (24 & 48 H, 1-175 µM) resulted in a dose- and time-dependent reduction in cell viability, mitochondrial membrane depolarization, G2/M phase arrest, and an increase in apoptotic cell populations. These phenotypic alterations were followed by the overexpression of pro-apoptotic genes and tumor suppressors (DIABLO, BAX, CASP3, CASP8, p53, DAPK1) and the downregulation of anti-apoptotic genes (BCL2, XIAP, Survivin), which was consistent at the protein level. Methylation sequencing across CpG contexts demonstrated that differential DNA methylation coincided with transcriptional changes, with alterations in CpG island methylation rather than non-CpG contexts exhibiting the most significant correlation with the modified expression of apoptotic and anti-apoptotic genes. These findings establish CpG methylation as a crucial epigenetic mechanism driving apigenin-induced transcriptional reprogramming, positioning apigenin as a dual-function agent that induces apoptosis and modulates the cervical cancer epigenome, with implications for enhanced cancer management strategies.

Article.Title: POI location-aware services package recommendation for random groups
Article.Authors: Shang L.; Song X.; Liu Z.; Zhang K.; Sheng Q.; Yu J.
Article.Abstract: Recently, with the rapid growth of Point of Interest (POIs) and increasing of social activities, more and more individuals tend to join parties or trips with groups formed randomly (named random groups, RGs). Although some works have proposed wonderful POI recommendation methods for RGs, they failed to consider how to recommend service packages for RGs after they accept the recommended POIs, which significantly degrades user experience. To address this issue, this work proposes a POI location-aware service package recommendation model for random groups (termed PLSPR-RG). First of all, PLSPR-RG generates fitted feature representations of random groups with an enhanced feature learning method. Then, it selects users with similar characteristics to the random group and utilizes service usage data of similar users as the training dataset for PLSPR-RG. Subsequently, PLSPR-RG constructs a service labeled bipartite graph of similar users, then it employs an edge-enhanced bipartite graph neural network with multi-view contrastive learning (EBGNN-CL) to learn service feature representations that capturing both positive and negative interaction preferences of similar users. Furthermore, PLSPR-RG builds a directed service transition graph based on the service interaction records of similar users and adopts the SRGNN network to learn service feature representations containing latent user preferences, as well as user preference representations. Finally, based on the learned service representations and the fitted features of random groups, PLSPR-RG generates a ranked list of recommended services, thereby completing POI location-aware service package recommendation for random groups. Extensive experiments have been conducted on three public datasets (Foursquare, Gowalla and Yelp dataset), which have proved that our proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art models.

Article.Title: The genetically determined role of the compact myocardial layer in excessively trabeculated left ventricular noncompaction
Article.Authors: Mester B.; Grebur K.; Farkas-Sütő K.; Tardy J.; Gyulánczi F.; Horváth M.; Panajotu A.; Suhai F.; Fekete B.; Bödör C.; Vágó H.; Merkely B.; Szűcs A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background: Left ventricular excessive trabeculation (LVET) ranges from preserved ejection fraction (EF) morphology to reduced EF Noncompaction cardiomyopathy. Emerging evidence indicates that EF reduction is more strongly associated with thinning of the Compact myocardial layer (CL) than with trabeculation alone, although the precise role of the CL in LVET has yet to be determined. Aim: We aimed to evaluate Trabeculated layer (TL) and CL thickness in LVET subjects with preserved EF across genotypes, establish genotype-specific CL thickness cut-offs, and analyse their association with LV parameters. Methods: We enrolled 54 LVET subjects with matched healthy Controls. In CMR, functional, volumetric and myocardial-mass parameters were measured using threshold-based analysis. TL thicknesses were assessed using calliper tools and CL thickness was measured using OptiLayer software. For genetic testing, cardiac NGS panels were used; LVET subjects were classidied into Benign (B), VUS, and Pathogenic (P) subgroups according to ACMG databases. Results: LVET subjects showed thicker TL and thinner CL compared to Controls. CL thickness differed among genetic subgroups: P variants were associated with significantly thinner apical segments, with a cut-off of 5 mm (93% of P <5 mm, 41% of VUS < 5 mm, 8% of B<5 mm, p < 0.05). TL thickness showed no association with genotype. CL thickness correlated with global circumferential strain ( r = 0.461, p < 0.01), indicating subclinical dysfunction. Conclusion: CL thinning in LVET with preserved EF was associated with P genetic background and may represent early morphological alterations. These findings suggest potential roles in diagnosis, risk stratification, and follow-up, which should be further evaluated in longitudinal studies.

Article.Title: Association between antinuclear antibodies, oxidative stress index, and immune markers in systemic lupus erythematosus
Article.Authors: Saeed L.; Naji S.; yousif R.; Alasmari M.; Alshaeri H.; Junaidi H.; Makai A.; Talib W.; Hock M.
Article.Abstract: Autoimmune disorders have been reported with a high incidence among the Iraqi population in the past year, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This study was designed to assess the association between oxidative stress index and antinuclear antibodies, as well as their relationship with clinical features in SLE cases. A case-control study was conducted involving 50 patients with SLE and 50 healthy individuals. Clinical features and oxidative stress markers—including total oxidant status (TOS), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), oxidative stress index (OSI), malondialdehyde (MDA), and antinuclear antibody (ANA)—were assessed. Data were analyzed using statistical tests with a significance level of p < 0.05. Results SLE patients exhibited significantly higher levels of total oxidant status (TOS), oxidative stress index (OSI), malondialdehyde (MDA), and nitric oxide (NO) compared with controls (p < 0.05), while total antioxidant capacity (TAC) was significantly lower. Age and BMI were comparable between groups. Oxidative stress parameters were largely similar across clinical subgroups, except for higher MDA levels in patients without fever. Correlation analysis demonstrated a strong association between OSI, TOS, and TAC. Regression models identified TOS and TAC as independent predictors of OSI, whereas antinuclear antibody (ANA) was not independently associated with oxidative markers. Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by a significant oxidative imbalance that occurs independently of demographic factors, alongside elevated autoimmune activity. Oxidative stress appears to be a core feature of the disease, operating partly independently of immune markers.

Article.Title: A deep feature-based approach for classifying flue gas pollutants and hazard identification using pyramid-dilated temporal convolution networks
Article.Authors: Renganathan K.; Umamaheswari B.
Article.Abstract: Nowadays, real-world monitoring and accurate prediction for toxic gas concentration have gained much attention from researchers, as it provides great work in emergency validation situations and rescue works. The Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based gas concentration prediction techniques face more problems in terms of poor convergence speed, equal feature importance, and minimal accuracy. But, choosing the best design and also validating the most suitable safety measures are difficult due to the lack of execution of the important field examinations under emission regulations. So, a deep learning-based flue gas analysis model is implemented for hazard detection. Here, required samples are gathered from benchmark resources and features are extracted through Convolutional-Autoencoder with Spatial–Temporal Attention (CA-STA). The flue gas classification is performed using a Pyramid Dilated-based Adaptive Temporal Convolution Network (PD-ATCN), where the extracted features are given as inputs. The flexibility of the suggested approach is enhanced by fine-tuning the parameters of PD-ATCN using Improved Random Variable-based Cray Fish Optimization (IRV-CFO). Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated through diverse performance metrics, which show higher robustness. In the accuracy analysis, the developed IRV-CFO-PD-ATCN gained superior typical flue gas pollutants classification and hazards identification outcome as 95.11% for dataset 1 and 92.6% for dataset 2, compared to baseline approaches. Hence, the experimental results showed that the suggested approach is capable of achieving more precise typical flue gas classification and hazards detection outcomes than others under dynamic conditions.

Article.Title: Frozen vision transformers can be reused via cross-scale feature fusion
Article.Authors: Qin L.; Kou L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As Vision Transformer (ViT) models continue to scale, the training and fine-tuning costs for achieving advanced performance have surged, forcing us to rethink the sustainability of relying solely on model scaling. In this work, we explore a more cost-effective alternative. By effectively exploiting the complementary potential of existing frozen models, we avoid the expense of training large models from scratch. Based on this idea, we propose the Dual-ViT Fusion Transformer (DVFT). This framework explicitly aligns and fuses heterogeneous features from different frozen backbones, thereby addressing the limited representational scope and insufficient cross-scale semantic coverage of a single frozen model. Such limitations are difficult to mitigate within existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning frameworks, which are primarily designed for single-model settings. Specifically, DVFT introduces two complementary guidance paradigms. The first is Intrinsic Anchor-based calibration, which uses the frozen models’ own global semantic representations as alignment references to establish cross-model semantic consistency. The second is Extrinsic Query-based guidance, which employs learnable queries as an information bottleneck to progressively extract and integrate complementary discriminative features across models, enabling flexible feature interaction. Experimental results show that our method approaches the performance of expensively trained models with very few training epochs. These findings indicate that DVFT provides a scalable and low-cost pathway for efficiently reusing existing frozen models to achieve high-performance visual recognition.

Article.Title: HERStory: development and process evaluation of a manualized drama therapy intervention for women with breast cancer
Article.Authors: Roehlig K.; de Abreu C.; Rosati C.; Becerik D.; Kobus S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite increasing recognition of creative arts therapies within psycho-oncology, manualized drama therapy interventions remain scarce. This article introduces HERStory, a six-session drama therapy group intervention for women with breast cancer, combining the Heroine’s Journey with role work, dramatic enactment, embodiment-oriented techniques, and resource-oriented approaches, and presents an initial process evaluation. The HERStory study was conducted as a prospective, non-randomized study with a pre–post–post design. Process evaluation used the newly developed Drama Therapy Process Observation Instrument (SK-BTP), a 43-item observer-rated instrument assessing eight dimensions of drama therapy group processes. Ratings were completed by an independent drama therapist. Descriptive analyses included 14 participants completing the intervention. Overall process quality demonstrated a positive trajectory. Mean scores increased from M = 3.56 to M = 4.31 in Group 1 and from M = 3.63 to M = 4.51 in Group 3, whereas Group 2 maintained consistently high scores (M = 4.19–4.30). Process openness reached relatively high levels early, whereas role flexibility, thematic development, and symbolic depth increased across sessions. The findings provide preliminary insights into the implementation of HERStory and the development of core drama therapy processes across the six sessions. The manual offers a transparent and reproducible intervention for future research and clinical practice. Further studies with larger samples and controlled designs are warranted to evaluate its effectiveness and applicability in other populations. Article.Title: Rapid reconstruction-free classification from Lissajous sparse sampling using deep learning
Article.Authors: Gardner M.; Rabaiah Y.
Article.Abstract: Non-raster laser scanning techniques such as Lissajous scanning provide mechanically efficient alternatives to conventional raster scanning, but typically require computationally expensive image reconstruction before automated analysis. This reconstruction step offsets many of the speed and efficiency advantages of sparse scanning and is a bottleneck in real-time imaging systems. Here, we demonstrate that accurate object recognition can be performed directly from one-dimensional Lissajous intensity measurements without reconstructing an intermediate image. In our proof-of-concept work, optimized Lissajous scan trajectories were used to sparsely sample MNIST handwritten digits, generating one-dimensional signal representations containing 50, 100, 200, or 500 measurements. These signals were classified using one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, and k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and compared with conventional reconstruction-based image classification pipelines using both pre-trained and retrained convolutional neural networks. The proposed 1D-CNN achieved 98.60% classification accuracy using only 500 sampled measurements while classifying 10,000 test images in 0.68 s. Reconstruction-based image classifiers achieved slightly higher peak accuracy (99.34%) but required more than 150 s to reconstruct and classify the same dataset. Across all evaluated models, direct signal-domain classification reduced end-to-end computational cost by more than two orders of magnitude while maintaining comparable or slightly diminished classification performance. These findings demonstrate that image reconstruction is not a prerequisite for accurate object recognition from sparsely sampled Lissajous measurements and establish reconstruction-free deep learning as an efficient framework for intelligent laser-scanning systems. The proposed approach has potential applications in LiDAR, optical coherence tomography, endoscopic imaging, image-guided surgery, and other computational imaging systems where rapid inference and reduced computational overhead are critical.

Article.Title: Feature-dependent agreement between markerless and marker-based motion capture during continuous Taijiquan movement
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Markerless motion capture is increasingly used outside specialist laboratories, but its validity may differ across kinematic features. We analysed paired Kinect V2 and Qualisys recordings from 12 participants performing 13 standardised Taijiquan gestures, comprising 1815 strictly paired segments and 156 participant-by-gesture units. Analyses used the official source files, timestamp-aware preprocessing, participant-cluster uncertainty estimates, absolute-agreement and consistency metrics, native-unit errors, and sensitivity analyses for anatomical mapping, filtering, bandwidth, synchronisation, scale normalisation, and data quality. Agreement was strongly feature-dependent. Pelvis features showed high agreement; knee and elbow angles preserved high relative consistency despite systematic offsets; hip agreement was mapping-sensitive; sagittal trunk orientation showed negligible cross-system association; and derivative-based velocity and smoothness measures remained distorted across sensitivity conditions. Participant-isolated feature-specific calibration corrected stable knee and elbow bias but did not restore features with weak underlying association. Exploratory participant-level quality ranking showed relatively high observed correlations for some models, but neither Ridge reference condition met the Holm-adjusted permutation threshold. These findings support feature-specific validation that distinguishes systematic bias, anatomical-mapping sensitivity, and residual measurement error.

Article.Title: Federated learning with adaptive reliability aware aggregation for privacy preserving healthcare IoT systems
Article.Authors: Barot V.; Dave J.; R. M.; Vahora S.; Maltare N.; Gangrade J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) devices generate vast amounts of sensitive patient data, creating significant privacy risks and regulatory challenges when processed through centralized architectures. Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising solution by enabling decentralized model training without sharing raw data. However, real-world deployment faces critical challenges including device heterogeneity, intermittent connectivity, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data, and unreliable node participation. This paper proposes a Reliability-Aware Adaptive Aggregation (RAAA) framework that dynamically evaluates client trustworthiness through three dimensions: update quality (local accuracy and gradient alignment), participation consistency (historical engagement patterns), and communication latency. These metrics are integrated into a composite reliability score using weighted aggregation, which adaptively prioritizes contributions from trustworthy nodes during global model updates. The framework was validated using PhysioNet electrocardiogram (ECG) datasets (MIT-BIH and PTB) with 20 simulated healthcare IoT clients under conditions of node dropout and data heterogeneity. Experimental results demonstrate that RAAA achieved 91.7% classification accuracy on arrhythmia detection, outperforming Federated Averaging (FedAvg) (85.2%), Federated Proximal (FedProx) (86.4%), and Q-FedAvg (87.1%) by 6.5%, 5.3%, and 4.6%, respectively. The proposed method converged 17% faster (43 versus 52 rounds) and maintained an 85.6% client participation rate. Cross-dataset validation on the PTB database confirmed consistent improvements across different physiological signals. The RAAA framework provides a robust, privacy-preserving FL solution for healthcare IoT environments with superior accuracy, faster convergence, and resilience to unreliable nodes. All evaluations are conducted in a simulated environment; while theoretical energy and complexity analyses suggest suitability for resource-constrained edge devices, real-hardware validation remains an important direction for future work.

Article.Title: A hybrid QSPR-MCDM framework for ranking organic acids using topological indices
Article.Authors: Xue Z.; Yousaf S.; Khalid W.; Tawfiq F.; Tola K.
Article.Abstract: Organic acids are industrially and pharmaceutically important compounds, yet selecting the most suitable acid for a given application is complicated by the need to reconcile multiple, often conflicting physicochemical properties. This study develops and validates a hybrid framework that integrates Quantitative Structure–Property Relationship (QSPR) modeling with Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) to systematically rank twenty organic acids. Thirteen degree-based topological indices were computed from the hydrogen-suppressed molecular graphs of the acids and used as structural descriptors to build linear QSPR models for five key physicochemical properties: boiling point, molecular weight, enthalpy of vaporization, flash point, and density. All five models were statistically significant ( \(p < 0.001\) ), with leave-one-out cross-validated \(Q^2\) values ranging from 0.52 to 0.77, confirming genuine predictive capability. The QSPR-estimated properties then constituted the decision matrix for the MCDM stage. Three MCDM methods (TOPSIS, VIKOR, and SAW) were combined with four weight-allocation approaches (Point Allocation, Mean Weight, Standard Deviation, and Entropy), yielding twelve distinct ranking scenarios that were subsequently integrated into a single composite ordering via rank-average aggregation. Unlike earlier applications of MCDM in chemical graph theory, where topological indices themselves served as criteria, the present framework employs indices exclusively as structure descriptors within the QSPR stage, ensuring that the final ranking reflects predicted chemical behavior rather than abstract graph-theoretic quantities. The results demonstrate strong robustness at the extremes of the ranking: Ascorbic acid and Gallic acid consistently occupy the top two positions across all twelve scenarios, while Tetraacetic acid is uniformly ranked last. In contrast, mid-tier acids such as Citric acid, Tartaric acid, Phthalic acid, and EDAHA display considerable rank variability, reflecting more balanced property profiles that are sensitive to weighting choices. Spearman rank correlation between individual scenarios and the composite ranking ranged from \(\rho \approx 0.87\) to \(\rho \approx 0.99\) , with differentiated weighting schemes (PA, SD, E) agreeing more closely with the composite than the equal-weight scheme. The proposed QSPR-MCDM framework offers a robust, objective, and adaptable tool for holistic compound assessment and rational selection in chemical, material, and pharmaceutical applications, moving beyond single-property prediction toward informed multi-criteria decision-making.

Article.Title: Collective action and livelihood transformation among Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) in Jharkhand: a multivariate integrated modelling framework identifying key drivers
Article.Authors: Maitra S.; Behera H.; Kumar R.; Sawarn K.; Jana R.; Ghosh K.; Kabiraj T.
Article.Abstract: Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) have emerged as important institutional mechanisms for improving smallholder livelihoods in India, yet evidence on their broader socio-economic impacts remains limited, particularly in regions such as Jharkhand. This study examines the factors shaping farmer participation and success within FPO systems using data from 498 farmers. The findings reveal a dominant dimension of livelihood improvement characterized by gains in living standards, nutrition, and technological adoption. Agricultural income and institutional capacity, particularly training and exposure, are consistently associated with higher levels of success. Distinct farmer typologies indicate that stronger institutional engagement is linked with better outcomes, even among farmers with relatively limited resources. Overall, the results highlight that livelihood transformation within FPO systems extends beyond income growth and is closely associated with sustained capacity-building and institutional support. The study underscores the need for context-specific, capacity-oriented policy interventions to enhance the effectiveness and long-term sustainability of FPO-led rural development, contributing to broader efforts toward inclusive and resilient rural transformation.

Article.Title: Element interaction manifolds for comparative analysis of geometric representations in protein-ligand recognition
Article.Authors: Shahi A.; Rana M.; Nguyen D.
Article.Abstract: Accurate modeling of protein–ligand interactions requires representations that capture both molecular geometry and chemically specific interactions. Existing approaches encode molecular recognition through several geometric formalisms, including differential geometry and spherical harmonic surface descriptors such as three-dimensional Zernike descriptors (3DZD). However, the relative roles of local curvature, surface area, volume, global shape, and chemical partitioning in protein–ligand recognition remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we present a unified geometric study centered on the Element Interaction Manifold (EIM) framework. We integrate element-interactive curvature, surface-area, and volume descriptors into a common representation and comparatively evaluate their roles in binding-affinity prediction and ligand-aware protein–ligand complex recognition. To place differential geometry in context, we compare EIM with standard 3DZD and a chemically partitioned extension termed element-pair 3DZD (EP-3DZD). Across PDBbind/CASF-2016 affinity prediction and unsupervised ligand-aware recognition tasks, chemically resolved interaction geometry provides strong predictive performance. Chemical partitioning improves the Zernike-based representation relative to standard global 3DZD, whereas combining Zernike descriptors with Hybrid EIM produces only small numerical gains, indicating limited additional complementarity under the evaluated protocols. Additional robustness and control analyses support the stability of the affinity-prediction results and clarify the contribution of shared ligand identity to the ligand-aware recognition task. Overall, these results support chemically resolved geometric information as an interpretable and informative representation for protein–ligand modeling.

Article.Title: Degradation-parameter-supervised restoration of optical borehole images for fracture-oriented structural characterization: leakage-audited cross-domain validation
Article.Authors: Shi D.; Zhai S.; Ma R.
Article.Abstract: Optical borehole televiewer (OTV) images support fracture-oriented structural characterization, but non-uniform illumination can obscure weak traces. We propose PG-BIE, a 47,170-parameter restoration network that supervises illumination, transmission and airlight estimates before analytic inversion and bounded refinement. The primary dataset comprised 220 training and 55 validation rock-wall OTV images. Across five runs, PG-BIE achieved 15.146 ± 0.035 dB PSNR and 0.8384 ± 0.0044 gradient similarity under a fixed synthetic-degradation protocol. An official LOL-v1-trained Retinexformer baseline achieved 13.144 dB PSNR and 0.4627 gradient similarity and produced marked cross-domain brightening. A conservative source-group leakage audit retained 28 validation images from 21 groups; PG-BIE improved PSNR over degraded input by 2.928 dB (95% cluster-bootstrap CI, 2.081–3.621) and gradient similarity by 0.2746 (0.2346–0.3088). Independent validation used 512 windows from two ROGUE ice OPTV logs and 193 interpreted fracture bands from 11 rock borehole-television wells. The two ROGUE sites responded oppositely. On the rock bands, SSIM and gradient similarity increased, but PSNR decreased by 1.113 dB (− 1.970 to − 0.073), indicating a domain-dependent color shift. PG-BIE therefore supports traceable illumination correction, but image-quality gains do not establish improved fracture detection or orientation measurement.

Article.Title: Alignment-free RGB-T salient object detection: a semantic-guided deformable alignment and asymmetric fusion network
Article.Authors: Zhai S.; Ba Y.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: RGB-T salient object detection aims to segment salient objects by exploiting complementary information from visible and thermal infrared modalities. However, existing methods often rely on manually aligned pairs and struggle with large-range offsets, scale variations, and local nonlinear deformations during acquisition. These discrepancies may weaken cross-modal correlations and introduce unsuitable fusion cues. To address these challenges, we propose a Semantic-guided Deformable Alignment and Asymmetric Fusion Network (SDAF-Net) for alignment-free RGB-T salient object detection. First, a multi-scale semantic constraint module extracts a shared saliency-aware representation and generates semantic priors for deformable feature sampling and fusion. Then, a semantic-guided dense deformation alignment module estimates a task-optimized Cross-modal Deformation Offset Map through coarse-to-fine refinement. The offset map resamples multi-scale thermal features on the RGB reference feature grid and provides spatially adaptive cross-modal cues. Finally, an asymmetric rectification fusion module uses task-driven masks generated jointly from RGB and resampled thermal features to calibrate RGB responses while preserving the original thermal features for fusion. Experiments on unaligned, weakly aligned, and aligned RGB-T benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance and more complete saliency maps in complex scenarios.

Article.Title: Endocytic CEACAM receptor loss and lack of positive selection in CEACAM1 of birds and snakes indicate absence of pathogen-CEACAM1 interactions in some reptiles
Article.Authors: Zimmermann W.; Kammerer R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The CEACAM gene family is among the fastest evolving in vertebrates. It likely originated from an ancestral CEACAM1 -like gene encoding an inhibitory receptor. In mammals, CEACAM1 is expressed on epithelial cells and can regulate leukocyte activation. Thus, several bacterial pathogens exploit it for host entry and immune suppression. Probably this threat selected for the evolution of decoy receptors with CEACAM1-like pathogen-binding domains. In humans, the granulocyte-specific decoy receptor CEACAM3 can redirect CEACAM1-binding pathogens to neutrophils, promoting their uptake and destruction via its endocytic motif. Whether this evolutionary pattern occurs across all vertebrate clades remains unclear. Here, we identified CEACAM families in more than 100 reptile and 244 bird species. Non-avian reptiles such as turtles and crocodiles possessed expanded CEACAM gene families. Alongside the conserved CEACAM19 , found in nearly all mammals, all non-avian reptiles carried CEACAM1 and variable numbers of CEACAM1 -related genes, mostly encoding transmembrane CEACAMs with endocytic ITAM motifs. Notably, snakes lacked these members. In contrast, some bird clades contained only a single CEACAM gene ( CEACAM1 ), while others lacked CEACAM genes entirely. The absence of both decoy receptors and positive selection of CEACAM1 in birds and snakes suggests these clades may lack CEACAM1-binding pathogens.

Article.Title: Identification of potential donors for bruchid (Callosobruchus maculatus) resistance in blackgram through multi-environments phenotyping and biochemical profiling
Article.Authors: Jaiswal S.; Pandey R.; Pandey A.; Tiwari B.; Chirag N/A.; Maurya P.; Rai A.; Singh S.; Mishra M.; Singh A.; Singh B.; Singh C.
Article.Abstract: Among the various threats limiting the blackgram production, bruchids ( Callosobruchus spp.) are a serious concern, particularly under storage conditions. The present experiments were carried out with 258 Vigna accessions belonging to V. mungo and V. umbellata to identify the potential donors for bruchid ( Callosobruchus maculatus ) resistance. The studies on biological parameters revealed that the percent damage ranged from 0.0 to 95.0%. The results indicated that two blackgram (SYNP-2, BLU-1) and two ricebean wild accessions (PRR 2008-2, PRR 2008-2-sel) were identified as highly resistant (HR) on the basis of percent damage. Further, based on the stability index and GGE biplot analysis, it was demonstrated that these genotypes have the potential of resistance over the year/ environments, considered as stable genotypes. Biochemical analysis showed that tannin, total phenol and flavonoid contents were higher in resistant genotypes compared to susceptible genotypes. These potential donors will serve as genetic stock in a breeding programme for improving the bruchid resistance.

Article.Title: Taurine ameliorates negative energy balance-induced gene expression alterations in buffalo granulosa cells
Article.Authors: Rani S.; Kapri A.; Patel P.; Singh D.; Onteru S.
Article.Abstract: Negative Energy Balance (NEB), characterized by high serum free fatty acids (FFAs) and low glucose levels, is a common condition during early postpartum in dairy animals. NEB impairs postpartum fertility by negatively impacting the function of granulosa cells, the key cells in regulating ovarian folliculogenesis and estrogen production. Our previous studies identified reduced serum taurine levels, a sulfur-containing beta-amino acid, during the postpartum period in buffaloes, suggesting a potential association between taurine deficiency and postpartum reproductive problems. Therefore, the objective of the present in vitro study was to evaluate whether taurine could ameliorate NEB-induced alterations in lipid accumulation and the expression of genes related to steroidogenesis, gonadotropin signaling and taurine function in primary buffalo granulosa cells. Buffalo granulosa cells were cultured for 48 h for initial establishment, and subsequently exposed to three different NEB conditions (NEB1: 200 µM FFA and 50 mg/dl glucose; NEB2: 400 µM FFA and 40 mg/dl glucose; NEB3: 800 µM FFA and 30 mg/dl glucose) for 24 h. The culture media under each NEB condition were then supplemented with taurine at four different concentrations (50, 100, 150, and 200 µg/ml), and the cells were cultured in taurine-supplemented media for an additional 24 h. Cells in NEB control groups were maintained under corresponding NEB conditions for 48 h. The cells were subjected to Oil-Red-O staining, MTT assay, and gene expression studies. MTT assay showed no significant change in cell viability between NEB conditions and vehicle control (VC) or between taurine-treated and NEB groups. However, lipid accumulation was higher in NEB compared to VC and taurine-treated groups. The NEB conditions downregulated the genes involved in steroidogenesis ( CYP19A1 , STAR , and HSD17B1 ), gonadotropin signaling ( FSHR and LHR ), and taurine biosynthesis (CSAD), transport ( TauT) and response ( TUG1 ), but upregulated the expression of CD36 , a fatty acid translocase. Taurine significantly ( P < 0.05) ameliorated NEB-induced alterations in gene expression, indicating taurine’s potential in mitigating NEB effects on buffalo granulosa cells. Bioinformatics analyses suggested that TUG1, a long non-coding RNA, may contribute to taurine-mediated regulation of gene expression through a putative miRNA sponge mechanism. Overall, 200 µg/ml of taurine showed the most consistent beneficial effect modulating the alterations in gene expression patterns in buffalo granulosa cells across the NEB conditions studied. Hence, in vivo studies are needed in the future to evaluate the potential of taurine as a nutritional supplement to buffaloes during early postpartum.

Article.Title: The role of sense of mission in rural physical education teachers’ turnover intention: a moderated mediation model
Article.Authors: Gao W.; Li T.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: The viability of the physical education teachers in rural areas is critical in the sustainability of the quality of the rural education system and the balance of holistic development of the students. Nevertheless, such teachers still experience a high turnover intention. In addition to external policy actions, other aspects need to be looked at internally on the psychological processes that lead to their readiness to stay in the job. The research follows the Job Demands-Resources Model and Resource Conservation Theory to develop a moderated mediation model and discuss the change of sense of mission on turnover intention among the rural physical education teachers. The research is aimed at examining the mediating variable of occupational burnout and the moderating variable of social support. Methods: Four hundred and thirty six physical education teachers in the township primary and secondary schools in Henan Province, Sichuan Province, and Gansu Province were surveyed by clustering sampling method. The Chinese versions of the Vocational Calling Scale, Maslach Burnout Inventory, Perceived Social supportive Scale as well as Job leaving intention Scale were used as Research instruments. The SPSS 26.0 and the PROcess macro (Model 59) were used to analyze the data. Findings: The correlation analysis results demonstrated that there was a positive correlation between the sense of mission and social support, and a negative correlation between the sense of mission and occupational burnout and turnover intention. Sense of mission had a direct and indirect (through occupational burnout) decrease in turnover intention. Conclusion: The effects of sense of mission on burnout, and the effects of burnout on turnover intention are buffered by social support- this effect was the greatest in conditions of a low level of social support. Occupational burnout mediates the mediating role of sense of mission on the turnover intention, social support moderates the first stage (sense of mission to occupational burnout) and the second stage (occupational burnout to turnover intention) of the mediating process. The results point to a mediated moderation process and indicate that the stabilization of the rural population of physical education teachers should be done through reinforcing the sense of mission in the teachers and the creation of a strong social support network at the same time. These measures will assist in alleviating work burnout and eventually decrease the turnover probability.
