Article.Title: Grey wolf optimization-driven convolutional neural network for robust cardiac MRI-based heart disease classification under class imbalance
Article.Authors: Asha M.; Prasath S.; Kesavulu D.; Lakshmi S.
Article.Abstract: Heart disease diagnosis through Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a vital clinical diagnostic technique that enables the non-invasive evaluation of cardiac structure and identification of cardiovascular diseases. Nevertheless, the automation of such a task using deep learning faces some critical problems in terms of limited data size, class imbalance, and manual tuning of hyperparameters, which might hinder the accuracy and reliability of the process. Therefore, this paper introduces a novel algorithm called GWO-CNN for heart disease classification based on cardiac MRI. In this algorithm, structured pre-processing, contrast enhancement, augmenting-based class balancing, CNN-based spatial features extraction, and GWO-based hyperparameters selection will be used for the classification process. Cardiac MRIs are preprocessed through normalization, Gaussian filtering, contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization, cropping, and resizing improve anatomical clarity and generate standardized image inputs. Moreover, the classifier model consists of a CNN model to identify between normal and abnormal heart MRIs and Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm to find optimal values of hyperparameters (learning rate, dropout rate, batch size, configuration of convolutional filters, and dense layer size). Experimental results, obtained via patient-level five-fold cross-validation repeated across five random seeds (25 runs in total), demonstrated that the GWO-CNN framework attained a mean accuracy of 98.30% ± 0.42% (95% CI: 98.13–98.47%), a mean F1-score of 97.50% ± 0.46%, and a mean AUC of 98.60% ± 0.39%, with a representative single-fold configuration reaching 98.42% accuracy, 97.86% precision, 97.31% recall, a 97.58% F1-score, a specificity of 98.91%, a Dice score of 97.52%, a Jaccard similarity index of 95.23%, a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 96.41%, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 98.74%. Paired statistical testing (t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < 0.001) confirmed that the improvements attributable to preprocessing, GAN-based augmentation, and GWO-based tuning, as well as the improvement over baseline CNN, ResNet-based, and transfer-learning-based comparators, are each statistically significant. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed GAN-assisted GWO-CNN framework for cardiac MRI classification under limited and class-imbalanced data conditions. A preliminary external evaluation on the independent ACDC dataset, performed without any retraining, yielded 92.00% accuracy, a moderate decrease from the internal cross-validated mean consistent with real but non-catastrophic distributional shift. However, because the primary evaluation is based on a relatively small single public dataset and external validation was limited to one additional cohort assessed once, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary proof-of-concept evidence rather than confirmation of clinical applicability. Further validation using larger and independent multi-center cardiac MRI cohorts is required before the proposed framework can be considered for clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Adverse childhood experiences are associated with intimate partner violence-related head and neck injuries and symptom burden among adult women
Article.Authors: Astridge A.; Mu E.; Copas C.; Hannon O.; Martins B.; Padgett C.; Spitz G.; Makovec Knight J.; McDonald S.; Edwards E.; Meyer S.; Shultz S.; Symons G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are a well-established risk factor for adult intimate partner violence (IPV) victimisation and traumatic brain injuries (TBI), but their relationship with IPV-related brain injury remains unclear. This retrospective cross-sectional study examined the associations between ACEs and subtypes (physical/sexual abuse, emotional abuse/neglect, family adversities, and witnessing domestic violence) on IPV-related head and neck injuries (mild TBI, head impacts, and non-fatal strangulation; NFS), as well as brain injury symptom burden among 170 community-dwelling women (aged 18–75 years). Participants completed the ACE questionnaire, Composite Abuse Scale, Brain Injury Screening Questionnaire (IPV module), and the Rivermead Post-concussion Questionnaire. Family adversities (59%) and emotional abuse/ neglect (54%) were the most prevalent ACE subtypes. Over 40% reported an IPV-related head impact, 27% reported IPV-related mild TBI, and 28% reported NFS experiences. Higher ACE scores increased the odds of IPV-related mild TBI, head impacts, NFS, and NFS-related brain injury (ORs 1.22–1.32). Associations between ACEs and symptom severity were no longer significant after controlling for PTSD, depression, and IPV recency, with a substantial amount of the variance accounted for by co-occurring PTSD. These findings highlight ACEs as an important upstream risk factor for IPV injury, which is critical for prevention, early identification, and policy.

Article.Title: Postural stability and shooting performance in adult and junior elite Brazilian recurve archers
Article.Authors: Ely M.; Schons P.; Clemente F.; de Barros Rodenbusch C.; Trybulski R.; Kawczyński A.; de Oliveira H.; Preissler A.
Article.Abstract: Postural stability is considered a crucial factor for performance in Olympic recurve archery. However, the extent to which it distinguishes athletes from different competitive categories remains unclear. This study aimed to compare postural stability and shooting performance between adult and junior athletes from the Brazilian national archery teams. A cross-sectional, comparative study was conducted with 20 elite athletes: 13 adults (28.00 ± 5.97 years) and 7 juniors (17.43 ± 0.79 years). Participants performed 18 shots at the official competition distance of 70 m while standing on a force platform (Vald Performance, 500 Hz). Center of pressure (COP) displacement variables in the lateral and anteroposterior directions were analyzed for dominant and non-dominant legs. Shot scores were recorded to assess performance. Data normality and homogeneity of variances were assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk and Levene tests, respectively. Independent t-tests were used for normally distributed variables, whereas Mann-Whitney U tests were applied to non-normally distributed variables (age and years of practice). Complementary ANCOVA models adjusted for body mass and years of practice were also performed. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in any stabilometric variable ( p > 0.05). However, adult athletes achieved significantly higher unadjusted average scores (8.67 ± 0.34) than junior athletes (7.85 ± 0.91; p = 0.009; Cohen’s d = 1.382). Age, body mass, and years of practice also differed significantly between groups ( p < 0.05). After adjustment, no significant group effect was observed for stabilometric variables, and the group effect for shooting score was attenuated (adjusted difference = 0.79, 95% CI − 0.01 to 1.58; p = 0.052; ηp² = 0.217). Although no statistically significant differences in postural stability were detected between groups, adult athletes achieved higher unadjusted shooting scores, with this group effect attenuated after adjustment for body mass and years of practice. Therefore, the stabilometric results should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between groups. These findings suggest that, within this elite Brazilian sample, shooting performance differed between groups in the unadjusted analysis, whereas the stabilometric variables did not show statistically significant differences, including after adjustment.

Article.Title: Efficacy and safety of a cetuximab biosimilar compared with Erbitux in patients with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Rezvani H.; Rezvani A.; Allahyari A.; Ghadiany M.; Esfahani A.; Mortazavizadeh S.; Mehrzad V.; Khodakarim N.; Gorji M.; Sharifi M.; Mohammad Doost H.; Hosseinzadeh M.; Bari A.; Nejati B.; Sadeghi A.; Chavoshi S.; Nekouee A.; Razavi M.; Hajigholami A.; Kalantari B.; Khosravi A.; Darakhshandeh A.; Ataei Azimi S.; Abrishami A.; Tavakkoli Shiraji S.
Article.Abstract: Cetuximab, an epidermal growth factor receptor monoclonal antibody, is a key therapy for RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), commonly used with folinic acid, 5-fluorouracil, and irinotecan (FOLFIRI). In Iran, the rising burden of mCRC and the high cost of imported cetuximab underscore the urgent need for a cost-effective, locally manufactured biosimilar to improve treatment accessibility and sustainability within the healthcare system. The objective of this study is to compare the efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of cetuximab (manufactured by CinnaGen Co.) versus reference cetuximab (Erbitux; manufactured by Merck) in patients with RAS wild-type mCRC. This phase III, double-blind, randomized, multi-center, active-controlled trial enrolled adult patients (n = 211) with RAS wild-type mCRC. Participants were allocated 2:1 to cetuximab (CinnaGen) plus FOLFIRI (n = 141) or Erbitux plus FOLFIRI (n = 70) for up to 48 weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), time to treatment failure (TTF), objective response rate (ORR), safety, and immunogenicity. The results show that cetuximab (CinnaGen) was comparable to Erbitux for PFS in both PP (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.95; 90% confidence interval [CI]: 0.62–1.45) and ITT (HR = 0.82; 90% CI: 0.55–1.24) analyses, with upper CIs below the non-inferiority margin (1.51). No significant differences were observed in OS (HR = 0.85; 95% CI: 0.45–1.58), TTF (HR = 1.07; 95% CI: 0.77–1.48), or ORR (43.3% vs 45.7%; P-value = 0.77). The majority of patients experienced adverse events, with anemia, neutropenia, and hypomagnesemia being among the most frequently reported. The frequency of serious adverse events was considered clinically acceptable, and immunogenicity analyses revealed no detectable anti-cetuximab antibodies in either treatment group. In conclusion, this study demonstrated that cetuximab (CinnaGen) is non-inferior to Erbitux (Merck) in terms of PFS, with comparable efficacy across other endpoints. The safety profiles of both products were acceptable and consistent with known data for cetuximab-based regimens in mCRC.

Article.Title: Surface ground-motion characteristics and path-corrected PGV prediction for mining-induced seismicity: a case study
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Zhang Q.; Zou J.; Jiao Y.; Ouyang L.; Jiang Y.
Article.Abstract: Strong mining-induced earthquakes in deep mines threaten surface infrastructure, yet their surface vibration fields are difficult to predict because propagation paths cross goafs, fractured overburden, and variable Quaternary cover. This study used a dense surface monitoring array at the Dongtan Coal Mine to characterize the time–frequency evolution and spatial attenuation of typical mining-induced seismic events. Goaf-path length and Quaternary cover thickness were incorporated into a conventional distance-attenuation relationship to build an improved peak ground velocity (PGV) prediction model. The results show that surface waveforms change from short, high-amplitude near-field pulses to multi-peaked coda wave trains in the mid-to-far field. This evolution is marked by envelope broadening, delayed peak arrival, spectral migration to lower frequencies, narrowed bandwidth, and increased spectral decay. Propagation through fractured goaf zones and thick shallow cover accelerates high-frequency attenuation and produces strong azimuthal differences in PGV. Compared with the distance-only model, the path-corrected model improved the coefficient of determination from 0.79 to 0.87 and reduced RMSE and MAPE from 0.38 cm/s and 24.0% to 0.09 cm/s and 21%, respectively. The model is empirical, but it illustrates how path and site effects shape mining-induced surface vibration. The representative M L 1.9 event remained below safety-control thresholds for major surface structures. The proposed framework supports rapid post-event assessment and refined risk zoning in deep mining areas.

Article.Title: Zonal instability identification and full-sequence hierarchical control strategies for surrounding rock in composite-roof coal roadway
Article.Authors: Yang S.; Yang L.; Chen D.; Yin J.; Zhao L.
Article.Abstract: Composite roof coal roadways suffer from developed bedding planes, low cementation strength and delayed staged surrounding rock instability, and conventional one-step support methods poorly adapt to these complex geological conditions. Taking the 1211(1) transportation roadway of Guqiao Coal Mine as the engineering background, this study adopts full-section real-time bolt stress monitoring to explore the temporal and spatial distribution of support stress, identify critical instability zones, and develop a graded, phased differentiated surrounding rock control system with optimized excavation and construction schemes. The results reveal that bolt axial force experiences three evolutionary stages: rapid growth, decelerated growth and stable fluctuation. Surrounding rock stress and support bearing capacity show distinct spatial heterogeneity, with the bearing capacity ordered as central roof > upper rib > lateral roof > lower rib. The central roof and upper rib are high-risk instability zones with severe stress concentration and sensitive bolt stress response, while other zones maintain sufficient support redundancy and good rock stability. Based on the staged deformation and stress redistribution mechanism of surrounding rock, a full-cycle closed-loop control system integrating advance pre-control, early intensive support, transitional stabilization and late cable reinforcement is established. A zonal differentiated support strategy is formulated, implementing intensive reinforcement in key hazardous zones and conventional support in stable areas. Combined with delayed cable support technology, a three-dimensional coupled stress field of shallow bolts and deep cables is constructed, which effectively remedies the defects of traditional support, such as uncoordinated stress adaptation, insufficient deep support and late structural failure. Three phased support modes with matched temporal and spatial parameters are determined, and construction processes are optimized for efficient parallel operation. Field applications verify that the optimized scheme ensures reliable stability and safety of composite roof roadways. After implementation, the daily excavation circulation increases from 6 to 15 ~ 18 cycles, and the daily advance footage rises from 6.0 m to 15 ~ 18 m, significantly improving excavation safety and construction efficiency.

Article.Title: G2T: Gate guided transformer for medical image segmentation
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Shokouhmand S.; Rahman S.; Bhatt S.; Mirbozorgi S.; Faezipour M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inspired by the human cognitive process and memory capabilities, we present a novel vision transformer (ViT) in this paper, called G ate G uided T ransformer (G2T) for medical image segmentation. G2T addresses a key limitation of cascaded decoder blocks in vision transformers; that is their difficulty in retaining and propagating important information from earlier stages, which often leads to suboptimal feature decoding in later blocks. Our proposed G2T has (i) a novel feature-aware decoder (FAD) consisting of three convolutional gates named Refine, Expand, and Produce (REP), which deal with forgetting irrelevant features, remembering relevant features, and generating the output features, respectively; (ii) a novel attention mixing module called LH-RAAM (Low to High-Resolution Attention Accumulation Module) that accumulates attentions computed in the encoder blocks from low-level features to high-level features, and aggregates them with the attentions computed in the decoder blocks to emphasize similar features during both the encoding and decoding stages. Evaluated on six medical imaging datasets, G2T consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art models by 1-3%, achieving a 94.67% mean Dice score ±0.01 standard deviation on the ACDC dataset and 92.90% ±0.02 on the Synapse dataset. Ablation studies additionally justify the utility of each component of G2T along with strong generalizability outside the medical domain.

Article.Title: Multidimensional spatiotemporal differentiation and driving mechanisms of soil erosion in a mountainous small watershed: an ST-TransUNet-R framework
Article.Authors: Miao H.; Zhang H.; Deng Z.; Hao N.; Zhu W.; Zou J.
Article.Abstract: Soil erosion threatens ecological security and water conservation in mountainous small watersheds. To improve pixel-level assessment under complex terrain and incomplete multi-source raster inputs, we developed ST-TransUNet-R, a deep-learning framework that integrates a ResNet-50 encoder, a Transformer module, a joint-validity mask, and masked mean squared error loss. The framework was applied to the Xikouwai Small Watershed upstream of the Miyun Reservoir for five assessment years between 2005 and 2020 and achieved R² = 0.87, RMSE = 2.08, MAE = 1.15, and PBIAS = − 3.13%. Multidimensional analysis showed that the 600–900 m elevation band contained 48.0% of the eroded area, whereas zones above 1100 m produced disproportionately high soil loss per unit area. Slopes > 35°, vegetation cover < 30%, unused land, and skeletal soils were consistently erosion-sensitive. SHAP analysis identified slope as the dominant predictor, followed by slope length and vegetation cover, indicating that terrain-controlled runoff concentration and surface protection jointly shaped spatial erosion heterogeneity. These findings provide a high-resolution basis for prioritizing erosion-control measures in mountainous water-source protection areas.

Article.Title: Longitudinal single-cell RNA-seq profiling of lung cell phenotypes, signaling, and cross-talk during fibrosis resolution
Article.Authors: Speth J.; Wong V.; Guzman S.; Walker N.; Liu Y.; Zemans R.; Blackwell T.; Aguilar C.; Peters-Golden M.; Fortier S.
Article.Abstract: Resolution of fibrosis following lung injury is distinguished from persistent/progressive parenchymal scarring through the timely clearance of aberrant cell types, removal of excess collagens, and regeneration of alveolar structure. The requisite signaling pathways, cellular cross-talk, and phenotypic shifts associated with, and required for, resolution of established lung fibrosis have not been well characterized. To address this critical knowledge gap, we performed longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing of whole mouse lung digests obtained during spontaneously resolving fibrosis. We observed a fibrosis-associated macrophage and an ECM-secreting Csmd1+ fibroblast population emerging during peak fibrosis and undergoing partial clearance during resolution. Our study also revealed conspicuous shifts in well-established pathways associated with tissue repair and fibrosis among immune, mesenchymal, and epithelial cells during spontaneous resolution. In addition to a decline in pro-fibrotic driver pathways, the putative anti-fibrotic pathways cAMP, HGF/MET, and TWEAK were enriched in several cell types during spontaneous resolution. CellChat analysis was used to predict the cellular senders and recipients of each pathway and characterize their longitudinal changes. Our characterization of the cellular and molecular dynamics in whole lungs during spontaneous fibrosis resolution provides a foundation for the identification of endogenous pathways that might be leveraged to treat pulmonary fibrosis.

Article.Title: Comparative phyto-biochemical profiling, antibacterial efficacy, and culturable rhizosphere bacterial dynamics of turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) variants from eastern India
Article.Authors: Mohapatra A.; Sahoo J.; Mohanty A.; Samal P.; Sahoo L.; Mahapatra S.; Hossain S.; Hossain S.
Article.Abstract: Different turmeric variants possess distinct medicinal and ecological attributes, yet a comprehensive comparative analysis of their phyto-biochemical profiles and associated culturable rhizobacterial profiles is lacking. To resolve this, the current study evaluated yellow, black, and white turmeric variants, revealing distinct phyto-biochemical constituent profiles characterized by peak phenolics in white turmeric (121.63 mg GAE/g), maximum flavonoids (49.85 mg QE/g) and proteins (9.65%) in black turmeric, and primary carbohydrate (63.52%) and carotenoid (35.44 µg/g) reserves in yellow turmeric. Multivariate analysis established marked negative correlations between protein and carotenoid content ( r = − 0.991), and total phenolics and carbohydrates ( r = − 0.970), with a two-component PCA model accounting for 100% total variance (PC1 = 59.42%, PC2 = 40.58%). Antibacterial evaluation against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli demonstrated the highest inhibitory activity in the ethanolic extract of yellow turmeric compared to the other tested variants; however, this activity remained significantly lower than that of ampicillin. In contrast, white turmeric extracts exhibited no antibacterial activity. Phylogenetic model selection based on the lowest Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) designated the Jukes–Cantor model with invariant sites (JC + I; BIC = 5,279.42) as the best fit for Bacillus sp. AKU 5 (putative Bacillus thuringiensis affinity), whereas the Tamura 3-parameter model (T92; BIC = 9,815.55) was optimal for Bacillus sp. AM 1 (putative B. cereus affinity). Maximum likelihood analyses revealed contrasting evolutionary patterns, with B. thuringiensis exhibiting a highly constrained substitution rate (α = 0.04; Log Likelihood = − 2006.341) and pronounced C→A substitution bias, whereas B. cereus showed a more uniform rate distribution (α = 30.23; Log Likelihood = − 4234.930) characterized by symmetric A↔G and T↔C transition biases, emphasizing preliminary nucleotide substitution variations within the turmeric rhizosphere. In-silico thermodynamic profiling of 16S rRNA amplicon secondary structures revealed distinct computational folding stabilities between B. thuringiensis AKU 5 (minimum free energy (MFE) = − 511.90 kcal/mol) and B. cereus AM 1 (MFE = − 506.50 kcal/mol). These baseline structural disparities reflect inherent differences in sequence length and GC-rich base-pairing density rather than in vivo physiological adaptations within the turmeric rhizosphere. Collectively, these findings establish an in-silico sequence modeling rather than verified genome-wide host-driven evolution, providing insights into preliminary turmeric chemotype-culturable rhizobacterial associations. Future research should focus on high-throughput metagenomic profiling to unravel whole-community dynamics, isolation of specific bioactive compounds, and exploiting target rhizosphere strains for agricultural biofertilizer or therapeutic formulations.

Article.Title: Perivascular injection of a pH-responsive and protease-degradable hydrogel with rapamycin-loaded liposomes inhibits neointimal hyperplasia after carotid wire injury in mice
Article.Authors: Wu M.; Zhang L.; Li X.; Li R.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Neointimal hyperplasia is a major cause of restenosis and graft failure after vascular interventions. Perivascular drug delivery offers a potential solution, but achieving sustained and condition-dependent release at injured sites remains challenging. Here, we developed an injectable hydrogel with pH-sensitive and protease-susceptible characteristics (OHA-CS/GelMA) encapsulating rapamycin-loaded liposomes (Rapa-Lipo@Gel). The Schiff-base network enabled pH-triggered degradation, while GelMA provided mechanical stability and intrinsic susceptibility to protease-mediated degradation. The hydrogel degraded faster and released more rapamycin at pH 6.5 than at pH 7.4 in vitro, with further enhancement by protease. Liposomes suppressed burst release. In PDGF-BB-stimulated VSMCs, Rapa-Lipo@Gel inhibited proliferation, migration, and phenotypic switching (α-SMA↑, OPN↓). In a mouse carotid wire injury model, perivascular application of Rapa-Lipo@Gel at day 14 significantly reduced neointimal area and intima-to-media ratio compared to controls. Mechanistically, treatment reduced Ki67⁺ proliferating cells, decreased CD68⁺ macrophage infiltration, reduced overall α-SMA burden, increased MYH11 expression in the neointima, and did not reduce CD31⁺ endothelial coverage. Collectively, this pH-responsive and protease-susceptible hydrogel with liposomal rapamycin provides a promising platform with preliminary safety evidence for local treatment of neointimal hyperplasia, with potential for preventing restenosis.

Article.Title: Force-based design of a novel self-centring concentrically braced steel frame validated by nonlinear time-history analysis
Article.Authors: Alwahsh H.; Salawdeh S.; Jiang Y.; Goggins J.
Article.Abstract: Self-centring concentrically braced frames (SC-CBFs) are intended to limit residual deformation after strong earthquakes, but practical code-oriented procedures for their design remain limited. This study presents a force-based design (FBD) procedure for a horizontally post-tensioned SC-CBF consistent with Eurocode 8 and Eurocode 3. The procedure defines the seismic base shear, brace sizing, allocation of shear resistance between the concentrically braced frame and post-tensioning system, and capacity checks for beams, columns, braces, and strands. A regular four-storey archetype was designed using q = 4 as a case-study assumption and evaluated using nonlinear time-history analyses in OpenSees under 12 spectrum-matched earthquake records. The first-mode period obtained numerically (0.356 s) was close to the Eurocode estimate (0.34 s). Record-specific peak responses and the suite mean were examined; mean peak floor displacements and inter-storey drifts remained within the FBD design profiles, residual drifts were substantially below the adopted tolerance, and post-tensioning forces remained below the specified design capacity. Within the scope of this single archetype, these findings support the proposed FBD procedure as a practical basis for preliminary design of the investigated SC-CBF configuration. The adopted q value and the final 60:40 CBF-to-PT shear allocation are case-study-specific and require further evaluation across other structural and seismic conditions.

Article.Title: Associations of empathy, occupational commitment, and ego-resilience with perceived stress among nurses in non-family-accompanied care wards
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Liu F.; Jiang S.; Cai L.; Ding M.; Lin X.; Gao S.
Article.Abstract: To examine the association between empathy and perceived stress among nurses in non-family-accompanied care wards and to explore the potential mediating roles of occupational commitment and ego-resilience. A convenient sampling method was employed to recruit 359 nurses from non-family-accompanied care wards in eight tertiary Grade A hospitals in Fujian Province from March to June 2025. The perceived stress, empathy, occupational commitment, and ego-resilience were assessed using the Chinese versions of the Jefferson Scale of Empathy-Health Professionals (JSE-HP), the Chinese Perceived Stress Scale (CPSS), the Measurement of Occupational Commitment (MOC), and the Ego-Resilience Scale (ERS), respectively. Chain mediation analysis was conducted to examine the potential indirect associations among these variables. Nurses in non-family-accompanied care wards reported a moderate level of perceived stress (35.38 ± 8.42), with significant differences observed across clinical departments ( P < 0.05). Empathy was negatively associated with perceived stress ( r = − 0.303, P < 0.01) and positively associated with occupational commitment ( r = 0.288, P < 0.01) and ego-resilience ( r = 0.233, P < 0.01). Occupational commitment was positively associated with ego-resilience ( r = 0.341, P < 0.01), and both variables were negatively associated with perceived stress ( P < 0.01). Mediation analysis identified three significant indirect associations: (1) an indirect association through occupational commitment (effect = − 0.0339, 95% CI [− 0.0560, − 0.0134]); (2) an indirect association through ego-resilience (effect = − 0.0429, 95% CI [− 0.0733, − 0.0147]); and (3) a sequential indirect association through occupational commitment and ego-resilience (effect = − 0.0463, 95% CI [− 0.0678, − 0.0291]). A significant direct association between empathy and perceived stress remained after accounting for the mediators (B = − 0.1106, P < 0.001). Perceived stress among nurses working in non-family-accompanied care wards varied across clinical departments. Empathy was negatively associated with perceived stress and was associated with perceived stress both directly and indirectly within the hypothesized serial mediation model through the sequential mediating pathway involving occupational commitment and ego-resilience. Nursing managers should recognize the potential value of fostering empathy, occupational commitment, and ego-resilience to support nurses’ role adjustment and adaptation to the non-family-accompanied care model. These findings may provide insights for developing targeted strategies to support nurses’ psychological well-being and stress management.

Article.Title: Multimodal deep learning with particle swarm guided feature refinement for automated pain detection
Article.Authors: Gasmi K.; Almaghrabi S.; Alzahrani I.; Mahmoud A.; Eltoum A.; Alenzi A.; Shahin O.; Taloba A.; Hamed Abdel Hameed F.
Article.Abstract: Pain assessment remains a significant challenge in clinical practice because conventional self-reporting methods are subjective and unreliable for non-verbal, cognitively impaired, and critically ill patients. Existing automated pain detection approaches primarily rely on single-modality data or limited multimodal integration, resulting in inadequate feature representation, feature redundancy, and reduced classification performance. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates physiological signals, facial images, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and clinical text for objective pain detection. The physiological branch employs a hybrid architecture comprising a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and Deep Neural Network (DNN) to learn hierarchical spatial-temporal representations. The facial branch combines EfficientNet and Residual Network (ResNet) to extract discriminative facial features, while a CNN-based architecture processes MRI images. Clinical narratives are encoded using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and BioBERT to capture contextual semantic information. An Adaptive Feature Refinement Layer (AFRL) enhances modality-specific feature learning, followed by Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) for feature selection and a novel PSO-Guided Feature Refinement Layer (PFRL) for adaptive feature weighting prior to multimodal fusion. We implement the framework in TensorFlow and PyTorch and evaluate it on the BioVid, UNBC-McMaster, and Trigeminal Neuralgia MRI datasets. Experimental results achieve 96.2% accuracy, outperforming Support Vector Machine (82.4%), K-Nearest Neighbors (79.6%), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (88.9%), and AdaBoost (90.7%). The proposed framework provides a robust, scalable, and clinically applicable solution for automated multimodal pain detection and improved clinical decision support.

Article.Title: Untargeted metabolomics identifies novel metabolites and pathways in Finnish men with heart failure
Article.Authors: Fernandes Silva L.; Vangipurapu J.; Oravilahti A.; Laakso M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early predictors of heart failure (HF) remain poorly defined. We measured plasma metabolites in a population-based Finnish cohort to identify metabolites that independently predict incident HF. We also performed an exploratory analysis of whether selected metabolites improved discrimination beyond traditional clinical and laboratory factors. Untargeted LC–MS/MS quantified 1009 known metabolites in 10,115 men from the METSIM study. A total of 663 participants developed HF during 14.2-year follow-up. We applied Cox regression analysis to associate the clinical factors and metabolites alone and combined with the risk of HF. Genetic variants that were associated with metabolites and increased the risk of HF were identified. Forty-five metabolites (33 were novel) increased significantly the risk of HF, including markers of catecholamine turnover, polyamine catabolites, very-long-chain acyl-carnitines, and bile-acid sulfates. ROC analysis showed that adding 12 metabolites to the clinical model increased significantly the AUC from 0.775 to 0.795. The metabolites identified converged to the adrenergic/mitochondrial redox stress, nitrogen-polyamine flux, and membrane-lipid/bile-acid remodeling pathways. Ten metabolite-quantitative-trait loci included signaling, nitrogen handling, lipid remodeling, and nucleotide detoxification pathways to specific genes. We also showed that these metabolites add prognostic value to conventional risk factors and highlight pathways of early myocardial injury in patients with HF.

Article.Title: Cobalt oxide nanoparticles disrupt cellular homeostasis through oxidative genomic instability and mitochondrial stress, driving necrosis in non-small lung cancer cells
Article.Authors: Mohamed H.; Elnawasani S.; Mohamed B.; Hakeem G.; Nagy M.; Essam R.; Diab A.; Safwat G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains one of the most aggressive and treatment-resistant malignancies worldwide, with current therapies often limited by poor tumor specificity, resistance, and systemic toxicity. Nanoparticle-based therapeutics offer a promising strategy to overcome these challenges. Cobalt oxide nanoparticles (Co 3 O 4 NPs), owing to their distinctive redox properties and capacity to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), have emerged as potential anticancer agents; however, their intrinsic effects against NSCLC cells and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study therefore investigates the novel cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects of pristine Co 3 O 4 NPs in non-small A549 lung cancer cells using an integrated mechanistic approach. Cell viability was measured with the sulforhodamine B (SRB) assay, while genomic DNA damage, ROS generation, mitochondrial membrane potential, and apoptosis induction were evaluated using alkaline comet assay, 2′,7′-dichlorofluorescein diacetate, rhodamine-123 dye, and flow cytometry, respectively. Mechanistic insights were further supported by quantitative real-time PCR analysis of apoptosis- and mitochondria-related genes ( p53 , ND3 , and Bcl-2 ). A 72-hour exposure to Co 3 O 4 NPs various concentrations significantly reduced A549 cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner with a markedly low IC50 value of 34.17 µg/ml. Moreover, treating A549 cells with the IC50 concentration (34.17 µg/ml) of Co 3 O 4 NPs caused excessive ROS production, severe genomic DNA damage, and dramatic mitochondrial depolarization. Gene expression analysis revealed remarkable upregulation of pro-apoptotic p53 and mitochondrial ND3 gene expression, alongside significant downregulation of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 gene expression. Despite p53 activation the pronounced mitochondrial dysfunction and bioenergetic collapse favored necrotic cell death over classical apoptosis. Flow cytometric analysis confirmed this shift, showing a substantial increase in necrotic A549 cells alongside a marked reduction in apoptotic A549 populations following Co 3 O 4 NPs exposure. These findings collectively provide integrated evidence that pristine Co₃O₄NPs induce oxidative stress, genomic DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cell death in A549 NSCLC cells. The predominance of necrotic cell death under the conditions examined suggests that severe oxidative and mitochondrial stress contributes to the observed cytotoxic response. Further studies using NSCLC models with different p53 statuses, appropriate normal-control cells, and in vivo systems are required to establish the selectivity, reproducibility, and broader biological relevance of these effects.

Article.Title: Genotyping by Sequencing (GBS) uncovers genetic diversity and population structure for salicornia breeding programs in Iran
Article.Authors: Loni F.; Sima N.; Ghaffari M.; Farsi M.; Zeinalabedini M.
Article.Abstract: Salicornia, a succulent halophyte flourishing in coastal and mangrove ecosystems, holds significant economic and ecological promise. Establishing sustainable cultivation systems requires a profound understanding of its geographical distribution, genetic potential, and the identification of agronomically superior populations. Despite this potential, comprehensive genomic investigations into the genus remain scarce. This study utilized genome-wide markers to elucidate the genetic diversity and population structure of Iranian Salicornia germplasm, a region recognized as a center of origin for several species. Sampling comprised 200 individuals from 26 geographically defined populations spanning 13 provinces. High-throughput genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) generated an average of 9.8 million raw reads per sample. From an initial pool of 253,630 raw single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), 84,215 high-confidence markers were retained following stringent quality control. Across the 26 population-level diversity summaries, mean observed heterozygosity was 0.081 (range = 0.0076–0.3734), with the highest values in Tashk, Shahr Babak, and Noq. Pairwise FST values ranged from 0.05 to 0.66 (mean = 0.241), indicating moderate to high differentiation. K-means clustering identified four primary genetic cohorts, while DAPC and co-ancestry analyses indicated substantial shared genetic background among parts of the germplasm. Formal migration analyses further resolved the temporal pattern of connectivity. Historical migration was the strongest between the Azerbaijan and Central-North units (M = 1.670 from Azerbaijan to Central-North; M = 1.528 in the reverse direction), whereas the weakest historical exchange occurred between Gwadar and Chabahar (M = 0.174–0.188). Contemporary migration was substantially lower than historical connectivity, with self-assignment ranging from 0.810 to 0.960 and the highest values in Chabahar (0.950) and Gwadar (0.960). Spatial analysis and ecological niche modeling further delineated current habitats and projected suitable regions for future expansion. Together, these population-genomic, migration, and spatial results provide a framework for conservation prioritization, germplasm management, and Salicornia breeding in saline and marginal environments of Iran.

Article.Title: Effects of biochar and vermicompost application on the physicochemical properties of acidic soils in Sidama Region, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Dogiso E.; Lemma B.; Yoseph T.; Haile W.
Article.Abstract: Soil acidity is a major constraint on crop productivity in tropical agriculture, particularly in regions like Ethiopia, where smallholder farmers often lack access to conventional amendments such as lime. While biochar (BC) and vermicompost (VC) have been studied individually, their combined potential for remediating acidic soils under local conditions remains insufficiently explored. This incubation study evaluated the effects of BC (0, 3, and 6 t ha -1 ) and VC (0, 2.5, and 5 t ha -1 ) application on the physicochemical properties of acidic soils from the Hula and Gorche districts in Sidama, Ethiopia. The treatments followed a completely randomized design (CRD) with three replications. Statistical analyses were performed using SAS 9.4. The findings indicated that the amendments significantly (p < 0.05) enhanced key soil indicators. The combined application of 6 t ha -1 BC and 5 t ha -1 VC increased soil pH by 18.4% (from 4.9 to 5.8) in Hula soil. While 3 t ha -1 BC and 5 t ha -1 VC in combination increased pH by 15.7% (from 5.1 to 5.9) in Gorche soil. Both individual and combined treatments improved soil organic carbon (OC), total nitrogen (TN), available phosphorus (AP), exchangeable bases (Ex. bases), cation exchange capacity (CEC), and percent base saturation (PBS), while reducing exchangeable acidity (EA) and extractable micronutrients. These results demonstrate that BC and VC can be effectively integrated to ameliorate soil acidity and enhance fertility, offering a sustainable alternative and a potentially useful amendment strategy for acidic soils. While these findings are encouraging, further field studies are recommended to assess their long-term effects on soil properties, crop agronomic performances and economic viability under real farming conditions.

Article.Title: Multifunctional gelatin/PVA hydrogels chemically crosslinked with grape pomace extract for controlled transdermal delivery of polyphenolic compounds
Article.Authors: Bialik-Wąs K.; Drozdowska-Sapuła P.; Miastkowska M.; Malarz K.; Mrozek-Wilczkiewicz A.; Barczewski M.; Aniśko-Michalak J.; Magot F.; Lanoue A.; Giglioli-Guivarc’h N.; Nowak A.; Ossowicz-Rupniewska P.; Muzykiewicz-Szymańska A.; Roman B.; Kucharski Ł.; Malinowska M.
Article.Abstract: Multifunctional and environmentally friendly hydrogel materials were developed through the reaction of chemically crosslinking biocompatible polymers and natural crosslinkers present in grape pomace, a waste product left over during the wine making process. This interesting approach to designing hydrogels, especially considering that many synthetic crosslinking agents, such as N, N’-methylenebisacrylamide, epichlorohydrin, and glutaraldehyde, all of which are harmful and toxic. It turns out that not only fresh grape berries but also grape pomace constitute a source of many beneficial active substances including anthocyanins, flavanols, flavonols, stilbenes, and phenolic acids. The application of grape pomace extract to obtain hydrogels not only enables chemical crosslinking of polymers, but also provides therapeutic properties to the final matrix. The obtained hydrogels were characterized using Scanning Electron Microscopy and Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy analysis as well as physicochemical (gel fraction, swelling ability, degradation) and thermal properties. Results confirm clearly that only some of the compounds from the grape pomace extract (malvidin-3-O-glucoside; catechin; epicatechin; citric acid; L-phenylalanine; procyanidins B1 and B2) participate in the polymer cross-linking reaction. The remaining active substances (mainly L-phenylalanine, malvidin-3,5-O-diglucoside, and catechin) are released in a controlled manner and penetrate the skin, which indicates the high therapeutic potential of the obtained hydrogels.

Article.Title: Myocardial extracellular volume reduction is associated with improved cardiac function after SGLT2 inhibitor therapy in HFpEF
Article.Authors: Marathonitis A.; Anastasiou A.; Vythoulkas-Biotis N.; Lama N.; Theofilis P.; Marinos G.; Margoni A.; Tsatsaragkou A.; Zisimos K.; Lysandrou A.; Oikonomou E.; Siasos G.; Tousoulis D.
Article.Abstract: In patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve prognosis and symptoms. To evaluate the short-term effects of SGLT2i on myocardial extracellular volume (ECV) and left ventricular (LV) function in patients with HFpEF and diabetes mellitus (DM). Patients with HFpEF and DM (32 subjects) received either SGLT2i (treatment group) or not (control group) in addition to standard care. Assessments were conducted at baseline and after six months. LV ejection fraction (LVEF) and global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) were measured to assess systolic function, left atrial strain (LAstrain) was used to evaluate diastolic function. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) was performed to measure ECV. C-reactive protein (CRP) and N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NTproBNP) levels were also measured. The mean age of the participants was 67 ± 9 years (62% male). No significant differences were observed between groups at baseline. In comparison to the control group, the SGLT2i group demonstrated improved LVGLS (SGLT2i: from − 16.4 (1.7)% to − 17.2 (2.5)%, p = 0.01 vs. Control group: from − 17.2 (1.8)% to − 16.9 (2.2)%, p = 0.13), LAstrain (SGLT2i: 14.0 (2.0)% to 15.5 (2.0)%, p = < 0.001 vs. Control group: 13.0 (1.8)% to 13.6 (1.8)%, p = 0.02), ECV (SGLT2i: 28.3 (1.9) % to 27.3 (1.8) %, p < 0.001; Control: 26.9 (2.4) % to 27.1 (2.3) %, p = 0.16) along with reductions in CRP and NT-proBNP. In patients with HFpEF and DM, SGLT2i treatment improves ECV along with systolic and diastolic echocardiographic parameters. These findings highlight the underlying mechanisms contributing to the cardioprotective effects of SGLT2i in this patient population.

Article.Title: OECD-compliant QSAR modeling and molecular simulations prioritize plant-derived potential COX-2 inhibitors with experimentally observed anti-inflammatory activity through NO inhibition
Article.Authors: Laskar Y.; Mazumder P.; Kumar N.
Article.Abstract: Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) is a key mediator of inflammation and a significant therapeutic target for numerous inflammatory disorders. We aimed to prioritize phytochemicals with potential COX-2 inhibitory activity using an integrated computational-experimental approach. Several OECD-compliant 2D- and 3D-QSAR models based on an assay-homogenized dataset of 50 known COX-2 inhibitors were developed and applied to screen 54 phytocompounds. The prioritized compounds were subsequently evaluated through computational ADMET, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD), and cellular assays. The QSAR models returned internal cross-validated Q 2 values of 0.63–0.70, with external predictivity assessed on small test and validation sets and interpreted as provisional. Applicability-domain analysis was extended to every screened compound, and predictions falling outside the modeled chemical space were identified as extrapolative. ADMET and predicted-toxicity screening narrowed the prioritized compounds to apigenin-7-sulfate and genistein, both within the AD. Molecular docking indicated favorable interactions within the COX-2 active site, and 50 ns molecular dynamics simulations showed both ligands remaining bound over the period sampled. Because apigenin-7-sulfate was commercially unavailable, its non-sulfated parent apigenin was evaluated in its place; apigenin and genistein inhibited nitric oxide production in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages in a concentration-dependent manner while maintaining > 90% cell viability. This endpoint reports suppression of the macrophage inflammatory response and does not establish COX-2 inhibition, which in this study remains a computational prediction. Collectively, the findings highlight apigenin-derived compounds and genistein as potential natural anti-inflammatory leads with likely involvement of multiple molecular pathways, including COX-2 modulation and NO inhibition. This also demonstrates the utility of integrating QSAR modeling, molecular simulations, ADMET profiling, and cellular validation for natural-product-based drug discovery.

Article.Title: The correlation between malondialdehyde (MDA) and cortisol levels with bone mineral density (BMD) in women diagnosed with osteoporosis and osteopenia
Article.Authors: Mohammadi S.; Mohammadi A.; Lotfi M.; Kamyari N.; Moghaddam F.; Radmanesh E.
Article.Abstract: Stress induces physiological and behavioral changes that can impair bone health and lead to bone loss, making chronic stress a risk factor for osteoporosis. Despite growing research on the effects of oxidative stress and cortisol on bone health, the relationship among MDA, cortisol, and BMD in patients with osteoporosis and osteopenia remains unclear. Investigating the combined effects of MDA and cortisol on BMD is essential for understanding the mechanisms of bone loss and identifying novel therapeutic targets in these patients. This study is a cross-sectional analytical investigation involving 49 women (mean age 59.53 ± 10.60; osteoporosis ( N = 12), osteopenia ( N = 20), and normal BMD ( N = 17)) who were referred to the Bone Densitometry Department at the Abadan Nuclear Medicine Center in 2024. The study included women seeking bone density assessments, with no restrictions on age, medical conditions, or medications. However, women with hypoadrenal or hyperadrenal disorders were excluded. All provided informed consent, while those hesitant to participate were excluded. Classification was based on T-scores: above − 1 for healthy bone density, between − 1 and − 2.5 for osteopenia, and below − 2.5 for osteoporosis. Bone indices, including BMD, Z-score, and T-score for the femur and lumbar vertebrae (L1-L4), were assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). MDA and cortisol levels were measured using specialized kits and an ELISA reader. Data collected from patients were entered into IBM SPSS Statistics (version 16) for analysis. All statistical analyses were performed with a significance level of α = 0.05. The osteoporosis group had the highest mean age, at 69.25 ± 6.43 years, which was significantly higher ( P < 0.001). They also had the lowest mean BMD, T-score, and Z-score, with significant differences among all groups ( P < 0.001). The mean MDA level in the osteoporosis group was higher than in the other groups, but not significantly so. Similarly, cortisol levels were elevated in the osteopenia (333.84 ± 31.42) and osteoporosis (318.01 ± 58.13) groups compared to the normal BMD group, but the differences were not significant. A significant positive correlation was found between BMD, Z-score, and T-score ( P < 0.001). A significant negative correlation was found between MDA and BMD ( r = -0.287, P = 0.046). A negative correlation was noted between cortisol and BMD, although it was not statistically significant ( r = -0.079, p = 0.589). This study showed a negative correlation between MDA levels and BMD, suggesting that higher oxidative stress may be associated with lower BMD and increased fracture risk. Although cortisol levels also showed a negative correlation with BMD, it was not statistically significant. Elevated cortisol can reduce bone formation and increase resorption, suggesting a need for further research on its impact on bone health. These findings highlight the complex relationship between stress markers and BMD in osteoporosis, underlining the importance of early detection and management for better bone health and quality of life.

Article.Title: Molecular surveillance of gastrointestinal parasites in wild herbivores of the Dooars region, India with implications for future one health monitoring
Article.Authors: Saha S.; Gupta M.; Saha R.; Chakraborti S.; Saha D.; Kundu K.; Korotkova E.; Saqib M.; Kar P.
Article.Abstract: Wild herbivores are important components of natural ecosystems, but gastrointestinal (GI) parasites can adversely affect host health and population dynamics. Understanding wildlife parasitism is also important in regions with close human–livestock–wildlife interactions, where some parasites may have zoonotic potential. However, information on the diversity and molecular characterization of GI parasites in free-ranging wild herbivores from the biodiversity-rich Dooars region of Northern West Bengal, India, remains limited. This study aimed to assess the occurrence and distribution of GI parasites in wild herbivores across three protected areas: Jaldapara National Park, Chapramari Wildlife Sanctuary, and Gorumara National Park of northern West Bengal, India utilizing an integrative approach of morphological and molecular identification. Faecal samples from bison, spotted deer, sambar deer, and hog deer were collected from the three protected areas and subjected to coprological screening for morphological identification of eggs and larvae followed by molecular validation, targeting the ribosomal ITS2 region through PCR amplification, Sanger sequencing, and subsequent phylogenetic analysis. Minimum free energy (MFE)-based RNA secondary structure prediction was employed to enhance species identification accuracy. The study identified eight distinct nematode species- Haemonchus placei , Trichostrongylus colubriformis , Trichostrongylus axei , Cooperia oncophora , Ostertagia ostertagi , Dictyocaulus cervi , Strongyloides papillosus , and Toxocara vitulorum . High ITS2 sequence homology (96.55–98.85%) confirmed identities. RNA secondary structure predictions provided robust genotypic differentiation. H. placei , T. colubriformis , S. papillosus , and C. oncophora dominated parasite infections across sites, with the highest prevalence seen in bison and sambar and lower rates in spotted deer. The occurrence of livestock-associated nematode taxa indicated a risk of bidirectional, cross-species transmission. This research provides critical baseline data on GI parasite diversity in wild herbivores of the Dooars region, highlighting significant zoonotic and ecological implications. Integrated multi-host longitudinal surveillance is essential to clarify parasite epidemiology and zoonotic risk. Sustained surveillance and a One Health approach are crucial to manage parasite spillover and safeguard regional biodiversity and public health in the region.

Article.Title: ARROWDE: an adaptive rotation-safe routed operator workflow for differential evolution
Article.Authors: Turgut O.
Article.Abstract: Optimizing continuous problems that combine rotated, non-separable, and multimodal landscapes under a limited budget of function evaluations is difficult. Most Differential Evolution (DE) methods use a static strategy or a fixed operator mixture, which can converge prematurely or spend the budget poorly when problem properties change during a run. This study proposes Adaptive Rotation-Safe Routed Operator Workflow Differential Evolution (ARROWDE). This bandit model combines upper-confidence-bound learning with landscape-aware priors, routing each trial to one of six single-evaluation operators: three exploratory and three exploitative. Implicit orthogonal transformations built from Givens rotations give robustness on rotated problems, and rotation-invariant population statistics are cached for the direct search operators at low cost. . On the CEC 2014 and CEC 2017 suites at 30 and 50 variables, ARROWDE attains the best mean Friedman ranks among the compared methods and is favored by the suite-level comparison against the most recent competition winner, with the margin widest at the higher dimension. The same tables mark its boundaries: IMODE and LSHADE-EpSin achieve lower mean errors on the 30-variable CEC 2014 composition functions, and the framework runs more slowly than L-SHADE and CMA-ES. Rather than proving every component strictly indispensable, ablation study ranks their relative importance, with stripping the rotation-safe layer causing the steepest performance drop, followed by the landscape prior and inherited adaptation, whereas the caps and bandit rule exhibit the smallest overall impact.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: differential evolution; Givens rotations; orthogonal transformations; exploration-exploitation balance

Article.Title: Adaptive online training for prenatal ultrasound image and video interpretation: a prospective controlled educational intervention study
Article.Authors: Rechenberg M.; Wittek A.; Koziol K.; Haverkamp N.; Walter A.; Recker F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ultrasound is the most important and commonly used imaging method for the detection of prenatal fetal pathologies, but is highly dependent on the interpreters’ knowledge. Regarding the current lack of ultrasound interpretation training in medical education, an individually adaptive online-learning tool was developed and evaluated against an unstructured control condition in which no learning activity was specified, prescribed or monitored. A prospective controlled educational intervention study with a pre–post design and quasi-random allocation to intervention and control groups was conducted. Within the learning tool, images and videos were presented together with corresponding questions to facilitate repetitive training in the recognition and assessment of relevant prenatal sonographic features. Participants in the intervention group ( n = 42) completed a baseline assessment (T1) on fetal image and video interpretation before using the tool. After completing the predefined requirements of the learning tool, they underwent a comparable post-intervention assessment (T2). Participants in the control group ( n = 46) completed the same T1 and T2 assessments but engaged only in unmonitored self-directed learning between the two time points. The primary outcome was the group difference in the change in overall prenatal ultrasound image and video interpretation performance from baseline assessment (T1) to final assessment (T2). Secondary outcomes included changes in image-based and video-based subscores, as well as learner satisfaction and educational benefit. Baseline performance did not differ between groups at T1 ( p = .878; intervention 69,14%, control 68.78%), although baseline variance was greater in the intervention group (SD 13.11 vs. 8.50% points; Levene p = .042). At T2 the intervention group scored substantially higher (82.76% vs. 65.83%), t(86) = 7.94, p < .001 (exact p = 6.88e − 12), Cohen’s d = 1.70 (Hedges’ g = 1.68; bootstrap 95% CI 1.24 to 2.26). The group × time interaction on the overall score was F(1, 86) = 44.35, p < .001 (exact p = 2.46e − 09), partial η² = 0.340, corresponding to a between-group difference in change of 16.58% points (95% CI 11.63 to 21.52). This result survived Bonferroni correction across the full family of 15 tests, as well as permutation, rank-based and trimmed-mean tests and leave-one-out deletion of every participant. The image subscore interaction was likewise robust (F(1, 86) = 46.93, p < .001, partial η² = 0.353); the video subscore interaction was nominally significant but did not survive correction for multiplicity ( p = .048, Holm-adjusted p = .335) and is reported as exploratory. Feedback was collected from the intervention group's participants. The findings indicate that the adaptive online tool produced substantially larger gains in prenatal ultrasound image and video interpretation than an unstructured control condition over the same interval. Because the control condition was neither standardised nor monitored, and because the trial included no non-adaptive comparator, the results should not be read as evidence that the tool is superior to structured conventional self-study, nor as evidence that the adaptive algorithm specifically accounts for the effect. A three-arm trial comparing adaptive training, an equivalent non-adaptive training sequence and a no-intervention condition is required to establish both. Clinical trial registration: Not applicable. This study was a prospective controlled educational intervention study and did not constitute a clinical trial according to the WHO/ICMJE definition, as it did not prospectively assign patients or participants to a healthrelated intervention in order to evaluate biomedical or healthrelated outcomes. The intervention consisted exclusively of an educational online learning tool, and the outcomes were educational performance measures and learner feedback.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of traditional, machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid models for short-term wind speed forecasting in Colombo, Sri Lanka
Article.Authors: Kudagama H.; Viswakula S.
Article.Abstract: Short-term wind speed forecasting is critical for optimizing wind-dependent operations in Sri Lanka. However, existing studies lack comprehensive comparisons across different time series forecasting frameworks and insufficiently examine performance differences between univariate and multivariate approaches. This study addresses these gaps by evaluating traditional time series models (ARIMA, ARIMAX, VAR), machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Regression), and deep learning models (Feed Forward Neural Network, Long Short-Term Memory, Convolutional Neural Network) for daily wind speed forecasting in Colombo, Sri Lanka. A residual-correction hybrid framework combining the optimal standalone XGB with deep learning models (XGB-FNN, XGB-LSTM, XGB-CNN) is systematically evaluated for the first time in the Sri Lankan wind speed forecasting context. Meteorological data from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2023, encompassing ten atmospheric variables, were analyzed. Model hyperparameters were optimized using Grid Search CV, Random Search CV, and Optuna with time series cross-validation. All residual-correction hybrid models used Optuna-tuned XGBoost, which is the optimal standalone model, as the primary model. The XGB-CNN with Optuna-tuned CNN achieved the best numerical performance with MSE of 0.5172, RMSE of 0.7192, MAE of 0.5432, and R 2 of 0.7855. Subsequent Diebold-Mariano testing and Multiple-Comparison Correction via Model Confidence Set confirmed that, although all hybrids showed numerically improved performance over the standalone XGBoost model, these improvements were not statistically significant. This suggests that both the optimal standalone XGBoost model and the proposed hybrid forecasting frameworks constitute robust and reliable approaches for forecasting in the present study. The most influential features identified were minimum, maximum, and average temperatures, precipitation, wind direction, southwest monsoon season, cloud cover, previous-day wind speed, previous-day sea level pressure, current and previous-day relative humidity, and surface pressure change from the previous day.

Article.Title: Empathy shortens perceived time in association with visual attention but not physiological measures
Article.Authors: Golbabaei S.; Hosseinnezhad M.; Karami Z.; Borhani K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Recent work suggests that empathic engagement can influence perceptual processes, yet its impact on time perception remains unclear. Whereas internal clock models predict that empathy-induced physiological arousal lengthens perceived duration, other frameworks predict the opposite. Specifically, findings that empathy reduces perceived distance, along with motivational dimensional theory, predict that empathy shortens perceived duration. To disentangle this, we employed an empathy-for-pain and duration estimation task, while measuring participants’ heart rate and skin conductance, to investigate how empathy and physiological arousal influence time perception. Further, we measured eye-movements to examine whether visual attention is associated with the possible effect of empathy on time perception. Crucially, we also assessed whether these effects are modulated by individual differences in trait empathy, alexithymia, and trait autism. Our findings show that empathy shortens estimated duration. Despite increases in physiological arousal during empathy, arousal was not associated with changes in time perception. Rather, greater visual attention to the eyes was related to stronger alteration in time perception. Furthermore, trait empathy and autism quotient modulated this effect, whereas alexithymia did not. These results provide the first empirical evidence that empathy alters time perception, elucidate the contribution of physiological and visual mechanisms to this phenomenon and extend current theories of time perception and empathy.

Article.Title: Attention-integrated hybrid CNN–vision transformer framework for robust multi-class cervical cytology classification using liquid-based cytology images
Article.Authors: Sathiya A.; Arieth R.; Nalayini C.; Balaji V.
Article.Abstract: The grading of cervical cytology images is a challenging task because some morphological changes are subtle, there are class imbalances and variability in staining of lesion grades. In order to overcome such difficulties, this work suggests MAH-CerviT, a Multi-Scale Attention-Guided Hybrid Cervical Transformer framework that combines dense hierarchical convolutional learning and window-based contextual modeling. In contrast to the traditional convolutional networks that mainly learn the local texture patterns, or the transformer-based networks that only focus on the global attention mechanism to improve the model, MAH-CerviT is a synergistic network with three major components: (i) a multi-scale dense convolutional backbone to learn the hierarchical morphological feature aggregation, (ii) a sequential channel-spatial attention refinement module to selectively enhance the diagnostically relevant cellular regions, and (iii) a Swin Transformer encoder to model structured contextual dependency. The hybrid fusion approach allows to discriminate between morphologically similar classes like HSIL and LSIL in a balanced manner and keep the computational efficiency. Massive experiments in 5-fold stratified cross-validation show that MAH-CerviT has a total accuracy of 95.92, macro F 1-score of 95.52 and macro-AUC of 96.40, significantly higher than DenseNet-121, EfficientNet-B4, ViT-Base, and Swin Transformer baselines. It is statistically proved that the increase in comparison to the strongest baseline is significant (p < 0.01). Ablation experiments demonstrate that multi-scale aggregation, attention refinement and contextual encoding have a cumulative beneficial effect on the performance of the baseline convolutional model, which justifies the complementary role of each. The robustness analysis also shows that the performance remains stable even when there are image corruptions and less data. The suggested MAH-CerviT framework provides an efficient trade-off between the accuracy of the discrimination system and the computational efficiency, and it is a reliable and scalable tool to solve the automated cervical cancer screening application.

Article.Title: Forest suberin fatty acids enable tailored and layered multifunctional electrospun polycaprolactone-chitosan nanofibers
Article.Authors: Avci T.; Yilmaz S.; Ismayilova N.; Kanli Z.; Kabak F.; Kaya E.; Bozkurt F.; Tinaz G.; Evran S.; Ficai D.; Ficai A.; Gunduz O.; Dogan C.
Article.Abstract: Current electrospun tissue engineering scaffolds still face challenges in simultaneously achieving adequate mechanical stability, tailored surface functionality, and multifunctional performance. To address this limitation, this study aimed to develop multifunctional biodegradable nanofibrous scaffolds using forest-derived suberin fatty acids (SFAs), selected as renewable functional additives because of their amphiphilic chemical structure and their potential to tailor both bulk and surface properties. Electrospun polycaprolactone/chitosan (PCL/CS) nanofibers were functionalized with SFA either by incorporation into the polymer matrix or by surface application through coating. The resulting nanocomposites were characterized in terms of their structural, thermal, mechanical, and biological properties by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), swelling and degradation analyses, tensile testing, antibacterial assays, and fibroblast viability studies. SEM analysis revealed that incorporating SFA into the PCL/CS matrix significantly reduced fiber diameter and narrowed the fiber diameter distribution. In contrast, coating the surface with SFA modified the fiber topography and surface compactness. Matrix incorporation of SFA enhanced early-stage water uptake and degradation, whereas surface coating resulted in a more gradual hydration response. Notably, the dual-loading system (PCL/CS/SFA + SFA coated) minimized both swelling and cumulative degradation, indicating enhanced barrier performance. Mechanical testing showed that matrix incorporation enhanced tensile strength while surface coating preserved ductility. Numerical analyses further revealed that SFA incorporation increased the critical buckling load and stress values, whereas SFA coating led to a decrease in these properties. Antibacterial assays demonstrated strong inhibition against Staphylococcus aureus (≈ 93%) with no effect on Escherichia coli . Biocompatibility studies confirmed excellent fibroblast compatibility for all SFA-modified nanofibers, while matrix incorporation of SFA favored early-stage cell proliferation. Overall, the proposed dual-functionalized PCL/CS/SFA nanofibrous system represents a sustainable strategy for tailoring both bulk and surface properties, highlighting its potential for wound dressing and other temporary biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Hydroclimatic controls and interaction-driven sensitivity of reference evapotranspiration across Indian climate regimes
Article.Authors: Nayak A.; Jeepsa N.; Pradhan S.; Barik S.; Panigrahi P.; Mohanty S.; Kumar M.; Satpathy B.; Patra P.; Sarangi A.; Jothimani M.
Article.Abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) represents atmospheric evaporative demand and is a key indicator of land–atmosphere interactions under climate variability and warming. However, how the sensitivity of ET₀ to its climatic drivers evolves across hydroclimatic gradients remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we examine regime-dependent sensitivity and interaction effects controlling ET₀ across five contrasting hydroclimatic regions of India (per-humid to arid) using long-term observations within the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith framework. A combined sensitivity approach integrating local perturbation analysis with global methods (Morris screening and Sobol’ variance decomposition) was employed to quantify both independent and interaction-driven effects of key meteorological variables. Results reveal a systematic transition in the dominant controls of ET₀ across the hydroclimatic gradient. Solar radiation explains more than 80% of ET₀ variability in humid and per-humid regions, whereas its contribution declines to 35–40% in arid environments, where temperature, humidity, and wind exert stronger influence. Concurrently, nonlinear interaction effects intensify with climatic dryness, with interaction strength increasing from < 5% in humid regions to 20% in semi-arid and arid regimes, reflecting strong coupling among thermodynamic and aerodynamic processes. A three-stage transition in ET₀ control emerges: radiation-dominated regimes in humid climates, vapor-pressure-deficit-driven regimes in semi-arid regions, and coupled radiative–aerodynamic regimes in arid environments.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based risk screening model for depressive symptoms in middle-aged and elderly cardiovascular disease patients
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Liu H.; Liang W.; Wang G.; Ma G.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and depression frequently co-occur, yet systematic depression screening remains underutilized in routine cardiac care. This study aimed to develop and compare machine learning algorithms for identifying concurrent depressive symptoms in middle-aged and elderly CVD patients. Data from 2,204 participants aged ≥ 45 years with physician-diagnosed CVD were obtained from the 2018 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Depressive symptoms were defined as CES-D10 score ≥ 10 (prevalence: 54.1%). Seven algorithms—logistic regression (LR), artificial neural networks, XGBoost, LightGBM, decision tree, random forest, and support vector machine—were trained and internally validated. Feature selection used LASSO regression. Performance was assessed via AUC-ROC, Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis, with bootstrap correction for optimism. Among 2,204 participants, 1,193 had depressive symptoms. The LR model showed strong discrimination (AUC = 0.832, 95% CI: 0.804–0.860), though performance differences among the top models were minimal (AUC range: 0.826–0.832). LR was selected for the final nomogram based on its favorable calibration and interpretability. Significant predictors included loneliness, life satisfaction, self-rated health, hearing status, gender, ADL score, sleep, and cognitive function. A web-based dynamic nomogram tool was developed as a research prototype to facilitate individualized risk estimation and illustrate the model’s potential application. An LR-based model using eight accessible variables demonstrated strong discrimination for identifying concurrent depressive symptoms in CVD patients. The nomogram may serve as a preliminary triage tool to prompt confirmatory assessment; external validation is required before clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Effects of coffee thermocycling on surface roughness, microhardness, and color stability of permanent crown materials
Article.Authors: Ersoy N.; Akgün S.; Tekin S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Permanent crown resins manufactured by additive technologies are increasingly used for definitive restorations, yet their resistance to combined thermal and chemical aging remains incompletely characterized. This in vitro study compared four 3D-printed permanent crown resins (VarseoSmile TriniQ, NextDent C&B MFH, CROWNTEC, and Permanent Crown Resin) with a milled composite-based CAD/CAM material (CeraSmart 270). Disk-shaped specimens ( n = 10/group) were evaluated for surface roughness, surface morphology, microhardness, and color before and after 10,000 coffee thermocycles between 5 °C and 55 °C. Surface roughness increased significantly in all materials. After aging, CeraSmart 270 showed the lowest Ra (0.159 ± 0.005 μm) and highest Vickers hardness (93.87 ± 4.80 HV), whereas Permanent Crown Resin showed the highest Ra (0.322 ± 0.014 μm), lowest hardness (20.22 ± 1.40 HV), and greatest color change (ΔE*ab = 4.19 ± 0.30). Permanent Crown Resin and NextDent C&B MFH exceeded the predefined ΔE*ab reference value of 3.3. Coffee thermocycling produced material-dependent effects, with CeraSmart 270 showing greater overall stability than the tested 3D-printed resins under the conditions of this study.

Article.Title: A dimensionless-entropy weight method for determining cloud physical parameter responses induced by aircraft cloud seeding
Article.Authors: Sha X.; Li X.; Chu R.; Cheng B.; Liu Y.; Ding J.; Zhang F.; Song C.; Xiao Y.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the challenges in evaluation of aircraft cloud seeding effect, this study proposes a physical evaluation method that integrates multiple key techniques to achieve an integrated quantitative evaluation based on multiple indicators. This evaluation approach was applied to six aircraft cloud seeding operations conducted in Henan Province of China during 2023–2024. Results show that the six operations exhibited nonlinear growth patterns for dispersion in both the target and control areas, with rapid expansion at the initial stage followed by a slower rate. The dispersion rate, distance, extent and concentration of the seeding agent vary significantly depending on the meteorological conditions, such as atmospheric turbulence, wind speed, stability and humidity. For the six operations, the vertically integrated liquid water content (VIL) showed notably high entropy weights (0.06–0.43) in multiple operations (No. 2, 3 and 6), making it a relatively stable indicator for evaluating the cloud seeding effects. Due to complex cloud microphysical processes such as latent heat release from deposition, downdrafts, cloud dissipation and cloud development, the responses of cloud-top temperature to seeding varied considerably (− 44.56 °C ~ − 6 °C). The effects of cloud seeding on cloud effective radius and optical thickness are complex and vary substantially depending on specific seeding conditions. The responses of liquid water path were time-dependent, the seeding-induced responses of radar reflectivity exhibited distinct patterns, including delayed manifestation, strong enhancement, and ineffectiveness or being masked. The strong-echo area and the VIL in the target areas fluctuated and generally decreased over time, respectively. The change rates of hourly precipitation induced by seeding varied from 3.82% to 8.91%. The integrated physical inspection dimensionless index (PIDI, a physical evaluation index for evaluating cloud seeding effects) values for the seven indicators ranged from 15.0% to 69.7%, showing a smaller variation magnitude compared with the change rates of individual indicators, which reflects the synergistic effects of multiple indicators. This study provides a quantifiable and robust algorithm that mitigates the interference of natural variability, and its application to six case studies demonstrates its potential for advancing cloud seeding techniques and improving effect evaluation capabilities.

Article.Title: Bone infills reveal the origin of the Middle Triassic Miedary vertebrate assemblage
Article.Authors: Rytel A.; Pawlak W.; Ruciński M.; Mujal E.; Bącal P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Taphonomic data is an important source of information related to fossil assemblages. Fossilised bones, characteristics of their preservation, and their sedimentary infill can serve as a basis for unravelling the origin of fossil bonebeds. Assessing the taphonomic data thereby allows for deciphering the genesis of multitaxic mass accumulations of elements of organisms from different habitats. Here we provide scenarios explaining the origin of the Middle Triassic Miedary vertebrate assemblage from Poland. In this locality remains of both freshwater and marine animals are found, but their sympatric co-occurrence in life could not be previously confirmed. We used a suite of analytical methods on a broad sample of thin sections made from bones of reptiles, amphibians and fishes, to assess the diversity of their taphonomic characteristics. This allowed us to propose a set of taphonomic trajectories that resulted in specific preservation characteristics, which can be extrapolated for other sites. The remains of the long-necked archosauromorph Tanystropheus do not differ in their preservation from those of aquatic taxa, supporting its interpretation as a water-dwelling animal. Our results demonstrate that in the Middle Triassic some environments combined faunistic elements from principally different habitats, underlining the complexity of these ecosystems.
