Article.Title: A unified stochastic random walk theory for Kolmogorov spectrum, halo mass functions, and halo density profiles
Article.Authors: Xu Z.
Article.Abstract: We develop a unified stochastic framework for a broad class of nonequilibrium systems and apply it to turbulence and cosmic structure formation. The evolution of spectra and distributions in these systems are modeled as transport processes in an appropriate ”scale space”, described by random walks and Fokker–Planck equations with scale-dependent waiting times. We reformulate the turbulent cascade as a random walk in wavenumber space with a k-dependent waiting time \(\tau _{gk}\propto k^{-{\gamma }}\) . With self-consistency condition determined value \(\gamma =2/3\) , we recover the Kolmogorov -5/3 law and obtain the full energy spectrum including the inertial-dissipation crossover, exponential cutoff, and spectrum constant without invoking dimensional analysis directly on the energy spectrum. For a bottom-up hierarchical halo structure formation, low-mass haloes collapse early and retain strong primordial imprints, while prolonged assembly of large haloes near the characteristic mass \(m_h^*\) tends to erase this memory and establishes a universal spectrum \(P(k)\propto k^{-1}\) . We model this process as an analogous random walk of dark matter haloes in mass space \(m_h\) with a mass-dependent waiting time \(\tau _g\propto m_h^{-\lambda }\) . The model yields a stretched Gaussian halo mass function that reproduces the Press-Schechter form, with both small-scale scaling \(f_M\propto m_h^{-\lambda }\) and exponential cutoff at \(m_h>m_h^*\) set by exponent \(\lambda \) . The framework naturally produces a double- \(\lambda \) mass function, where \(\lambda \) reflects the primordial spectrum at low masses and approaches \(\lambda \) =2/3 near \(m_h^*\) where gravity dominates. For individual haloes, a spatial random walk with waiting time \(\tau _{gr}\propto r^{-\gamma }\) generates a double- \(\gamma \) density profile that reproduces the Einasto profile, with both small-scale scaling \(\rho _r\propto r^{-2\gamma }\) and exponential cutoff at \(r>r_s\) set by exponent \(\gamma \) . In this case, \(\gamma \) is fixed by the initial spectrum in the inner core regions and approaches \(\gamma \) =2/3 and \(\rho _r\propto r^{-{4/3}}\) in the outer regions when gravity dominates. Our results demonstrate that this simple stochastic framework offers a common theoretical description of both turbulent cascades and cosmic structure formation.

Article.Title: Mechanical stabilization of non-vascular catheters using a low-profile suture-anchored device
Article.Authors: Naidu S.; Zhou C.; Ma Q.; Bercu Z.; Li H.; Moon J.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the mechanical performance of AnchorDoc, a novel, low-profile, two-piece, suture-anchored device, against standard securement methods. We hypothesized that AnchorDoc would provide superior mechanical stability without compromising catheter patency. Using a custom anatomically-informed gelatin phantom of the human flank with porcine-skin overlay, we compared the performance of AnchorDoc against a standard adhesive device (StatLock) and a suture-tape technique (Roman sandal) for 8.5, 10.2, and 12 French (Fr) catheters. We conducted: (1) static tensile testing under dry and wet conditions to measure peak force to catheter slip (≥ 5 mm); (2) dynamic gait simulation to assess time-to-failure; and (3) static flow testing to evaluate for lumen compromise. In tensile testing, AnchorDoc required a significantly higher dislodgement force than both StatLock and Roman Sandal under dry (e.g., 10.2 Fr: 31.1 ± 1.4 N vs. 20.5 ± 2.4 N and 18.8 ± 2.3 N, respectively; p < 0.0001) and wet conditions (25.5 ± 1.0 N vs. 10.9 ± 1.3 N and 18.7 ± 1.0 N; p < 0.0001). The adhesive device’s retention strength degraded by nearly 50% when wet, while AnchorDoc maintained its superiority. In dynamic gait simulation, Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that AnchorDoc had a significantly higher survival probability (fewer failures) while tested over 12,000 cycles compared to both comparators (p < 0.05). Flow testing confirmed that AnchorDoc did not cause a statistically significant reduction in flow rate or lumen diameter across all catheter sizes (p > 0.05). The AnchorDoc device provides significantly greater resistance to both static and dynamic dislodgement forces than common adhesive and suture-tape techniques, particularly in a laboratory-simulated wet environment, without impairing catheter function. Article.Title: A multidimensional proteomic framework of circulating inflammation identifies outcome-specific cardiovascular risk axes in 39,494 UK biobank participants
Article.Authors: Song X.; Zhang H.; Liu G.; Shen Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inflammation is central to cardiovascular disease, yet conventional biomarkers do not resolve the underlying organisation of circulating inflammatory biology. Among 44,787 UK Biobank participants passing proteomic quality control, 736 inflammation-related proteins were used to derive orthogonal proteomic dimensions in a White Development sample (n = 20,830), with definitions fixed and applied unchanged in White Validation (n = 20,831). A CVD-free multimodal cohort of 39,494 participants provided the source population for downstream analyses; primary prospective associations were evaluated in White Development complete cases (n = 17,334) and replicated in White Validation (n = 17,190). Eight dimensions showed high structural stability and distinct protein, pathway, metabolic, imaging, and cardiovascular profiles. In the primary analysis, 23 of 48 RC outcome associations were FDR significant; RC2 was positively associated with all six outcomes, with the strongest association for heart failure (HR 1.395, 95% CI 1.273–1.527), while RC8 showed a more moderate but similarly broad pattern. RC4 was mainly associated with coronary outcomes, RC6 showed inverse associations with several endpoints, and RC7 was most clearly related to heart failure and atrial fibrillation. Major patterns reproduced in White Validation. Adding RC1–RC8 improved discrimination across all six outcomes (ΔC-index 0.0055–0.0136), with incremental gains retained beyond CRP, GlycA, and NLR. These findings support a reproducible multidimensional proteomic architecture of inflammation with heterogeneous cardiovascular relevance.

Article.Title: Network-compartmental modeling for assessing core drivers of fascioliasis dissemination in definitive hosts
Article.Authors: Philipo H.; Hugo A.; Kung’aro M.; Shinzeh J.
Article.Abstract: Fascioliasis is a neglected zoonotic disease caused by Fasciola species, affecting livestock and humans worldwide and imposing substantial economic and public health burdens. Conventional compartmental models commonly assume homogeneous mixing and therefore may not adequately represent the heterogeneous contact patterns characteristic of smallholder farming systems. This study develops a network-informed multi-host compartmental model that integrates a Watts–Strogatz small-world contact network with effective exposure coefficients representing local and long-range connectivity among cattle, humans, snails, and environmental metacercariae. The framework incorporates short-range transmission within local communities and long-range transmission between geographically separated farming communities. Analytical results establish the basic reproduction number ( \(R_0\) ), demonstrate global asymptotic stability of the disease-free equilibrium when \(R_0<1\) , and provide a Jacobian-based criterion for local asymptotic stability of the endemic equilibrium. Numerical simulations characterize the temporal dynamics of infection and quantify the effects of treatment, environmental sanitation, network connectivity, and local exposure structure on transmission. Increased network connectivity and long-range interactions facilitate wider spatial dissemination, whereas reductions in transmission and environmental contamination suppress infection. The results demonstrate that incorporating network structure into fascioliasis transmission models provides a more realistic representation of heterogeneous contact processes and offers a quantitative framework for evaluating targeted control strategies in interconnected livestock and human communities.

Article.Title: Extraction, chemical fingerprinting, and dyeing-process evaluation of fungal pigments from Phaeolus schweinitzii

Article.Abstract: Colors have capacity to elicit human emotions in philosophy, arts, science, and many industrial areas. There is a lot of interest in natural color substitutes due to rising concerns about the detrimental effects of synthetic colorants on consumers and the environment. Although, plants serve as major non-viable sources of natural pigments with several limitations. In contrast, fungi thrive in diverse environments also exhibit adaptive metabolisms and catalytic pathways, make them valuable for natural pigment production. Furthermore, there is a growing demand for more sustainable and cost-effective extraction methods. Therefore, under suitable condition, extraction technique was carried out. In this study, Phaeolus schweinitzii was identified using morphological and ITS-based molecular approaches and investigated as a source of yellow, red, and reddish-brown fungal pigments. The effects of pH, agitation speed, sodium sulfate concentration, temperature, and dyeing time on pigment uptake were evaluated sequentially using a one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) experimental approach. The highest observed responses within the investigated ranges were generally associated with mildly acidic conditions, moderate-to-high agitation, low sodium sulfate concentrations, elevated temperatures, and intermediate dyeing times. However, because the variables were not studied simultaneously in a factorial design, these conditions are interpreted as preliminary operating ranges rather than a global multivariable optimum. Interactions among the process variables could not be estimated from the present design.

Article.Title: Long-term multi-section traffic flow forecasting using the CNN–RNLSTM–MLR neural network
Article.Authors: Rezaie N.; Shirmohammadi H.; Shirmohammadi Z.; Jafari M.
Article.Abstract: Nowadays, traffic congestion significantly contributes to severe economic and environmental problems in cities. Anticipating traffic flow is a highly effective strategy for mitigating congestion, and accurate predictions are vital for practical traffic guidance, management, and control. However, many existing approaches either treat spatial correlations and temporal dependencies separately or rely on single-architecture models, which limits their ability to capture complex spatiotemporal patterns in real-world networks. Even in cases where these factors have been considered in a combined manner, our proposed model is showed lower error rates compared to them. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network enhanced by Multiple Linear Regression (MLR). The proposed model utilizes CNN to extract meaningful latent features from input data while also taking advantage of LSTM-MLR's ability to capture temporal context. In the first stage, a CNN–RNLSTM model is employed to forecast traffic conditions on four highways in the United Kingdom that are closely associated with a target road, jointly modeling spatial interactions and nonlinear temporal dynamics. In the second stage, the CNN–RNLSTM–MLR model leverages these intermediate forecasts, together with explanatory variables, to estimate traffic conditions on the target roadway through a regression-based fusion layer. This two-stage design allows the model to combine the representation power of deep learning with the interpretability and correction capability of linear regression. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach consistently outperforms conventional baselines, including standalone MLR, LSTM, and MLR–LSTM models, as measured by Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). Notably, the RMSE exhibits a 22.96% improvement compared to the RNLSTM–MLR model. Overall, the proposed framework achieves the lowest error rate among state-of-the-art methods, indicating its superior ability to capture complex spatiotemporal dependencies in traffic flow forecasting.

Article.Title: Smart home device use influences older adults’ mental health through social interaction and digital benefits
Article.Authors: Zheng L.; Yuan Y.; Wang H.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: This study examines how smart home device use influences older adults’ mental health over time. Using three waves of the China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey (2018, 2020, 2023), we constructed a balanced panel of 4,541 adults and applied hierarchical regression and PROCESS Model 6 with 5,000 bootstraps. Results show that smart home device use is positively associated with subsequent mental health. However, after accounting for mediators, the direct association is no longer significant, indicating the effect is mainly indirect. Both social interaction and digital benefits mediate this association, with a sequential pathway from social interaction to digital benefits also supported. Subgroup analyses reveal stronger links among urban and higher-educated groups. These findings suggest that smart home technologies may promote mental health primarily by enhancing social engagement and perceived digital convenience, informing the integration of these technologies into aging-in-place and healthy aging strategies.

Article.Title: Ascorbic acid formulation using milk-derived extracellular vesicles: a stepwise process evaluation
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Ahn G.; Lee E.; Park D.; Lee P.; Min J.; Kim Y.; Ahn J.
Article.Abstract: Labile hydrophilic compounds, such as ascorbic acid (AA), present challenges for nanoscale formulation due to their chemical instability and strong tendency to recrystallize during processing and storage. Although various nanocarrier-based formulation approaches have been developed, achieving physical stability while maintaining biological compatibility remains difficult. In this study, we aimed to develop a practical and biocompatible formulation approach using milk-derived extracellular vesicles (mi-EVs) and to establish a solvent-free formulation strategy through stepwise evaluation of processing conditions. An AA formulation based on mi-EVs (milkCsome) was developed through sequential evaluation of key processing parameters. Sequential physical treatment—sonication followed by rotation—improved the visual homogeneity of the formulation, with no visible precipitation observed after 16 h of storage at 4 °C under the selected conditions. Under the selected processing conditions, milkCsome achieved approximately 16% AA retention after purification and retained antioxidant activity. Biological evaluations showed no detectable reduction in cell viability under the tested conditions, and the formulation was classified as non-irritant in a reconstructed human skin model. Overall, this study presents a simple, solvent-free process for preparing a milk-derived extracellular vesicle-based AA formulation with antioxidant activity and biological compatibility under the conditions tested.

Article.Title: Cost-performance evaluation of socks developed from post-consumer denim waste and recycled polyester
Article.Authors: Anas M.; Dabolina I.; Mikucioniene D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Post-consumer denim waste is a major cotton-rich waste stream, but its use in durable textile products remains challenging because mechanical recycling shortens and damages fibers. This study developed half-terry socks from recycled denim cotton blended with recycled polyester and compared them with virgin polyester/cotton control socks. Twelve variants of recycled yarns were produced using three recycled polyester/recycled cotton ratios: 90/10, 80/20, and 70/30, through ring and rotor spinning at two twist levels. The socks were evaluated for structural properties, comfort-related performance, durability and production cost. The recycled socks were successfully produced with comparable structural properties to the control and generally showed higher air permeability, indicating better breathability. Moisture management was mainly controlled by sock region, following the order leg > upper foot > terry sole, with the terry sole acting mainly as an absorbent and cushioning zone. Cost analysis showed that recycled socks were cheaper, costing 0.149 to 0.152 €/pair, compared with 0.160 €/pair for the virgin control. However, durability is the main limitation: all recycled socks showed pilling grade 1, while the control showed grade 3, and abrasion loss increased with recycled cotton content. Recycled denim-based socks demonstrated comparable structural properties, improved breathability, lower estimated production cost, slightly higher air permeability, and circular material benefits; however, poor pilling resistance and greater abrasion loss remain key barriers to commercial adoption, highlighting the need for further improvements in recycled yarn quality and surface durability.

Article.Title: A Graphormer approach for predicting peptide half-life, secondary structure, solvent accessibility, and post-translational modifications
Article.Authors: Cifuentes P.; Adàlia R.; Vasicek L.; Gundersdorf R.; Harradine P.; Zamora I.
Article.Abstract: Peptides represent a promising class of therapeutic agents due to their high target specificity, favorable safety profiles, and efficient tissue penetration. However, their clinical development remains limited by poor in vivo stability, rapid enzymatic degradation, and short plasma half-lives. The structural flexibility of peptides and their high solvent accessibility further increase their susceptibility to proteolysis, resulting in rapid clearance and reduced therapeutic efficacy. Although strategies such as cyclization and incorporation of non-natural amino acids can improve stability, it remains challenging at early stages to identify which peptides would benefit from such modifications based on their pharmacokinetic and physicochemical properties. Here, we present a Graphormer-based machine learning framework for predicting four key peptide properties: half-life, relative solvent accessibility, secondary structure, and post-translational modifications. The framework supports both cyclic peptides and non-natural amino acids, extending beyond the scope of many currently available tools. To evaluate performance, we benchmarked our predictive models against existing methods for each property. Rather than focusing on surpassing current approaches, this study emphasizes the practical applicability of the proposed framework for peptide property prediction. Additionally, the half-life prediction model was validated using an experimental dataset generated by a pharmaceutical company, demonstrating the flexibility of the approach for training on user-generated experimental data.

Article.Title: Bioacoustic raw-audio transformer effectively and efficiently encodes mixed sample rate data
Article.Authors: Faiß M.; Strandburg-Peshkin A.; Roch M.; Schäfer-Zimmermann J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep learning has been widely adopted in the field of bioacoustics, enabling behavioral and ecological research into many sound producing animals through the use of specially designed and trained models. So-called foundational models can generalize to novel species or tasks, but require larger and more diverse training datasets. But the broad range of frequencies that animals produce poses a problem: bioacoustic datasets are recorded at various sample rates to capture different frequency ranges. Combining these data to train generalist models becomes exceedingly costly the wider the frequency range is expanded with high resolution data, becoming untenable for bioacousticians. To approach this problem, we performed experiments using a state-of-the-art transformer model, animal2vec, and a custom dataset consisting of recordings with various sample rates and species whose vocalizations cover a broad frequency range. We designed a positional encoding that provides inductive information about the sample rate, but found that the model is natively able to compensate for the perceived time stretch in the receptive field induced by varying sample rates, with no effect on performance compared to the standard approach of upsampling. This opens up new possibilities of training powerful models on broad bioacoustic datasets and the creation of more generalizable tools for bioacousticians.

Article.Title: Bactrocera oleae gut microbiome shows metabolic potential to complement the decline of symbiotic ‘Candidatus Erwinia dacicola’ in artificially-reared flies
Article.Authors: Elsayed A.; Alma A.; Gonella E.
Article.Abstract: The olive fly Bactrocera oleae has a gut microbiome dominated by the symbiont ‘ Candidatus Erwinia dacicola’. Laboratory rearing conditions result in symbiont loss, reducing insect fitness. This work combined transcriptomics and culture-based approaches to examine B. oleae gut microbiome dynamics over multiple artificially-reared generations prior to complete symbiont loss. Ca. E. dacicola was dominant in field-derived parental generation but decreased in laboratory-reared offspring, which showed increased abundance of other bacterial taxa. Bacterial genes involved in nitrogen biosynthesis, glycolysis, and coenzyme A production pathways showed consistent expression differences between generations, with higher levels in flies with high Ca. E. dacicola density. Genomic pathway potential for these processes was also identified among other culturable gut community members. Laboratory-reared flies had significant infections with cultivable Enterobacter hormaechei , Pseudomonas sp., and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia , showing genomic pathway potential overlapping with Ca. E. dacicola and distinct genomic pathway specializations among isolates. These findings indicate that culturable bacteria with overlapping metabolic pathway potential may represent promising candidates for functionally compensating for the uncultivable obligate symbiont when it cannot be retained by the host.

Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Cui X.; Zhang C.; Zhang X.; Lin Y.; Wang Y.; Chen Y.; Liu J.; Yan C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Manganese (Mn) is an essential trace element with a biphasic, dose-dependent effect on neurodevelopment. Amidst the escalating risks of environmental Mn exposure, nationwide population-based reference values and the distribution of blood manganese levels (BMLs) in children remain undefined in China. To address this gap, we quantified BMLs in venous whole blood samples from 30,248 children aged 0 to < 84 months across 15 administrative divisions in China using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. The overall geometric mean (GM) of BMLs was 13.39 µg/L (95% CI: 13.33–13.44). Spatially and demographically, significantly higher BMLs were identified in Western China, rural areas, and in girls (all P < 0.001). BMLs exhibited an age-dependent profile characterized by a sharp decline to a 6-month nadir, a late-infantile rebound, followed by a gradual decrease towards a homeostatic plateau from 24 months onward. The age-stratified population-based reference values (P2.5–P97.5) were 7.67–49.15 µg/L for infants aged 0 to < 6 months, 7.21–30.33 µg/L for those aged 6 to < 24 months, and 6.59–24.34 µg/L for children aged 24 to < 84 months. In conclusion, this study is the first nationwide large-scale epidemiological investigation of BMLs in young children in China, providing a comprehensive characterization of their overall distribution, age-dependent profile, and regional and demographic factors associated with BMLs. Furthermore, these findings provide a valuable baseline for future research on environmental Mn exposure and pediatric neurodevelopment.

Article.Authors: Lee G.; Kang D.; Lee J.; Lee J.; Lee J.; Kim I.
Article.Abstract: Baroreflex dysfunction and autonomic imbalance are key pathophysiological features of hypertension, but current pharmacological approaches often fail to address these neural mechanisms. Blood pressure perturbation was induced with the head-up tilt test (supine–tilt–supine). Baroreflex sensitivity (BRS) was analyzed only during the 10-minute tilt phase, whereas heart rate variability (HRV) was analyzed across four 5-minute segments (S-baseline, early-tilt, late-tilt, recovery). In the direct crossover analysis of the primary BRS outcome, pre-to-post changes did not differ significantly between taVNS and sham, and the baseline-adjusted sensitivity analysis yielded the same conclusion. Among the secondary HRV outcomes, differences averaged across analysis segments were significant only for SDNN and pNN30, whereas no analysis-segment-specific interaction was significant. Descriptive within-visit comparisons showed increases in BRS and several HRV measures during the taVNS visit. These findings provide preliminary evidence compatible with cardiovagal modulation during orthostatic stress, but do not establish a taVNS-specific improvement in BRS or blood pressure regulation. Further research involving patient cohorts and longitudinal study protocols is needed.

Article.Title: Integrated preservative and packaging strategies suppresses senescence in loose marigold (Tagetes erecta L.) by preserving antioxidants and membrane integrity
Article.Authors: Viresh M.; Jain R.; Sethi S.; Singh M.; Tiwari A.; Singh B.; Lekshmy S.; Kumar M.; Vinaykumar L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Loose marigold flowers are highly perishable and suffer substantial postharvest losses because of rapid moisture loss, accelerated respiration, membrane deterioration, and oxidative damage. Although packaging technologies have been widely investigated for extending the shelf life of loose flowers, information on the integrated use of chemical preservatives and packaging materials remains limited. This study evaluated the combined effects of five preservative treatments [tap water (control), distilled water, boric acid (4%), salicylic acid (50 ppm), and ascorbic acid (50 ppm)] in combination with two packaging conditions (open/no packaging and muslin cloth bag) under ambient (30 ± 2 °C and 40–45% RH) and cold storage (5 ± 1 °C and 75–80% RH) conditions on postharvest quality of loose flowers. Cold storage extended flower longevity by 100–300% compared with ambient conditions, while muslin cloth bag packaging increased shelf life by 25–100% over unpackaged flowers. Among the treatments, 4% boric acid combined with muslin cloth bag packaging was the most effective, extending shelf-life from 4.0 to 7.0 days under low temperature and from 1.0 to 3.5 days under ambient storage. This treatment substantially reduced weight loss, resulting in approximately three-fold and four-fold lower PLW than the untreated unpackaged control under ambient and cold storage, respectively. It also maintained membrane stability, suppressed respiration, and preserved carotenoid content. In addition, it enhanced superoxide dismutase, catalase, and peroxidase activities, indicating improved antioxidant defence and reduced oxidative damage. These findings demonstrate that integrating boric acid with muslin cloth bag packaging delays postharvest senescence, extending shelf life up to 7.0 days and 3.5 days under cold and ambient conditions respectively, by maintaining membrane integrity and antioxidant defence, offering a practical strategy for reducing postharvest losses and extending the marketability of loose marigold flowers.

Article.Authors: Miki D.; Takigasaki H.

We replace the actor of Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) with an SNN: a Spiking Actor Network. The membrane potential, an internal SNN state, is reconstructed at update time from a short observation history through the current actor, rather than stored at collection time. To reduce the controller’s inference cost, we add a regularization term on the squared membrane potentials, encouraging actions from fewer spikes. In simulation the agent acquired the leg coordination needed to approach a target, and its firing patterns developed a periodicity matched to the SMA response. The resulting gait gives continuous propulsion without excessive firing. Goal error matched an ANN-actor TD3 baseline with smaller spread across seeds, and reconstruction gave the lowest goal error of the membrane-state treatments. The regularization lowered the firing rate until the estimated inference energy fell below the ANN’s.

Article.Title: Specific macronutrient clusters associated with biological aging
Article.Authors: Zheng M.; Li J.; Chen C.; Liu Y.; Wang X.; Du Y.; Dong X.; Guo Y.; Zeng X.
Article.Abstract: Nutrition is a key modifiable factor influencing aging, yet most studies focus on isolated nutrients or predefined dietary patterns, leaving the relationship between naturally occurring macronutrient clusters and biological aging poorly understood. This study aimed to identify naturally occurring macronutrient intake clusters using a novel three-dimensional approach and examine their associations with biological aging in U.S. adults. Data from 25,987 adults in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) were analyzed. Biological age was estimated using the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM-BA). Biological age acceleration (AA) was computed as the difference between biological age and chronological age. Dietary intake was assessed using 24-hour recalls. Participants were classified into macronutrient clusters based on energy percentages from protein, fat, and carbohydrates using percentile-based cutoffs. Multivariable weighted logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between macronutrient clusters and AA, with stratification by energy intake, sex, and age. Compared to the reference cluster (Pm: Fm: Cmh—moderate protein, moderate fat, moderate-high carbohydrate), the Pm: Fm: Cm cluster (moderate protein, moderate fat, moderate carbohydrate) (OR: 1.21, 95% CI: 1.06–1.38) and the Pm: Fmh: Cml cluster (moderate protein, moderate-high fat, moderate-low carbohydrate) (OR: 1.25, 95% CI: 1.03–1.50) showed suggestive positive associations with AA. However, after adjusting for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) method, neither cluster reached the prespecified level of statistical significance (FDR q = 0.063 and 0.086, respectively). These associations were more pronounced in females and middle-aged adults (40–60 years). In restricted cubic spline analyses, a U-shaped relationship was observed for carbohydrate intake within Cluster Pl: Fm: Cml: AA risk decreased as carbohydrate intake increased from low to moderate levels, then increased with further higher carbohydrate intake ( P overall = 0.031; P non-linear = 0.050). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential effect modification by demographic factors, but these findings should be interpreted with caution due to limited statistical power. Specific, naturally occurring macronutrient clusters showed suggestive associations with AA, with potential effect heterogeneity by energy intake, sex, and age. Our findings underscore the importance of moving beyond isolated nutrients toward a holistic dietary pattern approach and suggest preliminary avenues for personalized nutritional interventions. These associations warrant validation in future prospective studies.

Article.Authors: Benigni T.; Pena A.; Kuntaegowdanahalli S.; Abbas J.; Jung R.
Article.Abstract: Haptic feedback elicits sensations of touch to communicate information to the user. Recent developments in virtual reality and sensory prostheses have demonstrated the need for systems that can provide more information than the simple vibrotactor in your phone. A novel multidimensional encoding approach allows for percepts of signal intensity and flutter frequency in a single distal location using transcutaneous neural stimulation. In this study we aimed to determine if these percepts are able to convey useful information to participants performing motor control tasks and if they perform better than a typical intensity-only modulation approach. Eleven participants performed three types of tasks to assess the efficacy of multidimensional stimulation. The first set included discrete matching tasks, where participants had to differentiate between thirteen combinations of flutter frequency and intensity. In the other two sets, participants had to differentiate between simultaneous changes in the percepts. Participants in this study could correctly identify all discrete percept combinations and follow the changes in the percepts better than chance. Performance in the discrete task using a multidimensional approach showed increased information transfer compared to the individual modulation of intensity or flutter frequency. These results suggest that multidimensional encoding is a promising approach for increasing information throughput in sensory feedback systems. Hence, such an approach might improve upon conventional methods of providing graded percepts, creating more informative tactile percepts for haptic feedback through peripheral nerve stimulation.

Article.Title: Ingestion-mediated toxicity of dinotefuran against Aedes aegypti and its implications for future sugar based toxic bait development
Article.Authors: Boroomand M.; Soltani A.; Sanei-Dehkordi A.; Paksa A.; Gholami A.; Saeedi S.; Moosa-Kazemi S.; Nikbakhtzadeh M.; Azizi K.
Article.Abstract: Aedes aegypti (Linnaeus, 1762) is an important vector of dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever viruses. The increasing spread of insecticide resistance in Aedes populations highlights the need for alternative control strategies and insecticides with novel modes of action. Dinotefuran, a third-generation neonicotinoid, has shown promising activity against several vector species, but information on its oral toxicity in Aedes aegypti remains limited. The oral toxicity of dinotefuran was evaluated using a sugar-feeding bioassay under laboratory conditions. Female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes (2–5 days old) were exposed to 10% sucrose solutions containing dinotefuran at 0.00001, 0.0001, 0.0005, and 0.001 mg/mL. Uranine (0.8%) was used as a fluorescent feeding marker, and mortality was assessed after 24 h among fluorescent-positive mosquitoes. The mean sugar meal volume was quantified fluorometrically. Mortality data were analyzed using a generalized linear model with a binomial error distribution and probit link, using log10-transformed dinotefuran concentration as the predictor. Because overdispersion was detected, inference was based on a quasibinomial model with a probit link. Dinotefuran produced a clear concentration-dependent increase in mortality, reaching 81.86% at 0.001 mg/mL, while feeding rates ranged from 70% to 100%. The mean meal volume was 0.1 µL per mosquito and mean body weight was 1.427 mg. The estimated LC₅₀ and LC₉₅ were 0.00029 mg/mL (95% CI: 0.00022–0.00037) and 0.00405 mg/mL (95% CI: 0.00236–0.00696), respectively. The corresponding amounts were 0.027 ng/mosquito and 0.391 ng/mosquito, yielding LD₅₀ and LD₉₅ values of 0.019 ng/mg and 0.274 ng/mg, respectively. These findings provide laboratory-based evidence of oral toxicity of dinotefuran against adult Aedes aegypti and support further investigation of dinotefuran containing sugar-based toxic bait formulations under future experimental conditions.

Article.Title: Application study of a water conducting fracture zone height prediction model based on bp neural network optimized by genetic algorithme
Article.Authors: Ling C.; Zhao Y.; Cao B.; Gao S.; Tai Z.
Article.Abstract: It is important to accurately predict the height of the water conducting fracture zone (WCFZ) for the production safety of coal mines and ecological environmental protection. Through the field measurement data of WCFZ at working face in Shendong and neighboring mines. The correlation degree between the working face length, mining height, mining depth, coal seam dip angle, mining speed, hard rock proportionality coefficient and the height of WCFZ was analyzed by using gray relationship analysis theory. The BP neural network model optimized by genetic algorithm was trained, and the predicted WCFZ values of empirical formula, GA-BP and BP neural network model were compared with the actual measured values of WCFZ in the mine area. The comparison analysis showed that the GA-BP neural network model had the smallest error of 7.78% in the prediction value. Therefore, the GA-BP neural network model has sufficient prediction accuracy and generalizability and can be applied to study the WCFZ in the Shendong mine area.

Article.Title: Uncovering novel sources for Karnal bunt resistance in bread wheat using multi-environment phenotyping
Article.Authors: Aggarwal R.; Kumar S.; Tanwar V.; Nair R.; Kamboj D.; Singh V.; Kashyap P.; Srivastava P.; Bala R.; Saini J.; Kashyap S.; Singh R.; Tiwari R.
Article.Abstract: Karnal bunt caused by Tilletia indica remains a significant constraint to global wheat trade due to its detrimental impact on grain quality. Developing and deploying resistant cultivars is the most effective and sustainable management strategy, given the impracticality of large-scale chemical control and the limited efficacy of cultural practices. Two hundred fifty-nine diverse wheat genotypes, including genetic stocks, released varieties, advanced breeding lines, and exotic introductions, were evaluated for resistance to Karnal bunt under artificial inoculation in nine environments over two crop years (2022–23 and 2023–24). Syringe inoculation method was employed, and genotypes were classified into five resistance categories based on Coefficient of Infection (CI) values. CI ranged from 0.0% (highly resistant) to over 58% (highly susceptible). Significant variation was observed among genotypes and locations, highlighting genetic variability and strong influence of environmental factors on disease development. Across years, a consistent trend highlighted the importance of phenotyping in understanding the potential stability of resistance under different conditions. A core set of 28 stable resistant lines with an average CI below 1.0 was identified, including three genotypes TAB368.25//BUL//TURAACO, MRNG/BUC’S’CLD’S’PLN’S’X12, and HD29 that consistently showed complete resistance across all environments. The predominance of genetic stocks in this core set reinforces their critical role as reservoirs of durable resistance. These promising genotypes hold strong potential for incorporation into breeding programs to develop Karnal bunt-resistant wheat cultivars, thereby contributing to sustainable disease management and safeguarding wheat production and trade.

Article.Title: Studying and investigating the feasibility of utilizing buried condensers in steam power plants
Article.Authors: Haloui I.; Alromithy F.; Chaudhary S.; Umamaheshwer Rao A.; Mann V.; Bains P.; Singh R.; Jiriees A.
Article.Abstract: Conventional steam power plants reject a substantial fraction of their thermal energy through condenser systems, while this low-grade waste heat remains largely unutilized. This study proposes and evaluates a novel integrated concept in which buried condenser pipelines simultaneously function as a condenser cooling system and a seasonal thermal energy storage (STES) medium by storing rejected heat within the surrounding soil for subsequent winter recovery. A transient three-dimensional numerical model based on the finite-volume method was developed and implemented in ANSYS Fluent to simulate coupled heat transfer between condenser discharge pipes and the surrounding ground under realistic operating conditions of the 370 MW Tabriz steam power plant. The model incorporates actual plant operating data, local soil thermophysical properties, and practical engineering constraints, including burial depth, pipe diameter, and pipe spacing. Numerical predictions were validated against established analytical solutions and published benchmark studies, demonstrating good agreement with relative errors below 4.2%. The simulations indicate that a burial depth of 1 m, a pipe diameter of 250 mm, and a minimum pipe spacing of 3 m provide the most favorable compromise between heat transfer efficiency and thermal interference. The surrounding soil progressively accumulates thermal energy during prolonged operation, creating a stable underground thermal reservoir capable of supplying useful heat during colder seasons. The results further demonstrate that appropriate geometric optimization significantly enhances heat recovery potential while maintaining practical installation requirements. The principal novelty of this work lies in introducing buried condenser pipelines as a dual-function infrastructure that combines condenser heat rejection with large-scale seasonal thermal energy storage, rather than treating underground piping solely as a cooling mechanism. Unlike previous investigations that focused primarily on underground heat exchangers or geothermal applications, the present study develops a practical engineering framework specifically for recovering waste heat from steam power plant condensers and integrating it with future district-heating and agricultural heating systems. The proposed methodology provides a scalable design framework for improving overall power-plant energy utilization, reducing thermal pollution, and facilitating the integration of waste-heat recovery technologies into sustainable energy systems. The findings establish a foundation for future techno-economic optimization, hybrid renewable energy integration, and large-scale seasonal heat storage applications in thermal power plants operating under similar climatic conditions.

Article.Title: Pannonictis pliocaenica (Mustelidae, Carnivora) from the Early Pleistocene of Crimea (Taurida Cave)
Article.Authors: Lopatin A.; Gimranov D.; Zakharov D.; Lavrov A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A large mustelid Pannonictis pliocaenica Kormos, 1931 (Ictonychinae, Mustelidae) is described from the Early Pleistocene Taurida Cave in central Crimea. The material includes a complete hemimandible and four isolated teeth. Detailed morphological comparison and morphometric analysis indicate closest similarity of the Taurida finding to P. pliocaenica , supporting its attribution to this species. Although Pannonictis represents the most widespread member of Lyncodontini in the Plio-Pleistocene of Eurasia, its records in Eastern Europe and Western Asia remain scarce and are currently restricted to only a few localities. The discovery of P. pliocaenica in Taurida Cave significantly expands the known eastern range of the species during the Late Villafranchian and contributes to the understanding of the Early Pleistocene carnivore guild of Crimea. Given the frequent association of Pannonictis with riparian palaeoenvironments, the Taurida material also has palaeoecological implications, supporting the presence of water-influenced habitats in the region during the Late Villafranchian and complementing existing fossil evidence from the locality.

Article.Title: Nano-chelated nitrogen improves in vitro shoot growth of potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) as a novel nitrogen source
Article.Authors: Karimpour S.; Noshadi A.; Kalanaky S.; Burgos L.; Nazaran M.
Article.Abstract: Efficient nitrogen management is essential for sustainable plant production and environmental protection, and nano-based nitrogen fertilizers may provide an alternative approach to improve nitrogen-use efficiency and reduce nitrogen losses. We evaluated nano-chelated nitrogen (NCN) across a 2.6–20.77 mM range for the growth of Solanum tuberosum L. cv. Agria one-node cuttings under in vitro conditions, using 20.6 mM NH₄NO₃ (equivalent to 41.2 mM total nitrogen) as a control. NCN was synthesized via a nano-chelation strategy forming a crystalline architecture in which nitrogen is hypothesized to be stabilized through multidentate coordination within layered structures. Dose–response optimization using Differential Evolution identified an optimal NCN concentration (~ 5.5 mM), which was subsequently compared with the control treatment. Despite an 86.6% reduction in nitrogen input, NCN-treated plantlets exhibited 72% greater shoot length, 71% greater internode elongation, and 24% greater fresh biomass than those grown on the standard NH₄NO₃-containing medium. Although SPAD index and shoot nitrogen content decreased, an increased chlorophyll a/b ratio suggested altered photosynthetic organization under reduced nitrogen availability. Root nitrogen levels remained comparable to controls, suggesting the maintenance of root nitrogen homeostasis. These findings suggest that NCN can enhance nitrogen-use efficiency and biomass production in vitro, highlighting its potential for resource-efficient nanobiotechnological micropropagation systems.

Article.Title: Three distinct uterine microbiome community types in healthy women and their interconnection with the vaginal microbiome
Article.Authors: Morańska K.; Englert-Golon M.; Durda-Masny M.; Grabowska M.; Pluskota M.; Doijad S.; Brouns R.; Siemers M.; Sadowski W.; Bocheńska M.; Sajdak S.; Dutilh B.; Szwed A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract There is no consensus on the composition of the uterine microbiome in healthy women. Bacteria in the uterine cavity engage in reciprocal interactions with endometrial cells and the immune system, thereby maintaining a microecological balance. Given the continuity of the genital tract, the vagina may serve as a potential source of uterine microbiota, which should be included in the investigation. This study aimed to examine the uterine microbiome of healthy women and to provide a reference for further studies. Additionaly, we collected vaginal samples from the same women to compare both niches and investigate the vagina as a potential bacterial source for the uterus. The study cohort consisted of 34 healthy women. We investigated microbiome presence in the uterus by 16S rRNA gene sequence detection. We obtained positive results in all samples analyzed, supporting the hypothesis that the uterus is not a sterile niche. To check bacterial composition, we proceeded with full-length 16S rRNA gene nanopore sequencing. Analysis revealed in the uterus a heterogeneous spectrum of microbial communities, clustering into three distinct community types alongside a single-subject outlier. Among these, Lactobacillus crispatus and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii emerged as the most prevalent taxa. Notably, uterine microbiomes demonstrated greater diversity than corresponding vaginal microbiomes, with overlapping bacterial taxa across both anatomical sites in most individuals, particularly in women with microbial profiles dominated by Lactobacillus species. The uterine microbiome in healthy women is heterogeneous, reflecting considerable inter-individual variability. The presence of shared bacterial taxa between the uterus and vagina within the same individual indicates a connected genital tract microbiome, suggesting potential microbial exchange. These findings highlight the importance of adopting a systemic perspective when investigating the etiology of gynecological pathologies. Future longitudinal studies are necessary to elucidate the selective pressures and dynamics shaping these microbial communities over time.

Article.Title: Continuous degradation representation learning for remaining useful life prediction
Article.Authors: Li W.; Ning R.; He S.; Li B.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of aero-engines is crucial for aviation safety and maintenance scheduling. Existing deep learning approaches, however, often learn fragmented or discontinuous degradation representations from multivariate sensor data, limiting their ability to accurately model degradation trajectories and estimate RUL. To address this issue, we propose CoDeR, a continuous degradation representation learning framework for aero-engine RUL prediction. CoDeR is designed to learn temporally coherent degradation representations that better capture the progressive degradation process. Specifically, a dual-axis coupled transformer encoder (DCTE) is developed to jointly model temporal dynamics and latent feature interactions along two complementary axes. In addition, we introduce a time-aware contrastive learning (TACL) module that incorporates temporal priors into contrastive learning. The module explicitly regulates relationships among samples at different degradation stages, thereby preserving degradation continuity in the feature space. By jointly optimizing degradation representation learning and RUL regression, CoDeR learns more discriminative and continuous degradation representations, leading to improved prediction accuracy. Experimental results on representative aero-engine benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed framework.

Article.Title: Structural lightweight design of bogie bolster based on surrogate models
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Dong Z.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: The bogie bolster is one of the key components of railway freight cars, and its lightweight design plays an important role in improving the transportation capacity of freight vehicles. However, the bolster features complex geometry, leading to high costs and long design cycles in structural development. In this paper, finite element analysis (FEA) is performed to evaluate the static strength and stiffness of the bolster. An optimization model is established taking the geometric dimensions of process holes as design variables, the minimum mass of the bolster as objective function, and allowable stress and deformation as constraint conditions. The Kriging surrogate model is constructed for mass, stress and deformation responses. Then expected improvement (EI) criterion is adopted for sample infilling to improve model prediction performance, and genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to solve the optimization problem. Global Sobol sensitivity analysis is further implemented to quantify the contribution of each design variable to structural responses. After obtaining the lightweight scheme, finite-element-based fatigue simulation and modal characteristic analysis are carried out for post-verification to assess the service reliability of the optimized bolster. Numerical results show that the optimized structure satisfies the static-strength and stiffness constraints in the optimization formulation. Post-verification demonstrates that the optimized structure also meets fatigue and modal-performance specifications. The total mass of the bogie bolster is reduced by 16.20 kg, achieving the lightweight target for heavy-duty freight bogie bolsters.

Article.Title: SCADA-based multiobjective calibration of hydraulic models for multi-fluid petroleum pipelines
Article.Authors: Mandel A.; Housh M.
Article.Abstract: Cross-country, multi-fluid pipeline networks are critical for petroleum transport, yet their operation remains challenging because of dynamic hydraulic conditions, fluid transitions, and limited diagnostic capability between periodic inspections. This study presents a SCADA-based calibration framework that transforms routine operational data into a well-calibrated, system-wide hydraulic model for multi-fluid petroleum pipelines. The framework is designed to support large-scale deployment and to provide a practical basis for improved operational analysis, predictive maintenance planning, and energy-efficient management of petroleum transportation infrastructure. Conventional calibration approaches are typically component-wise and rely on a single calibration criterion. Such approaches may fit local hydraulic behavior well but fail to ensure system-level consistency. In contrast, we develop a network-wide multiobjective optimization framework to estimate the hydraulic parameters of pipelines, pumps, and valves across different fluids directly from SCADA data. The key innovation is the simultaneous calibration of two distinct and non-intuitively conflicting performance metrics: nodal head accuracy, which governs operational safety and delivery reliability, and head loss accuracy, which governs the fidelity of local hydraulic behavior. Rather than collapsing the objectives into a single arbitrary objective, the proposed Pareto-front formulation systematically exposes the trade-off and supports principled selection of balanced calibration solutions according to operational priorities. Results from a real multi-fluid pipeline system show that traditional component-by-component calibration yields inferior solutions compared with the proposed Pareto-optimal, system-wide approach. At matched head loss accuracy, the proposed method reduces nodal head prediction error by 7.3–21.4% across the three fluids studied. These findings demonstrate that single-objective calibration can miss practically important system-level improvements and that the proposed framework offers a more informative and operationally relevant basis for hydraulic model calibration.

Article.Title: Failure analysis of axle box lower cover plate bolts considering bending damage
Article.Authors: Zou H.; Hou X.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the premature fatigue failure of axle box lower cover bolts in railway vehicles. Field measurements were conducted to obtain the axial tensile and bidirectional bending loads of the bolts during operation. The results showed that excessive bending was the dominant contributor to the premature failure. Bench tests further showed that the clearance between the axle box and guide column had increased from the designed 0.6 mm to approximately 1.1 mm, and the measured response corresponded to a bending moment of about 19 N·m. An angle-dependent cumulative damage method was used to synthesize the axial and bidirectional bending stresses around the bolt circumference. The maximum cumulative damage of the Grade 8.8 bolt occurred near 60°, with a value of approximately 6.0, consistent with the observed crack-initiation direction. Based on the bench and line tests, clearance restoration and a replacement configuration using Grade 10.9 bolts with an increased tightening torque were evaluated. Using the observed service life of the Grade 8.8 bolt as a reference, the fatigue life of the replacement configuration was predicted to increase from approximately 4 months to 44 months.

Article.Title: Protective role of carvacrol and carnosine against cadmium-induced liver injury via reducing oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis
Article.Authors: Zakaria G.; Shalaby S.; Abdel-Wahab N.; El-Demerdash A.; Abdelkhalek A.; El-Sherbini E.; El-Adl M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated the protective effects of carnosine and carvacrol against cadmium-induced hepatotoxicity and elucidated the associated cellular mechanisms in a rat model. Rats were allocated into five equal groups: control, Cd, Cd + CAR10, Cd + CRV50, and Cd + CAR10 + CRV50. While the control group remained untreated, the remaining four groups received intraperitoneal (IP) cadmium (2 mg/kg) three times weekly for a duration of four weeks, after that the 3rd, 4th, and 5th groups were treated with carnosine, carvacrol, or a combination of them (10 and 50 mg/kg, IP) once daily for 2 consecutive weeks. At the end, hepatic function was evaluated by measuring serum ALT, AST, and ALP levels, as well as the lipid profile, to determine the hepatoprotective efficacy of carnosine and carvacrol. Both agents significantly improved liver biochemical parameters and attenuated histopathological alterations. Moreover, they alleviated cadmium (Cd)-induced hepatic oxidative stress and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, as evidenced by the upregulation of key antioxidant defenses and the downregulation of ER stress–associated markers. Carnosine and carvacrol suppressed the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines while enhancing the expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, thereby contributing to the restoration of hepatic homeostasis. Carnosine and carvacrol induced apoptotic cascades by deregulating the pro-apoptotic Bax marker, concomitant with increased anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 mRNA expression. Furthermore, histopathological examination indicated severe hepatic tissue damage in Cd-treated rats, which was improved in the treated groups. This study demonstrated that carnosine and carvacrol exhibit significant antiapoptotic effects and hepatoprotective effects against Cd-induced hepatic toxicity.

Article.Title: A comparison of two contrast agents for dynamic contrast enhanced photoacoustic imaging in a preclinical model of breast cancer
Article.Authors: Murphy D.; Raikar S.; Liddicoat A.; Andres J.; Pagel M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dynamic contrast enhanced photoacoustic imaging (DCE PAI) can measure vascular perfusion in preclinical tumor models by monitoring the wash-in and wash-out of an exogenous contrast agent in tumor tissue. Indocyanine green (ICG) is often used for DCE PAI studies, but this agent is amphiphilic and non-specifically binds to proteins, complicating pharmacokinetics analyses of tumor vascular perfusion. A fluorescent agent, ZW800-1, may be repurposed for PAI. ZW800-1 is more hydrophilic than ICG and therefore may be a superior contrast agent for DCE PAI studies. Herein, we compared ZW800-1 and ICG during phantom studies of PA spectra, signal amplitude and photostability. ZW800-1 demonstrated narrower PA spectral features, stronger signal, and less dependence on proteins than ICG, while maintaining comparable photostability in protein-rich media. We then performed a DCE PAI study with an orthotopic 4T1 model of breast cancer before and after treatment with an acute vascular disrupting agent, combretastatin A4 phosphate. In vivo pharmacokinetics measurements of tumor vascular perfusion showed a greater dynamic range with ZW800-1 than with ICG, resulting in statistically significant decreases at each time point after vascular disruption treatment when using ZW800-1, but not with ICG. Therefore, ZW800-1 is a superior contrast agent for DCE PAI studies.

Article.Title: Preloaded and premoistened foundation that overlaps sabkha collapse treatment with construction evaluated by coupled infiltration and consolidation analysis
Article.Authors: Alsanabani N.; Al-Gahtani K.; Mahmoud A.; Akhtar S.
Article.Abstract: Conventional improvement methods applied to sabkha soil (collapse soil) are time-consuming, lengthening the project schedule. This paper presents a novel preliminary concept for a pre-loaded, pre-moistened shallow foundation engineered construction. A single-footing cast directly on dry sabkha incorporates a 3 × 3 array of vertical holes through which distilled water is introduced, advancing as a Green-Ampt wetting front and dissolving the evaporitic bonds before superstructure load application. The improvement phase overlaps temporally with foundation construction, thereby removing the improvement task from the critical path, as per the schedule overlap principle. A coupled boundary-value problem (Terzaghi consolidation) and a transient infiltration problem are developed to model consolidation and collapse settlement due to wetting, and they are verified against a plane-strain elastic stress analysis and a one-dimensional coupled hydro-mechanical Richards-BBM model. Results show that the innovative foundation mobilizes approximately 434 mm of collapse settlement within 12 days (reaching 509.6 mm total settlement including elastic deformation), accounting for close to 90% of the layer's 480 mm theoretical collapse potential (CP. H). Analytical (477 mm) and numerical BBM-LC (456 mm) models confirm near-complete collapse mobilization to superstructure placement. The schedule overlap reduces the pre-superstructure phase by 62% compared with traditional pre-wetting. This saving depends on the in-situ hydraulic conductivity. At 0.70 m sleeve spacing, the probability of completing wetting-collapse within the 14-day window is 0.62, so site-specific k v measurement and a pilot infiltration test are required.

Article.Title: Comparative antifungal activity of plant- and microbe-mediated silver nanoparticles against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense
Article.Authors: de la Paz Cruz J.; Mendoza N.; Chong P.; Galarza L.; Espinoza R.; Fonseca Y.; Debut A.; Vielma J.
Article.Abstract: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense , the causal agent of banana wilt, is a destructive soil-borne pathogen. Because no chemical treatment can eliminate F. oxysporum f. sp. cubense once it becomes established in soil, control relies on prevention, hygiene, and containment, underscoring the need for complementary, sustainable suppression tools. In this work, silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were synthesized via two eco-friendly routes: a plant-mediated method using Psidium guayaquilensis leaf extract and a microbe-mediated method using extracellular filtrate from Trichoderma spp. isolates; and their in vitro antifungal activity was compared against four F. oxysporum f. sp. cubense race 1 isolates. UV–Vis spectroscopy was used to guide synthesis parameter selection (AgNO₃ concentration, extract fraction, pH, time, temperature), and both preparations exhibited LSPR bands consistent with AgNP formation, with route-specific trends. FTIR FTIR identified organic functional groups associated with the respective biological matrices, and TEM revealed route-dependent morphology and particle-size distributions, with microbe-mediated AgNPs exhibiting a smaller characteristic ECD than plant-mediated AgNPs. Antifungal activity was evaluated in 96-well microdilution (24 h, 28 °C), revealing concentration-dependent inhibition for both nanoparticle types. Notably, microbe-mediated AgNPs consistently outperformed the plant-mediated counterpart, achieving lower IC 50 values across strains (≈ 22.18–27.87 mg L − 1 for microbe-mediated vs. ≈47.78–67.10 mg L −1 for plant-mediated AgNPs), with complete or near-complete growth suppression at the highest dose tested. These findings indicate that the synthesis route was associated with differences in nanoparticle characteristics and antifungal performance. Overall, microbe-mediated AgNPs emerge as a promising, sustainable candidate for F. oxysporum f. sp. cubense suppression, while the comparative framework presented here provides practical guidance for tailoring biogenic nanomaterials for plant disease management.

Article.Title: A fuzzy c-means based dual-layer flux-blending framework for high-resolution dam-break simulations
Article.Authors: Seyedashraf O.
Article.Abstract: Dam-break flow modelling involves a trade-off as resolving steep gradients requires high-order discretisations, yet these tend to generate spurious oscillations near discontinuities. Moreover, classical limiters used to suppress such oscillations rely largely on single-parameter algebraic indicator rules. This study replaces the procedure with a fuzzy c-means flux-blending framework for the finite-volume solution of the shallow water equations. To this end, an unsupervised classifier is trained on local hydraulic descriptors to assign each interface a shock-membership grade, and a second fuzzy inference layer converts that grade into a weight that blends a high-order flux with a dissipative low-order flux. The limiter-based transition is thereby replaced by a data-driven transition whose behaviour is determined by a measurable flow structure rather than a fixed algebraic rule. Accordingly, dissipation is graded continuously with the local flow structure. To validate the framework, one- and two-dimensional wet-bed and dry-bed dam-break benchmarks, including circular and partial-breach configurations, are considered. Against the exact Stoker and Ritter solutions, the scheme attains $$\:{L}_{1,h}$$ errors of 0.0664 and 0.0257 for the one-dimensional wet-bed and dry-bed cases, respectively, placing it between the first-order Rusanov scheme and the Minmod-TVD limiter. In the two-dimensional partial breach, the framework produces a qualitatively similar diffraction pattern to the Minmod-TVD scheme without inducing non-physical oscillations. For the configurations tested, graded and interpretable flux control provides a viable alternative to limiter-based transition.

Article.Title: Biomechanics-driven deep reinforcement learning improves Wushu skill acquisition in physical-education students over an eight-week controlled intervention
Article.Authors: Fu C.; Yin L.; Yang F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wushu instruction still rests on the coach’s eye and on repeated demonstration, an approach that resists quantification, delivers feedback only after a routine ends, and cannot retune difficulty for each learner. We therefore asked a deliberately narrow question: does a training paradigm in which biomechanically grounded features drive a reinforcement learning policy improve skill acquisition more than conventional coaching? Four directional hypotheses, stated before analysis, framed the test. Open-source inertial sensing was fused with markerless pose estimation to recover joint kinematics and inverse-dynamic torques, and a joint-angle-torque coupling scheme encoded those descriptors as a structured state tensor. A proximal-policy-optimization agent, driven by a composite reward and a dynamic difficulty-adjusting function, selected the training difficulty and the feedback shown to each learner. Sixty physical-education students completed an eight-week controlled intervention that compared the adaptive system with conventional coaching, with assessments at weeks 0, 4 and 8. Across sessions the instrumented measures proved reliable, with intraclass correlation coefficients from 0.82 to 0.91, and expert scoring showed good-to-excellent agreement both between raters, 0.91, and within raters, 0.93. Linear mixed-effects models with a random intercept for participant returned significant group-by-time interactions on all four skill dimensions: movement accuracy, $$F$$ (2, 116) = 18.42, $$p$$ < 0.001, partial $${\eta }^{2}$$ = 0.24; movement fluency, $$F$$ (2, 116) = 14.68, $$p$$ < 0.001, partial $${\eta }^{2}$$ = 0.20; force-control rationality, $$F$$ (2, 116) = 21.17, $$p$$ < 0.001, partial $${\eta }^{2}$$ = 0.27; and rhythmic stability, $$F$$ (2, 116) = 11.31, $$p$$ < 0.001, partial $${\eta }^{2}$$ = 0.16. The first three sit clearly above the conventional large-effect benchmark, whereas rhythmic stability only just clears it, and we read it accordingly. At the post-test the adaptive group exceeded the control group by 10.50 points on accuracy (95% CI 4.14 to 16.86, $$d$$ = 0.85) and by 11.60 points on force control (95% CI 5.06 to 18.14, $$d$$ = 0.92). Joint-angle variability also settled at a reduced plateau in the adaptive arm, and every within-participant change in an instrumented parameter exceeded the minimal detectable change of its own instrument. The convergence and transfer results point to the quality of the state encoding as a decisive design factor, although network depth itself was never varied, and the prediction that lower-baseline learners would gain most was not borne out. Because feedback modality and difficulty control were manipulated together, their separate contributions cannot be isolated in this design; the findings therefore support the packaged paradigm rather than either component on its own, and transfer to other coordination-intensive sports or to rehabilitation remains an untested conjecture. Trial registration : The trial was registered retrospectively rather than prospectively. Registration with a public clinical trial registry was applied for once data collection had ended, and the registration identifier will be supplied to the editorial office as soon as the registry record is issued; the absence of prospective registration is stated as a limitation in Section “Discussion”.

Article.Title: Data-driven, integrated control of Streptococcus suis substantially reduces mortality and antimicrobial use in a commercial swine herd
Article.Authors: Gombos L.; Búza L.; Szűr V.; Révész T.; Varga L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Streptococcus suis is a major cause of meningitis, septicemia, and arthritis in swine, and its control is complicated by antimicrobial resistance and the absence of broadly protective vaccines. We evaluated a data-driven, integrated control program in a 3-year prospective, single-site quality-improvement study using an interrupted time-series design in a PRRSV-free, 1,000-sow herd comprising approximately 126,000 liveborn piglets. The program combined clinical, pathological, and bacteriological surveillance, including capsular polysaccharide ( cps ) serotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing with performance and antimicrobial-use monitoring. Interventions included sow vaccination with a herd-specific autogenous bacterin (serotypes 2 and 1/2), strengthened internal biosecurity, structured colostrum management supported by Brix refractometry, and antimicrobial stewardship. Data were captured using an in-house animal-health monitoring and decision-support platform. Within 6 months of program implementation, S. suis -associated mortality had markedly declined, and pathological lesions detected at necropsy decreased by approximately 50%. Within 1 year, use of Category B antimicrobials, including ceftiofur and enrofloxacin, was eliminated. By the end of year 2, metaphylactic amoxicillin use had been discontinued, and florfenicol metaphylaxis had decreased by nearly 25%. Total antimicrobial use, expressed as active antimicrobial ingredient, in suckling and weaned piglets decreased by 98.2% (from 615.8 to 11.1 kg), S. suis -associated mortality declined by approximately 90%, post-weaning mortality decreased from 2% to < 1%, and mean weaning weight increased by 10% (from 6.8 to 7.5 kg). These findings demonstrate a strong temporal association between implementation of the integrated herd-health program and substantial reductions in S. suis -associated disease and antimicrobial use, including elimination of Category B antimicrobials. Because multiple interventions were implemented concurrently and no contemporaneous control herd was available, the observed improvements cannot be attributed to any single program component.

Article.Title: Prevalence and associated factors of COPD in primary care settings: a cross-sectional study in Chongqing, China
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Xu L.; Zhou X.; Li S.; Wang Q.; Fu J.; Zhou C.; Xie C.; Jiang J.; Tan B.; Xiong L.; Wang J.; Ren C.; Sun W.; Shu C.; Zhang W.; Gu Y.; He J.; Huang S.; Yue X.; Yu T.; Xia H.; Wang G.; He B.; You Z.
Article.Abstract: We aimed to estimate the population-standardized prevalence, absolute number of cases, and life-course factors associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in primary care settings of Chongqing, China. This cross-sectional study was conducted from February to October 2025 across 17 survey sites within 12 districts and counties in Chongqing. Permanent residents aged ≥ 20 years were recruited by convenience sampling at the participating facilities. Trained interviewers collected data on sociodemographics, lifestyle, environmental factors, and medical history using a standardized face-to-face questionnaire. Spirometry was performed according to the ATS/ERS 2019 technical standards. COPD was defined utilizing the GOLD 2025 guidelines (post-bronchodilator FEV 1 /FVC ratio < 0.70) alongside strictly verified medical records. The prevalence was standardized according to the age and sex distribution of the Chongqing population. Among the 4,914 adults aged ≥ 20 years, 1,371 met the case definition (crude prevalence 27.90%). After age - sex standardization to the 2020 Chongqing population structure, the standardized prevalence of COPD among adults aged ≥ 40 years was 26.76% (95% CI 25.44–28.12), which was significantly higher in men (36.93%, 95% CI 34.98–38.92) than in women (14.35%, 95% CI 12.83–16.03). GOLD staging was available for 1,020 of the 1,371 COPD cases (74.4%); Among the staged cases, the majority in both sexes were GOLD stage II (men 61.95% [503/812]; women 64.90% [135/208]). Multivariable analyses revealed that older age, male sex, lower education and income, underweight, and a history of tuberculosis were significantly associated with higher odds of COPD. Furthermore, adverse early-life factors and a family history of respiratory diseases were independently associated with the disease. Extrapolating the primary-care prevalence to the corresponding population strata suggests an estimated 3,933,463 adults aged ≥ 40 years in Chongqing have COPD (2,635,217 men and 1,298,246 women). The disease burden of COPD among adults attending primary healthcare facilities in Chongqing is substantial, with notable sex disparities in both prevalence and associated factors. The disease was associated with a constellation of factors across the life course in mutually adjusted analyses.

Article.Title: LNFformer: an enhanced transformer-based network for intelligent fault diagnosis
Article.Authors: Cai S.; Zhang H.; Mo Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis of rolling bearings under strong noise conditions remains challenging, as noise can significantly degrade feature quality. Although data-driven methods such as convolutional neural networks and Transformer-based models have shown strong feature extraction capabilities, their performance often deteriorates in low signal-to-noise ratio environments due to insufficient modeling of global correlations and loss of subtle fault-related information. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a dual-branch fusion diagnostic model, termed LNFformer. The model integrates a local normalization mapping (LNM) branch to preserve structural information and a Gramian-based correlation-enhanced representation (LNR) branch. A patch-based Transformer is employed to capture long-range dependencies, while an invertible neural network is introduced to retain detailed information. In addition, a bridging fusion module is designed to effectively integrate complementary features. Experiments on the CWRU and PU datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy and robustness compared with existing methods, particularly under strong noise conditions.

Article.Title: Variability of suspended sediment transport dynamics between seasons and flow pathways in a small agricultural catchment
Article.Authors: Thoma C.; Szeles B.; Krammer C.; Schmaltz E.; Blöschl G.; Strauss P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Suspended sediment dynamics in small agricultural catchments are shaped by the interaction of overland and subsurface flow processes, yet no event-scale, flow pathway-specific comparisons of seasonal discharge (Q)–suspended sediment concentration (SSC) relationships within a single catchment exist. This study addresses this gap by analysing Q–SSC relationships during 18 overland flow events (2014–2016) using high temporal resolution (1-min) discharge and turbidity data combined with event-based SSC monitoring at three different flow pathways within the Hydrological Open Air Laboratory (HOAL), Lower Austria: a partly tile-drained piped headwater inlet, an overland flow station, and the aggregated catchment outlet. The catchment is under annual crop rotation of mainly winter wheat, maize, barley, and oilseed rape. Seasonal Q–SSC relationships were fitted for each station, and event-based coefficients were compared. Results revealed clear scale effects between flow pathways and strong seasonal contrasts. SSC was highest in overland flow, lowest at the partly tile-drained headwater inlet, and in-between at the catchment outlet. All flow pathways showed increased SSC magnitude and variability in the growing season. Event-scale Q–SSC coefficients showed no systematic seasonal variation for the partly tile-drained piped headwater inlet, while both the overland flow and catchment outlet showed higher intercepts and flatter slopes in the growing season, reflecting higher baseline SSC during the growing season and sediment transport concentrated at higher discharges during the dormant season.

Article.Title: Global evolutionary dynamics of CLCuD-associated Begomoviruses reveal convergent adaptation and recombination hotspots in CP, Rep, and C4
Article.Authors: Iqbal Z.
Article.Abstract: Cotton leaf curl disease (CLCuD), a most destructive viral disease of cotton, is caused by at least six different begomoviruses (family Geminiviridae ). Among these, cotton leaf curl Multan virus (CLCuMuV), cotton leaf curl Kokhran virus (CLCuKoV), and cotton leaf curl Gezira virus (CLCuGeV) predominate. Despite extensive surveillance, prevalence, and genetic studies, the evolutionary mechanisms underlying their emergence, adaptation, and global dissemination remain poorly resolved. In this study, comprehensive analyses were conducted to infer evolutionary forces, including phylogeny, genetic diversity, selection pressures, and recombination patterns, shaping the emergence of three major cotton leaf curl disease (CLCuD)-associated begomoviruses (CAB) using their full-length global genomic datasets. In phylogeny, three CABs showed geographically associated clustering, revealing the long-distance dispersal, and further resolved into regional sub-clades, showing inter-regional (localized) mixing and robust evolutionary relationships. Codon-based selection analyses revealed the predominance of purifying selection across most genomic regions; nonetheless, CP, Rep, and C4 harbored strong signals of episodic diversifying- and positive selection. Recombination analysis deemed credible recombination breakpoints in CP and Rep as major recombination hubs. Population genetic analyses showed high haplotype- and low-to-high genetic diversity in CAB populations, revealing recent population expansion in CLCuKoV but more complex or prolonged evolutionary trajectories in CLCuMuV and CLCuGeV. These findings highlight that CAB evolution is being shaped by purifying selection, differential episodic diversification, and recombination, with CP, Rep, and C4 as key regions of evolutionary changes.
