Article.Title: An explainable AI framework using wearable IMU-based motion sensing for estimating and explaining motor skill improvement in school-based Baduanjin education
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhang Y.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: Estimation of individual skill improvement within specific school-based physical education units remains methodologically underdeveloped, with existing approaches typically lacking external validation and interpretability. Because the full model incorporates training-load features aggregated across the same temporal window as the outcome, it is epistemologically retrospective; readers should not interpret it as a prospectively deployable prediction tool. This study aimed at developing and externally validating an explainable machine learning ensemble to retrospectively explain and estimate standardized skill gain (Δz) in Baduanjin (eight-section brocade) qigong, a mandatory traditional martial arts skill in the Chinese national PE curriculum, among students from four schools ( n = 727). A stacking meta-learner composed of five candidate algorithms, including XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, LASSO, and MLP, was trained using biomechanical, psycho-cognitive, and semester-aggregated training-load features obtained from the development cohort (Schools A + B, n = 486) and then validated against two geographically independent but regionally situated cohorts (Schools C + D, n = 241). Because the training-load features were aggregated across the full 16-week semester, the model functions as a retrospective semester-level estimation framework rather than a prospective early-warning tool. The model yielded an external validation R² of 0.691 (95% CI: 0.661–0.718), with robust subgroup performance across gender, initial skill quartiles, and sport types. SHAP-based interpretability analysis identified exercise self-efficacy as the highest-ranking modifiable feature in model-derived importance, with its predictive contribution predominantly associated with the training-response component rather than baseline level. A baseline-only sensitivity model excluding semester-aggregated training-load variables retained moderate external validity (R² = 0.573), indicating that prospective application at semester onset is feasible in principle but at substantially reduced precision. These findings suggest that, within this dataset and model specification, psycho-cognitive features contributed more strongly to model estimations than biomechanical features.

Article.Title: Compound chamomile and lidocaine hydrochloride gel for postoperative sore throat after nasotracheal intubation: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Luo W.; Jiang L.; Zhang D.; Chen M.; Zhao L.; Lin J.; Liu L.; Ji Y.
Article.Abstract: The incidence of postoperative sore throat (POST) following nasotracheal intubation ranges from 21 to 65%. Despite possessing anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties, the efficacy of Compound Chamomile and Lidocaine Hydrochloride Gel (CCLH-Gel) in relieving POST remains unproven. We hypothesized that CCLH-Gel applied to the endotracheal tube would reduce the incidence and severity of POST compared with a placebo gel. In this prospective, single-center, assessor-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, superiority trial conducted at West China Hospital of Stomatology, Sichuan University (August 2025–April 2026), 140 patients undergoing bilateral temporomandibular joint (TMJ) surgery were randomly assigned to receive either CCLH-Gel ( n = 70) or plain gel without active ingredients (PL-Gel, n = 70) applied to the surface of the endotracheal tube for nasotracheal intubation. The gel was applied using a standardized two-step technique: first to the cuff and distal tip of the tube before insertion, and then under direct vision via video laryngoscopy after the tube was advanced through the nasal orifice into the hypopharynx. The primary outcome was the incidence of moderate-to-severe POST (Numerical Rating Scale [NRS] ≥ 4) at 3 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes, including successful intubation rate and postoperative outcomes, including POST, postoperative airway complications, epistaxis, dry throat, and hoarseness, were recorded within 24 h after surgery. A total of 140 patients completed follow-up and were included in the analysis. The incidence of moderate-to-severe sore throat (NRS ≥ 4) at 3 h postoperatively was significantly lower in the CCLH-Gel group than in the PL-Gel group (8/70 [11.4%] vs. 30/70 [42.9%]; absolute risk difference 31.4%, 95% CI 18.6%–44.3% relative risk [RR], 0.267; 95% CI 0.132–0.540, P < 0.0001;number needed to treat [NNT] ≈ 3.2). Furthermore, NRS scores for sore throat in the CCLH-Gel group were lower than those in the PL-Gel group at multiple time points (1, 2, 6, and 24 h postoperatively; all P < 0.001). Additionally, the overall incidence of post-extubation adverse events, including coughing, laryngospasm, and agitation, was significantly lower in the CCLH-Gel group compared to the PL-Gel group (10/70 [14.3%] vs. 24/70 [34.3%]; P < 0.05), with a particularly pronounced reduction in the incidence of coughing. CCLH-Gel applied to the endotracheal tube was associated with reduced incidence and severity of POST and fewer post-extubation airway adverse events after nasotracheal intubation, with no safety concerns observed. Multicenter trials are warranted to confirm its generalizability across diverse surgical populations. Clinical trial registration: The trial was registered on August 25, 2025, at Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500108092; https://www.chictr.org.cn ).

Article.Title: Progressive deformation and reinforcement control of a mountain slope under sequential excavation of multiple underground openings
Article.Authors: Yan F.; Li X.; Liao Z.; Pan Y.; Zheng Y.
Article.Abstract: Sequential excavation of multiple underground openings in steep slopes can reactivate previously disturbed ground and adversely affect tunnel support and slope stability. This study investigates disturbance-zone evolution and reinforcement effects in a mountain slope containing two tunnel anchorages and a main tunnel. A three-dimensional finite difference model was developed to simulate anchorage excavation followed by main tunnel excavation. The simulated displacement trends were generally consistent with the measured trends. Seven numerical cases were compared in terms of deformation, shear localization, primary-support safety, and global slope stability. The results indicate that anchorage excavation generated localized shear deformation and yielded zones, which underwent further deformation during main tunnel excavation, with increased connectivity of shear deformation and plastic yielding among the openings and toward the slope surface. Compared with conventional support, integrated tunnel reinforcement reduced the maximum system displacement from 94.2 to 40.3 mm (57.2%) and increased the minimum primary-support safety factor from 0.61 to 1.10. For the reinforcement arrangement examined, omitting prestressed bolts caused the greatest deterioration among the component-omission cases, increasing the peak displacement at tunnel monitoring points from approximately 39 to 46 mm and reducing the minimum support safety factor to 0.98. Adding the field-designed left- and right-side anti-slide pile configurations increased the global slope safety factor from 1.20 to 1.32 and 1.28, respectively. Among these configurations, the left-side piles more effectively reduced the continuity of the potential shear-deformation pathway toward the lower slope surface. These findings highlight the role of inherited excavation disturbance in subsequent slope deformation and the importance of coordinating tunnel reinforcement and pile placement with the spatial development of disturbance zones.

Article.Title: Hantavirus species detection from viral genome sequences using explainable artificial intelligence techniques
Article.Authors: Sorayaie Azar A.; Bagherzadeh Mohasefi A.; Mohammadi F.; Bagherzadeh Mohasefi J.; Ebrahimi A.; Knudtzen F.; Wiil U.
Article.Abstract: Hantaviruses are important zoonotic pathogens associated with severe human diseases, including hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome. The World Health Organization (WHO) has recognized the importance of strengthening hantavirus surveillance and early detection because of their public health impact. Nevertheless, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based approaches for hantavirus species identification from viral genome sequences remain largely unexplored. This study developed and evaluated an explainable AI-based approach for hantavirus species identification using viral genome sequence fragments representing six hantavirus species. A transformer-based genomic representation approach (DNABERT-2) was used to generate representations for various Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models. Sequence redundancy was quantified before model development, and performance was assessed using a 99%-sequence-identity group-aware partitioning strategy with five-fold group-aware cross-validation and an independent internal test set. Direct sequence-similarity auditing confirmed that no sequence pair with ≥ 99% global nucleotide identity crossed the development and test boundary. LightGBM achieved the highest mean group-aware cross-validation performance, with an Accuracy and weighted F1-Score of 99.51%, Cohen’s Kappa coefficient of 99.41%, and Brier Score of 0.19%. On the independent internal test set, LightGBM achieved an Accuracy and weighted F1-Score of 99.25%. SHAP analysis identified influential nucleotide sequence tokens contributing to LightGBM predictions, while a separate DNABERT-2 attention-based analysis identified highly attended nucleotide sequence patterns within the genomic encoder. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed approach as an auxiliary method for post-sequencing hantavirus species identification, genomic surveillance, and sequence-based research.

Article.Title: Serum uric acid and incident sepsis risk: sex-specific nonlinear associations modified by kidney function in the UK Biobank
Article.Authors: Hu Z.; Su Y.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Serum uric acid (SUA), the end product of purine metabolism, has opposing biological effects: it acts as an antioxidant at physiological concentrations but contributes to inflammation and endothelial dysfunction at elevated concentrations. Whether these effects translate into a concentration-dependent association with incident sepsis remains uncertain. We included 466,753 UK Biobank participants. Sex-specific associations were examined using restricted cubic splines, two-piecewise Cox regression models, and multivariable Cox models. A three-way interaction among sex, SUA, and eGFR was evaluated to assess whether baseline eGFR modified the SUA-sepsis association differently by sex; following a significant interaction, sex-specific SUA–eGFR interactions were examined separately in males and females. During a mean follow-up of 13.5 years, 17,249 incident sepsis cases occurred. Restricted cubic spline analyses revealed U-shaped associations between SUA and incident sepsis in both sexes, with sex-specific risk nadirs of 6.21 mg/dL (bootstrap 95% CI, 5.75–6.55) in males and 4.47 mg/dL (bootstrap 95% CI, 2.24–5.02) in females. In multivariable analyses, compared with the reference sextile, males in the lowest and highest SUA sextiles had higher risks (Q1: HR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.18–1.36; Q6: HR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.08–1.24), as did females (Q1: HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.01–1.21; Q6: HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02–1.21). The three-way interaction was significant ( P = 0.0065), indicating that eGFR modification differed by sex. The SUA–eGFR interaction was not significant in males ( P = 0.70) but was significant in females ( P = 1.7 × 10⁻⁵): the SUA–sepsis association was U-shaped at lower eGFR and became progressively monotonic at higher eGFR, with risk rising mainly with increasing SUA. This study provides novel evidence that baseline SUA is associated with incident sepsis in a nonlinear, sex-specific, and kidney function-dependent manner. In males, both low and high SUA concentrations were associated with higher sepsis risk. In females, the SUA–sepsis association was U-shaped at lower eGFR and became progressively monotonic at higher eGFR, with the modification by kidney function evident in females but not in males.

Article.Title: Multi-wavelength optical encoding enabled by excitation-dependent luminescence in rare-earth activated La2O3 phosphors
Article.Authors: Jagdale A.; Khode P.; Mishra G.; Shelke T.; Nikolay N.; Dhoble S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multifunctional luminous phosphors with controllable emission properties have been developed in response to the increasing demand for improved photonic and optical security systems. Here, urea was used as fuel in a simple combustion process to create Tm 3+ , Er 3+ , and Tm 3+ /Er 3+ activated La 2 O 3 phosphors. The development of a single-phase hexagonal lattice with improved crystallinity and decreased defect concentration was verified by structural studies. Rare-earth inclusion have affected the lattice strain, crystallite size, and defect density, while co-doping resulted in near-zero net strain and increased structural stability. While co-doped phosphors showed excitation-dependent color tunability through selective excitation and energy-transfer processes, optical investigations showed strong blue emission from Tm 3 ⁺ and high-purity green emission from Er 3 ⁺ (~ 98%). The multi-wavelength luminescence response is promising candidate for next-generation photonic security applications, encrypted barcode authentication, and sophisticated anti-counterfeiting.

Article.Title: Cognitively robust model using a deep learning framework for target recognition under suboptimal illumination in intelligent video surveillance system
Article.Authors: Bhat P.; Dharani A.; Krishna M.; Kumar S.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a cognitively robust deep learning framework for target recognition under suboptimal illumination, which is developed to enhance the recognition performance and stability of intelligent video surveillance systems. The proposed framework integrates three complementary modules: an Illumination-Adaptive Enhancement Module (IAEM) that performs LIME-based illumination estimation and correction followed by linear contrast adjustment; a Deep Recognition Backbone (DRB) based on transfer-learned CNNs for robust feature extraction; and a Cognitive Robustness Evaluator (CRE) that quantitatively assesses recognition stability across optimization and illumination conditions. Importantly, CRE operates exclusively as a post-training evaluation module and does not participate in model training, parameter optimization, loss computation, or inference. The framework was evaluated on the Extended Yale Face Database B and NIR Dataset for closed-set face recognition and on the BDD100K Night Subset for multi-class object detection. The proposed IAEM–DRB pipeline achieved classification accuracies of 99.81% and 99.62% on the two face-recognition datasets, respectively, while BDD100K performance was evaluated using detection-specific metrics. Under illumination levels ranging from 20 to 400 lx, recognition accuracy varied from 98.16% to 99.87%, with a Cognitive Robustness Index (R c ) of 0.981. Component-wise ablation experiments further examined the effects of input enhancement, backbone selection, and alternative enhancement methods. The results demonstrate high recognition accuracy and limited performance variation under the evaluated illumination conditions. The results demonstrate high recognition accuracy and limited performance variation under the evaluated illumination conditions, therefore, the framework showing its potential for illumination-robust video surveillance systems.

Article.Title: Optimal number of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy sessions for cervical low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions with high-risk HPV infection: a retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Wei Y.; He Z.; Liu J.; Qi W.; Qu Z.; Zhang M.; Chen F.; Li J.; Chen Y.; Tan H.; Guo H.; Chen H.; Wu A.; Hong Z.; Gu L.; Qiu L.
Article.Abstract: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection is the principal cause of cervical cancer, and although 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) has emerged as a minimally invasive treatment for cervical low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) with hrHPV infection, the optimal number of treatment sessions remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 326 women with histologically confirmed cervical LSIL and hrHPV infection from 11 medical centers in China between June 2019 and April 2023 to compare the effectiveness of three-session and six-session ALA-PDT regimens. A total of 268 women completed follow-up and were evaluated 3–6 months after treatment. Overall clinical remission, pathological remission, and hrHPV clearance rates were 77.24%, 91.42%, and 74.25%, respectively. Compared with the three-session regimen, the six-session regimen was associated with significantly higher clinical remission (82.61% vs. 71.54%, P = 0.041) and hrHPV clearance (84.06% vs. 63.85%, p < 0.001), whereas pathological remission did not differ significantly between groups. Subgroup analysis demonstrated that the six-session regimen was associated with significantly improved clinical remission, pathological remission, and hrHPV clearance in women with non-HPV16/18 infection, while no significant differences were observed among those with HPV16/18 infection. These findings suggest that an extended six-session ALA-PDT regimen may provide additional short-term benefit for selected patients with cervical LSIL and hrHPV infection, particularly those with non-HPV16/18 infection. Rather than routinely extending treatment for all patients, treatment duration should be individualized according to baseline characteristics and treatment response. Given the retrospective design and relatively short follow-up, prospective randomized studies with longer-term evaluation are warranted to determine the optimal ALA-PDT treatment strategy.

Article.Title: An improved binary arithmetic optimization algorithm with synchronous strong guidance for high-dimensional feature selection
Article.Authors: Li S.; Wang Y.; Wang J.; Jin S.; Xu Z.; Si Z.; Zhao C.
Article.Abstract: To address the high redundancy and excessive dimensional issues of high-dimensional data, an improved binary arithmetic optimization algorithm with synchronous strong guidance (SSG-BSIAOA) is proposed. Firstly, to increase the diversity of exploration and the richness of decision-making directions, a bidirectional probability selection strategy is proposed. Then, a trigonometric function factor strategy with eight trigonometric function factors are respectively used to replace the fixed constants so as to increase the algorithm diversity. To improve the insufficient optimization ability of the wrapper method, a synchronous strong guidance strategy based on mutual information and ReliefF dual indicators is proposed, which explores high-quality candidate features from multiple perspectives and breaks through the limitations of single-index evaluation. In the experimental part, the effectiveness of the bidirectional probability selection strategy and the trigonometric function factor strategy is verified through CEC-2022 benchmark functions, and it is proved that the sec-IAOA algorithm is the best variant. Then the performance of the SSG-BSIAOA is verified through 21 high-dimensional UCI datasets, proving the advantages of the proposed method in fitness, accuracy and dimension compression ability. Then, SSG-BSIAOA is applied to 18 micro-array datasets. By comparing with 9 algorithms, it is found that the SSG-BSIAOA has strong optimization ability, good stability, high accuracy and feature simplification. Finally, non-parametric statistical tests, including direct paired Wilcoxon signed-rank comparisons with Holm correction, were conducted to further assess the robustness of the observed performance differences.

Article.Title: Proteomic insights into the antifouling molecular responses of nature-inspired gallic and bile acid derivatives in Mytilus galloprovincialis
Article.Authors: Pereira S.; Turkina M.; Vasconcelos V.; Campos A.; Correia-da-Silva M.; Almeida J.
Article.Abstract: Nature-inspired compounds are increasingly recognized as promising sources of effective and environmentally safer antifouling (AF) agents. However, the development of new AF solutions under current regulatory frameworks requires a better understanding of the biological responses associated with their activity. Previous studies identified two synthetic derivatives of gallic and bile acids, 2-(3,4,5-trihydroxybenzamido)ethan-1-aminium bromide ( 1 ) and methyl deoxycholate ( 2 ), as potent inhibitors of Mytilus galloprovincialis larval settlement, a prominent biofouling species. Building on these findings, here we used an untargeted shotgun proteomics approach to explore the molecular responses of mussel plantigrades following exposure to compounds 1 and 2 . Proteomic analysis identified 3,214 and 2,091 proteins in plantigrades exposed to compounds 1 and 2 , respectively. Based on a predefined two-fold abundance-change threshold, 999 and 393 proteins, respectively, were identified as candidate abundance-shifted proteins. Exposure to both compounds was associated with abundance shifts in proteins containing von Willebrand factor (vWF) and epidermal growth factor (EGF)-like domains, which are also found in some mussel adhesive proteins. Functional enrichment analysis identified candidate abundance shifts associated with ciliary motility, vesicle transport pathways, and protein-processing pathways, while exposure to gallic acid derivative 1 was additionally associated with proteins involved in ATP-related metabolic processes. These patterns highlight cellular processes that may be associated with the response to compound exposure and provide potential hypotheses regarding processes linked to settlement inhibition. Although these findings require further validation through complementary targeted approaches, they provide valuable insights into the molecular processes associated with exposure to compounds 1 and 2 and reveal candidate pathways that may contribute to their settlement-inhibitory activity. Overall, this study expands the molecular understanding of AF responses in mussel plantigrades and strengthens the rationale for further developing these nature-inspired derivatives as promising candidates for safer and more environmentally compatible biofouling control.

Article.Title: Hybrid stacked bidirectional deep learning with attention based air pollution prediction for environmental sustainability
Article.Authors: Wei Z.; Amalraj P.
Article.Abstract: Environmental sustainability for air pollution monitoring necessitates utilization of advanced technologies like internet of things (IoT) devices and Artificial Intelligence (AI) AI to track air quality in real-time, controlling policy and measures to reduce to mitigate pollution for ensuring long-term environmental health. This mechanism aids sustainable development by safeguarding general public, combating climate change and establishing more flexible communities. Hence pollutant level monitoring is of paramount significance to maintain the pollutant concentrations under control. Nevertheless, pollutant concentration monitoring is not easy as it necessitates installing monitoring stations to obtain pertinent pollutant data that comes with high installation and maintenance costs. In this research, an attempt has been made to simulate the concentrations at three districts in Dhaka, Bangladesh using Deep Learning (DL) methods by applying Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention Mechanism (HSBi-LSTMA) method for environmental sustainability. An efficient model specifically tailored for encoding and generating multi-class imbalance results using Label Encoded Synthetic Edited Nearest Neighbor-based pre-processing for different air pollution concentration features provided as input is introduced. Next, Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory with Attention Mechanism first used attention mechanism to select the most influential features of the original air pollution concentration features and then used Hybrid Stacked Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory to generate the classified results for air pollution prediction. Extensive experiments were conducted on Air Pollution Monitoring Generated Using IoT dataset, comparing the HSBi-LSTMA method with two existing methods. The results demonstrate that the HSBi-LSTMA method significantly improves the air pollution prediction accuracy by 25% and reduces the mean absolute error by 46% as compared to the existing methods. With this the HSBi-LSTMA method represents a notable evolution in advancing environmental sustainability.

Article.Title: Allele-specific GNB3 modulation of APOE ε4 memory effects
Article.Authors: Xiao L.; Su Y.; Lin C.; Hsu H.; Hsueh P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Modern environmental improvements have extended average lifespan, leading to increased prevalence of neurodegenerative diseases such as dementia. While memory decline is a natural physiological process of aging, numerous studies have demonstrated that certain genotypes increase the risk of cognitive decline and dementia. The apolipoprotein E ( APOE ) ε4 allele is a well-established risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), the primary cause of dementia. APOE ε4 carriers not only have significantly elevated AD risk but also exhibit poorer cognitive performance and episodic memory decline. However, APOE ε4 alone inadequately predicts AD; its predictive power is limited by incomplete penetrance and polygenic interactions. Genome-wide association studies identify guanine nucleotide-binding protein beta polypeptide 3 ( GNB3 ), a G-protein β subunit hub in APOE ε4-specific co-expression networks, but evidence linking GNB3 C825T to cognition or its interaction with APOE ε4 remains absent. In this study, we genotyped APOE and GNB3 C825T (rs5443) in 369 cognitively healthy adults at a healthy aging exhibition in Taiwan and assessed short-term memory performance. APOE ε4 carriers showed poorer short-term memory performance compared with non-carriers. While GNB3 genotype alone was not associated with memory performance, subgroup analyses suggested a trend toward poorer performance among APOE ε4 carriers with the GNB3 T allele (OR = 2.08, p = 0.08). However, formal interaction analysis did not demonstrate a statistically significant interaction effect. These findings suggest a potential association between APOE ε4 and short-term memory performance and indicate that GNB3 genotype may influence this relationship.

Article.Title: A comparative study of dual organelle pH tracker, red-blue and red-green sensors and its applications in cancer cells studies
Article.Authors: Akshita N/A.; Tiwari G.; Goyal R.; Javed S.; Mishra S.; Singh S.; Roy P.; Kumar R.; Srivastava P.; Singh V.; Genger U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A systematic study on structurally similar, spectrally distinguishable dual-mode pH sensors ( 1 ) with red–blue and ( 2 ) with red–green emission is presented covering optical spectroscopic measurements in solution and in HeLa cells and their sensing performance is compared. Both sensors, which contain a piperazine unit that targets organelles such as lysosomes and mitochondria, exhibit different colors in acidic and neutral media, and rely on specific photophysical mechanisms for acidic pH sensing—namely photo-induced electron transfer (PET), intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), and fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)—for acidic pH sensing. As determined from their emission and excitation spectra, dual-mode sensors 1 and 2 exhibit a broad range of p K a values, including four different p K a for 2 calculated by the ratiometric emission intensities in the neutral to acidic pH range. A comparison of the sensing behavior of these novel sensor molecules with Mito and Lysotracker dyes highlight their significant application potential, as the fluorescence of one fluorophore confirms the sensor’s presence within cells, while the other reflects the pH of the cellular environment.

Article.Title: Broadband low-frequency energy harvesting using graded metamaterial piezoelectric
Article.Authors: Kouritem S.; Bashmal S.; Alshaqaq M.
Article.Abstract: This study presents the numerical design and optimization of a graded piezoelectric metamaterial for low-frequency and broadband piezoelectric energy harvesting applications. The proposed metamaterial structure consists of an aluminum host beam integrated with twenty local resonators, each comprising a steel core with an attached PZT-5H patch. The harvested power from surrounding wasted energy is utilized to power sensors in structural health monitoring applications. The design is numerically investigated using the Finite Element Method (FEM) in COMSOL, and the results are validated with experimental results from the literature. Several configurations are symmetrically investigated: the conventional periodic arrangement, assembled beams in the middle, complete graded resonators, cavity-enhanced complete graded configurations, and arrangements with additional piezoelectric patches on both the host and the resonators. The optimized configuration achieves a broadband frequency response of 0–400 Hz and a maximum harvested power of 0.42 mW, representing a 60-fold enhancement compared to the conventional design and a 22-fold improvement over fully graded configurations.

Article.Title: An assessment of migraine knowledge and associated factors among the Jordanian public
Article.Authors: Al-Omari A.; Rabayaa M.; Alshoh A.; AL-Kharabsheh H.; Alarman M.
Article.Abstract: Migraine is a prevalent, disabling neurological disorder with substantial socioeconomic burden, yet it remains under-recognized and underdiagnosed globally, particularly in the Arab world, due to limited public awareness of its clinical features and management. This study aimed to assess public migraine knowledge, perceptions, prevalence and their sociodemographic correlates among the general population in Jordan. A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based survey was conducted between February and June 2026 among adult Jordanians. The questionnaire assessed sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics, perceptions of migraine causes, complications, treatment, and general knowledge. Descriptive statistics summarized participant characteristics, perceptions, and knowledge scores. Associations with knowledge scores were examined using independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and Pearson correlation, while chi-square tests assessed factors associated with migraine diagnosis. Multiple linear and binary logistic regression identified sociodemographic variables independently associated with knowledge scores and migraine diagnosis, respectively. Among a total of 463 participants with a mean age of 31.4 ± 12.6 years, 15.1% reported a physician-diagnosed migraine and 34.3% reported a family history. Many participants were unaware of migraine causes (37.6%), complications (30.9%), or treatment (27.4%), and most correctly recognised that young individuals are predominantly affected (86%). The mean knowledge score was 8.34 ± 1.96 out of 12. Female gender, personal history of migraine, and a medical educational background were independently associated with higher knowledge scores (all p < 0.05), together explaining 13.1% of the variance in scores. Female gender (odds ratio 3.08, 95% CI 1.46–6.50) and family history of migraine (odds ratio 4.58, 95% CI 2.61–8.03) were independently associated with migraine diagnosis. Migraine prevalence in Jordan appeared consistent with global estimates, though lower than most regional reports. Public knowledge of migraine in Jordan was moderate, scoring higher than some regional levels, yet notable gaps persisted in awareness of its causes, complications, and treatment. Knowledge was shaped mainly by personal and educational exposure rather than demographic factors. At the same time, female gender and family history were strongly associated with migraine diagnosis, highlighting the need for targeted public health education to improve migraine literacy and reduce diagnostic delay in Jordan and similar settings, and to support the good health and well-being of patients.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: migraine; associated factors; Jordanian population

Article.Title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for predicting bacterial meningitis in preterm infants with late-onset sepsis
Article.Authors: Lu N.; Lang Y.; Shen L.; Cai N.
Article.Abstract: Late-onset sepsis (LOS) is a common and severe condition in preterm infants and may progress to bacterial meningitis (BM), which is associated with high mortality and adverse neurological outcomes. Cerebrospinal fluid examination relies on LP, an invasive procedure that can be challenging in preterm infants. Therefore, an early and practical tool for identifying infants at high risk of BM is needed. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an exploratory nomogram for estimating the risk of BM among preterm infants with LOS who underwent LP. This retrospective single-center study included 275 preterm infants with LOS who underwent LP after LOS onset, including 53 infants with BM and 222 without BM. Candidate predictors were derived from maternal, neonatal, clinical, and laboratory variables. Univariable analysis and univariable logistic regression were initially performed for variable screening. Penalized regression methods, including LASSO, Elastic Net, and Ridge regression, were compared, and LASSO regression was used for predictor selection. Predictors with non-zero coefficients at the lambda.1se value were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to construct the nomogram. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, and complete-pipeline bootstrap internal validation. Five predictors were retained in the final model: gestational hypertension, maternal age, gestational age, time from initial symptom onset to initiation of antibiotic therapy, and albumin. Gestational hypertension (OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.23–5.94, P = 0.013), maternal age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.02–1.17, P = 0.008), and time from initial symptom onset to initiation of antibiotic therapy (OR 1.04 per hour, 95% CI 1.02–1.06, P < 0.001) were positively associated with BM, whereas gestational age (OR 0.85 per 7-day increase, 95% CI 0.75–0.97, P = 0.019) and albumin (OR 0.90 per 1-g/L increase, 95% CI 0.84–0.97, P = 0.007) were inversely associated with BM. The apparent AUC was 0.805 (95% CI 0.75–0.86). After complete-pipeline bootstrap validation, the optimism-corrected C-index was 0.739 (95% CI 0.71–0.84) and the calibration slope was 0.734. We developed and internally validated a nomogram for estimating the risk of BM among preterm infants with LOS who underwent LP. The model retained moderate discrimination after optimism correction but showed evidence of overfitting. It may support preliminary risk stratification before definitive CSF results are available; however, it should not be used as a stand-alone tool to determine the need for LP or to provide definitive individual risk estimates. Prospective external validation and potential recalibration in a broader, consecutively enrolled LOS population are required before clinical implementation.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: bacterial meningitis; late-onset sepsis; preterm infants; nomogram; risk prediction
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health > Neonatal and Maternal Infections; Immunology and Microbiology > Microbiology > Bacterial Infections and Vaccines; Medicine > Epidemiology > Sepsis Diagnosis and Treatment

Article.Title: Vitamin D status and lower urinary tract symptoms in children: Findings from a prospective comparative study
Article.Authors: Çetin B.; Şahinler E.; Selvi İ.; Ercan G.; Eker P.; Dönmez M.; Sinanoğlu O.
Article.Abstract: Vitamin D has been suggested to influence bladder function, but evidence in children remains limited and inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate serum vitamin D levels in children with lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) and healthy controls and to investigate whether vitamin D was associated with LUTS severity and bladder diary parameters. A total of 244 children were included, comprising 136 children with LUTS and 108 controls. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations and vitamin D categories were compared between groups. Associations between vitamin D and symptom severity or bladder diary measures were evaluated within the LUTS group. Logistic regression models assessed the association between vitamin D and LUTS, with adjustment for age and sex and, in an expanded model, for age, sex, raw body mass index (BMI), and season. An age-restricted analysis of children aged 5–8 years was also performed. Median serum vitamin D concentrations were 17.15 ng/mL in the LUTS group and 16.60 ng/mL in controls ( p = 0.150), with no significant difference in vitamin D category distributions ( p = 0.277). In the unadjusted analysis, higher vitamin D was associated with LUTS (OR 1.217 per 5-ng/mL increase, 95% CI 1.012–1.464; p = 0.037); however, this association was attenuated after adjustment for age and sex (OR 1.084, 95% CI 0.891–1.318; p = 0.421). In the expanded model adjusted for age, sex, raw BMI, and season, vitamin D was not independently associated with LUTS (OR 0.971, 95% CI 0.754–1.251; p = 0.821). The age-restricted model yielded a similar result (OR 0.812, 95% CI 0.609–1.074; p = 0.144). Within the LUTS group, vitamin D showed no significant association with DVISS score, bladder capacity measures, wet-night frequency, or voiding frequency after correction for multiple comparisons. An exploratory comparison showed higher vitamin D with ≥ 8 versus ≤ 7 voids/day (18.56 vs. 17.00 ng/mL; unadjusted p = 0.037), but it was not multiplicity-adjusted and was not supported by corrected analyses. Serum vitamin D concentration was not independently associated with pediatric LUTS, symptom severity, or bladder diary parameters. Although an association was observed in the unadjusted analysis, it disappeared after adjustment for relevant covariates and was not supported by age-restricted or sensitivity analyses. These findings do not support an independent relationship between vitamin D status and LUTS in this cohort.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: vitamin D status; lower urinary tract symptoms; children; vitamin D deficiency; pediatric urology

Article.Title: HAAF-RT-DETR: hybrid attention and high-resolution feature fusion based RT-DETR for kidney stone detection
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Ma X.; Ming W.; Lu X.; Gao H.
Article.Abstract: Accurate localization and detection of kidney stones in computed tomography (CT) images are important for computer-aided medical image analysis. However, accurate detection remains challenging due to the small size of stones, weak boundaries, and complex renal anatomical backgrounds. To address these issues, this work proposes HAAF-RT-DETR (Hybrid Attention and High-Resolution Feature Fusion Based RT-DETR) for kidney stone detection. HAAF-RT-DETR integrates hybrid attention mechanisms and high-resolution feature fusion strategies into the RT-DETR framework to enhance feature representation and improve small-object detection performance. Within this framework, the HGBlock-AssemFormer module is introduced to jointly model local convolutional feature aggregation and Transformer-based global dependencies, thereby strengthening high-level semantic representations. In addition, a Convolution–Attention Fusion Module (CAFM) is employed to further refine high-level feature representations and reduce background interference. Furthermore, a high-resolution P2 feature level is incorporated, extending the original three-scale pyramid (P3–P5) to a four-scale representation (P2–P5), enabling fine-grained spatial details to participate in the DETR-style unified decoding process. Experiments on stone-positive CT slices from TEZ_ROI_AUG and the Kidney Stone Dataset demonstrate improvements in mAP, Recall, and F1-score over the evaluated YOLO-based detectors and RT-DETR baseline.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: kidney stone detection; RT-DETR; object detection; hybrid attention mechanism; medical image analysis

Article.Title: Effects of within-season temporal aggregation of weather variables on performance and interpretability in rice yield machine learning models
Article.Authors: Lee N.; Jeong W.; Yang H.; Cho H.; Ju H.; Iizumi T.; Kim K.
Article.Abstract: While crop responses are inherently stage-dependent, machine learning yield models often rely on weather variables aggregated over the entire growing season. This study evaluates how within-season temporal aggregation of weather variables affects both predictive performance and interpretability in machine learning-based rice yield modeling. Using CYGMA (Crop Yield Growth Model with Assumptions on Climate and Socioeconomics)-simulated potential yield as a synthetic response variable, we minimized confounding effects from observational noise and management variability, enabling a clearer evaluation of the role of within-season weather aggregation. Daily weather variables were averaged over the rice growing period after dividing each season into multiple equal-length segments, and several machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated using temporally independent validation. Increasing within-season temporal resolution improved model performance up to a moderate level, after which gains diminished. Interpretation using SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and response diagnostics consistently indicated that yield sensitivity concentrates in specific windows of the season, with temperature-related effects emerging most strongly early in the season and humidity-related effects later. Finer temporal aggregation sharpened the identification of window-specific nonlinear and threshold-like responses that were obscured under coarse seasonal averages. Overall, moderate within-season aggregation provides a practical balance between predictive skill and mechanistic interpretability, supporting more reliable identification of phenology-relevant meteorological risks for climate-impact assessment and decision support.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: model interpretability; machine learning models; temporal aggregation; rice yield; meteorological parameters; crop yield prediction

Article.Title: Automated corneal endothelial cell detection and segmentation in specular microscopy images using Attention and Faster U-Net
Article.Authors: Doke A.; Palaniswamy S.
Article.Abstract: Monitoring the density of corneal endothelial cells (CECs) is important for assessing corneal health. Manual calculation is time consuming and prone to error, which drives the need for reliable automated methods. U-Net, a neural network for biomedical image analysis, has shown promising results in the automated detection of cells in healthy and good-quality corneas. The purpose of this study was to assess the performance of two deep learning models namely, Attention and Faster U-Net, on real-world CEC images of variable quality and differing ocular disease from the publicly available SREP-18-33533B dataset. The outcome measures were precision, recall of CEC detection, correctness of CEC density estimation and detection of ungradable images. A classical marker-controlled watershed approach was used for comparison. There was good agreement between the automated image analysis and manual annotation from Attention and Faster U-Net. R² derived from the regression was 0.95 for the Attention U-Net and 0.94 for the Faster U-Net. Recall of CEC was averaged to 0.65 for both models and precision averaged to 0.66 and 0.64 respectively. The marker-controlled watershed underperformed with an R² derived from regression was only 0.12. This framework provides a reproducible foundation for future clinical research in ophthalmology.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: corneal endothelial cells; specular microscopy; cell segmentation; attention mechanism; cell detection

Article.Title: Experimental infection of avian paramyxoviruses in chickens and mice
Article.Authors: Lee J.; Kim T.; Lee H.; Seo Y.; Kim J.; Song C.; Youk S.
Article.Abstract: Avian paramyxoviruses (APMVs) are being increasingly detected in wild birds, yet the pathogenic potential of novel species remains poorly defined. We characterized the molecular determinants and pathogenicity profiles of seven APMV strains. Sequence analyses identified conserved hemagglutinin-neuraminidase (HN) receptor-binding and V protein immune-modulatory motifs, whereas F cytoplasmic-tail motifs, P and W trafficking signals, and L methyltransferase motifs were strain-specific. In day-old chicks, all strains showed low-pathogenic phenotypes, but APMV-1 class II, a wild-bird-origin strain developed and commercialized as a Newcastle disease vaccine strain, exhibited broader tissue distribution, oral and cloacal shedding, lung cytokine induction, and hemagglutination inhibition (HI) seroconversion. Other APMVs showed restricted replication, characterized mainly by oropharyngeal shedding, limited lower respiratory tract involvement, and no detectable serum HI response. In BALB/c mice, viral RNA was detected predominantly in respiratory tissues; APMV-13 and APMV-14 were associated with mild body weight loss. Cytokine responses in the lung and spleen varied among APMVs, while HI seroconversion was detected in mice inoculated with APMV-1 class I, APMV-14, and APMV-16. These results highlight strain-specific infection profiles, with APMV-1 class II exhibiting greater adaptation to chickens, whereas the other tested APMVs caused subclinical infections and induced variable immune responses in mice.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: mice; chickens; avian paramyxovirus; experimental infection; interspecies transmission

Article.Title: German dairy cows expose heterogenous bovine meat and milk factor DNA repertoires in milk and reveal Rep expression in mammary tissue
Article.Authors: Duduyemi O.; Didier A.; Ernst C.; Gunst K.; Grewe I.; Hesse M.; Shukla G.; König M.; Siqin S.; Bund T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bovine Meat and Milk Factors (BMMFs) are plasmid-like DNA elements isolated from bovine blood and milk. Histological studies demonstrated increased expression of a BMMF-encoded protein (Rep) in colorectal cancer tissues, suggesting BMMFs as potential carcinogenic biomarkers. However, the limited BMMF DNA repertoire identified in cancer patients in the context of the high number of known sequences, and BMMF detection in non-bovine foods challenge the hypothesis that early-life meat and milk consumption might contribute to cancer. Therefore, we investigated BMMFs at individual cow level, with immunohistochemical detection of BMMF-Rep in mammary glands of 27 dairy cows and characterisation of BMMF DNA and Rep in milk from 18 cows via PCR and immunoblotting. BMMF Rep expression was detected in lactocytes or interstitial tissue in 59% of animals, albeit with limited spatial distribution. BMMF DNA was present in 16 of 18 individual milk samples, with 26 sequences identified comprising both animal-specific and shared BMMF repertoires. However, only one isolate showed 99% identity with a cancer-identified isolate. Three milk samples were BMMF Rep-positive. This study provides a first hint that bovine milk, although frequently containing BMMF DNA, might not be a major source of protein and DNA of BMMF types found in cancer patients.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: mammary gland; colorectal cancer biomarkers; dairy cattle

Article.Title: Symptom bother is associated with health-care-seeking beyond severity in Japanese men with lower urinary tract symptoms: a cross-sectional web survey
Article.Authors: Kawahara T.; Hashizume A.; Yamazaki M.; Takamoto D.; Ito H.; Takeshima T.; Kuroda S.; Hasumi H.; Uemura H.; Makiyama K.; Teranishi J.
Article.Abstract: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) are common and reduce quality of life, yet many affected men do not seek medical care. We examined how symptom severity and patient bother relate to health-care-seeking, the reasons for not seeking care, and willingness to pay (WTP) for symptom relief in Japanese men. In a cross-sectional web survey, 3999 community-dwelling Japanese men aged 40 years or older completed the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) and the Overactive Bladder Symptom Score (OABSS) and rated overall symptom bother on a 0–10 scale. The primary outcome was having visited a clinic. Independent predictors of clinic visit were assessed with multivariable binary logistic regression; reasons for non-attendance, awareness of treatability, and WTP were also summarized. Overall, 44.7% of men were symptomatic and 13.7% had visited a clinic (24.1% of symptomatic men). The clinic-visit rate rose with severity (5.7% mild, 21.2% moderate, 37.5% severe IPSS), with care-seeking rising steeply across the moderate-to-severe range (a graded, dose–response pattern rather than a discrete threshold). IPSS ≥ 8 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.05), bother ≥ 3 (aOR 2.76), age ≥ 65 years (aOR 1.97), and being married (aOR 1.44) were each independently associated with clinic visit, whereas household income, presence of children, and home ownership were not. Among symptomatic non-attenders (n = 1,358), the leading reasons were attributing symptoms to aging (44.3%) and the symptoms not being bothersome enough (19.4%); 45.3% were unaware that the symptoms are treatable. WTP rose with bother: the proportion willing to pay a non-zero amount was 36%, 72%, and 90% across the none, low, and high bother groups. In Japanese men with LUTS, care-seeking was associated with both symptom severity and, independently, patient bother, and the most frequently reported barriers were the belief that symptoms are part of aging and limited awareness of treatability. As a cross-sectional web-panel survey, these are associations rather than causal or population-level estimates.

Article.Title: Composite inflammatory indices and incident lung cancer risk in an exploratory statistical mediation analysis
Article.Authors: Chu Y.; Wang L.; Song Q.; Ruan C.
Article.Abstract: This study aims to assess the prospective associations between six composite inflammatory indices and incident lung cancer risk and to identify plasma metabolites that may statistically mediate the observed association. Based on the UK Biobank, we derived six composite inflammatory indices, including platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), platelet-to-albumin ratio (PAR), C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR), C-reactive protein-to-lymphocyte ratio (CLR), and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate their associations with incident lung cancer risk. Time-dependent ROC curves compared discriminative ability among the significant indices in clinical models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis tested the nonlinear relationship. A two-step screening and directionality filter procedure identified candidate mediators from 169 plasma metabolites, which were entered into an exploratory statistical mediation analysis. Among 416,656 participants, 4,105 developed lung cancer during follow-up. Increased PAR, CAR, CLR, and NLR were significantly associated with higher lung cancer risk across all three adjusted models. CAR showed the largest magnitude of association (HR = 1.289, 95% CI: 1.247—1.332 per 1-SD increment in Model 3). RCS analysis revealed a significant nonlinear association between CAR and lung cancer risk. The screening procedure identified 16 candidate mediators. Glycoprotein acetyls (GlycA) showed the largest statistical contribution (proportion mediated = 13.0%), while several lipid-related metabolites and fatty acid measures showed smaller contributions. Elevated baseline CAR was prospectively associated with a higher incidence of lung cancer. Several baseline metabolic biomarkers statistically accounted for a portion of this association; however, the findings are exploratory and may be influenced by residual confounding, reverse causation, and the concurrent measurement of exposure and mediators.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: mediation analysis; inflammation; lung cancer risk; inflammatory indices

Article.Title: Intelligent fault detection and classification in DC microgrids using MEMD and Deep Neural Decision Forests
Article.Authors: Abhisek A.; Biswal C.; Samanta I.; Sahoo B.; Rout P.; Panda G.; Jha S.
Article.Abstract: Fault detection and classification in the Distribution Generation (DG) integrated DC microgrid demands a very robust and efficient approach to handle many inherent issues and challenges related to zero crossing, low inertia factor, high variation in short-circuit current and different modes of operation. This paper presents a hybrid novel approach comprised of Multivariate Empirical Mode Decomposition (MEMD) for feature extraction from the non-stationary power signals and Deep Neural Decision Forests (DNDF) for classification for the correct decision. The reason for exploiting MEMD for fault detection and classification is that it enables the simultaneous decomposition of multiple related faulted power signals, ensuring mode alignment, preserving joint information, and facilitating direct comparison of their shared non-stationary and non-linear characteristics. On the other hand, the DNDF approach is exploited for microgrid fault classification because they combine deep learning’s powerful feature extraction with decision forests’ robust, interpretable, and noise-tolerant classification. The proposed approach is tested through extensive simulation under various normal and faulted operating conditions, even under varying fault resistances and operational uncertainties. MEMD decomposes multivariate microgrid signals, enabling the extraction of meaningful temporal features. Later, these features are used as input to a DNDF to categorize fault types. Extensive simulations on test DC microgrid configurations demonstrate that the integrated MEMD and Deep Learning (DL) strategy provides superior Accuracy, robustness, and resilience in comparison to conventional and other prominent techniques.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: fault classification; DC microgrid; fault detection; decision forest; multivariate empirical mode decomposition; deep neural network

Article.Title: Process-intensified continuous-flow synthesis of azaperone via a microreactor system
Article.Authors: Ghobadian A.; Taghizadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Azaperone is a butyrophenone-type neuroleptic agent widely utilized in veterinary medicine for its potent sedative and anti-aggressive properties. This study reports the development of a streamlined, process-intensified synthesis of azaperone utilizing a continuous-flow microreactor system. In the first step, bis(2-chloroethyl)amine was synthesized via the chlorination of the hydroxyl groups of diethanolamine using thionyl chloride, affording an excellent yield of 96%. Subsequently, 2-aminopyridine underwent alkylation with the synthesized bis(2-chloroethyl)amine in the presence of tetrabutylammonium bromide (TBAB) as a phase-transfer catalyst to produce 1-(pyridin-2-yl)piperazine in 75% yield. Finally, this key intermediate was alkylated with 4-chloro-1-(4-fluorophenyl)butan-1-one under solvent-free conditions to afford azaperone in 65% yield. The continuous-flow strategy successfully minimized reaction times and suppressed by-product formation compared to conventional batch methods.
Article.Topic: Innovative Microfluidic and Catalytic Techniques Innovation

Article.Title: Secure signal encoding and temporal feature extraction for multi class intrusion detection in smart grid environments
Article.Authors: Chandrakala D.; Raja S.; Sudha S.
Article.Abstract: To ensure the reliability, security and operational stability of smart grid environments, real-time monitoring of electrical data is necessary. It is especially crucial that proper anomaly detection becomes the key to detecting malicious events, preventing disruption of the service, and supporting secure energy transmission. Nonetheless, traditional intrusion detection systems are typically not able to represent long-range temporal relationships, signal variations arising behind secured communication links, and attack-specific relationships, which can result in slow or inaccurate detection. To overcome these weaknesses, this paper suggests a hybrid intrusion detection system called Dilation-Gated Multi-Scale Fusion Encoding-Hierarchical Shifted Window Attention Network-Quadratic Discriminative Capsule Network (DG-MFE + H-SWANet + QDC-Net). In the proposed setting, meter readings are protected in transit by a lightweight chaotic Advanced Encryption Standard-Recursive Diffusion Embedding (AES-RDE) scheme and are decrypted by the authorized grid gateway, so detection is carried out on the recovered measurement stream and not on ciphertext. Then, DG-MFE extracts multi-scale time features, H-SWANet captures local and cross-window contextual dependencies, and QDC-Net performs classification of multi-class intrusion based on confidence. The proposed model was tested on the Smart Grid Real-Time Load Monitoring dataset, with intrusions injected into the measurements before encryption or into the ciphertext during transmission, covering false data injection, replay attack, stealth drift, binary tampering, and protocol corruption. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieved 98.32% accuracy, 98.72% precision, 98.93% recall, 98.82% F1-score, 97.67% Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), 99.08% specificity, 0.91% false acceptance rate (FAR), and 12.8 ms inference time, outperforming Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), ConvNeXt-1D, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Residual Attention Network-1D (RAN-1D), and Depthwise Separable Convolutional Neural Network (DSCNN) baselines. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective task-specific solution for multi-class intrusion detection under the configured secure-transmission smart-grid signal modeling and synthetic attack evaluation setup.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: temporal feature extraction; intrusion detection; smart grid security; multi-class classification; signal encoding
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Smart Grid Security and Resilience; Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Network Security and Intrusion Detection; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Electricity Theft Detection Techniques

Article.Title: Deep learning-assisted graphene-based THz metasurface for label-free and high-performance MCF-7 breast cancer cell sensing
Article.Authors: Zakeri H.; Moradi G.; Tavakoli A.
Article.Abstract: A triple-band graphene-based terahertz metasurface, integrated with a DL framework, is proposed for high-efficiency polarization conversion and label-free MCF-7 breast cancer cell detection. The unit cell, comprising concentric graphene elements and silver strips on an \(\mathrm {Al_2O_3}\) substrate with a silver ground plane, facilitates reflective-mode operation with polarization conversion ratios (PCR) exceeding 90% across three distinct operational bands. The finite-element method (FEM), finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique, and multiple-interference theory rigorously validate the physical mechanisms and electromagnetic responses, showing strong agreement. For biosensing applications, the metasurface leverages the distinct dielectric signatures of MCF-7 cells, inducing measurable resonance shifts at 1.48, 2.85, and 4.12 THz. The platform achieves a peak sensitivity of 0.866 THz/RIU and a figure of merit of 4.04 RIU \(^{-1}\) . To improve spectral analysis, we develop a one-dimensional convolutional neural network to predict PCR responses directly from THz spectral data. This model shows exceptional robustness, achieving an \(R^2\) of 0.972 even under 5% additive white Gaussian noise. By accurately resolving minute refractive-index variations associated with early-stage cellular-level oncogenic alterations, the proposed deep-learning-assisted biosensor offers a highly sensitive, non-contact, and non-destructive platform with significant potential for early-stage breast cancer screening.

Article.Title: Transmission path of blasting vibration in a cross-tunnel and PPV prediction of the full section of the existing tunnel
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Zhang Z.; Ren J.; Li P.; Du P.; Xu Y.; Liu Z.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: In cross-tunnel projects, excessive blasting-induced vibration may threaten the operational safety and structural stability of existing underground structures. Accurate prediction of tunnel blasting vibration intensity is essential for effective vibration control. Based on the Caomaoshan intersecting tunnel project of the Beijing–Zhangjiakou High-Speed Railway, this study combines field monitoring and numerical simulation to investigate blasting vibration propagation characteristics and PPV prediction approaches. First, the applicability of traditional PPV prediction models for the existing tunnel sidewalls is evaluated using field monitoring data. Subsequently, three-dimensional numerical simulations are conducted to reveal the PPV distribution mechanism from the perspective of stress wave propagation. To consider stress wave diffraction caused by the cavity formed during excavation of the new tunnel, the PPV prediction model for the full cross-section of the existing tunnel is modified by introducing a minimum diffraction distance ( R m ). The results indicate that diffraction of waves around the excavated cavity is a primary cause of non-uniform PPV distribution across the existing tunnel cross-section. Taking the USBM equation as an example, the modified model achieves coefficients of determination of 0.924, 0.971, and 0.949 when the new tunnel face approaches( L < 0 m), reaches( L = 0 m), and passes beyond( L > 0 m) the intersection, respectively, representing increases of 23.38%, 20.74%, and 6.33% compared with the original model. These findings demonstrate that introducing R m provides a more accurate representation of effective stress wave propagation paths considering cavity-induced diffraction, thereby improving PPV prediction across the existing tunnel cross-section under different relative positions of the blast source.

Article.Title: Multiscale computational modeling of photoacoustic generation from micrometer-size polymeric bead suspensions in liquid media
Article.Authors: Sfregola F.; Pizzi F.; Caragnano S.; De Palo R.; Volpe A.; Patimisco P.; Jofre L.
Article.Abstract: Photoacoustic sensing has emerged as a promising technique for detecting polymeric particles suspended in liquids through the conversion of absorbed optical energy into acoustic signals. Here, we present a multiscale computational study of the photoacoustic response of polystyrene (PS) beads suspended in water under pulsed optical excitation. The framework combines particle-resolved simulations of individual beads with point-particle descriptions of randomly distributed multi-particle suspensions. The results reveal a rapid acoustic transient followed by a residual pressure field persisting in the liquid. As particle concentration increases, the residual pressure level progressively rises and exhibits an approximately square-root dependence on the number of photoacoustic sources. The point-particle study further shows that the pressure response is closely related to the effective number of irradiated particles rather than to the nominal suspension concentration, while the induced particle motion remains negligible. Overall, the present results provide a physically grounded basis for interpreting photoacoustic signals from PS bead suspensions in water and support future developments of photoacoustic sensing strategies for applications ranging from microplastic detection in aqueous media to polymer-bead-based microfluidic and bioanalytical platforms.

Article.Title: A cross-sectional study assessing the information quality of refractive surgery for myopia videos on Douyin, Bilibili, and Kwai
Article.Authors: Lei Y.; Ma D.; Wang Y.; Lyu H.
Article.Abstract: Although short-video platforms have rapidly emerged as prominent channels for health communication, the quality and reliability of content regarding refractive surgery for myopia remain unevaluated. To address this research gap, 300 videos retrieved with the search term “refractive surgery for myopia” within a 48-hour window across Douyin, Bilibili, and Kwai were screened, and 264 eligible videos were included in the final analysis. Videos were classified by uploader identity, theme, and verification status. Two independent reviewers evaluated video quality using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), and JAMA benchmark criteria. Results showed that overall information quality was moderate, with platform-specific variations: Bilibili provided longer educational content, Douyin focused predominantly on patient experiences, and Kwai featured more surgical procedures. Quality scores varied significantly by uploader identity, and videos uploaded by ophthalmologists, institutional accounts, and Blue-V verified creators scored substantially higher than those uploaded by independent or unverified users. User engagement indicators showed only weak correlations with clinical quality scores. A key challenge and limitation is related to platform algorithm dynamics and the 48-hour sampling window, which primarily captured algorithmically promoted content rather than the overall quality of all available videos on each platform. Given that elective refractive surgery for myopia relies heavily on preoperative expectations, platforms should optimize recommendation mechanisms to better balance evidence-based professional content with highly engaging user narratives.

Article.Title: Molecular, agro-morphological, and phytochemical analysis of goldenrod (Solidago spp.) genotypes grown under two contrasting climates
Article.Authors: Parsafar S.; Eghlima G.; Mirjalili M.; Nejad Ebrahimi S.; Petty M.; Hadian J.
Article.Abstract: Solidago , belonging to the Asteraceae family, is used as an herbal medicine and possess diuretic, anti-microbial, cytotoxic, anti-inflammatory, gastroprotective and immunobiological properties. However, the extent to which genetic differences among wild and cultivated Solidago materials contribute to variation in agronomic performance and phytochemical quality under contrasting environmental conditions remains insufficiently understood. This study was conducted to analyze the genetic relationships of Iranian natural populations of S. virgaurea with cultivated varieties (three S. virgaurea and one S. canadensis varieties ) and evaluate their agro-morphological and phytochemical characteristics in field condition in two different climates (Tehran and Sari). Fourteen inter-simple sequence repeat (ISSR) primers were applied for DNA analysis and a total of 105 bands were amplified, out of which 103 bands were polymorphic (91.1%). The polymorphic information content (PIC) of the assessed markers varied between 0.21 for IS8 and 0.37 for IS4, yielding a mean value of 0.28. The ISSR-based clustering analysis revealed three principal clusters, with S. canadensis genotypes forming one cluster, the three cultivated S. virgaurea varieties comprising another, and the Iranian wild populations forming the third cluster. Considerable diversity was likewise observed in their agro-morphological traits and phytochemical profiles. Solidago cultivars and populations grown in Sari had higher plant height (137.2 cm), inflorescence length (78.1 cm), plant fresh weight (338.11 g plant − 1 ), plant dry weight (144.69 g plant − 1 ) and drug yield (366.86 g m − 1 ). However, higher total phenol content (26.07 vs. 18.25 mg GAE g − 1 DW) and leiocarposide content (8.96 mg g- 1 DW) was measured in plants cultivated in Tehran. Stepwise multiple regression analysis revealed polymorphic markers, exhibiting significant correlations to agro-morphological and phytochemical traits. Overall, the findings highlight substantial genetic, agro-morphological, and phytochemical diversity among the studied Solidago materials and provide useful information for the selection of promising genetic resources for cultivation and breeding programs.

Article.Title: Sexual function problems, sexual distress, and operationally defined female sexual dysfunction among women with infertility in southern Iran: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Azizi Kutenaee M.; Toghroli R.; Mohseni S.; Ezati Rad R.; Roozbeh N.; Taghvaei E.; Banaei M.
Article.Abstract: Infertility can negatively affect women’s sexual health. However, low sexual function and sexual distress are different concepts and should not be used interchangeably. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of low sexual function, sexual distress, and operationally defined female sexual dysfunction (FSD) among women with infertility in southern Iran, and to examine their associations with selected sociodemographic and infertility-related characteristics. In this cross-sectional study, 455 women attending an infertility center in Bandar Abbas, southern Iran, were recruited by simple random sampling from November 2023 to September 2024. Sexual function and sexual distress were assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) and the Female Sexual Distress Scale-Revised (FSDS-R), respectively. Low sexual function was defined as FSFI ≤ 26.55, sexual distress as FSDS- R ≥ 11, and operationally defined FSD as the concurrent presence of both conditions. Three separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for low sexual function, sexual distress, and FSD. The prevalence of low sexual function, sexual distress, and FSD was 92.1%, 33.8%, and 31.6%, respectively. In the revised multivariable models, longer infertility duration was associated with higher odds of sexual distress and FSD. Compared with an infertility duration of 1 to 5 years, a duration of 16 to 25 years was associated with higher, but imprecisely estimated, odds of sexual distress (adjusted OR = 3.14, 95% CI: 1.40 to 7.09; p = 0.006) and FSD (adjusted OR = 3.07, 95% CI: 1.36 to 6.91; p = 0.007). Moderate economic status was associated with lower odds of FSD than unfavorable economic status (adjusted OR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.35 to 0.91; p = 0.018). Estimates from the exploratory low-sexual-function model were less precise and should be interpreted cautiously because the outcome distribution was markedly imbalanced. Among women receiving infertility care in southern Iran, low sexual function was highly prevalent, whereas about one-third experienced sexual distress or met the combined criteria for FSD. Longer infertility duration was associated with higher odds of sexual distress and FSD. These findings support the importance of assessing both sexual function and sexual distress in infertility care, and of interpreting combined questionnaire-based definitions cautiously in the absence of a formal clinical diagnosis.

Article.Title: Federated learning with update level noise perturbation and blockchain audit logging for privacy-preserving healthcare ECG classification
Article.Authors: Manwal M.; Londhe G.; Purohit K.
Article.Abstract: We propose FedChainDP, a federated learning framework that combines update-level noise perturbation with blockchain audit logging for privacy-preserving collaborative ECG classification across multiple healthcare institutions. Healthcare institutions face a fundamental tension: deep learning models require large, diverse training datasets to achieve high diagnostic accuracy, yet strict privacy regulations such as HIPAA and GDPR restrict the sharing of raw patient data across organizational boundaries. FedChainDP resolves this tension by enabling hospitals to collaboratively train a shared CNN model without exchanging raw electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. Each hospital trains locally on its private data and shares only noise-perturbed model updates, to which Gaussian noise is added once per federated round; these updates are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before transmission and logged on an immutable blockchain with Merkle-tree integrity protection and smart-contract policy checks on the reported noise parameters. Because this round-level noise schedule does not satisfy the assumptions of the Rényi differential privacy (RDP) accountant, the accountant output for the main configuration (ε_nom = 7.84 at δ = 10⁻⁵) is reported only as a nominal indicator, and no formal (ε, δ)-differential privacy guarantee is claimed. We evaluate FedChainDP on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia dataset partitioned across 5 hospitals using Dirichlet-based non-IID distributions. Our CNN model achieves 98.91% ± 0.14% accuracy under federated learning with update-level noise injection (σ_mult = 1.1), compared to 98.81% ± 0.31% for centralized training and 98.57% ± 0.17% for federated learning without noise-based privacy protection. These accuracies were obtained under a beat-level random split performed after duplication-based class balancing, so duplicated minority-class beats and beats from the same patients can occur in both training and test sets; they therefore reflect performance within this resampled benchmark and do not establish generalization to independent unseen beats or patients. A comprehensive privacy-utility analysis across noise multiplier settings (σ_multiplier ∈ {1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 100}) demonstrates that classification accuracy remains above 98% across all evaluated noise levels. A black-box membership inference attack achieved 50.28% accuracy (near random guessing) against the noise-perturbed model; however, comparable near-chance accuracy was also obtained against the models trained without noise (49.16% centralized; 49.48% federated), so this result neither isolates a benefit of the noise mechanism nor substitutes for a formal privacy guarantee. A single-machine scalability simulation across 2 to 20 simulated hospitals produced accuracies of 98.90% (2 hospitals), 95.10% (5 hospitals), 93.80% (10 hospitals), and 97.20% (20 hospitals), respectively, while the simulated blockchain audit trail adds negligible overhead (0.059–0.091 s average mining time per block within the single-machine environment). FedChainDP incorporates technical safeguards relevant to healthcare privacy and accountability objectives across four dimensions: multi-technique privacy integration, blockchain-logged policy checks on reported noise parameters, smart contract access control, and empirical membership-inference evaluation.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: federated learning; healthcare data privacy; ECG classification; privacy-preserving machine learning
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data; Computer Science > Information Systems > Blockchain Technology Applications and Security; Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > ECG Monitoring and Analysis

Article.Title: Growth performance, carcass traits, blood indices, and cecal bacterial load of Koekoek chickens fed diets containing neem leaf meal, bitter leaf meal, and garlic powder
Article.Authors: Yegrem M.; Animut G.; Mekuriaw Y.; Menale M.; Yilkal S.; Yimer Y.; Fentahun M.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary inclusion with phytogenic feed additives, namely neem leaf ( Azadirachta indica ), bitter leaf ( Vernonia amygdalina ), and garlic powder ( Allium sativum ), on growth performance, carcass traits, haematobiochemical indices, and cecal microbial load in Koekoek chickens. A total of 192 male Koekoek chicks were randomly allocated to four dietary treatments in a completely randomized design (CRD): a basal control diet (T1) and three experimental diets supplemented with neem leaf meal (T2), bitter leaf meal (T3), and garlic powder (T4), each at an inclusion level of 2.5%. The results demonstrated that chickens fed the phytogenic-supplemented diets, particularly the bitter leaf-inclusion diet (T3), exhibited significantly higher ( P < 0.05) average daily body weight gain, feed conversion ratio (FCR), and final body weight than control diet (T1). Carcass trait analysis revealed significant enhancement ( P < 0.05) in slaughter weight, dressing weight, different cut parts, and liver. The haematological analysis indicated a reduction in white blood cell counts in chickens fed the control diet (T1). Serum biochemical analysis revealed significant differences ( P < 0.05) among treatments in total protein, globulin, creatinine, glucose, and high-density lipoprotein levels. Analysis of the cecal microbiota revealed a significant increase ( P < 0.01) in Lactobacillus counts, accompanied by a notable reduction in pathogenic bacteria, including Escherichia coli and Salmonella . Overall, chickens receiving the bitter leaf-inclusion diet (T3) showed the most pronounced improvements in body weight gain and FCR, together with a favorable cecal microbial profile characterized by higher Lactobacillus counts and lower E. coli and Salmonella loads. This finding suggests that bitter leaf supplementation has potential as a dietary strategy for improving growth performance and promoting a favorable gut microbial balance in Koekoek chickens.
