Article.Title: An interpretable ANFIS-NSGA-II framework for evidence-stratified modular wearable risk fusion in elder-health monitoring
Article.Authors: Leonid T.; Londhe G.; Theivadas J.
Article.Abstract: Wearable health monitoring spans fall, cardiac, oxygenation, sleep, mobility, behavioural and long-horizon neurodegenerative indicators that arise from different sensors, labels and time scales. This study presents an evidence-stratified Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System optimized with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (ANFIS-NSGA-II) that fuses module-specific actionability scores into an interpretable monitoring-priority index (MPI) without treating heterogeneous risks as equivalent disease probabilities. Because no synchronized seven-modality older-adult cohort was available, the complete fusion mechanism is evaluated in a controlled subject-indexed synthetic benchmark of 240 subjects and 2,880 observation windows, while real datasets provide module-level evidence and prospective validation targets. The full 3 7 antecedent grid is reduced to a training-derived 64-rule library by an explicitly specified ranking criterion, and the Pareto-selected policy retains 20 active rules. On 48 held-out subjects the frozen policy achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.914 (95% participant-cluster bootstrap CI 0.871–0.948), area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) 0.888 (0.824–0.935), sensitivity 0.868 (0.779–0.935) and specificity 0.751 (0.639–0.832). Paired participant-cluster comparisons show that logistic regression, a generalized additive model, a random forest and a quality-weighted mean all reach discrimination that is statistically indistinguishable from the proposed model after correction for multiple comparisons; the proposed model is significantly better only than a max-risk rule. Ablations show that the 17 mandatory anchor rules alone are significantly worse than the selected policy (AUROC 0.861), that relaxing the anchor requirement lets the optimizer reach significantly higher discrimination with only 8 rules, and that quality-weighted marginalization is preferable to zero-filling but significantly inferior to simple imputation when signal quality is uniformly high, the alternatives converging only when quality is genuinely variable. A scenario analysis that varies interaction strength, interaction identity, label noise, target functional family and the share of escalation propensity driven by unobserved latent state quantifies how much of the reported performance reflects recovery of the authors' own generating mechanism: without label noise the target is deterministic conditional on the seven scores and the generator's subject-level offset, the model attains 72–98% of the oracle discrimination computed from the true propensity, and it exceeds logistic regression in only 1 of 14 scenarios. The contribution is therefore an auditable, reproducible fusion and policy-selection architecture rather than a gain in predictive accuracy, and every quantitative result is a proof-of-concept methodological finding on synthetic data. Prospective synchronized multimodal validation with clinician evaluation remains necessary before any clinical use.

Article.Authors: Saito Y.; Kobayashi M.; Sakamoto T.; Takekuma Y.; Sakakibara-Konishi J.; Shimizu Y.; Kinoshita I.; Sugawara M.
Article.Abstract: Cisplatin (CDDP)-induced nephrotoxicity (CIN) commonly arises during CDDP-based therapy. Similar outcomes were observed in the propensity score-matched cohort. Even after excluding patients concurrently administered bevacizumab, consistent results were obtained. Article.Title: Assessment of content and quality of thyroid nodule management information on Chinese video-sharing platforms
Article.Authors: Li R.; Zhou Z.; Zhu Y.; Xu J.; Li M.; Wang X.; Wang G.; Ma W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As short videos have emerged as a promising medium for disseminating health information, the quality and reliability of thyroid nodule (TN) management content on video platforms require critical evaluation. On November 12, 2025, the top 120 videos returned on each platform using the prespecified composite search were screened. Ultimately, 151 eligible videos were included in this cross-sectional study (Bilibili, n = 76; TikTok, n = 75). Five distinct quality-related domains were assessed: overall educational quality and usefulness, information reliability and balance, source transparency and accountability, patient understandability and actionability, and coverage of selected TN-specific management elements, using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN, Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria, Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT-A/V), and the study-specific Video Integrity 5 checklist, respectively. Spearman’s rank correlation was used to analyze relationships between video characteristics and quality-related scores. Videos on Bilibili were significantly longer than those on TikTok (median, 2.46 vs. 1.35 min; p < 0.001). In unadjusted comparisons, TikTok videos had higher GQS, JAMA, and Video Integrity 5 checklist scores than Bilibili videos; however, none of the six predefined quality-related outcomes remained significantly associated with platform after adjustment for uploader category, publication age, and video duration. Videos uploaded by medical professionals scored higher than those uploaded by non-professionals in overall educational quality, information reliability and balance, source transparency, and TN-specific management coverage. A large proportion of videos lacked key transparency indicators, with 88.74% lacking literature citations and 82.78% lacking conflict-of-interest disclosures. Associations between audience engagement metrics and quality-related scores were generally weak and inconsistent across platforms. Although 76.82% of the sampled videos were uploaded by medical professionals, limitations in source transparency, balance of presentation, and coverage of key TN management elements remained. These findings may inform future efforts to improve the transparency and clinical contextualization of patient-facing TN management information on short-video platforms.

Article.Title: An adaptive behavioural zero-trust security framework with proactive cryptographic caching for continuous authentication in 5G non-terrestrial networks
Article.Authors: Sankeerthana N.; Dakshayini M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) are key to future global broadband and military communications, but their high latency and dynamic topologies require security approaches beyond perimeter defences and static authentication. To overcome these vulnerabilities, we propose an adaptive behavioural zero trust security framework (BZTSF) for continuous 5G NTN authentication. Our method continuously evaluates node trustworthiness using network signal information processed by an isolation forest machine learning algorithm. A proactive cryptographic caching mechanism reduces re-authentication latency to 7.2 ms with 99.5% session continuity (evaluated under warm-cache rule-based conditions), compared to traditional 1600 ms handover peaks. When subsequently integrated with the ML engine, the framework demonstrated a highly efficient signalling overhead of 0.75%, well below the 8% target. A policy decision point engine instantly translates anomaly scores into access control decisions. Evaluating 50,000 simulated NTN telemetry samples (4:1 class imbalance) yielded 88.00% accuracy, 0.9856 average precision, and a 0.9969 ROC AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve). Within the simulated environment, the framework delivered 100% live spoofing detection and 1.0000 attack recall with zero false negatives. Feature importance analysis reveals that physics-based kinematic metrics-specifically velocity deviation, GPS distance, and Doppler shift-drive the zero-trust scoring. Ultimately, this framework serves as a proof-of-concept demonstrating that adaptive, low-overhead security integrations are theoretically viable under orbital constraints, paving the way for future physical validation in next-generation 6G networks.

Article.Title: A prospective pilot cohort study of hydrocyn gel as a dressing agent compared with conventional flavin-based pin-site care for infection prevention
Article.Authors: Md Yusoff B.; Jasmin L.; Nik Kamaruzman N.; Mohamad N.; Ramlan M.; Azwan Aziz M.
Article.Abstract: Pin-site infection (PSI) is a pervasive complication of external fixation, whose prevention is hampered by a lack of consensus on optimal care. This study aims (a) to generate preliminary estimates of pin-site infection rates associated with Hydrocyn gel compared to conventional flavin dressing and (b) to characterize the pattern and severity of infections (using the Checketts-Otterburn scale) in both groups over a four-week follow-up period. A prospective cohort study was conducted from April 2024 to December 2025. Sixteen patients with external fixators were included: 10 used Hydrocyn gel and 6 used conventional flavin dressing. Patients in both groups performed self-dressing every three days. Patients were followed weekly for four weeks, with pin-site infection diagnosed and graded using the Checketts and Otterburn scale. Due to the non-randomized design, small sample size, and retrospective trial registration, no inferential statistical tests were performed; results are descriptive. The Hydrocyn gel group had a lower pin site infection rate of 20% (2/10) compared to 66.7% (4/6) in the flavin group. In the Hydrocyn gel group, two patients developed Grade 1 infections; one resolved spontaneously, and one had worsening infection that required surgical debridement and pin removal. The flavin group experienced earlier and more frequent infections, with one patient requiring early debridement and multiple cases progressing to Grade 2 and 3. No osteomyelitis was reported in either group. Hydrocyn gel was associated with a lower observed rate of pin-site infection n compared to conventional flavin dressing in a trauma population. Because treatment allocation was based on patient consent rather than randomization, the observed association between Hydrocyn gel and lower infection rates should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of treatment efficacy. Article.Title: Multimodal speech perception in noise after multisensory perceptual training in autistic children and adolescents
Article.Authors: Möde L.; Ghaneirad E.; Szycik G.; Worthmann H.; Bleich S.; Borgolte A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autistic children and adolescents exhibit alterations in multisensory processing of simple audiovisual stimuli and complex speech stimuli. Multisensory perceptual training improves audiovisual simultaneity perception in typically developed adults, thereby facilitating speech comprehension in noise. We hypothesized that multisensory training would enhance audiovisual integration and speech comprehension in noise in autistic youth. A brief simultaneity judgment task (SJT) with feedback as the training paradigm was administered to a sample of autistic participants (aged 8–17). Simple audiovisual integration and speech comprehension were assessed before training (T0), immediately (T1), seven (T2) and 14 days (T3) after training. For simple audiovisual stimuli, changes in simultaneity judgements were observed at T1 and T2. At T1, these changes may reflect a shift in response criteria, whereas at T2, a narrower TBW and a steeper slope may indicate improved simultaneity perception. In a Word Recognition Task (WRT), no significant improvements were observed. This study suggests that multisensory training alters simultaneity judgement in a SJT in autistic youth, with the effects persisting seven days. Future studies should determine whether these effects reflect changes in response criteria or genuine improvements in simultaneity perception and determine how training paradigms must be adapted to enhance speech comprehension in autistic youth.

Article.Title: Microgrid design and optimization
Article.Authors: Gupta O.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Microgrids are rapidly transforming modern power systems by enabling decentralized, resilient, and sustainable energy solutions. As the penetration of renewable energy resources increases, the challenges associated with system design, optimization, control, and protection have become more complex and interdependent. This Guest-Edited Collection on “Microgrid Design and Optimization” brings together recent advances addressing these challenges through innovative methodologies and practical implementations. The contributions span hybrid system design, intelligent optimization techniques, protection strategies, and real-world deployment scenarios. Selected studies within the Collection demonstrate novel approaches to enhancing operational reliability, economic feasibility, and system resilience under uncertain conditions. This editorial provides an overview of the research landscape, contextualizes key contributions, and highlights emerging directions, including AI-driven control, hybrid energy integration, and sustainable microgrid architectures. The Collection aims to serve as a valuable reference for researchers working toward next-generation energy systems.

Article.Title: Outcomes of empirical ceftazidime avibactam plus colistin versus colistin regimens in carbapenem resistant gram negative infection under diagnostic uncertainty
Article.Authors: Muqtadir J.; Batool I.; Bhatti S.; Rasool S.; Gohar F.; Rasheed A.; Fatima U.
Article.Abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacterial ( CR-GNB ) infections are linked with high mortality, and therapeutic regimens remain limited in many regions. Where carbapenemase genotyping and reference-standard colistin susceptibility testing are unavailable, clinicians must select regimens empirically. We compared outcomes associated with two empirical strategies. In this prospective observational cohort study conducted from June 2021 to May 2025 in Karachi, Pakistan, adults with microbiologically confirmed CR-GNB infection received ceftazidime–avibactam plus colistin or a colistin-based regimen without ceftazidime–avibactam. Assignment to ceftazidime–avibactam followed an open alternating sequence; the comparator regimen was at the discretion of the treating physician. Follow-up ran from admission to in-hospital death, discharge alive, or 28 days. After 1:1 propensity-score matching, 846 patients were included (423 per group). Among comparator patients, 156 (36.9%) received colistin alone and 267 (63.1%) colistin plus meropenem. In-hospital death occurred in 36/423 (8.5%) versus 70/423 (16.5%); absolute risk difference − 8.0% (95% CI − 12.5 to − 3.6). Treating discharge alive as a competing event, ceftazidime–avibactam plus colistin was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard of death (adjusted sHR 0.55, 95% CI 0.37–0.83). Cumulative incidence curves were superimposable to day 14 and diverged thereafter. Microbiological failure occurred in 54/423 (12.8%) versus 83/423 (19.6%) (OR 0.60, 0.41–0.87), and new invasive mechanical ventilation in 14/383 (3.7%) versus 72/386 (18.7%) (OR 0.17, 0.09–0.30). Ceftazidime–avibactam plus colistin was associated with lower in-hospital mortality than colistin-based regimens without ceftazidime–avibactam. Because the in vitro activity of either regimen against the infecting organism could not be established, these findings describe outcomes associated with empirical treatment strategies under diagnostic uncertainty and do not establish the comparative efficacy of a specific antimicrobial combination.

Article.Title: Engineering a bivalent anti-CsGRP78 nanobody via CDR grafting: in silico design and cytotoxic validation
Article.Authors: Shahreza R.; Ebrahim-Habibi A.; Mohammadi E.; Jahanian-Najafabadi A.; Bakherad H.
Article.Abstract: GRP78 is a central endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperone and the primary sensor for the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR). Under cellular stress, GRP78 translocates to the cell surface (CsGRP78), where it functions as a signal-transducing receptor. CsGRP78 acts as a port of entry for viruses and plays a critical role in cancer pathogenesis by promoting tumor cell proliferation, survival, stemness, invasion, and metastasis. Its dysregulation in diseases like diabetes and cardiovascular disorders makes it a significant therapeutic target. Anti-GRP78 antibodies have therapeutic potential. However, conventional full-length antibodies face challenges, including insufficient tissue penetration and production difficulties. To overcome these, we engineered a novel, nanobody-based antagonist. Using CDR grafting and subsequent point mutations, we transferred the specificity of a parental antibody onto two nanobody scaffolds to create a bivalent construct, termed “CsGRP78-diaNb.” In silico docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested promising target engagement. CsGRP78-diaNb was expressed, and its cytotoxicity was evaluated using an MTT assay. It demonstrated selective cytotoxicity against B16F10 cancer cells that overexpress CsGRP78, compared with the negative control CHO-S cells. These preliminary findings suggest that CsGRP78-diaNb is a promising candidate for further development as a targeted therapeutic, pending direct validation of cell-surface binding and in vivo efficacy.

Article.Title: State-backend-dependent fidelity of the CCZ gate on superconducting quantum computers
Article.Authors: AbuGhanem M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We present an experimental characterization of the three-qubit controlled-controlled-Z (CCZ) gate on IBM Quantum’s 127-qubit superconducting quantum computers, revealing state-backend-dependent performance variations. Using quantum state tomography (QST), we evaluate the gate’s output-state fidelity when applied to three algorithmically significant input states—the W state, the Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) state, and the uniform superposition state. Each state probes distinct aspects of the reconstructed state fidelity, the GHZ state tests coherence in maximally entangled systems, the W state reveals sensitivity to asymmetric errors, and the uniform superposition assesses basis-state-independent behavior. Experiments were conducted across three computational environments, noise-free simulation, noisy simulation, and actual hardware executions on three IBM Quantum computers, ibm_osaka , ibm_brisbane , and ibm_sherbrooke . State fidelities for the qasm_simulator remained above 99.2% for all input states. Noisy simulations yielded fidelities around 80–82%, while hardware results showed more significant degradation: 67.6% (GHZ), 59.0% (uniform superposition), and 50.3% (W)—highlighting the combined importance of state selection and hardware characteristics for reliable quantum computation. These results quantify the current performance gap between simulated and physical implementations of multi-qubit gates and provide a benchmark for error profiles relevant to near-term quantum algorithms

Article.Title: Ophthalmological misconceptions among adults in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Alabdrabulridha A.; Alhithlool A.; Alenizi A.; Almulla S.; Alotaibi Z.; Almutlaq A.; Alsaif O.; Ismail Al Somali A.
Article.Abstract: Ophthalmological health misconceptions represent a significant barrier to appropriate eye care-seeking behaviour. Despite increasing educational attainment and digital connectivity in Saudi Arabia, the prevalence of eye health myths among the adult population remains poorly characterised. This study assessed ophthalmological health knowledge and identified prevalent misconceptions among adults in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia, and examined associations with sociodemographic factors. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among adults aged ≥ 18 years in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia (January–March 2024). A pre-tested, self-administered questionnaire assessed awareness of common eye health misconceptions. Following peer review, one item with an ambiguous clinical key was excluded, yielding a 27-item scoring instrument (25 myths, 2 facts). Awareness was classified as poor (< 40%), fair (40–59.9%), or good (≥ 60%). Chi-square tests, Benjamini–Hochberg correction, and binary logistic regression were applied, with p < 0.05 significant. Of 441 participants, 59.9% were female and 57.6% aged 18–25 years. Poor awareness was observed in 45.8%, fair in 40.8%, and good in 13.4%. The most prevalent misconceptions concerned television proximity (90.9%) and computer use (90.0%). In unadjusted analysis, younger age (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.72–0.97, p = 0.015) was associated with better awareness; in a model adjusting for age, gender, education, and ocular history, postgraduate education (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.12–4.76, p = 0.024) was also associated with better awareness; however, age and employment were strongly collinear and age did not remain a robust independent predictor after full adjustment. After Benjamini–Hochberg correction, no individual myth differed significantly by ocular history. Widespread ophthalmological misconceptions persist among educated adults in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. Younger age was associated with better awareness in unadjusted analyses but could not be disentangled from employment and was not a robust independent predictor; postgraduate education remained associated with awareness across model specifications. Personal experience of eye disease was not associated with awareness. Targeted, digitally delivered eye-health education warrants evaluation as a potential strategy for addressing these misconceptions.

Article.Title: Split-intein-mediated engineering of VSV-G-free extracellular vesicles for enhanced cargo loading and delivery of functional proteins
Article.Authors: Ghazi Birjandi R.; Dehghani H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Extracellular Vesicles (EVs) are a heterogeneous group of membranous nanoparticles. Due to their unique properties, they are considered promising nanocarriers for therapeutic applications. Cargo loading and functional delivery to the target cell are challenging areas and are receiving increasing attention in EV research. Here, we introduce a novel one-step and VSV-G-free loading system based on pH-sensitive split inteins to improve protein loading into EVs. To this end, we fused the EV membrane protein CD9 to the NpuN component and the cargo of interest to the NpuC component. We reasoned that the interaction between NpuN and NpuC facilitates loading of the fused cargo into the EVs. We expected that the pH-sensitive sequence between NpuC and the cargo would cleave at acidic pH within the intraluminal vesicles of producing cells or in the endosomes of recipient cells. Our results showed that the NpuN/NpuC system, compared with passive loading, improved the loading of DsRed2 and tdTomato into the EVs by 1.3-fold. We employed this system to assess the functional delivery of proteins into recipient cells. To this end, piggyBac transposase was fused to NpuC, and EVs were added to reporter cells, where the excisionase activity of piggyBac was consistent with the excision of 5′ITR-EGFP-Polyadenylation signal-3′ITR and expression of mCherry. Isolated EVs were characterized by TEM, DLS, and dot blot detection of the engineered mEmerald-CD9 membrane protein and DsRed2 cargo in the vesicle fraction. No endogenous EV markers or negative-contamination markers were assessed; consequently, EV identity and sample purity were not established by protein marker profiling.

Article.Title: Ant colony optimization plus temporal difference and opposition-based learning for semi-supervised multi-label feature selection
Article.Authors: Beyranvand S.; Mehrdad V.; Dowlatshahi M.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a novel feature selection method for multi-label data, combining Ant Colony Optimization with Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Opposition-Based Learning in a semi-supervised framework. Ant colony optimization navigates the feature space, while RL dynamically updates heuristic functions to predict rewards for selected features. Opposition-Based Learning enhances exploration by evaluating both original and complementary solutions. The semi-supervised learning aspect allows the algorithm to leverage the structure of the unlabeled data, improving the quality of feature selection even when labeled data is scarce. For the first time, the impact of the proposed algorithm has been systematically investigated. Compared to baseline methods, the approach achieves 7% and 3% relative improvement in Accuracy, 6% and 4% relative reduction in Hamming loss with 20% and 40% labeled data. Evaluated on 8 datasets using the Multi-Label K-Nearest Neighbors classifier, the method outperforms traditional techniques by refining feature subsets through unlabeled data. The method’s higher computational complexity and memory requirements compared to baseline techniques make it better suited for high-accuracy tasks where real-time processing is not critical, such as precision-driven biomedical analysis or batch-oriented industrial data mining. This work establishes a new benchmark for semi-supervised multi-label feature selection, prioritizing accuracy in scenarios where computational latency is tolerable.

Article.Title: Surrogate assisted robust optimization balances mechanical performance and workability in fiber reinforced self compacting concrete
Article.Authors: Shirvani E.; Habibi M.; Tavana M.; Roudsari M.
Article.Abstract: Mechanical performance, workability, fiber efficiency, and uncertainty must all be taken into account when designing a mix for fiber-reinforced self-compacting concrete (FRSCC), and adding more fiber does not always translate into a corresponding improvement in performance. In order to assess and optimize FRSCC using Forta, glass, ceramic, binary-hybrid, and triple-hybrid reinforcement systems, this study created a surrogate-assisted robust multi-objective framework. The analysis used 274 experimental observations to construct surrogate models, which were subsequently evaluated across a design space of 274 measured and model-derived mixture–curing combinations with total fiber dosages ranging from 0% to 9% and curing ages between 7 and 180 days. Statistical analysis, response surfaces, Pareto analysis, and bootstrap-based robustness assessment were used to measure compressive strength (f c ), tensile strength (f t ), flexural strength (f f ), slump flow, T 500 , mechanical efficiency index (MEI), and a total performance score. Compressive-to-tensile strength balance, fracture energy, characteristic length, inferred ITZ bonding, pore structure, and fiber dispersion were further explored using mechanically derived proxy indicators. With f c =21.68 MPa, f t =5.68 MPa, f f =9.66 MPa, a total score of 14.48, and MEI of 5.52, Forta demonstrated the best mean mechanical performance. With a total score of 13.53, Forta+Glass was the most effective hybrid system. Forta-D5-T180 was the robust optimum, ranking first in 63.6% of bootstrap resamples and obtaining a cumulative score of around 17.71. Within the surrogate-evaluated design space, Forta-D5-T180 was the highest-ranked model-predicted candidate, ranking first in 63.6% of the bootstrap iterations. However, because the original experiments covered curing ages only up to 90 days, this candidate requires independent experimental validation at 180 days. R 2 = 0.631 and 0.535 were found in the f c -f t and f c -f f correlations, respectively. Mechanically derived indicators were used to explore differences in strength balance and estimated fracture-related behavior among reinforcement systems. These indicators provide supplementary comparisons but do not directly establish interfacial bonding, pore structure, fiber dispersion, crack-bridging mechanisms, or post-cracking performance. Overall, the framework shows that rather than just optimizing fiber dosage or hybridization, reliable FRSCC design necessitates objective-specific optimization.

Article.Title: Gait-triggered neuromuscular electrical stimulation as an adjunct to an offloading knee brace in medial knee osteoarthritis: a pilot randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Jafarian M.; Komeili A.; Salehi R.; Barati K.; Arjmand N.
Article.Abstract: Medial compartment knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a disabling condition with a growing prevalence. Off-loading bracing is a treatment commonly used to reduce medial knee loading and improve symptoms. This study evaluated whether combining gait-triggered neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) with an off-loading brace provides additional clinical and biomechanical benefits over bracing alone. Twenty-eight patients with mild-to-moderate KOA (14 per group) were randomized to a brace-only or brace plus gait-triggered-NMES group and were instructed to complete twelve walking sessions over 4 weeks with daily brace use. Primary and key secondary outcomes were WOMAC total score and VAS pain, respectively. Biomechanical assessments included kinematic, kinetic, and electromyographic analyses during gait, sit-to-stand, and balance tasks. Of the 23 patients who completed the interventions (Control = 12, NMES = 11), no significant between-group difference was found in the primary outcome (WOMAC: MD = 3.48; 95% CI –3.47 to 10.44, p = 0.309). For the secondary outcome, a modest reduction in VAS pain was observed in the NMES group (MD = –1.11; 95% CI –2.20 to –0.03). Bracing alone produced greater reductions in peak KAM and KAM impulse, whereas the NMES group showed reduced postural sway and reduced muscle activation. Taken together, these findings do not support the superiority of adding NMES to bracing for overall clinical function or mechanical unloading; NMES may offer only limited analgesic and localized neuromuscular responses. The intervention was feasible and safe. Future studies should explore whether refined NMES parameters can provide clinical benefit without interfering with brace mechanical unloading. These multi-task findings may help guide the design of future focused clinical studies.

Article.Title: A dual-input coarse-to-fine residual correction network for underwater acoustic OFDM channel estimation in doubly selective channels
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Guo T.; Guo Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In doubly selective underwater acoustic channels, time-varying multipath and Doppler spread destroy the orthogonality among orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) subcarriers. As a result, the least squares (LS) estimates at pilot positions are affected by noise, inter-carrier interference (ICI), and spectral distortion. To address this problem, this paper proposes a dual-input coarse-to-fine residual correction network for underwater acoustic OFDM channel estimation in doubly selective channels, named Dual-Input Residual Correction Network (DIRCNet). The proposed method takes the LS estimates at pilot positions and the received frequency-domain signal as joint inputs. The pilot-position LS estimates supply amplitude and phase references after normalization by the known symbols, and the received frequency-domain signal captures signal variations over the complete subcarrier grid. In the network structure, DIRCNet first recovers an initial channel profile through the pilot LS coarse estimation branch. Then, the received signal branch extracts auxiliary time-frequency features. Feature-level late fusion and a residual refinement backbone then predict the correction term relative to the coarse estimate, yielding a coarse-to-fine channel estimation process. Experiments are conducted on the Bellhop-SSML time-varying simulated channel and the WATERMARK NOF1 and KAU1 measured-replay channels, with file-level five-fold cross-validation adopted for the WATERMARK experiments. The proposed method is evaluated in terms of normalized mean square error, bit error rate, model complexity, and robustness to residual carrier frequency offset. The results show that DIRCNet maintains relatively stable channel estimation and demodulation performance on both the simulated channel and the WATERMARK measured-replay channels, and achieves better NMSE and BER performance than conventional methods and multiple single-input and dual-input deep-learning baselines under most test conditions. The residual CFO experiment shows that DIRCNet maintains good robustness over the tested frequency-offset range, while the ablation study further verifies the effectiveness of the received-signal branch, feature-level late fusion, and the residual refinement structure.

Article.Title: A pseudo-three-dimensional work-balance correction for sidewall friction effects in centrifuge slope models
Article.Authors: Liu F.; Sun L.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Centrifuge model tests are widely used to investigate slope stability; however, frictional interactions between the sliding mass and rigid container sidewalls introduce boundary effects that compromise similitude with ideal plane-strain prototypes. These effects can lead to an apparent increase in the stability of finite-width models relative to the corresponding plane-strain reference. In this paper, a pseudo-three-dimensional work-balance correction based on a classical plane-strain upper-bound mechanism is developed by introducing an additional out-of-plane sidewall-friction work-rate term evaluated from an assumed lateral normal-stress distribution into the global work rate balance. A random-search optimisation technique is employed to identify the critical failure surface geometry and the corresponding stability factor. The proposed formulation is checked against the classical plane-strain upper-bound solution and further compared with published centrifuge test data. Across the reported configurations, the calculated and measured critical acceleration scale factors show the same decreasing trends with increasing model height and slope inclination, although substantial differences remain for individual cases. A parametric study reveals that sidewall friction significantly increases the apparent stability factor at low width-to-height ratios, but this discrepancy diminishes rapidly as the ratio increases. For the representative cases examined at β = 60°, the sidewall friction angle and width-to-height ratio exert larger influences on the sidewall-induced relative deviation than the soil internal friction angle, while the influence of the soil internal friction angle is retained explicitly in the broader reference charts and tables. Reference charts and tables are further developed to quantify the width-dependent deviation for selected parameter combinations and relative-deviation thresholds. These resources provide preliminary, assumption-dependent references for selecting model widths and interpreting sidewall-induced deviations in centrifuge slope tests.

Article.Title: Patient-reported burden and adverse events of urodynamic investigation in adults with neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction
Article.Authors: Gross O.; Kasten M.; Wettstein M.; Anderson C.; Birkhäuser V.; Borer J.; Lehner F.; Liechti M.; McCallin S.; Mehnert U.; Röthlisberger R.; Sadri H.; Stächele L.; Kessler T.; Leitner L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urodynamic investigation (UDI) is the gold standard for evaluating refractory lower urinary tract symptoms but may cause pain, emotional discomfort, and adverse events, particularly urinary tract infections. In this secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial, adults undergoing UDI for neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction rated pain and emotional discomfort on an 11-point numeric rating scale (0–10), with ≥ 4 defining moderate-to-severe burden; a structured telephone interview at 7–14 days assessed post-procedural adverse events. Among 490 patients, most reported low pain and emotional discomfort (median 2, IQR 0–4 and 0–5). Pain did not differ by sex, whereas emotional discomfort was higher in females (median 2.5 vs 1; p = 0.004). Post-procedural symptoms included pain (30%), worsening lower urinary tract symptoms (18%), and macrohematuria (8%); 99% were transient. Urinary tract infection occurred in 6% and was associated with pre-procedural bacteriuria (OR 6.69; 95% CI 2.15–20.81). Assuming risk equalization, the number needed to treat to prevent one infection was 15 (95% CI 9.6–38.6). In conclusion, UDI is generally well tolerated, although approximately one-third of patients experience moderate-to-severe pain or emotional discomfort. Pre-procedural bacteriuria increases infection risk, but the number needed to treat does not support antibiotic prophylaxis.

Article.Title: Graphite paste electrode integrated with pomegranate peel extract-derived ZnO nanoparticles and MWCNTs for green voltammetric analysis of asenapine maleate
Article.Authors: Farrag M.; El-Mosallamy S.; Mohammed B.; Ahmed H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing need for environmentally favorable analytical methods has encouraged the development of eco-friendly materials for drug analysis. This work explores the use of green nanoparticles for the electrochemical sensing of the antipsychotic drug asenapine maleate (ASEP). Pomegranate peel extract (PPE) was utilized as a green reducing and stabilizing agent for the synthesis of zinc oxide nanoparticles (PPE@ZnO NPs). The synthesized PPE@ZnO NPs were characterized by UV–Vis, SEM–EDX, XRD, HR-TEM, and FT-IR, revealing a spherical morphology and hexagonal wurtzite structure, with a mean particle diameter of 5.28 ± 1.0 nm based on TEM image analysis and a crystallite size of 8.86 nm estimated from XRD. The PPE@ZnO NPs were integrated with multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) into a graphite paste matrix to fabricate the optimized green electrochemical sensor (5% MWCNTs/10% PPE@ZnO/GPE). Under optimized conditions at pH 5, differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) exhibited an irreversible anodic peak for ASEP at + 0.98 V. The proposed method showed a linear range of 8 × 10⁻⁶–1 × 10⁻⁴ M, with detection and quantification limits of 1.71 × 10⁻⁶ and 5.18 × 10⁻⁶ M, respectively. The method was successfully applied to the determination of ASEP in commercial tablets, yielding a satisfactory mean percentage found of 100.13 ± 1.70%. The Analytical GREEnness (AGREE) metric and Analytical Eco-Scale indicated a favorable greenness profile for the proposed method, with an AGREE score of 0.76. Overall, the study highlights the potential of PPE-derived ZnO nanoparticles as green electrode-modifying materials for the voltammetric determination of ASEP.

Article.Title: Hybrid transformer and CNN for hyperspectral image classification with spectral band selection
Article.Authors: Abdelhafez E.; Hagag A.; Abassy T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral images (HSI) play a vital role in remote sensing applications such as surveillance and precision agriculture, yet they face challenges including limited labeled samples and class imbalance. This paper presents a new method for HSI classification by integrating spectral band selection with advanced deep learning techniques. First, we propose an optimized band selection method alongside data augmentation using crop-and-resize transformations to enhance feature diversity. Second, we introduce a hybrid convolution-transformer framework that combines Vision Transformer (ViT) and 2D-CNN architectures, supplemented with a sequence aggregation layer to mitigate overfitting on small datasets. This hybrid model effectively captures both spatial and spectral features while preserving critical spectral details. Finally, we employ a support vector machine for robust classification. Extensive experiments on three widely used HSI datasets demonstrate that our proposed ViT-CNN-BS framework achieves superior classification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art few-shot learning methods and traditional approaches. Beyond achieving higher accuracy, our approach also reduces computational complexity, making it suitable for resource-constrained applications. The findings highlight the potential of hybrid deep learning frameworks for advancing remote sensing analytics, with possible extensions to environmental monitoring, disaster management, and precision agriculture.

Article.Title: Collective charge excitations in the kagome lattice driven by Holstein phonons and magnetic fields
Article.Authors: Azizi F.; Rezania H.
Article.Abstract: The combined effects of Holstein electron–phonon coupling and an external magnetic field on the tunable charge-response resonances of the kagome lattice are investigated. Within the Holstein model supplemented by nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hopping, a staggered sublattice potential, and Zeeman splitting, the single-particle Hamiltonian is diagonalized analytically to obtain the band dispersions and eigenvectors. The non-interacting Matsubara Green’s functions are constructed, and the frequency-dependent effective electron–electron interaction arising from virtual exchange of dispersionless Einstein phonons is incorporated into the random-phase approximation for the dynamical charge susceptibility. For the site-local Holstein kernel the defining RPA is the $$3\times 3$$ matrix equation in sublattice space; at the representative wave vector of the figures this matrix response coincides with the scalar total-density formula on the two principal resonances. The dynamical charge structure factor $$S_c({\textbf{q}},\omega )$$ and the static charge structure factor are subsequently obtained from the retarded susceptibility and the fluctuation–dissipation theorem, respectively. Numerical results at a representative wave vector in the Brillouin zone show that increasing the electron–phonon coupling strength redistributes spectral weight and shifts the high-energy charge resonance to higher frequencies, whereas the external magnetic field mainly suppresses the intensities of both charge resonances without appreciably shifting their positions. The next-nearest-neighbor hopping amplitude and the staggered gap allow selective tuning of the spectral weights of the low- and high-energy charge resonances. The static charge correlations exhibit non-monotonic dependencies on temperature and magnetic field, originating from the competition among thermal fluctuations, Zeeman splitting, and phonon-mediated attraction. These results demonstrate that Holstein phonons and an external magnetic field can be used in combination to control both the dynamical and static charge responses of the kagome lattice, including the tunable charge resonances.

Article.Title: Numerical investigation of valence band offset at the HTL/Cs2PdBr6 interface for high-performance double perovskite solar cells
Article.Authors: Arane S.; Patel P.
Article.Abstract: All-inorganic lead-free Cs 2 PdBr 6 perovskite solar cells have attracted significant attention owing to their excellent environmental stability and promising optoelectronic properties. In this work, the influence of HTL valence band offset on the electrostatic behaviour, carrier transport, recombination kinetics, and photovoltaic performance of Cs 2 PdBr 6 solar cells is systematically investigated using SCAPS-1D simulation. Different HTLs spanning cliff-type, intermediate spike regime and excessive spike-type alignments are analysed. The results reveal a strong non-monotonic dependence of device performance on the HTL valence band offset. Cliff-type alignment produces weak interfacial electric fields and diffusion-limited carrier extraction, leading to increased interfacial recombination losses. In contrast, balanced positive VBO generates an optimised depletion field that promotes efficient drift-assisted carrier transport and suppresses interfacial recombination. Among the investigated HTLs, V 2 O 5 with a + 0.3 eV VBO achieves the best performance, delivering a power conversion efficiency of 27.48% with V OC = 1.26 V, J SC = 25.1 mA cm − 2 , and FF = 87.3%. Large positive VBO alignment induces carrier accumulation and a transport barrier, causing performance degradation. QE analysis further confirms that optimised VBO engineering enhances long-wavelength carrier collection by extending the effective drift region across the absorber bulk. These findings establish HTL VBO engineering as a key strategy for achieving high-efficiency lead-free Cs 2 PdBr 6 perovskite solar cells.

Article.Title: Modulation of dysregulated ATG5 and ATG16L1 expression in IBD by Akkermansia muciniphila and its extracellular vesicles (EVs)
Article.Authors: Kazemifard N.; Farmani M.; Basiji K.; Ghavami S.; Ashrafian F.; Jahankhani K.; Mohammadi P.; Shahrokh S.
Article.Abstract: Akkermansia muciniphila is a next-generation probiotic known for its ability to degrade mucin within the intestinal mucus layer. Notably, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from A. muciniphila can mimic many of the bacterium’s functional properties. Autophagy, a vital cellular mechanism, maintains homeostasis by recycling damaged cellular components. Key genes in this pathway, including ATG5 and ATG16L1 , are essential for autophagosome formation. In this study, we analyzed the expression levels of ATG5 and ATG16L1 in patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn’s disease (CD) (two major forms of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)) compared to healthy controls using real-time PCR. Additionally, we evaluated the regulatory effects of A. muciniphila and its EVs on these genes in an inflamed Caco-2 colonic epithelial cell model. Our findings revealed significant overexpression of both ATG5 and ATG16L1 in UC and CD patients relative to controls. In vitro, IL-1β-induced inflammation in Caco-2 cells led to marked dysregulation of autophagy-related genes, with ATG5 upregulated and ATG16L1 downregulated. Treatment with live A. muciniphila and its EVs modulated the expression of these genes in a dose-dependent manner. While live bacteria consistently reversed inflammation-induced gene dysregulation, EVs exhibited a biphasic response, with higher concentrations more effectively restoring ATG16L1 expression. These results suggest that A. muciniphila and its EVs may offer therapeutic potential for managing autophagy-related inflammatory disorders, particularly in the context of IBD.

Article.Title: High-precision machining of silicon surface with intense femtosecond extreme ultraviolet pulses
Article.Authors: Lipp V.; Yamaguchi G.; Egawa S.; Inoue I.; Sakurai K.; Plakhuta D.; Noei H.; Toleikis S.; Ziaja B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Femtosecond laser direct writing (LDW), which uses ultraviolet, visible or infrared lasers, is a maskless subtractive manufacturing approach that is widely used for precision surface processing. This is because of the strong spatial confinement of laser energy and minimal collateral damage. Here, we present a conceptual scheme for the high-precision machining of semiconductor materials using LDW with sub-micron-focused extreme ultraviolet (EUV) laser pulses. A proof-of-concept study was conducted at the SACLA free-electron laser facility, which confirmed the feasibility of the machining process by creating reproducible craters with similar geometries in a single EUV femtosecond laser shot, with fixed pulse parameters. Dedicated computer simulations reproduced the experimental trends and provided insight into the ablation mechanism. These results establish the feasibility of controlled and reproducible semiconductor surface machining at micrometer and sub-micrometer length scales, and with further development, femtosecond EUV LDW could provide a route to maskless, high-precision patterning and machining of semiconductors and other technologically relevant materials.

Article.Title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease and long-term kidney function decline: a 16-year population-based cohort study
Article.Authors: Kim W.; Woo H.; Cho D.; Shin J.; Lee Y.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD), but its long-term impact on kidney function remains unclear. We investigated the association between MAFLD and kidney outcomes over 16 years using data from the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study. Among 10,030 participants aged 40–69 years recruited in 2001–2002, 8,827 with sufficient baseline and follow-up data were included. MAFLD was defined using the fatty liver index (FLI ≥ 30) combined with metabolic criteria. The primary outcome was the longitudinal estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope assessed using linear mixed-effects models. The secondary outcome was incident CKD (eGFR < 60 ml/min/1.73 m 2 ). At baseline, 45.1% ( n = 3,978) had FLI-defined MAFLD. Over 16 years, the median annual eGFR decline was − 0.61 mL/min/1.73 m 2 per year. After multivariable adjustment, MAFLD was independently associated with accelerated eGFR decline (β: −0.29; 95% CI:−0.39 to − 0.18; P < 0.001). During a median follow-up of 15.4 years, 19.5% ( n = 1,662) developed CKD, and MAFLD was associated with a 26% increased risk of incident CKD (hazard ratio: 1.26, 95% CI: 1.11–1.43; P < 0.001). Higher FLI categories were associated with progressively steeper eGFR decline. In conclusion, MAFLD was independently associated with accelerated kidney function decline and increased CKD risk over 16 years, highlighting the importance of kidney function monitoring in individuals with MAFLD.

Article.Title: Salicylic acid ameliorates Meloidogyne incognita suppression of growth and modulates defense gene expression in contrasting tomato cultivars
Article.Authors: ELKobrosy D.; Mohamed R.; Halawa E.; Abdelsalam N.; Zeid A.; EL-Wakeel H.; Elkelany U.; El-Sayed G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Root-knot nematodes ( Meloidogyne incognita ) are a major threat to tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ) production. This study evaluated exogenous salicylic acid (SA) as a root-zone soil drench (0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 g/L) for reducing M. incognita infection and alleviating nematode-induced growth suppression in two tomato cultivars with contrasting infection outcomes, the highly susceptible cv. ‘380’ and the phenotypically less susceptible cv. ‘Thuria’, under greenhouse conditions over 45 days. SA suppressed nematode infection and reproduction in a clear, dose-dependent manner, with 1.0 g/L most effective in both cultivars; the reduction in J2 infection was proportionally greatest in the susceptible cv. ‘380’, while cv. ‘Thuria’ maintained consistently lower infection, egg-mass formation, and egg production throughout. This suppression is best explained by a dual mode of action rather than a single pathway: soil J2 populations declined in step with SA concentration, consistent with a direct rhizospheric effect, while time-course qRT-PCR of the defense genes PR2 (β-1,3-glucanase) and PR4 (hevein-like protein), normalized to time-matched non-inoculated and untreated controls, showed strong early upregulation at 1 day post-inoculation followed by suppression at 3 days, an early, transient host defense response consistent with a priming component that was subsequently weakened as nematode infection proceeded. These two mechanisms diverged in magnitude between cultivars: cv. ‘Thuria’ showed higher absolute PR2/PR4 induction and lower baseline nematode burden despite lacking the Mi-1 resistance gene, supporting its classification as phenotypically less susceptible rather than tolerant, whereas cv. ‘380’ derived comparatively greater relative benefit from exogenous SA. SA also alleviated nematode-induced growth suppression in both cultivars, particularly at 1.0 g/L, improving shoot and root length, fresh and dry biomass, and root morphology, with visibly reduced galling. Overall, SA mitigated M. incognita infection in tomato through a combination of direct rhizospheric suppression and host defense-gene priming, with the relative contribution of each shaped by cultivar background—supporting its potential as a dual-action, plant-compatible tool for integrated nematode management.

Article.Title: Psychological resilience mediates links between nursing career attitude and negative emotions among eastern China nursing students in multicentre cross‑sectional research
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Bao Y.; Tang X.; Lou Y.; Zhang S.; Song C.
Article.Abstract: To assess psychological resilience and negative emotional states in nursing students in Eastern China, and to test whether resilience mediates their association with attitude toward the nursing profession. A multicentre cross-sectional survey of 500 nursing students (450 women; mean age 19.57 ± 1.08 years) at three institutions in Eastern China, recruited by cluster sampling of intact classes in April 2024. Resilience was measured with the CD-RISC and negative emotional states with the DASS-21. Analyses (SPSS 26.0) comprised t tests, one-way ANOVA, Spearman correlations, dummy-coded regression and PROCESS Model 4 mediation with 5000 bootstrap samples. Mean resilience was 59.76 ± 16.33 and mean DASS-21 total 29.32 ± 25.50; 48.8% of students scored above the normal range for depression and 53.8% for anxiety. Attitude toward nursing, household income, parental education and work experience were associated with resilience, negative emotional states, or both; all effect sizes were small (partial η 2 = 0.003–0.074). Resilience accounted for 31.2% of the attitude–distress association (indirect effect 3.09, 95% CI 1.33–5.43). Resilience was inversely associated with depression, anxiety and stress, and attitude toward the nursing profession showed the strongest association with both outcomes, partly through resilience. Because the design is cross-sectional, these findings identify correlates rather than causes.

Article.Title: AquaSteady seaweed-derived alginate hydrogel alters soil chemistry and biological indicators in a rate- and soil-dependent manner
Article.Authors: Bello A.; Ojekanmi A.; Idowu O.; Kehlet C.; Chorover J.; John G.; Sotamayor-Ramírez D.; Angadi S.; Darapuneni M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract AquaSteady (AQST) is a biodegradable, alginate-based, seaweed-derived hydrogel used in agriculture to enhance soil water retention, but its effects on soil physicochemical and biological indicators across contrasting soils remain poorly understood. We evaluated four AQST rates (0, 2, 5, and 10 mg/g soil) in six contrasting soils over a 56-day incubation, and measured soil chemistry and phospholipid fatty acid (PLFA)-based biological indicators. Soil pH rose from 7.38 (control) to 8.23 (high rate; p < 0.001), shifting several soils toward alkaline, while cation exchange capacity declined from 25.32 to 23.83 cmolc kg − 1 ( p < 0.001 ). Exchangeable K, Ca, and Mg fell by ~ 13%, 8%, and 12%, and sulfate and nitrate-N decreased by ~ 29% and 62%, at high AQST rates versus control, while Na roughly doubled (271 to 548 mg kg − 1 ; p < 0.001), indicating salinization risk in Na-sensitive soils. Total living microbial, fungal, protozoa, and undifferentiated microbial biomass increased mainly at medium and high rates; bacterial biomass and functional diversity showed no dose response. Mantel analysis found no statistically robust physicochemical-biological association after correction for multiple comparisons in any soil. Biological indicators were generally highest at the high rate, though medium (5 mg g⁻¹) did not differ statistically from high for most indicators, while sodium rose less and pH rose comparably at both rates. The medium rate may offer a better trade-off between biological benefit and salinity risk for sodicity-prone soils, pending calibration. These findings show soil-dependent trade-offs between biological stimulation and chemical shifts, indicating field validation is needed before broader AQST recommendations.

Article.Title: Increased expression of hPGDS‑PGD2 in patients with eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhu X.; Cai L.
Article.Abstract: The existing studies on the hPGDS–PGD2 pathway in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) mostly focus on the tissue-level expression characteristics of single molecules and lack systematic correlation verification between peripheral circulating indicators and local lesion indicators, and few studies have specifically explored the differential diagnostic efficacy and early clinical application potential of serum PGD2 for eosinophilic CRSwNP (eCRSwNP). On the basis of filling the above research gaps, this study aimed to systematically investigate the expression characteristics of hPGDS-PGD2 signal pathway in eCRSwNP patients, and further evaluate the accurate clinical value of serum PGD2 as a non-invasive biomarker for early diagnosis and phenotypic identification of eCRSwNP. This prospective study enrolled patients diagnosed with CRSwNP or chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps (CRSsNP) who underwent endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) at our hospital between October 2022 and April 2024. Patients undergoing surgery for simple nasal septum deviation or traumatic nasal bone fracture during the same period served as the control group. Serum PGD2 levels were measured by enzyme‑linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Protein expression of hPGDS in nasal tissues was detected by Western blot and immunohistochemistry, and mRNA expression of hPGDS was determined by real‑time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT‑qPCR). Statistical analyses were performed using appropriate statistical software. (1) Peripheral blood eosinophil (EOS) count, EOS%, serum total IgE, and serum PGD2 levels were significantly higher in the eCRSwNP group than in the non‑eCRSwNP, CRSsNP, and control groups ( P < 0.05). (2) The total CT score and E/M ratio of paranasal sinus were both significantly higher in the eCRSwNP group than in the non‑eCRSwNP and CRSsNP groups. (3) Immunohistochemical staining intensity, Western blot gray value, and mRNA expression of hPGDS in nasal polyp tissues were significantly higher in the eCRSwNP group than in the non‑eCRSwNP and CRSsNP groups ( P < 0.05). (4) Serum PGD2 was positively correlated with hPGDS mRNA expression in nasal polyp tissues ( r = 0.398, P < 0.05) and showed statistically significant positive correlations with peripheral blood EOS count, serum total IgE, and E/M ratio ( P < 0.05). (5) Serum PGD2 exhibited diagnostic value for eCRSwNP (AUC = 0.775, P < 0.05), with accuracy comparable to peripheral blood EOS count, EOS%, serum total IgE, total CT score, and E/M ratio. The pathway-specific molecular axis of hPGDS-PGD2 is confirmed to be a key pathogenic mechanism of eCRSwNP. Clinically, serum PGD2, as a novel non-invasive peripheral biomarker, avoids the limitations of traditional invasive tissue detection and cumbersome imaging evaluation, and can be used for early screening, phenotypic differentiation and auxiliary diagnosis of eCRSwNP, solving the clinical pain point of difficult early precise identification of eCRSwNP. Meanwhile, the confirmed aberrant activation of the hPGDS-PGD2 pathway may offer a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome the refractory and recurrent nature of eCRSwNP.

Article.Title: Dual-stream attention and feature fusion for human activity recognition via wearable sensors
Article.Authors: Fan J.; Jindal A.; Atapour-Abarghouei A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multi-sensor-based human activity recognition (HAR) has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Despite significant advancements achieved through deep learning, extracting refined and subtle features from multiple sensors placed on different parts of the body remains a challenge. Accurate sensor modality attention and temporal information processing are crucial for enhancing model performance. In this paper, we propose a new Temporal and Sensor-Modality Attention with Feature Fusion Network (TSFF). TSFF consists of two modules: the Temporal and Sensor Modality Attention block (TS) and the Global and Local Feature Fusion block (GLFF). The TS module extracts sensor modality attention and temporal attention in parallel using two branches, while the GLFF module dynamically fuses features from the sensor modality attention branch and the temporal stream through global and local attention mechanisms. We evaluated TSFF on three widely used public datasets–PAMAP2, Opportunity, and WISDM. When integrated with the ResNet backbone, TSFF achieved accuracies of 94.64%, 92.18%, and 97.96% on these datasets, respectively. Ablation studies further indicate that jointly modelling temporal and sensor-modality information with adaptive global–local fusion improves performance over the corresponding backbone under the evaluated settings. Visual analyses additionally provide qualitative evidence that the learned representations exhibit clearer class separation and differentiated weighting patterns across sensors and time steps.

Article.Title: Peripheral serum biomarkers and MRI-derived accelerated brain aging: a cross-sectional study using deep learning-based brain age estimation
Article.Authors: Zhong Y.; Chai L.; Jiang J.; Hao Y.; Peng F.; Ju Y.; Liu Y.; Zheng H.; Zhao X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Brain age gap is an emerging neuroimaging marker that captures interindividual variation in brain structural aging. Identifying accessible peripheral biomarkers associated with accelerated brain aging may improve early risk recognition and provide insight into systemic biological processes linked to brain health. This study investigated the associations between routine serum laboratory biomarkers and MRI-derived brain age gap in a health examination cohort. We included 852 participants with available structural MRI and routine laboratory data. Brain age was estimated from structural MRI using a deep learning model, and corrected brain age gap (CorrectedBAG) was derived to reduce age-related prediction bias. We evaluated 25 serum laboratory biomarkers spanning metabolic, immune-inflammatory, hepatic, renal, and bone/nutrition-related domains. Multivariable linear regression was used to examine associations with CorrectedBAG, and restricted cubic spline models were applied to assess potential nonlinear dose-response relationships. Binary logistic regression was further used to evaluate accelerated brain aging defined by brain age gap thresholds. Among the 25 biomarkers examined, serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) showed independent positive associations with CorrectedBAG. Higher ALP was associated with greater CorrectedBAG (β = 0.4073, 95% CI 0.1534–0.6613; P = 0.0017), as was higher NLR (β = 0.2558, 95% CI 0.0164–0.4952; P = 0.0365). In logistic regression analyses, ALP was consistently associated with greater odds of accelerated brain aging defined as BAG > 0 years (OR = 1.011, 95% CI 1.003–1.019; P = 0.010) and BAG > 3 years (OR = 1.013, 95% CI 1.004–1.023; P = 0.006). NLR was also associated with BAG > 3 years (OR = 1.333; P = 0.005). Restricted cubic spline analyses supported approximately linear associations of ALP and NLR with CorrectedBAG. In this Asian health examination cohort, higher serum ALP and NLR were associated with greater MRI-derived brain age gap. These findings suggest that routinely available serum biomarkers may capture peripheral biological processes related to accelerated brain structural aging. Further studies are warranted to clarify the temporal relationships and biological pathways underlying these associations.

Article.Title: Landscape fragmentation and carbon storage dynamics under co-evolving governance in the Shaanxi Yellow River wetland
Article.Authors: Gao M.; Lee K.; Shamsuddin A.; He B.
Article.Abstract: Wetland sustainability emerges from coupled interactions among governance, hydrology, land-use change, landscape structure and ecosystem services. Guided by Evolutionary Governance Theory, this study examines their co-evolution in the Shaanxi Yellow River Wetland from 1992 to 2023. Governance trajectories, hydrological dynamics and human land-use processes are treated as interacting antecedent conditions expressed through land use/land cover transitions, while multidimensional landscape fragmentation and land use/land cover-based estimated carbon storage are assessed as complementary structural and functional outcomes. Descriptive policy-document frequency and milestone analyses, multi-source remote sensing, the Integrated Landscape Fragmentation Index, InVEST carbon modelling, spatial autocorrelation, and overlay analysis were integrated to examine the relationships between governance evolution, landscape fragmentation and carbon storage. Estimated total carbon storage increased by 34.64%. Fragmentation, however, followed a fluctuating trajectory, intensifying through 2010, temporarily easing in 2020 and increasing again by 2023, with persistent spatial hotspots. High estimated carbon storage repeatedly co-occurred with high fragmentation, indicating heterogeneous pattern–function alignment and mismatch rather than uniform ecological recovery. Interpreted contextually, these trajectories show that more frequent policy issuance and increasing legal integration coexisted with hydrological variability, cropland transitions, aquaculture expansion and path-dependent land-use pressures. Carbon-storage gains alone therefore cannot indicate landscape recovery. Adaptive wetland governance should align restoration with hydrological processes, landscape configuration and multiple ecosystem functions.

Article.Title: Whole blood metabolomics reveals coordinated redox-one-carbon axis disruption in NSCLC: a pilot study in an Indian cohort
Article.Authors: Baswal K.; Sharma S.; Adimoolam B.; Kulandaisamy R.; Kumar V.; Singh D.; Kushwaha T.; Vardhan R.; Kumar S.; Mohan A.; Malik P.; Thota J.; Appaiahgari M.; Inampudi K.
Article.Abstract: Metabolic reprogramming is a defining feature of cancer progression. However, systemic metabolic alterations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), particularly at the whole-blood level, remain insufficiently characterized, especially in Indian patient cohorts. Untargeted whole blood metabolomic profiling was performed using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution Orbitrap Exploris 120 mass spectrometry in treatment-naïve NSCLC patients (n = 14) and age-matched healthy controls (n = 13). Data were analyzed using univariate and multivariate statistical approaches, followed by pathway enrichment and network analyses. Metabolites were annotated at MSI Level 2 using accurate mass matching and MS/MS spectral library matching. A secondary exploratory comparison was conducted between metastatic and non-metastatic cases. A total of 572 metabolites were putatively annotated, of which 40 showed significant differences between NSCLC patients and controls. Differential metabolites were mainly involved in methylation and one-carbon metabolism (SAM, SAH, MTA), antioxidant defense and redox regulation (GSH, cysteinylglycine, GSNO, γ-Glu-HMC-Gly), and energy metabolism. Additional classes included dipeptides, signaling molecules, and polyamines. PCA, sPLS-DA, and oPLS-DA showed distinct patient-control clustering, supported by VIP scores and hierarchical clustering. Enrichment analysis revealed significant associations with betaine, methylhistidine, methionine, histidine, and phosphatidylcholine metabolisms. In an exploratory subgroup analysis, five metabolites including DFA-III, 3-HC, DL-arginine, Leu-Phe, and Leu-Leu showed preliminary evidence of downregulation in metastatic compared to non-metastatic NSCLC patients. This exploratory whole-blood metabolomics study, the first in an Indian NSCLC cohort, identifies coordinated disruptions in redox and one-carbon metabolic pathways as systemic hallmarks of NSCLC. SAM, MTA, and GSH emerged as candidate biomarkers warranting validation, while DFA-III and 3-HC represent preliminary metastasis-associated leads. All findings require confirmation using authenticated reference standards and validation in larger independent cohorts before clinical utility can be established.

Article.Title: Multi‑temporal investigation of brine hydrogeochemical evolution under sustained potash mining in the Qarhan Salt Lake, Qaidam Basin, China
Article.Authors: Jing Z.; Miao Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Qarhan Salt Lake, located in the eastern Qaidam Basin of Qinghai Province, China, is the largest potash-producing base in the country. Decades of sustained brine extraction for potassium chloride (KCl) production have profoundly altered the subsurface hydrogeological and hydrogeochemical regime. However, systematic multi-temporal assessments of these changes remain scarce. This study presents a comprehensive investigation of brine dynamics across approximately 177 monitoring sites in the Qarhan mining district, comparing initial (pre-mining baseline), 2020 (fourth quarter), and 2024 (fourth quarter) datasets. Results indicate a progressive decline in brine water levels, with median depth to water table (DWT) increasing from − 0.44 m (baseline) to − 2.98 m (2020) and − 3.95 m (2024), reflecting cumulative drawdown induced by long-term extraction. Concurrently, the median KCl content decreased from 1.22% (baseline) to 0.90% (2020) and 0.57% (2024), indicating a gradual lowering of brine grade over the observation period. Between 2020 and 2024, additional hydrogeochemical shifts were observed: NaCl increased slightly from 6.39% to 7.08%, LiCl rose from 293 mg/L to 397 mg/L, while MgCl 2 declined from 17.4% to 16.6%, B 2 O 3 from 457 mg/L to 341 mg/L, total dissolved solids (TDS) from 335 g/L to 324 g/L, and specific gravity from 1.24 g/cm 3 to 1.23 g/cm 3 . Spatial contour mapping revealed pronounced heterogeneity in the distribution and temporal evolution of these parameters, potentially linked to the spatial configuration of extraction well fields and recharge pathways. These findings provide critical data support for sustainable resource management and offer new insights into the long-term hydrogeochemical evolution of continental evaporite aquifer systems under anthropogenic stress.

Article.Title: Microstructural wear analysis of laser cladded new generation mining tools
Article.Authors: Eshaghian O.; Hoseinie S.; Salimi Jazi H.
Article.Abstract: Pick tip falling and breaking are the main causes of shearer picks' failure. In the current study, by removing the tungsten carbide (WC) tip of the picks, the pick structure is integrated and the pick tip is coated with hard and resistant NiBSiFe + 60% WC nanostructure materials with laser-cladding technology, Specifically, the PTA (Plasma Transferred Arc) method to increase hardness and wear resistance. The performance of these picks was studied and compared to picks with a conventional structure in real operating conditions on the shearer of the Tabas Parvadeh Coal Mine. The results of operational field data showed that by removing the tungsten carbide tip from conventional coal cutting picks, the dominant problems caused by the failure or falling off the tungsten carbide tip of the pick have been completely solved. The wear rate after 12,000 m of cutting in the pick tip area, which has the greatest impact on pick function and lifespan, is about 5% in laser-claded picks and about 10% in traditional picks, which indicates that the final wear rate in laser-cladded picks is about half of the traditional picks, and in other words, the useful life of new picks is about twice that of traditional picks.

Article.Title: Exploratory pilot study of a spray-type probiotic delivery system for vaginal health in women at risk for bacterial vaginosis
Article.Authors: Park S.; Kim J.; You Y.; Hur Y.; Jung Y.; Lee G.; Son D.; Lee H.; Ha M.; Kim Y.
Article.Abstract: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is a common gynecological condition affecting women of reproductive age, characterized by disruption of vaginal microbiota. Current probiotic interventions, including oral supplements and vaginal suppositories, face limitations in vaginal colonization and user compliance. This study evaluated the preliminary clinical, microbiological, and safety outcomes of a novel spray-type probiotic powder (BalanceTalk Probiotic Feminine Hygiene Powder) containing multiple Lactobacillus strains for BV prevention and treatment. This single-arm exploratory clinical study was conducted at Ewha Womans University Hospital from December 2023 to June 2025. Premenopausal women aged 19–55 years were enrolled and instructed to apply the spray-type probiotic powder (containing L. plantarum , L. rhamnosus , L. paracasei , and L. crispatus ) to underwear or panty liners in contact with the vulvovaginal area once daily for 4 weeks. Primary outcomes included vaginal symptom improvement and Nugent score changes. Secondary outcomes assessed vaginal microbiome composition using 16 S rRNA gene sequencing. Statistical analyses included Wilcoxon signed-rank test, McNemar’s test, and mixed-effects logistic regression. Of 60 enrolled participants, 45 completed the study (75% completion rate). Overall improvement in vaginal symptoms approached statistical significance ( p = 0.051), particularly in the high-risk group (Nugent score ≥ 4; p = 0.020). In the high-risk group ( n = 16), mean Nugent scores decreased significantly from 6.13 to 4.63 ( p < 0.001), with 8 of 16 participants (50.0%) showing a reduction in Nugent score. Lactobacillus abundance was significantly associated with lower Nugent score (OR = 0.077, 95% CI: 0.009–0.634). Alpha diversity indices correlated significantly with Nugent score ( p < 0.05). Beta diversity and overall Lactobacillus abundance showed no significant changes. Three mild adverse events were reported with no serious safety concerns observed. The spray-type probiotic was associated with improvement in vaginal symptoms and reduced Nugent scores, particularly among women with baseline Nugent scores ≥4, with no serious safety concerns observed. The observed negative correlation between Lactobacillus abundance and Nugent score is consistent with the known role of Lactobacillus in maintaining vaginal health, although a causal effect of the intervention cannot be established from this single-arm study. Larger randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these findings and establish clinical utility.

Article.Title: Interpretable inverse design of optical multilayer thin films based on global neural adjoint
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Existing artificial intelligence methods for the inverse design of optical multilayer thin films (OMTs) often function as “black boxes,” offering limited insight into parameter–performance relationships. We propose the global neural adjoint (GNA) framework, which achieves a strong balance across six criteria: accuracy, efficiency, diversity, scalability, flexibility, and interpretability. At its core is the OMT-mixer, a forward architecture that accurately and efficiently predicts optical properties across diverse material configurations, a predefined set of layer numbers, and thicknesses. By incorporating material and constraint loss functions into the neural adjoint loss, the GNA enables scalable and flexible inverse design, while gradient-based sensitivity profiles quantify the accumulated sensitivity of the design loss to the thickness and material index of each layer during optimization. The OMT-mixer achieves accuracy comparable to transformer-based surrogates while reducing the training time per epoch by approximately 37–42%, and by approximately 61% relative to OptoGPT. Evaluated against a genetic algorithm, GNA without material loss, and OptoGPT across six test spectra and six band-pass-filter targets, the GNA achieves mean accuracy comparable to the strongest reference methods while providing significantly better peak accuracy and substantially greater diversity. Under a fabrication constraint fixing the first layer to 100-nm-thick \(\hbox {SiO}_2\) , the GNA retains significantly better peak accuracy and greater diversity than OptoGPT with top-k sampling, albeit at a higher computational cost. Gradients in the relaxed material space and the effects of rounding and filtering are quantitatively analyzed, while the reliability of the sensitivity profiles is further validated through gradient-aggregation, perturbation, and ablation analyses. These results establish the GNA as a robust, interpretable, and versatile framework for advanced OMT inverse design.

Article.Title: A scalable process aware routing architecture for resilient wireless communication in industrial and control networks
Article.Authors: Alghawli A.; Raza A.; Ahmed A.; Bakhit S.; Farman M.
Article.Abstract: Industrial carbon-capture plants depend on timely and reliable communication among distributed sensors, controllers, and process models. Existing studies commonly examine fault recovery, energy-aware routing, reinforcement learning, or digital-twin monitoring as separate problems, leaving limited evidence on their coordinated use in one reproducible industrial communication framework. This study presents a process-aware MeshStar wireless sensor network (WSN) that combines low-overhead star clusters with redundant mesh links among cluster routers. A tabular Q-learning controller selects recovery and traffic-management actions from network reliability, latency, congestion, residual energy, link availability, and thermal-process criticality. The framework is evaluated through OMNeT++/INET network simulation coupled with a MATLAB/Simulink carbon-capture process model. Thirty independent seeds are used for each method and operating scenario, with comparisons against static Dijkstra, RPL-MRHOF, energy-aware RPL, conventional Q-routing, and deep Q-network routing. Under the revised evaluation protocol, the proposed method achieved a 95th-percentile latency of 84.6 ms, a packet delivery ratio (PDR) of 98.32%, and a route-recovery time of 3.74 s, corresponding to improvements of 12.6%, 0.78 percentage points, and 16.1%, respectively, over the strongest baseline. Scalability, security stress, process stability, and scenario-based economic results are reported separately. Because the validation is software-dominant, the findings demonstrate comparative feasibility rather than field-deployment readiness.
