Article.Title: Bioassay-guided isolation and characterization of antiplasmodial compounds from Ximenia caffra bark and their interaction with PfHsp70-1
Article.Authors: Maboya K.; Mhlongo M.; Pooe O.; Simelane M.
Article.Abstract: Malaria continues to pose a major global health challenge, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, where increasing resistance to frontline antiplasmodial therapies threatens disease control efforts. The emergence of artemisinin-resistant Plasmodium falciparum strains necessitates the discovery of novel antiplasmodial agents. Ximenia caffra , traditionally used across sub-Saharan Africa for treating various ailments, represents an underexplored source of antiplasmodial compounds. Bark samples of Ximenia caffra were sequentially extracted using solvents of increasing polarity (hexane, dichloromethane, ethyl acetate, and methanol). Extracts were screened for antiplasmodial activity using the parasite lactate dehydrogenase (pLDH) assay. Active extracts underwent bioassay-guided fractionation. Isolated compounds were characterized using LC-MS and NMR spectroscopy and evaluated for cytotoxicity against CHO cells. Mechanism of action studies were conducted using recombinant Pf Hsp70-1, including malate dehydrogenase aggregation assays and intrinsic tryptophan fluorescence spectroscopy. Hexane and methanol extracts demonstrated potent antiplasmodial activity (IC₅₀ = 5.96 and 7.48 µg/mL, respectively). Four compounds were isolated and identified: lupeol, betulinic acid, ursolic acid, and palmitoleic acid. Lupeol and ursolic acid showed moderate antiplasmodial activity (IC₅₀ = 7.56 and 8.39 µg/mL; 17.7 and 18.4 µM, respectively). While betulinic acid and palmitoleic acid showed weaker antiplasmodial activity, all four isolated compounds showed low cytotoxicity against CHO cells (IC₅₀ > 50 µg/mL), indicating a favourable selectivity margin, particularly for lupeol and ursolic acid. Mechanistic studies revealed that ursolic acid and palmitoleic acid potently inhibited Pf Hsp70-1 chaperone activity, while intrinsic tryptophan fluorescence demonstrated distinct binding modes for each compound. X. caffra bark contains antiplasmodial compounds warranting further investigation. The identified triterpenoids represent candidates for antiplasmodial drug development, with ursolic acid of particular interest for combining direct antiplasmodial activity with candidate inhibitory activity against the essential Pf Hsp70-1 chaperone, lending in vitro support to the plant’s traditional medicinal use.

Article.Title: Assessing preparedness for extreme weather events in community health centers and free clinics across North Carolina
Article.Authors: Speicher K.; Reed C.; Shapley-Quinn K.; Runkle J.
Article.Abstract: Extreme weather is increasingly affecting population health in North Carolina, with disproportionate impacts on communities served by safety-net clinics. Despite growing recognition of weather-related health risks, limited evidence exists on the readiness of community health centers and free and charitable clinics to address these challenges. We conducted a community-engaged, mixed-methods study to assess extreme weather risk perceptions, institutional barriers, anticipatory guidance, and preparedness among safety-net clinics across North Carolina. Following eight regional listening sessions with safety-net clinics, we developed and administered a statewide survey to administrators, clinicians, and staff affiliated with community health centers and charitable clinics between August and September 2024. Descriptive statistics summarized quantitative responses and narrative synthesis were applied to open-ended questions. A total of 199 respondents representing safety-net clinics statewide completed the survey. More than 90% agreed that climate change was occurring and affecting North Carolina. Nearly three-quarters of respondents (73.9%) perceived climate change as likely to significantly affect their service populations. However, fewer than half (45.8%) reported access to sufficient workplace information to take action. More than 90% of respondents ranked air pollution and extreme heat as the top climate concerns, while > 80% ranked seasonal allergies and mental health as the most salient health impacts. Safety-net clinics in North Carolina demonstrated high concern, but limited capacity to address weather-related health risks. Closing this awareness-action gap will require targeted investments in staffing, funding, clinical screening tools and anticipatory guidance, and implementation support to strengthen climate resilience in safety-net health systems.

Article.Title: Stromal-derived Anxa1 engages neutrophil Fpr2 to brake the Nlrp3 inflammasome in otitis media with effusion
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Wen Z.; Lu X.; Tong Q.; Qin M.; Li H.; Sun S.; Yu H.
Article.Abstract: Uncontrolled neutrophilic inflammation and Nlrp3 inflammasome activation contribute to a wide range of mucosal disorders, yet the endogenous circuits that constrain this process at the cellular level remain poorly defined. Using single-cell RNA sequencing of the Eustachian tube in a rat model of ovalbumin-induced otitis media with effusion (OME), we identified massive neutrophil infiltration coupled with intrinsic Nlrp3 inflammasome activation as dominant features of the early OME microenvironment. Systematic intercellular communication analysis using CellChat predicted a disease-specific Annexin A1 (Anxa1)–formyl peptide receptor 2 (Fpr2) ligand-receptor axis converging on infiltrating neutrophils. Intratympanic pre-treatment with Anxa1 dose-dependently suppressed Nlrp3, IL-1β, and IL-18 without altering the priming cytokine TNF-α, reduced middle ear effusion volume on micro-CT, and preserved ciliary and goblet cell architecture. Co-administration of the Fpr2 antagonist WRW4 reversed the Anxa1-mediated reduction in IL-18 and middle ear effusion, indicating that the Anxa1-Fpr2 axis functions as an Fpr2-dependent checkpoint that limits inflammasome amplification rather than initial inflammatory priming. These findings identify a pharmacologically tractable, neutrophil-targeted brake on the Nlrp3 inflammasome and provide a mechanism-based direction for local anti-inflammatory therapy in OME.

Article.Title: Post-fatigue neuromuscular performance after pre-fatigue nap or quiet rest in men with ACL reconstruction: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Bafrouei M.; Seyedi M.; Mirkarimpour S.; Mirmoezzi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To compare post-fatigue landing mechanics, dynamic balance, and knee joint repositioning between men with anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and dynamic knee valgus (DKV) who underwent a short daytime nap opportunity versus quiet rest before a standardized functional fatigue protocol. An assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial was conducted in 44 men. Participants were allocated to a 30-min daytime nap opportunity or a time- and environment-matched quiet-rest control group using block randomization. After baseline assessment, participants underwent either the nap or quiet-rest intervention, followed by a standardized functional fatigue protocol based on stretch-shortening cycle exercises. Actigraphy-estimated sleep duration during the nap opportunity was 22.8 ± 4.6 min. Landing mechanics, Y-Balance test normalized composite score, and knee joint position sense absolute error (at 30 ∘ and 60 ∘ ) were assessed at baseline) before the nap/quiet-rest intervention (and immediately after the fatigue protocol. Between-group differences in post-fatigue outcomes were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusted for baseline values. Holm–Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons. The trial was retrospectively registered with the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20250519065806N4) on 26 June 2026. After adjustment for baseline values, post-fatigue landing-error scores were lower in the nap group than in the quiet-rest group (adjusted mean difference, − 1.39 points (95% CI, − 2.03 to − 0.74); p < 0.001; partial η² = 0.32). Knee joint repositioning error at 60° was also lower in the nap group (adjusted mean difference, − 2.41° (95% CI, − 3.44 to − 1.37); p < 0.001; partial η²= 0.35). No significant between-group differences were observed for Y-Balance test normalized composite score (adjusted mean difference, − 0.79%; 95% CI, − 2.15 to 0.56; p = 0.244; partial η² = 0.03) or repositioning error at 30° (adjusted mean difference, 0.91° (95% CI, − 0.61 to 2.42); p = 0.235; partial η² = 0.03). Post-fatigue landing-error scores and knee joint repositioning error at 60° were lower in participants assigned to the short daytime nap opportunity than in those assigned to quiet rest, whereas no between-group differences were observed for the Y-Balance test normalized composite score or repositioning error at 30°. Because outcomes were not assessed immediately after the nap or quiet-rest period and before the fatigue protocol, these findings do not establish that napping specifically attenuated the response to fatigue. Clinical trial registration: This study was retrospectively registered with the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT) under registration number IRCT20250519065806N4 on 26 June 2026.

Article.Title: An enhanced model-based EEG source imaging method captures dynamic changes during motor skill learning
Article.Authors: Daryayi M.; Hassanzadeh Z.; Mahdavian A.; Bahrami F.; Kalhor A.; Moshiri B.
Article.Abstract: Understanding brain reorganization during motor learning requires methods with both high temporal and spatial resolution. We developed an enhanced model-based approach to solve the EEG inverse problem that combines a multi-layer perceptron neural network with finite element modeling for subject-specific head conductivity estimation. The framework resolves up to six simultaneously active sources across 116 cortical and subcortical regions and achieves 85.98% source localization accuracy, outperforming existing methods (67.1% accuracy, 1 even under varying noise conditions. A dedicated leakage analysis using single- and multi-region simulations confirmed minimal cross-talk between cortical motor and deep subcortical/cerebellar sources, supporting reliable separation of activity across brain depths. As a proof-of-concept application, we used this framework to analyze EEG data from five healthy adults performing a novel foot-drawing motor learning task across multiple sessions, with behavioral performance improving after the fourth session. Model-based source estimates revealed a broad reorganization of cortical and subcortical activity across sessions, consistent with functional refinement of motor networks with practice; given the small cohort ( n = 5), these findings are preliminary and offered as suggestive of learning-related dynamics rather than definitive evidence. This enhanced model-based EEG source localization approach offers a practical, non-invasive method for combining computational modeling with neuroimaging of motor behavior.

Article.Title: Associations of planned pre-iftar walking and Ramadan step count with cardiometabolic changes among Palestinian university students
Article.Authors: Al-Lahham S.; Hayek M.; Zabin L.; Said N.; Ziraeni A.; Najajra F.; Alrob S.; Al Ali M.; Shokr E.; Sabola N.
Article.Abstract: Ramadan fasting is accompanied by changes in eating patterns, sleep, hydration, and physical activity. Walking may be a practical health-promoting behavior during Ramadan, but its association with cardiometabolic changes among young adults remains insufficiently studied. This study examined whether planned pre-iftar walking and mobile-app-recorded daily step count during Ramadan were associated with cardiometabolic changes among apparently healthy Palestinian university students. A quantitative observational pretest, posttest study was conducted among university students in Palestine during Ramadan 2022. Cardiometabolic indicators were measured before Ramadan and at the end of Ramadan. Walking was assessed using two distinct exposure measures: planned walking for approximately 1 h before iftar on 4–7 days per week and mobile-app-recorded average daily step count during Ramadan. Outcomes included changes in weight, BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, heart rate, fasting glucose, C-reactive protein, triglycerides, HDL-C, HbA1c, and sleep duration. Unadjusted group comparisons, Spearman correlations, baseline-adjusted linear regression models, and false discovery rate correction for multiple testing were performed. Planned pre-iftar walking status was available for 112 participants, including 80 in the comparison group and 32 in the planned-walking group. The planned-walking group showed greater unadjusted reductions in weight (− 1.46 ± 1.59 vs. − 0.53 ± 2.01 kg, p = 0.024) and BMI (− 0.56 ± 0.61 vs. − 0.19 ± 0.76 kg/m², p = 0.018), but neither difference remained significant after false discovery rate correction (both q = 0.153). In baseline-adjusted models, planned walking was not significantly associated with post-Ramadan weight (B = − 0.82 kg, 95% CI − 1.69 to 0.05; p = 0.064) or BMI (B = − 0.33 kg/m², 95% CI − 0.67 to 0.02; p = 0.063), and no significant association was observed for triglycerides or the other assessed cardiometabolic outcomes. Among 68 participants with interpretable Ramadan daily step-count data, step count was not significantly associated with cardiometabolic change scores in Spearman or adjusted regression analyses. Planned pre-iftar walking was associated with nominally greater reductions in weight and BMI in unadjusted analyses, but these associations were not robust after adjustment for multiple testing and baseline characteristics. Ramadan daily step count was not independently associated with the assessed cardiometabolic changes. These findings provide exploratory real-world evidence on physical activity during Ramadan and support the need for larger prospective or randomized studies using standardized activity measurement and verified adherence before specific pre-iftar walking recommendations can be made.

Article.Title: Remote ischemic conditioning mitigates diesel exhaust-induced pulmonary fibrosis by alleviating pulmonary inflammation and fibrogenesis
Article.Authors: Kumari S.; Mishra K.; Singh K.; Kumar G K.; Kumar R.; Parihar A.; Kumari R.; Nagar E.; Arora N.; Bansal V.; Mishra A.
Article.Abstract: Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC), a promising non-pharmacological strategy, mitigates ischemia-reperfusion injury in multiple conditions. However, its potential as a therapeutic strategy in pulmonary fibrosis (PF), which is associated with poor survival outcomes and limited pharmacotherapies, remains unexplored. Thus, the present study aimed to explore the therapeutic utility of RIC in a diesel exhaust (DE)-induced mouse model recapitulating PF pathology. The effects of RIC were comprehensively assessed by measuring physiological and molecular endpoints, including weight, heart rate variability (HRV), lung histopathology, circulating plasma biomarkers, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cytokine profiles, and indices of pulmonary mitochondrial health in age-matched mice allocated to nine study groups. DE-induced PF groups receiving RIC showed marked improvements in body weight, HRV, and lung mitochondrial function, along with substantial attenuation of histopathological damage and significant reductions in inflammatory and fibrotic markers. These effects were comparable to those observed in the pharmacotherapy group receiving pirfenidone, suggesting that RIC may have the potential to mitigate DE-induced pulmonary fibrotic damage. Further, the observations were supported by bulk transcriptome sequencing and analysis of lung tissue from eight experimental groups, which revealed downregulation of PF markers in RIC-receiving groups, highlighting RIC’s efficacy in attenuating PF features. Additionally, potential PF-relevant markers, including Calhm6 , Hrc , Dnase1l3 , Pla2g2d , Stab2 and Timd4 , were identified across these groups that may be linked to therapeutic benefits conferred by RIC.

Article.Title: Increased risk of hepatic outcomes after SARS-CoV-2 infection in individuals with pre-existing chronic liver disease
Article.Authors: Collins J.; Hadidchi R.; Katz L.; Lee P.; Channar A.; Henry S.; Duong T.
Article.Abstract: Viral infections can accelerate chronic liver disease (CLD) progression, yet whether SARS-CoV-2 infection drives worse long-term hepatic outcomes in patients with pre-existing CLD remains unknown. This retrospective cohort study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with mortality, hepatic decompensation, and abnormal fibrosis-related laboratory markers in patients with pre-existing CLD up to 4.5 years post-infection. Adults with pre-existing CLD in the Montefiore Health System in the Bronx, NY (February 2020-August 2024) were stratified by COVID-19 hospitalization status and 1:1 propensity-score matched to uninfected controls, with associations estimated using Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models. Among 37,559 adults with pre-existing CLD, 6,178 tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 (2,182 was hospitalized for COVID-19). Compared with matched controls, hospitalized COVID-19 patients showed higher mortality (HR = 2.92, 95% CI 2.00-4.27, p < 0.005) and higher odds of abnormal Fibrosis 4 score (FIB4, OR = 1.37, 1.21–1.56), aspartate aminotransferase (AST, OR = 1.60, 1.04–2.47), and platelet count (PLT, OR = 1.40, 1.02–1.92) within the first year, with FIB4 remaining abnormal beyond one year (OR = 1.20, 1.06–1.37, p = 0.006). In contrast, non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients did not show increased mortality but showed lower odds of hepatic decompensation, and lower odds of abnormal aminotransferases within the first year and beyond ( p < 0.005). These paradoxically favorable associations likely reflect selection bias, as non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients represent a healthier subgroup while controls are enriched for sicker patients. A sensitivity analysis in a matched cohort with FIB4 staging confirmed overall findings. Severe, hospitalized COVID-19 is a clinically actionable risk marker in patients with pre-existing CLD, warranting structured hepatic surveillance, whereas patients with mild infection can be reassured.

Article.Title: Evaluation of aspirin effects on zebrafish (Danio rerio) embryos at clinically relevant plasma concentrations: a multi-omics approach
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Liu Y.; Sun H.; Chen J.; Luo M.; Lin Z.; Chen F.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Aspirin is a widely used clinical medication during pregnancy that can pass through the placental barrier. While high-dose animal studies have linked aspirin to developmental toxicities like neural tube defects and other structural abnormalities, its effects across a broader clinical concentration spectrum remain unclear. In this study, we evaluated the concentration-dependent toxicity of aspirin during zebrafish embryonic and larval development. The zebrafish embryos and larvae exposed to aspirin induced dose-dependent decreases in heart rate, body length, and locomotor activity ( measured by movement speed and distance); all changes were statistically significant. Although the incidence of curled tails exhibited an upward trend, it did not achieve statistical significance. In situ hybridization, transcriptomic, and epigenomic analyses revealed neurodevelopmental, muscular, cardiovascular, and renal abnormalities consistent with the relevant research reports. This study outlines potential mechanisms between differentially expressed genes and molecular modification effects of aspirin at varying concentrations. This provides a new reference for a comprehensive toxicological profile and evaluates the potential developmental risks of aspirin exposure during pregnancy.

Article.Title: A statistical learning framework for explainable forest disturbance-agent attribution with provable guarantees and theoretical foundations for spatial transfer
Article.Authors: Ahmad K.; Abdelfattah W.; Sallah M.; Alrashood J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We develop the mathematical foundations of a framework that attributes a disturbance agent, namely wildfire, harvest, insect defoliation, windthrow, or drought, to each disturbance event detected in standardized satellite time-series change metrics. The attribution task is posed as a statistical decision problem on a feature space built from spectral-temporal descriptors, object geometry, terrain, and climate. Within this formulation we prove the Bayes optimality of the posterior-maximizing rule and of its cost-sensitive counterpart, a finite-sample generalization bound for the empirical-risk minimizer over a finite class, the variance-reduction identity that governs ensemble estimators together with a bias-variance decomposition, an ordering between the Gini and entropy impurities, the convexity and second-order optimality conditions of gradient-boosted trees, the gradient identities of the softmax and focal objectives, the efficiency, symmetry, and null-player properties of the Shapley attribution used for explanation, the order preservation of temperature scaling, and the distribution-free lower and upper coverage bounds of the marginal and class-conditional conformal predictors used for uncertainty. We further prove an unbiasedness and variance result for the design-based accuracy estimator and a decomposition of the cross-region transfer gap, together with an estimable form of that decomposition. Many of these results are specializations of established statistical-learning theory to the attribution setting; the contribution lies in their unified formulation on a standardized metric product, in the explicit statement of the assumptions under which each guarantee holds, and in a small number of new corollaries. The paper is theoretical: all results are established by proof and illustrated with synthetic numerical examples, no empirical forest-disturbance dataset is analysed, and the empirical transferability, calibration, and accuracy of an implemented system remain to be evaluated.

Article.Title: Salvianolic acid B antagonizes hepatocarcinogenesis by inhibiting the p300/pSmad2 complex
Article.Authors: Zhou H.; Wang M.; Wang Y.; Ren H.; Zhang Y.; Chen R.; Gong Y.; Yang Y.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: E1A-binding protein p300 (p300)/CREB-binding protein (CBP) and phosphorylated Smad2 (pSmad2C/L) are highly activated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but their relationship remains unclear. Salvianolic (Sal B) exhibits potential anti-HCC activities. We previously reported Sal B downregulates p300/CBP and pSmad2C/L, thereby inhibiting hepatic stellate cell activation and exerting anti-fibrotic effects. Given that hepatic fibrosis is a vital early stage of HCC, we hypothesized that the anti-HCC activities of Sal B are likely to be correlated with p300/CBP and pSmad2C/L. Therefore, we employed diethylnitrosamine (DEN)/carbon tetrachloride (CCl 4 )/ethanol (C 2 H 5 OH)-induced HCC mice and TGF-β1-stimulated HepG2 and HuH-7 cells to explore Sal B intervention. Meanwhile, co-immunoprecipitation and nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation were used to assess the binding and subcellular localization of p300 with pSmad2C/L. This study revealed that Sal B significantly enhanced hepatic function, ameliorated histopathological abnormalities, and downregulated p300/CBP and pSmad2C/L protein levels in DEN/CCl 4 /C 2 H 5 OH-induced HCC mouse model. Meanwhile, Sal B suppressed proliferation and invasion in both HepG2 and HuH-7 cells, reduced p300/CBP mRNA and protein expression, and decreased pSmad2C/L protein levels. Additionally, Sal B suppressed the nuclear expression of p300, pSmad2C and pSmad2L, and p300 was found to specifically interact with pSmad2C. Collectively, these data illustrated that Sal B might antagonize hepatocarcinogenesis via inhibiting p300/pSmad2 complex, providing a molecular basis for its therapeutic potential against HCC.

Article.Title: Physics-informed learning detects islanding and discriminates power-quality disturbances in grid-forming inverter-dominated distribution networks
Article.Authors: Xu Y.; Seedahmed E.; Alyounis E.; Kraiem N.; Ahmad M.
Article.Abstract: The proliferation of grid-forming (GFM) inverters in modern distribution networks has fundamentally altered the islanding-detection problem. Unlike grid-following converters, droop- and virtual-synchronous-generator (VSG)-controlled GFM units actively regulate voltage and frequency, suppressing the very deviations that conventional passive schemes rely upon and thereby enlarging the non-detection zone (NDZ) under near-balanced power conditions. This paper proposes a Physics-Informed Lightning-Search-Optimised Temporal Attention Network (PI-LSO-TAN) that jointly detects unintentional islanding and discriminates it from power-quality disturbances (PQDs) and non-islanding faults in GFM-dominated feeders. The framework fuses a physics-informed feature set rate-of-change-of-frequency (ROCOF) estimated from the analytic signal, total harmonic distortion, phase-jump and current-imbalance descriptors with a raw-window convolutional embedding processed by a self-attention pooling layer. A Lightning Search Algorithm (LSA) simultaneously optimises the network hyperparameters and a physics-informed decision threshold, removing manual tuning. Across 10 independent dataset realisations of a documented, fully reproducible synthetic GFM feeder operated in the near-balanced NDZ regime, PI-LSO-TAN attains a four-class test accuracy of 96.34% (SD 0.96 percentage points), a macro-F1 of 0.9636 and an islanding recall of 93.49% at an islanding false-positive rate of 0.70%, misdeclaring 2.40 of 175 power-quality windows as islanding. Two findings define what the method does and does not contribute. First, when ten baselines spanning kernel, ensemble, convolutional, recurrent, attention-based and graph architectures are given the identical physics-informed side-channel, all 11 models fall within 1.20 percentage points of one another; none of the 6 deep sequence architectures differs significantly from the proposed model under Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests, and of the ten baselines only 1 differ significantly at all MLP-SVM hybrid, ahead by up to 0.73 percentage points these being among the simplest feature-space classifiers in the comparison. On this task the discriminative power resides in the physics-informed representation rather than in the temporal-modelling mechanism. Substituting an alternative fourteen-dimensional representation confirms this directly principal components of the raw window reach 52.37%, wavelet band energies 73.60%, generic statistics 62.94%, and a purely learned embedding 30.17%, against 96.20% for the physics-informed set. Second, noise resilience is a property of the training distribution, not of the architecture: training at a single SNR leaves accuracy at 52.18% when the measurement noise floor moves to 30dB, whereas sampling the training SNR across 15 dB to 50 dB restores 88.79% at 30dB and 84.54% at 20dB for a cost of − 6.14 percentage points at the nominal operating point. The practical contribution is protective rather than architectural. A security-calibrated passive over/under-frequency, ROCOF and over/under-voltage relay detects none of the 3872 scanned near-balanced islanding events, leaving a 100.0% non-detection area, whereas the proposed detector reduces it to 0.00%, with no cell of the power-mismatch plane falling below 87.5% detection. Measured sliding-window detection latency is 80 ms on average and 130 ms at the 95th percentile, inside the 2 s envelope of IEEE 1547-2018 and IEC 62116, at 337 μsof computation per window and 28.7 kB of parameters. The results indicate that reliable anti-islanding protection in inverter-dominated grids is obtained by pairing a physics-informed representation with noise-augmented training, and that the resulting detector covers a region of the operating plane in which conventional passive protection is blind by construction.

Article.Title: Screening compounds of the phenylpropanoid pathway and commercial products to mitigate methane emissions using batch culture in vitro incubations
Article.Authors: Hodgson M.; V. Chaves A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Enteric methane (CH₄) produced during ruminal fermentation is a major contributor to agricultural greenhouse gas emissions and represents an energy loss to the animal. Plant-derived phenolic compounds have been proposed as dietary strategies to mitigate methane formation; however, their efficacy depends on compound identity and inclusion level. This study evaluated phenylpropanoid-derived phenolics identified in Brassica rapa subsp. chinensis and selected commercial feed additives for their effects on methane production and ruminal fermentation. Lucerne ( Medicago sativa ) pellets (0.5 g dry matter) were incubated for 24 h in three independent runs, each using rumen fluid collected from a pasture-fed, ruminally cannulated cow. Each treatment was represented by three technical bottles per run, run × treatment was the experimental unit, and variation among bottles was retained as residual error. Data were analysed separately by category using mixed models. Compound or product, active-treatment dose, and their interaction were fixed effects, whereas incubation run and run × treatment were random effects. Control-inclusive overall dose-response tests, compound- or product-specific orthogonal-polynomial contrasts, and Dunnett-adjusted comparisons with the control were conducted separately. Treatments included p-coumaric acid (5, 10, and 15 mM), trans-cinnamic acid (5, 10, and 15 mM), their 1:1 combination (2.5 + 2.5, 5 + 5, and 7.5 + 7.5 mM), gallic acid (5, 10, and 15 mM), tannic acid (actual concentrations of 0.41, 0.81, 1.22, and 4.05 mM after correction for 81% purity), N-carbamyl-L-glutamic acid (5, 10, and 15 mM), and two proprietary formulations (4.5% and 9% of substrate dry matter). The proprietary products comprised a medium-chain fatty-acid blend and an organic-acid blend with plant essential oils; individual ingredient concentrations were not disclosed by the manufacturer. Gas production, CH₄ concentration and yield, in vitro dry matter disappearance (IVDMD), fermentation pH, and volatile fatty acid (VFA) profiles were measured. p-Coumaric acid reduced CH₄ concentration and yield in a dose-dependent manner, with CH₄ yield reduced by up to 43.3% at 15 mM; however, IVDMD was reduced at ≥ 10 mM. CH₄ yield decreased linearly with trans-cinnamic acid, although only the 27.4% reduction at 15 mM differed from the control. The combination reduced CH₄ yield by up to 41.4% and maintained IVDMD at the two lower inclusion levels. Gallic acid did not affect CH₄. Tannic acid reduced CH₄ yield by 19.4%–85.0%; the lowest dose caused no detectable reductions in gas production, IVDMD, or total VFA concentration, whereas higher doses increasingly inhibited fermentation. N-Carbamyl-L-glutamic acid and the two proprietary formulations did not reduce CH₄. The hypothesis was therefore partially supported: the lowest tested doses of p-coumaric acid and its combination with trans-cinnamic acid produced the clearest selective reductions in CH₄, while low-dose tannic acid was also effective but had a narrow margin before adverse fermentation effects emerged. These responses warrant in vivo validation and dose optimisation.

Article.Title: Dynamic periodic event-triggered adaptive PD-like composite neural control with iterative disturbance observer for 3D tracking of UUVs
Article.Authors: Li Q.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: This work focuses on the 3D tracking control issue for underactuated underwater vehicles (UUVs) subject to model uncertainties, external disturbances, and actuator mechanical degradation by mechanical wear. To reconstruct the uncertain dynamics within the system, an adaptive PD-like composite neural network (NN) is constructed. In contrast with conventional adaptive NNs, the constructed PD-like composite NN accelerates the network learning process and improves the reconstruction accuracy of uncertain dynamics. Furthermore, to counteract the adverse effects of external disturbances, an NN disturbance observer is designed with a gain iteration protocol. Unlike conventional disturbance observers that employ fixed gains, the designed observer dynamically adjusts its gains through an iterative protocol to achieve accurate disturbance estimation and enhance the robustness of the UUV system. To mitigate actuator wear and avoid unnecessary control updates, a dynamic periodic event-triggered protocol is proposed, which inherently precludes Zeno behavior. Building on these developments, a novel adaptive PD-like composite neural control law that integrates the aforementioned iterative disturbance observer and the dynamic periodic event-triggered protocol is formulated. The Lyapunov theory is employed to demonstrate that all signals within the closed-loop control system are bounded. Simulation results substantiate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed control strategy.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: 3D trajectory tracking; adaptive control; event-triggered control; unmanned underwater vehicles

Article.Title: Microbial profiling of endometrioma and eutopic endometrium using 16S rRNA sequencing
Article.Authors: Furui K.; Muraoka A.; Bayasula N/A.; Takeda T.; Seki T.; Miyake N.; Sonehara R.; Nakamura T.; Kajiyama H.
Article.Abstract: The involvement of microbiota in the pathogenesis of endometriosis has been increasingly suggested; however, existing evidence remains inconsistent, largely owing to the challenges of analyzing extremely low-biomass samples. To clarify whether distinct microbial signatures exist among the non-endometriosis endometrium (nEM), eutopic endometrium with endometriosis (eEM), and endometrioma, we performed a comparative microbiome analysis using 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing of the V4–V5 region on an Illumina NextSeq 1000 platform. Of 48 samples collected, 37 (10 nEM, 18 eEM, and 9 endometrioma) yielded data suitable for analysis. No significant differences were observed in alpha or beta diversity. Lactobacillus was the predominant genus in both nEM and eEM, although no genus differed significantly between groups after correction for multiple comparisons. Sequence-level examination of all 146 amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) showed that background-associated sequences accounted for 41% of the dataset. Because no extraction blank was processed, contamination among the remaining sequences could not be excluded. Inter-individual variation exceeded any difference between groups, and no disease-specific microbial signature was identified. These findings indicate that 16S rRNA gene sequencing of low-biomass endometrial tissue is unlikely to yield a usable biomarker for endometriosis on its own.

Article.Title: Systematic review and meta-regression analysis of the prevalence of Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever in humans, ticks and animals in Sub-Saharan Africa from 1980 to 2025
Article.Authors: Wasswa A.; Rascón-García K.; Abizera H.; Ainebyoona S.; Amanyire W.; Nkamwesiga J.; Kimuda P.; Mayanja M.; Muhanguzi D.
Article.Abstract: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) is an emerging infectious tick-borne virus that continues to impact public health globally. To re-evaluate and improve CCHFV control strategies in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), there’s a need to aggregate CCHFV prevalence data and explore the factors which affect observed variations in prevalence in humans, animals and ticks. Articles reporting prevalence of CCHFV in humans, animals and ticks in SSA between 1980 and 2025 were retrieved from five research databases, namely: Scopus, PubMed, Springer Nature, Web of Science and Science Direct. A random effects model was fit using a binomial generalised linear mixed effects model with a logit link to estimate pooled prevalences for each host species, along with their 95% confidence intervals. Between study-variation (heterogeneity) was assessed using index statistic (I 2 ). Subgroup analyses, meta-regressions and sensitivity analyses were performed using trim and fill and leave-one-out methods to identify sources of variation and reliability of results, respectively. Evidence of asymmetry was assessed using the Luis-Furuya Kanamori (LFK) index. Following PRISMA guidelines, 114 studies from 31 SSA countries that obtained samples from twenty-two host species were included in the analysis. Molecular and serological detection methods estimated a CCHFV pooled prevalence of 1.15% (95% CI: 0.70–1.89) , 31.11% (95% CI: 21.56–42.81) among humans and cattle respectively and pooled pool-positivity of 1.04% (95% CI: 0.57–1.90) in ticks. East and southern African countries accounted for the highest prevalence among humans and cattle, respectively. The diagnostic method used and region where the study was conducted accounted for the majority of variation in prevalence of CCHFV in cattle and humans respectively. In this study, we detected widespread circulation of CCHFV in non- Hyalomma ticks, signaling a need to explore the potential role of other tick species in transmission of CCHFV in SSA, as well as a need to evaluate the impact tick acaricide resistance might have on the persistence and maintenance of CCHFV in ticks. Despite limitations, such as under-representation of countries in central Africa and other host species, such as wildlife and birds, the data generated in this review can be an important tool in the design of regional and cross-continental control strategies for CCHFV .

Article.Title: Comparison of lower extremity peak muscle forces and force-generating capacities during the functional side hop test in male collegiate football players with and without chronic ankle instability
Article.Authors: Suwanmana S.; Jamkrajang P.; Robinson M.; Kim H.; Kong T.; Limroongreungrat W.
Article.Abstract: Chronic ankle instability (CAI) alters lower extremity kinematics and neuromuscular function during dynamic tasks, yet potential compensatory mechanisms in muscle forces and force-generating capacity remain unexplored during repeated lateral movements. This study examined muscle force and force-generating capacity as primary outcome measures, with kinematics and performance as secondary measures, during the side-hop test (SHT) in athletes with and without CAI. Thirteen male football players with CAI and thirteen healthy (CON) players performed the SHT with maximum effort, during which motion capture, force platform, and electromyography (EMG) data were recorded. Individual peak muscle forces and force-generating capacities were estimated using a scaled, generic lower-limb musculoskeletal model in OpenSim, driven by joint kinematics and ground reaction forces via static optimisation, verified against EMG signals. Players with CAI demonstrated significantly greater peak force of the peroneus longus (CAI: 0.14 ± 0.05 N/kg vs. CON: 0.08 ± 0.02 N/kg; p = 0.001) and vastii muscles (CAI: 5.34 ± 2.25 N/kg vs. CON: 2.52 ± 1.32 N/kg; p < 0.001) during the lateral hop contact (LHC), alongside elevated vastii force-generating capacity during the medial hop contact (MHC) (CAI: 0.86 ± 0.07 vs. CON: 0.73 ± 0.12; p = 0.005). Additionally, athletes with CAI exhibited significantly increased sagittal ankle ROM, prolonged ground contact time and slower completion times in the SHT ( p < 0.05). These findings suggest that CAI athletes exhibited compensatory adaptations in muscle force and force-generating capacity, which may be associated with an ankle functional deficit and reflected in altered lower-extremity kinematics and reduced SHT performance.

Article.Title: p300 exacerbates lung injury following cardiopulmonary bypass in AnxA1-deficient rats
Article.Authors: Han M.; Zhang H.; Zhou Y.; Dou X.; Zhuang Y.; Chen S.; Zhang H.
Article.Abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is one of the most common postoperative complications, significantly impairing postoperative recovery and, in severe cases, endangering patient survival. CPB-induced ALI is predominantly associated with systemic inflammatory responses, although multiple factors contribute to this inflammation. Annexin A1 (AnxA1), a potent anti-inflammatory protein, is widely expressed in various organs and has been shown to mitigate lung injury by suppressing inflammatory responses in ALI. In contrast, p300, a histone acetyltransferase, promotes inflammation by enhancing the expression of pro-inflammatory mediators in ALI. These opposing roles suggest a critical regulatory interplay between AnxA1 and p300 in modulating pulmonary inflammation. This study establishes a clinically relevant cardiopulmonary bypass combined left lung ischemia-reperfusion (CPB-I/R) acute lung injury (ALI) rat model, distinct from widely used LPS-induced ALI models, to dissect the interactive regulatory relationship between AnxA1 and p300 in perioperative lung injury for the first time. CPB triggers systemic inflammatory priming, while unilateral left lung ischemia-reperfusion imposes localized pulmonary endothelial damage; the two insults together produce synergistic severe lung injury, which closely mimics clinical cardiac surgery-related perioperative lung dysfunction. In this study, we established CPB-induced ALI models in both wild-type (WT) and AnxA1-knockout rats. We observed upregulated p300 expression and exacerbated inflammatory responses in AnxA1-knockout rats compared to WT controls. Furthermore, co-expression and potential protein complex formation between AnxA1 and p300 were detected in WT animals; however, the current co-immunoprecipitation assay lacks critical IgG negative controls and reciprocal pull-down validation, limiting definitive confirmation of specific bidirectional protein binding.Notably, pharmacological inhibition of p300 with C646 partially alleviated lung injury in the CPB-induced ALI model. Intriguingly, C646 treatment reduced total p300 protein abundance in lung tissue despite functioning as a catalytic activity inhibitor, which we further interpret via potential transcriptional feedback and protein stability mechanisms. Our findings provide novel mechanistic insights into the pathogenesis of CPB-related ALI and highlight the AnxA1-p300 axis as a promising potential therapeutic target, offering a theoretical foundation for future clinical interventions.

Article.Title: Bacillus velezensis UTB96 mitigates saffron fusarium corm rot and promotes plant growth and phytochemical quality
Article.Authors: Kolahderazi N.; Hosseini S.; Ahmadzadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Saffron corm rot, predominantly associated with Fusarium species, is a major constraint to saffron production and may adversely affect both yield and spice quality. In this study, the causal agents of saffron corm rot were isolated from diseased corms collected in Iran, and identified based on morphological characteristics and pathogenicity tests. Three pathogenic isolates were characterized as Fusarium oxysporum , F. solani , and F. culmorum . The biocontrol potential of Bacillus velezensis strain UTB96 was subsequently evaluated through dual-culture and volatile organic compound assays, greenhouse experiments, and a field trial. Under in vitro conditions, UTB96 significantly inhibited the mycelial growth of all three Fusarium isolates, with the greatest inhibition in the dual-culture assay observed against F. solani (68.35%). Volatile compounds produced by UTB96 also suppressed fungal growth, with inhibition rates of 59.28, 66.00, and 73.00% against F. oxysporum , F. culmorum , and F. solani , respectively. In planta experiments, corm treatment with UTB96 significantly reduced disease severity caused by all three pathogens compared with infected controls, with the highest reduction recorded against F. solani (70.74%). In addition, UTB96 significantly enhanced leaf length, leaf number, sprouts number, root length, and corm number, whereas daughter-corm weight was not significantly affected. Field application of UTB96 improved important yield-related traits, including stigma length, stigma weight, and flower weight. Moreover, according to ISO3632-based measurements, the treatment significantly increased crocin and picrocrocin contents at P < 0.01 and safranal content at P < 0.05. Correlation analysis revealed strong positive associations between agronomic traits and crocin and picrocrocin, while safranal was significantly correlated with the other quality indices but not with the measured yield traits. Overall, B. velezensis strain UTB96 demonstrated substantial antifungal, disease-suppressive, and plant growth-promoting activities, highlighting its promise as a multifunctional bioinoculant for sustainable saffron production.

Article.Title: Secretome-dependent antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activity of Lactobacillus johnsonii against multidrug-resistant Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli
Article.Authors: Vasamsetti S.; Ligory M.; Khaderbad Y.; Gupta A.; Morampudi V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) is a leading cause of persistent diarrhea in children in low- and middle-income countries, and the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains necessitates non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies. This study evaluated Lactobacillus johnsonii , previously characterized by our group, as a probiotic candidate against a clinically confirmed MDR EAEC isolate resistant to ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, azithromycin, amoxicillin, and gentamicin. Probiotic properties of L. johnsonii were assessed through gastrointestinal stress tolerance, cell surface hydrophobicity, phenol tolerance, and autoaggregation assays. Antimicrobial and anti-biofilm activity against MDR EAEC were evaluated using agar overlay and crystal violet biofilm assays. Epithelial interaction was assessed through adherence and protection assays on HCT-116 intestinal epithelial cells. Gas production suppression, macrophage nitric oxide modulation in RAW 264.7 cells, and nutrient competition were examined as mechanistic endpoints. The L. johnsonii cell-free supernatant was fractionated by fast protein liquid chromatography (FPLC) and active fractions confirmed by Gram staining. Statistical analyses were performed using unpaired Student’s t-test, one-way ANOVA, or two-way ANOVA with Dunnett’s multiple comparisons test. L. johnsonii demonstrated robust gastrointestinal resilience, high cell surface hydrophobicity, and rapid autoaggregation reaching 80.4 ± 2.3% by 4 h, collectively supporting mucosal colonization potential. It produced zones of inhibition against MDR EAEC substantially exceeding those of gentamicin, reduced viable biofilm-associated EAEC by over 80%, and displaced pre-adhered EAEC from intestinal epithelial cells in a time-dependent manner requiring prior epithelial establishment. L. johnsonii attenuated EAEC-induced gas production and reduced macrophage nitric oxide levels by 67.7%. Inhibition was predominantly secretome-dependent, as nutrient competition did not contribute to pathogen suppression. FPLC fractionation identified fractions S5 and S6 as the principal bioactive components with sustained bactericidal activity at 6 h, with S6 exhibiting greater killing potency than S5. L. johnsonii exhibited potent secretome-dependent antimicrobial activity against MDR EAEC in vitro and significantly suppressed macrophage nitric oxide production, indicating its potential to modulate inflammatory responses. These findings support its potential as a non-antibiotic biotherapeutic strategy for antibiotic-resistant enteric infections. However, further in vivo validation and molecular characterization of the active antimicrobial components are required before clinical translation.

Article.Title: Data-driven optimization and multiscale characterization of sustainable epoxy-benzoxazine hybrid composites for high-performance structural applications
Article.Authors: Vinod B.; Ebenezer N.; Venkataramana P.; Mohammed Z.; Bellary S.; Tamboli S.
Article.Abstract: The polymer composites with enhanced mechanical, thermal, and tribological properties are increasingly important for advanced structural applications. In this study, hybrid composites based on an epoxy-benzoxazine matrix reinforced with basalt fibers (BF), waste cotton textile fibers (WCTF), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) were developed. Optimization of BF content, WCTF content, GNP loading, and curing temperature for tensile strength, flexural strength, impact strength, and Shore D was performed using a Taguchi L9 experimental design. The optimized composite (30% BF, 10% WCTF, 1% GNPs, and a curing temperature of 160 °C) achieved a tensile strength of 138 MPa, flexural strength of 208 MPa, impact strength of 42 kJ m⁻², and Shore D hardness of 87. In addition, the optimized composite exhibited a storage modulus of 5.2 GPa and a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 132 °C. FTIR, AFM, FESEM with EDS, DMA, DSC, TGA, and wear analyses supported enhanced matrix-reinforcement interactions, improved interfacial adhesion, and favorable thermomechanical and tribological performance. Random Forest and XGBoost machine learning models were created for predicting the composite properties, and XGBoost yielded the highest prediction accuracy (R² = 0.9870–0.993). The proposed experimental, statistical, and machine learning strategy is effective for the design of high-performance epoxy–benzoxazine hybrid composites for applications in structural engineering.

Article.Title: Fixed-qubit CVaR-VQE and quantum-inspired QUBO sampling for static and dynamic restricted vertex multicut in telecom resilience
Article.Authors: Abbassi A.; Dujardin Y.; Gourdin E.; Lacomme P.; Prodhon C.
Article.Abstract: A central question in hybrid quantum–classical optimization is how to assign the classical and quantum components according to the structure of the problem, rather than attempting to transfer the full optimization model to a quantum device. We investigate this question on static and finite-horizon dynamic restricted vertex minimum multicut, an NP-hard network-isolation problem with exponentially many path constraints. A classical row-generation layer handles graph separation, feasibility verification, and constraint generation, while quantum or quantum-inspired samplers are used only for the current restricted optimization problem. We develop two such algorithms: an exact-slack QUBO formulation sampled by simulated annealing, and a fixed-register CVaR-VQE formulation in which generated constraints modify a classical loss without enlarging the static quantum register. Exact MILP row generation provides the certifying reference. Experiments on SNDlib-derived telecom instances show that both approaches can be integrated consistently within this workflow, while classical-sampler controls do not establish a quantum-specific performance advantage. The dynamic study further shows how temporal coupling creates a distinct resource bottleneck, motivating decomposed formulations for larger horizons.

Article.Title: Longitudinal proxy pack benchmark generation for remaining useful life assessment of light electric vehicle battery packs in swapping systems
Article.Authors: Zhu L.; Zheng W.; Zhang F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Battery swapping enables rapid energy replenishment for light electric vehicles (LEVs), but high-turnover pack circulation requires reliable pack-level health and remaining useful life ( RUL ) assessment. Publicly reusable longitudinal ageing datasets for complete LEV packs remain scarce. We develop a proxy-pack data-generation and learning framework that organizes independently tested cell-ageing records into fixed-member trajectories representing a 48 V-class 16-series configuration. Each trajectory retains 16 physical-cell identities over their common-cycle sequence. Cycle-level member states are aggregated into pack features for predicting a conservative minimum-member proxy RUL, with test barcodes isolated before combinatorial augmentation. Across ten barcode-level splits in each of three source cohorts, same-source tests with endpoints within the augmented training lifetime range achieved a median R² of 0.909 and a median Spearman correlation of 0.997. Tests beyond this range retained strong degradation ordering but showed larger absolute errors. A secondary mixed-source audit of 80 held-out trajectories achieved a median R² of 0.714 and a median Spearman correlation of 0.992. A matched composition-control analysis yielded a median R² by change of -0.015 after balancing barcode reuse and limiting composition overlap, indicating limited sensitivity to training-composition sampling. A complementary physical audit using one fixed 12S3P pack confirmed cell-to-branch-to-pack electrical closure and revealed persistent voltage limitation and migration of the maximum-temperature location. Proxy-pack generation therefore provides a reproducible approach for constructing longitudinal member-aware benchmarks from cell-ageing records and evaluating pack-health and RUL models across varied compositions and lifetime conditions.

Article.Title: Multi-year dynamics of soil quality and sorghum yield under conservation tillage in Northern Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Kebede M.
Article.Abstract: Global dry land agricultural systems face intensifying structural and climatic pressures, demanding innovative soil management paradigms to sustain crop productivity and preserve scarce hydrological and nutritional resources. Conventional tillage (CT) practices, characterized by intensive mechanical soil inversion, accelerate the oxidation of soil organic matter, disrupt macro-pore continuity, and generate high subsoil bulk density that limits water permeability and exacerbates terminal drought vulnerability. To address these systemic challenges, A five-year field study (2016–2020) was conducted at the Shire-May-Tsebri Agricultural Research Center in northern Ethiopia to assess the long-term impact of five tillage systems Zero Tillage (ZT), Mulch Tillage (MT), Reduced Tillage (RT), Strip Tillage (ST), and Conventional Tillage (CT) on topsoil properties and sorghum productivity. While the 2016 baseline season exhibited uniform initial soil parameters, progressive multi-year divergence established distinct structural equilibria over time. By 2020, continuous conservation management led to highly significant modifications in topsoil infrastructure ( P < 0.001). MT and ST maximized soil organic carbon accumulation to 2.34% and 1.89%, respectively, and drastically reduced bulk density down to 0.23 g/cm 3 and 0.42 g/cm 3 compared to the relatively higher BD under CT (0.89 g/cm 3 ). Two-way split-plot ANOVA confirmed that ST significantly preserved late-season soil profile moisture during terminal post-monsoonal drying phases, retaining a substantial hydrological reserve of 38.98% by November 2020. Agronomical, intensive mechanical inversion under CT optimized initial stand counts and functional heads but compromised the root microenvironment. Conversely, ST effectively bypassed early crop establishment barriers, achieving a stable intermediate plant population and unlocking an overwhelming 63.13% grain yield improvement over CT by the final 2020 season (51.99 kg/ha vs. 31.87 kg/ha). Pearson correlation analysis confirmed that final grain yield was profoundly coupled with late-season moisture retention ( r = 0.79) and organic carbon buildup ( r = 0.74). Ultimately, continuous Strip Tillage progressively rehabilitates dryland soil infrastructure, steadily elevating terminal water-use efficiency and providing a resilient climate-adaptation paradigm for dryland agricultural systems.

Article.Title: Measurement and calibration method of dynamic stress in rock mass based on PDV technology
Article.Authors: Shi Y.; Xing Y.; Huang X.; Li Z.; Jiao X.; Ba Z.; Song S.; Zhang L.; Zhang G.
Article.Abstract: To address the challenge of measuring the dynamic stress of engineering rock mass structures under blast loading, a rock mass dynamic stress measurement and calibration method based on Photonic Doppler Velocimetry (PDV) was developed. Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) loading tests were conducted under different wave impedance and coupling conditions to investigate the stress wave transmission effect and to verify the accuracy of the proposed measurement method. The experimental results show that the SHPB-based calibration method for the rock mass dynamic stress measurement system is accurate and reliable. Under the conditions of identical wave impedance and coupling fixation with a thin adhesive layer, the feasibility of the PDV-based dynamic stress measurement method for engineering rock masses is preliminarily verified, providing a feasible technical approach for measuring dynamic response parameters such as stress and strain of structures under blast loading.

Article.Title: Regional nerve blocks are associated with greater early analgesia for femoral neck fractures in the emergency department
Article.Authors: Uysal Ş.; Akçay G.; Sönmez B.; Çevik H.; Akkaya Ö.; Güner N.; Şirin İ.
Article.Abstract: Femoral neck fractures are highly painful emergency department (ED) presentations, particularly among older adults, and early analgesia is essential for imaging, positioning, and surgical preparation. This prospective, comparative, non-randomized ED study compared intravenous (IV) paracetamol, IV tramadol, ultrasound-guided femoral nerve block (FNB), and ultrasound-guided pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block in adults with isolated femoral fractures, particularly femoral neck fractures. The primary outcome was maximum pain reduction during the 240-minute follow-up. Because baseline pain scores differed between groups, maximum pain reduction was compared using analysis of covariance adjusted for age, fracture type, and baseline pain score. Among 125 patients, 113 (90.4%) had femoral neck fractures. Among 125 patients, 113 (90.4%) had femoral neck fractures. Ultrasound-guided regional blocks were associated with faster and greater pain reduction than systemic analgesics across visual analog, numeric rating, and facial pain scales. The largest early reductions occurred within the first 15 min after the FNB and PENG block. Effect sizes for maximum pain reduction were large on both the visual analog and numeric rating scales. Rescue analgesia was rarely required after regional blocks, whereas adverse events occurred mainly in the opioid group. These findings suggest that ultrasound-guided regional blocks may provide effective early analgesia in similar ED fracture analgesia settings where trained clinicians are available.

Article.Title: Selection signatures in Apis mellifera jemenitica suggest candidate genes potentially involved in energy metabolism, proteostasis, reproduction, and cellular regulation
Article.Authors: Hedayat N.; Khalkhali-Evrigh R.; Seyedsharifi R.; Khanzadeh H.; Pourasad K.; Tanveer H.
Article.Abstract: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) help pollinate plants, support biodiversity, and make a significant contribution to food production. Among their subspecies, A. m. jemenitica (JEM) inhabits desert and semi-desert regions, representing a valuable model for understanding genomic adaptation to extreme environmental conditions. We performed a comparative whole-genome resequencing analysis between JEM and A. m. mellifera (MEL) to identify genetic variants and selection signatures underlying adaptation to arid environments. A total of more than 2.9 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were identified and analyzed for population structure, linkage disequilibrium (LD), and genome-wide scans for selection signals using FST, XP-EHH, and π-ratio approaches. Population analyses revealed distinct clustering patterns and clear genetic differentiation between JEM and MEL, accompanied by faster LD decay in JEM, which is consistent with the larger effective population size in JEM (Ne = 2523) compared to MEL (Ne = 952). Through the combined selection scans, we identified 222 overlapping candidate genes that appear to be under positive selection. Many of these genes are involved in diverse biological processes, including energy metabolism, cellular regulation, protein homeostasis, stress response, genome maintenance, and cellular communication, with several having documented roles in heat tolerance, oxidative stress response, circadian regulation, and reproduction. Notable examples include LpR , inositol monophosphatase 1 , AcCoAS , enolase , BAG6 , alpha-Man-Ia , JHE , nocte , CRH-BP , and Est-6 , highlighting potential roles in osmotic and thermal stress tolerance, energy hemostasis, protein quality control, circadian regulation, and reproductive biology. These findings enhance our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying environmental adaptation in honey bees. Nevertheless, further multi-omics investigations, including transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, as well as functional assays are needed to validate the adaptive relevance of the candidate genes and pathways identified in this study.

Article.Title: Associations of physical function and multimorbidity with cognitive impairment in community-dwelling Chinese octogenarians
Article.Authors: Bian S.; Tong C.; Meng F.; Tian X.; Luo X.; Zhou X.; Wang P.; Gao Q.
Article.Abstract: China’s rapidly aging population has intensified concerns about cognitive impairment and chronic disease burdens among older adults. Despite this, research on the interplay between physical function, multimorbidity, and their associations with cognitive impairment in community-dwelling octogenarians remains limited. This study investigates the associations between physical function, chronic disease prevalence, and cognitive impairment among home-dwelling adults aged ≥ 80 years in China, with a focus on demographic and clinical predictors of cognitive decline. A cross-sectional analysis of 13,027 octogenarians assessed physical function using the Barthel Index (BI) and cognitive status via the Mini-Cog. Logistic regression models evaluated the impact of demographic factors (age, gender, occupation), chronic diseases (hypertension, stroke), and psychosocial factors (aggression, depression) on cognitive impairment severity. Of the participants, 37.88% exhibited high functional independence (BI = 100). Cognitive impairment was significantly influenced by age, gender, and multimorbidity ( p < 0.01). Depression (OR 11.335; 95% CI 8.853–14.514) and aggression (OR 1.93; 95% CI 1.161–3.217) were strongly associated with cognitive impairment severity. Hypertension was moderately correlated with mild cognitive impairment (OR 1.495; 95% CI 1.285–1.739), while stroke tripled the odds of mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment (OR 3.301; 95% CI 2.131–5.113). Reduced self-care ability was associated with nearly fourfold higher odds of cognitive impairment ( p < 0.01). Age, occupation, and lifestyle factors synergistically are associated with chronic disease burden and cognitive impairment in China’s oldest-old population. These findings underscore the urgency of personalized healthcare strategies to preserve independence and mitigate cognitive decline in high-risk octogenarians.

Article.Title: Association of PROMIS Profile-29 based quality of life with heart failure in asymptomatic patients (HERZCHECK)
Article.Authors: Nolden A.; Thiede G.; Beyer R.; Müller M.; Wieditz J.; Kentenich H.; Graja D.; Sehlen S.; Steen H.; Remppis B.; Huppertz A.; Landmesser U.; Falk V.; Frey N.; Stock S.; Fischer F.; Friede T.; Kelle S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Heart failure is often diagnosed only when symptoms become acute, but early detection could help prevent disease progression. As patient-reported quality of life is strongly associated with heart failure outcomes, it may also serve as an additional correlate with the disease before symptoms occur. This cross-sectional study investigates the associations of quality of life and asymptomatic heart failure and was conducted as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis. It was based on data of 4,509 asymptomatic patients aged 40 to 69 years with at least one cardiovascular risk factor and without known heart failure at the time of quality of life assessment, whose heart failure status was determined during the baseline evaluation. The quality of life of patients with and without asymptomatic heart failure was compared, using logistic regression. Lower Physical Function was associated with higher odds of asymptomatic heart failure in females generally. Among females with hypercholesterolemia, lower physical function and lower pain interference were associated with asymptomatic heart failure, while in females who smoke, lower physical function was associated with asymptomatic heart failure. In males generally, lower Pain Interference and higher Pain Intensity were associated with higher odds of pre-HF, with additional associations of lower Pain Interference in males with diabetes, higher Depression and higher Pain Intensity in males with hypercholesterolemia, and lower Pain Interference and higher Pain Intensity in males who smoke. This study highlights the association between patient-reported physical health domains and asymptomatic heart failure. The findings provide hypothesis-generating insights into the relationship between quality of life and asymptomatic heart failure and highlight the need for longitudinal research.

Article.Title: Domain adaptation affects adversarial robustness in autonomous steering models
Article.Authors: Mehraban Z.; Glaser S.; Milford M.; Schroeter R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Domain adaptation is commonly used to transfer autonomous steering models across regions with different road configurations, such as from right-hand to left-hand traffic. While prior work has largely evaluated adaptation using clean target-domain steering accuracy, its effect on adversarial robustness remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates two steering architectures, PilotNet and ResNet-18, under four adaptation strategies: U.S.-trained, flipped U.S.-trained, U.S.-trained + fine-tuned, and flipped U.S.-trained + fine-tuned. Robustness is assessed under FGSM and PGD attacks across multiple perturbation levels using normalized robustness scores and absolute steering-error metrics. Results show that domain adaptation improves clean target-domain accuracy but affects adversarial robustness in a metric-dependent manner. Fine-tuned models often show degraded normalized adversarial robustness, especially after flipped pretraining, indicating larger relative sensitivity to adversarial perturbations compared with their clean baselines. However, absolute adversarial errors show that fine-tuned models are not always worse than pretrained baselines under attack. These results show that, after domain adaptation, clean accuracy and normalized robustness can diverge, and RS may rank robustness differently from absolute steering-error metrics when clean baselines differ. The contribution of this study is to show that metric choice materially affects robustness conclusions for domain-adapted steering models; therefore, RS remains useful for measuring relative degradation, but should be interpreted alongside absolute steering-error metrics and statistical uncertainty.

Article.Title: Two-stage classification of glioma subtypes using a hybrid CNN-ViT model
Article.Authors: Aboelenin S.; Eltoukhy M.; Mohammed M.; Hosny K.
Article.Abstract: Gliomas are among the most serious brain tumor types due to their aggressive behavior. Recent advances in automated methods for early brain tumor detection that analyze whole-slide images of brain tissue enable rapid and precise diagnosis. Therefore, we propose a hybrid approach combining a convolutional neural network and a vision transformer for deep analysis of whole-slide patches. This hybrid model employs a two-stage classification strategy to address highly imbalanced class distributions. The first stage uses a binary-label classifier to label patches as either normal or abnormal. The second stage employs a multi-label classifier to classify abnormal patches into their corresponding glioma subtypes. We evaluated the two-stage hybrid model on an imbalanced test set, achieving the highest balanced accuracy (95.31%), macro-averaged precision (96.08%), and macro-averaged F1-score (95.51%). The two-stage classification approach addressed class imbalance. Furthermore, the hybrid model, which combines a convolutional neural network and a vision transformer, captured deeper features, achieving superior performance and outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

Article.Title: 4-Methoxydalbergione triggers ferroptosis in bladder cancer by suppressing the AKT/mTOR/GPX4 axis
Article.Authors: Li R.; Luo T.; Tao T.; Li X.; Zhou H.; Su T.; Xu C.; Xia L.; Du H.
Article.Abstract: Due to its high recurrence and pronounced metastatic potential, bladder cancer (BC) remains a significant and persistent clinical challenge. Here, we investigate the anti-tumour effects of 4-Methoxydalbergione (4MOD), a naturally occurring flavonoid obtained from Dalbergia sissoo Roxb. In T24 human and MBT2 mouse BC cell lines, 4MOD dose-dependently suppressed proliferation, migration, and invasion; colony formation was additionally suppressed in T24 cells. These effects were associated with a reversal of the epithelial- mesenchymal transition (EMT) process, as evidenced by elevated E‑cadherin and reduced N‑cadherin and vimentin expression. Moreover, 4MOD induced both apoptotic cell death and ferroptosis. The induction of ferroptosis was evidenced by mitochondrial shrinkage, accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the decreased levels of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). Caspase and ferroptosis inhibition experiments demonstrated that ferroptosis is the predominant driver of 4MOD‑induced cell death. Mechanistically, 4MOD inhibited AKT and mTOR signaling, as shown by reduced p‑AKT and p‑mTOR levels. Ferroptosis‑specific rescue with Ferrostatin‑1 (Fer‑1) and functional rescue with the AKT activator SC79 indicated that AKT/mTOR inhibition is causally linked to GPX4 downregulation and ferroptosis induction. In a BALB/c‑nu mouse xenograft model, 4MOD markedly suppressed tumour growth without causing significant body weight loss or histopathological abnormalities in liver and kidney tissues, correlating with reduced GPX4, elevated E‑cadherin, decreased vimentin, increased malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and reduced Ki‑67 positivity in tumour tissues. Notably, 4MOD synergized with the ferroptosis inducer erastin to enhance ferroptosis, apoptosis, and anti‑proliferative activity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 4MOD induces ferroptosis via the AKT/mTOR‑GPX4 axis, highlighting its therapeutic potential for bladder cancer.

Article.Title: A study on user continuance intention for children’s intelligent companion robots based on BERTopic-PLS-SEM-fsQCA
Article.Authors: Fan L.; Wu F.; Lai S.; Cheng C.
Article.Abstract: The children’s intelligent companion robot market faces the industry-wide challenge of “high initial adoption yet low sustained retention.” Existing research has predominantly relied on single-method approaches, leaving the psychological mechanisms and configurational pathways driving user continuance intention insufficiently understood. This study constructs a sequential multi-method research framework integrating “BERTopic thematic mining—PLS-SEM linear validation—fsQCA configurational analysis.” Drawing on 6,405 valid online reviews from JD.com and 440 valid questionnaire responses, the study adopts an integrated theoretical framework combining the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) and the Value-based Adoption Model (VAM). BERTopic thematic mining identified six core demand dimensions from consumer reviews: perceived usefulness, perceived enjoyment, visual aesthetics, social/gifting value, technical reliability, and expectation confirmation. PLS-SEM analysis reveals that satisfaction is the strongest predictor of continuance intention ( β = 0.705, p < 0.001), explaining 50.3% of its variance ( R ² = 0.503). Perceived value ( R ² = 0.571) is jointly driven by expectation confirmation ( β = 0.230), perceived usefulness ( β = 0.197), technical reliability ( β = 0.163), social/gifting value ( β = 0.141), visual aesthetics ( β = 0.106), and perceived enjoyment ( β = 0.104). Notably, perceived enjoyment exhibits a distinctive dual-pathway mechanism, influencing continuance intention both indirectly through perceived value and directly through satisfaction ( β = 0.232, p < 0.001). Further fsQCA configuration analysis identified four configurations of high continuance intention (with a solution consistency rate of 0.811 and a coverage rate of 0.469), which can be grouped into three broader patterns based on their theoretical coherence: the “expectation confirmation-dominated” pattern (Configurations 1 and 2, with consistency rates of 0.855 and 0.839, respectively), the “full-dimensional attribute-driven” pattern (Configuration 3, consistency rate of 0.814), and the “Social-Hedonic Compensation” pattern (Configuration 4, consistency rate of 0.836), indicating substantial heterogeneity in continuance intention logic across different segments. Theoretically, this study extends the ECM-VAM framework to the context of children’s embodied intelligent products by introducing visual aesthetics and technical reliability as context-specific antecedents of perceived value, demonstrates that unstructured online review texts can serve as a valid source for the contextualized operationalization of theoretical constructs, and qualifies the linear assumptions of conventional net-effect models through a configurational perspective.

Article.Title: Petrographic and magnetic fabric evidence for magmatic emplacement and hydrothermal alteration in the Shadan Au porphyry deposit, Eastern Iran
Article.Authors: Sheibi M.; Yun S.; Raeisi D.; Lotfi M.; Chang C.
Article.Abstract: Magmatic processes and subsequent hydrothermal alterations within porphyry deposits are well-documented through the analysis of mineral chemistry and the magnetic fabrics of their host intrusions. This study integrates structurs, petrography, mineral chemistry, and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) data to investigate the evolution of magmatic and hydrothermal fabrics in the Shadan porphyry Au-rich deposit, located in northeastern Iran. Fresh quartz monzodioritic intrusions exhibit primary magmatic fabrics characterized by oblate AMS ellipsoids, predominantly aligned with magnetite. Progressive hydrothermal alteration—including potassic, phyllic, propylitic, and argillic zones—systematically modifies these fabrics. These alterations are associated with the destruction of magmatic magnetite, hematitization, the replacement of biotite by sericite, and Fe–Mg re-equilibration in amphibole, biotite, and chlorite. Quartz–carbonate and late argillic zones exhibit very weak magnetic susceptibility due to the oxidation and obliteration of primary magnetic minerals. AMS fabrics are controlled by both ferromagnetic (magnetite) and paramagnetic silicate minerals and indicate a predominantly compressional brittle–ductile deformation regime, locally overprinted by late-stage extensional structures. The spatial distribution of magnetic fabrics further highlights the influence of regional and local structural controls on fluid pathways and alteration development within the deposit. The findings indicate that AMS effectively records the superimposed magmatic and hydrothermal processes, providing quantitative insights into the physicochemical evolution, alteration zoning, and mineralogical transformations in porphyry gold systems.

Article.Title: Profiling forward playing styles in big five European football leagues through PCA and cluster analysis
Article.Authors: Xia C.; Cao D.; Ye J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Attacking contributions in elite football are multi-dimensional, and broad forward-line labels often obscure functional variation within nominally homogeneous groups. This exploratory study mapped the technical-function space of forward-line players in Europe’s Big Five leagues using principal component analysis (PCA) and clustering, and evaluated the extent to which the data support discrete categories versus continuous variation.Publicly available FBref player-season data for the 2021–2022 and 2022–2023 seasons were analysed for 381 attacking player-season observations from 331 players with at least 900 league minutes. Sixteen technical process indicators were reduced using PCA, and three retained, standardised component scores were used for clustering (K-means, K = 2–5), with additional fuzzy c-means and archetypal analyses to assess profile distinctness.Three PCA components explained 62.7% of the variance and were interpretable as ball-carrying progression, creative playmaking and penalty-area presence; parallel analysis supported retention of these three components. The primary finding across multiple validation approaches is that the technical-function data among forward-line players were more consistent with continuous variation than with sharply separated, temporally stable clusters. K = 2 had the highest silhouette coefficient, whereas a five-region descriptive summary provided a more differentiated heuristic framework. However, fuzzy c-means showed that the median maximum membership across the five regions was 0.505, with 68.5% of player-seasons below 0.60, indicating substantial overlap. Cross-season centroid replication for the five-region solution was markedly weaker than for smaller-K solutions, further supporting the view that the data were more consistent with continuous variation than with temporally stable categories.The five regions were associated with descriptive differences in npxG + xA, npxG/Shot and G + A, but these associations reflect differences in chance access and shot quality and are not independent validation of the regions as distinct player types. Non-penalty goals relative to non-penalty expected goals did not differ significantly across regions.These findings indicate that technical tendencies within forward-line players are more consistent with continuous variation in chance access and contribution than with fixed, discrete roles. The three PCA dimensions offer a more stable framework for describing functional variation among forwards. The five-region heuristic summary is an exploratory, communication-oriented device for navigating this continuous space, not a validated player taxonomy.
