Article.Title: Multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graph construction for conflict-event analysis: an integrated framework with geographic entity-map association
Article.Authors: Guo L.; Zhang W.; Jia N.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: Heterogeneous conflict-event information is distributed across textual reports, web images, and scanned maps, making it difficult to represent entities, events, geographic locations, temporal attributes, and multimedia evidence within a unified knowledge graph. This study proposes an integrated framework for constructing multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graphs from event-oriented heterogeneous data. The framework combines textual entity, relation, and event extraction; visual object detection; scanned-map coordinate recognition; geographic entity grounding; cross-modal entity fusion; provenance-aware storage; and graph visualization. A cascaded YOLOv5-PaddleOCR procedure first detects and crops coordinate annotation regions from scanned maps and then reconstructs the map extent from the recognized coordinates. Textual place entities are geocoded using GeoNames and linked to relevant maps through point-polygon spatial intersection. Quantitative experiments showed F1-scores of 0.76-0.84 for the evaluated text extraction tasks. For aircraft, ship, and general web-image detection, YOLOv8 obtained mAP@0.5 values of 0.935, 0.890, and 0.922, respectively. On the 287-map scanned-map dataset, YOLOv5 achieved a region-detection F1-score of 0.977. In the 278-map paired out-of-fold OCR evaluation, complete map-coordinate recognition increased from 64.03% with direct PaddleOCR to 87.05% with the cascaded procedure, and the paired difference was statistically significant (exact McNemar test, p < 0.001). Under an event- and source-document-grouped evaluation protocol, the complete constrained cross-modal entity-fusion method achieved an F1-score of 0.884. A conflict-event case study further demonstrates the practical applicability of the framework.

Article.Title: A cross-sectional study on the mental health status and influencing factors of medical staff in northwestern China
Article.Authors: Niu Z.; Zhang Z.; Yang X.; Pei H.; Pan L.
Article.Abstract: Healthcare workers in Northwest China face heavy workloads and limited resources, yet region-specific evidence on their health is scarce. In this multicentre cross-sectional study, 1143 doctors, nurses and other clinical staff from 151 public hospitals in Northwest China were surveyed in November–December 2023 using a questionnaire compiled from existing Chinese instruments that assessed occupational stressors, mental health, chronic physical diseases and body image. Nearly 60% of participants worked more than five days per week. Longer daily working hours and more weekly working days were independently associated with greater psychological distress, although the model explained only a small proportion of the variance. Staff in secondary hospitals and non-provincial capital cities reported greater psychological distress than those in tertiary hospitals and provincial capitals. Physical diseases were more common among men, emergency department staff and those working longer hours. Physical exertion was the most prominent stressor, followed by psychological and economic stress, and doctors reported higher stress levels than nurses. These findings suggest that workload management, mental health support and occupational health policies targeting high-risk groups may help to protect the well-being of healthcare workers in this region.

Article.Title: Simultaneous methanol recovery and CO2 capture in a single rotating packed bed (RPB) reactor
Article.Authors: Hamidi A.; Eini S.; Ahmadian M.; Farzaneh E.
Article.Abstract: Waste gas streams from methanol production contain recoverable methanol together with a significant amount of CO 2 . Conventional treatment relies on large multi-stage packed columns. In this study, a process-intensified strategy is experimentally demonstrated for simultaneous methanol recovery and CO 2 capture within a single rotating packed bed (RPB) reactor under various operating conditions (gas flow rate, solvent flow rate, and rotational speed). A lab-scale RPB was operated using a synthetic waste gas mixture (air, CO 2 , and methanol) and 30 wt% aqueous monoethanolamine as the solvent. At a representative operating condition (gas flow rate of 30 L/min, solvent flow rate of 0.3 L/min, and rotational speed of 600 rpm), the RPB achieved approximately 80% CO 2 absorption and 93% methanol recovery. To benchmark performance, equivalent separation configurations using conventional fixed packed columns were evaluated through simulation. Accordingly, the RPB provides a volumetric intensification factor of at least 15.2 relative to the conventional configurations. These results demonstrate that a single RPB can simultaneously recover methanol and capture CO 2 with a substantially reduced equipment footprint, offering a compact and high-throughput alternative for waste stream valorization.

Article.Title: Automated whole slide Allred score estimation for estrogen receptor assessment in breast cancer
Article.Authors: Wadood A.; Fauzi M.; Wong L.; Rehman Z.; Nabi M.; Lee J.; Khor S.; Looi L.
Article.Abstract: Accurate assessment of estrogen receptor (ER) status is critical in breast cancer diagnosis and treatment planning, as it directly determines eligibility for endocrine therapy. ER expression is routinely evaluated on immunohistochemistry (IHC) slides using the semi-quantitative Allred scoring system, which combines the proportion of ER-positive tumor nuclei with staining intensity into a composite score of 0–8. However, manual Allred scoring is labor-intensive, subjective, and prone to inter- and intra-observer variability, particularly in cases that are borderline. In this work, we present a whole-slide image (WSI)-level Allred score estimation pipeline built around MOSAIC, our previously developed multi-scale, orientation-aware nuclei analysis network. The pipeline incorporates a patch-based WSI inference strategy that requires only nucleus-level annotations for training; a centroid-guided instance separation and majority-voting scheme that converts pixel-level segmentation outputs into clinically interpretable proportion scores and intensity scores; and a systematic aggregation protocol that derives the final Allred score without requiring slide-level supervision. MOSAIC integrates multi-scale context extraction to handle nuclear size variability, rotation-enhanced fusion to improve robustness to arbitrary nuclear orientation, and a transformer-inspired multi-scale integration hub to model long-range contextual dependencies across heterogeneous tissue regions. Experimental evaluation on an institutional ER-IHC cohort comprising 37 WSIs from different patients demonstrated strong pixel-level segmentation accuracy, robust instance-level nuclei detection, and improved stability in borderline ER cases. At the WSI level, the pipeline achieved the highest concordance with pathologist-assigned hormonal therapy decisions (89.2%) among all compared approaches, requiring an average of 3.5 minutes to analyze the pathologist-defined tumor regions of each WSI, compared with 11 minutes to 2 hours for the baseline methods evaluated under the present experimental protocol.

Article.Title: Loss of nono impairs cardiac morphogenesis and excitation–contraction coupling via the PI3K/Akt pathway in zebrafish
Article.Authors: Zhang Q.; Yan C.; Liu H.; Zhao H.; Sun K.; Peng X.; Lin Y.; Wang X.; Lei Y.; Cao H.
Article.Abstract: Pathogenic variants in NONO are clinically linked to congenital heart disease (CHD), but in vivo mechanisms and gene-targeted interventions remain poorly explored. Using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing and morpholino silencing, we established knockout (KO) and knockdown (KD) zebrafish models to study nono in cardiogenesis. Adult KO hearts displayed severe structural remodeling, characterized by ventricular distortion, disorganized sarcomeres, and myocardial fibrosis. High-speed optical mapping and calcium imaging revealed reduced conduction velocity, increased dispersion, and spatial heterogeneity in action potential and Ca 2+ transients, disrupting excitation–contraction coupling. In larvae, nono deficiency downregulated core transcription factors ( nkx2.5, gata4 ), suppressed the PI3K/Akt pathway, and triggered myocardial apoptosis. Exogenous delivery of nono mRNA (Rescue) restored PI3K/Akt signaling, mitigating embryonic cardiovascular defects and functional failure. Collectively, our dual-model system demonstrates that NONO is required for structural integrity and electrophysiological homeostasis. This study provides vital in vivo functional validation of nono as a molecular target for myocardial dysfunction, offering a proof-of-concept for gene-based therapeutic restoration in NONO -associated CHD.

Article.Title: Fine-tuned U-Net and time-weighted bi-directional LSTM for low-latency cardiopulmonary monitoring in WBSN data
Article.Authors: Rubia R.; Sasikala S.
Article.Abstract: The evolution of Wireless Body Sensor Networks (WBSNs) has dramatically changed the Smart Emergency Monitoring (SEM) landscape, enabling continuous and non-invasive monitoring of vital signs such as blood pressure, SpO 2 , respiratory rate, and even CO 2 levels. However, the timely and precise detection of transient yet clinically significant events remain an enormous statistical challenge owing to the lower sensitivity and specificity offered by traditional deep learning methods. Such salient experimental alerts usually go with a higher error in prediction rate, hence generalizing poorly with sub-average temporal context modeling from U-Net architectures combined with LSTM layers. To defeat such weaknesses, it proposed a statistically refined hybrid approach, followed by the fine-tuned U-Net framework for spatial feature extraction, interfaced with a Time-Weighted Multi-Task Bi-Directional LSTM (TW-MT-BiLSTM) for temporal sequence modeling. Three enhancements are considered statistically significant, such as: (1) attention-based temporal weighting limiting higher consideration to important time segments, (2) bidirectional LSTM giving better inference capitalizing on past and future contexts, and (3) multi-task learning simultaneously predicting the variables of blood pressure, SpO 2 , and respiratory rate, which decreases variance and enhances the robustness of overall prediction. An extensive set of experiments on benchmark datasets such as Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-III) and PhysioNet is compared in terms of statistical performance metrics, including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square, and the superiority of the proposed methods was revealed over existing methods.

Article.Authors: Rukmangad P.; Thomas B.; Murali G.
Article.Abstract: Auxetic structures, with a negative Poisson’s ratio, have gained significant attention for aerospace and automotive applications due to their superior mechanical performance. In this study, two different Auxetic Structures were used, namely Re–entrant Hexagon (A) and Re-entrant star triangular structure (B). They were designed and fabricated with the use of Stereolithography (SLA) Additive Manufacturing with the use of Standard Photopolymer Resin Material. The mechanical Behaviour was investigated with the help of compression testing according to ASTM D695 Standards using a Universal Testing Machine (UTM). These findings confirm that Auxetic geometry strongly influences mechanical behaviour and performance. The namely Re–entrant Hexagon (A) Geometry is better suited for Flexible and cushioning applications, such as biomedical devices used in implants, ergonomic materials, shoe soles, and soft protective paddings, while the Re- entrant Star triangular (B) geometry is suitable for applications requiring High Strength and Impact Resistance, such as aerospace Sandwich Structures, automotive crash absorbers, and protective equipment.

Article.Title: Smart rubber sensor repeatability and between-system agreement for peak plantar pressure in healthy and older adults during standing and walking
Article.Authors: Yoshikawa Y.; Matsushita C.; Yamaguchi A.; Ma X.; Maeshige N.
Article.Abstract: Smart Rubber technology enables a low-cost, platform-based approach to clinical plantar pressure monitoring, yet its metrological properties relative to established in-shoe sensors remain uncharacterised. We evaluated the within-session repeatability of a Smart Rubber platform sensor (SR Soft Vision) and its agreement with an established in-shoe resistive sensor array (F-Scan) during quiet standing and walking in 20 healthy adults and 10 ambulatory older adults receiving low-level long-term care support. Repeatability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients [ICC(A,1) and ICC(A, k)] with 95% confidence intervals, standard error of measurement (SEM), minimal detectable change (MDC95), and coefficient of variation. Between-system agreement was evaluated using Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland–Altman analysis, while Pearson’s r was additionally reported as an index of linear association. During standing, directly calculated ICC(A,3) values for SR Soft Vision ranged from 0.974 to 0.993, and during walking they ranged from 0.952 to 0.989. Between-system agreement was task- and region-dependent: forefoot walking peak plantar pressure (PPP) showed near-zero concordance (CCC = 0.04) with large systematic bias (− 497 to − 528 kPa), persisting after exclusion of ceiling-attainment cases (sensitivity analysis). These findings demonstrate high within-session repeatability of SR Soft Vision and support its potential use for repeated within-device assessment under a consistent protocol, while indicating that absolute PPP values are not interchangeable with F-Scan during dynamic forefoot loading.

Article.Title: REDD1 regulates the cGAS-STING signaling pathway in adipocytes
Article.Authors: Clary R.; Dumas K.; Gilleron J.; Lacas-Gervais S.; Peraldi P.; Jager J.; Britto F.; Favier F.; Ollendorff V.; Cormont M.; Tanti J.; Giorgetti-Peraldi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mitochondria are regulators at the interface between metabolism and immunity in adipocytes. In addition to maintaining metabolic homeostasis, mitochondria control immune responses through the activation of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway. This pathway is a central component of the innate immune system for detecting cytosolic DNA and initiating immune responses. The stress-response protein REDD1 (Regulated in Development and DNA damage response 1) has been described as a regulator of mitochondria-associated membranes and may modulate mitochondrial functions. However, the role of REDD1 in controlling mitochondrial integrity and cGAS–STING signaling in adipocytes remains unclear. We showed that REDD1 expression knockdown increased the ER-mitochondria contacts, mitochondrial enlargement and cytosolic mitochondrial DNA release in 3T3-L1 adipocytes. The downregulation of REDD1 expression increased cGAS and STING protein levels through oxidative stress- and mTORC1 dependent pathways. However, increase in cGAS/STING protein expression is uncoupled from canonical inflammatory and autophagy pathways. Instead, decrease in REDD1 expression reduced fatty acid desaturase 2 (FADS2) expression, a key enzyme in polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism in a STING-dependent manner. In conclusion, our study identifies REDD1 as a novel regulator of mitochondrial homeostasis and cGAS-STING signaling in adipocytes, potentially linking mitochondrial stress to FADS2 protein expression.

Article.Title: Entropy measures of degree-based topological indices for hyper carbon nanotubes
Article.Authors: Nadeem M.; Shabbir A.; Husin M.; Muda Y.
Article.Abstract: Carbon nanotube structures have potential applications in nanoelectronics, molecular sensors, energy-storage devices, nanocomposites, and multi-terminal nanoscale interconnects. Motivated by their structural complexity, this paper investigates entropy measures of degree-based topological indices for a hyper armchair carbon nanotube (HCN) graph. The HCN graph is constructed by replacing the vertices of an armchair nanotube template with Y-shaped junction modules and its edges with armchair nanotube segments. Complete vertex-degree and vertex-degree-based edge partitions are established and checked against the order, size, and degree-sum identity of the graph. These partitions yield closed forms for the selected topological indices and for the Shannon entropies obtained by normalizing their edge contributions. Numerical comparisons show that the entropy values increase along the selected structural-parameter sequence, and the dominant degree class explains why the entropy values of different indices become close for larger HCN graphs.

Article.Title: Gradual mitochondrial collapse underlies cytotoxicity induced by a B-type prymnesin-containing Prymnesium parvum extract in rainbow trout gill cells
Article.Authors: Neer Z.; Kiss E.; Tillmann U.; Vajna B.; Felföldi T.; Csályi K.; Matkó J.; Varga E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bioactive secondary metabolites produced by the haptophyte microalga Prymnesium parvum are key mediators of ichthyotoxicity during harmful algal bloom events. In the present study, we investigated the effects of a P. parvum extract containing B-type prymnesins, from an isolate obtained during the 2022 Oder River bloom, on mitochondrial health and cellular homeostasis in the rainbow trout gill epithelial cell line RTgill-W1, a widely used model in aquatic toxicology. Mitochondrial function and structure were assessed using multiparameter flow cytometry and high-resolution confocal microscopy (Airyscan). Exposure to prymnesin-containing extract (PRYMCE) induced concentration-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by loss of mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), changes in mitochondrial mass-associated fluorescence, and reduced cardiolipin-associated 10-N-nonyl acridine orange (NAO) fluorescence. Structural analysis revealed mitochondrial network remodeling across PRYMCE concentrations, including perinuclear clustering and a transition from elongated filamentous structures to condensed spherical forms. Time-resolved imaging further demonstrated that mitochondrial structural alterations preceded overt plasma membrane permeabilization. Single-cell analysis demonstrated pronounced cellular heterogeneity, with distinct injury-associated subpopulations exhibiting increased side scatter and a ΔΨm low /mitochondrial mass low phenotype. These findings identify mitochondrial impairment and network remodeling as early, quantifiable hallmarks of PRYMCE-induced cytotoxicity and provide mechanistic insight into how P. parvum blooms may damage aquatic organisms.

Article.Title: Valorizing palm date wastes for supercapacitor electrode synthesis and evaluation
Article.Authors: Mostafa A.; Mohammed S.; Ghazaly N.; ElSheikh A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Climate and energy issues continue to drive researchers to develop fossil-free energy technologies that are both sustainable and scalable. In this work, date seeds (DS) are used to produce activated carbon (DSAC), which is then used as a supercapacitor electrode. The synthesis method uses KOH activation coupled with argon-gas flow calcination at 950 °C. The produced DSAC has a high specific surface area of 1374 m 2 /g and a turbostratic microporous structure (pore size = 1.14 nm), in addition to oxygen-containing functional groups (–C–O–, –OH). The DSAC electrochemical performance exhibits an electric double-layer capacitor (EDLC) with a minor pseudocapacitive contribution and delivers a 3-electrode specific capacitance of 1800 F/g at 4 A/g (estimated full-device specific capacitance is 450 F/g, energy, and power densities: 40 Wh/kg and 1440 W/kg, respectively). These numbers are remarkably higher than the current state-of-the-art carbon supercapacitor findings. Furthermore, it retains 83.3% of its initial discharge capacity after 2000 galvanostatic charge-discharge cycles at 10 A/g. Finally, the DSAC electrode performance is slightly enhanced with increasing the KOH concentration from 1 M to 3 M.

Article.Title: An integrated explainable machine learning framework for prediction explanation and audit in high stakes binary classification
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Shi M.; Huang J.; He C.
Article.Abstract: Machine learning classifiers are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision systems, yet their opacity creates governance risks that undermine accountability and trust. This study proposes an integrated framework unifying predictive modelling, explainability, and model auditing, evaluated on a primary public tabular dataset (Lending Club) and an independent benchmark dataset (Give Me Some Credit) drawn from the consumer-credit domain. The framework enforces a strict decision-time feature-availability policy under which all post-origination repayment variables are excluded, defines default over a fixed 24-month outcome horizon, and combines class-imbalance handling, seven benchmark classifiers (including a traditional scorecard), probability-calibration assessment, global and local explainability analysis with quantified SHAP–LIME agreement, and a six-dimension audit covering performance stability, feature reasonableness, error structure, subgroup fairness screening, threshold policy, and robustness to missing inputs. On the temporally held-out Lending Club test set, LightGBM achieved the strongest discrimination, with an AUC-ROC of 0.8451 (95% CI 0.8421–0.8481), AUC-PR of 0.6118, F1-score of 0.6097, and KS statistic of 0.5127; its advantage over CatBoost was not statistically significant, whereas both exceeded the non-boosting baselines. A similar ordering was observed on the independent benchmark, where severe class imbalance made AUC-PR more informative than accuracy. SHAP explanations identified interest rate, loan grade, revolving utilization, debt-to-income ratio, credit-history length, and income as the dominant predictors, and SHAP–LIME attributions agreed strongly across a systematic evaluation sample (mean Spearman correlation 0.84). The audit revealed stable cross-validation performance, mild temporal drift, adequate post-calibration reliability, and elevated false-positive rates for low-income and short-credit-history subgroups; because the datasets contain no directly observed protected attributes, these results constitute socioeconomic subgroup screening rather than a demonstration of demographic fairness. The study shows that predictive performance, interpretability, calibration, and auditability can be jointly evaluated in a single reproducible workflow, providing an operational technical-audit template that complements, but does not replace, legal and institutional review.

Article.Title: Self-compassion and rumination mediate the relationship between attachment styles and sleep quality in patients with gastrointestinal disorders
Article.Authors: Fadakar M.; Abdollahi A.; Rasouli A.; Doosalivand H.; Mohammadi P.
Article.Abstract: Sleep disturbances are highly prevalent among patients with gastrointestinal (GI) disorders, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying this vulnerability remain poorly understood. Attachment theory offers a valuable framework for examining how early relational patterns, through cognitive-affective pathways involving self-compassion and rumination, ultimately influence sleep outcomes. This study investigated the mediating roles of self-compassion and rumination in the relationship between attachment styles and sleep quality in patients with GI disease. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 348 adult patients diagnosed with GI disorders at a tertiary referral center in Tehran, Iran. Participants completed validated self-report measures, including the Adult Attachment Scale (AAS), the Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), the Ruminative Response Scale (RRS), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Structural equation modeling with bias-corrected bootstrapping (5000 resamples) was used to test mediation hypotheses. Secure attachment was positively associated with sleep quality, while insecure attachment showed a negative association. Both mediation models demonstrated good fit to the data. Self-compassion and rumination each significantly and partially mediated the relationship between attachment styles, both secure and insecure, and sleep quality. Attachment styles influence sleep quality in GI patients through cognitive-affective pathways involving self-compassion and rumination. These findings highlight the clinical utility of attachment-informed, psychologically integrated interventions, targeting rumination and self-compassion, to improve sleep outcomes in this population.

Article.Title: Conventional diversity metrics underestimate gut microbiome disruption under florfenicol exposure in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
Article.Authors: Streb L.; Assane I.; de Souza G.; Pilarski F.; Queiroga A.; Walch S.; Rath S.; Schloter M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome is an integral component of fish health and growth performance and therefore represents an important production factor in aquaculture. Antibiotics are a major stressor, not only by disturbing microbial diversity, but also by altering microbial interactions involved in digestion, colonization resistance and functional redundancy. Current risk assessments, however, rely largely on diversity-based evaluations and rarely consider changes in network topology. Here, we investigated the impact of florfenicol on the gut microbiome of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) using 16S rRNA sequencing, combining conventional diversity metrics with microbial co-occurrence network modelling. While the microbial community remained overall stable at the diversity level, with treatment explaining only a minor proportion of the observed variation, network analysis revealed substantial fragmentation and a less robust network structure. Network connectivity was significantly reduced, with a near-complete turnover of central hub taxa in the florfenicol network. Our findings demonstrate that diversity-based assessments alone may substantially underestimate the extent of antibiotic-induced microbiome disturbance, with network analysis capturing changes within the community that are highly relevant for microbiome stability and would otherwise remain undetected when evaluations are restricted to diversity metrics.

Article.Title: Formation and preservation mechanisms of ultra-deep microbialite-dominated reservoirs in the ediacaran dengying formation from the central to Northern Sichuan Basin, SW China
Article.Authors: Xu Z.; Li W.; Qiao Z.; Jin Y.; Zhou J.; Fu X.; Lan C.; Yang D.; Zhu X.; Li M.; Long H.; Jin D.
Article.Abstract: The microbialites in the Ediacaran Dengying Formation of the Sichuan Basin exhibit significant hydrocarbon potential. Investigating the formation and preservation mechanisms of ultra-deep microbialite-dominated reservoirs is critical for expanding exploration domains. Based on observations of 374 samples from outcrops and cores, thin-section quantification, porosity and permeability testing, and diagenetic sequence reconstruction, this study systematically analyzes reservoir characteristics under different burial conditions and establishes an evolution model for microbialite-dominated reservoirs. The reservoir rocks are dominated by stromatolites and thrombolites, with an average porosity of 4.52% and a geometric mean permeability of 0.127 mD. The deposition of microbialite provided high initial porosity. Penecontemporaneous dissolution expanded along primary pores, forming fabric-selective vugs. Regional exposure karst of the Tongwan period further created non-fabric-selective dissolution cavities and fractures, preferentially affecting high-porosity zones. Cementation and hydrothermal activity during the middle to deep burial realm caused limited porosity reduction, and hydrocarbon charging may have helped to preserve pore space. Comparative analysis of Well PS6 (~ 8 km burial depth), Well MX9 (~ 5 km), and the Hujiaba section (outcrop exposure) reveals that the second member of the Dengying Formation reservoirs are primarily influenced by meteoric fluid dissolution during the Tongwan Movement. In contrast, the key diagenetic processes affecting the fourth member reservoirs predominantly occurred during the near-surface to shallow burial stages. This indicates that microbialite-dominated reservoirs in ultra-deep settings retain moderate porosity despite strong heterogeneity. Therefore, reservoir quality is essentially determined during the near-surface to shallow burial stage, where early dolomitization and hydrocarbon charging are critical for porosity preservation in deep to ultra-deep settings. The results provide a theoretical reference for predicting ultra-deep microbialite reservoirs and guiding global exploration of analogous systems.

Article.Title: An explainable machine learning model based on ultrasound and clinical features for impacted gallstone
Article.Authors: Gong Z.; Hu Z.; Xue R.; Liu Z.; Fu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Impacted gallstones present a severe form of gallstones. Although positional adjustment during ultrasound examination has well-established clinical utility for evaluating stone impaction, there are still differences between the preoperative diagnosis results and the intraoperative findings. Machine-learning model may help accurate diagnosis prior to surgery. This retrospective cohort study included 1119 patients with gallbladder neck or duct stone. They underwent cholecystectomy to verify the stones were impacted or not. Fifteen candidate variables were evaluated, encompassing ultrasound features and clinical indicators. Six supervised algorithms were constructed with tenfold cross validation. Model performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis, and interpretability was assessed with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Nine variables were retained, including C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, Alkaline phosphatase, γ-glutamyltranspeptidase, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, gallbladder’s length and Length/Width, wall thickness, stone Length/Width. The GBM model exhibited the best performance with an AUC of 0.951 (95% CI: 0.930–0.973), and the lowest Brier score (0.1561) in the internal validation set. A proof-of-concept web calculator was developed to explore individualized risk assessment. The GBM model shows promise in identifying impacted gallstones preoperatively. Pending external validation, this tool may assist clinicians in making more precise decisions.

Article.Title: Fed-SecureCvT: optimized federated learning with cryptographic protection and transformer-based intrusion detection for HER
Article.Authors: Gokila S.; Suresh Babu A.
Article.Abstract: Digital healthcare technologies have transformed the sharing of medical information and collaborative clinical decision-making while raising critical concerns about privacy leakage, unauthorized data manipulation, and cyber risks in remote healthcare settings. Current methods generally focus on collaborative learning, cryptographic security, and network security as separate functions, which reduces their potential to offer an all-round solution in an integrated framework and leaves a key gap in research for the context of secure multi-institutional healthcare systems. To address these challenges, this work presents a multilayer secure collaborative framework that combines intelligent learning, optimized cryptography, integrity assurance, and intrusion detection in a seamless coordinated platform for secured EHR management. The proposed approach is Federated Learning and Federated Dynamics optimization (FL–FedDyn), which could support decentralized medical prediction across multiple hospitals without sharing raw patient data, thus protecting privacy and enhancing the generalization performance of the medical prediction model under heterogeneous data distributions. A Decentralized Multi-Authority Attribute-Based Encryption (DMA-ABE) mechanism is embedded to promote fine-grained access control, with each authority independently providing credentials and eliminating the single-point trust dependency. The Mandrill Optimization Algorithm (MOA) is used to generate optimized keys, which maximizes the entropy and minimizes the computational cost to enhance the cryptographic robustness and efficiency. The Merkle Directed Acyclic Graph (Merkle-DAG) structure is used to link encrypted records via hash relationships for efficient tamper detection and secure storage. Moreover, an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on a Convolutional Vision Transformer (CvT) is incorporated to constantly monitor the traffic in a healthcare network and identify known and unknown threats through hybrid feature learning of spatial and attention features. The modules are executed in a streamlined process that includes data preprocessing, collaborative training, encryption, secure storage, integrity validation, and real-time threat monitoring, all of which work together to provide holistic protection over multiple layers of security. Experimental evaluation conducted on the EHR and CIC-IDS2017 datasets demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves superior performance with a prediction accuracy of 99.31%, convergence time of 118.42 s using only 36 communication rounds, privacy preservation level of 98.74%, encryption time of 5.26 ms, integrity verification time of 11.38 ms, and intrusion detection accuracy of 99.31% with a false alarm rate of 1.38%. The framework also demonstrates efficient resource utilization with a reduced CPU consumption of 54.18% and energy usage of 0.196 mJ compared with existing techniques. These results confirm that the proposed multilayer approach provides an effective, scalable, and secure solution for collaborative healthcare data management in distributed medical infrastructures.

Article.Title: Fluoride enrichment, hydrogeochemical processes, and health risks from groundwater ingestion in the Zabzugu District, Ghana
Article.Authors: Sunkari E.; Cobbiah M.; Okyere M.; Ambushe A.
Article.Abstract: Groundwater quality in the Zabzugu District, Northern Ghana, is increasingly affected by geogenic processes and anthropogenic activities, particularly agriculture. This study examined the hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling mechanisms, and health implications of groundwater in the district. Groundwater samples from thirteen (13) locations were analysed using physicochemical measurements, hydrogeochemical modelling, and multivariate statistical techniques, including correlation, factor, and cluster analyses. Groundwater was generally neutral to slightly alkaline (pH 7.01–8.22) and predominantly fresh, with total dissolved solids and electrical conductivity largely within WHO and Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) permissible limits. The dominant cations and anions followed the order Mg²⁺ > Ca²⁺ > Na⁺ > K⁺ and HCO₃⁻ > Cl⁻ > SO₄²⁻, respectively, with Mg–K–HCO₃ identified as the principal water type. Hydrogeochemical evolution was mainly controlled by rock–water interaction, mineral dissolution, and ion exchange, with additional anthropogenic influences from agricultural activities. Fluoride concentrations ranged from 0.231 to 6.90 mg/L, with over 76% of samples exceeding the WHO guideline value of 1.5 mg/L. Higher fluoride concentrations occurred mainly in the northwestern and north-central areas, attributed predominantly to geogenic processes, including carbonate mineral dissolution and ion exchange. Health-risk assessment using estimated daily intake and hazard quotient indicated that children were the most vulnerable, with HQ values exceeding 1 in several communities. The findings support targeted monitoring, groundwater treatment, public health interventions, low-cost defluoridation technologies, and improved agricultural practices to safeguard groundwater quality and public health in Zabzugu District.

Article.Title: Soil parameters associated with Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense incidence and their integration into an IoT-based monitoring system for banana plantations
Article.Authors: Uwamahoro B.; Kuradusenge M.; Bakari A.; Gatera O.; Gaidashova S.; Mtonga K.
Article.Abstract: Fusarium wilt, caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Foc) , is a major soil-borne threat to banana production and food security in economies such as Rwanda. Although soil physicochemical conditions are known to influence pathogen persistence, the precise relationships between specific soil parameters and disease severity along with the potential for real-time field monitoring to replace laboratory testing remain insufficiently studied. This study collected soil samples from healthy and Fusarium-contaminated plots at three banana plantation sites in Rwanda namely Huye-Rusatira, Kamonyi-Gacurabwenge, and Ruhango-Byimana), analyzing nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH, and electrical conductivity in the laboratory. Independent-samples t-tests and Pearson correlation analysis compared healthy and contaminated soils and quantified parameter–severity associations, while a paired t-test evaluated agreement between laboratory and IoT-based real-time measurements. Results showed that contaminated soils were consistently more acidic, nitrogen-depleted, and lower in EC than healthy soils ( p < 0.001 at nearly all sites). pH ( r = − 0.922), nitrogen ( r = − 0.777), and EC ( r = − 0.536) exhibited the strongest negative correlations with disease severity, whereas potassium and phosphorus showed weak associations. These findings identify pH, nitrogen, and EC as reliable indicators of Fusarium wilt risk, supporting their integration into IoT-enabled monitoring systems, with future research aimed at developing AIoT-based predictive models combining soil and climatic data for proactive disease forecasting.

Article.Title: Adjudicator sensitivity of safety estimates in large language models for open-ended cardiovascular reasoning: a blinded multi-adjudicator benchmark study running title: adjudicator variability in LLM safety
Article.Authors: Çelik A.; Kiris T.; Kocabas U.; Karaca M.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated for safety-critical clinical reasoning, but safety estimates in open-ended tasks may depend on expert adjudication thresholds. We evaluated 300 blinded responses generated by three API-accessed LLM configurations across 100 cardiovascular scenarios. Two cardiologists independently scored all responses, and the original workflow used predefined triggers for safety adjudication. First-adjudicator ascertainment was subsequently completed for all responses, after which a separate non-author cardiologist independently re-adjudicated all 300 responses while blinded to model identity, reviewer information, and prior decisions; 53 discordant classifications were then assessed by a third blinded cardiologist using a majority-resolution rule fixed before receipt of the third-adjudicator results. Continuous quality-score reliability was poor (ICC 0.028). The first adjudicator classified 53/300 responses (17.7%) as safety-positive, whereas the independent second adjudicator classified 0/300. First–second crude agreement was 82.3%, but positive agreement was 0%. Third-adjudicator resolution yielded 8/300 majority-classified safety-relevant errors (2.7%, 95% CI 1.4–5.2%). Safety estimates in open-ended cardiovascular LLM benchmarks were highly adjudicator-sensitive. Multi-rater reliability and transparent resolution procedures should accompany numerical safety estimates, which should not be interpreted as real-world clinical error prevalence.

Article.Title: A literature-weighted composite index for integrating reproductive dysfunction and cancer-associated molecular features: a reproducible computational pipeline
Article.Authors: Dashti Z.
Article.Abstract: To construct a literature-weighted composite Disease Activity Index (DAI) integrating gene-expression and DNA-methylation features associated with reproductive dysfunction and cancer, and to establish a reproducible computational pipeline for calculating the index from gene-level data. A hybrid dataset comprising 120 gene-level profiles was assembled from 50 literature-derived profiles seeded from 17 peer-reviewed sources and 70 synthetically augmented profiles. For each gene, DAI was calculated deterministically from cancer- and infertility-associated Log2FC values and a literature-derived weight according to a pre-specified formula, within a general mathematical framework that additionally specifies methylation main and interaction terms. The computational pipeline was implemented to reproduce the index and characterize its distribution. K-means clustering (k = 3) with principal component analysis (PCA) was used descriptively to characterize groupings within the resulting feature space. The pipeline reproduced the pre-specified DAI calculation, and the resulting scores showed three descriptive groupings with mean DAI values of 1.62, 1.17, and 0.91. The groupings reflected variation in the standardized molecular features used to construct the index rather than independently derived biological or clinical risk categories. This study provides a transparent, literature-weighted composite index and a reproducible computational framework for integrating gene-expression and DNA-methylation features at the intersection of reproductive dysfunction and cancer. Because DAI is derived directly from its input features and the dataset includes synthetic augmentation, the present findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Independent evaluation using patient-derived molecular measurements and clinically observed outcomes is required before clinical or diagnostic interpretation.

Article.Title: Optimized piezoelectric energy harvester for hydrogen generation from automotive vibration
Article.Authors: Ehab N.; Kouritem S.; Elmaghlany W.; Harraz E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents the design and optimization of a piezoelectric vibration energy harvesting system integrated with electrolysis-based hydrogen production. The suggested harvester is integrated into an automotive engine block and designed as a bimorph cantilever beam, experiencing authentic low-frequency vibrations from the engine at primary working frequencies of 37 Hz and 52 Hz. Finite element analysis (FEA) is performed in COMSOL Multiphysics 6.1 to assess the electromechanical response of the system under dynamic excitation conditions. Three piezoelectric materials PZT-5 H, PVDF, and improved PVDF (PVDF-E) are comparably analyzed under uniform working circumstances to assess their viability for automobile vibration energy harvesting applications. Structural optimization is conducted with BOBYQA and Monte Carlo techniques to enhance harvested electrical output while adhering to geometric and frequency limitations. The numerical model is evaluated against experimental data from the literature, exhibiting a maximum error of 4.47%, hence affirming its trustworthiness. The results suggest that both material characteristics and frequency adjustment substantially influence electromechanical performance. Among the examined materials, PZT-5H obtains the maximum output power of 1.2507 mW at an ideal load resistance of 10 kΩ due to its better piezoelectric coupling coefficient. PVDF and PVDF-E demonstrate reduced power output but greater mechanical flexibility and durability, making them more appropriate for high-stress and flexible applications, whereas PZT-5 H is chosen for low-stress, high-power-density systems. The captured electrical energy is immediately utilized for hydrogen synthesis using a simplified post-processing electrochemical estimate derived from Faraday’s law, as opposed to a fully integrated Multiphysics electrochemical simulation. Over an operational duration of 600 s, the system generates roughly $$\:1.5123\times\:{10}^{-6}\:\:$$ mol of hydrogen, equating to an energy content of 0.363 J and an equivalent gasoline volume of $$\:1.134\times\:10{-}^{11}$$ L. This study reveals a unique hybrid piezoelectric–electrochemical energy conversion framework that permits direct translation of ambient vibration energy into storable chemical energy, giving a scalable approach for self-powered automobile and hybrid energy systems.

Article.Title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of T1N0M1 lung cancer: a population-based retrospective study
Article.Authors: Sun W.; Zhu C.; Li X.; Zhang H.; Ding X.
Article.Abstract: Metastatic T1 lung cancer has received significant attention in recent years. Stage T1N0M1 lung cancer is a rare subgroup that remains inadequately comprehended. This study aims to describe the clinical characteristics and develop a model to predict the prognosis of T1N0M1 lung cancer. The study selected patients with T1 metastasis lung cancer diagnosed between 2010 and 2016 from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. A nomogram prognostic model was constructed to predict the survival of T1N0M1 patients. The discrimination, calibration and clinical utility of the nomogram were assessed using the Harrells concordance index (C-index), receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA) and calibration curves in the train and validation group. This analysis included 1822 patients with T1N0M1. The T1N0M1 group had better overall survival (OS) and cancer—specific survival (CSS) than the other M1. A nomogram model was established using multivariate COX analysis to predict T1N0M1 patient survival. The overall performance of the nomogram was assessed, producing a C-index of 0.75 (95%CI: 0.73–0.78) in the training group and 0.72 (95%CI: 0.68–0.77) in the validation group. The DCA curves and calibration curves exhibited good concordance from the predicted survival probabilities to actual observation. Our study demonstrated that T1N0M1 has particular clinical features, and that age, race, sex, histology, metastasis site and therapy are closely associated with OS and CSS. Knowledge of clinical characteristics of patients with T1N0M1 is critical to guide individualized treatment and predicting prognoses.

Article.Title: Unsupervised domain adaptation for dialogue summarization with augmented heuristic intermediate domains
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Jiang J.; Qi Y.; Zhang D.; Niu X.; Sheng L.; Lou H.
Article.Abstract: Dialogue summarization, an essential component of intelligent dialogue systems, holds significant importance. While end-to-end summarization models exhibit robust performance, their success is contingent upon access to adequately sized annotated datasets. This requirement creates significant acquisition costs, particularly for summarizing dialogues. In this study, we investigate a challenging dialogue summarization scenario where annotated summaries are not available and the availability of data is also limited, broadening the reach and practicality of text summarization techniques. To address this, we propose an unsupervised domain adaptation method for dialogue summarization that leverages rich external, such as news domain data. To address the significant divergences between conversational dialogues–typically characterized by informality, repetition, and multi-party interaction–and standard documents, which are usually formal and succinct, this work proposes a ratio-adaptive mixup approach. This technique enhances data augmentation by generating multiple inferred transitional domains bridging the source and target. With the guidance of heuristic representations and language model discriminator, we develop both source-dominant and target-dominant models exhibit complementary characteristics. Our proposed methods facilitate the gradual transfer of domain knowledge from the source to the target domain. Extensive experiments conducted on three widely-used benchmarks, namely SAMSum, DIALOGSum, and TODSum, demonstrate the superiority of our approach.

Article.Title: LIPT1 is associated with rheumatoid arthritis fibroblast phenotypes and Wnt-related signaling
Article.Authors: Li S.; Wan L.; Zhang X.; Cheng N.
Article.Abstract: Lipoyltransferase 1 (LIPT1) supports mitochondrial protein lipoylation, but its role in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) fibroblasts remains unclear. We integrated synovial transcriptomes from 39 RA and 27 control samples, evaluated expression in an independent cohort of 152 RA and 28 healthy synovial samples, and examined peripheral blood mononuclear cells from six RA participants and six healthy controls. Commercially obtained primary RA fibroblast-like synoviocytes (RA-FLS) underwent LIPT1 silencing and treatment with the Wnt/β-catenin agonist SKL2001. Independent synovial validation showed higher LIPT1, but not metal-regulatory transcription factor 1, expression in RA. LIPT1 depletion reduced migration and Cell Counting Kit-8 signals, increased apoptosis-associated Annexin V positivity and intracellular copper, increased superoxide dismutase and peroxidase activities, and decreased malondialdehyde. WNT5A transcripts, WNT5A/B-reactive protein signals, and total β-catenin expression also decreased. Compared with knockdown alone, SKL2001 increased migration, Cell Counting Kit-8 signals, malondialdehyde, and LIPT1 and Wnt-related expression while reducing Annexin V positivity, copper content, and antioxidant enzyme activities. These findings associate LIPT1 with RA-FLS survival and migration. SKL2001 counteracts the effects of LIPT1 depletion, although the underlying signaling mechanism remains unresolved.

Article.Title: Spatial-temporal graph convolutional attentional network for motor imagery EEG classification
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Zhang T.; Li Z.; Hua M.; Liao H.; Li R.; Luo Z.; Han J.; Wang F.; Hu G.; Kong X.
Article.Abstract: To address the challenge of insufficient capture of learnable functional connectivity and discriminative spatial-temporal features in motor imagery EEG (MI-EEG) decoding, this paper proposes a Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Attentional Network (STGCAN-MI). The method first explicitly models the functional connectivity and temporal dependencies among electrodes through a learnable dynamic graph convolution module. It then introduces a lightweight parallel spatial-temporal attention module to perform adaptive recalibration of feature responses across channel and time dimensions, thereby enhancing critical discriminative information and suppressing irrelevant noise. Experiments on the BCI Competition IV dataset 2a (four-class) and 2b (binary-class) show that STGCAN-MI achieves average best classification accuracies of 83.17% and 87.50%, respectively, outperforming several representative baseline models. Ablation studies and visualization analysis validate the effectiveness of each core component. This research provides a new approach for developing high-performance decoding methods for motor imagery EEG.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based prediction of clinical pregnancy in infertile women undergoing in vitro fertilization
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Cao J.; Qin Q.; Jiao M.
Article.Abstract: Infertility is a public health issue that cannot be ignored. We investigated the value of routine clinical data for building prediction models in infertile women undergoing IVF. The 6,076 included women were randomly assigned to a training set and an internal validation set in a 7:3 ratio. Candidate variables were first screened using univariate analysis and then further selected with the Boruta algorithm. Seven machine-learning models were subsequently constructed and compared. Their performance was examined from the perspectives of discrimination, classification, calibration, and clinical utility. Among the included women, 3,056 achieved clinical pregnancy, while 3,020 did not. Boruta feature selection retained age, AMH, AFC, day of embryo transfer, and FSH as confirmed predictors. In the internal validation set, XGBoost performed best overall, yielding an AUC of 0.606 (95% CI: 0.582–0.632), a sensitivity of 0.701, an F1 score of 0.619, and a Brier score of 0.241. SHAP further indicated that age contributed most strongly to model prediction. XGBoost showed the best overall performance among the evaluated models, but its discriminatory ability remained limited. Further model development and external validation are required before clinical application can be considered.

Article.Title: Bidirectional interconversion of microwave and light with diamond nitrogen vacancy center
Article.Authors: Yektaaval J.; Mahmoudi M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the conversion of microwave signals to optical frequencies and vice versa, utilizing atomic coherence control and gain-based nonlinear optics within a closed-loop quantum system. We implement this method to establish a three-level quantum system based on a nitrogen vacancy center crystal, owing to its exceptional properties. It has been demonstrated that bidirectional interconversion of microwave and light is possible in the closed-loop quantum system via cross-Kerr nonlinearity due to the scattering of the microwave into the light field, in multi-photon resonance condition. Our investigation delves into the underlying mechanisms and demonstrates that significant efficiencies can be achieved through careful engineering of the system parameters. The capability to convert microwave-to-visible and visible-to-microwave frequencies underscores the potential applications of this technology in quantum communications, radio-optical systems, security applications, radar technology and quantum information processing by superconducting circuits.

Article.Title: Anti-inflammatory effects of active Vitamin D hormone on extracranial vessels after subarachnoid hemorrhage in a murine model
Article.Authors: Kashefiolasl S.; Leisegang M.; Schroeder K.; Brandes R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) causes systemic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction, contributing to cerebral vasospasm and poor outcomes. While Vitamin D hormone (1,25-dihydroxy cholecalciferol, calcitriol, 1,25-VitD) has known vasoprotective and anti-inflammatory effects, its role in extracranial vascular response and neurological recovery after SAH remains unclear. Adult male C57BL/6N mice received daily intraperitoneal injections of 1,25-VitD (100 ng/kg) for five days prior to experimental SAH induction via cisterna magna blood injection. Vascular inflammation was quantified in carotid, femoral, and basilar arteries using RT-qPCR. Endothelial function was assessed ex vivo by wire myography. Neurological deficits and systemic responses were evaluated using the modified Neurological Severity Score (mNSS) and body weight change. VDR knockout lines were used to dissect cell-specific mechanisms. SAH triggered robust upregulation of TNF-α, IL-6, VCAM-1, and ICAM-1 across extracranial arteries. 1,25-VitD pretreatment significantly suppressed this inflammatory response (p < 0.05), preserved endothelial-dependent vasorelaxation (p < 0.01), and improved neurological scores and attenuated systemic weight loss (p < 0.05). Notably, the protective effects of 1,25-VitD were not observed in mice lacking VDR in LysM-positive myeloid or endothelial cells. 1,25-VitD pretreatment attenuates the systemic vascular dysfunction occurring after SAH. These findings identify VDR-dependent modulation of early vascular inflammation and endothelial dysfunction as a potential mechanism of 1,25-VitD-mediated vascular protection after experimental SAH. Whether these effects can be achieved by treatment initiated after SAH and translated into clinical benefit requires further investigation.

Article.Title: GLP-1 receptor agonists counteract the detrimental effects of pasireotide on pancreatic beta-cell function and survival
Article.Authors: Biondi G.; Marrano N.; Rella M.; Galasso V.; Galluzzi G.; Borrelli A.; D’Oria R.; Genchi V.; Caccioppoli C.; Cignarelli A.; Leonardini A.; Perrini S.; Vincenti L.; Aquilino F.; Cascardi E.; Chiurlia S.; Laviola L.; Giorgino F.; Natalicchio A.
Article.Abstract: Pasireotide is a somatostatin analogue used to treat acromegaly, Cushing’s disease, and neuroendocrine tumors. Due to its high affinity for somatostatin receptors 5 and 2, highly expressed in pancreatic beta-cells and enteroendocrine cells, pasireotide may reduce the secretion of insulin, GLP-1, and GIP, causing hyperglycemia in some patients. The diabetogenic effects of pasireotide appear to be hampered in vivo by co-administration of incretin-based drugs. This study investigated the effects of pasireotide on beta-cell function and survival, the protective role of different GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), and the underlying mechanisms. INS-1E cells and human pancreatic islets were exposed to pasireotide without or with pretreatment with a GLP-1RA (exendin-4, lixisenatide, or liraglutide). Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS), insulin content, and apoptosis were assessed using ELISA and fluorescence microscopy, while intracellular signaling, calcium and cAMP levels by immunoblotting and fluorimetric or luminescent assays. Pasireotide reduced GSIS without altering insulin content and induced apoptosis in both models. Exendin-4 and liraglutide prevented pasireotide-induced secretory dysfunction by modulating cAMP, PKA and calcium levels. All investigated GLP-1RAs prevented pasireotide-induced apoptosis via AKT pathway activation. Overall, these findings demonstrate that pasireotide impairs beta-cell function and survival, and support the co-administration of GLP-1RAs with pasireotide to mitigate its diabetogenic action.

Article.Title: Synergistic effects of climatic drivers and anthropogenic land degradation on cascading geomorphic hazards in Iran
Article.Authors: Mohseni N.; Dadashi-Roudbari A.; Mohseni A.
Article.Abstract: Environmental hazard adaptation frameworks have predominantly focused on susceptibility to isolated hazards, often overlooking the complex dynamics of cascading land degradation. This study assessed the synergistic impacts of anthropogenic and climatic drivers on cascading geomorphic hazards in Iran. Our framework integrated land degradation models (MEDALUS and RUSLE) with downscaled outputs from 23 General Circulation Models. We introduced the Dust Hotspot Severity Index (DHSI) utilizing a multi-threshold spatial intersection of Aerosol Optical Depth anomalies. Our analysis revealed hydro-aeolian telecoupling, in which upstream hydrological alterations drive downstream aeolian dynamics. Severe upstream soil erosion and the expansion of hydrological infrastructure have reduced environmental flows to downstream wetlands, triggering neo-playa formation. The subsequent accumulation of erodible sediments transforms desiccated wetland and lake beds- such as Lakes Urmia and Hamun- into hyper-productive dust sources (DHSI > 20%). Copula-based ensemble projections under the SSP2-4.5 scenario for the near-future period (2026–2050) indicate that desertification and water erosion rates will increase by 17.53% and 15.30%, respectively. The spatial extent of moderate-to-severe cascading hazard potential (encompassing desertification, water erosion, and dust emissions) is projected to expand from a historical baseline of 45.30% to 58.60%. These findings demonstrate how the convergence of unsustainable resource management and climatic drivers pushes arid landscapes toward cascading multi-hazard regimes.

Article.Title: Assessing the comparative longitudinal immunogenicity of two commercial foot-and-mouth disease vaccines in crossbred dairy calves in Sebeta Hawas, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Gizaw D.; Fentie A.; Worku T.; Negessu D.; Mekonnen G.; Mokopasetso M.; Ashenafi H.; Temesgon W.; Kassa T.; Legesse M.
Article.Abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) poses a significant threat to livestock production in East Africa, with serotypes O, A, SAT 1, and SAT 2 persistently circulating in Ethiopia. The objective of this study was to evaluate field-level vaccine performance and compare the seroconversion kinetics of two distinct multi-serotype inactivated formulations among crossbred dairy calves in Sebeta Hawas. To achieve this, a longitudinal trial was conducted comparing a quadrivalent formulation (Vaccine 1; n = 58 calves; containing serotypes O, A, SAT 1, and SAT 2) against a trivalent formulation (Vaccine 2; n = 57 calves; containing serotypes O, A, and SAT 2). Humoral responsiveness was monitored using a solid-phase competitive ELISA (SPCE) over a 168-day post-vaccination period. To account for repeated measures, antibody reactivity profiles over time were analyzed using a Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM), complemented by area under the curve (AUC) summation to evaluate total integrated longitudinal percent inhibition kinetics. AUC analysis demonstrated a highly significant main effect of serotype (F(3,396) = 14.32, p < 0.0001), However, neither the main effect of vaccine type (F(1,396) = 1.33, p = 0.250) nor its interaction with the shared serotypes (F(2,396) = 0.063, p = 0.939) on AUC was statistically significant, suggesting comparable total cumulative antibody profiles globally between the formulations. Vaccine 1 maintained significantly higher estimated marginal means at specific time points (e.g., Day 56) for shared serotypes including O ( p < 0.0001), A ( p = 0.0292), and SAT 2 ( p = 0.0203), while additionally providing an independent, robust response against SAT 1. Notwithstanding these short-term kinetic advantages, both vaccines exhibited significant waning of Serotype A antibody reactivity by 168 days post-vaccination, highlighting that FMD seroconversion profiles are context-dependent and vary by serotype and duration. The quadrivalent vaccine (Vaccine 1) is the preferred choice for FMD control in Ethiopia, providing essential broader coverage via its SAT 1 component despite waning Serotype A immunity. Strategic multivalent deployment remains vital, with future work required to optimize booster strategies.

Article.Title: Drainage of Kronshtadskiy subglacial lake in Antarctica observed by double-differential SAR interferometry
Article.Authors: Moon J.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Hundreds of subglacial lakes in Antarctica have been reported by using radio-echo sounding and satellite altimetry, but the detection of small and short-lived hydrological events has remained challenging due to limited spatial and temporal resolution. In this study, we applied the Double-Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (DDInSAR) technique to analyze surface-elevation changes associated with the Kronshtadskiy subglacial lake near the Amery Ice Shelf, East Antarctica. A total of 77 DDInSAR interferograms were generated from DInSAR interferograms with a 24-day temporal baseline by using Sentinel-1 SAR images acquired between 2016 and 2021. A rapid drainage event was observed at a circular-shaped subglacial lake with an area of 61 km 2 . The associated volume loss of the subglacial water was 78.0 million cubic meters (Mm 3 ). Most of the total subsidence (6.37 m) at the center of the subglacial lake occurred during 2016–2017, with a subsidence rate of 2.54 m/yr, followed by a marked decrease to 0.88 m/yr in 2018 and to less than 0.30 m/yr during 2019–2021. Comparison with satellite altimetry data from CryoSat-2 and ICESat-2 confirmed the overall subsidence trend. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of DDInSAR for monitoring subglacial hydrology in fast-flowing polar environments.

Article.Title: TriAlign UDA for hybrid domain adaptation of frozen histopathology foundation model representations
Article.Authors: Ozkan M.; Ozcan C.
Article.Abstract: Foundation models produce strong patch-level representations in histopathological image analysis; however, domain shifts across different centers, staining protocols, and scanner conditions can limit the direct generalizability of these representations. In this study, a hybrid feature-level unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework called TriAlign-UDA, which operates on frozen histopathology foundation model representations, is proposed. TriAlign-UDA aims to reduce the mismatch between the labeled source domain and the completely unlabeled target domain without requiring encoder fine-tuning. The method combines statistical alignment, prototype-based semantic preservation, and adversarial adaptation components within a common learning framework based on a bottleneck residual adapter. In the experiments, NCT-CRC-HE-100K was used as the labeled source domain, TCGA-COAD/READ as the unlabeled target domain, and CRC-VAL-HE-7K as the independent external evaluation dataset. In the results obtained over five different seeds, TriAlign-UDA reached the highest mean accuracy of 0.9669 ± 0.0050, balanced accuracy of 0.9560 ± 0.0063, and Macro-F1 of 0.9515 ± 0.0067 on CRC-VAL-HE-7K among the evaluated methods, including the recent EUDA and PLADA-f baselines. DANN and EUDA produced closely competitive results; however, the differences between TriAlign-UDA and DANN, EUDA, or PLADA-f did not reach statistical significance. These findings indicate that frozen-feature UDA should be evaluated not only through individual alignment objectives but also through independent external generalization performance.

Article.Title: A moderated mediation model of the association between parental psychological control and internalizing problems among college students
Article.Authors: Li W.; Meng J.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Parental psychological control is consistently associated with internalizing problems among college students. However, less is known about the indirect role of interpersonal sensitivity in this association and whether upward social comparison on social media is related to variation across different pathways. A questionnaire survey was conducted among 1026 college students (proportion of males: 56.53%, age: 20.28 ± 1.09). A moderated mediation model was then constructed. Parental psychological control was positively associated with stress, anxiety, and depression. Interpersonal sensitivity accounted for significant indirect associations between parental psychological control and each dimension of internalizing problems. Upward social comparison on social media negatively moderated the association between parental psychological control and interpersonal sensitivity, as well as the associations of parental psychological control with stress and depression. In contrast, upward social comparison on social media positively moderated the association between interpersonal sensitivity and stress. These findings provide targeted intervention ideas for college students’ mental health education in the digital media era through parental psychological control.

Article.Title: Tail reliability of metro bus bridging under spatially correlated road closures
Article.Authors: Li H.; Li Y.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Flood-induced metro disruption can disable rail service and replacement-bus corridors. We examine how spatial dependence in binary passability shapes the mean and lower tail of service from a fixed pre-event bus-bridging plan, and whether shortfalls arise from allocation or candidate-path disconnection. A vehicle-hour-constrained model is evaluated in a controlled stress test using the public Line 5 topology, constructed surface corridors, and nominal demand. At target closure probability 0.529, a distribution-informed plan served 44.59% of demand, compared with 38.80% for the best tested failure-blind rule using the same 540 vehicle-hours, leaving a 5.79-percentage-point matched-budget advantage. At target closure probability 0.35, increasing dependence length from 0 to 12 km raised mean service from 44.98% to 67.92%; bottom-decile service fell from 20.25% to zero. All four dependence kernels reproduced this divergence, with variation in magnitude. Increasing the training sample from 70 to 1,120 scenarios changed mean and bottom-decile service by 0.26 and 0.03 percentage points; no tested conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) weight produced a detectable tail improvement. Added destinations improved tail service; paired marginal gains fell from 22.17 to 0.50 points. After local calibration, the framework can help distinguish tail risk addressable through allocation from risk requiring additional reachable response options.

Article.Title: Improving arteriovenous fistula maturation through anastomotic angle control: A preclinical goat study
Article.Authors: Raut A.; Uddanwadikar R.; Padole P.; Ookalkar D.; Bhatkule M.; Shahane P.; Shelke N.; Akhare S.; Mundhada S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neointimal hyperplasia (NIH) is one of the primary constraints of hemodialysis vascular access, leading to arteriovenous fistula (AVF) maturation failure. One of these factors is the non-physiologic wall shear stress at the anastomosis. This pilot study tested a new external-assist device to standardize the anastomotic angle (~ 45°) and decrease undesirable hemodynamics. Six adult male goats underwent creation of an end-to-side arteriovenous fistula between the medial leg vein and the adjacent medial leg artery. The device group ( n = 3) received an assistive device to maintain an angle of approximately 45°, whereas the control group ( n = 3) underwent standard surgery. Patency was monitored clinically and via Doppler ultrasound for 28 days, followed by terminal explantation surgery for histopathological studies and serum MMP-9/TIMP-1 analysis. All device-equipped AVFs exhibited a strong thrill and maintained patency for 28 days. One control AVF thrombosed, and the other two developed severe venous outflow stenosis (VOS). Histology revealed markedly less NIH in the device group, with all device-group fistulas showing < 25% luminal narrowing compared with 25–100% in the control group. The TIMP-1/MMP-9 ratio, a marker of fibrosis (elevated in progression), was reduced in the device group compared to that in the control group. No foreign body reactions or infections were observed. These results suggest that the device is biocompatible and may improve early AVF patency by reducing NIH, warranting further preclinical evaluation.

Article.Title: An interpretable machine-learning signature predicts early triple-negative breast cancer recurrence but adds no prognostic value beyond clinicopathological factors in external validation
Article.Authors: Nan H.; Di R.; Kou X.; Ma G.
Article.Abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype that lacks targeted therapies and carries a high risk of early distant metastasis, yet interpretable tools for predicting early recurrence remain scarce. We develop an end-to-end, leakage-safe machine-learning framework that predicts 3-year distant recurrence from the gene-expression profiles of 101 TNBC patients in GSE58812, and evaluate it in an independent, clinically annotated cohort—the triple-negative subset of METABRIC ( \(n=320\) ). Supervised feature selection is embedded within every fold of repeated stratified cross-validation, so that seven classifiers are compared on honest out-of-fold predictions; an \(\ell _2\) -regularised logistic regression on a fifty-gene panel attained a mean per-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.689 (standard deviation 0.137) and a repeat-averaged out-of-fold ROC-AUC of 0.738 (95% CI 0.626–0.837), with good calibration (Brier score 0.171). The two are not interchangeable: 0.689 estimates the discrimination of one fitted model and is the primary, more conservative figure, whereas 0.738 describes the repeat-averaged ensemble and is the value to which the calibration, decision-curve and internal survival analyses correspond. Both retain the optimism of having chosen the reported learner as the best of seven on the same resampling: nested selection of the learner gives 0.648. The panel size was fixed a priori; nested tuning did not improve honest discrimination (0.648), and performance was flat for panels of 30–100 genes. Coefficients and SHAP attributions agreed almost perfectly, which for a standardised linear model holds by construction and is reported as an internal consistency check; a model-agnostic explainer applied to three non-linear learners gave much weaker cross-model agreement (Spearman \(\rho \) 0.54–0.94, median 0.62). Functional annotation showed natural-killer-cell-mediated cytotoxicity and antigen presentation, with proliferation up (E2F targets, NES \(+2.23\) ) and interferon- \(\gamma \) response down (NES \(-2.77\) ) in early-recurring tumours. Because GSE58812 records no clinicopathological variable beyond age, METABRIC was used to test the signature against, and on top of, the routine factors that govern treatment decisions. A clinicopathological Cox model discriminated relapse-free survival well (concordance index 0.673), driven chiefly by nodal burden, whereas only 20 of the 50 genes are quantified on the Illumina array, so what could be scored externally is the cross-platform-transferable component. It carried only a weak univariable signal (hazard ratio 1.23 per standard deviation; 3-year AUC 0.55) and did not improve discrimination over clinicopathological factors (combined concordance index 0.652; likelihood-ratio \(p=0.13\) ). Re-deriving the panel within the gene universe common to both platforms yielded a fully scoreable signature that separated relapse-free survival externally (hazard ratio 1.30 per standard deviation, \(p=0.004\) ) but still added nothing ( \(p=0.09\) ), and ComBat changed the external AUC by less than 0.01 while a within-METABRIC refit reached only 0.56–0.57. The endpoint mismatch does not account for this: the signature performs no better against a metastasis-dominated cause-specific endpoint, and even if three first relapses in ten were local the corrected concordance index would rise only to 0.58. A transcriptomic signature can therefore be developed and interpreted reliably, but clinicopathological variables remain the dominant determinants of recurrence risk. The signature is best regarded as a hypothesis-generating molecular adjunct rather than a clinically ready tool.

Article.Title: Ranking handwriting legibility with foundation-model embeddings at human-level consistency on the HaLO dataset
Article.Authors: Bauer M.; Lents M.; Schmidt E.; Hamann T.; Pieger L.; Salata S.; Di Salvo F.; Hoffmann T.; Barth J.; Ledig C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Legibility reflects the visual quality of handwriting and can signal difficulties in underlying motor and cognitive processes as well as developmental disorders. Early identification of handwriting problems is therefore crucial for providing targeted support. However, automated legibility assessment remains underexplored, partly due to the subjective nature of legibility and limited annotated data. To address this, we introduce HaLO, a dataset of 1, 907 handwriting images from 202 students, annotated with 19, 070 pairwise legibility judgments, and release its image features and annotations. We propose a comparative ranking approach for legibility assessment that leverages relative judgments and global rankings instead of absolute scores. Using a linear probe on Pixtral 12B embeddings, we identify which of two samples is more legible with strong performance ( $$\textrm{ACC}=0.83$$ , $$\mathrm {ROC\,AUC}=0.92$$ ), approaching the ceiling implied by the inconsistency of the annotations. The induced ranking reaches human-level consistency ( $$\tau =0.70$$ , $$\rho =0.89$$ ), and the inferred ordinal scores match or exceed inter-annotator agreement ( $$\alpha \ge 0.61$$ ). Additional concept-vector analyses suggest that pretrained Pixtral-ViT embeddings linearly encode interpretable visual properties related to legibility, including cursiveness, stroke thinness, and image aspect ratio. Overall, this work introduces a novel dataset and a ranking approach for automatic handwriting legibility assessment, demonstrating that a linear probe on foundation-model image representations can achieve human-level performance.

Article.Title: Development and multi-response optimization of sustainable hemp fibre/cassia gum reinforced polyester hybrid composites for structural and insulation applications
Article.Authors: Anbalagan A.; Thangapandian E.; Paramasivam B.; Irayyanavar S.; Manivasagan N.; Prakash B.; Kumar J.; Sriariyanun M.; Karupasami M.; Yeshachew M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing demand for lightweight and sustainable materials has prompted the development of natural fibre-reinforced polymer composites with multi-functional properties. In this study, hemp fiber/Cassia gum reinforced polyester hybrid composites (HC0–HC5) were prepared by hand lay-up and then compression molding. The effect of Cassia gum loading on mechanical, thermo-mechanical, thermal, dielectric, morphological, and water absorption properties was systematically investigated. Tensile, flexural, impact, dynamic mechanical, dielectric strength, water absorption, SEM, FTIR, DSC, TGA, and DTG analyzes were carried out. Overall differences among the HC0-HC5 formulations were evaluated by one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and equal-weight multi-response optimization. The overall performance enhanced with increasing Cassia gum loading up to HC3. The HC3 formulation showed the best overall performance among the investigated formulations, with tensile strength of 46.5 MPa, flexural strength of 69.3 MPa, impact strength of 5.70 kJ/m 2 , storage modulus of 4250 MPa, dielectric strength of 16.3 kV/mm, and Tmax of 411 °C. The water absorption increased with Cassia gum loading, but HC3 showed the best overall performance index of 91.4%. ANOVA showed significant differences in formulations overall ( p < 0.05). These results provide a base for further research on sustainable hemp fibre/Cassia gum reinforced polyester composites for multifunctional engineering applications.
