Article.Title: Development and psychometric validation of the healthcare professionals’ psychosocial subjective well-being scale (HP-PSWB)
Article.Authors: Nagle E.; Zolovs M.; Nyberg A.; Skrūzkalne I.; Perevozčikova J.; Ivanovs A.; Reine I.
Article.Abstract: Healthcare professionals are exposed to substantial psychosocial demands that may affect their well-being, health, and professional functioning. This study developed and provided a preliminary psychometric evaluation of the Healthcare Professionals’ Psychosocial Subjective Well-Being Scale (HP-PSWB). A total of 566 healthcare professionals were randomly divided into exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 260) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 306) subsamples. Ordinal EFA using polychoric correlations was applied to identify the factor structure, followed by CFA using the WLSMV estimator. The provisionally retained 35-item model comprised five correlated dimensions: Job Satisfaction and Reward, Work Engagement and Vitality, Occupational Distress and Strain, Organizational Trust and Support, and Autonomy and Work Control. The model demonstrated acceptable fit (CFI = 0.925; TLI = 0.918; RMSEA = 0.071; SRMR = 0.080). Composite reliability ranged from 0.690 to 0.928. The AVE criterion of 0.50 was met only for Job Satisfaction and Reward, indicating that convergent validity for the remaining dimensions should be interpreted cautiously. HTMT values were below 0.85, supporting discriminant validity. The findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the proposed five-factor structure. Further validation in larger and independent healthcare samples is required.

Article.Title: The influence of upper-body dimensions and physical fitness on performance in young swimmers: a PLS-PM mediation-effect analysis
Article.Authors: Song S.; Zhao D.; Yin W.; Tang Q.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: This study applied partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) to examine the relationships among upper-body dimensions, dry-land physical fitness, trunk muscular endurance, and sprint freestyle performance in adolescent swimmers. Forty-seven competitive swimmers aged 14–18 years were assessed for body morphology and physical fitness using standardized strength and endurance tests. Their recent official race times for 50 and 100 m freestyle were recorded. PLS-PM was used to evaluate model fit and the significance of path coefficients. The model showed a good fit (R² = 0.77 for 50 m; R² = 0.56 for 100 m). Upper-body dimensions had significant positive effects on dry-land physical fitness and endurance ( p < 0.01), but no direct effect on performance. Dry-land physical fitness strongly predicted 50 m (β = −1.04) and 100 m (β = −0.85) race times, with negative β coefficients indicating that higher dry-land physical fitness levels were associated with shorter race times, thereby reflecting improved swimming performance. In adolescent swimmers, upper-body dimensions underpin physical fitness development, and physical fitness is the key determinant of short-distance freestyle performance. Body morphology exerted a significant indirect positive effect on performance primarily through enhanced physical fitness.

Article.Title: Age- and sex-based clustering of foot dimensions in northwest Iran
Article.Authors: Hazrati E.; Azghani M.
Article.Abstract: Ethnicity and sex influence foot dimensions, essential for ergonomic footwear to reduce injury. This study analyzes Azeri men and women in Iran’s northwestern region; 4,297 subjects’ feet aged 20–60 were scanned; 3,122 healthy feet were selected. Twenty-nine foot anthropometric dimensions were computed via Python (2021). Principal component analysis (PCA) using SPSS (26) reduced these to three principal components (PCs) explaining most variance in foot shape. K-means clustering was applied across eight age subgroups (AG 1 –AG 8 ) and the total group (AG T ), with clustering quality assessed using the Davies–Bouldin index. Key findings revealed significant sex-related differences in foot dimensions ( p < 0.00). Regarding age-related differences, significant variations were observed in length, girth, and height dimensions for women (p-values: 0.00–0.03), while for men, only length showed significant age-related changes ( p = 0.00). In the total group, PC1–PC3 represented length, width/girth, and height in men, and girth, length, and height in women, respectively. Cluster analysis classified feet into small, medium, and large categories, with medium size being the most common across all age subgroups except AG3. Forefoot shape analysis revealed that men predominantly exhibited Egyptian, Semi-Roman, and Greek types, while women primarily showed Egyptian and Semi-Roman types, with the Egyptian type being the most frequent in both sexes. These findings support age- and sex-specific footwear design, especially for foot length in men and girth in women, and provide a quantitative basis for region-specific manufacturing, potentially improving foot health and offering economic benefits for local producers.

Article.Title: Uncertainty-aware estimation of compressive strength for fly ash concrete with enhanced probabilistic prediction performance by incorporating the associated mortar strength
Article.Authors: Chen P.; Li C.; Li A.; Mo Y.; Huang Z.; Xue M.; Meng G.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: Machine learning (ML) has been widely utilized to estimate the compressive strength ( f c ) of fly ash (FA) concrete due to its high efficiency and accuracy. However, the inherent variability in concrete materials introduces significant uncertainty in f c value, which traditional deterministic ML models cannot quantify. To address this engineering problem, this study proposes to adopt natural gradient boosting (NGBoost), a renowned probabilistic ML model, to estimate f c for FA concrete. Normal distribution-based prediction interval is determined to quantify model uncertainty. Furthermore, the associated mortar strength of the FA concrete is incorporated into NGBoost as an additional feature to evaluate its impact on prediction performance and to explore underlying mechanisms. Results demonstrate that including mortar strength (Model 2) improves the generalization performance of NGBoost compared to excluding it (Model 1). Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) reveal that for the deterministic interpretation, adding mortar strength does not significantly alter the variation trends between original features and their corresponding SHAP values. Mortar strength itself exhibits a strong positive correlation with its SHAP value, allowing Model 2 to capture variations in f c more accurately with an improved coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.921 on the testing dataset. For the probabilistic interpretation, incorporating mortar strength inevitably introduces some uncertainty, with its mean absolute SHAP value of 0.12 MPa in Model 2, but it significantly reduces uncertainties for other features, decreasing their corresponding values by 0.17–0.33 MPa. Consequently, Model 2 attains better probabilistic prediction performance, with a negative log-likelihood of 3.802 on the testing dataset. This study offers a new perspective for observing the reduction and redistribution of uncertainty in ML models and provides a new method for the probabilistic prediction of the strength of FA concrete.

Article.Title: From wetting-front coalescence to urban road collapse: interpretable machine learning of hydro-mechanical failure under coupled rainfall and pipeline leakage
Article.Authors: Xue L.; Huang Q.; Liang J.; Gou Y.; Dong J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban ground collapse poses a severe threat to public safety, road operation and underground infrastructure in densely developed cities. This study investigates the hydro-mechanical failure mechanism of road collapse induced by coupled rainfall infiltration and pipeline leakage through physical model testing, finite element simulation and interpretable surrogate modelling. A validated numerical model incorporating saturation-dependent strength and stiffness degradation was used to generate 120 cases with different pipe burial depths, rainfall intensities and leakage pressures.The results indicate that collapse develops through shallow-soil pre-wetting, leakage-induced wetting-zone expansion, convergence of the upper and lower wetting fronts, and upward propagation of deformation. Leakage pressure is the dominant factor, contributing 86.42%, 87.79% and 92.77% to the variations in collapse depth, near-saturated zone area and wetting-front depth, respectively. Rainfall mainly dissipates matric suction and lowers the failure threshold, whereas burial depth regulates the wetting-front convergence and deformation-transfer path. GPR/Kriging achieved test-set (R 2 ) values of 0.997–0.998, while XGBoost-SHAP confirmed the mechanism of leakage-pressure domination, rainfall amplification and burial-depth regulation. Risk zoning further shows that increasing rainfall shifts high-risk conditions towards lower leakage pressures, particularly at intermediate burial depths. The proposed framework provides an efficient tool for identifying vulnerable pipeline sections and supporting targeted inspection and collapse prevention.

Article.Title: Evaluating the accuracy of the judging support system in artistic gymnastics compared to the 3D motion analysis system
Article.Authors: Ishikawa M.; Koizumi K.; Hata K.; Oda T.; Yasu Y.; Harada M.; Tomita H.; Hisanaga S.; Nonomura S.; Kozachenko O.; Yanagiya T.; Sun Z.; Noro H.; Yamazaki Y.; Waki H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, the measurement accuracy of split angle data obtained using the Judging Support System (JSS), a markerless motion analysis system used in artistic gymnastics, was evaluated in comparison with a gold-standard optical motion capture system (VICON). Nine female collegiate artistic gymnasts executed split leap trials recorded simultaneously using both systems. We defined the split angle as the angle between the left and right leg vectors, each extending from the hip joint center to the toe center, and compared time-series waveforms and maximum split angles between systems. Agreement in maximum split angle was assessed using Bland–Altman analysis and the concordance correlation coefficient, and similarity in time-series movement patterns was evaluated using dynamic time warping. The JSS showed slightly larger maximum split angles than VICON, with a mean difference of − 1.1°, and no significant proportional bias was observed. Nevertheless, the concordance correlation coefficient was high across trials, and the time-series waveforms showed similar patterns during the aerial phase, including the maximum split angle. Temporal discrepancies were mainly observed during take-off and landing. These findings suggest that the JSS can capture the main time-series kinematic characteristics of split angle during split leap broadly comparable to those obtained using VICON, supporting its potential use as a practical biomechanical measurement tool in gymnastics.

Article.Authors: Sutharsan M.; Kavitha K.
Article.Abstract: Accurate lung tumor segmentation and classification from computed tomography (CT) images remain challenging because of heterogeneous tumor appearance, indistinct boundaries, and inter-class similarity. This study presents BAMR-HF, an integrated framework combining boundary-aware segmentation, hybrid radiomic–deep feature fusion, and context-aware classification. BAMR-Net performs tumor segmentation using multi-scale residual learning and boundary refinement, while TRFF-Net combines radiomic and deep features through learnable weighted fusion, while MTCA-Net incorporates tumor and peritumoral contextual information. The framework was evaluated on the processed Lung Cancer Segmentation Dataset with Lung-RADS Class comprising 972 CT images, with 708 images in the training partition and 264 images in the repository-defined held-out test partition. The source labels were consolidated into Mild (LR2), Moderate (LR3), and Severe (LR4A–LR4B) categories. BAMR-Net achieved a test Dice score of 0.8563. TRFF-Net and MTCA-Net achieved test accuracies of 0.9038 and 0.9327, respectively, while the complete BAMR-HF framework attained an accuracy of 0.9478, F1-score of 0.9476, AUC of 0.9872, and MCC of 0.9215. These findings support the complementary use of boundary-aware segmentation, hybrid feature representation, and contextual modeling, while broader validation on independent multi-institutional data remains necessary.

Article.Title: Effects of dielectric barrier discharge cold plasma generated with different working gases on seedling growth and biomass traits in two barley cultivars (Bahman and Novosadski)
Article.Authors: Martami M.; Fard M.; Sabzevari S.; Mohajer M.; Monfaredi M.; Hamidi A.; Ghomi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) has attracted considerable attention as an eco-friendly technology for enhancing seedling vigor, seedling biomass, and early plant development. In this study, the effects of dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma on two barley cultivars, Bahman and Novosadski (Hordeum vulgare L.), were investigated under different exposure times and working gases. Seeds were first treated with air plasma at 1, 2, and 3 min to determine the optimal exposure duration, followed by comparison of different gases (air, Ar, N₂, O₂, N₂+O₂, and Ar + O₂). Final germination percentage remained unchanged (100%) across all treatments; however, plasma significantly affected seedling growth parameters in a cultivar-dependent manner. The optimal treatment for Bahman was 3 min air plasma, while Novosadski showed the best response at 1 min. Air plasma produced the highest overall improvements in shoot length, root length, fresh weight, and dry weight in both cultivars, whereas nitrogen plasma generally showed inhibitory effects. Surface analyses including FTIR, SEM, water contact angle, and water absorption indicated that plasma treatment modified seed surface properties and increased hydrophilicity, which likely enhanced water uptake and seedling development. These findings demonstrate that DBD cold plasma can improve early barley growth, although the effectiveness strongly depends on treatment conditions and cultivar type.

Article.Title: A robust resilience improvement method for distribution network based on pre-layout and dynamic scheduling of grid-forming mobile energy storage
Article.Authors: Su L.; Wei M.; Feng W.; Cao K.; Chen Z.; Gu R.
Article.Abstract: To enhance the resilience of distribution networks (DN) against extreme disasters, this paper proposes a robust resilience improvement method based on the pre-layout and dynamic scheduling of grid-forming mobile energy storage (GF-MES). The method follows a pre-disaster defense (PD) and post-disaster recovery (PR) framework. In the PD phase, a two-stage robust optimization (TS-RO) model is formulated considering PV output uncertainty, aiming to optimize both investment costs and load curtailment. The Column-and-Constraint Generation (C&CG) algorithm is used to determine the initial GF-MES deployment plan. In the PR phase, by leveraging the capabilities of GF-MES in frequency regulation and power support and integrating changes in the operation status of the traffic network (TN), a power supply recovery (PSR) model is developed to coordinate GF-MES and electric vehicle stations (EVS). This model is solved as a mixed-integer second-order cone problem (MISOCP) to obtain the optimal scheduling strategy. Finally, simulations are conducted on a modified IEEE 69-bus DN, and the simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the resilience of the DN.

Article.Title: Lipoprotein-related biomarkers HDL-C and apoA-I predict infection risk in patients with liver cirrhosis
Article.Authors: Rainer F.; Trieb M.; Horvath A.; Douschan P.; Scharnagl H.; Heinemann Á.; Marsche G.; Stadlbauer V.; Stauber R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infections are major drivers of decompensation and mortality in cirrhosis. High-density lipoprotein (HDL) and its major protein component apolipoprotein A-I (apoA-I) exhibit immune-modulatory properties, yet their role in predicting infection risk in cirrhosis remains poorly defined. This single-centre cohort study evaluated baseline HDL cholesterol (HDL-C) and apoA-I in 311 patients with cirrhosis (training: n = 225; temporal validation: n = 86). The primary endpoint was infection requiring antibiotic therapy within 12 months. Cox regression, C-indices and censoring-adjusted time-dependent ROC analyses assessed prognostic performance. In the training cohort, both biomarkers improved discrimination when added to MELD. The biomarker models achieved higher C-indices and numerically higher 12-month AUCs than MELD and Child-Pugh alone. Discrimination attenuated in the validation cohort, where the biomarker-based models performed comparably to the established MELD and Child-Pugh scores. Training-derived exploratory cut-offs of HDL-C < 40.4 mg/dL and apoA-I < 98.5 mg/dL identified groups with higher infection risk. Occurrence of infection signaled a clear transition towards an unfavorable clinical trajectory, with a mortality rate of 41% during follow-up. These findings support HDL-C and apoA-I as candidate prognostic biomarkers of infection susceptibility. External validation and prospective assessment of clinical utility are needed; causal and therapeutic implications require dedicated investigation.

Article.Title: A schema-enforced large language model framework produces largely reproducible decision codes in simulated sarcoma tumor boards
Article.Authors: Ammo T.; Englich M.; Adrego F.; Jacobi M.; Wilckens A.; Kruppa P.; Bonaventura B.; Niemuth S.; Weiler S.; Wachenfeld-Teschner V.; Boos A.; Freund G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models require reproducible outputs for systematic evaluation in tumor boards. We developed a sarcoma tumor-board simulator using Claude Opus 4.5 at temperature 0.0, schema-enforced JSON output, and prompt-specified semantic and conditional-logic rules. The framework was evaluated on 51 de-identified cases across 154 runs. Reproducibility was defined as agreement across all runs of a case per decision code. In the 41 cases not used during development, reproducibility was 94.2% (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI 91.9–96.1); in the 10 development cases, 93.3% (95% CI 88.6–97.6). Pooled, it was 94.0% (95% CI 92.0–95.8); 17 cases agreed on all 21 codes. Estimates are model-specific. A post hoc ablation on 15 cases compared the framework with and without these rules: 94.6% versus 82.5% (difference 12.1 points; 95% CI 7.6–17.1). The improvement was driven mainly by exact wording agreement in three free-text fields (+ 60.0 points), whereas the 18 categorical and numeric codes differed by 4.1 points (95% CI − 0.7 to 9.3). Without any schema, a decision was stated for only 37.6% of instances versus 100% under schema enforcement; seven codes were never addressed. Single-reviewer screening detected no fabricated numbers, references, or measurements. Clinical correctness was not assessed. Consistent recommendations may still be incorrect.

Article.Title: Insights into cardiovascular development of zebrafish embryo after exposure to dolutegravir
Article.Authors: Ferretti S.; Zizioli D.; Manenti M.; Tiecco G.; Monti E.; Castelli F.; Quiros-Roldan E.; Zanella I.
Article.Abstract: The use of the up-to-date antiretroviral therapy (ART), including the integrase strand-transfer inhibitors (INSTIs), has significantly reduced mortality associated with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection. Nonetheless, some INSTIs like dolutegravir (DTG) have been found to affect fetal development, particularly regarding neural tube defects. In vivo studies, mainly aimed to evaluate the DTG effects on neurodevelopment, also described cardiovascular defects, prompting further investigations into DTG cardiovascular embryotoxic potential. Here we used the zebrafish embryo model to elucidate the effect of DTG exposure on cardiovascular system function and development. Embryos were treated with DTG at several concentrations, resulting in cardiovascular toxicity, demonstrated by the presence of pericardial edema and hemorrhage. At dosage (1 µM), we found a profound impairment of cardiovascular function, characterized by decreased vessel blood flow and heartbeat. Cardiovascular function impairments were accompanied by morphological developmental defects, characterized by shrunken atria and ventricles, altered cardiac looping and defects in angiogenesis. Molecular analysis of DTG-induced cardiovascular mechanisms of those effects revealed the DTG-induced impairment of genes that are crucial in cardiac myofibrillar organization, cardiomyocyte contractility and vascular morphogenesis and function ( myh6/amhc , myl7/cmlc2 , vegfaa , kdrl/vegfr2a , flt1/vegfr1 , hif1aa , runx1 and gata1a ). Our exploratory findings suggest that exposure of zebrafish embryos to 1 µM DTG results in embryonic cardiovascular functional and morphological impairments, mechanistically could be linked to the disturbed regulation of key genes involved in cardiovascular development.

Article.Title: Immunoinformatics design and in vitro evaluation of dendritic cell-targeting brucellosis multi-epitope vaccine based on Omp28 and GroEL
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Chen N.; Shi J.; Luo J.; Chai Z.; Li C.; Zhang S.; Pang N.; Zhu Y.; Zhang F.
Article.Abstract: Brucellosis is a zoonotic infectious disease caused by bacteria of the genus Brucella, with an estimated global annual incidence of approximately 2.1 million cases. Currently, there is no safe and effective human vaccine available. Utilizing a reverse vaccinology strategy, this study screened 16 cytotoxic T lymphocyte epitopes, 10 helper T lymphocyte epitopes, and 3 B cell epitopes derived from Brucella Omp28 and GroEL proteins. These epitopes were fused with a dendritic cell-targeting peptide to design a stable, hydrophilic, non-toxic, and non-allergenic multi-epitope vaccine. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations demonstrated that the vaccine could stably bind to major histocompatibility complex molecules and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4). Immune simulations using C-ImmSim indicated that the vaccine could elicit a robust immune response. Subsequently, the recombinant plasmid pET-28a(+)-D-OG was constructed and introduced into Escherichia coli for induced expression and purification. Further in vitro experiments, including indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, cytometric bead array assay, and flow cytometry, were conducted to validate the immunogenicity of the vaccine ( P < 0.01). The D-OG constructed in this study exhibits excellent structural stability and strong immunogenicity, effectively activating dendritic cells and enhancing antigen presentation efficiency to elicit robust specific immune responses. Combined bioinformatic analyses and multiple in vitro experiments in this study collectively suggest that the candidate vaccine exhibits robust immunogenicity. It holds promising prophylactic potential against brucellosis and offers a valuable blueprint for developing multi-epitope vaccines targeting other intracellular bacterial pathogens.

Article.Title: Numerical study of scattering and polarisation characteristics of marine spherical aerosol particles illuminated by non-diffracting Tricomi beams
Article.Authors: Arfan M.; Althobaiti A.; Althobaiti S.; Meglinski I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-diffracting light beams have exceptional self-healing and propagation characteristics that make them unique for free-space optical communication, atmospheric optics, and remote sensing. Tricomi beams are a novel type of diffraction-free, structure-shaped beam whose scattering characteristics in humid maritime aerosol environments remain mostly unexplored. In this work, we present a comprehensive theoretical study of the scattering as well as the polarisation response of marine spherical aerosol particles illuminated by non-diffracting Tricomi beams. We use the generalized Lorenz–Mie theory to calculate the Tricomi beam shape coefficients. Then we examine the far-field scattering intensity and polarisation characteristics. We display that the scattering intensity and polarisation response can be meticulously controlled by tuning the beam configuration parameters, i.e., topological charge, asymmetry parameters, and half-cone angle, alongside variations in marine aerosol size and refractive index impacted by the relative humidity factor. The scattered intensity is enhanced by increasing the aerosol radius or topological charge, whereas the presence of marine aerosols caused by humidity induces significant changes for scattering amplitude as well as relative polarisation response. These findings explore Tricomi beams’ basic scattering response in humid maritime surroundings and highlight their potential for vigorous optical communication over aerosol-laden channels and polarisation-based environmental monitoring.

Article.Title: Energy-dependent underwater abrasion behavior of sustainable lightweight concrete incorporating agro-waste aggregates and natural fibers under rotational hydraulic conditions
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Karthikeyan K.; Murali G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lightweight aggregate concrete has become a popular material in hydraulic engineering and coastal and offshore engineering, and understanding its durability under underwater rotational abrasion is critical. Comparative studies on the abrasion resistance of several agricultural waste aggregates under high-energy underwater conditions have been conducted for the production of sustainable concrete; however, such studies are still scarce, especially considering the combined effects of rotational speed, abrasion time, aggregate properties, and properties of the interfacial transition zone between the aggregate and cement matrix. This study aims to fill this research gap by comparing conventional concrete with lightweight aggregate concrete using coconut shell, expanded clay aggregate, oil palm shell, and areca nut shell aggregates with natural fibers (hemp, jute, and coir) under underwater rotational abrasion. Abrasion tests were conducted at 1200 rpm and 1600 rpm to investigate the influence of exposure time, abrasion energy, and aggregate nature on the abrasion resistance. Findings indicated that the Abrasion loss increased linearly with exposure time, confirming cumulative mechanical erosion. After 6 h at 1600 rpm, weight loss increased from 461.93 g for conventional concrete to 549.44–698.91 g for lightweight concretes. Wear rate ranged from 23.35–38.80 g/h (1200 rpm) and 55.42–116.49 g/h (1600 rpm), while weight loss ratio varied between 1.78 and 2.60. Among lightweight mixtures, palm oil shell-hemp fiber exhibited the lowest speed sensitivity and the most stable abrasion performance under severe underwater conditions.

Article.Title: HOXA5 silencing via DNA methylation reveals the critical role of HOX gene deregulation in oral carcinogenesis
Article.Authors: Basavarajappa D.; Alhedyan F.; Hunter K.; Colley H.; Hunt S.; Naveena Kumar A.; Chakrabarty S.; Radhakrishnan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract HOXA5 , a member of the HOX family, has been characterized as a tumor suppressor in several cancers. However, its regulation and role in oral cancer (OC) remain unclear. HOXA5 expression was assessed by transcriptome analysis and qRT-PCR, while methylation was evaluated using methyl-capture sequencing and bisulfite Sanger sequencing in a clinical cohort comprising OPMD, LN(-) and LN(+) groups and in vitro models. The effects of DNA methylation and retinoic acid were examined using DNMT inhibitors (DNMTi) and/or retinoic acid (RA). Promoter activity and RARB occupancy were assessed by dual-luciferase reporter and ChIP-qPCR assays, respectively. Effects of ectopic HOXA5 expression were evaluated using functional assays, whole-transcriptome profiling, and in-silico analyses. HOXA5 was upregulated and relatively hypomethylated in OPMD and the dysplastic DOK cell line, whereas its expression did not differ between LN(-) or LN(+) tumors and matched normal tissues despite increased promoter methylation. In SCC9 cells, HOXA5 was downregulated and promoter hypermethylated. Weak but significant inverse correlations between expression and promoter methylation were observed. DNMTi and/or RA treatment reversed HOXA5 expression. HOXA5- EPD2 region showed the highest promoter activity and RARB occupancy at the promoter regions was validated. HOXA5 overexpression reduced proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inducing S-phase arrest and apoptosis. Transcriptome and enrichment analyses identified pathways associated with cancer-related phenotypes, while protein interaction and in silico drug sensitivity analyses identified candidate drug-gene associations for further investigation in OC. Our findings support a role for DNA methylation in HOXA5 regulation and suggest tumor-suppressive properties of HOXA5 in OC.

Article.Title: A multiphysics computational framework for evaluating ATP response and thermal loading during skeletal muscle photobiomodulation
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Liu Y.; Qin S.; Lin Y.; Zheng S.; Jiang X.
Article.Abstract: Photobiomodulation outcomes depend on how light delivery, tissue heating, and cellular energy-related activity change together. This study develops a three-dimensional computational framework that combines light transport, heat transfer, and a phenomenological model of adenosine triphosphate-related activity in layered skin, fat, and skeletal muscle. The model compares wavelengths of 810, 850, and 900 nm and evaluates the effects of optical power, beam radius, and a 180 s exposure period. Under the common optical condition, 900 nm produces the highest average and maximum light levels in muscle, whereas 850 nm provides an intermediate response and is retained as a representative wavelength for the coupled analyses. Increasing the beam radius markedly reduces local light concentration near the tissue surface while producing little change in the average light level within muscle. At 850 nm with a Gaussian \(1/e^2\) beam radius of \(w=4\) mm, the modeled muscle-averaged ATP-related response increases at low optical power, reaches a near-flat maximum of approximately 14.73% between 0.50 and 0.75 W, and then gradually decreases to approximately 12.29% at 2.50 W. In contrast, maximum tissue temperature and cumulative thermal exposure increase continuously with optical power. At 0.75 W, the maximum temperature is 38.584 \(^\circ \textrm{C}\) , while at 2.50 W it rises to 45.857 \(^\circ \textrm{C}\) . A local sensitivity analysis further shows that the magnitude and location of the modeled response maximum depend on the selected inhibition threshold. The results show that greater light delivery does not necessarily produce a greater modeled cellular energy response and may instead increase thermal loading. The framework supports comparison of coupled optical, thermal, and biological trends, but its predictions remain conditional on the selected tissue properties, geometry, and phenomenological parameters. Experimental measurements and higher-fidelity light-transport models are required before quantitative physiological or clinical interpretation.

Article.Title: A Covariance-Guided Pursuit Birds of Prey-Based Optimization for global optimization and UAV path planning
Article.Authors: Li G.; Chen H.; Cui Y.; Cao Y.
Article.Abstract: Birds of Prey-Based Optimization (BPBO) may suffer from insufficient directional guidance, undifferentiated population learning, and premature stagnation when solving rotated, multimodal, and high-dimensional optimization problems. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Covariance-Guided Pursuit Birds of Prey-Based Optimization (CGP-BPBO) algorithm integrating three complementary mechanisms. Elite Memory Covariance Rotation Guidance (EMCRG) uses the covariance structure of elite individuals to introduce anisotropic correction into the best-guided branch. Rank-Based Dynamic Pursuit Learning (RBDPL) assigns different learning behaviors according to individual fitness ranks. Stagnation-Aware Gaussian-Cauchy Mutation (SAGCM) applies state-dependent perturbations to restore diversity when search improvement ceases. CGP-BPBO was evaluated using the IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation 2017 (CEC2017) and 2022 (CEC2022) benchmark suites under 30 independent runs. After excluding the officially deprecated CEC2017 F2 function, CGP-BPBO achieved the best mean result on 17 of the remaining 29 CEC2017 functions and outperformed the original BPBO on all 29 functions in terms of the reported mean values. On the 10- and 20-dimensional CEC2022 suites, it outperformed BPBO on 12 of 12 and 11 of 12 functions, respectively. Based on the mean results reported in the benchmark tables, CGP-BPBO obtained the lowest Friedman mean ranks of 1.79, 1.79, and 2.96 for CEC2017-30D, CEC2022-10D, and CEC2022-20D, respectively. In the three-dimensional unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) path-planning experiment, CGP-BPBO achieved a mean path cost of 239.8048 and a standard deviation of 26.2686, representing reductions of 21.74% and 59.68%, respectively, compared with BPBO. These results demonstrate the competitiveness of CGP-BPBO in numerical optimization and constrained path planning, while its covariance decomposition introduces additional computational cost in high-dimensional problems.

Article.Title: Differential interactions of curcumin with POPC/cholesterol and POPS/cholesterol mixed monolayers at air-water interface
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Wang B.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, the differential interaction mechanism of curcumin with the lipid/Chol monolayer (molar ratio 7:3) rich in electrically neutral PC groups and rich in negatively charged PS groups was revealed at the membrane level. Using the Langmuir monolayer technique combined with atomic force microscopy, the effects of different concentrations of curcumin (22, 41, 253 ng/mL) on the surface pressure-mean molecular area isotherms, elastic modulus, relaxation time, and microscopic morphology of the two mixed monolayers were systematically studied. The results showed that the interaction strength between curcumin and the POPS/Chol monolayer was significantly greater than that of the POPC/Chol monolayer, and the response pattern was quite different. The AFM results further shown that curcumin may be adsorbed in the form of aggregates in POPC/Chol monolayer films, while no curcumin aggregates were observed in POPS/Chol monolayer films. The above difference are most likely due to the negative charge of the PS head group and its high exposure on the surface of the monolayer, allowing curcumin to interact with it more strongly through ion-dipole interaction.This study revealed a new mechanism of curcumin’s anti-tumor selectivity at the level of the membrane and provided experimental evidence for designing curcumin delivery strategies targeting the characteristics of tumor membrane phospholipids.

Article.Title: CDCA5 promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression by suppressing ferroptosis through PP2Ac/p53/STEAP3 signaling
Article.Authors: Wu D.; Zhou H.; Liu S.; Wu H.; Jin Y.; Xing R.; Yang H.; Wu G.
Article.Abstract: Cell Division Cycle-Associated 5 (CDCA5), also known as Sororin, is an essential regulator of sister chromatid cohesion and cell-cycle progression. Although CDCA5 has been implicated in several malignancies, its functional role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly in relation to ferroptosis and tumor-associated molecular features, remains incompletely understood. CDCA5 expression and clinical relevance were evaluated using transcriptomic sequencing of clinical HCC specimens, TCGA/GTEx datasets, and pan-cancer bioinformatic analyses. Associations between CDCA5 and genomic instability, DNA repair-related signatures, immune infiltration, alternative splicing, and ferroptosis-related genes were assessed using public multi-omics resources. The biological functions of CDCA5 in HCC were investigated through gain- and loss-of-function experiments, including CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell, cell-cycle, apoptosis, and xenograft assays. Ferroptosis was evaluated by cell-death rescue experiments, MDA, ROS, GSH, mitochondrial activity, iron measurements, and C11-BODIPY lipid peroxidation staining. Mechanistic studies included proteomic analysis, pharmacological and genetic perturbation of PP2Ac, p53 modulation, ChIP-qPCR, and dual-luciferase reporter assays. CDCA5 was significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and was associated with advanced clinicopathological features and unfavorable prognosis. Pan-cancer analyses revealed that CDCA5 expression correlated with genomic instability, DNA repair-related signatures, epigenetic features, immune infiltration patterns, and drug-response-related profiles, although these findings were primarily correlative. Functionally, CDCA5 knockdown suppressed HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, induced G2/M arrest, and reduced xenograft tumor growth, whereas CDCA5 overexpression promoted malignant phenotypes. CDCA5 depletion increased ferroptosis-associated changes, including lipid peroxidation, ROS accumulation, GSH depletion, mitochondrial dysfunction, and Fe 2+ accumulation, while these effects were attenuated by ferroptosis inhibitors. Mechanistically, CDCA5 promoted PP2Ac expression, reduced p53 phosphorylation, and decreased p53-dependent STEAP3 transcription, thereby limiting ferroptotic sensitivity. Genetic and pharmacological modulation of PP2Ac and STEAP3 further supported this regulatory mechanism. This study identifies CDCA5 as a clinically relevant biomarker and functional promoter of HCC progression. Our findings suggest that CDCA5 contributes to ferroptosis resistance through a PP2Ac/p53/STEAP3-related regulatory mechanism, providing a potential therapeutic entry point for restoring ferroptotic vulnerability in HCC.

Article.Title: A deep hybrid feature extraction model based on MobileNet and vision transformer for acute lymphoblastic leukemia prediction
Article.Authors: Elavarasi A.; Jaisankar N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early and accurate identification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from peripheral blood smear images can support microscopic screening, but reliable evaluation requires both discriminative feature learning and transparent reporting of the experimental protocol. This study presents MoViTHAFX-Net, a hybrid MobileNet–Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with Hierarchical Attention Fusion (HAF) and Grad-CAM++ visualization for binary classification of ALL blasts and healthy hematogones (HEM) using the 10,661 labelled cell images in the training component of the C-NMC 2019 dataset. MobileNet extracts local morphological information, whereas ViT models long-range contextual relationships. HAF first refines the two branches and then adaptively combines three learnable morphology-guided feature projections before binary classification. The reported experiment uses an image-level stratified partition containing 7462 training images, 1600 validation images, and 1599 held-out test images; augmentation is restricted to the training partition. On the held-out test partition, the model correctly classified 1583 of 1599 images, corresponding to 99.00% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-score of approximately 0.990 and an AUC of 0.99. Ablation results within the same experimental setting indicate an incremental advantage of HAF over direct CNN–ViT concatenation. Grad-CAM++ is used as a qualitative post hoc visualization of image regions contributing to predictions. Because the reported custom split is image-level rather than subject-disjoint and evaluation is limited to a single benchmark dataset, the results should be interpreted as internal benchmark performance rather than evidence of patient-independent or multicentre clinical generalization.

Article.Title: Exploring transcriptomic and genomic latent variable correction approaches in differential expression analysis
Article.Authors: Appulingam Y.; Jammal J.; Ali A.; Topp S.; N/A N/A.; Phatnani H.; Kwan J.; Sareen D.; Broach J.; Simmons Z.; Arcila-Londono X.; Lee E.; Van Deerlin V.; Shneider N.; Fraenkel E.; Ostrow L.; Baas F.; Zaitlen N.; Berry J.; Malaspina A.; Fratta P.; Cox G.; Thompson L.; Finkbeiner S.; Dardiotis E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Differential expression analysis is a central tool for studying the biological processes altered in human diseases via transcriptomic signatures. However, transcriptomic datasets are systematically confounded by latent variables from two distinct sources: unmeasured technical and biological heterogeneity within the expression data, and expression differences driven by population stratification. Correction using expression-based surrogate variables (SVs) and genotype-based principal components (PCs) addresses these sources independently, yet no study has directly evaluated their combined use against either method alone within a differential expression framework. In this study we hypothesised that simultaneously including both correction layers would produce more biologically valid and reproducible results than either approach alone, and tested this in two independent post-mortem RNA-seq datasets of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) cases and controls with paired genotype data. Four nested differential expression models (corrected for PC-only, SV-only, both SV and PC, and neither PCs nor SVs) were evaluated across the KCLBB (96 cases and 52 controls) and ALS Consortium (272 cases and 35 controls) datasets. Models were evaluated on cross-dataset effect size concordance, cross-dataset replicability quantified by the Jaccard Similarity Index, and biological recall against a curated reference set of 66 known ALS genes. The combined SV + PC framework outperformed simpler models across most metrics. Replicability improved nearly ten-fold compared to the non-corrected model, (Jaccard index: 2.28% to 19.5%), and the combined framework exhibited a statistically significant 2.2% gain over the SV-only model. Biological recall doubled compared to SV correction alone. Effect size magnitude consistency was preserved, though a reduction in Spearman’s rank correlation indicates PC correction refines magnitude rather than gene rankings. These findings remained generally robust to genotype PC number and sequencing platform adjustment, with more variable performance observed under ancestry restriction and upon extension to an independent tissue. This study found that SVs and genotype PCs address non-redundant sources of confounding, and we recommend their combined use as standard practice in differential expression analysis where paired genotype data are available, with the greatest benefit expected in ancestrally diverse cohorts. Notably PCs capturing population structure can also be derived directly from RNA-seq data, potentially extending this framework’s applicability to studies lacking paired genotype data. Although this analysis was restricted to ALS datasets, we expect these findings to generalise to other traits.

Article.Title: BurnAreaNet: a deep learning method for total body surface area estimation from 2D masks
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zheng K.; Zeng S.; Liang Y.; Xiong Z.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of total body surface area (TBSA) is critical for burn diagnosis, triage, and prognosis. It represents the burned area as a proportion of the total body surface area, and is usually expressed as a percentage value. Traditional methods are subjective, while existing computer-aided approaches require specialized equipment or suffer from projection errors. To address these limitations, we constructed MassHumanBurn, a synthetic dataset comprising 5,000 diverse human models with simulated burns across eight TBSA levels, yielding 320,000 rendered views with paired body and burn masks. We propose BurnAreaNet, a neural network that estimates TBSA from frontal and dorsal whole-body and burn region masks. On ground-truth masks, BurnAreaNet achieved a descriptive mean absolute error (MAE) of \(0.55\% \pm 0.49\%\) , substantially outperforming the direct area ratio baseline ( \(1.99\% \pm 1.66\%\) ). To evaluate the impact of segmentation errors, we further constructed SAM_Preprocessed_MHB, where masks were generated using Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2). When masks were generated by SAM2 using box prompts derived from ground-truth masks, BurnAreaNet achieved an MAE of \(0.68\% \pm 0.70\%\) , while the baseline method yielded an MAE of \(2.48\% \pm 3.52\%\) . In a preliminary evaluation on four high-resolution human scan models (HSR_Burn dataset), BurnAreaNet outperformed the baseline on three of four models, while performance was lower for one high-BMI model (BMI 39.1) that may be underrepresented in the training distribution. These results suggest that BurnAreaNet represents a promising step toward rapid, objective, and device-independent TBSA estimation. Future work should incorporate more diverse human model sources, more controllable burn synthesis methods, and support for additional viewpoints to address occluded surface regions, while further validation on real patient data remains essential.

Article.Title: Causality-driven hybrid intrusion detection with entropy-aware feature learning and federated intelligence
Article.Authors: Gupta S.; Gupta Y.; Verma A.
Article.Abstract: Modern IDSs should be capable of detecting and recognizing new forms of attack traffic (including both attacks from known adversaries) and to do so in ways that remain computational feasible when deployed across multiple, geographically distributed sites. Rule based, representation learning, and federated approaches have been used separately, or in combination in some cases. However, each approach operates independently in many cases. Therefore, they fail to support causal interpretability, efficient use of feature information, stable performance against adversarial attacks, and generalizability across multiple sites. This paper outlines a causality driven hybrid ids framework. The hybrid framework includes the Causal-Adaptive Signature Learning Engine; the Entropy-Guided Feature Compression Network; the attention-based Hybrid Cognitive Detection Synthesizer; the Adversarial Robustness Calibration Module; and the trust-weighted Federated Threat Intelligence Evolution Framework. The proposed framework has been tested on three separate publicly available network traffic datasets (cicids2017, unsw-nb15, and IoT-23). Testing included: use of dataset specific partitions that controlled for leakage in training; five fold validation to test the ability to learn patterns within the training data; ten different random seed controlled evaluations. A comparison of the hybrid ids framework was made to: block chain-based collaborative ids frameworks; traditional machine-learning based ids frameworks; optimized XGBoost-based ids frameworks. All comparisons were completed under similar preprocessing conditions and distributions of classes. The proposed ids framework produced detection accuracies of 97.4% and 96.1% on the cicids2017 and unsw-nb15 datasets respectively. An overall detection accuracy rate of 95.6% was achieved on the IoT-23 dataset. Additionally, the proposed framework reduced the number of features retained to 18 (a reduction of 70.9%) compared to the original number of features present in each of the datasets. Across ten iterations, the reported aggregate performance metrics were: overall accuracy = 96.37%; precision = 95.97%; recall = 95.43%; F1-score = 95.68%. In addition, the proposed framework had an average processing time per inference of 18.6 milliseconds. Finally, testing performed under bounded gradient-based perturbation conditions indicated that the proposed framework maintained high levels of detection accuracy (>91.5%).

Article.Title: A comparative investigation on molten salt hot corrosion of GTA and SMA-welded super-heater pipes of 70 MW CFBC boilers
Article.Authors: Pillai L.; Aravind A.; Dhanushwaran R.; Praveen S.; Prabu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The tubular SA 335 P91 joints are generally used as super-heater pipes in CFBC boilers. This research work presents hot corrosion studies on similar SA 335 P91 joints using ErNiCrMo-3 and E9018 B9 fillers via GTAW and SMAW. The HTC studies were conducted at 770 ± 1˚C employing Na 2 SO 4 +60% V 2 O 5 molten salt mixture on parent metal (PM) and GTA and SMA-weldments with 50 cycles. To predict the corrosion kinetics, TGA were generated. The layer of oxide formed on the surface of weldments and PM has been methodically described using SEM/EDS. The phases of oxide layers were examined through XRD analysis. The investigation confirms that the Ni-rich filler fusion zone coupon exhibits superior oxidation resistance due to the formation of spinel oxide (NiFe 2 O 4 ), which acts as a protective barrier against the penetration of corrosive species. The cross-sectional SEM image and XRD results confirmed that the thin scale formed on the oxidized weldments which were well adherent with the substrate. Blistering was experienced at the E9018 B9 weld zone and found to be more vulnerable to degradation. Consequently, ERNiCrMo-3 filler is recommended for joining similar joints of P91 metals employing the GTAW process used in CFBC boilers.

Article.Title: Differentiated service delivery and peer-led digital messages to strengthen health outcomes among young men and non-binary persons who have sex with men in Brazil
Article.Authors: Jalil C.; Torres T.; Coutinho C.; Santos C.; Scarparo R.; Araujo T.; de Sousa S.; Nazer S.; Hoagland B.; Cardoso S.; Luz P.; Wilson E.; Veloso V.; McFarland W.; Grinsztejn B.; Jalil E.
Article.Abstract: Despite the disproportionate burden of HIV among young men and non-binary persons who have sex with men (YMSM/NB) in Latin America, interventions among this population are scarce. We aimed to evaluate changes in health outcomes associated with a targeted intervention. Conectad@s was a 48-week single-arm study among Brazilian YMSM/NB (18–24 years) using an intervention combining differentiated service delivery (DSD) and peer-led weekly digital messages. We used generalized estimating equations to evaluate changes over time during two periods: (1) DSD plus weekly messages (weeks 0–24) and (2) DSD only (weeks 24–48). Most participants reported they would recommend text messages for supporting HIV prevention and treatment (99.4%) and found the weekly frequency to be adequate (92.1%). Article.Title: Breastfeeding self-efficacy in mothers and its association with maternal functioning, maternal knowledge, and attitudes toward breastfeeding: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Fathnezhad-Kazemi A.; Nayebinia A.; Nayebinia F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breastfeeding constitutes a cornerstone intervention, delivering extensive benefits to children, women, and society. Although breastfeeding self-efficacy plays a crucial role in the initiation and continuation of breastfeeding, evidence regarding the factors associated with breastfeeding self-efficacy remains limited in Iran. This study aimed to examine breastfeeding Self-Efficacy in Mothers and Its Association with Maternal Functioning, Maternal Knowledge, and Attitudes Toward Breastfeeding. This cross-sectional study involved 245 breastfeeding mothers with infants under 6 months of age, recruited via multistage cluster sampling. Participants completed five assessment tools for evaluating demographic and obstetric characteristics, infant feeding attitudes, breastfeeding knowledge, maternal functioning, and breastfeeding self-efficacy (BES). Univariate and multiple linear regression analyses were conducted to identify predictors of breastfeeding self-efficacy. The mean (SD) scores of maternal functioning, breastfeeding self-efficacy, breastfeeding knowledge, and feeding attitude were 113.71 (13.83), 56.29 (7.38), 5.42 (1.45), and 52.91 (6.40), respectively. Pearson’s correlation analysis showed positive associations between breastfeeding self-efficacy and knowledge (r = 0.552, P < 0.001), feeding attitude (r = 0.413, P < 0.001), and maternal functioning (r = 0.308, P < 0.001). In the final adjusted regression model, which included previous breastfeeding experience, the model explained 32.4% of the variance in breastfeeding self-efficacy. Breastfeeding knowledge remained a significant independent predictor (β = 0.441, P < 0.001), as did previous breastfeeding experience (B = 1.628, P = 0.039), whereas feeding attitude and maternal functioning were not statistically significant after adjustment. Breastfeeding knowledge was the strongest independent predictor of breastfeeding self-efficacy, and previous breastfeeding experience was also independently associated with higher self-efficacy after adjustment. Although feeding attitude and maternal functioning were positively associated with breastfeeding self-efficacy in unadjusted analyses, their associations were not statistically significant in the final adjusted model. These findings highlight the potential importance of strengthening breastfeeding knowledge and building on mothers’ previous breastfeeding experiences in interventions aimed at improving breastfeeding self-efficacy.

Article.Title: Comparative study of chemical treatments on the mechanical and moisture absorption behavior of coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composites
Article.Authors: Mylsamy B.; Sampath P.; Aruchamy K.; Balaji K.; Palanisamy R.; Rajeshkumar G.
Article.Abstract: Rising demand for eco-conscious-based functional material drives the focus of materials science field scientists towards research on natural fiber-reinforced polymer composites (NFRPCs), which hold significant attention due to their high strength-to-weight ratio and sustainability. For further enhancement, composites are reinforced with surface-treated fibers, which exhibit optimal performance. This work focuses on fabricating epoxy composites reinforced with Coccinia indica fiber. Different surface-treating chemicals were utilised to determine the optimal chemical and its concentration to obtain effective mechanical and water absorption properties of the composite. Results revealed that Coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composite reinforced with 0.5% of KMnO 4 showed superior performance with a tensile strength of 40.13 MPa and a flexural strength of 89.74 MPa. The compression strength and impact strength of this composite were recorded as 50 MPa and 650 J/m, respectively. By comparison, the untreated CIF/epoxy composite exhibited a tensile strength of 34.59 MPa, flexural strength of 66.63 MPa, compressive strength of 34.4 MPa, and impact strength of 386.7 J/m. The failure mechanism of the fractured samples was determined by employing SEM analysis. Hydrophilic characteristics were determined through the water absorption process, revealing the lowest water intake percentage for this composite, indicating the effective function of KMnO 4 in bonding between the matrix and reinforcement. These findings suggest Coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composite reinforced with 0.5% of KMnO 4 as a viable alternative to conventional materials, offering a balanced combination of performance, cost-effectiveness, and environmental advantage for semi-structural and automobile applications.

Article.Title: Analysis of macular ganglion cell status in dry AMD using single-nucleus transcriptomics
Article.Authors: Hameed S.; Sharma T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is classically defined by photoreceptor and retinal pigment epithelium degeneration; however, increasing evidence suggests that retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) may also be affected. The RGCs, including intrinsically photosensitive RGCs (ipRGCs), play essential roles in visual and non-image-forming functions, yet their vulnerability in the human dry AMD macula remains poorly understood. Here, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) of macular tissue from non-AMD and dry AMD human donor eyes to comprehensively assess RGC populations and subtype-specific alterations. The clustering and re-embedding identified distribution of RGC subtypes across distinct transcriptional clusters, with no evidence of global RGC depletion in dry AMD. Comparative analyses revealed largely preserved expression of pan-RGC markers and subtype-specific genes across dry AMD maculae. Notably, ipRGCs, defined by expression of melanopsin (OPN4) and the transcription factor EOMES, exhibited stable spatial distribution, consistent cluster enrichment, and comparable transcriptional levels between non-AMD and dry AMD samples. Log₂ fold-change and volcano plot analyses further confirmed the absence of selective loss or transcriptional dysregulation of ipRGC markers in dry AMD. Together, these findings demonstrate that RGCs, including the melanopsin-rich ipRGC population, are transcriptionally preserved in the human dry AMD macula. This study provides critical insight into inner retinal neuronal resilience in dry AMD and establishes a foundation for future investigations into focusing ipRGC based neuroprotective strategies targeting RGCs in advanced stages of AMD.

Article.Title: A consortium-driven framework for biomarker prioritization in the HEBE aging study
Article.Authors: Bollati V.; Rota F.; Lucini D.; Mandò C.; Bianchi F.; Clerici M.; Biganzoli E.; N/A N/A.; Federico A.; Beatrice A.; Massimo A.; Giovanna B.; Mirko B.; Cristina B.; Chiara B.; Stefano B.; Clara B.; Giuseppina B.; Francesca B.; Elia B.; Valentina B.; Marco B.; Francesca B.; Paola B.; Antonio B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aging is a complex biological process influenced by chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysregulation, collectively termed inflammaging. The HEBE (Healthy aging versus inflamm-aging: the role of physical Exercise in modulating the Biomarkers of age-associated and Environmentally determined chronic diseases) project developed and implemented a consortium-driven, cost-effective methodological framework for biomarker profiling aimed at capturing these mechanisms and their modulation by lifestyle interventions, particularly physical exercise. This framework integrates interdisciplinary expertise and high-throughput analytical strategies to guide biomarker selection while balancing physiological relevance, analytical feasibility, and cost-effectiveness. The framework was applied within a large multidisciplinary consortium structured across multiple research lines (RLs), each addressing specific domains of inflammaging-related conditions, including obesity, cancer, frailty, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, neuroinflammation, psychological stress, autoimmune disorders, and fertility. The resulting biomarker panel spans molecular, cellular, and systemic levels, encompassing inflammatory cytokines, metabolic regulators, neurotrophic factors, extracellular vesicle-derived molecules, lipidomics, proteomics, and platelet activation markers. A key output of this framework is the harmonized integration of cross-disciplinary biomarker data while minimizing biological sample consumption and analytical costs. The prioritization of multiplex technologies and targeted omics approaches enables the simultaneous assessment of multiple biomarkers from limited biospecimens, enhancing efficiency and scalability. Centralized data management and statistical coordination further support consistency of implementation. This work also highlights methodological challenges inherent to large-scale biomarker studies, including inter-individual variability, platform standardization, and the need for longitudinal validation. Addressing these issues through harmonized protocols and extended follow-up will be essential to strengthen future empirical applications. By formalizing and documenting this consortium-driven approach, the HEBE Project provides a transferable methodological framework to support biomarker-based monitoring of aging processes and lifestyle interventions in complex, resource-constrained research settings.

Article.Title: Integrated differential transcript usage and transcript abundance analyses reveal isoform-level remodeling in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Nnam C.; Li Y.; Zhang M.; Mboya E.; Kolling F.; Perreard L.; Palys T.; Pflugradt E.; Seigne J.; Pettus J.; Ren B.; Pioli P.; Song L.; Ernstoff M.; Brugarolas J.; Christensen B.; Salas L.
Article.Abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by transcriptional reprogramming driven by hypoxia signaling, metabolic rewiring, and immune modulation. While gene-level analyses have defined key features of ccRCC biology, they do not capture isoform-level variation arising from alternative splicing. Differential transcript usage (DTU) represents an additional regulatory layer that may influence protein function, pathway activity, and clinical outcomes, yet its role in ccRCC biology and prognosis remains incompletely understood. We assessed differential expression in 127 ccRCC tumors and 33 normal-adjacent tissues from the Dartmouth Cancer Center cohort, with external validation in 94 CPTAC tumors, adjusting for cell-type proportions. Formal DTU was first tested using DRIMSeq/stageR, which evaluates shifts in relative isoform proportions within genes. StageR-significant transcripts were then evaluated in a separate covariate-adjusted limma-voom transcript-abundance analysis incorporating clinical and tumor microenvironment covariates. Consensus clustering of transcript-level expression defined tumor subgroups, and Cox proportional hazards modeling integrated transcript-level features with clinical variables. In tumor versus normal comparisons, 1,170 transcripts passed both the formal DTU screen and the covariate-adjusted transcript-abundance criteria, mapping to canonical ccRCC pathways with distinct patterns across functional and non-functional transcript classes. Consensus clustering based on transcript-level expression identified two subgroups with distinct angiogenic profiles and significant survival differences. Cluster-level analysis revealed DTU-supported transcript-abundance changes in genes involved in cytoskeletal organization ( ACTB ), immune processes ( B2M ), extracellular matrix organization ( FN1 , APLP2 ), and iron metabolism ( FTH1 ), with protein domain alterations including the loss of actin-associated domains in ACTB and immunoglobulin-like domains in B2M . Prognostic modeling identified twelve candidate transcripts passing an exploratory selection threshold across repeated train-test splits and provided preliminary evidence of additional prognostic information when combined with clinical variables. External validation was limited to two overlapping candidates, FGFR1 and NUCB1 . Isoform-level features may serve as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in ccRCC.

Article.Title: Watermelon vine as dual-functional additive in ecological porous concrete
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Zhuang J.; Ma L.
Article.Abstract: Ecological porous concrete (EPC) is constrained by a persistent trade-off: the dense cementitious matrix required for strength reduces porosity and generates a highly alkaline pore environment (pH > 11) inimical to plant growth. To address this, the present study investigates watermelon vine (WV), an abundant agricultural waste, as a dual-functional additive that simultaneously provides physical reinforcement and chemical alkalinity regulation. An integrated orthogonal array–response surface methodology–entropy-weighted TOPSIS framework was established for multi-objective mix optimisation. WV content was identified as the dominant factor governing pore pH, reducing it to 7.6 at an optimal dosage of 3 wt% within 14 days. The optimised mix—comprising 16–20 mm coarse aggregate, 20 wt% fly ash, a water-to-binder ratio of 0.26, and 3 wt% WV—achieved a compressive strength of 10.4 MPa and an effective porosity of 27.7%, with compressive strength remaining stable at 60 d. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a dense interfacial transition zone containing crystalline products morphologically consistent with calcium oxalate, and plant germination tests confirmed vegetation establishment exceeding 80% coverage within 60 days. These converging lines of evidence support an in-situ acid–base neutralisation mechanism, positioning WV as a viable, low-cost functional resource for sustainable construction.

Article.Title: CNS localization drives a profoundly immunosuppressive microenvironment in B‑cell lymphoma
Article.Authors: Niemi J.; Badillo-Godinez O.; Hellström M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) has significantly poorer outcomes than peripheral diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, suggesting need for novel therapies and a deeper understanding of the unique tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) within the brain. To investigate these CNS‑specific immune features, we established an orthotopic syngeneic murine PCNSL model using intracranial injection of A20 B‑cell lymphoma cells. This model showed reliable engraftment and recapitulated key pathological features of PCNSL. Compared with subcutaneous tumors, intracranial tumor‑draining lymph nodes displayed marked immunosuppression, including reduced memory CD8⁺ T-cells, impaired cytotoxicity, increased regulatory T-cells, and altered dendritic‑cell composition with expanded DC2 populations and elevated CD200 and PD‑L1. The tumor microenvironment exhibited even more pronounced dysfunction, with heightened T‑cell exhaustion and diminished CD4⁺ T‑cell activation. These findings indicate that CNS localization imposes a strongly tolerogenic immune milieu that may contribute to the inferior therapeutic responses observed in PCNSL.

Article.Title: An attention-enhanced residual network framework for structural damage detection based on structural health monitoring data
Article.Authors: Xie B.; Cui J.; Lu N.
Article.Abstract: Local damage in steel structures often produces only subtle differences in vibration responses, and measurement noise can further reduce identification robustness. First, vibration responses are discretized into a finite number of states using approximate equal-frequency binning and then converted into MTF images. Coordinate attention (CA) is subsequently embedded into residual blocks to model channel dependencies and directional positional information. The method was validated using experimental data from the Qatar University Grandstand Simulator (QUGS) and the IASC–ASCE benchmark structure. Comparative experiments were conducted across image-encoding methods, attention mechanisms, noise levels, and baseline models. The results show that MTF generally outperforms the Gramian angular difference field (GADF), recurrence plot (RP), and short-time Fourier transform (STFT). Under noise-free conditions, ResNet-50-CA achieves an accuracy of 94.5% and also demonstrates strong robustness under noisy conditions. Through one-dimensional coordinate pooling, ResNet-50-CA jointly calibrates spatial and channel information. Feature visualization further shows that CA suppresses irrelevant redundancy in MTF images through coordinate-aware spatial modeling, producing highly compact and nearly non-overlapping feature clusters with the best discriminability.

Article.Title: Lodging resistance in older and modern soybean cultivars
Article.Authors: Malanchuk J.; Schuchovski C.; Umburanas R.; Anderle L.; Kawakami J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Brazilian soybean yield has increased over time, coinciding with improvements in lodging resistance in modern cultivars. This study aimed (i) to evaluate the impact of simulated upright growth on yield components of lodging-susceptible (older) and lodging-resistant (modern) cultivars, and (ii) to characterize the morphological changes and biomechanical evolution of stem resistance using a historical set of cultivars (1966–2018). Field experiment used a split-plot design evaluating the response of older and modern cultivars to canopy staking. Greenhouse experiment assessed morphological and biomechanical attributes of cultivars. Results showed that natural lodging historically reduced the yield potential of older cultivars by 36%. Preventing lodging through staking unmasked a latent potential in older cultivars, resulting in a 57% increase in grain yield, driven by a 45.2% increase in grains per plant and a 20.1% increase in grains per pod. Biomechanically, modern cultivars exhibited a localized mechanical reinforcement in the middle third of the stem, where breaking force increased by 107.2% across eras, accompanied by a descriptive increase in middle-stem diameter (+ 46.9%). Modern genotypes demonstrated structural stability and high yields regardless of physical support. We conclude that modern cultivars are characterized by an optimized plant architecture featuring morphological compacting (reduced height and vegetative biomass) and middle-third stem reinforcement, which is essential since greater middle-stem breaking force is associated with higher pod dry weight in modern high-yield environments.

Article.Authors: Panda A.; Jana D.; Srivastav A.; Hussain S.; Badola R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Freshwater chelonians face severe extinction risk, and head-starting programs increasingly rely on captive rearing to offset poor recruitment. However, evaluating success by growth and release numbers overlooks welfare and post-release competence. We assessed head-started Critically Endangered Batagur dhongoka and Batagur kachuga under five enrichment treatments, combining growth data with individual-level behavioural scans and 24-hour group activity budgets over 367 days. Final body mass was highest under mixed enrichment (141.1 g) and lowest under no-enrichment (108.1 g). B. kachuga were heavier than B. dhongoka under all treatments. Enrichment-related behaviour was highest under natural enrichment (52.5%) and lowest under no-enrichment (11.9%), while stress-related behaviour was lowest under seminatural enrichment (1.6%) and highest under no-enrichment (10.7%). Mixed enrichment produced the highest basking response and most balanced group activity budget; natural enrichment the highest shelter-use response. Integrating growth and behaviour at the same month × species × treatment scale, natural enrichment ranked first, mixed second, and no-enrichment last. Environmental enrichment shapes growth and behaviour differently; growth and behavioural metrics should therefore be treated as complementary rather than interchangeable indicators of captive-rearing success. Each species-treatment combination comprised a single chamber, with individual-level behaviour from one marked animal; results are therefore descriptive rather than independently replicated.

Article.Title: An adaptive federated deep learning approach for efficient DDoS detection in IoT edge networks
Article.Authors: Kumar P.; Pallavi P.; Saurabh P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has expanded the attack surface of modern networks, motivating the need for accurate detection of DDoS and botnet activity in resource-constrained settings. Centralised intrusion detection systems (IDS) face privacy, scalability, and heterogeneity challenges that limit their suitability for IoT. This study suggests a Federated Learning-based Intrusion Detection System (FL-IDS) for IoT edge networks in order to get around these restrictions. Each client trains a hybrid CNN-LSTM model locally, and a central server aggregates client updates with Federated Averaging (FedAvg). An adaptive global decision-threshold optimisation is used post-training to the pooled predictions of the global model on the held-out test partition in order to address class imbalance. The system is evaluated on the N-BaIoT benchmark together with preliminary validation on a recent public healthcare IoT dataset, with the nine N-BaIoT devices treated as independent federated clients during the primary federated evaluation. The global model achieves an accuracy of 0.9238, precision of 0.9265, recall of 0.9963, F1-score of 0.9601, ROC-AUC of 0.8133, and PR-AUC of 0.969 at the optimal operating point $$\tau = 0.15$$ . SHAP-based post-hoc analysis identifies the traffic features that most influence model decisions.

Article.Abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare anterior mediastinal tumors with heterogeneous perioperative recovery. This dual-center retrospective study included 726 surgically treated patients with pathologically confirmed TETs. The Qilu Hospital cohort was used for model development and internal validation, and 169 patients from the First Affiliated Hospital of Shandong First Medical University formed the external validation cohort. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression selected 26, 14, and 13 predictors for the three outcomes, respectively. Neural-network models were selected for complications and prolonged LOS, and a decision-tree model for pain. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) in training cross-validation, internal validation, and external validation were 0.824, 0.814, and 0.775 for complications; 0.824, 0.809, and 0.776 for prolonged LOS; and 0.695, 0.734, and 0.660 for pain. External AUC 95% confidence intervals were 0.658–0.892, 0.697–0.855, and 0.570–0.749, respectively. Shapley-based attribution analyses supported model interpretation, and a web calculator was developed for visualization. Further multicenter prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

Article.Authors: Yang M.; Ha K.
Article.Abstract: Korean medical question answering requires evaluation resources that reflect local terminology, clinical specialty structure, and essential-care priorities. We characterized the AI Hub Specialized Medical Knowledge and Essential Medical Knowledge datasets, audited the independence of their distributed validation labels, and implemented a package-specific baseline evaluation. Question-type distributions differed between datasets (χ²(2) = 165.82, p < 0.001; Cramér’s V = 0.069). On an AI Hub-supplied 2494-row KorMedMCQA-derived evaluation file containing 2489 unique normalized questions, essential-care and specialized-care Qwen2.5-14B models achieved 64.35% and 64.03% accuracy, respectively; the paired difference was not significant (exact McNemar p = 0.440). Article.Authors: Zheng Y.; Wanghu H.; Xia Z.; Huang Y.; Luo X.; Wang X.; Qiu L.; Chen N.; Han X.; Lai J.; Rao Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Technical variability in pre-analytical and analytical steps significantly hinders the reproducibility of gut metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). To address this, we developed and validated a practical mNGS workflow. First, by evaluating three commercial preservation buffers at 37°C, we identified Buffer C as the most effective for maintaining microbiome integrity under simulated transport stress. Second, we introduced a cost-effective, self-prepared inhibitor removal buffer (Self-IB) for automated extraction, which yielded species abundances highly concordant with the manual reference method (R² > 0.998). Finally, the optimized workflow demonstrated high intra- and inter-batch reproducibility, with most species-level coefficients of variation below 10%. This integrated, end-to-end pipeline (Buffer C + Self-IB + automated workflow) facilitates high data fidelity and robustness, offering a practical strategy for industrial and clinical applications requiring longitudinal consistency, such as dynamic monitoring following fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT).

Article.Title: Exploring artificial intelligence usage preferences among medical students in Iran: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Karimian Z.; Molazehi A.; Hooshmandja M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical education, offering opportunities to enhance learning, research, and clinical preparation. Although previous studies have explored medical students’ attitudes and acceptance of AI, evidence regarding their AI usage preferences remains limited, particularly in developing countries where AI integration into medical education is still evolving. Understanding these preferences is essential for designing context-appropriate educational strategies and responsible AI integration. This study aimed to examine the preferences and patterns of AI usage among students at Shiraz University of Medical Sciences (SUMS), Iran. This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among undergraduate and postgraduate students at SUMS. Using stratified random sampling, 384 students were recruited. Data were collected between July and October 2025 using a validated self-administered questionnaire (AI-UPSS; Cronbach’s α = 0.935), assessing AI usage across eight domains. Responses were rated on a 4-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed using one-sample t-tests, independent t-tests, and one-way ANOVA in SPSS version 24, with a cutoff mean score of 2.5. The highest mean preference scores were observed in Research & Writing (Mean = 2.66 ± 0.79, p < 0.001) and Self-learning/Education (Mean = 2.61 ± 0.81, p = 0.010). Moderate preferences were found for Curiosity & Entertainment (Mean = 2.36 ± 0.81, p = 0.001) and Health Counseling (Mean = 2.40 ± 0.96, p = 0.044). The lowest scores were reported in Design & Programming (Mean = 1.54 ± 0.79, p < 0.001) and Art (Mean = 1.68 ± 0.77, p < 0.001). Significant gender differences were observed in Art ( p = 0.010), Self-learning ( p = 0.027), and Health Counseling ( p < 0.001). GPA was significantly associated with Content Development ( p = 0.004), Design & Programming ( p = 0.031), and Art ( p = 0.032), with higher usage among students with lower GPAs. Undergraduate students showed significantly higher preferences across several domains, including curiosity and health counseling ( p < 0.01). Medical students primarily use AI for academic, research, and self-directed learning purposes, while engagement with technical and creative applications remains limited. AI usage preferences are influenced by academic level, gender, and GPA rather than age or field of study. These findings underscore the need for structured, level-specific AI education to promote effective and ethical AI integration in medical curricula.
