Article.Title: ECO-EDGE: joint DAG offloading and fabric routing in Multi-AP MEC via conic optimization
Article.Authors: Alymani M.; Almutairi A.; Alhayan F.; Alnori A.; Al-Dayil R.; NEMRI N.; Ebad S.
Article.Abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) enables low-latency services by migrating computational resources closer to end-users. However, as mobile workloads increasingly adopt complex Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) topologies, system performance is strongly affected by interdependent data shuffling across the inter-server fabric and synchronization constraints during uplink transmission. Existing models frequently neglect physical fabric capacity limits and decouple communication from computation, leading to inefficient energy usage and increased latency. In this paper, we propose a coupled Mixed-Integer Non-Linear Programming (MINLP) formulation that jointly optimizes multi-AP association, task placement, Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), and explicit inter-server routing under per-application deadline constraints. To address the inherent non-convexity and combinatorial complexity of the joint problem, we introduce the ECO-EDGE framework. ECO-EDGE decomposes the original MINLP using a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) architecture and solves relaxed subproblems via tailored convexification techniques, including McCormick-based convex envelopes for bilinear placement products, a “Bits-per-RB” formulation that maps communication constraints into exponential cones, and power- and rotated second-order cone representations for computation and fabric delay modeling. The resulting relaxed BCD scheme exhibits monotonic objective decrease under exact block solution, while deterministic rounding and topological list-scheduling are applied to recover feasible schedules, which are subsequently verified for deadline satisfaction. Simulation results in dense multi-AP deployments show that ECO-EDGE reduces total system energy by up to \(81.8\%\) compared to a Local-Only baseline and achieves an empirical deadline satisfaction rate of \(97.9\%\) , outperforming heuristic, fabric-oblivious, and disjoint optimization baselines.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: mobile edge computing; task placement; block coordinate descent; dynamic voltage and frequency scaling; energy efficiency; deadline constraints; mixed-integer nonlinear programming; conic optimization

Article.Title: Intelligent adaptive energy management framework for hybrid solar-grid EV fast-charging stations with energy storage and time-based demand response optimization
Article.Authors: Govindasamy D.; Rathinam R.; Zneid B.; Bereznychenko V.; Touti E.
Article.Abstract: The rapid expansion of electric vehicle (EVs) is significantly increasing pressure on the conventional electrical grid and introducing new challenges in load management, peak demand, and grid stability. Conventional grid systems, dependent on fossil fuel-based generation, contribute to greenhouse gas emissions and limit the environmental benefits of EV adoption. Although several studies have integrated photovoltaic (PV) systems with EV charging networks, most have not addressed real-time coordination between multiple power sources, time-of-use (ToU) pricing, and dynamic demand response (DR). To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an Intelligent Adaptive Energy Management Framework (IAEMF) for a 1 MW hybrid solar-grid EV DC fast-charging station equipped with a 600-kWh energy storage system (ESS). The framework incorporates a time-adaptive multi-mode control algorithm that dynamically allocates power among PV generation, ESS, and the utility grid based on irradiance, electricity pricing, and load demand. The proposed system supports five operational modes PV-to-ESS, PV-to-EV, Grid-to-EV, ESS-to-EV, and PV-to-Grid facilitating fully bidirectional energy exchange across the DC bus. A variable-step Perturb and Observe (P&O) MPPT algorithm is implemented to maximize solar energy extraction, while the adaptive allocation strategy continuously adjusts PV distribution factors according to ESS state-of-charge (SOC) and demand variations. Time-of-use (ToU) pricing enables cost-effective energy management by shifting grid charging to off-peak periods and the demand response (DR) enables priority-based scheduling during peak periods by balancing user urgency, PV utilization, and grid cost simultaneously. MATLAB/Simulink simulations demonstrate that the proposed IAEMF achieves 87.8% renewable energy utilization, a grid export-to-import ratio of 4.2:1, and 71.8% average daily solar contribution, while maintaining stable DC bus voltage and efficient ESS utilization. Furthermore, the proposed system achieves CO₂ emission reduction of 659.5 tonnes/year by minimizing through grid imports. In addition, the total PV generation-based CO₂ offset reaches 1,853 tonnes per year. The results validate that the proposed hybrid architecture provides a scalable and sustainable solution for next-generation EV fast-charging infrastructure.

Article.Title: Optimization of UV-C irradiation time for biologically treated saline wastewater using artificial neural networks and a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making framework
Article.Authors: Omidvar M.; Farahbod F.
Article.Abstract: Biologically treated saline industrial wastewater may still contain residual organic matter, nutrients, petroleum hydrocarbons, and dissolved constituents that limit the quality and potential reuse of the treated effluent. Ultraviolet-C (UV-C) irradiation is a chemical-free polishing technology with potential for further improving effluent quality; however, its treatment performance depends strongly on irradiation time, and excessive exposure may increase energy consumption without providing proportional improvements. Moreover, optimization based on a single water-quality parameter cannot adequately represent the simultaneous changes and trade-offs among multiple effluent-quality indicators. Existing approaches commonly evaluate UV treatment using individual quality parameters or conventional statistical analyses, while artificial neural networks provide prediction capability but have limited interpretability for selecting an operating condition. Conversely, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approaches can support transparent optimization but are generally restricted to experimentally investigated conditions. Therefore, an integrated framework that combines experimental UV-C treatment, predictive modeling, and interpretable multi-criteria optimization is required for systematic determination of the irradiation time. This study aimed to experimentally investigate the effect of UV-C irradiation time on biologically treated saline industrial wastewater and to develop an integrated ANN–MCDM framework for predicting wastewater-quality responses, identifying influential quality parameters, and determining the optimum irradiation condition. A laboratory-scale reactor equipped with a 30 W low-pressure mercury lamp emitting at 254 nm was employed at irradiation times of 40–320 s. Prior to irradiation, 4.8 g of dry ice was used for pH conditioning. Nine wastewater-quality parameters, namely COD, BOD, phosphate, nitrate, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH), turbidity, total dissolved solids (TDS), and pH, were evaluated. A 64–32–16–9 multilayer perceptron ANN was developed for simultaneous prediction of the normalized quality parameters. In parallel, Min–Max normalization, K-Means clustering, principal component analysis (PCA), a Composite Wastewater Quality Index (CWQI), TOPSIS, and sensitivity analysis were integrated to classify treatment regimes, determine parameter weights, evaluate overall treatment quality, rank irradiation times, and identify the most influential quality indicators. Wastewater quality generally improved with increasing irradiation time, with the most pronounced overall improvement occurring between 240 and 280 s, followed by a saturation tendency at longer exposure. The integrated analysis identified 280 s as the optimum irradiation time , yielding a maximum CWQI of 0.977 and a TOPSIS score of 0.966 . At this condition, COD and BOD reductions reached approximately 41.1% and 17.5% , respectively, while improvements were also observed in DOC, TPH, phosphate, nitrate, turbidity, and TDS. At 320 s, the CWQI and TOPSIS score decreased to 0.925 and 0.894 , respectively, indicating that prolonged irradiation did not provide a corresponding improvement in overall treatment performance. PCA identified phosphate as the most influential parameter, with a normalized weight of 0.168 , followed by COD ( 0.149 ), DOC ( 0.139 ), and BOD ( 0.125 ). The sensitivity analysis produced the same parameter-importance sequence. The ANN achieved an average test RMSE of approximately 0.12 on the normalized scale and provided predictions for irradiation times not explicitly included in the experimental dataset. The ANN and hybrid MCDM approaches provide complementary capabilities: the ANN enables simultaneous nonlinear prediction at untested irradiation times, whereas the hybrid framework provides greater mathematical transparency through clustering, objective weighting, composite quality assessment, ranking, and sensitivity analysis. The agreement between CWQI and TOPSIS in identifying 280 s demonstrates consistency between two independent multi-criteria evaluation approaches. From a practical perspective, the results indicate that extending irradiation beyond the optimum does not necessarily improve overall effluent quality and may increase irradiation time and associated energy demand without proportional treatment benefits. The proposed integration of UV-C polishing, ANN-based prediction, and an interpretable hybrid MCDM framework provides a systematic approach for evaluating and optimizing biologically treated saline industrial wastewater. The methodology enables simultaneous consideration of multiple water-quality parameters while retaining predictive capability for untested operating conditions. The identified optimum of 280 s provides a data-driven operating condition for the investigated laboratory system and establishes a basis for further studies involving repeated experiments, uncertainty analysis, explicit UV fluence measurements, microbial inactivation, and scale-up toward practical wastewater reuse applications.

Article.Title: Prioritizing climate-resilient housing recovery in conflict-affected Yemen: a district-level MCDA and uncertainty framework
Article.Authors: Al-Azazi S.; Alezi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. The model combines seven dimensions: flood hazard, human exposure, built exposure, climate stress, conflict fragility, displacement pressure and humanitarian severity. Four weighting scenarios are tested, and Monte Carlo perturbation examines rank stability when normalized inputs and scenario weights vary. The model does not estimate direct housing damage; it screens districts under combined physical and social pressures and compares the national ranking with heterogeneous city-level evidence. The highest-ranked districts are Ma’rib, Ma’rib City, Sirwah, Al Marawi’ah, Khur Maksar, Ad Durayhimi, Tuban and Bani Sa’d. Flood-gate, missing-data, internal-weight and sparse-RDT ablation tests preserve the leading pattern, although uncertainty increases near selection thresholds. The framework provides a transparent national screening tool for recovery sequencing, subject to local engineering assessment and stakeholder validation before implementation.

Article.Title: Device-assisted calf-raise training combining high-speed and eccentric exercises improves gait speed in older adults
Article.Authors: Kanayama A.; Ueba R.; Yamamoto S.; Kinoshita S.; Nagao H.; Yano Y.; Kamimukai C.; Doma K.; Iwata A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plantar flexors are critical for mobility in older adults. Although movement velocity contributes to gait performance in addition to strength, few interventions target both plantar flexor strength and velocity. To address this gap, we developed a novel device to support a program incorporating both high-speed and eccentric plantar-flexor exercises and examined whether this device-assisted program improves plantar flexion strength, movement velocity, and gait speed. In a nonrandomized controlled trial, 40 older adults were allocated to either a training group ( n = 20) or a control group ( n = 20). The training group undertook a 10-week calf-raise program using a custom-built device, whereas the control group continued usual activities. The program was performed twice daily, 5 days per week, and included high-speed calf-raises (20 repetitions) and eccentric calf-raises (30 repetitions). Of the 19 participants who initiated the intervention, 18 completed the program (retention rate, 94.7%), and all achieved the prescribed target dose (adherence, 100%). Compared with controls, the training group showed greater improvements in gait speed (+ 0.17 m/s) and plantar flexion strength (+ 7.5 kgf) and movement velocity (+ 104.9 °/s). These findings suggest that device-assisted calf-raise training may improve plantar flexor function and gait performance in older adults. Trial registration: UMIN-CTR, UMIN000052504; 15/10/2023.

Article.Title: High-pressure processing and thermal pasteurization of blueberry purée-based baby food differentially modulate polyphenol bioaccessibility and intestinal cell responses
Article.Authors: Mazurkiewicz B.; Matusiewicz M.; Wojcik-Gront E.; Krucon T.; Uhrynowski W.; Jeznach N.; Jaworski S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proper processing of baby foods, ensuring both safety and the highest possible nutrient retention and bioaccessibility, is of particular importance for the health and development of infants and young children. In this study, blueberry purée-based baby food was subjected to conventional thermal pasteurization (TP) and high-pressure processing (HPP) at moderate temperature, and their effects on sensory quality and the availability of bioactive compounds were compared. Polyphenol stability and antioxidant bioaccessibility were evaluated during storage and simulated gastrointestinal digestion, while intestinal cell responses and prebiotic-related activity were assessed separately. HPP-treated purées showed significantly higher phenolic bioaccessibility, whereas differences in antioxidant bioaccessibility and anthocyanin recovery between treatments were not statistically significant. Caco-2 cell viability varied with treatment and incubation time, whereas intracellular reactive oxygen species levels were not significantly affected by processing treatment and decreased with incubation time. The effects of both preservation methods on microbial growth were dependent on bacterial group and incubation time. Positive PAS values were observed for Lactobacillus after both 24 and 48 h, whereas Bifidobacterium did not show a selective growth advantage over Enterobacteriaceae under the applied experimental conditions. Short-chain fatty acids remained below the detection threshold in the fermented purée samples and the inulin control, although several unsaturated fatty acids were quantifiable after fermentation in both processed purées. These results demonstrate that HPP and thermal pasteurization differentially modulate the functional properties of blueberry purée-based baby food and highlight the importance of preservation strategy selection in the development of foods intended for sensitive consumer groups.

Article.Title: Tribological performance of PTFE/polyimide pulp/GCNT composites
Article.Authors: Zhou J.; Sun X.; Zhao D.; Si C.; Wu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is widely used as a solid lubricant but suffers from poor wear resistance, limiting its application in demanding mechanical components. In this study, PTFE-based composites reinforced with polyimide (PI) pulp and graphitized carbon nanotubes (GCNTs) were prepared via a cold-press sintering process. The tribological properties were evaluated under different loads (2 N and 10 N) and frequencies (1 Hz and 4 Hz) using a ball-on-disk tribometer. The results show that the composite with 5 wt% PI pulp and 1 wt% GCNT (designated as #3) exhibits the best overall performance. At 2 N and 1 Hz, its coefficient of friction (COF) reaches 0.025, which is 69.3% lower than that of pure PTFE. Meanwhile, the wear rate is reduced by up to 75% under 10 N and 4 Hz. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analyses indicate that the improved tribological performance is mainly attributed to the formation of a continuous and uniform transfer film on the counterface. PI pulp constructs a load-bearing fibrous network that enhances mechanical strength, while GCNTs promote the adhesion and stability of the transfer film, effectively changing the sliding contact from composite–steel to film–steel and reducing both friction and wear. This work offers a practical route for developing PTFE-based self-lubricating composites with balanced mechanical and tribological properties.

Article.Title: Higher plasma oleic acid is associated with slower progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer’s disease in men and women
Article.Authors: Dakterzada F.; Jové M.; Cantero J.; Mota-Martorell N.; Pamplona R.; Piñol-Ripoll G.
Article.Abstract: The contribution of sex differences in lipid metabolism to the pathophysiology of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains under Investigation. This study aimed to investigate sex-stratified associations of fatty acid (FA) profiles in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma across the AD continuum, and their associations with AD pathology and progression. FA profiles were analyzed in 198 CSF and 286 plasma samples from AD, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and control subjects using GC-FID. The MCI subjects were followed up for 58 (± 12.5) months. Analysis of FA profiles of control subjects revealed minor sex differences in both CSF and plasma biofluids. In men, a higher CSF anti-inflammatory index was associated with lower odds of AD than MCI (OR = 0.025), whereas higher CSF α-linolenic acid (C18:3n-3) levels were associated with higher odds of AD (OR = 2.826). In women, higher CSF levels of palmitoleic acid (C16:1n-7) were associated with lower odds of amyloid-β (Aβ) positivity (OR = 0.500). Higher plasma oleic acid (C18:1n-9) levels were associated with lower odds of MCI-to-AD progression in men (OR = 0.666) and a longer time to progression in women (HR = 0.404). Our results suggest that higher plasma oleic acid levels were associated with slower disease progression in both men and women, whereas higher CSF anti-inflammatory index and α-linolenic acid were associated with AD diagnosis in men. These findings may reflect differences in lipid metabolism associated with AD across men and women, although reverse causation and residual confounding cannot be excluded.

Article.Title: Nature-inspired antenna design using hybrid ANN and Bayesian optimization techniques for biomedical applications
Article.Authors: Sharma M.; Jhajharia T.; Rawat S.; Saraswat K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper is presenting a systematic approach for designing of antenna resonating at 3.18 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 3.10–3.285 GHz which lies at the lower edge of the UWB spectrum used in IEEE 802.15.6-based Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) research. The proposed compact antenna becomes more suitable for WBAN-assisted healthcare monitoring and microwave biomedical sensing applications. The antenna designing is covered in two sections. First one deals with the non-linear regression analysis with correlation analysis to achieve final design for patch. The surrogate modelling for reflection coefficient parameter for complete 50 samples of the patch design is presented and compared with other techniques. The non-linear regression based surrogate modelling along with correlation analysis by Pearson and Spearman techniques helps in making prediction of the patch design structure by selecting most featured and significant design parameters. The second section caters the process of ‘Artificial Neural Network (ANN)’ modelling with optimization techniques to achieve optimized design of ‘Defected Ground Structure (DGS)’ structure. The optimization is performed by ‘Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II)’, Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO)’, ‘Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO)’, and ‘Bayesian Optimization using Gaussian Process Regression (BO + GPR)’ techniques. The optimized antenna having size of $$0.2968 {\lambda}_{0} \text{m}\text{m} \times 0.318 {\lambda}_{0} \text{m}\text{m}$$ at resonant frequency of 3.18 GHz, is fabricated on FR-4 substrate. The excellent agreement is observed between simulated results and practical results which confirms the robustness of the proposed systematic approach for the antenna designing and making it suitable for biomedical application.

Article.Title: Exploring multidimensional perceptions of cervical cancer severity and self-efficacy in prevention through the perspectives of patients and healthcare workers
Article.Authors: Harun S.; Hassan N.; Azlan A.; Manoharan A.; Ibrahim I.; Mustapha F.; Jasman N.; Mohamad E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cervical cancer remains a preventable disease, yet screening uptake in Malaysia continues to fall below national targets, particularly among women from lower socioeconomic groups. While previous studies have highlighted knowledge gaps and structural barriers, limited attention has been given to how women in vulnerable groups interpret the severity of cervical cancer and how these perceptions interact with self-efficacy to shape screening intention and behaviour. This qualitative study explored how lower socioeconomic status women perceived the severity of cervical cancer and assessed their ability to undergo Pap smear screening and how these perceptions influenced screening intention and behaviour. The study also examined healthcare workers’ observations of patient-related constraints and motivational factors affecting preventive behaviour. Four focus group discussions were conducted at two public health clinics in Selangor, Malaysia, with 11 women who had never been screened or were non-adherent to the Ministry of Health Malaysia’s recommendations and 11 healthcare workers involved in screening services. Data were analysed using abductive thematic analysis approach. Findings showed that perceived severity extended beyond biomedical consequences to include fear of losing the motherhood role and concern for children, fear of treatment side effects, fear of being a burden to family members, marital strain and impact on intimacy, family cancer experiences that reinforced fatalistic views of disease severity, fear of cancer progression and death as well as emotional and psychological distress. Self-efficacy was undermined by time constraints due to work commitments and daily responsibilities, fear and discomfort with the screening procedure, absence of social support and encouragement, feeling unready for screening and perceiving it as unnecessary, as well as negative experiences with healthcare workers. These findings suggest that future intervention research could explore approaches such as improved health communication, flexible service delivery models and HPV self-sampling to address barriers identified by women from lower socioeconomic backgrounds. The acceptability, feasibility and effectiveness of these approaches should be evaluated in subsequent intervention and implementation studies.

Article.Title: Evaluation of acute FGF2 and PRDX3 for long COVID prediction across cohorts and proteomic platforms
Article.Authors: Duan C.; Yang L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blood proteins measured during acute COVID-19 may help predict Long COVID, but models may fail when moved between cohorts and proteomic platforms. We fitted a reference model using age and sex (C0) in Su/INCOV and a protein model that also included FGF2 and PRDX3 (C2). The pair was fixed before outcome access because both proteins had one-to-one assay mappings. Protein values were standardized within each cohort, and Su coefficients were applied to Zurich without outcome-based refitting. Lower Brier scores indicate better prediction. Su contained 204 participants with complete predictors, but only 125 had linked follow-up. The strict analysis included 122 participants (75 events). Its optimism-corrected C2-minus-C0 Brier difference was + 0.00342 (95% interval, − 0.00608 to + 0.02834). Zurich included 113 participants (40 events). The transferred model difference was + 0.01093 (− 0.01721 to + 0.03882), and strict-model transfer gave + 0.00902 (− 0.01809 to + 0.03696). Both models overpredicted Zurich risk. Reviewer-requested intercept updating also yielded an inconclusive difference. Thus, FGF2 and PRDX3 did not reliably improve prediction beyond age and sex. Because protein standardization depends on a target cohort, this pipeline is not ready to predict risk for a patient.

Article.Title: AVMD-ST: attention-variational mode decomposition based spectrogram transformer for differential diagnosis of asthma and COPD
Article.Authors: Sahu P.; Kumar S.; Behera A.; Verma V.; Dubey R.
Article.Abstract: Lung auscultation analysis is a fundamental and mostly used clinical method for diagnosing pulmonary disorders; however, distinguishing between chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and Asthma remains difficult because of the overlap in physiological and structural characteristics of respiratory systems. This study introduces AVMD-ST, an IMF-guided spectrogram Transformer framework that employs FIR-conditioned VMD to preserve complementary spectral representations of non-stationary respiratory sounds, for the early detection and differential classification of lung conditions. The investigation utilizes lung sound recordings obtained from 200 participants (100 healthy, 50 with asthma, and 50 with COPD) collected via a custom Android application at AIIMS Raipur and two publically available datasets ICBHI challenge and KAUH data. Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filtering is employed for noise reduction, while Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) is utilized to derive intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) that isolate clinically significant components such as wheezes and crackles. Mel-spectrograms generated from these IMFs are provided as input to the AST model, which leverages self-attention mechanisms to detect subtle acoustic variations and capture long-range temporal dependencies. The model is trained and evaluated on a pooled dataset combining AIIMS Raipur recordings with the publicly available ICBHI 2017 and KAUH datasets, using a subject-wise train/test split to prevent recording-level leakage. Achieving 95.75% classification accuracy, the proposed framework demonstrates strong potential as a non-invasive, scalable solution for early respiratory disease screening.

Article.Title: The novel HUGS colon model enables high-throughput parallel cultivation of metabolically active human gut microbiomes in vitro
Article.Authors: Beck F.; Gottumukkala L.; Pedersen N.; Nielsen D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In vitro models simulating the human gut are useful tools for understanding the complexity of the gastrointestinal microbiome and its interactions with food components and other environmental factors. However, existing colon models are either relatively simple, leaving important parameters uncontrolled (such as colonic pH), or suffer from low throughput. Here, we introduce the HUGS (High-throughput Universal Gut Simulator) protocol for simulating colonic passage in vitro , offering a high-throughput approach for studying gut microbiome dynamics. By replicating ascending colon conditions, including controlled pH, anaerobicity, and temperature, we aimed to simulate the gut environment while maintaining experimental scalability. The microbiome modulatory effects of fermented rapeseed meal, soybean meal, seaweed, and different xylans, both individually and in various combinations, were evaluated using the HUGS protocol. The resulting in vitro colonic microbiome composition was determined by 16 S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, while short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production was quantified by ion-exchange chromatography to assess microbial metabolic activity. During a single 24-hour run, HUGS enables 32 individual fermentations to be performed simultaneously, each with independent pH control under anaerobic conditions. The model supported the growth of key anaerobic gut microorganisms, including Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Akkermansia muciniphila , while preserving the dominant phylum-level characteristics of the original fecal microbiomes. Although alpha diversity decreased following fermentation, as commonly observed in short-term in vitro colon models, obligate anaerobic taxa remained abundant throughout the experiments. Overall substrate treatments did not produce distinct clustering patterns. However, differential abundance analysis identified substrate-dependent shifts in specific taxa, including increased relative abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila and Leuconostoc citreum , together with reduced abundance of Cutibacterium acnes and Clostridium perfringens in fermentations containing fermented plant materials. SCFA production varied between substrate formulations, including a significant reduction in total SCFA concentration (p-adj. = 0.016) following xylan supplementation of the fermented soybean meal and seaweed formulation. These findings demonstrate that the HUGS in vitro colon model combines physiologically relevant environmental control with substantially increased throughput compared to existing colon simulation platforms. By supporting growth of key anaerobic gut microorganisms while maintaining sensitivity to biologically meaningful substrate-dependent responses, HUGS is proposed a promising platform for high-throughput screening of dietary fibers, feed additives, and microbiome-modulating compounds in both fundamental and translational future research.

Article.Title: Options for mitigating multi-stressor interactions on managed bees in European agricultural landscapes
Article.Authors: Willcox B.; Senapathi D.; Brown M.; Garratt M.; Breeze T.; Alix A.; Allen M.; De la Rúa P.; Gospodinov K.; Hartfield C.; Ivarsson K.; Maus C.; McDowell D.; Michez D.; Mielgo P.; Nazzi F.; Padurean C.; Paxton R.; Pettis J.; Pistorius J.; Stout J.; Strobl T.; Strobl V.; Van Oystaeyen A.; Underwood E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Managed bees provide valuable pollination services to a wide range of European crops yet they face multiple, interacting stressors including pesticides, pathogens and poor nutrition. Despite incomplete evidence, there is an urgent need to identify effective options to mitigate these stressors. Using a modified Delphi process, 21 experts ranked 29 response options across four case studies. They assessed (a) the response options ability to effectively mitigate pesticide exposure in combination with either poor nutrition or parasite load for either Apis mellifera , Bombus terrestris or Osmia bicornis and (b) the overall feasibility of implementing the response option. The scoring identified perceived effective mitigation responses, that could be prioritised to benefit multiple pollinator species facing different interacting stressors. They included flower patch creation, rewarding farmers for pollinator friendly practices, reducing spray application frequency and reducing spray drift. We also highlight ‘feasibility priorities’, where effective mitigation responses are only feasible to implement with additional targeted support. Maximising the value of currently available evidence, in combination with expert knowledge, we demonstrate a structured decision-support approach for prioritising perceived effective responses. This approach can provide evidence to help support pollinator policy and management, by bridging the current knowledge gap we have around the impacts of interacting stressors on pollinators and how to best mitigate these.

Article.Title: Generation and characterization of phenylketonuria mouse models carrying East Asian–relevant patient-derived PAH mutations
Article.Authors: Yaku Y.; Imafuku J.; Kurosaki A.; Onuma H.; Sato Y.; Miura H.; Ohtsuka M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inherited metabolic disorder caused by mutations in the Pah gene, resulting in impaired phenylalanine hydroxylase activity and elevated blood phenylalanine levels. Although dietary management and enzyme replacement can reduce disease burden, they require lifelong treatment and do not correct the underlying genetic defect. Here, we generated two PKU mouse strains carrying patient-derived PAH mutations, p.R111X and p.R413P, which are relatively frequent in East Asian populations and particularly relevant to Japanese PKU patients. Homozygous mice for each mutation exhibited marked hyperphenylalaninemia and coat hypopigmentation, recapitulating key features of classical PKU. The Pah R111X strain showed a more severe biochemical and pigmentation phenotype than the Pah R413P strain, suggesting mutation-dependent differences in allele severity, likely reflecting the null nature of p.R111X and possible residual function of p.R413P. We further established compound heterozygous Pah R111X/R413P mice and performed a preliminary evaluation of genome editing-based correction using allelic exchange or interhomolog recombination. RT-PCR analysis of liver tissue detected partial restoration of wild-type Pah transcripts, supporting the utility of these patient-mutation-based PKU mice as a platform for evaluating endogenous gene correction strategies.

Article.Title: Association between circadian syndrome and biological age acceleration among Chinese middle-aged and older adults: evidence from CHARLS
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Zhu L.; Wang H.; Ma J.; Fang Y.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Circadian syndrome (CircS), characterized by circadian rhythm disruption and metabolic abnormalities, has been associated with various adverse health outcomes. However, its association with biological age acceleration remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between CircS and biological age acceleration and the potential mediating role of estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). A total of 8,703 participants were included in the cross-sectional analysis and 3,075 participants in the longitudinal analysis. CircS was defined as the presence of at least four of seven predefined components. Biological aging was assessed using Klemera-Doubal method biological age (KDM-BA), and biological age acceleration was calculated as biological age minus chronological age. Multivariable linear regression and Cox proportional hazards models were applied to evaluate the associations of CircS with biological age acceleration in cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses, respectively. Restricted cubic spline (RCS), exploratory mediation analysis, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were additionally performed. CircS was significantly associated with biological age acceleration in both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses. In the fully adjusted cross-sectional model, CircS was associated with a 1.61-year increase in biological age acceleration (β = 1.61, 95% CI: 1.37–1.85). In the longitudinal analysis, CircS was associated with a 55% higher risk of incident biological age acceleration (HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.36–1.77). Increasing numbers of CircS components were associated with progressively higher levels and risks of biological age acceleration (all P for trend < 0.001). Exploratory mediation analysis showed that baseline eGDR partially mediated the association between CircS and incident biological age acceleration during follow-up, with an estimated mediated proportion of 47.8%. CircS was significantly associated with biological age acceleration among Chinese middle-aged and older adults in both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses. Exploratory mediation analysis suggested that eGDR may partially account for this association. These findings suggest CircS may represent an important risk factor for biological aging and underscore the potential importance of maintaining circadian rhythm and metabolic health in slowing biological aging.

Article.Title: A randomized trial of high versus low serum bicarbonate targets and glomerular filtration rate decline in stage 3–4 chronic kidney disease
Article.Authors: Gaggl M.; Aigner C.; Repitz A.; Riesenhuber S.; Sliber C.; Madern M.; Gleiss A.; Fraunschiel M.; Schmidt A.; Sunder-Plassmann G.
Article.Abstract: Treatment of metabolic acidosis with alkaline is established in clinical care of chronic kidney disease (CKD), although clinical studies revealed conflicting results whether it slows CKD. The aim of the study was to determine whether treatment strategies targeting serum bicarbonate concentrations of approximately 20 ± 1 or 24 ± 1 mmol/L differed with respect to eGFR decline over 104 weeks follow-up. The SoBic study was an open-label randomized trial in CKD stage 3 to 4 patients and serum bicarbonate ≤ 21 mmol/L. Sodium bicarbonate was applied according to serum bicarbonate targets. We randomized 58 subjects and 49 completed follow-up, 2 died, and 4 started dialysis. The median sodium bicarbonate dose in the intervention group was 6.7 (IQR: 4.2 to 8.4) g/day. About 70% in each group reached the target, resulting in a mean difference in serum bicarbonate of 3.57 (95%CI: 2.29 to 4.85) at week 47 and 3.64 (95%CI: 2.21 to 5.07 mmol/L at week 104 across groups. There was an estimated mean decrease in eGFR of 5.8 (95%CI: − 8.77 to − 2.84) and a non-significant difference of eGFR change of − 0.98 (− 3.08 to 1.12, p = 0.648) ml/min per 1.73 m². In conclusion, targeting higher serum bicarbonate concentrations was not associate with a clinically meaningful benefit in subjects with advanced CKD and overt metabolic acidosis.

Article.Title: Chlorhexidine MIC distribution, efflux pump gene profiles, and genotypic characteristics among clinical methicillin-resistant and methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus isolates
Article.Authors: Golban M.; Charostad J.; Kazemian H.; Madadizadeh F.; Heidari H.
Article.Abstract: Reduced antiseptic susceptibility mediated by multidrug efflux pumps in drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus poses an additional infection control concern. This study investigated chlorhexidine susceptibility status and efflux pump gene distribution across different accessory gene regulator (agr) types in methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA) isolates from two major hospitals in Iran. The minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of chlorhexidine against the isolates were determined. Methicillin resistance determinants, efflux pump genes, and agr types were also analysed. Furthermore, the relative expression of the mepA efflux pump gene was measured after exposure to a sub-inhibitory concentration of chlorhexidine using real-time PCR. Methicillin resistance was detected in 27.3% of isolates, and chlorhexidine MICs ranged from 0.25 to 2 mg/L. Elevated chlorhexidine MIC (≥ 1 mg/L) was observed in 33.9% of isolates and was significantly more frequent among MRSA isolates. The prevalence of sepA , mdeA , mepA , lmrS , and norA exceeded 85%, whereas qacA/B and smr were detected in 5% and 0.8% of isolates, respectively. Isolates carrying lmrS showed significantly elevated chlorhexidine MICs, and agr type III was also associated with elevated MICs. mepA expression increased significantly after exposure to a sub-MIC of chlorhexidine, with 2.158-fold and 2.729-fold increases at 30 and 60 min, respectively ( p < 0.001), and was also elevated in agr II-positive and agr III-positive isolates. Our findings reveal region-specific MRSA prevalence and reduced chlorhexidine susceptibility, suggest an association between chlorhexidine exposure and mepA overexpression, and support integrating molecular typing into surveillance of emerging resistant strains.

Article.Title: Unpacking the institutional and psychological pathways of community empowerment in cultural heritage governance
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Li W.; Cui P.; Ai Q.; Fan Q.; Yuan J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Community empowerment is widely recognized as an effective strategy for improving resident satisfaction in the governance of cultural heritage sites. However, existing studies focus primarily on institutional design and do not systematically explore the underlying psychological conversion mechanisms. To fill this gap, this paper selects Baisha Ancient Town and Xijiang Qianhu Miao Village as cases, uses Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to analyze data from 775 completed questionnaires, and explores the mediating effect of empowerment on residents’ satisfaction through cultural pride and community resilience. The results show that community empowerment not only directly promotes satisfaction, but also has significant indirect effects through emotional and institutional pathways, and the two show differences in different communities. Through unpacking the “institutional empowerment-psychological response-satisfaction feedback” process, this study contributes to theory by clarifying the synergistic roles of emotional and structural mechanisms and their contextual variations. Practically, it provides a governance framework that helps policymakers calibrate empowerment strategies to community development stages, thereby promoting both cultural continuity and socio-economic sustainability.

Article.Title: Free vibration analysis of multidirectional FG porous annular sector plates based on three-dimensional elasticity using GDQ with RSM-derived predictive frequency formulas
Article.Authors: Adineh M.; Pourhoseini S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Annular sector plates are widely used in advanced engineering systems, where their dynamic characteristics play a crucial role in structural performance. Tailoring material distributions and introducing controlled porosity provide an effective approach for tuning their vibration response, particularly the natural frequencies, without modifying the structural geometry or base constituents. In this study, for the first time, the free vibration behavior of multidirectional functionally graded (FG) porous annular sector plates with material properties varying along the thickness, radial, and circumferential directions is investigated based on three-dimensional elasticity theory, and the governing equations are solved using the generalized differential quadrature (GDQ) method to obtain highly accurate results even for relatively thick plates. The accuracy of the proposed formulation is verified through comparisons with available results in the literature and finite element simulations performed in Abaqus. Furthermore, response surface methodology (RSM) is employed to develop predictive relations describing the influence of key parameters on the natural frequencies. The proposed framework combines the flexibility of GDQ-based numerical analysis with the simplicity of RSM-derived predictive formulas, while the use of three-dimensional elasticity ensures high accuracy of the obtained vibration responses. The results are presented and discussed through graphical representations, providing insight into the natural frequency characteristics of these structural elements.

Article.Title: Young children’s knowledge of ChatGPT and its relationship with their achievement in english as a second language
Article.Authors: Al-Barakat A.; AlAli R.; Aboras A.; Alribdi N.; Abdullatif A.; Zaher A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated young children’s (aged 7–8 years) knowledge of ChatGPT and its relationship with their achievement in English as a Second Language. The sample consisted of 255 third-grade young children from the Eastern Region of Saudi Arabia. A mixed-methods approach was employed, comprising a ChatGPT knowledge questionnaire assessing five dimensions: general knowledge, applied knowledge, awareness of risks and limitations, ethical knowledge, and self-assessment in using ChatGPT. Semi-structured interviews were conducted to gain deeper insights into young children’s understanding and experiences with the tool. The findings revealed that young children’s overall knowledge of ChatGPT was moderate, with relative strengths in general and practical knowledge. In contrast, awareness of risks and limitations, ethical knowledge, and self-assessment/confidence were relatively low. Regarding English achievement, young children demonstrated an acceptable level, with overall performance ranging between “Good” and “Very Good.” Furthermore, the results indicated a statistically significant positive relationship between young children’s ChatGPT knowledge and their English achievement. General and practical knowledge, together with self-assessment and confidence, showed the strongest effects, whereas knowledge of risks, limitations, and ethics had a weaker impact on academic performance. These findings highlight that enhancing both theoretical and practical knowledge of ChatGPT can directly support improved academic outcomes. Overall, increasing young children’s knowledge of ChatGPT can facilitate their language achievement. Integrating digital literacy education with the development of self-assessment and ethical awareness is essential for the responsible and effective use of AI tools in educational settings.

Article.Title: Technical validation and feasibility of video particle tracking for low-volume measurement of biliary micro-viscosity after liver transplantation
Article.Authors: Lenz L.; Friedrich P.; Stock P.; Nickel S.; Mandl L.; Schnurpel A.; Haak F.; Scheuermann U.; Sternkopf R.; Ricken T.; Alfons Käs J.; Tautenhahn H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable quantification of the biophysical properties of human bile requires analytically validated methods and standardized pre-analytical conditions. We hypothesized that biliary micro-viscosity can be quantified in human bile after liver transplantation (LTx) with predefined analytical performance (accuracy $$\le 15\%$$ deviation from reference, reproducibility CV $$<10\%$$ ). In this method-development and technical-validation study, we established a method to quantify micro-viscosity in human bile after LTx. Validation using sucrose standards demonstrated high accuracy ( $$\le 15\%$$ deviation from reference), strong linear correlation ( $$\textrm{R}^2 = 0.996$$ ), and good reproducibility (CV $$<10\%$$ ). The method was applied to 21 bile samples from nine patients collected longitudinally after LTx. Mean micro-viscosity was $$1.58 \pm 0.54~\text {mPa s}$$ (postoperative day 1), $$1.94 \pm 0.63~\text {mPa s}$$ (day 7), and $$1.44 \pm 0.16~\text {mPa s}$$ (day 14). Pre-analytical freezing and cooling introduced measurement variability, supporting analysis shortly after collection. These findings demonstrate the analytical performance and practical feasibility of video particle-tracking-based biliary micro-viscosity measurements after LTx. Larger studies combining standardized fresh-sample workflows, biochemical bile characterization, and longitudinal clinical outcome data are required to determine the biological relevance of biliary micro-viscosity and its potential value for future graft modeling.

Article.Title: Entanglement-assisted coherent control for deterministic quantum gate teleportation
Article.Authors: Ávila S.; Enríquez M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quantum gate teleportation enables spatially separated parties to implement nonlocal quantum operations using preshared entanglement, local operations, measurement, and classical communication. Here, we present a two-branch entanglement-assisted coherent-control architecture for the deterministic remote implementation of nonlocal two-qubit gates. In this architecture, the two parties coherently select between two pairs of local unitary operations acting on their respective input qubits, a structure that can be naturally encoded through spatial-path superposition. The protocol is formulated at the operator level, allowing deterministic operation to be established independently of the input-state parametrization and making its scope explicit. For two-qubit unitary targets, we show that the deterministic branch conditions restrict the nonlocal domain of the balanced two-branch ansatz: apart from local product operations, any implementable nonlocal unitary must be locally unitarily equivalent to the CNOT/CZ class. We construct explicit CNOT and controlled- Z realizations as two representatives of this unique nonlocal equivalence class. We also introduce a photonic path-encoding and destructive branch-readout scheme in which spatial path encodes the coherent-control degree of freedom and polarization carries the computational qubits, illustrating how the proposed architecture can be physically encoded.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: controlled-Z gate; CNOT gate; photonic qubits; local unitary equivalence

Article.Title: Effects of myofascial release on clinical outcomes and muscle viscoelastic properties in patients with breast cancer: A randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Feyzioğlu Ö.; Dinçer S.; Öztürk Ö.; Saldıran T.
Article.Abstract: Evidence regarding the effects of myofascial release (MFR) on clinical outcomes in breast cancer patients is inconsistent, and its effects on muscle viscoelastic properties have not been well established. To evaluate the effects of MFR on the viscoelastic properties of the pectoralis major (PM) and sternocleidomastoid (SCM) muscles and on clinical outcomes in breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy.Thirty-one breast cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy after surgery were randomly assigned to a control group (CG) or an MFR group (MFRG). Both groups performed a home-based exercise program for six weeks, while the MFRG additionally received MFR therapy twice weekly. Shoulder mobility was assessed using a digital goniometer, muscle strength using a handheld dynamometer, pain intensity using the Visual Analog Scale, quality of life using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy–Breast, and kinesiophobia using the Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia. The viscoelastic properties of PM and SCM muscles were evaluated using the MyotonPRO device. PM muscle tone increased in the MFRG; however, no significant group × time interactions were found for PM or SCM viscoelastic properties (p>0.05). The MFRG showed significant improvements in most clinical outcomes except quality of life. Significant group × time interactions favored the MFRG for shoulder mobility, pain, and shoulder flexion and abduction strength (p<0.05). The addition of therapist-delivered MFR to home exercise was associated with greater improvements in shoulder mobility, muscle strength, and pain, but did not significantly affect PM or SCM viscoelastic properties. The specific contribution of MFR remains uncertain due to additional therapist contact in the MFRG. Article.Title: Immuno-oxidative biomarkers and histopathological evaluation of heart and spleen tissues in doxorubicin- and cisplatin-induced toxicity in male albino rats
Article.Authors: Badr N.; Abdelmeguid N.; Kotet S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Doxorubicin (DOX) and cisplatin (CIS) are extensively used chemotherapeutic drugs, but their clinical use is hindered by systemic and organ-specific toxicities. This study comparatively evaluated the oxidative, inflammatory, hematological, immune, and tissue responses induced by DOX and CIS administered at the same dose. Adult male albino rats were randomly allocated into control and chemotherapy-treated groups. The chemotherapy groups received a single intraperitoneal injection of DOX or CIS (7.5 mg/kg). Serum oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and glutathione (GSH)), inflammatory markers (tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6, and myeloperoxidase), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), troponin T, immunoglobulins (IgG and IgM), and hematological parameters were assessed. Cardiac and splenic tissues were evaluated for MDA, SOD, Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), and caspase-3, together with histopathological examination and scoring. Both DOX and CIS caused anemia, leukocyte imbalance, thrombocytosis, and increased IgG and IgM, with more severe effects in DOX. Both agents also induced systemic oxidative stress, inflammation, and increased LDH and troponin T levels. In cardiac and splenic tissues, these treatments were associated with increased MDA, NF-κB, and caspase-3 levels, with reduced SOD activity. Histopathological examination and scoring revealed myocardial degeneration, vacuolation, necrosis, and inflammatory infiltration, as well as splenic white pulp depletion and disruption of the red–white pulp boundaries, with more pronounced damage observed in the DOX group. DOX and CIS induced systemic and tissue oxidative, inflammatory, hematological, and apoptotic disturbances, supporting an oxidative stress–NF-κB–apoptosis pathway in cardiac and splenic toxicity.

Article.Title: Assessing the resilience of water supply infrastructure to climate variability: a current status assessment in rural India
Article.Authors: Srivastava S.; Nair A.; Sultana N.; Jabbi A.; Raj M.; Sabarinath S.; Ramesh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rural Indian communities, characterised by the decentralised and informal nature of water governance, are extremely vulnerable to climate shocks that impair local water supply infrastructures (WSIs). This study assesses WSI resilience in the face of current climate variability and examines the multidimensional elements that influence resilience results. The research uses a participatory, bottom-up, mixed-method approach to apply the “How Tough is WASH (HTIW)” framework across four rural communities—Srayikkadu (Kerala), Ahirpurwa (Bihar), Kali Nagar (West Bengal), and Kanti (Haryana), which represent distinct geological, climatic, and socio-cultural settings. According to the findings, Kanti village in Haryana has the most resilient WSIs, which appear to be associated with significant private sector and local government participation, whereas Ahirpurwa and Kali Nagar are the least resilient due to low institutional, social, and physical support. Despite contextual variations, disrupted community governance and supply chains were recognised as the prevalent constraints across all communities, indicating limited public engagement and insufficient restoration mechanisms. These results suggest that social and institutional factors are important for understanding WSI resilience in these study communities, and that resilience is not determined by the performance of physical infrastructure alone. The study offers a new, bottom-up assessment of WSI resilience and outcomes, and emphasises the need for policy measures that develop institutional capacity, improve participatory governance, and understand the existing level of WSI climate resilience capability in order to prepare for long-term rural water security.

Article.Title: Phase–velocity disk model for predicting output-gap velocity distribution for the design of high-efficiency Klystrons
Article.Authors: Mandal S.; Koley C.; Bandyopadhyay A.; Pal D.; Duari C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Klystrons require continued efficiency improvement to satisfy the growing demands of energy efficiency in modern high power microwave and accelerator systems. At the output gap, the phase–velocity distribution of the bunched electron beam governs beam-to-RF energy extraction and thus strongly affects electronic efficiency. In this work, a disk-based prediction model is developed to evaluate the phase and velocity distribution of beam disks at the output gap and to estimate the corresponding energy extraction behaviour. A novel diagnostic quantity, cavity energy transfer ratio, is developed as a figure of merit of the work for cavity wise energy transfer diagnosis and klystron efficiency optimization. The model incorporates RF gap interaction, drift-space phase slippage, velocity modulation, and space-charge-influenced bunch evolution in a self-consistent framework. Two drift-length cases are investigated to examine the role of space-charge-dominated bunching in efficiency enhancement using this model. The longer-drift configuration produces stronger bunch evolution before the output cavity, and yields improved electronic efficiency. The predicted disk energy-extraction efficiency agrees closely with KLyC and CST results, validating the proposed approach for rapid efficiency evaluation in klystron design

Article.Title: Deep reinforcement learning-driven cross-layer optimization of IRS-assisted NOMA with blockchain for secure 6G oriented networks spectrum management
Article.Authors: Pradeep S.; Ramkumar M.; Karthikeyan A.; Ravi S.
Article.Abstract: The rapid development of connected devices and data intensive applications is demanding the need for smart spectrum management mechanisms in emerging 6G Networks. Traditional centralized spectrum allocation schemes often find it challenging to cope with excessive wireless environments and larger-scale distributed networks and results in underutilizing the spectrum and adding more communication latency. To get over these difficulties, a cross-layer architecture with intelligent reflecting surface assisted communication, decentralized spectrum coordination and collaborative learning is proposed in this paper. The framework makes use of Federated Learning, in order to teach spectrum prediction models jointly at the edge devices, thus allowing data privacy preservation while making better decisions regarding resource allocation. In addition, adaptive signal propagation is achieved by configurable reflecting elements for improving communication reliability under different channel conditions. The proposed system is tested using the MATLAB simulations of a dense wireless network with multiple edge devices. The spectrum utilization, communication latency, network throughput, secrecy rate, and federated-learning convergence are used to evaluate the performance. The simulation results show that the proposed framework can achieve a spectrum utilization rate of around 82%, and the communication latency is around 12ms, with the federated-learning accuracy of about approximately 92% in the case of a dense network. These results show that the proposed design for a cross layer offers an efficient and scalable solution for decentralized spectrum management in the next generation of wireless systems.

Article.Title: Radiomics and machine learning analysis to differentiate low grade glioma and encephalitis on non-contrast MRI
Article.Authors: Picchi E.; Di Donna C.; Cavallo A.; Minosse S.; Castelli A.; Bonomi C.; Izzi F.; Amatruda A.; Da Ros V.; Garaci F.; Di Giuliano F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate differentiation between low-grade gliomas and encephalitis remains challenging due to overlapping MRI features. This study investigated whether MRI-based radiomics derived from routine non-contrast MRI could improve the differentiation of these entities in diagnostically challenging cases presenting in emergency settings. This retrospective single-center study included 41 patients with ambiguous MRI findings who underwent 3T MRI within 48 h of symptom onset. Radiomic features extracted from T2-FLAIR, DWI, and T1-TSE images, together with laboratory data available at presentation, were analyzed. Random Forest classifiers were developed using selected radiomic features, and model performance was evaluated using nested cross-validation, independent validation, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and DeLong’s test. The cohort included 23 patients with histologically proven low-grade gliomas and 18 with confirmed encephalitis and was divided into training ( n = 31) and validation ( n = 10) sets. FLAIR-based models showed the best discriminatory performance, achieving an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.54–1.00) for both the radiomics-only and radiomics-clinical models outperforming T1-weighted (AUC 0.52 for radiomics-only and 0.60 for radiomics-clinical model) and DWI models (AUC 0.72 for both radiomics-only and radiomics-clinical approaches). The combined-sequence radiomics-clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.41–1.00), with 100% sensitivity, 80% specificity, and 90% accuracy. Comparison of the ROC curves using DeLong’s test did not demonstrate statistically significant differences between the radiomics-only and radiomics-clinical models for any MRI sequence. This proof-of-concept study suggests that radiomic features extracted from routine non-contrast MRI may help differentiate low-grade gliomas from encephalitis in diagnostically challenging cases; however, these preliminary findings warrant validation in larger multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Orbital Hall conductivity in a d-wave altermagnet: a multi-orbital tight-binding study
Article.Authors: Arucu M.
Article.Abstract: Altermagnets combine zero net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting, and their hallmark transport phenomenon—the spin-splitter effect—requires no spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Here we ask how the orbital degree of freedom fits into this picture. Using a minimal multi-orbital ( \(t_{2g}\) ) tight-binding model of a d -wave altermagnet with exact intra- \(t_{2g}\) angular-momentum operators and the Kubo formalism, we compute on equal footing the charge, spin, and orbital Hall conductivities together with the dissipative Fermi-surface (“splitter”) spin and orbital responses. We uncover a duality between the two transport channels: in the Hall channel the orbital Hall conductivity is large and essentially independent of SOC while the spin Hall conductivity is purely SOC-induced; in the splitter channel the hierarchy is exactly reversed—the spin-splitter response is large and SOC-free, whereas its orbital counterpart vanishes identically in the SOC-free limit—a consequence of orbital-current quenching whenever the Hamiltonian admits a real matrix representation at every crystal momentum, verified explicitly for the microscopic models studied here, with the \([C_2\Vert C_{4z}]\) symmetry fixing the tensor structure once SOC is present—and is activated only by SOC. We verify the symmetry protection at machine precision, map the responses across the exchange–SOC parameter plane, and validate the model against spin-polarized density-functional calculations of RuO \(_2\) . Our results position d -wave altermagnets as tunable sources of orbital currents.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: d-wave altermagnet; orbital magnetism

Article.Title: Performance of ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini 3, and copilot 2026 in answering chemistry course questions: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Dorri H.; Gol M.; Naraki K.; Khosravi M.
Article.Abstract: Chemistry, environmental health, and occupational health have historically developed in close collaboration. This study aimed to evaluate the performance of LLMs, in responding to a chemistry course questionnaire used in environmental and occupational health department for educational purposes. This was a cross-sectional study conducted in 2026. The study used a 50-item multiple-choice questionnaire, primarily in Persian with limited English terms and formulas, which was administered to LLMs (ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini 3, and Copilot 2026). Performance was evaluated using confusion matrix analysis. Cochran`s Q test, McNemar`s test for pair-wise comparisons, and Point-biserial correlation were also conducted to further evaluate the study data. The LLMs presented mean sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 0.81, 0.29, and 0.68, respectively. Gemini 3 presented a high level of performance, achieving the highest sensitivity (0.85), specificity (0.56), and accuracy (0.80). ChatGPT-5.5 had the lowest sensitivity (0.76), while Copilot showed the lowest specificity (0.07) and an accuracy of 0.62. No significant correlations were found between performance and questionnaire characteristics; however, all models performed poorly on negatively framed items requiring identification of incorrect options. The study presented some preliminary insights on the performance of LLMs in chemistry-related questions. Further research is warranted.

Article.Title: Hydroxysafflor yellow A alleviates high fat diet induced hyperlipidemia and improves host intestinal environment via hepatic signaling regulation
Article.Authors: Xu C.; Ji K.; Li H.; Zhang J.; Wu M.; Chen C.; Niu R.; Sun Y.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hyperlipidemia is a metabolic disorder characterized by abnormally elevated circulating lipid levels and is closely associated with host metabolic homeostasis. In this study, we integrated network pharmacology, in vivo and in vitro experiments to investigate the lipid-lowering effects and mechanisms of hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA), the major bioactive component of Carthamus tinctorius L. HSYA significantly ameliorated HFD-induced metabolic abnormalities, including body weight gain, dyslipidemia, and hepatic steatosis, reduced serum levels of total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, and lipopolysaccharide, enhanced hepatic superoxide dismutase activity, and suppressed tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1β. 16S rRNA sequencing revealed that HSYA restored gut microbiota homeostasis, increased beneficial bacteria such as Bacteroidota and Verrucomicrobiota, and upregulated intestinal barrier proteins zonula occludens-1 and occludin. Network pharmacology indicated close associations among HSYA, hyperlipidemia, gut microbiota, and metabolites, and identified the PI3K/AKT/HIF-1α pathway as a key mediator, with gut microbiota and intestinal barrier restoration as related mechanisms. In vitro, HSYA exhibited no cytotoxicity and reduced TC, triglycerides (TG), and lipid droplets in palmitic acid-treated HepG2 cells, confirming its metabolic benefits. Thus, HSYA may alleviate HFD-induced dyslipidemia and hepatic steatosis through PI3K/AKT/HIF-1α and gut–liver axis modulation, supporting its clinical potential in metabolic diseases.

Article.Title: Pilot intraindividual secretome profiling of adipose-derived stem cells in multiple symmetric lipomatosis
Article.Authors: Reinhard R.; Felthaus O.; Siegmund A.; Limm K.; Oefner P.; Ruewe M.; Eisenmann S.; Festbaum C.; Prantl L.; Oliinyk D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multiple symmetric lipomatosis (MSL) is a rare adipose tissue disease characterized by progressive, non-encapsulated, symmetrical fat accumulation. Its pathophysiology is still not completely understood. Here, we performed the first intraindividual comparison of secretomes of human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) isolated from affected and unaffected regions of n = 15 patients (proteomic discovery cohort n = 5). Affected MSL-hASCs tend to show accelerated metabolic signals and higher cell densities with preserved adipogenic differentiation capacity. Secretome transfer of affected MSL-hASCs significantly increased metabolic activity of wt-hASCs after 24 h in 4/7 samples (all explorative Benjamini-Hochberg corrected p = 0.040). Bottom-up proteomic analysis identified 811 proteins, of which 220 were classified as secreted. Thirteen proteins exhibited nominally significant dysregulation of expression, including CALR ( p = 0.0061), LAMC1 ( p = 0.0241), S100A7 ( p = 0.0281) and HDGF ( p = 0.0474), but none remained significant after application of the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction to control the False Discovery Rate (FDR) at 0.05. Transcriptional validation by rt-qPCR revealed a trend toward downregulation of hLAMA4 and hCFB (both p = 0.0625). In conclusion, convergent patterns are consistent with extracellular matrix remodeling and PI3K/AKT-ERK-associated proliferative signaling. This model supports a hypothesis of progenitor-level dysregulation rather than a single clonal driver in MSL, which will require further mechanistic validation in larger cohorts.

Article.Title: Mitochondrial and retroviral markers reveal high genetic diversity and regional structure in the Lebanese Awassi sheep
Article.Authors: Hage J.; Boyer F.; Viginier B.; Terzian C.; Pompanon F.; Arnaud F.; Abi-Rizk A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Awassi is a native sheep breed of Lebanon with high historical and economic value. Despite its importance, its genetic background has not been characterized, leaving limited understanding of its origins, diversity, and regional connections. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity and population structure of Awassi sheep from Lebanon and neighboring Syria using two complementary genetic systems that trace distinct evolutionary histories: maternal mitochondrial DNA and insertional polymorphisms of endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retroviruses. Genetic analyses were conducted on two hundred seventy-seven animals. Sequencing of a one thousand thirty-four base pair fragment of the mitochondrial cytochrome b gene identified eighty-six maternal haplotypes that clustered into four haplogroups (A, B, C, and E). Maternal haplotype diversity was high, and most individuals belonged to haplogroups A and B, indicating contributions from both western and eastern maternal lineages. Retroviral insertion profiling showed that the retroviral type carrying only endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus element eighteen was predominant. A Mediterranean retroviral type carrying both endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus eighteen and seven was also present, especially in coastal flocks, suggesting ancient gene flow through maritime trade. Other retroviral combinations were rare. Analysis of endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus six revealed a high frequency of solo long terminal repeat alleles, indicating an ancient recombination event. Approximately half of the animals were heterozygous for this allele and some homozygous. No pre-integration alleles were detected, confirming fixation of endogenous Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus six in domestic sheep. Lebanese Awassi sheep exhibit substantial genetic diversity across both maternal and retroviral systems, reflecting a complex population history shaped by multiple lineages and regional exchanges. This study provides the first comprehensive genetic characterization of this native breed and contributes to broader understanding of sheep domestication in the Middle East, while supporting evidence-based conservation of this valuable genetic resource.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning classification of rural rescue service proximity coverage using OpenStreetMap data
Article.Authors: Tryhuba A.; Koval L.; Rudynets M.; Androshchuk I.; Fomenko V.; Miernik A.; Vasylyshen Y.; Hutsol T.
Article.Abstract: Assessing the spatial proximity of rural settlements to rescue-service locations remains an important task for sustainable community safety planning, particularly in regions characterized by dispersed settlements, limited infrastructure, and incomplete spatial data. This study proposes a data-driven framework for classifying rural rescue-service proximity-based coverage using OpenStreetMap-derived geospatial data and explainable machine learning methods. A spatially structured dataset containing 304 rural settlements was constructed using infrastructural and settlement-related indicators, including schools, medical facilities, places of worship, industrial facilities, buildings, and major-road access. The target variable represented binary proximity-based coverage defined using a 5 km Euclidean buffer around rescue-service locations and was intended solely for comparative territorial screening; it does not represent observed emergency-response time or operational performance. To ensure methodological validity, leakage-prone variables directly related to target construction were excluded from model training. Several classification approaches were comparatively evaluated using stratified cross-validation, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, MLP, and XGBoost models. The obtained results demonstrated that ensemble machine learning methods provided the most stable and interpretable performance for spatial tabular data. The Gradient Boosting model achieved the highest mean F1-score of 0.77, with a balanced accuracy of 0.85, ROC–AUC of 0.95, and PR–AUC of 0.82 under stratified five-fold cross-validation. Model interpretability was additionally assessed using permutation feature importance, SHAP analysis, and multicollinearity diagnostics, which identified model-specific associations between infrastructural characteristics and the proximity-based coverage class. Spatial decision-support maps were developed to identify settlements with lower model-based proximity-coverage probabilities that may warrant further detailed assessment. The proposed framework demonstrates the feasibility of integrating OpenStreetMap data and explainable machine learning into practical decision-support systems for sustainable rural safety management and infrastructure planning under conditions of limited and fragmented spatial information.

Article.Title: The impact of clinically and urodynamically classified urinary incontinence subtypes on female sexual function
Article.Authors: Ünal F.; Küçükyurt A.; Kolcu S.; Demirel E.
Article.Abstract: Urinary incontinence (UI) adversely affects women’s quality of life and sexual health; however, whether female sexual function differs according to UI subtype remains unclear. This cross-sectional study evaluated 93 women with stress (SUI, n = 45), urgency (UUI, n = 24), or mixed urinary incontinence (MUI, n = 24), classified using clinical assessment and multichannel urodynamic evaluation. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI); total FSFI score was the primary outcome. No statistically significant between-group difference was detected in total FSFI score (Kruskal-Wallis H = 3.65, p = 0.161; ε² = 0.018) or individual domains. UUI showed a numerically lower median total FSFI score than SUI and MUI (3.4 vs. 17.7 and 15.1), but pairwise Hodges-Lehmann 95% confidence intervals crossed zero. Sexual activity during the preceding four weeks was not recorded separately; therefore, low FSFI scores may partly reflect sexual inactivity and should not be interpreted as diagnostic estimates of female sexual dysfunction prevalence. These findings do not establish equivalence among UI subtypes. Larger studies incorporating validated UI severity measures and explicit assessment of recent sexual activity are needed.

Article.Title: Machine learning assessment of industrial corrosion and public health risks in data limited aquifers of Northeastern Algeria
Article.Authors: Eid M.; Saeed O.; Szűcs P.; Mikita V.; Tamma A.; Elsayed S.; El-baki M.; Abukhadra M.; Bin-Jumah M.; Allam A.; Kamel M.; Dąbrowska D.; Gad M.
Article.Abstract: Industrializing arid regions face a dual challenge: ensuring water suitability for emerging industries while protecting public health amidst chronic data scarcity. This study confronts this issue in northeastern Algeria by developing and validating an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework to predict industrial water quality and associated health risks from limited groundwater data. Based on 45 samples collected from the Debila and El-Oued regions of the Souf Valley, Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), and Decision Tree (DT) models were trained to predict seven corrosion and scaling potential (CSP) indices, namely the Langelier Saturation Index (LSI), Ryznar Stability Index (RSI), Aggressive Index (AI), Puckorius Scaling Index (PSI), Larson-Skold Index (LS), Chloride-Sulphate Mass Ratio (CSMR), and Revelle Index (RI), alongside the Canadian Council of Ministers of the Environment Water Quality Index (CCME-WQI). Physicochemical analysis revealed pervasive water quality deterioration, with 60% of samples exhibiting corrosive tendencies (LSI < 0) and 85% showing high corrosion risk (RSI > 6.8). All sites were uniformly classified as “Poor” by the CCME-WQI, and Monte Carlo simulations (10,000 iterations) confirmed significant non-carcinogenic health risks from nitrate for children (mean Hazard Index > 1.0). The ANN and RF models demonstrated robust predictive power, achieving R² values above 0.90 for six of the eight predicted indices. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis identified the dominant hydrochemical drivers for each index, providing a transparent and actionable basis for targeted monitoring. This study presents a novel, validated, and transferable ML-based decision support tool that simultaneously integrates industrial process risks with public health assessment, offering a replicable water management paradigm for data-limited, industrializing regions worldwide.

Article.Title: Free and adsorbed gas control P-wave velocity in coal through effective stress and adsorption-induced swelling
Article.Authors: Sun X.; Cui R.; Qi Z.; Wu Z.; Sun J.; Gao H.
Article.Abstract: Understanding how free and adsorbed gas affect seismic-wave velocity in coal is important for evaluating gas-bearing reservoirs, but their individual roles remain difficult to separate. Here, ultrasonic measurements with helium and methane were combined with simulations on three-dimensional coal models reconstructed from X-ray computed tomography to distinguish the effects of free gas, gas adsorption and pore pressure on P-wave velocity. The results show that free gas mainly changes P-wave velocity by reducing effective stress as pore pressure increases, whereas adsorbed methane alters the coal framework through adsorption-induced swelling. Under constant confining pressure, methane adsorption dominates at low pore pressure and increases P-wave velocity. At higher pore pressure, effective-stress reduction becomes dominant and P-wave velocity decreases. The numerical simulations reproduce these experimental trends and show that the observed non-monotonic velocity response arises from competition between adsorption-induced strengthening of the coal framework and pressure-induced weakening associated with lower effective stress. These findings clarify the distinct but coupled roles of free and adsorbed gas in controlling acoustic properties of coal and provide a physical basis for interpreting P-wave measurements in coalbed methane reservoir evaluation and gas monitoring.
