Article.Title: The dual destructive effects of cantharidin on red blood cell structure and function: an analysis from membrane elasticity to the metabolic network
Article.Authors: Su X.; Xu H.; Guo Z.; Zhang G.; Gong H.; Feng X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cantharidin (CTD), a potent anticancer terpenoid, is clinically limited by its hepatotoxicity and nephrotoxicity, while its impact on the hematopoietic system-particularly on red blood cells (RBCs), remains poorly understood. This study aimed to explore CTD-induced structural and functional changes in RBCs. A series of assays were conducted, including assessments of hemolysis rate, morphological changes, programmed cell death, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) activity, as well as untargeted metabolomics (LC–MS) and proteomics (LC–MS/MS) analyses. Results showed that high-dose CTD (0.8 mM) caused obvious RBCs morphological abnormalities, reduced adhesion and increased intracellular ROS, leading to RBC rupture, LDH release, and ultimately triggering programmed cell death. Multi-omics profiling identified 377 differential metabolites (enriched in ABC transporters and purine metabolism) and 45 differential proteins associated with Hippo and PI3K-Akt pathways. Among these, the PI3K-Akt pathway emerged as the core mechanism underlying CTD-induced RBCs injury. Collectively, this study has accumulated data on CTD-induced morphological and functional disruptions in RBCs, providing some insights for the subsequent evaluation of toxic drugs in the hematopoietic system.

Article.Title: Estimating heart rate variability using facial video photoplethysmography: a pilot validation study
Article.Authors: Pstras L.; Okupnik T.; Ponikowska B.; Paleczny B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Video photoplethysmography (vPPG) uses a digital camera to detect pulsations in the blood vessels of the skin, which can be used to estimate various physiological parameters. The aim of this study was to investigate the accuracy and precision of heart rate variability (HRV) indices estimated using a smartphone camera and facial vPPG technology. The study group included 35 healthy volunteers (17 females) with median age 25 years (range 20–42 years). The subjects were in a sitting position, keeping their heads relatively still. A smartphone mounted on a tripod was used to acquire 1-min video recordings of participants’ faces. In parallel, a 1-lead chest electrocardiogram (ECG) was recorded to obtain reference values of two analysed time-domain HRV indices: SDNN and lnRMSSD. For SDNN, the median absolute error was 3.0 ms (7.1% in relative terms), and the root-mean-square error was 4.5 ms (15.7%). For lnRMSSD, the median absolute error was 0.20 (5.6%) and the root-mean-square error was 0.31 (9.9%). Correlations between the vPPG-based and ECG-based HRV values were strong, with the Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.98 for SDNN and 0.88 for lnRMSSD ( P < 0.001 in both cases). In a young, white population, the tested vPPG technology estimated the HRV indices (SDNN and lnRMSSD) with good overall accuracy, with a slight systematic overestimation, especially for low values. The results should be confirmed in a larger study with greater diversity in age and skin tone.

Article.Title: Prevalence of posterior root resorption in open bite patients undergoing clear aligner treatment: a single-arm retrospective CBCT study
Article.Authors: Aljahdali R.; Baeshen H.; Al-Turki G.; Alsulaimani F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to quantify posterior root volume loss and assess its association with posterior intrusion. Linear root length changes were also evaluated and compared with three-dimensional measurements. This retrospective single-arm study included 27 patients with anterior open bites treated with clear aligners. Cone-beam computed tomography scans obtained before and after treatment were analyzed. Volumetric and linear root changes of maxillary posterior teeth were measured, and intrusion was assessed relative to the palatal plane. Significant volumetric reductions were observed in selected molar and premolar roots, with the highest percentage loss in the palatal root of the maxillary left first molar. Linear reduction was minimal and significant only in one premolar. Posterior intrusion was limited and not statistically significant. Root volume loss was not associated with intrusion but showed correlations with age and treatment duration. Volumetric assessment detected changes not consistently identified by linear measurements.

Article.Title: AICAR attenuates senescence-associated phenotypic remodeling of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells via the AMPK–SIRT1/p53 axis in CCl₄-induced liver fibrosis
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Zhao Z.; Li T.; Mu F.; Wang Z.; Xu L.; Zhang X.; Zhou C.; Hu L.; Wang B.
Article.Abstract: Liver fibrosis is a common consequence of chronic liver injury and is driven not only by extracellular matrix accumulation but also by disruption of the hepatic sinusoidal microenvironment. Liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) are specialized endothelial cells that maintain sinusoidal homeostasis, and their dysfunction is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to fibrotic progression. In this study, we investigated whether LSECs undergo senescence-associated phenotypic remodeling during CCl₄-induced liver fibrosis and explored potential regulatory mechanisms involved in this process. Using mouse models of CCl₄-induced liver fibrosis and natural aging, we found that fibrotic LSECs exhibited loss of fenestrae, impaired scavenging function, enhanced capillarization, altered paracrine profiles, and increased expression of senescence markers. These changes partially overlapped with abnormalities observed in LSECs from naturally aged mice, suggesting that fibrotic stress is associated with an aging-like endothelial phenotype. Transcriptomic analysis of fibrotic LSECs further revealed that dysregulation of the AMPK–SIRT1/p53 axis may contribute to these phenotypic alterations. In vivo, systemic pharmacological activation of AMPK with AICAR was associated with partial restoration of AMPK–SIRT1/p53 signaling in LSECs, attenuation of sinusoidal capillarization, and improvement of liver fibrosis, supporting LSEC senescence-related pathways as potential therapeutic targets for liver fibrosis.

Article.Title: The impact of public discourse on healthcare utilization during the COVID-19 pandemic
Article.Authors: Schilling J.; Bayindir E.; Fuchs R.; Schreyögg J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare systems worldwide, leading to substantial declines in preventive service utilization. We examine whether public discourse about COVID-19, measured as sentiment and topic salience on Twitter and in German newspapers, was associated with healthcare utilization in Germany between 2020 and 2022. Using computational text analysis and fixed-effects panel regressions of administrative outpatient data, we link monthly discourse measures from national and regional newspapers, Bild , and geolocated Twitter posts to utilization changes across screenings, vaccinations, chronic care, and psychotherapy. More positive sentiment and higher COVID salience were generally associated with lower use of discretionary services such as cancer screenings and group psychotherapy. By contrast, influenza and pneumococcal vaccination uptake increased when COVID-related attention was higher, particularly on Twitter and in Bild . Associations varied by media source, indicating that salience and evaluative tone capture distinct aspects of the information environment that relate differently to healthcare behavior.

Article.Title: ConvWaveFormer: a hybrid wavelet and CNN-transformer framework for ECG biometric identification
Article.Authors: Asif M.; Choi Y.; Iqbal M.; Kim S.
Article.Abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG)-based biometrics have shown strong potential as an alternative authentication modality because ECG signals contain subject-specific cardiac morphology and provide inherent liveness information. However, recognition performance remains sensitive to signal noise, morphological variability, and detector-dependent R-peak localization errors, which may misalign segmented heartbeats and reduce feature consistency. This study proposes ConvWaveFormer , a hybrid wavelet and CNN-Transformer framework for ECG biometric identification. Following morphology-preserving preprocessing, fixed-length R-peak-centered heartbeats are processed through two branches. A Daubechies-4 wavelet branch captures multiresolution time-frequency information, while a residual 1D-CNN-Transformer branch learns local ECG morphology and within-heartbeat temporal dependencies. The deep and wavelet representations, together with their element-wise interaction, are fused to generate a compact biometric embedding. Margin-based supervision using ArcFace and CosFace further promotes intra-subject compactness and inter-subject separability. The framework was evaluated on ECG-ID, Heartprint, MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, and MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm using three R-peak detection and heartbeat segmentation methods: NeuroKit2, SciPy FindPeaks, and XQRS. Although the relative performance of the detectors varied across datasets, XQRS achieved the strongest or comparable overall performance in most cases and was therefore selected for the final five-fold evaluation. ConvWaveFormer achieved mean identification accuracies of 92.99%, 76.47%, 97.70%, and 99.63%, with corresponding EER values of 5.84%, 11.11%, 1.72%, and 0.34%, respectively. In cross-dataset evaluation, a three-source score-level ensemble achieved 87.35% Rank-1 accuracy, 6.09% EER, and 0.9808 ROC-AUC on ECG-ID without target-domain model retraining. These results demonstrate that ConvWaveFormer learns discriminative and transferable ECG representations across heterogeneous offline datasets. Nevertheless, strictly session-disjoint, cross-device, and continuous wearable evaluations remain necessary to establish robustness under unconstrained real-world conditions.

Article.Title: Seismic performance and hybrid retrofit strategies for a historical four-legged masonry minaret
Article.Authors: Kiral A.; Tonyali Z.; Ergun M.; Yurdakul M.; Sever A.; Evci P.
Article.Abstract: Comparisons of global response modification and local strengthening for a complex heritage monument remain limited. This study evaluates lead-rubber-bearing (LRB) and friction-pendulum-bearing (FPB) isolation, carbon-fibre-reinforced polymer (CFRP) fabric and laminate, steel plates, and their hybrid combinations for the historical Four-Legged Minaret in Diyarbakır, Türkiye. A three-dimensional equivalent-continuum layered-shell macro-model was subjected to nonlinear direct-integration time-history analysis using one DD-2/ZD spectrum-compatible ground motion. The unretrofitted structure developed tensile-stress concentrations at the lower column–beam–body and upper balcony–shaft transitions. After isolation, corresponding maximum tensile stresses were 2.741 and 4.375 MPa for LRB and 0.813 and 4.740 MPa for FPB, showing that isolation alone did not control every critical local demand. Under the idealised full-bond assumption, all representative hybrid configurations satisfied the project-specific 2 MPa design-control target in both strengthened and adjacent regions; their all-region maxima ranged from 1.194 to 1.685 MPa for LRB and from 1.142 to 1.231 MPa for FPB. Steel plates gave the lowest demands inside the applied bands, but stress redistribution sometimes shifted the all-region maximum into adjacent masonry. The findings are scenario-specific and do not demonstrate crack prevention or unconditional safety; multi-record, site-specific and interface-validated assessment is required before implementation.

Article.Title: Physically constrained Mamba forecasting supports multiobjective reservoir water quality decisions
Article.Authors: Shu P.; Zhu J.; Huang Z.; Yu X.; Li X.; Cai F.; Wen X.
Article.Abstract: Reservoir water-quality management requires forecasts that remain dynamically plausible and scenario choices that balance water-quality objectives against the magnitude of requested trajectory change. Historical monitoring archives, however, rarely contain labelled control actions. We develop a physics-informed inverse-decision framework that combines a decomposition–interaction Mamba forecaster, observation-space oxygen-balance diagnostics, a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and preference-conditioned multi-objective search. The forecaster separates multiscale dynamics before channel-specific state-space encoding and gated cross-variable exchange. A lumped Streeter–Phelps residual regularises dissolved-oxygen forecasts, while the CVAE represents DO–CODMn recovery changes observed after natural events. Evaluation on Miyun Reservoir observations from June 2021 to January 2025 gives 24-step RMSE values of 0.305 for dissolved oxygen and 0.318 for CODMn. The physical-violation rate, defined as disagreement between predicted and Streeter–Phelps model-implied DO-increment signs, decreases from 8.4% without the two output-space terms to 0.3% with the full model. Fixed-horizon latent search yields a hypervolume of 0.824, compared with 0.706 for NSGA-III and 0.487 for weighted-sum latent search, with no diagnostic-margin crossings in 55 evaluated decisions. Because the archive contains no device-action records, the method returns candidate target trajectories and dimensionless concentration-equivalent demand-and-roughness values, not executable commands or calibrated costs. Prospective use requires independent validation of the physical diagnostic, event generalisation, recursive forecasting and measured actuator response.

Article.Title: Association between postoperative serum calcium and complications after pancreaticoduodenectomy in a retrospective multicenter study
Article.Authors: Huang T.; Pu S.; Xie W.; Shen A.; Huang Z.; Li D.; Wu Z.; Zong K.
Article.Abstract: Serum calcium is an important indicator for assessing the severity of acute pancreatitis. The physiological processes following pancreatitis and pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) are similar; however, it is unknown whether serum calcium is associated with outcomes after PD. The present study analyzed serum calcium on postoperative days 3, 6, 9, and 12. Logistic regression was used to identify correlations between serum calcium, clinical postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF), and other complications. Generalized additive models (GAM) were used to determine serum calcium thresholds. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) was used to visualize linear or non-linear relationships between serum calcium and outcomes. Latent class analysis (LCA) was used to identify potential categories based on serum calcium levels at various time points. Generalized additive mixed-effects models (GAMM) were combined to analyze the relationship between serum calcium and outcomes at four-time points. The study analyzed 447 PD patients. Serum calcium levels at four-time points were negatively associated with clinical POPF, with thresholds of 1.96 and 1.98 calculated using GAM. RCS was used to visualize the relationship between serum calcium and outcomes in a possible L-type. We identified four potential classes through LCA, and further logistic regression demonstrated that persistently lower serum calcium levels were associated with an increased risk of clinical POPF. GAMM-exposed postoperative serum calcium was negatively associated with clinical POPF. In this retrospective cohort, lower postoperative serum calcium levels were associated with higher odds of clinical POPF and other postoperative complications. These findings are exploratory and require prospective validation before serum calcium can be considered for clinical risk assessment.

Article.Title: Automated detection of carotid artery encasement on CT scans using an AI-driven approach
Article.Authors: Hedesiu P.; Eftimie S.; Hedesiu I.; Barrera C.; Trombitas V.; Iacob L.; Zahu R.; Ozyoruk K.
Article.Abstract: Carotid artery encasement can complicate the surgical resection of head and neck squamous cell carcinomas, increasing the risk of surgery. Incomplete tumor excision due to the proximity of the carotid artery may affect long-term outcomes by promoting tumor recurrence. This study leverages artificial Intelligence to detect carotid artery encasements in computed tomography images. CT images and tumor masks were sourced from the National Cancer Institute’s CPTAC-HNSCC dataset. The study included 100 patients, yielding 1,367 images with tumor presence. For HNSCC segmentation, a pre-trained ResNet-50 backbone of a U-Net model was fine-tuned on the CT images. Carotid segmentation was performed using the SAM-Med2D foundation model. Both models returned segmentations for the tumor and carotid, respectively. Encasement was assessed by calculating the minimum distance and encasement angle between the masks provided by the models. In validation, the tumor segmentation model achieved a mean F1 score of 86% and an Intersection over Union score of 75%, with 73% IoU for the tumor class and 99% for the non-tumor class. Carotid segmentation was most effective when using the bounding-box method, reaching 79% accuracy. Both models were successfully applied to the same image for the final assessment. This study developed an automated method for evaluating CAE in CT images, demonstrating promising potential for future clinical applications.

Article.Title: Evaluating the performance of long short-term memory to other time series models for univariate and multivariate data
Article.Authors: Prakash C.; Kumar B.; Lodhi A.; Dhyani B.; Joshi C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Time series data analysis is one of the difficult tasks in real-world data problems because the data entities are determined not only by physical causes, but also by the chronological sequence in which they occurred. In this work, we have examined how Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is perform well to traditional statistical methods and other machine learning models for performing univariate and multivariate time series single-step forecasting. We have also studied how memory cells and gated structures work in LSTM model with different cases to show advancement of LSTM as compared to other time series analysis tools. The key contributions of this work are methodological and empirical rather than architectural. Specifically, this study (i) provides a mechanistic, architecture-level interpretation of LSTM’s gating and memory dynamics that explains its temporal learning behavior, distinct from post-hoc explainable AI (XAI) feature-attribution techniques, and (ii) establishes a benchmarking framework that evaluates LSTM against statistical models, machine learning models, a forecasting-specific Transformer architecture (PatchTST), and a baseline (vanilla) Transformer under identical experimental settings on a real-world environmental dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that, within context-specific empirical evidence, the LSTM model exhibits more stable and consistent performance than the considered baselines. Cross-regional validation further shows that the observed performance trends remain largely consistent across both datasets, suggesting that the advantages of LSTM are not solely attributable to local characteristics of a single region. The findings are presented as context-specific empirical evidence rather than claims of universal model superiority and provide practical insights into forecasting under data-constrained environmental conditions.

Article.Title: A picture fuzzy SWARA–VIKOR framework for evaluating drone-swarm navigation and mission-coordination strategies under uncertainty
Article.Authors: Saadaoui K.; Farhad A.; Ullah K.
Article.Abstract: Intelligent decision-making frameworks need to be able to handle operational uncertainty, ambiguous expert judgments, and interactions among mission attributes to navigate and coordinate missions in an autonomous drone swarm efficiently. Traditional optimization and decision models do not effectively represent ambiguous expert judgments and critical navigation and coordination factors that impact the behavior of the systems in a nonlinear way. To overcome all these limitations, this study proposes a Picture Fuzzy Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis–VIšekriterijumsko KOmpromisno Rangiranje (PF-SWARA–VIKOR) framework for evaluating drone-swarm strategies under uncertain conditions. PF-SWARA weighting begins with an expert-based screening phase to determine the relevance of the criteria, allowing only the most relevant criteria to proceed to the weighting and ranking phase. Picture Fuzzy Sets (PFSs) provide a more complete representation of uncertainty and hesitation compared to ordinary or intuitionistic fuzzy sets by means of positive, neutral, negative, and refusal degrees that model expert ratings. While the criterion weights are obtained by PF-SWARA, the five strategies centralized, decentralized consensus-based, leader–follower, hybrid-adaptive, and behaviour-based reactive coordination strategies are ranked by PF-VIKOR. According to the hypothetical application, \({U}_{4}\) is the first preference, since it has the minimum compromise value \({\mathcal{Q}}_{4}=0.0000\) , and the preference order is \({U}_{4}\succ {U}_{2}\succ {U}_{1}\succ {U}_{5}\succ {U}_{3}\) . The most influential criteria are \({L}_{7}\) and \({L}_{1}\) , with weights of \(0.1360\) and \(0.1357\) , respectively. Furthermore, \({U}_{4}\) is first across all values of \(\tau =0.1 to 0.9\) , but the rankings in-between shift depending on the relative strength of the group's utility and the individual's regret. Since the case study uses simulated experts and hypothetical evaluations, the results are of methodological applicability and not empirically generalizable.

Article.Title: Clinical and MEFV variant characteristics of pediatric patients with an FMF-compatible phenotype and PFAPA-compatible features in a Palestinian referral cohort: a retrospective study
Article.Authors: Abuhammad A.; Alnatsha A.; Bali I.; Abozalata N.; Zabin L.; Shakhshir A.; Abunejma F.
Article.Abstract: Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) and periodic fever, aphthous stomatitis, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis (PFAPA) syndrome may share clinical manifestations, complicating phenotypic classification in children from populations in which MEFV variants are frequent. This study characterized the clinical and genetic features of a pediatric Palestinian referral cohort with an FMF-compatible phenotype and described the subgroup that also fulfilled PFAPA clinical classification criteria. This retrospective two-center cohort included 169 patients aged ≤ 18 years who were retrospectively classified with an FMF-compatible phenotype using available clinical and genetic information and the Eurofever/PRINTO classification framework. Patients were subsequently assessed for PFAPA-compatible features using the corresponding clinical classification criteria. Genetic analyses were restricted to the 143 patients with available MEFV testing. Of the 169 patients with an FMF-compatible phenotype, 32 (18.9%) additionally fulfilled PFAPA clinical classification criteria. MEFV genetic testing was available in 124/137 (90.5%) patients with an FMF-only phenotype and 19/32 (59.4%) patients with PFAPA-compatible features. Among the 143 genetically tested patients, M694V was the most frequently recorded variant, occurring in 84 (58.7%). Of the 19 genetically tested patients with PFAPA-compatible features, 10 were recorded as heterozygous; E148Q was the most frequent heterozygous variant pattern. Clinical manifestations incorporated into the PFAPA classification algorithm were interpreted descriptively rather than as independent between-group associations. A subgroup of children classified with an FMF-compatible phenotype also fulfilled PFAPA clinical classification criteria. The findings demonstrate clinical overlap but do not establish coexistence of two independent diseases or a causal genotype–phenotype relationship. Unequal availability of genetic testing and the limitations of retrospective phenotypic classification warrant cautious interpretation.

Article.Title: Identification and validation of T cell proliferation-associated transcriptomic biomarkers in ischemic stroke
Article.Authors: Zhou J.; Nan Y.; Wang X.; Tang Q.; Ma Y.; Li C.; Qu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke (IS) is a major global cause of mortality and chronic disability, with complex immune dysfunction. This study aimed to identify T-cell proliferation-related genes (TRGs) in IS pathogenesis and explore their diagnostic/therapeutic potential. IS patients’ gene expression profiles were obtained from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differential expression analysis identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs), which overlapped with AmiGO2-derived TRGs to get candidate genes. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression and Support Vector Machine-Recursive Feature Elimination (SVM-RFE) selected biomarkers (with validation). The diagnostic capacity of these biomarkers was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and nomogram development. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and immune infiltration analyses were done to characterize the biomarkers. Biomarker expression levels were confirmed in clinical samples by Reverse Transcription quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-qPCR). Both ARG1 and TNFSF13B were consistently upregulated in IS across cohorts and demonstrated strong diagnostic performance (area under the curve (AUC) > 0.7). The AUC for the nomogram model reached 0.92, suggesting favorable predictive performance that warrants further validation. GSEA showed ARG1 positively enriched in CD4 + T cell activation-related sets, TNFSF13B negatively in stemness-related sets. Immune profiling: ARG1 negatively correlated with activated B cells (cor = -0.63, p < 0.001); TNFSF13B inversely associated with activated CD8 + T cells (cor = -0.34, p < 0.01). RT-qPCR confirmed their higher expression in IS vs controls (p < 0.05). The above findings represent preliminary hypothesis-generating evidence and require further validation in larger cohort studies. Overall, this study identified/validated TRG-related IS diagnostic biomarkers, offering insights into immune dysregulation and personalized immunotherapy targets.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a deep learning model for differentiating cytomegalovirus and herpes simplex virus esophagitis using endoscopic images
Article.Authors: Kim J.; Lee Y.; Oh Y.; Kim T.; Lee H.; Min B.; Lee J.; Rhee P.; Min Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) and herpes simplex virus (HSV) are the most common causes of infectious esophagitis in immuno-compromised patients. However, their endoscopic features frequently overlap, making real-time etiologic differentiation difficult and often requiring delayed confirmation by immunohistochemistry. Methods: We developed and validated a deep learning model to distinguish CMV from HSV esophagitis using endoscopic images from biopsy-proven cases at a tertiary referral center. The model was trained with domain-specific pretraining and a curriculum learning strategy that sequentially introduced cases according to diagnostic difficulty, mimicking clinical learning processes. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using an independent test set and compared with experienced endoscopists. Results: The curriculum learning–based model demonstrated improved classification performance over conventional training approaches, achieving an AUROC of 0.783 (95% confidence interval 0.680–0.885). Its sensitivity and specificity were comparable to those of expert endoscopists. Model visualization showed attention to clinically relevant mucosal abnormalities. Conclusion: Deep learning analysis of routine endoscopic images can assist in differentiating CMV and HSV esophagitis. A curriculum learning strategy may enhance clinical applicability by improving performance in visually ambiguous conditions, potentially supporting earlier therapeutic decision-making while awaiting histopathologic confirmation

Article.Title: Transcriptomic profiling of human iPSC-derived Schwann-like cells reveals NF2-regulated gene regulatory networks
Article.Authors: Lazaro O.; Li S.; Smiley J.; Carter W.; House A.; Awosika O.; Robertson S.; Haskell A.; Hinkel R.; Hickey B.; Angus S.; Clapp D.; Syed A.; Johnson T.; Rhodes S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Schwann cells are vital to development and maintenance of the peripheral nervous system, and their dysfunction has been implicated in a range of neurological and neoplastic disorders, including NF2 -related schwannomatosis ( NF2 -SWN). We have developed a human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) model for the study of Schwann-like cell differentiation in health and disease. We performed sequence-based transcriptomics, immunofluorescence-based morphological analysis, and CRISPR-Cas9-based validation of differentiation from hiPSCs derived Schwann cell precursors (SCPs) to terminally differentiated Schwann-like cells (SLCs) representing 6 distinct stages of development across a period of 31 days. To further validate our findings, we performed integrated, cross-species analyses at bulk and single cell resolution. Our hiPSCs model of Schwann cell development shared overlapping gene expression signatures with human amniotic mesenchymal stem cell (hAMSCs) derived SLCs and in vivo mouse models but also revealed unique features that may reflect species-specific aspects of Schwann cell biology. Moreover, we have identified gene co-expression modules that are dynamically regulated during hiPSCs to SLCs differentiation associated with ear and neural development, cell fate determination, the NF2 gene, and extracellular matrix (ECM) organization. Through integrated analysis of multiple datasets and genetic disruption of NF2 via CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing in hiPSC derived SCPs, we have identified transcriptomic signatures suggesting a series of novel ECM associated genes potentially regulated by Merlin, providing a hypothesis-generating framework for future functional studies. The hiPSC model generated in this study further provides a system for studying NF2-regulated gene expression throughout Schwann-like cell development in the context of widely available data on iPSC Schwann cells and rare diseases that lack effective treatments such as NF2 -SWN.

Article.Title: Effects of different disinfectants and culture substrates on aseptic germination and aseptic seedling establishment of Cajanus cajan (L.) Millsp
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Li S.; Yang C.; Zhang X.; Zheng P.; Zhao H.; Wang Y.; Luo J.; Zhang L.; Zhang W.; Luo C.; Li G.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: To establish an efficient and stable aseptic germination system for pigeonpea seeds ( Cajanus cajan (L.) Millsp. ), the present study investigated the effects of disinfectant type, disinfection time, and culture substrates on the pigeonpea seed germination rate, germination dynamics, aseptic seedling rate, aseptic seedling growth dynamics, and contamination. Disinfectant, disinfection time, and culture substrates all influenced the aseptic germination and establishment of aseptic seedlings of pigeonpea seeds significantly ( P < 0.05). Disinfection with 5% sodium hypochlorite (NaClO) for 5 min was the ideal treatment, with the seed germination rate and aseptic seedling rate being significantly higher than those under 0.1% mercuric chloride (HgCl₂) and the control group. The germination rates on Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium and sterile filter paper were 80.00% and 81.11%, respectively, and the aseptic seedling rates were 55.56% and 81.11%, respectively. Seed germination and aseptic seedling rates of the 5% NaClO group decreased slightly with an increase in disinfection time, whereas the 0.1% HgCl₂ group exhibited a significant declining trend due to higher toxicity. Under the same disinfection conditions, culture on sterile filter paper was superior to that on MS medium in terms of germination speed, final germination number, aseptic seedling quantity, and contamination control. The contamination level was in the order of sterile water control group > 0.1% HgCl₂ group > 5% NaClO group. According to the results, disinfection with 5% NaClO for 5 min combined with culture on sterile filter paper was the ideal disinfection and culture strategy for pigeonpea seeds. The system above featured stable disinfection efficacy, low phytotoxicity, high germination and aseptic seedling rates, and it could control contamination effectively. The results could provide theoretical and technical support for pigeonpea tissue culture, in vitro regeneration, genetic transformation, and industrial seedling production.

Article.Title: Explainable artificial intelligence of things integrated spatio-temporal feature modeling for traffic congestion framework on intelligent urban mobility system
Article.Authors: Binyamin S.; Salama R.; Mohaisen L.; Altwijri M.; Aboalela R.; Alqassim M.; Milyani A.; Ragab M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Recent developments of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) are transforming several sectors like Industry 4.0, smart cities, intelligent healthcare, and smart transportation. The AIoT can be employed in urban mobility to enable real-time monitoring and intelligent decision-making in the transportation sector. Traffic congestion classification is a significant aspect of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), as the rising urban population has contributed to severe congestion complexity that impacts air quality, road safety, and travel time. Accurate classification of congestion patterns improves traffic management and mitigates environmental impacts. Although precisely predicting congestion spread is still problematic, owing to the complex, non-linear, and dynamic nature of traffic patterns. As deep learning advances, efficient models are required to address the challenges in smart urban mobility systems. Therefore, this study presents a Deep Learning-Based Urban Mobility Intelligent System for Traffic Congestion Framework (DLUMIS-TCF). The proposed DLUMIS-TCF model analyzes urban mobility data with trip-level records for precise traffic congestion level classification. The preprocessing stage includes missing value handling, outlier detection, feature scaling, temporal attribute extraction, and spatial coordinate utilization to prepare the data for effective learning. For feature selection, the model utilizes Elastic Net to select the relevant spatio-temporal features from the dataset. In addition, the traffic congestion level classification is performed using a heterogeneous spatiotemporal graph attention network. Furthermore, the optimization of the model is carried out using the AdaBelief optimizer to improve convergence and performance. To improve the interpretability of the model, SHAP is used to explain the contribution of input features toward the classification results. To assess the performance of the proposed DLUMIS-TCF model, experiments are carried out on an Urban Mobility Intelligence Dataset obtained from the Kaggle repository. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed model in predicting traffic congestion compared to other methods. Thus, the proposed DLUMIS-TCF approach can be useful for urban traffic management, congestion control, and intelligent transportation systems.

Article.Title: Thinning and mulching reduce winter drought impacts on dryland forest soil moisture
Article.Authors: Sankey T.; Tatum J.; Ozment L.; Dinsdale K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Regional drought events are becoming more frequent and severe across the western US. In particular, winter droughts have important ecohydrological impacts that last across the entire year. Using a uniquely extensive sensor network across Arizona, we examined soil matric potential during and after 2024–2025 winter drought in thinned, thinned and mulched, and adjacent non-thinned forest sites from three study areas across an elevation and climate gradient. Our results consistently indicate that the winter drought prolonged soil drought at all sites throughout the subsequent spring, when soil matric potential remained below critical thresholds and plants sustained biologically important water stress for up to 293 days. Importantly, thinning treatments reduced these impacts and had significant interaction effects with winter drought. Our results also demonstrate the added benefits of mulching that further enhanced thinning effects on soil matric potential during winter drought periods. Treatment benefits for soil matric potential become particularly significant during winter droughts, although they might not be apparent during periods of average precipitation. Taken together, our results demonstrate that dryland forest thinning and mulching treatments improve winter drought resiliency.

Article.Title: Bi-DaR4D: a distance-adaptive quaternion embedding with bidirectional rotation for knowledge graph completion
Article.Authors: Dong Y.; Wang R.; Feng P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Knowledge graph embedding (KGE) models encode entities and relations in continuous spaces, but existing translation-, rotation-, and quaternion-based methods still struggle to jointly represent relational directionality and semantic distance. We propose Bi-DaR4D, a quaternion embedding framework that combines bidirectional isoclinic rotation with a distance-adaptive translation mechanism. The model uses paired unit quaternions to perform coordinated rotations in four-dimensional space, strengthening the representation of inverse and multi-relational structures. It further learns relation-specific distance adjustments that balance directional transformation with geometric sensitivity. Experiments on WN18RR and FB15k-237 show that Bi-DaR4D achieves competitive or superior link prediction performance across ranking metrics, including MRR, Hits@3, and Hits@10. Ablation results indicate that the distance-adaptive module provides the clearest contribution, while bidirectional rotation contributes to relational expressiveness with smaller changes across the tested metrics. These results support Bi-DaR4D as a geometrically interpretable framework for knowledge graph completion in settings with complex relational patterns.

Article.Title: Validity and reliability study of the Turkish version of the Bipolar recovery questionnaire in Bipolar affective disorder
Article.Authors: Yagci Z.; Eraslan B.; Eraslan O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to assess the validity and reliability of the Turkish versions of the Bipolar Recovery Questionnaire (BRQ) and to examine the clinical variables associated with personal recovery. This was a single-center cross-sectional study. Outpatients with the diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder (BD I) were included in the study. The BRQ was translated from English into Turkish and back-translated into English. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha, corrected item-total correlations, and Cronbach’s alpha if item deleted. Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5,Clinical Version (SCID-5/CV), administered by the clinician, was used to confirm the diagnosis BD I. Subjective Recovery Assessment Scale (SubRAS), Personal and Social Performance Scale (PSP) and Global Assessment of Functioning (GAF) were used to examine convergent validity. The clinician-administered Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) and Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) were used to evaluate symptom severity in patients. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to evaluate the clinical variables associated with BRQ total scores. Cronbach’s alpha coefficient for BRQ was 0.888 and showed very good internal consistency. Corrected item-total score correlation coefficients ranged from − 0.114 to 0.742. Total BRQ score had moderate positive correlations with PSP (ρ = 0.432 , p < 0.001) and SubRAS (ρ = 0.383, p < 0.001), a weak positive correlation with GAF (ρ = 0.304 , p = 0.004), and a weak negative correlation with the HAM-D total score (ρ = -0.301 , p = 0.004). A weak positive correlation was observed between the total score of BRQ and the total duration of education (ρ = 0.265 , p = 0.012). Multivariable regression analysis showed that having a university degree was associated with higher BRQ scores compared with the reference education category. The present study provides preliminary evidence supporting the reliability and validity of the Turkish version of the BRQ for assessing personal recovery in individuals with BD I.

Article.Title: “DNA damage activates cGAS-STING signaling through ROS dependent p62 recruitment”
Article.Authors: Barbato F.; Micheli E.; Iris F.; Berardinelli F.; Sgura A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ionizing radiation (IR) induces DNA damage that activates innate immunity through the cyclic GMP–AMP synthase (cGAS) pathway, yet the mechanisms determining why only a subset of radiation-induced micronuclei (MNi) become cGAS-positive remain unclear. Here, we investigated the dose- and time-dependent dynamics of cGAS-positive MNi and the molecular events regulating their formation in HaCaT human keratinocytes. cGAS recruitment occurred with delayed kinetics relative to total MNi formation and was associated with micronuclear envelope destabilization and lamin B1 loss. Structural observations support a sequential model in which early recruitment of the autophagy receptor p62 precedes micronuclear envelope destabilization and subsequent cGAS recruitment. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated following irradiation emerged as key upstream regulators by promoting p62 recruitment and micronuclear destabilization. Accordingly, ROS scavenging with N-acetylcysteine markedly reduced both p62-positive and cGAS-positive MNi. Conditioned-medium experiments further demonstrated that diffusible ROS-dependent signals generated by irradiated cells promote the formation of cGAS-positive MNi in non-irradiated bystander cells. Finally, cGAS activation was accompanied by delayed induction of type I interferons and ISG15, which was attenuated by ROS scavenging. Together, these findings identify oxidative stress as a critical regulator linking radiation-induced genomic instability to innate immune activation through p62-dependent micronuclear sensing.

Article.Title: Classification accuracy, assessment time, and preference of shock index versus simple shock index: a randomized-order within-participant repeated-measures simulation study
Article.Authors: Kamikawa Y.; Muto O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although previous studies have demonstrated comparable predictive performance between shock index (SI) and simple shock index (sSI), the practical aspects of sSI has not been evaluated. This study aimed to compare the classification accuracy, assessment time, and preference of SI and sSI. This randomized-order within-participant repeated-measures simulation study included fifth-year medical students at a single university from 2025 to 2026. Participants assessed 10 clinical cases using SI and sSI and classified each case as high or low risk. Classification accuracy and assessment time were analyzed using participant-level paired analyses. Preference was evaluated using a three-category questionnaire (sSI, SI, or no difference). Eighty-seven students participated in the study. Classification accuracy was 93.3% for sSI and 94.0% for SI, with no significant difference between the two methods (difference, − 0.7% points; 95% confidence interval [CI], − 4.1 to 2.8; P = 0.629). Assessment time using sSI was shorter than that using SI in the primary analysis (median, 7.6 vs. 8.3 s; median difference, − 0.9 s; 95% CI, − 1.6 to − 0.5; P = 0.002). Regarding preference, 57 participants preferred sSI, 18 preferred SI, and 12 reported no preference; among participants who expressed a preference for either method, sSI was preferred significantly more often than SI ( P < 0.001). In this exploratory study, no statistically significant difference in classification accuracy or practically meaningful difference in assessment time was observed between sSI and SI, although participants preferred sSI. Further studies are needed to determine whether these findings translate into clinically meaningful advantages.

Article.Title: Double-network silica–polyacrylamide composite aerogels with enhanced mechanical integrity and multifunctional adsorption performance
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Lee W.; Mahadik D.; Kim T.; Park H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A facile strategy was developed to synthesize silica/polyacrylamide composite aerogels that simultaneously exhibit high mechanical strength and large surface area. An interpenetrated organic polyacrylamide network was incorporated within the silica framework without additional cross-linkers, enabling efficient stress distribution and enhanced structural integrity. The optimized TDB-Pam(2 M) composite aerogel possesses a homogeneous mesoporous network with a specific surface area of 774 m 2 g -1 , low density (0.346 g cm -3 ), and superior compressive strength (22.3 MPa) with a Young’s modulus of 25.3 MPa. The incorporation of amide-rich polyacrylamide also provided selective binding sites for heavy-metal ions, achieving more than 90% Hg 2+ removal efficiency and a Langmuir maximum adsorption capacity of 626.79 mg g -1 for TDB-Pam(2 M). This synthesis route provides an effective approach to fabricate mechanically reinforced, multifunctional silica-based aerogels applicable to environmental purification and other advanced porous-material applications.

Article.Title: Robust uncertainty-aware attack-fault diagnosis in hydrogen-based energy system based on a copula-meta-learning approach
Article.Authors: Singh N.; Mohammed A.; Hussein Z.; Saeed T.; Karimipouya A.; Sabzevari K.
Article.Abstract: Active Distribution Power Systems (ADPS), including hydrogen-based renewable energy units, are becoming essential components of modern electrical grids. These systems integrate distributed energy resources with advanced communication technology to enhance efficiency, flexibility, and reliability. However, a significant challenge they face is distinguishing between malfunctions and cyberattacks, particularly False Data Injection (FDI) attacks, which can severely impact grid performance. Traditional fault detection methods often struggle to differentiate between these two causes, leading to inaccurate diagnoses and delayed responses, which jeopardize system reliability. This paper presents the GAN–LSTM method, which utilizes a hybrid model combining Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). This approach enhances the system’s ability to adaptively detect faults and attacks by learning from past incidents. A major obstacle the method encounters is the inherent uncertainty in data monitoring. ADPS data is often noisy, incomplete, or inconsistent, which can undermine model performance. Factors such as incomplete sensor readings, varying environmental conditions, and unstable network states contribute to this uncertainty. To address this issue, we employ the Copula method, which captures and models relationships within uncertain data. By using the Copula approach, we ensure that our model remains reliable and accurate, even when dealing with ambiguous or insufficient data. Experimental results indicate that the proposed GAN-LSTM-based GAN–LSTM model outperforms traditional techniques, achieving approximately 6–15% higher detection accuracy in differentiating between faults and cyberattacks. Furthermore, when compared to conventional machine learning techniques that do not account for uncertainty, our model’s detection accuracy improves in scenarios characterized by significant data uncertainty, such as missing or corrupted sensor data. These findings validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, demonstrating its capability to provide precise and trustworthy diagnostics, even in uncertain situations. The method represents a promising strategy for enhancing the security and resilience of ADPS while ensuring efficient fault diagnosis and cyberattack detection.

Article.Title: Molecular detection of Acanthamoeba genotypes and Pneumocystis jirovecii in bronchoalveolar lavage specimens from immunocompetent patients with respiratory disorders
Article.Authors: Tabaripour R.; Fakhar M.; Javanmard E.; Gholami Koohestan M.; Hosseini S.; Gholami S.; Saberi R.
Article.Abstract: Opportunistic pathogens such as Acanthamoeba spp., Microsporidia , and Pneumocystis jirovecii are well recognized causes of pulmonary infections in immunocompromised patients. However, their prevalence and clinical significance in immunocompetent individuals with respiratory disorders remain poorly understood. This study aimed to determine the presence of Acanthamoeba spp., Microsporidia , and P. jirovecii in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples from immunocompetent patients with various respiratory disorders referred to the Iranian National Registry Center for Lophomoniasis (INRCL) at Imam Khomeini Hospital, Mazandaran province, northern Iran. This cross-sectional study analyzed 146 BAL samples collected from immunocompetent patients with respiratory disorders during 2024. DNA was extracted using a phenol-chloroform-isoamyl alcohol method. Molecular detection was performed using conventional PCR with genus-specific primers (JDP1/JDP2) for Acanthamoeba spp., and nested PCR assays targeting the ITS region for Microsporidia and the mitochondrial large subunit rRNA (mtLSU rRNA) gene for P. jirovecii . Genotype identification of Acanthamoeba isolates was achieved through bidirectional Sanger sequencing, and sequences were analyzed using BLASTn. A phylogenetic tree was constructed using MEGA-x software employing the Maximum Likelihood method with the Tamura 3-parameter model and 1,000 bootstrap replicates. Statistical analysis was performed using the Chi-square test (SPSS v20), with a P-value < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Molecular analysis identified Acanthamoeba spp. in six cases (4.11%), which were classified as genotypes T4 ( n = 5) and T5 ( n = 1). All six patients had underlying chronic respiratory conditions, with chronic cough as the predominant symptom. Additionally, P. jirovecii was detected in nine patients (6.16%), including one case of co-detection with Acanthamoeba T4. Among P. jirovecii -positive cases, the majority resided in rural areas, and all had pre-existing pulmonary diseases. Microsporidia genus were not detected in any of the samples analyzed, which may reflect their low prevalence in immunocompetent populations or possible methodological limitations. Molecular detection of Acanthamoeba (primarily genotype T4) and P. jirovecii DNA in BAL specimens from immunocompetent patients with underlying chronic lung diseases indicates the presence of these organisms in the respiratory tract. The relatively higher detection rate of P. jirovecii among rural residents warrants further epidemiological investigation. Importantly, PCR positivity alone should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of clinical disease, and the significance of these molecular findings requires careful clinical correlation. Future prospective studies with longitudinal follow-up are needed to determine whether these colonizers contribute to disease progression or exacerbation in immunocompetent individuals with pre-existing pulmonary conditions.

Article.Title: Endometrial evolution assessment using a high-resolution mini-hysteroscope for virtual biopsies
Article.Authors: Cruz F.; Kolatt T.; Mashiach S.; Pellicer A.; Or Y.
Article.Abstract: Virtual histology is a method by which live magnified images of tissue’s upper layers are combined with computerized analysis to provide tissue diagnosis. It provides a useful two-fold view of both the tissue’s in-vivo appearance and morphological characteristics. The method is particularly efficient for the endometrium due to its rapid remodeling during the normal menstrual cycle. Endometrial dating is routinely assessed for embryo transfer timing in IVF, yet currently, it remains inaccurate and controversial. High magnification, safe and usable hysteroscopy, with minimal image deformation, can offer more accurate endometrial dating. Utilizing a mini-hysteroscopic system, we captured 363 high-quality images during 77 sessions performed on 20 participants, on different cycle days. With zero severe adverse events, physicians defined the use of the system to be “very easy” to “reasonable” in 95% of all sessions. Among participants, in all sessions, 86% did not report any pain. Image quality was evaluated “good” to “excellent” in > 65% of the sessions. Image-based endometrial dating compared to dating according to participant’s report and urine LH test, yields correlation coefficients of ≥ 0.9 ( P < 10 − 3 ). In this study we demonstrate that the mini-hysteroscope system is safe, highly usable and provides high-quality images for endometrial virtual histology assessment and dating. Article.Title: Evaluation transit-oriented development potential using GIS-MCDA: “a spatial framework for Greater Cairo”
Article.Authors: Elwan K.; Effat H.; Yousry T.; Abd-AlMoity E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) is a sustainable planning approach that integrates land use and transportation to promote compact, accessible, and efficient urban growth. However, in rapidly urbanizing metropolitan contexts, TOD assessment is often centered on planned station areas, while dense and historically established districts receive less attention despite their relevance for retrofit-oriented intervention. Addressing this gap, the originality of this study lies in developing a highly granular, multi-scalar GIS-MCDA framework to assess TOD retrofit and readiness potential across 413 administrative units (shiyakha) in the Greater Cairo Region. This approach combines literature-informed and expert-validated socio-economic, land-use, and transport indicators into a composite TOD Index. The framework integrates spatial normalization, hybrid weighting, and multi-criteria aggregation to generate a fine-grained map of TOD readiness that captures local variations in urban form and accessibility. The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity. Central districts such as Al-Sayeda Zainab, Bulaq, Azbakeya, Shubra, and Abdeen exhibit the highest TOD potential due to compact urban fabric, strong transit accessibility, and land-use diversity, whereas peripheral areas such as 15th May City, Tura, and Atfih show low suitability because of dispersed development, weaker infrastructure, and limited public transport coverage. The findings highlight the need to distinguish between consolidated districts requiring TOD retrofit and peripheral areas that demand longer-term structural transformation. Overall, the proposed framework offers a replicable decision-support tool to assist decision-makers and urban planners in prioritizing targeted interventions and infrastructure improvements, thereby guiding sustainable urban policy in rapidly growing metropolitan contexts.

Article.Authors: Younas A.; Iqbal J.; Bodlah M.; Mohsin A.; Kanwal A.; Tahir H.; Zaheer M.; Adil M.; Bodlah I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cigarette beetle ( Lasioderma serricorne ) is a widely distributed pest of stored products, causing significant economic losses worldwide. Pakistan’s tobacco business suffers economically from L. serricorne , and this insect can seriously deteriorate tobacco that has been stored. The most destructive of these are the larval and adult stages. This study aims to develop a life table L. serricorne on six tobacco varieties SPT-G-28, K-339, SPT-G-227, OK-940, Gulshery and RG-17. Results show significant variations in survival rate, population growth parameters and developmental periods of cigarette beetle across different tobacco varieties. RG-17 variety supported longest developmental period and highest reproductive metrics, indicating its susceptibility to infestation. Conversely, Gulshery variety showed higher intrinsic rates of increase and fecundity. According to results, this information may provide valuable insights into the L. serricorne infestation in warehouses settings and contribute to the development of effective for mass rearing and management strategies.

Article.Title: Investigating the effect of natural aggregate on asphalt mixture performance by integrating experimental evaluation and explainable machine learning
Article.Authors: Ragab M.; Arnaout M.; Ibrahim M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Natural aggregate (NA) is commonly incorporated into asphalt mixtures as part of the aggregate skeleton; however, excessive NA content may adversely affect mechanical strength and deformation resistance. This study investigates the influence of NA content on asphalt mixture performance using an integrated experimental, statistical, and explainable machine learning (XML) framework. Asphalt mixtures were prepared using crushed coarse aggregate with varying NA contents of 0%, 4%, 8%, 12%, 16%, 20%, and 24% by weight. The experimental program included Marshall stability and flow, indirect tensile strength (ITS), and wheel tracking tests to evaluate strength and deformation responses. Pearson correlation, ANOVA, and stepwise regression examined relationships between mixture variables and performance indicators. Random Forest (RF) models were then developed to predict mixture performance, achieving strong predictive capability, with testing R 2 values exceeding 0.95 and corresponding MAPE values below 2.5% for all targets. Feature importance identified NA content as the most influential variable governing mixture performance. SHAP and response surface analyses further quantified the contribution of mixture variables and illustrated their combined interaction effects. The obtained results indicated that increasing NA content reduced stability and ITS while increasing flow and rut depth. The findings also revealed that the most pronounced incremental deterioration occurred between 12% and 16% NA, where tensile strength and deformation responses exhibited high sensitivity to increasing NA replacement. This integrated framework supports reliable prediction, engineering interpretation, and informed design decisions for NA-containing asphalt mixtures.

Article.Title: First-principles investigation of the pressure dependent physical properties of intermetallic kagome ZrRe2
Article.Authors: Naher M.; Yusuf Haider A.; Paul D.; Rahman M.; Haque F.; Naqib S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Intermetallic compounds hosting Kagome lattices have drawn great interest as a vibrant emerging field in condensed matter physics. We present a first-principles density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the pressure-dependent structural, electronic, mechanical, thermophysical, vibrational, and optical properties of the intermetallic Kagome compound ZrRe₂. The calculated ground-state structural parameters are in excellent agreement with available experimental results. The estimated structural parameters, elastic constants, and phonon dispersion confirm the structural, chemical, mechanical, and dynamical stability of ZrRe 2 up to 25 GPa. The Kagome feature in the material has been identified from the electronic band structure for the first time. ZrRe 2 exhibits topological feature (Dirac point) at 0 GPa, which vanishes at a critical pressure of ~ 12 GPa. Fermi surface (FS) analysis predicts that ZrRe 2 could potentially host a charge density wave (CDW) phase. The electronic and optical studies confirmed its metallic nature. The estimated Pugh’s ratio, Poisson’s ratio, and machinability index indicate that the compound remains ductile and exhibits excellent machinability within the studied pressure range. The Debye temperature and phonon thermal conductivity are moderate, while the melting point is relatively high. Furthermore, ZrRe 2 possesses moderate electron-phonon coupling, which weakens under pressure as the phonon modes harden. Consequently, the superconducting transition temperature decreases with increasing pressure. The compound also shows potential as a promising TBC (thermal barrier coating) material. Most of the properties studied and analyses performed in this paper are novel in nature.

Article.Title: A global–local momentum contrastive framework with critical feature calibration for field plant disease identification in precision agriculture
Article.Authors: Pan R.; Yang Q.; Qin S.; Chen S.; Yang C.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Plant diseases can substantially affect crop production and food supply stability, making accurate disease identification important for effective crop management. Although deep learning has been widely applied to plant disease recognition, model performance may degrade in complex field environments because of large intra-class variations, subtle inter-class differences, and background interference. To address these challenges, we propose GLC-Net, which integrates global–local momentum contrastive learning with critical feature calibration (CFC) for field plant disease identification. Specifically, a label-guided momentum contrastive learning mechanism is introduced to dynamically construct multiple positive pairs through a labeled queue, thereby promoting intra-class compactness and inter-class separability in the feature space. In addition, a global–local contrastive strategy based on cropped local views is designed to enhance multi-scale representation learning, enabling the model to capture both global contextual information and fine-grained pathological details. Furthermore, the proposed CFC module calibrates global representations using complementary local features, allowing the network to preserve more disease-relevant information under complex background conditions. Experiments on the Paddy and Soybean disease datasets demonstrate that GLC-Net consistently improves recognition performance across different backbone networks and compares favorably with representative existing methods. Ablation and visualization analyses further verify the contributions of the proposed components to feature discrimination and disease-region representation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of GLC-Net for field plant disease identification, while further evaluation across additional crop species and more diverse field conditions remains necessary to establish its broader generalization capability.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: momentum contrastive learning; plant disease detection; feature calibration; precision agriculture; plant image classification
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Smart Agriculture and AI; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Domain Adaptation and Few-Shot Learning

Article.Title: Comparison studies between Cesium-137 and X-ray irradiators in epithelial injury using in vitro and in vivo models
Article.Authors: Lakha R.; Orzechowska-Licari E.; Kesavan S.; Wu Z.; Rotoli M.; Giarrizzo M.; Liao Y.; Yang V.; Bialkowska A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Radiation-induced intestinal injury is a widely used model for studying mechanisms regulating tissue injury and regeneration. Traditionally, Cesium ( 137 Cs) radiation has been used in research applications, but over the past decade, X-ray irradiation has become increasingly favored due to its improved safety and non-radioactive profile. Since each type of radiation has distinct physical characteristics that drive its performance, we sought to systematically compare the effects of the X-ray and 137 Cs irradiators on intestinal epithelial injury and regeneration. Using established in vitro models, including colorectal cancer cell lines such as HCT116, RKO, and DLD-1, and mouse intestinal organoids, alongside an in vivo model, Bmi1-CreER ; Rosa26eYFP , we evaluated differences in transcriptional, protein, and histopathological responses to irradiation. Our results demonstrate that X-ray produced intestinal injury and regenerative responses comparable to those induced by 137 Cs, supporting its reliability as an alternative modality for studying intestinal radiation.

Article.Title: Nonlinear settlement prediction theory for CEP piles considering the effect of the consolidated body
Article.Authors: Wang W.; Liu S.; Wang X.; Liu L.; Gao Y.; Wang H.; Pan Z.; Han D.
Article.Abstract: A key construction feature of the Consolidated Expanded-Plate (CEP) pile is that the plate section is formed within a pre-consolidated soil mass, thereby eliminating the risk of borehole collapse associated with conventional squeezed branch piles. However, existing settlement prediction models for uniform-diameter and squeezed-branch piles generally neglect the influence of the consolidated body, leading to significant errors in settlement prediction. Accordingly, a nonlinear settlement prediction theory for CEP piles is developed based on the load-transfer method. The proposed model explicitly incorporates the shaft resistance contributions of both the consolidated transition section and the plate section, and is solved using a displacement-based iterative algorithm implemented in MATLAB. An orthogonal experimental design and sensitivity analysis are conducted to quantify the contributions of pile diameter, plate diameter, and six empirical parameters to the ultimate settlement, while investigating their effects on the load-settlement response. The results indicate that the plate diameter is the dominant factor governing the ultimate pile-head settlement, with a contribution rate of 45.68%. The consolidation amplification factors for the friction angle, cohesion, and elastic/shear modulus rank next, each contributing approximately 9–15%, whereas the remaining parameters have a combined contribution of less than 10%. Comparisons with field static load test results demonstrate excellent agreement between the predicted and measured responses. Under high loading levels, the average prediction error for pile axial force remains below 5%, while the maximum relative errors for plate resistance and pile tip resistance are less than 7%. The proposed method provides a reliable analytical framework for predicting the settlement behaviour of CEP piles and offers a practical basis for calibrating parameters and optimising design under similar geological conditions.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: pile-soil interaction; soil consolidation

Article.Title: Explainable plant disease classification and severity assessment using MobileNetV3-large for crop health monitoring
Article.Authors: Gaur K.; Mittal R.; Chowdhury B.; Raj R.; Wani N.; Kumar P.
Article.Abstract: Plant pests and diseases are estimated to cause losses of up to 40% of global crop production, while plant diseases alone are associated with economic losses exceeding US$220 billion annually 1 . Although deep learning-based plant disease classification methods have achieved high accuracy on benchmark datasets, many existing systems focus primarily on disease identification and provide limited information regarding visual explanation and disease burden. In this study, an integrated framework for plant disease classification, visual explanation, and severity estimation is developed using a MobileNetV3-Large backbone on a 38-class PlantVillage-derived benchmark. A three-phase progressive transfer-learning strategy is employed, combining Focal Loss with label smoothing, automated class-balanced weighting, AdamW optimization, and cosine-annealing learning-rate scheduling with linear warm-up. Grad-CAM++ is incorporated to provide spatially localized visual explanations of disease predictions, particularly for images containing multiple symptomatic regions. In addition, an EPPO-informed three-tier operational severity scheme is implemented using HSV-derived pseudo-labels to estimate visible disease burden. On the 38-class PlantVillage-derived benchmark, the proposed framework achieved 98.50% test accuracy, with a macro-F1 score of 0.984 and macro-precision of 0.985, demonstrating competitive classification performance rather than state-of-the-art accuracy. Across five independent random seeds, where applicable, classification performance was 98.49 ± 0.12% accuracy and 98.43 ± 0.12% macro-F1. The severity module achieved 89.1% agreement with the HSV-derived pseudo-labels in the original experiment. These severity results should be interpreted as agreement with an automated reference rather than independent validation against expert agronomic annotations. The proposed framework integrates classification, confidence estimation, visual explanation, and operational severity estimation into a unified inference pipeline, while recognizing the limitations of controlled PlantVillage-derived imagery and the need for future validation on independently collected field data.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: plant disease classification; disease severity assessment; crop health monitoring; MobileNetV3; explainable AI

Article.Title: Magnitude of tracheal stenosis and contributing factors among adult intubated patients in intensive care units in Northern Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Alemu G.; Asfaha F.; Meles G.; Abreha G.; Abraha T.; Lema G.
Article.Abstract: Tracheal stenosis is a potentially life-threatening complication of endotracheal intubation associated with significant morbidities. However, its burden is not well studied in developing countries. This study aimed to assess the frequency of clinically detected tracheal stenosis and its associated factors among adult patients who underwent intubation in ICUs in Northern Ethiopia. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted using retrospective chart review of adult intubated patients between September 01 and August 30, 2022, at Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital (ACSH), Ethiopia. Of the total 376 intubated patients admitted to surgical and medical ICUs, 151 were included in the study. Diagnosis of tracheal stenosis was based on clinically bronchoscopic findings, and no systematic screening protocol was applied. Data were extracted from the patients’ medical charts. Bivariate and multivariable Firth logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with tracheal stenosis. Possible effects of confounders were controlled during regression analysis, and a p -value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant for predictors. A total of 151 intubated patients were included in the analysis. The most common admission diagnosis was trauma (51.7%). Thirteen patients (8.6%) were diagnosed with tracheal stenosis based the documented bronchoscopic findings. The majority of patients admitted to the the adult ICUs were transferred to the wards 93 (61.6%), while 54 patients (35.8%) died. Multiple intubations were observed in 10.6% of patients. Patient age, admission diagnosis, presence of tracheostomy, multiple intubations, and prolonged intubation were associated with the development of tracheal stenosis. In the multivariable analysis, prolonged intubation was the only factor that remained statistically significant. Patients with prolonged intubation periods had seven times higher odds of developing tracheal stenosis independently. The frequency of clinically detected of tracheal stenosis among adult ICU patients was high, occurring in approximately one out of every twelve patients. A prolonged intubation was associated with tracheal stenosis. Improving the quality of care for intubated patients is essential to reduce the burden of tracheal stenosis and its associated adverse outcomes.

Article.Title: Targeting REV7 confers cervical cancer cell radiosensitivity and ferroptosis by negatively regulating SFXN1
Article.Authors: Huang X.; Feng Y.; Yang Y.; Cui H.; Yun Y.; Fang M.; Luo J.; Lu X.
Article.Abstract: Cervical cancer is the 4th most common malignancy in women. Radiotherapy (RT) plays an essential role in cervical cancer treatments, and this study reports the role of REV7 in cervical cancer RT. Results showed that loss of REV7 contributed to increased the radiosensitivity of cervical cancer both in vitro and in vivo. Further molecular biology experiments demonstrated REV7-silence enhanced apoptosis, aggravated radiation-induced ROS, and accelerated ferroptosis after RT. Mass spectrometry was used to explore the candidate substrates of REV7 involved in the regulation of cervical cancer cell radiosensitivity. Mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation confirmed that SFXN1 is a candidate substrate for REV7. The expression of SFXN1 was negatively regulated by REV7 in HeLa cells. Consistently, REV7 deficiency aggravated ferroptosis by increasing SFXN1. Our findings revealed that REV7 conferred radioresistance of cervical cancer cell by downregulating SFXN1 expression. Moreover, REV7 physically interacts with SFXN1 and negatively regulates its expression through an ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation pathway. In conclusion, REV7 depletion induce ferroptosis and enhance the radiosensitivity of cervical cancer cells in an SFXN1-dependent manner, indicating that targeting REV7 is a plausible candidate that possesses potential for the radiosensitization of cervical cancer.

Article.Title: PredKlebAMR: A machine learning framework prioritizing sensitivity in Klebsiella pneumoniae resistance profiling
Article.Authors: Babajide A.; Mordecai J.; Gyasi K.; Garba J.; Sougue S.; Awe O.
Article.Abstract: The global increase in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) has undoubtedly changed the management of infectious diseases. Meropenem resistance in K. pneumoniae is a response to bacterial strategies, these includes production of carbapenemases (KPC, NDM, OXA-48), a reduction in membrane permeability through mutation of porin (OmpK35/36), and genomic plasticity via gene amplification and/or plasmid exchange. This study developed a machine learning model that targets “Very Major Errors” (VMEs) and predicts antimicrobial resistance (AMR) for prognosis. Genomic datasets (6000) were retrieved from the Bacterial and Viral Bioinformatics Resource Center (BV-BRC) database and preprocessed. Gene-based feature engineering was performed using Kleborate, and a Random Forest model was trained and deployed via an interactive R Shiny web application. Internal validation of the tool PredKlebAMR was done using a stratified 80/20 split of the training dataset, and a 5-fold cross-validation was implemented to optimize the Random Forest hyperparameters. While benchmarking against ResFinder 4.1 and AMRFinderPlus 4.2.7 was done using an independent external cohort consisting of three-tiered datasets from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) database. PredKlebAMR , trained using 5,942 K. pneumoniae genomes (38 Kleborate-derived predictors), achieved a strong performance on a held-out global test set (accuracy 91.92%, sensitivity 94.67%, specificity 89.47%; Kappa 0.839), with key predictors including fluoroquinolone mutations, high-risk sequence types, KPC-2/KPC-3, and OmpK35/36 porin changes. When benchmarked against AMRFinderPlus 4.2.7 and ResFinder 4.1, PredKlebAMR delivered a higher sensitivity and fewer VMEs in the global cohort (95.45% vs 90.91% | 86.36% sensitivity; VMEs 1 vs 2 | 3), the African cohort (95.56% vs 91.11% | 82.2% sensitivity; VMEs 2 vs 4 | 8), and the Thailand cohort (95.62% vs 92.5% | 63.12% sensitivity; VMEs 7 vs 12 | 59) with statistically significant sensitivity improvement in Africa (McNemar’s p = 0.041). PredKlebAMR, with its high sensitivity to VMEs, and via an interactive dashboard ( https://igmr.org/software/predklebamr ) that translates predictions into biological rationale, will support clinicians in making life-changing decisions while managing patients.

Article.Title: Cross-modal attention fusion of ultrasound imaging and clinical tabular data for breast lesion classification: A multimodal deep learning framework
Article.Authors: Akula R.; Rakesh K.; Vimala N.; Parvez S.; Mehanoor S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate classification of breast lesions in ultrasound images is an important yet challenging task, plagued by visual ambiguity between classes and morphological variability within classes. This paper presents a multimodal deep learning framework combining EfficientNet-B4 visual features with an 11-dimensional, leakage-free clinical tabular feature vector, organized into three feature-group tokens (intensity, texture, and geometry), through a multi-token cross-modal attention fusion mechanism. A systematic audit of candidate tabular features identified that eight commonly used lesion-shape descriptors (area, width, height, aspect ratio, solidity, eccentricity, and mask-region intensity statistics) are only defined when a segmentation mask exists, and their availability, not merely their value, correlates with class label; these features are excluded from the tabular branch, retaining only whole-image intensity and texture statistics defined identically for every image. On the BUSI breast ultrasound dataset (780 samples: 437 benign, 210 malignant, 133 normal) evaluated by five-fold stratified cross-validation, the tabular-only ablation using this leakage-free feature set achieves 66.72% macro AUC and 51.28% accuracy, well below both the image-only ablation (86.92% AUC) and every multimodal fusion configuration tested, indicating limited independent diagnostic signal in the retained tabular features alone. The proposed multi-token cross-modal attention mechanism achieves 95.46% macro AUC and 88.59% accuracy, comparable to, but not exceeding, a plain concatenation baseline (96.28% AUC) and two of three additional fusion strategies evaluated (additive fusion, 96.00%; bilinear fusion, 95.82%). All differences among the fusion strategies tested fall within approximately one fold-to-fold standard deviation of one another, indicating no statistically meaningful separation on this dataset at this sample size. We report the tabular-feature leakage audit as the primary methodological contribution of this study, applicable to multimodal medical imaging pipelines more broadly, and report the fusion-strategy comparison directly rather than selectively emphasizing the proposed attention mechanism.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: breast lesion classification; cross-modal attention; breast ultrasound; multimodal fusion; EfficientNet-B4; BUSI dataset; texture features; feature leakage
