Article.Title: Electronic structure, NBO, and radical stability analyses of thymol and carvacrol along metabolic transformation pathways: a DFT study
Article.Authors: Faal M.; Mehrafarin A.; Naghdi Badi H.; Asadi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the proposed reaction mechanisms and radical stabilization processes leading to the formation of the two bioactive monoterpenes, thymol and carvacrol, remains challenging because of complex reaction networks, tautomeric interconversions, and electron delocalization effects. In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed at the B3LYP/6-311 + G(d) level using Gaussian 09 software. Ten proposed reaction pathways and twenty transition states were identified and analyzed, including key tautomeric transformations and intermediate rearrangements. Activation energies and Gibbs free energies were evaluated to assess the feasibility of the proposed reaction routes. To gain deeper mechanistic insight, molecular electrostatic potential (MEP), Natural Bond Orbital (NBO), and spin density analyses were performed for selected intermediates, transition states, and radical species. MEP analysis revealed notable changes in charge distribution during tautomeric interconversions, while NBO analysis indicated strong donor–acceptor interactions and extensive π-electron delocalization within the aromatic framework. Spin density analysis confirmed resonance-assisted delocalization of the unpaired electron following hydrogen abstraction, supporting the stabilization of the corresponding phenoxy radicals. Comparative analysis revealed slightly greater electronic delocalization in thymol than in carvacrol. Overall, the present computational results provide molecular-level insight into the proposed reaction mechanisms, electronic structure evolution, and radical stabilization behavior associated with the formation of thymol and carvacrol.

Article.Title: TrustAdaptRL: an online reinforcement learning framework for attack-resilient trust management in Fog-IoT networks
Article.Authors: .B P.; Venkatesh K.
Article.Abstract: Fog-empowered IoT networks (Fog-IoT) can support latency-sensitive, large-scale applications; however, they remain susceptible to adaptive trust attacks such as collusion, on–off, and grayhole attacks, while still requiring reliable QoS. Available trust-management schemes often use static weighting or rely on short-lived uncertain information from probabilistic or anomaly-detector-based analysis, and thus suffer from limited adaptivity to changing adversarial behaviours, ineffective security–performance management, and low scalability or poor understanding. This study aims to overcome these limitations by introducing an online reinforcement-learning framework, TrustAdaptRL, to enable attack-resilient trust management in Fog-IoT (F-IoT) networks. Behavioural, contextual, temporal, security, and cross-neighbour observations are used as inputs to formulate the long-term trust-updating decision process. An attack-aware reward function explicitly rewards grayhole, on–off, and collusive behaviours while maintaining packet-delivery and delay performance.The inference is finished at the IoT devices, while the replay-buffer management, model optimisation, and policy update are executed at the fog nodes. Evaluation is based on a public-traffic-driven simulation using realistic traffic and security attributes created in cooperation with TON_IoT, BoT-IoT, and IoT-23, as well as syntactic topology, trust labels, and attacks based on specific routes. TrustAdaptRL achieves 93.7% trust accuracy, surpassing the highest baseline by 4.3% points. The benefit of grayhole, on–off, and collusion detection increases by 6.4%, 13.8%, and 15.3%, respectively, and the packet delivery ratio is 95.1%. Cross-cluster transfer, statistical testing, and explainability analysis results further demonstrate stable, interpretable, and scalable transfer of trust within dynamic Fog-IoT environments. The complete TrustAdaptRL implementation and reproducibility materials are publicly available at: https://github.com/Pallavi-1981/TrustAdaptRL .

Article.Title: Efficacy of sound therapy in chronic tinnitus patients with mild hearing loss: a multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial
Article.Authors: Fournier P.; Thai-Van H.; Reynard P.; Gallego S.; Liegeon F.; Weckel A.; Viudez P.; Loche V.; Lépingle O.; Holler-Houdoux C.; Villatte V.; Bonnard D.; Rio M.; Kossowski M.; Londero A.; Bischoff H.; Essebag C.; Noreña A.; Estève-Fraysse M.
Article.Abstract: Chronic tinnitus affects 10–15% of the population and can substantially impair quality of life. Sound therapies, including amplification and sound generators, are commonly used, but evidence from placebo-controlled trials remains limited. This multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial evaluated the efficacy of sound therapy in adults with chronic bilateral tinnitus and mild hearing loss. Participants with tinnitus (THI ≥ 38) and mild bilateral hearing loss (PTA < 35 dB HL at 0.5–4 kHz) were randomized (1:1:1) to receive placebo amplification, sound generators, or sound generators combined with amplification. The intervention lasted 12 weeks and included a 6-week monotherapy phase followed by a 6-week polytherapy phase, during which participants in the active arms could switch between amplification, sound generators, or a combined approach. The primary outcome, change in Tinnitus Functional Index (TFI) score, improved significantly in the active treatment arms compared with placebo (mean change: -21 and − 18 vs. -6; p < .001). Clinically meaningful improvement on the Global Rating of Change Scale was reported by 88% of participants in the sound generator group, 77% in the combined therapy group, and 33% in the placebo group ( p < .001). These findings support sound therapy as an effective intervention for chronic tinnitus in individuals with mild hearing loss.

Article.Title: A reliability-guided RGB-IR object detection network with complementary information decoupling for autonomous driving
Article.Authors: Yang M.; Guo F.; Cheng L.; Fang P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autonomous driving systems require robust object detection under complex open-road conditions, where RGB images are sensitive to illumination changes and background interference, while infrared images may suffer from weak textures and unreliable thermal responses. To improve RGB-IR detection performance, this paper proposes a Feature-level Scale-aware Multispectral Fusion Network, termed FSMF, for autonomous driving scenarios. The network consists of three key components. First, a Reliability-Guided Modulation module estimates RGB and IR feature reliability from channel, spatial, and cross-modal perspectives, and adaptively adjusts their contributions before fusion. Second, a Complementary Information Decoupling module separates shared semantics, complementary differences, and redundant interference, thereby enhancing target-related cross-modal cues while suppressing ineffective responses. Third, a Scale-Aware Fusion Pyramid Network performs differentiated enhancement for shallow, middle, and deep features to improve multi-scale feature representation. Experiments on M3FD and FLIR demonstrate the effectiveness of FSMF. The proposed FSMF-s achieves 85.9% mAP@50 on M3FD, and 72.2% mAP@50 and 38.3% mAP@50:95 on FLIR, outperforming mainstream detectors and existing RGB-IR methods. Ablation results further verify the effectiveness of the proposed modules.

Article.Title: Highly active and stable functionalized MOF-based heterogeneous catalyst (Zn-MOF-Gly-Cef@Pd) for the Suzuki and Sonogashira reactions
Article.Authors: Mazini F.; Alinezhad H.; Tajbakhsh M.; Baharfar R.
Article.Abstract: A novel metal–organic framework-based nanocatalyst named Zn-MOF-Gly-Cef@Pd was synthesized by modifying Zn-MOF (TMU-17-NH 2 ) with glyoxal (Gly) and cephalexin (Cef) and palladium nanoparticles (Pd NPs), and its catalytic characteristics for Suzuki and the Sonogashira coupling reactions were examined. Prior to incorporating the Zn-MOF-Gly-Cef@Pd catalyst in the Suzuki and Sonogashira reactions, its structural features were comprehensively characterized using a series of analytical techniques and approved accordingly. The results confirmed that the Zn-MOF-Gly-Cef@Pd demonstrated good catalytic efficiency in the synthesis of biphenyl derivatives from the reaction between phenylboronic acid and iodobenzene in EtOH under reflux conditions and the synthesis of diphenylacetylene derivatives from the reaction between phenylacetylene and iodobenzene in EtOH under reflux conditions. It is noteworthy that the functionalization of the Zn-MOF structure with the electron-rich ligand of cephalexin notably increased the loading capacity and stability of Pd nanoparticles, which could be due to the strong interaction between the metal species and the substrate of the catalyst. Short reaction time, highly efficient activity, stability, and excellent reusability up to 6 consecutive cycles are some of the extraordinary advantages of the present protocol.

Article.Title: Alkaloidal constituents of Crinum asiaticum L., toxicology and in silico studies against some piercing-sucking pests
Article.Authors: El‑Rokh A.; Suliman A.; Elaraby A.; Ibrahim T.; Darwish A.; El-Salam S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Many important crops around the world have been severely damaged by piercing-sucking pests. These pests can be managed with botanical pesticides. A major alkaloid, hippeastrine- N -oxide 3 , was isolated from the Crinum asiaticum alkaloid fraction. In addition, four known compounds, 11-hydroxyvittatine- N -oxide 1 , lycoramine- N -oxide 2 , lycorine 4 , and vittatine 5 , were identified by LC-MS/MS. 1 H NMR and ESI-MS spectroscopy were used to identify the structure of the isolated compound. Pesticidal activity of the alkaloid fraction and hippeastrine N -oxide was tested against four piercing-sucking pests along with azadirachtin as a positive control under laboratory conditions. Hippeastrine- N -oxide showed high toxicity against four pests, especially Aphis craccivora , compared to the control, with LC 50 values of 16.00 and 26.90 mg/L, respectively. The LC 50 value of hippeastrine- N -oxide was used to evaluate the biochemical characteristics of six Aphis craccivora enzymes. Molecular docking and fingerprint analysis of the lead compound revealed strong binding interactions with key amino acid residues in the target enzymes, further validating the experimental findings. These computational results make it possible to understand the mechanism of action observed in the laboratory assays. These findings indicate that the C. asiaticum alkaloid fraction, and hippeastrine N ‑oxide in particular, exhibit insecticidal activity against the piercing‑sucking pests tested under laboratory conditions, supporting further evaluation of their potential as botanical pest-control agents.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning maps the efficiency-NOx trade-off of a hydrogen dual-fuel engine fuelled with a diesel–Mahua methyl ester-pine oil blend
Article.Authors: Elumalai P.; Subramonian S.; Yee S.; Kadirgama K.; Poungthong P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-enriched dual-fuel combustion offers a route to decarbonising compression-ignition (CI) engines, but its interaction with oxygenated ternary fuels remains poorly quantified. This study evaluates a Span 80-stabilised diesel-Mahua methyl ester (MME)-pine oil (PO) blend on a Kirloskar TV1 CI engine (5.2 kW, 1500 rpm, compression ratio 17.5:1). Twenty operating points for D70 + MME15 + PO15 were measured across five loads (20–100%) and four hydrogen rates (0, 5, 10 and 15 L min −1 , equivalent to a 0–15.4% hydrogen energy share at full load); the remaining sixty points of the design (D100, D80 + MME10 + PO10, D60 + MME20 + PO20) were generated with a calibrated zero-dimensional thermodynamic model and are identified as model-predicted throughout. Raising hydrogen from 0 to 15 L min −1 at full load increased brake thermal efficiency (BTE) by 5.6–8.0% and reduced CO by 59.1–63.0%, HC by 59.3–61.5% and smoke by 20.7–26.3%, while NOx rose by 15.0–21.4%; the highest BTE observed was 31.74%. A Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) outperformed XGBoost and an artificial neural network under five-fold cross-validation (mean R 2 = 0.9913). SHAP attribution identified engine load as the dominant driver of BTE (65.7%) and NOx (69.6%), and hydrogen induction as the dominant driver of CO (75.4%) and HC (54.7%), while conformal prediction supplied calibrated 95% intervals. NSGA-II optimisation of the KAN surrogate returned a 118-point Pareto front: an efficiency-priority solution retained 99.4% of the maximum BTE while lowering NOx by 7.4% and smoke by 10.4%, and a balanced solution traded 11.2% of BTE for a 40.9% NOx reduction. All optimisation results are surrogate predictions reported with calibrated 95% intervals and await experimental confirmation.

Article.Title: Exploring biomarkers related to branched-chain amino acid metabolism in childhood obesity based on transcriptomics and experimental verification
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Lei Y.; Guan L.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Childhood obesity (CO) is a complex chronic disease driven by environmental, behavioral, and genetic factors. Dysregulation of branched-chain amino acid metabolism (BCAAM) contributes to CO development, highlighting the need to identify reliable biomarkers for diagnosis and treatment. Biomarkers associated with BCAAM remain largely unexplored in pediatric populations. In this study, we used BCAAM-focused co‑expression network analysis with machine learning to identify biomarkers and construct a diagnostic nomogram for CO using transcriptomic data from blood and adipose tissue. Multidimensional analyses, including functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and drug prediction, were subsequently performed. Three putative biomarkers, PLEK, NIN, and COX1, were identified, and the resulting nomogram exhibited good predictive performance. These biomarkers showed strong transcriptional association with mitochondrial respiration pathways and immune cell infiltration signatures, suggesting mitochondria–immune crosstalk. We also predicted multiple candidate drugs that target these biomarkers, with quercetin among the top candidates. Validation of their expression by RT‑qPCR in clinical blood samples confirmed significant dysregulation of PLEK and COX1, which supports their potential as biomarker candidates. These results indicate that PLEK, NIN, and COX1 are candidate BCAAM-associated transcriptomic markers for CO. The nomogram shows promising diagnostic potential in retrospective datasets; however, its clinical utility and the underlying mechanistic framework require further study.

Article.Title: A randomized double-blind non-inferiority trial comparing LUCENTRA with DYSPORT for moderate-to-severe glabellar line improvement
Article.Authors: Kafi H.; Samadi A.; Zartab H.; Nassiri Kashani M.; Ayatollahi A.; Yazdanparast T.; Ahmad Nasrollahi S.; Sabzvari A.; Firooz A.
Article.Abstract: Botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) formulations are widely used for the treatment of glabellar lines, with DYSPORT being a well-established option; however, its high cost limits accessibility. LUCENTRA, a newly developed BoNT-A, may offer a more affordable alternative. This phase III, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled non-inferiority clinical trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of LUCENTRA compared with DYSPORT in participants with moderate to severe glabellar lines. Participants received 40–60 units of intramuscular injections of either formulation, and the primary endpoint was the proportion of responders at day 30, defined as a ≥ 2-grade improvement on the glabellar line severity score at maximum frown. Secondary endpoints included onset of action at maximum frown, response rates based on the glabellar line severity scale, and subject self-assessment at maximum frown and rest, and safety was assessed on days 14, 30, 90, and 120. A total of 146 participants were enrolled (73 per arm). LUCENTRA was non-inferior to DYSPORT, with responder rates of 69% and 60.8%, respectively (95% CI: − 7.0 to 24.7%). Median onset was four days for LUCENTRA and five days for DYSPORT. Adverse events, mainly mild headaches and injection site discomfort, were comparable, and no serious events occurred. LUCENTRA is non-inferior to DYSPORT in terms of improving glabellar lines at day 30 post-injection, supporting its efficacy as an alternative option of DYSPORT. Adverse events were also comparable between the two groups suggesting safety and tolerability of DYSPORT and LUCENTRA.

Article.Title: Dye-affinity functionalized magnetic nanoparticles enable direct immobilization of cellulase from cell-free microbial culture medium
Article.Authors: Hadadi M.; Habibi A.
Article.Abstract: Enzyme recovery and purification remain major challenges for the economical application of enzymes. In this study, one-step separation and immobilization of cellulase from fermentation medium of Trichoderma reesei was investigated using dye-affinity-functionalized Fe₃O₄ magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs), with multi-covalent coupling proposed as a possible immobilization mechanism. This approach achieved a selective enzyme immobilization with a loading capacity of 70.29 ± 0.99 mg Protein g Support −1 and immobilization yield of 33.16 ± 0.83%. Evaluations of the catalytic activities of the immobilized biocatalyst showed the endoglucanase, exoglucanase, and β -glucosidase activities of about 143.3, 62.9, and 63.1% in comparison with the original free cellulase, respectively. The immobilized cellulase was stable in repeated saccharification cycles of carboxymethylcellulose and sustained 70.12% of the original activity after six cycles. Also, the immobilized biocatalysts retained 100% activity after being stored at 4 °C for 180 days. Further evaluation of the immobilized biocatalyst was performed on the hydrolysis of paper waste at different initial concentrations. The Michaelis-Menten model with observable constants of K m = 4.142 ± 0.700 mg mL − 1 and V max = 0.043 ± 0.003 µmol Glucose mg Protein −1 h − 1 well-described this hydrolysis reaction. Therefore, the developed biocatalyst shows promising potential for the enzymatic conversion of paper waste into value-added products.

Article.Title: Fecal microbiome dynamics across reproductive stages in primiparous Świniarka sheep: a longitudinal study
Article.Authors: Cholewinska P.; Wojnarowski K.; Nazar P.; Greguła-Kania M.; Junkuszew A.; Rant W.; Radzik-Rant A.; Szeligowska N.; Bodkowski R.
Article.Abstract: Reproductive transitions in ruminants are accompanied by substantial endocrine and metabolic changes that may be associated with alterations in gut microbial communities. However, temporal variation in the fecal microbiome across reproductive stages in primitive sheep breeds remains poorly characterized. This longitudinal study aimed to characterize temporal patterns in the fecal microbiome in primiparous Świniarka sheep across three reproductive stages: mating (T1), lambing (T2), and the end of lactation (T3), using 16 S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Alpha diversity did not differ significantly between stages, although several indices showed numerically higher values at T2 and T3; these differences did not reach statistical significance in repeated-measures analyses. Beta diversity analyses based on Bray–Curtis, weighted UniFrac, and unweighted UniFrac distances showed overlapping community profiles, with no significant stage-associated differences after accounting for repeated measurements within animals (PERMANOVA, P > 0.05). The fecal microbiome was dominated by Firmicutes and Bacteroidota across all reproductive stages. Core microbiome analysis identified 28 genera present at a relative abundance of at least 0.1% in at least 80% of samples, together accounting for an average of 83.45% of the microbial community. PICRUSt2 identified 329 predicted MetaCyc pathways, none of which differed significantly among reproductive stages after false-discovery-rate correction. DESeq2 identified stage-associated differences in selected genus-level taxonomic features, with 14 significant features between T2 and T1, 13 between T3 and T1, and four between T3 and T2. Within this exploratory longitudinal cohort, reproductive stage was not associated with statistically detectable differences in alpha diversity, overall microbial community structure, or predicted functional pathway profiles genus-level abundance after correction for multiple testing. However, differential-abundance analysis identified stage-associated changes in selected genus-level. Dominant taxonomic features, particularly in comparisons of T2 profiles and T3 with T1. A high-abundance shared microbial core was observed across all stages, indicating limited global restructuring of the fecal microbiome detectable temporal variation under the studied conditions. These findings do not establish ecological resilience or equivalence among reproductive stages.

Article.Title: Preparation of a magnetic Escherichia coli biosorbent for efficient dye removal from aqueous solutions
Article.Authors: Kazemi M.; Maleki B.; Ashrafi S.; Kargar P.
Article.Abstract: Synthetic dyes in industrial wastes are highly toxic, non-biodegradable and resistant to treatment processes and may pose serious threats to the environment and human health. Due to their high adsorption capacity, biocompatibility and easy magnetic separation, magnetic biosorbents, especially E. coli -based bio-nanocomposites, are considered promising adsorbents. However, studies on the simultaneous removal of both anionic and cationic dyes using such materials remain limited. The γ-Fe 2 O 3 @ E. coli magnetic biosorbent was successfully synthesized and characterized using various analytical techniques, including FT-IR, XRD, VSM, EDX, DLS, and FE-SEM. The effects of solution pH, initial dye concentration, biosorbent dosage, temperature and contact time were systematically investigated, with optimum conditions of pH 4, 30 °C, 20 mg/L, 0.025 g and 30 min for MO, and pH 10, 35 °C, 8 mg/L, 0.02 g and 30 min for MB, respectively. Under these conditions, the removal efficiencies were 94.90 and 95.14%, with equilibrium adsorption capacities of 9.49 and 3.81 mg/g for MO and MB, respectively. Equilibrium studies indicated that the Freundlich and Temkin isotherm models best described the experimental data, indicating heterogeneous adsorption with multilayer characteristics and non-uniform adsorption sites. The biosorbent maintained high removal efficiencies over six consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles, decreasing from 95.14 to 91.36% for MB and from 94.90 to 87.62% for MO. These results demonstrate that the γ-Fe 2 O 3 @ E. coli biosorbent combines effective dye removal with magnetic recoverability and good reusability, supporting its potential application in sustainable wastewater treatment.

Article.Title: Integrated technology acceptance model and theory of planned behavior explain anti-osteoporosis medication prescribing among Thai orthopedic surgeons after hip fracture
Article.Authors: Piyaprapaphan P.; Wannamakok W.; Chotiyarnwong P.; Sithiwichankit N.; Gerdsri N.; Vanitcharoenkul E.
Article.Abstract: A persistent care gap leaves many patients without anti-osteoporosis medications (AOMs) after hip fracture, despite their proven benefit in preventing secondary fractures. We investigated the factors associated with orthopedic surgeons’ intention to prescribe AOMs. A cross-sectional online survey of 264 Thai orthopedic surgeons involved in hip fracture care integrated the technology acceptance model and the theory of planned behavior. Partial least squares structural equation modeling assessed the measurement model’s reliability and validity and tested the hypothesized structural relationships. The integrated model accounted for 63.4% of the variance in prescribing intention. Perceived usefulness of AOMs ( β = 0.427; P < 0.001) and subjective norms ( β = 0.228; P < 0.001) predicted the surgeons’ attitude toward use. Attitude toward use was the strongest predictor of the intention to prescribe AOMs ( β = 0.622; P < 0.001). Self-efficacy did not moderate the attitude–intention relationship but was directly associated with intention ( β = 0.201; P = 0.004). These results indicate that prescribing intention is primarily predicted by perceived clinical value and professional norms rather than by procedural simplicity. Interventions to reduce the care gap should therefore emphasize clinical effectiveness, reinforce professional norms, and build surgeons’ self-efficacy through targeted education and training.

Article.Title: Comparative assessment of sexual satisfaction in Polish patients with benign thyroid disease
Article.Authors: Sawicka-Gutaj N.; Nijakowski K.; Ziółkowska P.; Trocha M.; Miśkiewicz P.; Derwich-Rudowicz A.; Ruchała M.
Article.Abstract: The study aimed to assess sex life satisfaction among Polish patients with thyroid disease. A total of 378 participants (300 women, 78 men) treated between January 2018 and December 2019 completed validated questionnaires, including ThyPRO, WHO Quality of Life, the Sexual Satisfaction Questionnaire (women), the International Index of Erectile Function-15 (men), and the Self-Esteem and Relationship (SEAR) questionnaire (men). Overall, 58.7% of women and 40.3% of men reported a negative impact of thyroid disease on their sex life, and 71.4% of women and 47.2% of menreported decreased sexual desire. Among women with autoimmune thyroid disease, 67% with hypothyroidism and 65% with hyperthyroidism reported a negative impact despite pharmacological treatment. Among women, ThyPRO Impaired Sex Life scores correlated strongly with ThyPRO overall quality-of-life scores across all diagnoses ( p < 0.001). WHO-QoL scores correlated significantly only in patients with autoimmune thyroid disease. In men with autoimmune hyperthyroidism, sexual quality of life scores correlated with ThyPRO Overall Quality of Life ( p < 0.031), all IIEF-15 domains ( p = 0.011 for erectile function; p = 0.004 for intercourse satisfaction; p = 0.004 for orgasmic function; p = 0.003 for sexual desire; p < 0.001 for overall satisfaction), and most SEAR domains ( p < 0.001 for sexual relationship; p = 0.036 for confidence; p = 0.029 for self-esteem; p = 0.001 for overall score). These findings suggest that nearly 60% of women and 40% of men with benign thyroid disorders experience deterioration in sexual well-being, even when thyroid hormone levels are within normal ranges. Women with autoimmune hypothyroidism appear to be at the highest risk for impaired sexual quality of life.

Article.Title: A biomimetic bilayered vascular graft integrating electrospun polyurethane and gelatin/elastin hydrogel achieves arterial-like compliance and enhanced endothelialization
Article.Authors: Ebrahimi F.; Solouk A.; Yousefzadeh M.; Bahrami S.; Seifalian A.
Article.Abstract: Small-diameter (< 6 mm) vascular grafts continue to face high failure rates, primarily due to thrombosis, intimal hyperplasia, and mechanical mismatch with native arteries. In this study, a biomimetic bilayered vascular graft was developed by integrating an electrospun polyurethane (EPU) nanofibrous inner layer with a gelatin/elastin (Gelastin) hydrogel outer layer to address these limitations. The bilayer architecture integrated the complementary functions of the two layers, combining the structural support of the EPU inner layer with the porous, hydrophilic, and swelling characteristics of the Gelastin hydrogel outer layer. Following cyclic tensile preconditioning, the bilayered grafts exhibited anisotropic mechanical behavior, reduced hysteresis, and improved elastic recovery compared with electrospun polyurethane alone. Among the fabricated samples, EPU/G 1 E 0.2 showed the highest elastic recovery (82.77 ± 2.54%) and compliance (10.93 ± 2.50%/100 mmHg) while maintaining high burst pressure (> 12,000 mmHg). Hemocompatibility assessment demonstrated low hemolysis ratios (< 2%), prolonged clotting times compared with commercial ePTFE ® , and limited platelet adhesion and activation on EPU. In vitro studies using human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) confirmed favorable cell attachment, spreading, and proliferation over 7 days of culture.

Article.Title: Conditional survival and dynamic prognostic nomogram for histologically defined anaplastic ganglioglioma: a SEER-based analysis
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Ni J.; Tu C.; Qian H.
Article.Abstract: Anaplastic ganglioglioma (AGG) is an extremely rare glioneuronal tumor with low incidence and heterogeneous survival patterns driven by a limited set of prognostic factors, and conditional survival has not been systematically evaluated in this entity. Patients histologically diagnosed with AGG between 2000 and 2022 were extracted from the SEER 17 registries. Age-adjusted incidence and annual percentage change (APC) were estimated by Joinpoint regression. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed with Kaplan–Meier curves and log-rank tests; 5-year conditional survival (CS) was computed at successive landmark times. Independent prognostic factors were identified by univariate and multivariate Cox regression. A CS-nomogram was constructed and evaluated by calibration plots, time-dependent ROC and C-index. Nomogram-derived risk scores were dichotomized using a cut-point selected on the basis of restricted cubic splines (RCS), and survival between strata was compared. A total of 143 AGG patients were identified, with 62 deaths during follow-up. Patients included pediatric (29.4%), AYA (38.5%), and adults ≥ 40 years (32.2%), and 64.3% were male; most tumors arose in cerebral lobes (73.4%). Age-adjusted incidence of AGG remained low throughout the study window, with crude annual rates of approximately 0.082 per 1,000,000 person-years. Five-year OS was 64.7%, while CS5 increased from 64.7% at diagnosis to 73.7% at 1 year, 82.5% at 2 years, and > 90% after 3 years. Multivariate analysis identified age ≥ 40, regional/distant stage, and multiple primary tumors as independent adverse factors. The CS nomogram showed good performance, with time-dependent AUCs > 0.75 and well-calibrated predictions, and risk stratification yielded significantly separated survival outcomes ( P < 0.001). Long-term prognosis in AGG is highly dynamic: patients who survive the first three years acquire a substantially improved residual life expectancy. A CS-based nomogram, combined with RCS-guided risk stratification, translates this dynamic information into an individualized tool for counselling and risk-adapted surveillance.

Article.Title: Quantum random access codes for image transmission
Article.Authors: ur Rehman J.; Iqbal N.; Rizvi S.; Shin H.
Article.Abstract: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) enable multiple classical bits to be encoded into fewer qubits, while allowing only a selected bit to be retrieved with probability greater than the corresponding classical limit. Here, we use $$2 \rightarrow 1$$ and $$3 \rightarrow 1$$ QRACs for simultaneous transmission of multiple binary images through a single quantum data stream. At the receiver, the measurement choice determines which encoded image is reconstructed, while the remaining image information is disturbed by the measurement process. The inherent correct-bit probabilities of these QRACs are approximately 85.4% and 78.9%, respectively. By applying median and morphological filtering to the decoded binary images, we improve the reconstruction accuracy in an image-dependent manner, reaching 99.17% for $$2 \rightarrow 1$$ QRACs and 98.36% for $$3 \rightarrow 1$$ QRACs. We also analyze the effect of depolarizing noise on reconstruction quality using accuracy, peak signal-to-noise ratio, and structural similarity index measure. These results demonstrate a selective-access framework for QRAC-based image transmission with potential applications in controlled image/video transmission.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal coordination between a sports-tourism proxy subsystem and ecological conditions in Zhejiang Province, China, 2010–2024
Article.Authors: Liu C.; Samsudin N.; Wei X.
Article.Abstract: Sports tourism is closely related to ecological conditions, spatial resources and regional tourism-service capacity. Using 11 prefecture-level cities in Zhejiang Province as the study area, this study develops an evaluation framework comprising a sports-tourism proxy subsystem and an ecological subsystem for 2010–2024. The entropy-weight method, coupling coordination degree model, Global Moran’s I and exploratory spatial-association models are used to examine temporal variation, inter-city differences and conditional spatial associations in the coupling coordination degree.The ecological subsystem generally has a higher composite score than the sports-tourism proxy subsystem. This comparison reflects the selected indicators, standardization procedure and weighting scheme and does not independently demonstrate ecological stability or insufficient resource transformation. The coupling coordination degree follows a staged pattern of “early improvement–shock-related decline–gradual recovery”: it increased overall during 2010–2019, declined during 2020–2022 and increased again during 2023–2024. The cities exhibit distinct combinations of sports-tourism-related and ecological conditions, with Hangzhou and Wenzhou generally showing relatively high coordination levels. Global Moran’s I is negative in most years, but two-sided permutation tests based on 9,999 random permutations provide no evidence of statistically significant global spatial autocorrelation during 2010–2024. To reduce mechanical overlap with the construction of the coupling coordination degree, the spatial-association analysis uses external contextual variables, including GDP per capita, total employment, public-service expenditure, total water resources and ecological-space share. The exploratory spatial-association models identify conditional relationships between these local and neighbouring-city contextual variables and the coupling coordination degree. The findings provide a basis for comparing tourism-related and ecological conditions and for informing coordinated regional planning, but the aggregate index and observational spatial models should not be interpreted as direct evidence of causal interaction, ecological-service enhancement or ecological-resource transformation.

Article.Title: Cognitive phenotypes and neuropsychological trajectories in post-COVID-19 syndrome: a 12-month follow-up study
Article.Authors: Herrera E.; Señoráns A.; Barrenechea A.; Pérez-Sánchez M.; González-Nosti M.
Article.Abstract: Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) has been associated with cognitive difficulties, particularly in attention, processing speed, memory, and executive functions, but longitudinal evidence based on comprehensive neuropsychological assessment remains limited. This study examined the one-year evolution of neuropsychological performance and cognitive phenotypes in 92 patients with PCS who had participated in a previous assessment. Pre-post changes were analysed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with false discovery rate correction. Cognitive phenotypes were characterized in the complete phenotype sample ( N = 83) using a domain-based approach derived from the IC-CoDi-COVID criteria, with two representative tests for each cognitive domain and two impairment cutoffs: ≤ -1 SD and ≤ -1.5 SD. Significant improvements were observed mainly in verbal and visual memory, matrix reasoning, inhibitory control, and action processing (fluency and naming), whereas attention and processing speed measures remained largely stable. Phenotype analyses showed a shift toward less impaired cognitive profiles at follow-up. Normal cognition increased from 65.1% to 77.1% under the ≤ -1 SD criterion and from 83.1% to 86.7% under the ≤ -1.5 SD criterion. Impaired phenotypes were primarily driven by attention/processing speed. These findings suggest partial cognitive recovery in PCS, alongside persistent domain-specific cognitive vulnerability, particularly in attention and processing speed.

Article.Title: Terrain-corrected differential GNSS gravity potential leveling method and its application to elevation determination in mountainous areas
Article.Authors: Lyu B.; Duan H.; Li S.; Yin Y.; Duan Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the difficulties in conventional elevation surveying caused by the strong topographic relief in mountainous areas and the dual constraints imposed on GNSS gravity potential leveling by the selection of the absolute gravity potential reference and local short wavelength terrain effects, a terrain corrected differential GNSS gravity potential leveling method is proposed. The proposed method takes the normal height difference between two points as the quantity to be determined and directly determines the height difference of a survey segment through a differential strategy, thereby reducing the influence of common systematic errors at the two endpoints and weakening the dependence on the absolute gravity potential reference. Considering the significant local short wavelength terrain effects in mountainous areas, a residual terrain model is constructed using a high resolution digital elevation model. The Helmert second condensation method is employed to process the terrain mass, and the residual terrain potential is calculated based on the prism–plate model. The difference in residual terrain potential between the two endpoints is then taken as the terrain correction for the survey segment to compensate for the local short wavelength terrain effects that are not adequately represented by the global gravity field model. 28 height difference segments in the reservoir area of the Cihaxia Hydropower Station in southern Qinghai Province were used for testing, with precise trigonometric leveling results adopted as the reference. The results show that, within the GNSS gravity potential leveling framework, the differential determination of height differences achieves a higher accuracy (RMS = 0.218 m) than the single point determination (RMS = 0.341 m). The terrain corrected differential GNSS gravity potential leveling method further improves the accuracy to RMS = 0.062 m, which is significantly better than that without terrain correction (RMS = 0.218 m) and substantially reduces the systematic bias of approximately − 0.22 m. The proposed method can improve the accuracy of normal height difference determination for survey segments in complex mountainous areas and provides a feasible technical approach for elevation control surveying in reservoir areas.

Article.Title: Physical simulation of roadway surrounding rock cumulative failure characteristics under dynamic loading and energy-absorbing support solutions
Article.Authors: He Y.; Li Z.; Zhang Z.; Qian R.; Fu Y.; Ma K.
Article.Abstract: Roadway surrounding rock in deep coal mines is subjected to the combined effects of static loading and dynamic disturbances, which can induce progressive deformation, crack propagation, and catastrophic instability. To investigate the progressive failure characteristics and mechanisms of roadway surrounding rock under different dynamic impact energies, a physical similarity simulation experiment based on the 21170 transportation roadway of Changcun Coal Mine in the Yima mining area, China. A physical model was established using sand, gypsum, calcium carbonate, and mica powder, with a geometric similarity ratio of 1:25. A dynamic impact loading system equipped with a 20 kg pendulum and a 1 m pendulum rod was employed, and pendulum heights of 0.1–1.1 m were used to generate different impact-energy levels. The corresponding simulated impact energy ranged from 2.42 × 10 4 to 1.31 × 10 6 J. The deformation and failure processes of the roadway surrounding rock were systematically monitored using displacement measurements, an 8-channel acoustic emission monitoring system, pressure sensors, and high-speed imaging. The results show that roadway deformation increases progressively with increasing impact energy, with the maximum roof displacement reaching 43.7 mm and the maximum displacements of the left and right sides reaching 39.4 and 19.9 mm, respectively. The failure process exhibits a distinct progressive and asymmetric evolution: initial microcracks develop in the roof, followed by intensified damage to the floor and the left side close to the impact source, and finally large roof cracks and separation develop, resulting in complete roadway instability. The AE amplitude and ringing counts increase markedly with impact energy, indicating progressive accumulation and release of damage energy. The main innovation of this study is the integrated characterization of dynamic roadway failure by combining displacement evolution, AE localization and signal characteristics, and macroscopic crack observations, thereby revealing the spatially asymmetric and progressive failure process induced by different impact energies. A soft-structure energy-absorption concept is proposed to transfer concentrated static stress and attenuate dynamic stress waves, providing a potential strategy for improving the impact resistance and stability of deep roadways.

Article.Title: Robust trajectory tracking of an underactuated ROV under compound flow disturbances using ADRC-GISMC
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Yao P.; Shen Z.; Chen J.; Yin Y.; Chen Z.; Zou C.; Chen P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Trajectory tracking of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) remains difficult when hydrodynamic coupling, plant uncertainty, actuator constraints, and spatially varying flow disturbances act simultaneously. This study presents a simulation-based evaluation of an ADRC-GISMC strategy for an underactuated ROV under an engineering-oriented compound disturbance model combining background-current and local outfall-plume components. SMC, ADRC, ADRC-SMC, and ADRC-GISMC are compared using the same full six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body plant, rank-deficient thruster-allocation layer, reference trajectory, and actuator settings. Under the tested balanced and strong conditions, ADRC-GISMC does not minimize every tracking metric; instead, it provides a metric-dependent trade-off among position tracking, attitude response, executed moment-energy demand, and allocation feasibility. This trade-off is further examined through a paired Monte Carlo analysis with 100 plant-parameter samples, actuator-constraint and measurement/sampling tests, a local one-factor-at-a-time disturbance-sensitivity analysis, a local point-of-action sensitivity study, and geometric path-following and tolerance-band diagnostics. The results support ESO-based disturbance compensation combined with global integral sliding mode as an application-level control integration for the numerical evaluation of underactuated ROV trajectory tracking under the specified conditions. Accordingly, the conclusions are restricted to the specified numerical scenarios, parameter ranges, actuator settings, and evaluation metrics.

Article.Title: Tuning structural, optical, charge storage, and electronic transport properties of graphene oxide through functional group engineering
Article.Authors: Ismail W.; Ramadan A.; El-khair F.; Elsheikh A.; Abdelfatah M.; El-Shaer A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the effect of oxidation temperature on the structural, electronic, and electrochemical properties of graphene oxide (GO) synthesized at 75, 95, and 115 °C. Increasing the oxidation temperature resulted in a reduction in crystallite size from 9.95 ± 1.24 to 8.05 ± 0.49 nm and a decrease in the interlayer spacing, accompanied by partial reorganization of the sp² carbon domains. The electrical properties were significantly improved, with enhanced carrier transport at higher oxidation temperatures. The optical band gap decreased from 4.11 to 3.69 eV, while the Urbach energy increased from 285 to 625 meV, indicating enhanced energetic disorder and band-tail formation. Electrochemical analysis revealed improved charge-transfer kinetics, with the charge-transfer resistance decreasing from 911 to 598 Ω and the relaxation time decreasing from 0.842 to 0.671 ms. The electrochemical response also showed a predominantly diffusion-controlled charge-storage contribution, while the apparent diffusion coefficient decreased from 2.094 × 10⁻⁷ to 5.792 × 10⁻⁸ cm²/s with increasing oxidation temperature. In contrast, the specific capacitance decreased from 668 to 328 F/g, which is attributed to the reduction of oxygen-containing redox-active sites and restricted ion accessibility. Despite the reduced capacitive performance, the capacitance retention improved from 84.25% to 95.84% after 6000 cycles. Overall, increasing oxidation temperature promotes electronic transport and electrochemical kinetics while reducing redox-based charge-storage capacity, demonstrating a clear trade-off between electronic conductivity, ion-transport behavior, and capacitive performance.

Article.Title: Cross-cultural modeling of body satisfaction using social media selfies and self-descriptions
Article.Authors: Qiuyang H.; Hua W.; Zhengjun C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Body satisfaction is a core component of psychological well-being and is closely intertwined with how individuals present themselves on social media. While prior research has examined body image through self-report measures or qualitative analyses of online content, it remains unclear whether body satisfaction is systematically associated with naturally occurring multimodal self-presentation behaviors, particularly across cultural contexts.In this study, we propose a cross-cultural multimodal mixed-methods framework to examine self-reported body satisfaction using social media selfies and self-descriptions. A sample of 240 participants from Western and East Asian cultural contexts provided self-reported body satisfaction measures alongside selected social media images and textual materials. Visual features were extracted using convolutional neural networks, while linguistic features were derived from multilingual transformer-based language models. These modalities were integrated through a late-fusion strategy to examine the extent to which multimodal self-presentational features were associated with self-reported body satisfaction.Results indicate that multimodal models outperform single-modality approaches in both regression and classification tasks. Moreover, feature importance and explainability analyses reveal culturally differentiated patterns of self-presentation: visual cues such as facial expression and body posture were more predictive in Western participants, whereas contextual and linguistic cues contributed more strongly among East Asian participants. Qualitative analyses of a purposively selected subset of misclassified and high-attention cases further illustrate cultural patterns in self-expression, modesty, and self-objectification strategies.Together, these findings suggest that body satisfaction is systematically associated with multimodal social media self-presentation and that cultural context plays an important role in shaping how such associations manifest online. This study illustrates the value of integrating computational modeling with qualitative interpretation to advance cross-cultural research on body image and digital mental health, while underscoring that predictive associations should not be interpreted as causal, clinical, or diagnostic evidence.

Article.Title: Nonlinear mapping of random graph properties for cryptographic S-boxes
Article.Authors: Alali A.; Jamil M.; Ali R.; Alotaibi R.; Albalawi W.
Article.Abstract: Secure communication in the digital era depends on cryptographic primitives whose nonlinearity withstands side-channel, algebraic, and emerging quantum cryptanalytic threats. Among these primitives, the substitution box (S-box) is the principal source of confusion in modern block ciphers, and constructing S-boxes that combine high nonlinearity with strong avalanche and diffusion behaviour remains an open design problem. The objective of the present study is to develop a reproducible framework for generating 8-bit S-boxes whose cryptographic profile is competitive with state-of-the-art algebraic, chaos-based, and metaheuristic constructions. The framework formalises the link between random-graph topology and S-box confusion by deriving substitution values from vertex-level graph parameters and subsequently refining them through metaheuristic optimisation. The methodology consists of two phases. In the first phase, the vertex degree, eccentricity, and clustering coefficient of a 16-vertex Erdős–Rényi random graph are combined through a nonlinear modular mapping to produce an initial bijective candidate; non-injective outputs are repaired through a deterministic greedy fill-in. In the second phase, a temperature-controlled simulated-annealing routine with an average-coordinate-nonlinearity-based acceptance criterion and a swap-based neighbourhood operator refines the candidate, preserving bijectivity while SAC, LAP, DAP, and BIC are evaluated after optimization. The evaluation is conducted by numerical simulation in MATLAB R2023a on a standard workstation, using edge probabilities \(p = 0.7\) and \(p = 0.4\) to represent dense and sparse graph regimes. The two representative S-boxes reported in detail attain average coordinate nonlinearities of 111.25 and 111.50 for \(p=0.7\) and \(p=0.4\) , both with minimum coordinate nonlinearity 110, SAC of 0.5056 and 0.5054, BIC-nonlinearity of 103.86 and 103.64, LAP of 0.1328 and 0.1406, DAP of 0.0391 and 0.0469, and maximum algebraic degree 7. To establish that these figures are typical rather than exceptional, the complete pipeline is replicated on 100 independent random graphs for each edge probability: the target \(\textrm{AvNL}\ge 110\) is reached in 100% of the runs, with final average coordinate nonlinearity \(111.13\pm 0.28\) ( \(p=0.7\) ) and \(111.14\pm 0.23\) ( \(p=0.4\) ) and a mean of about \(1.7\times 10^{4}\) annealing iterations within a budget of \(5\times 10^{4}\) . An edge-probability sweep over \(p\in [0.15,0.95]\) , a seven-way ablation of the mapping terms, and a matched-budget comparison against uniformly random permutation initialisation quantify the individual contribution of every component of the construction. These figures indicate that the proposed S-boxes are competitive with recent graph-based, chaos-based, and optimisation-based S-box designs under the reported evaluation metrics. In particular, the proposed designs show favourable average coordinate nonlinearity and SAC values, while some comparison methods remain stronger in specific criteria such as LAP, DAP, or BIC-NL.

Article.Title: Hopf bifurcations and period-doubling cascade in a two-delay predator–prey model with Holling type II response
Article.Authors: Alawfi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We investigate the dynamics of a predator–prey model with Holling type II functional response, and two ecologically distinct delays: a prey maturation delay $$\tau _1$$ acting through density-dependent self-regulation, and a predator conversion delay $$\tau _2$$ acting through delayed recruitment. After establishing well-posedness, positivity, and uniform boundedness of solutions, we perform a detailed numerical bifurcation analysis using DDE-Biftool. As $$\tau _1$$ increases, the coexistence equilibrium undergoes a sequence of Hopf bifurcations whose criticality alternates between subcritical and supercritical, with the transition organised by generalized Hopf (Bautin) bifurcations in the $$(\tau _1,\tau _2)$$ -plane. Continuation of the emerging periodic branch reveals a fold of periodic orbits that produces bistability between coexistence and large-amplitude cycles, and a complete period-doubling cascade through period-2, period-4, period-8, period-16, and period-32 orbits. The Floquet multiplier at each detected period-doubling bifurcation equals $$-1$$ to numerical accuracy, and the spacing of successive doublings yields empirical Feigenbaum ratios that converge toward the universal value $$\delta \approx 4.6692$$ . Aitken $$\Delta ^2$$ extrapolation places the accumulation point of the cascade at $$\tau _1^{\infty }\approx 18.64$$ , beyond which periodic continuation no longer resolves the dynamics and direct numerical integration is consistent with aperiodic oscillation. These results show that the combination of maturation and conversion delays in a biologically interpretable predator–prey model can generate stability switching, bistability, and a classical Feigenbaum route to complex temporal variability.

Article.Title: Elastoplastic analysis and stability investigation of water-rich mudstone roadway surrounding rock based on true triaxial loading tests
Article.Authors: Guo J.; Wang L.; Jiang C.; Wang S.; Fan H.
Article.Abstract: Due to geological constraints and engineering layout requirements, many mine roadways must be excavated in soft rock strata such as mudstone. Under the influence of groundwater, the mechanical properties of mudstone deteriorate significantly, seriously compromising roadway stability. To address this issue, true triaxial loading tests were first conducted on mudstone specimens with varying moisture contents. The results indicate that water saturation induces a transition of mudstone from brittle to ductile failure, with its strength behavior well described by the Mogi-Coulomb criterion. On this basis, an elastoplastic analysis model was developed by comprehensively considering the effects of moisture content and the dilatancy characteristics of the surrounding rock, with particular emphasis on the plastic flow characteristics and the Mogi-Coulomb strength criterion of water-rich mudstone. The approximate analytical solutions were derived for the displacement, failure zone radius, and plastic zone radius of the surrounding rock in a water-rich mudstone roadway under a non-uniform stress field. The parametric analysis based on an engineering case indicates that a higher moisture content markedly promotes surrounding rock deformation and the expansion of both the plastic and failure zones; variations in the lateral pressure coefficient alter the distribution patterns of deformation and failure zones at the roadway roof and sidewall, with roof conditions deteriorating as the coefficient increases and the sidewall conditions showing an opposite trend; in addition, enhanced support pressure can suppress overall roadway deformation and the development of failure zones to a certain extent. This study can provide a theoretical reference for the stability assessment and support design of similar water-rich mudstone roadways under comparable geological conditions.

Article.Title: Prognostic role of the naples prognostic score in advanced gastric cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a retrospective multicenter study
Article.Authors: Tang W.; Ma L.; Fu Z.; Li F.; Zhou S.; Chen J.; Li C.; Xu X.; Zheng H.; Fu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), such as by programmed death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors, combined with chemotherapy have been established as a new first-line standard of care for patients with advanced gastric cancer (AGC), significantly prolonging survival in some patients. However, the overall benefit remains markedly heterogeneous, and prognostic assessment tools that can integrate multidimensional clinical and laboratory indicators to accurately quantify individual survival risk are lacking. Therefore, systematically analyzing the survival characteristics and independent prognostic factors of patients with AGC, and constructing a stable and reliable prognostic prediction model are important for achieving individualized treatment decisions and precise risk stratification. In this retrospective study, 252 patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative AGC who received ICIs across three institutions were included. We investigated the associations between various clinical factors, including the Naples Prognostic Score (NPS), and overall survival (OS). On the basis of the predictors identified through multivariate analysis, we developed a prognostic model and evaluated its predictive performance using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and calibration curves. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was subsequently performed to assess the clinical utility of the prognostic model. The cohort had a median OS of 15.0 months (95% CI: 13.7–17.0), a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 8.5 months (95% CI: 7.2–10.0), and an objective response rate (ORR) of 36.1%. Univariate Cox regression revealed sex, performance status (PS), Lauren classification, Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS2002) score, NPS, PD-L1 expression, number of metastatic organs, and ascites as significant prognostic factors. Variables with P < 0.05 and clinically relevant factors were subjected to least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, which included PS, Lauren classification, NPS, PD-L1 expression, and the number of metastatic organs. Multivariate Cox analysis revealed that these five factors remained independent predictors of OS (PS: HR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.27–3.20, P = 0.003; Lauren classification: HR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.03–2.38, P = 0.037; NPS: HR = 3.72, 95% CI: 1.48–9.34, P = 0.005; PD-L1 expression: HR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25–0.86, P = 0.016; number of metastatic organs: HR = 1.61, 95% CI: 1.10–2.35, P = 0.015). A nomogram integrating these variables was constructed. The combined model showed better discrimination than the clinical-only and pathological-only models (AUC = 0.800 vs. 0.672 and 0.653, respectively). The apparent C-index was 0.746 (95% CI: 0.703–0.789), and the optimism-corrected C-index was 0.730 (optimism = 0.016), indicating minimal overfitting. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis yielded 1- and 2-year AUCs of 0.780 and 0.782, respectively; after bootstrap correction, these values remained stable at 0.778 (95% CI: 0.706–0.865) and 0.785 (95% CI: 0.691–0.847), respectively. The calibration curves showed good agreement between the predicted and observed 1-year OS probabilities; however, the 2-year calibration results should be interpreted with caution (calibration intercept = 0.376). The proportional hazards assumption was satisfied (global Schoenfeld test P = 0.67 ). DCA showed that the net benefit of the nomogram was greater than that of the clinical-only and pathological-only models, with the predictive model consistently outperforming the clinical-only model across the 0.05–0.70 threshold range (ΔNB: 0.025–0.202) and showing comparable benefit at low thresholds (0.05–0.30) but substantially greater benefit at high thresholds (0.40–0.70; ΔNB: 0.024–0.169) than the pathological-only model. In patients with AGC receiving ICIs plus chemotherapy, an elevated NPS is associated with poor outcomes and serves as an independent prognostic factor. Integrating the NPS with PS, Lauren classification, PD-L1 expression, and the number of metastatic organs may yield a composite indicator reflecting immune-nutritional status. The NPS has potential value as a prognostic biomarker in patients with AGC treated with ICIs and chemotherapy, and warrants further validation in prospective studies.

Article.Title: Recovery of genomic and transcriptomic profiles from decades-old FFPE brain tissues
Article.Authors: Christiansen C.; Firoozfard E.; Oskolkov N.; Gilbert M.; Mak S.; Wirenfeldt M.; Kjaer C.; Mármol-Sánchez E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neurological, neurodegenerative, and psychiatric disorders impose substantial morbidity and disability worldwide, yet their molecular basis remains incompletely understood, in part due to limited access to human brain tissue. The Danish Brain Collection, comprising brains from individuals who lived in Danish psychiatric institutions from the 1940s to the 1980s, represents a unique but largely untapped resource for retrospective molecular investigation. Here, we assess the feasibility of extracting and sequencing DNA and RNA from decades-old FFPE brain tissue. We systematically evaluate how extraction and library preparation strategies influence nucleic acid yield and quality, and show that RNA end-repair prior to library preparation substantially enhances transcript diversity, improving data quality from highly degraded samples. Despite extensive fragmentation, we recover biologically informative transcriptomic profiles, including protein-coding and microRNA expression profiles that retain tissue-specific signatures. These results establish the Danish Brain Collection as a viable resource for genomic and transcriptomic analyses and demonstrate the broader potential of archival FFPE tissues for large-scale molecular studies.

Article.Title: Pseudotime trajectory analysis reveals divergent rod photoreceptor states during dark adaptation
Article.Authors: Ishii R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rod photoreceptors face a high ATP demand in darkness, yet the molecular programs supporting dark adaptation remain difficult to dissect in vivo. Here, I re-analyzed publicly available murine retinal single-cell RNA-seq data and reconstructed rod-state dynamics across the light-to-dark transition using pseudotime trajectory inference. I found that dark-adapting rods diverge from a common state into two distinct lineages. Lineage 1 is characterized by elevated MYC-driven anabolic programs alongside increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) response and unfolded protein response (UPR)/ER stress signatures. In contrast, Lineage 2 exhibits an altered RNA-processing state with a markedly higher unspliced RNA fraction. Furthermore, Lineage 2 relatively preserves the STRADA/MO25β (CAB39L) module, which supports LKB1-AMPK energy sensing. Together, these findings support a model in which dark-adapting rods bifurcate into a MYC-driven anabolic state and an RNA-processing-altered state, a balance that may be biased by an LKB1–AMPK-associated mechanism. This integrative computational analysis provides a descriptive framework for rod photoreceptor adaptation, guiding future biochemical and molecular experiments to determine the molecular basis and drivers of this divergence.

Article.Title: A new approach to improve natural dye fixation on textile fabrics using Trichoderma viride lac418 laccase enzyme: production, characterization and molecular docking studies
Article.Authors: Wehaidy H.; Salim R.; El-Sayed G.; Ibrahim M.; El-Hennawi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Natural dyes like flavonoids are used for many applications because they are eco-friendly and non-toxic. However, they have no affinity to fibers and need a mordant to enhance this affinity. Mordants (dye fixatives) are environmental hazards, as they are toxic and carcinogenic, so it is important to identify alternative methods for textile dyeing with natural dyes. Laccase enzyme is capable of oxidizing natural dyes that contain phenolic hydroxyl groups. This process is followed by polymerization, which leads to the formation of a colored compound on the textile surface. Therefore, it can be utilized as an alternative to conventional mordants. In the current study, the most potent laccase producer was a fungus isolated from rotten wood. It was identified and submitted to the NCBI GenBank database as Trichoderma viride lac418 under accession number PV594963. The partially purified Trichoderma viride lac418 laccase has maximum activity at a temperature of 60 °C and pH 5.0. The activation energy ( Ea ) was 7.7 kJ/mol. The values of Km and Vmax were calculated as 1.7 mg/mL and 102041 U/mL, respectively. Trichoderma viride lac418 laccase has enhanced the affinity of cotton and viscose fabrics to the water-extracted dye obtained from Hibiscus sabdariffa flowers. Excellent color strength and color fastness properties were observed with viscose fabric and 2:1 dye-enzyme ratio. The molecular docking studies revealed that rutin and rosmarinic acid exhibited the strongest binding affinity to laccase enzyme, which confirms the potential role of laccase in the fixation of the water-extracted dye from Hibiscus sabdariffa flowers. Therefore, Trichoderma viride lac418 laccase is recommended as an eco-friendly substitute for the hazardous mordants in textile dyeing and printing.

Article.Title: Association of novel hybrid and traditional anthropometric indices with kidney function among adolescent girls in Northeast Iran
Article.Authors: Ghayour-Mobarhan M.; Ebrahimzadehkour B.; Jowshan M.
Article.Abstract: The relationship between novel composite adiposity indices (Visceral Adiposity Index [VAI] and Lipid Accumulation Product [LAP]) and traditional anthropometric measures (body mass index [BMI] and waist-to-height ratio [WHtR]) with kidney function in adolescents remains unclear. This study investigated the associations of these four indices with kidney function in adolescent girls. In this cross-sectional study, 802 adolescent girls were recruited from northeastern Iran. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 90 mL/min/1.73 m 2 defined reduced eGFR. Logistic regression and covariate-adjusted ROC analysis were used to assess the associations and discriminatory ability of VAI, LAP, BMI, and WHtR. Non-linear associations were assessed by including quadratic and cubic terms in the adjusted models. BMI showed the highest discriminatory ability (AUC = 0.718, 95% CI 0.668–0.769), followed by LAP (AUC = 0.704, 95% CI 0.654–0.755), WHtR (AUC = 0.697, 95% CI 0.645–0.749), and VAI (AUC = 0.689, 95% CI 0.636–0.741). BMI, LAP, and WHtR were significantly associated with reduced eGFR in adjusted models, whereas VAI was not (OR = 1.448, 95% CI 0.956–2.194, p = 0.081). Consequently, no clinically valid cut-off was reported for VAI. These models revealed a significant linear association for BMI, WHtR, and VAI, whereas LAP showed a non-linear pattern (quadratic p = 0.009, cubic p = 0.027). All indices had limited explanatory power (adjusted R 2 ≤ 23.2%). BMI and WHtR, as simple and widely available anthropometric measures, were the most useful indices for identifying reduced eGFR, albeit with modest discriminatory ability. VAI was not independently associated with reduced eGFR and lacked a clinically valid cut-off, limiting its utility. The non-linear relationship for LAP warrants further investigation. Longitudinal studies are needed to refine risk assessment in this population.

Article.Title: A unified pipeline for traffic sign detection using resolution aware dataset reduction
Article.Authors: Vijayalakshmi U.; Babu M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Robust traffic sign detection is an important factor of safe autonomous driving, allowing vehicles to accurately interpret and comply with dynamic road regulations. However, real world deployment remains heavily challenged by distant, extra-small signs, as well as partial occlusions from trees, structures, or other vehicles. While optimizing training datasets through size reduction can dramatically lower computational overhead and storage footprints, conventional pruning methods often discard critical spatial features, severely degrading model accuracy. In light of these limitations, this paper introduces a novel, end to end processing pipeline that simultaneously tackles dataset size and small object detection bottlenecks. First, a lightweight VGG16 model is trained on representative samples to evaluate scene complexity patterns and dynamically predict an image specific compression threshold. Using this prediction, an adaptive, multi scale compression mechanism is applied exclusively to images that require it. A saliency guided image processing strategy is used to selectively compress background regions and preserve important Regions of Interest. This resolution aware dataset is then used to train the proposed Edge-Texture Fusion (ETF) YOLO11 network. By incorporating attention mechanisms to capture low-level edge and texture information, ETFYOLO11 improves the detection of distant and heavily compressed traffic signs. Three diverse publicly available traffic sign datasets are used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. This method reduces dataset storage requirements by 50–90%, cuts model parameters by 50%, and lowers GFLOPs by 20%.and at the same time achieve a higher mAP@50 than the baseline YOLO11n model.

Article.Title: Epilepsy knowledge and attitudes among syrian university students: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Alsalloum T.; Almansour S.; Issa J.; Salame H.; Alharke Q.; Aldosh T.; Alsamman H.; Alkhatib F.
Article.Abstract: Epilepsy is a significant global health challenge with profound psychosocial impacts. University students, as future leaders, play a pivotal role in shaping societal perceptions and reducing stigma. This study aimed to assess epilepsy-related knowledge and attitudes among Syrian university students and to identify sociodemographic and academic factors associated with adequate knowledge and positive attitudes. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 394 Syrian university students (63.5% in health and medical fields) using a previously validated epilepsy knowledge and attitude instrument comprising a 16-item knowledge test and a 13-item attitude scale. Only 34.5% of participants demonstrated adequate knowledge, and 41.9% had positive attitudes. Major knowledge gaps were identified regarding epilepsy’s curability and appropriate seizure first-aid practices. Students from other academic fields had lower odds of adequate knowledge than those in health and medical science fields (aOR = 0.333, 95% CI: 0.200–0.553, p < 0.001). Male students had lower odds of a positive attitude than female students (aOR = 0.525, 95% CI: 0.347–0.794, p = 0.002). Self-rated knowledge was independently associated with both adequate knowledge and positive attitudes. The internet was the most commonly reported source of information (60.8%), whereas only 7.6% reported awareness campaigns as a source. Significant gaps in epilepsy-related knowledge and persistent elements of social stigma were identified among Syrian university students. The findings support the need for targeted epilepsy education, particularly regarding seizure first aid, common misconceptions, and stigma reduction, with evidence-based digital resources representing a potentially useful complementary approach.

Article.Title: Optimizing nanoLC-TIMS-TOF and lipidomics sample preparation for low volume of plasma
Article.Authors: Rellin K.; Abel L.; Barsch A.; Witting M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lipidomics provides critical insights into disease mechanisms, biomarker discovery, and precision medicine, but conventional LC-MS workflows often require sample volumes that limit their application in minimally invasive studies. Here, we evaluated a nanoflow liquid chromatography workflow coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry and time-of-flight mass spectrometry (nanoLC-TIMS-TOF) for positive ion lipid profiling from as little as 1 µL of plasma. Two commonly used single-phase extraction protocols, MeOH: MTBE and IPA: H₂O, were scaled to microsample volumes using NIST ® SRM ® 1950 plasma. The effects of plasma input volume and mobile-phase ammonium formate concentration (2, 5, and 10 mM) on feature detection and chromatographic performance were evaluated. Descriptive comparisons revealed extraction-, volume-, and buffer-associated differences in the detected feature profiles, while putative lipid annotations were evaluated using MS/MS and ion-mobility information, where available. The optimized workflow enabled broad positive ion lipid class profiling and detection of low intensity features from only 1 µL of starting material. The 1 µL extracts retained the dominant annotated lipid classes observed at higher input volumes, although profiling depth and feature distributions remained dependent on plasma input volume. Among the tested mobile phase conditions, 5 mM ammonium formate produced the highest detected feature count while limiting pressure drift during extended acquisition. These results support the feasibility and practical scalability of positive ion nanoLC-TIMS-MS lipid profiling for sample-limited applications under the evaluated conditions.

Article.Title: PGFT-IGR: position-guided feature transformation for incremental gait recognition
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Li Y.; Dong L.; Mei Z.
Article.Abstract: Real-world gait recognition systems must continuously enroll new users while coping with evolving gait patterns over time. Conventional model training methods cannot adapt to such ongoing changes, leading to catastrophic forgetting and performance degradation. Moreover, in practical scenarios, sensor wearing positions vary across users and usage habits (e.g., thigh or handheld). This observation motivates the explicit use of positional information to guide the learning of more discriminative and separable gait features. Based on these considerations, we propose the Position-Guided Feature Transformation framework for Incremental Gait Recognition (PGFT-IGR), which explicitly incorporates positional guidance and supports continuous enrollment of new users. Specifically, the framework generates pseudo-features for old classes from new class features to mitigate forgetting and retain knowledge of previously learned classes, using a structure alignment module composed of two complementary components: an isotropic scaling component that corrects the spatial distribution of pseudo-features by matching feature dispersion between new and old classes, and an affine transformation component that refines the covariance structure of pseudo-features via an affine matrix to better approximate the true distribution of old classes. Additionally, a dual-layer graph propagation module smooths feature manifolds and optimizes decision boundaries by constructing separate position and class graphs. Experimental results on the publicly available Luo-Gait and HuGaDb datasets show improvements in average accuracy by 6.56% and 2.73%, respectively, compared to current several existing methods. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness and complementarity of each module. This work presents a practical approach for incremental gait recognition with multi-position sensors.

Article.Title: Feasibility, safety, and acceptability of robotic-assisted rehabilitation for patients with knee osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Shankar R.; Neoh E.; Chua K.; Tan T.; Tay M.; Kim J.; Aguirre-Ollinger G.; Kulkarni S.; Ong P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Total knee replacement (TKR) is an effective treatment for end-stage knee osteoarthritis (KOA), yet optimal preoperative rehabilitation strategies remain undefined. Robot-assisted rehabilitation offers potential advantages in delivering controlled, intensive, and reproducible exercise protocols for patients with knee osteoarthritis. This early-phase feasibility study evaluated the safety, usability, and patient acceptability of the Knee-LOCOBOT, a novel robotic rehabilitation device designed for patients with KOA. No inference regarding efficacy can be drawn given the absence of a control group, randomization, or blinding. A single-arm feasibility study was conducted at Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Singapore (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07539948; NHG DSRB Reference: 2024–3529). Ten patients with KOA were recruited, with nine completing the intervention prior to TKR. Participants underwent four sessions of robot-assisted exercises incorporating cycling, leg press, and isometric quadriceps strengthening modes. Outcome measures included the Oxford Knee Score (OKS), EQ-5D-5 L, Knee Society Score (KSS), 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), Timed Up and Go (TUG), 30-second Chair Rise, quadriceps strength, and patient satisfaction survey. Recruitment, retention, and adherence were the primary feasibility outcomes. From 15 patients screened, 10 were enrolled (consent rate 71%, 10 of 14 eligible), of whom nine completed all four sessions, giving a retention rate of 90% (9/10) and 100% session completion and adherence among completers; the single withdrawal was for personal reasons unrelated to the device. A statistically significant within-group change in 6MWT distance was observed (median 291 m to 360 m; median within-participant change + 15 m, mean change + 31 m; p = 0.012, n = 9). In the absence of a control group this change cannot be attributed to the intervention. Right quadriceps strength showed a non-significant numerical increase ( p = 0.05, unadjusted, one of multiple comparisons). Exercised vs. non-exercised limb strength difference was small and non-significant (Cohen’s d = 0.11, p = 0.75). No adverse events were recorded. Patient acceptability was high (88.9% agreement). This small, single-arm, uncontrolled feasibility evaluation in nine selected low-pain KOA patients suggests that four supervised sessions can be completed without recorded adverse events, with high patient acceptability. No conclusions regarding clinical effectiveness or suitability for rehabilitation pathway integration can be drawn. An adequately powered randomised controlled trial is required before any efficacy claims can be made. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07539948, date of first registration 27/03/2026.
