Article.Title: Defense mechanisms of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical strains against lytic phages and counter-defense
Article.Authors: Armán L.; Blasco L.; Blériot I.; Fernández-García L.; Drulis-Kawa Z.; Dorotkiewicz-Jach A.; Nir-Paz R.; Pirnay J.; Green S.; Lavigne R.; Cantón R.; Oliver A.; Pérez Vázquez M.; Tomás M.; N/A N/A.; Cañada-Garcia E.; Oteo-Iglesias J.; Morelli H.; Adriaenssens E.
Article.Abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae are major Gram-negative pathogens in which the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains has increased the need for alternative antimicrobial strategies, including phage therapy. However, bacterial antiphage defense systems and the corresponding phage-encoded counter-defense mechanisms can critically influence phage infectivity and therapeutic potential. Here, we characterized bacterial defense systems in 75 clinical P. aeruginosa and 47 K. pneumoniae isolates and analyzed anti-defense repertoires in collections of 13 and 11 corresponding lytic phages, respectively. Abortive infection (Abi) systems were the predominant characterized defense category in P. aeruginosa , whereas systems of unknown function were the most abundant in K. pneumoniae . Among P. aeruginosa phages, DEDDh_I_II_III_IV_V_VI_1, a DnaQ-like exonuclease associated with anti-CRISPR activity, was the most frequently detected anti-defense determinant (76.92%). In K. pneumoniae phages, stp (anti-restriction) was detected in 54.55% and acb1/acb2 (anti-CBASS) in 27.27%. Phage–host interaction analysis revealed substantial heterogeneity in infectivity and showed that the presence or number of anti-defense systems alone did not consistently predict infection outcome. To investigate the functional contribution of specific anti-defense mechanisms, time-kill assays were performed against P. aeruginosa PA14 and CECT-110 and K. pneumoniae ATCC 700721, and bacterial growth inhibition was quantified from the area under the growth curve (AUC). Notably, anti-CBASS-positive P. aeruginosa phages showed significantly greater growth inhibition than anti-CBASS-negative phages (65.28% vs. 15.77%; difference, 49.51 percentage points; P = 0.0007), whereas no significant association was observed in K. pneumoniae . No significant association with growth inhibition was identified for the other anti-defense categories evaluated. Based on this genotype–phenotype association, we designed a LAMP–CRISPR-Cas13a assay targeting queC (CBASS_associated defense) as a proof of concept for rapid detection of CBASS-associated determinants in P. aeruginosa . Although validation in larger bacterial and phage collections is required, our findings support the integration of bacterial defense profiling with complementary phage anti-defense characterization as a potential strategy for prioritizing candidate phages for subsequent phenotypic evaluation and rational phage therapy.

Article.Title: An innovative reconfigurable shield-to-leg mechanism for UAVs in built cultural heritage inspection
Article.Authors: Carbone G.; Khadem M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper introduces a reconfigurable structural mechanism for unmanned aerial vehicles that transforms the same mechanical elements from propeller shields into adaptive landing legs. The concept is developed for drones operating in built cultural heritage sites, where safe navigation, stable landing on irregular surfaces, and non-intrusive inspection are critical. The mechanism can be reconfigured according to the flight phase: in flight, it forms a protective enclosure around the propellers to reduce the risk of collision with surrounding structures, while during landing it deploys into independently adjustable legs that adapt to the ground using real-time attitude feedback. The structural design of the drone is presented together with the kinematic and dynamic models of the reconfigurable mechanism. A prototype system was built and experimentally evaluated under controlled laboratory conditions and representative surface configurations. The results demonstrate the self-leveling and stabilization capability of the mechanism under the tested conditions, highlighting the potential of reconfigurable UAV mechanisms for future inspection and monitoring applications in constrained and sensitive cultural heritage environments. This study presents a unified shield-to-leg mechanism for morphing quadcopters. The functional performance of the mechanism in post-touchdown attitude leveling on uneven surfaces was validated using a ground-based physical prototype, while its dynamic stability and disturbance rejection were evaluated in numerical multi-body simulations.

Article.Title: Streptococcus agalactiae pigment toxin induces a rapid non-canonical cell death in human dendritic cells
Article.Authors: Riegner A.; Friedrich E.; Tölken L.; Siemens N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus, GBS) is a major cause of neonatal sepsis and is increasingly associated with invasive infections in non-pregnant adults. GBS produces a cell wall-associated lipid toxin, the pigment (granadaene), a key virulence factor with cytotoxic and immunomodulatory properties. While its effects on several immune cells have been described, its impact on human dendritic cells remains largely unknown. Here, the role of the GBS pigment during infection of human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs) was assessed. Infection with pigmented GBS induced rapid cell death, characterized by early loss of mitochondrial membrane potential and phosphatidylserine exposure, culminating in membrane disruption. Inhibition of canonical cell death pathways indicated that moDC death occurs predominantly via a caspase-independent, mitochondria-driven mechanism, with caspase-8 activity enhancing the process. Blocking phagocytosis did not reduce cytotoxicity, whereas restriction of bacteria to the intracellular compartment markedly diminished cell death, indicating that the pigment primarily acts extracellularly. Following removal of extracellular bacteria and 24-h incubation, infected moDCs remained largely viable and exhibited comparable maturation and cytokine responses, regardless of whether the infecting bacteria expressed the pigment. Together, these findings indicate that pigment-dependent cytotoxicity in moDC infections is mediated by extracellular GBS.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based record linkage for brazilian health databases validated in Espírito Santo
Article.Authors: Lages D.; Silva T.; Oliveira P.; de Oliveira D.; Leandro G.; da Silva D.; de Oliveira Cardoso L.; de Sá N.; de Freitas P.; Medeiros-de-Souza A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A machine learning–based record linkage approach was developed within the TRAUMA project to support the integration of Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS) information systems. However, evidence comparing traditional linkage approaches with supervised machine learning models in large health datasets remains limited. This study evaluated the TRAUMA linkage method and compared it with CIDACS-RL, a widely used probabilistic linkage tool in Brazil. This methodological validation study used records from the Mortality Information System (SIM), Hospital Information System (SIH-SUS), Notifiable Diseases Information System (Sinan), and e-SUS Health Surveillance (e-SUS VS) from Espírito Santo, Brazil, between July 2018 and June 2025. Candidate pairs were generated through a multi-pass blocking strategy. The proposed method incorporated supervised machine learning to automate the classification of uncertain record pairs that would otherwise require manual review. A total of 106,363 labelled record pairs were used for model development and testing. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. The best-performing algorithm was incorporated into the TRAUMA framework and compared with CIDACS-RL using a validated gold-standard dataset of 11,662 record pairs. LightGBM achieved the best performance. In the test dataset, the model obtained an ROC-AUC of 0.99996, sensitivity of 0.99731, precision of 0.99464, F1-score of 0.99597, and specificity of 0.99895. Performance remained stable in independent validation (ROC-AUC = 0.99988; F1-score = 0.99252). SHAP analysis identified date-of-birth variables and Jaro–Winkler and Levenshtein similarity measures as key predictors. Compared with CIDACS-RL, TRAUMA showed higher sensitivity, F1-score, and specificity estimates, with similar precision, and recovered more reference links. Both approaches demonstrated high performance for record linkage in administrative health databases. TRAUMA showed higher estimates of sensitivity, F1-score, and specificity while maintaining high precision and recovering more links contained in the reference dataset. These findings support both approaches as robust record linkage solutions, with the observed differences interpreted descriptively rather than as evidence of statistical superiority.

Article.Title: Goldfish keratocyte migration dynamics differ among horizontal, vertical, and clinorotation conditions
Article.Authors: Kasashima D.; Shinkura S.; Hamamura M.; Tatsumi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gravity influences biological systems at many levels, yet its contribution to vertebrate cell migration remains poorly understood. Here, we examined how fish keratocytes alter their migratory behavior when the orientation of the gravity vector relative to the substrate is changed. At 30-s sampling intervals, keratocytes displayed distinct trajectory statistics on vertically and horizontally oriented substrates, including differences in migration speed and turning-angle dynamics. On vertical substrates, clinorotation and culture in medium with a specific gravity of 1.055 shifted these migration patterns toward those observed on horizontal substrates. Conversely, on horizontal substrates, weak externally applied medium flow induced changes resembling those observed under vertical culture. These responses developed rapidly, within 60 s, and were reversible in single cells during clinorotation experiments. Together, these findings demonstrate that keratocyte migration is sensitive to changes in the physical environment associated with substrate orientation, clinorotation, medium density, and weak flow. Although the results are consistent with a contribution of gravity-associated mechanical loading, they do not identify a specific force-transduction mechanism. The study therefore provides a phenomenological description of rapid, reversible modulation of keratocyte migration statistics by defined physical perturbations.

Article.Title: Seminal bradykinin, fetuin-a, pentraxin-3, and adipolin levels in infertile men with varicocele and varicocelectomy: a cross-sectional case–control study
Article.Authors: Oc M.; Dundar A.; Yildiz S.; Irmak H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Varicocele is characterized by abnormal dilatation of the pampiniform plexus accompanied by venous reflux and is one of the leading correctable causes of male infertility. Although several mechanisms have been proposed, the molecular pathways underlying varicocele-induced testicular dysfunction remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate seminal bradykinin, fetuin-A, pentraxin-3, and adipolin levels in infertile men with varicocele and to compare these biomarkers among patients with varicocele, patients who had undergone varicocelectomy, and controls. This cross-sectional case-control study included 90 participants: 30 infertile men with clinical varicocele, 30 patients who had undergone varicocelectomy and 30 healthy controls. Seminal bradykinin, fetuin-A, pentraxin-3, and adipolin concentrations were determined using ELISA. Sperm concentration, rapid progressive, non-progressive, and immotile sperm percentages, together with bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 levels, differed significantly among the study groups. Fetuin-A and pentraxin-3 levels were significantly elevated in the varicocele group compared with healthy controls. Patients assessed approximately 3 months after varicocelectomy exhibited significantly higher bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 levels than controls. No significant differences were observed among the groups regarding age, height, body weight, body mass index, abstinence duration, semen volume, slow progressive sperm percentage, or Adipolin levels. Our findings indicate that patients with varicocele and patients assessed after varicocelectomy exhibit differences in inflammatory and cellular stress-related biomarkers compared with healthy controls. The higher levels of bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 observed in patients assessed after varicocelectomy may reflect differences in inflammatory and cellular stress-related profiles between the study groups; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow these findings to be interpreted as postoperative persistence or treatment-related changes. These biomarkers may provide complementary information regarding inflammatory and cellular stress-related profiles in varicocele; however, their clinical significance and utility for monitoring postoperative changes require confirmation in larger prospective longitudinal studies.

Article.Title: Point of choice visual feedback prompts elicit motor behavior changes in persons with multiple sclerosis
Article.Authors: Fox S.; Jangraw D.; Mascia G.; Gurchiek R.; Feng Y.; Meyer B.; Solomon A.; McGinnis E.; McGinnis R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Falls are common in persons with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), and their consequences further undermine quality of life. Current fall prevention interventions fail to address real-time stability challenges that may occur during cognitively complex daily activities. This need may be fulfilled by means of just-in-time interventions that leverage prompts delivered via a mobile app, having the aim of producing beneficial targeted biomechanical changes. Fourteen ambulatory PwMS completed multiple Timed Up-and-Go tests under cognitive load across two different visits. Two visual feedback prompts targeting trunk flexion during sit-to-stand transitions (STS-TF) and stance width (SW) during gait were delivered terminally via the Just in Time Fall Prevention app. Linear mixed-effects models with Dunnett’s correction were implemented to evaluate prompt-induced changes relative to baseline. Prompts were successfully able to systematically reduce STS-TF by 7.1° (p < 0.001, d = − 0.483) and to increase SW by 8.1 mm (p = 0.021, d = 0.259). The majority of participants reported willingness to use the app with and without physician prescription (95% and 68%, respectively). This study demonstrated for the first time that PwMS can produce targeted biomechanical adaptations in response to point-of-choice visual feedback prompts delivered by a mobile app, supporting just-in-time mobile interventions as a proactive fall prevention strategy.

Article.Title: Machine learning estimation of prosumer net metering using optimal polynomial basis functions for dimensionality reduction
Article.Authors: Tutsoy O.; Zor K.; Çelik Ö.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Solar energy has become an essential renewable resource for residential prosumers engaging in bidirectional electricity exchange with the grid. However, accurately estimating net consumption remains a challenge due to the prevalence of limited yet redundant local Photovoltaic (PV) data. This paper designs an input dimension reduction approach using optimal polynomial basis functions to enhance machine learning estimation. Optimal higher-order powers are determined via an L 2 -norm performance function based on matrix conditioning. Additionally, Pearson correlation and the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) are employed to eliminate redundancies and quantify key input–output relationships. The refined data is used to train Batch Least Squares (BLS), Neural Network (NN), and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms. Results demonstrate that the BLS model, integrated with Pearson-based feature selection, achieves superior precision with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0037 and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0048. Validation on unseen test data confirms the model's robustness, maintaining a low MAE of 0.0036 and RMSE of 0.0046.

Article.Title: Research on key node identification method based on multi-attribute fusion in complex networks
Article.Authors: Cai P.; Xie Y.; Wang Q.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate assessment of node importance in complex networks is crucial for enhancing network robustness and security, for instance, by protecting critical data nodes or reinforcing core hubs. However, existing importance metrics often struggle to simultaneously accommodate local connectivity, neighborhood influence and global mediation effects. Moreover, they frequently yield similar importance scores for a large number of nodes, resulting in insufficient discriminability and failing to effectively identify key nodes. In this paper, we propose the CRITIC-based Multi-Attribute Fusion Indicator (CR-MAFI) within the CRITIC (Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation) framework. CR-MAFI integrates degree centrality, degree and neighborhood information centrality, and betweenness centrality, and employs Shannon entropy and inter-criterion conflict to derive objective weights, thereby enhancing the dominance of high-discriminability metrics in the fusion process. By integrating network structural information from multiple perspectives, the proposed method provides a more comprehensive assessment of node importance. Experiments are conducted on four types of real-world networks, including the aviation network USAir97, social network fb-pages-food, criminal collaboration network crime-moreno and power network 1138_bus. The results show that CR-MAFI achieves stable and relatively good performance in both simulated attack and spreading experiments, exhibits reliable damage effectiveness and spreading influence, and demonstrates reliable robustness and applicability across different types of networks and task scenarios. Analysis of the score distribution further reveals pronounced skewness and positive excess kurtosis across all tested networks, confirming that CR-MAFI consistently reproduces a score distribution that discriminates a small set of nodes.

Article.Title: Robust knowledge tracing via bidirectional context and conditional diffusion
Article.Authors: He B.; Huang Z.; Liu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Knowledge Tracing (KT) is essential in online education for modeling learners’ evolving knowledge states to support personalized instruction. However, conventional KT approaches often exhibit instability when confronted with abrupt shifts in learner performance—such as sudden errors amid consistent success or unexpected recoveries after prolonged failure. These non-stationary response patterns challenge models that rely on local sequential updates, leading to overreaction, delayed adaptation, or inconsistent predictions. To address this, we propose DiffKT , a knowledge tracing framework that enhances robustness through holistic sequence modeling. DiffKT first introduces a Bidirectional Global Context-aware State Estimator (GCSE), which leverages the full interaction sequence—past and future—to construct stable, context-rich representations of latent knowledge states, thereby mitigating myopic bias. Building on these representations, DiffKT employs a conditional diffusion process to iteratively refine knowledge state estimates by denoising corrupted sequence-level proxies. This enables the model to distinguish transient anomalies from genuine learning signals and maintain temporal consistency across dynamic response patterns. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets show that DiffKT achieves competitive or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in next-response prediction. Further case studies and ablation analyses confirm that the integration of bidirectional context and diffusion-based refinement jointly improves robustness to abrupt performance shifts and generalization across diverse learning trajectories.

Article.Title: Transcriptome profile of s-SHIP expressing breast cancer cells identifies PIERCE1 as a novel drug-resistance gene
Article.Authors: Louvieaux J.; Tian L.; Mougel A.; Chomy A.; Laneret N.; Toillon R.; Vicogne J.; Bourhis X.; Bourette R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer is an aggressive subtype of breast cancer that is not sensitive to hormone inhibition. Its treatment is mainly limited to conventional therapies, including neoadjuvant chemotherapy. But the acquisition of drug resistance is a major obstacle to the eradication of the tumor cells, especially the breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs). Using a double-transgenic mouse model 11.5 kb-GFP x C3(1)-Tag, we have previously shown that s-SHIP expression identifies a breast cancer stem cell–related population in primary tumors. To investigate the chemoresistance of s-SHIP/GFP-expressing tumor cells, we used the MAM326 cell line, established from a tumor isolated from these double-transgenic mice. A subset of s-SHIP/GFP+ MAM326 cells, displaying a drug-tolerant stem-related phenotype, exhibited enhanced resistance to various chemotherapy drugs, including paclitaxel and doxorubicin. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that these s-SHIP/GFP+ cells exhibited upregulation of several genes associated with chemoresistance. Furthermore, this analysis highlighted Pierce1 which plays a role in DNA damage response. We showed that Pierce1 was significantly overexpressed in transiently surviving cells treated with paclitaxel and doxorubicin, both in MAM326 cells and in a primary tumoroid model. Overexpression of PIERCE1 in human TNBC SUM159PT cells led to increased resistance to chemotherapy, while its knockdown reduced this resistance. Importantly, clinical data further supported the association of high PIERCE1 expression with poor prognosis and reduced survival in TNBC patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. This study unveils the potential of PIERCE1 as a therapeutic target for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in breast cancer.

Article.Title: Sepsis and septic shock after breast cancer surgery: risk modeling and machine learning validation across 328,292 cases
Article.Authors: Jiang J.; Wirtz J.; Gizlenci M.; Kong V.; Däster K.; Elfgen C.; Tausch C.; Nguyen A.; Watson J.; Prantl L.; Moog P.; Machens H.; Moltaji S.; Hofer S.; Falkner F.; Knoedler S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postoperative sepsis is a rare but life-threatening complication after breast cancer surgery. Although infection risk in breast surgery is generally low, cancer-related immune dysregulation combined with surgical stress may increase susceptibility, yet large-scale data on incidence, risk factors, and outcomes remain limited. We conducted a retrospective analysis of the ACS-NSQIP database (2008–2022). Adult female patients undergoing breast cancer surgery were included. The primary outcome was ACS-NSQIP-coded 30-day postoperative sepsis; septic shock was analyzed separately and descriptively. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with postoperative sepsis. Model performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with bootstrap correction for optimism and compared with machine-learning approaches trained with explicit handling of class imbalance. Among 328,292 patients (47.8% partial, 38.6% simple, 13.6% radical mastectomy), sepsis occurred in 838 (0.26%), with incidence increasing across procedure categories (0.08% vs. 0.40% vs. 0.46%; p < 0.001). Patients with sepsis had markedly higher rates of reoperation (46.5% vs. 4.0%) and unplanned readmission (73.7% vs. 2.1%; both p < 0.001). The strongest adjusted associations with postoperative sepsis were observed for prior sepsis (aOR 4.51), functional dependence (aOR 3.80), and ASA class III (aOR 3.16; all p < 0.001). Reconstruction was also associated with higher adjusted odds of sepsis, with aORs of 2.15 for autologous and 1.59 for implant-based reconstruction. The model showed good discrimination (apparent AUC 0.752; optimism-corrected AUC 0.746) and was well calibrated (bootstrap-corrected calibration slope 0.967). No machine-learning approach outperformed logistic regression on the held-out test set (DeLong p = 0.077–0.409). Sepsis after breast cancer surgery is uncommon but clinically significant, with incidence increasing across procedure categories. Reconstruction, particularly autologous reconstruction, was associated with sepsis after adjustment for measured covariates. Because oncologic and treatment-related variables are not captured in ACS-NSQIP, this association should be interpreted as observational rather than causal. These findings may inform individualized preoperative risk assessment and counseling.

Article.Title: Patient and healthcare professional preferences among predefined features of a peritoneal dialysis monitoring application in South Korea: an exploratory choice-based conjoint study
Article.Authors: Kim K.; Kim T.; Lee S.; Kim B.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is performed at home, where contact with healthcare professionals between clinic visits is limited. This exploratory study examined how patients receiving PD and healthcare professionals traded off five predefined attributes of a mobile monitoring application, derived from the Korean PD home-care reimbursement framework (monthly price, regular consultation, unscheduled consultation, educational content, and data management), and estimated conditional willingness-to-pay (WTP) . Between March and May 2022, 130 patients and 32 healthcare professionals completed a forced-choice conjoint survey without an opt-out alternative. Within the experiment, price accounted for about one quarter of relative importance in both groups. Among the functional attributes, patients assigned the greatest importance to unscheduled (23.0%) and regular consultation (22.2%), whereas healthcare professionals assigned it to data management (22.4%). Both groups preferred nurse consultation over a 24-hour chatbot (part-worth utility 0.814 vs. 0.117 in patients; 0.901 vs. − 0.185 in professionals). Among healthcare professionals, perceived institutional WTP was highest for monitoring patients’ daily health records. These values were reported by individual clinicians, not institutional purchasers, and are conditional on the selected price range, an assumed linear price coefficient, and the forced-choice design. These exploratory findings describe stakeholder trade-offs within a predefined, reimbursement-based choice set and are hypothesis-generating.

Article.Title: Temporal evolution and decline of seismicity associated with cyclic operations at the Serajeh underground gas storage, Iran
Article.Authors: Songhori A.; Rahimi H.; Jamalreyhani M.; Niu F.; Karampour B.; Ebrahimi Moghaddam M.; Zeynaddini-Meymand R.; Ghods A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Underground gas storage (UGS) operations can perturb reservoir conditions and modulate local seismicity, but the temporal evolution of this response under cyclic injection–withdrawal remains poorly constrained. We investigate seismicity around the Serajeh UGS in central Iran by combining 29,781 deep-learning-based single-station earthquake detections, multi-station relocation, centroid moment tensor inversion, and operational records. The relocated hypocentres form a compact cluster near the Serajeh structure, primarily at depths of 3–8 km, overlapping with and extending below the 2.4–3.0 km storage interval. Independent comparison with relocated earthquakes confirms that S–P time at the nearby GHVR station provides a useful first-order proxy for local source distance. Cross-correlation between monthly gas injection and seismicity shows a distinct maximum at an offset of approximately 8 months. This feature is reproduced by the phase-randomized ReshuffleCorr analysis, while additional structure-preserving tests indicate that its global statistical strength and exact timing depend on the treatment of temporal variability. An objective change-point analysis identifies a marked decrease in seismicity centred on April 2015, nearly four years after storage operations began, and the decrease remains evident using a conservative magnitude threshold. Seismicity subsequently remains lower despite continued cyclic operations. The selected focal mechanisms show predominantly strike-slip to oblique source kinematics across pre-operational, operational, and post-operational periods. We interpret these observations as evidence for an evolving temporal and spatial association between storage operations and a pre-existing fault–reservoir system. These results highlight the value of integrating high-resolution seismic monitoring with independently constrained locations and operational records for seismic-hazard assessment at UGS sites.

Article.Title: Longitudinal red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio trajectories are associated with 28-day mortality in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury
Article.Authors: Hu X.; Wang P.; Wang K.; Zou Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SAAKI) involves rapidly evolving inflammatory and nutritional disturbances, yet most prognostic studies rely on single baseline biomarkers. We examined whether longitudinal red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) trajectories identify reproducible mortality-risk phenotypes. This multicenter retrospective study included MIMIC-IV v3.1 as the development cohort ( n = 4,273), MIMIC-III CareVue as temporal validation ( n = 1,287), and eICU-CRD v2.0 as external validation ( n = 3,195). Group-based trajectory modeling characterized 14-day RAR patterns. Multivariable Cox models evaluated 28-day all-cause mortality. Six machine-learning models predicted the highest-risk trajectory using first-24-h variables, with SHAP used for interpretation. Four trajectories were identified: Persistently Low, Moderate-Stable, Moderate-Elevated, and Persistently High. Mortality increased from 17.54% in Persistently Low to 38.48% in Persistently High. Compared with Persistently Low, Persistently High was associated with higher adjusted mortality in MIMIC-IV (HR 2.22, 95% CI 1.79–2.74), MIMIC-III CareVue (HR 3.32, 95% CI 2.31–4.78), and eICU-CRD (HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.40–2.07). XGBoost achieved AUCs of 0.895, 0.918, and 0.904, respectively. SHAP highlighted baseline RAR, lactate, other infection source, albumin, and creatinine. Longitudinal RAR trajectories identify reproducible mortality-risk phenotypes across the three cohorts and may support early risk stratification, although prospective validation is required.

Article.Title: Human amniotic epithelial cells display donor dependent RPE lineage priming that is better preserved when cultured within the native membrane
Article.Authors: Pisu R.; Saponara S.; D’Alterio M.; Di Michele S.; Angioni S.; Peiretti E.; Vitale S.; Marongiu F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) plays a central role in maintaining retinal function, and its degeneration contributes to diseases such as age-related macular degeneration. The human amniotic membrane (hAM), an ethically accessible tissue with immune privilege and epithelial organization, has been proposed as a potential source for RPE-like cells, particularly in its epithelial cell component. In this study, we investigated the baseline expression of RPE markers in freshly collected hAM to assess interindividual variability. In addition, we compared the behavior of intact hAM sheets and isolated human amniotic epithelial cells (hAECs) in culture, both under maintenance conditions and after treatment with RPE-inductive factors. Fresh hAM fragments and isolated hAECs were analyzed for RPE-associated markers and cultured either as intact epithelial sheets or isolated monolayers. Morphology, gene expression, and protein localization were assessed over time under standard conditions and following exposure to RPE-inductive factors noggin (NOG), CHIR99021 (CHIR), nicotinamide (NIC), and trichostatin A (TSA). Our results show that fresh hAM and isolated hAECs inherently express several RPE-associated markers, although with marked donor-dependent variability. hAM fragments preserved epithelial morphology and marker expression more effectively than isolated hAECs. Stimulation with NOG and CHIR variably modulated RPE-associated marker expression and localization, with largely consistent treatment-related trends across donors. NIC + TSA produced only limited modulation of RPE-associated features and was associated with a progressive reduction in nuclear density, even at the lower TSA concentration tested. Variability in responsiveness compared to previous studies suggested that inter-placental heterogeneity might also affect the response to RPE-inductive cues. Epithelial cells within hAM display donor-dependent RPE-like priming that is better preserved in the native sheet context. Intact hAM may therefore provide a useful system for refining RPE-induction strategies while accounting for donor variability and preserving a tissue format that may be advantageous for future retinal repair applications.

Article.Title: Characterizing single-shell NODDI-DTI estimates through associations with plasma biomarkers and cognitive performance
Article.Authors: Restuccia G.; Ielo A.; Buono V.; Quartarone A.; Bonanno L.; N/A N/A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract White matter (WM) degeneration is an important feature of aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging derived from diffusion tensor imaging (NODDI-DTI) is a technique that allows the estimation of neurite density index (NDI) and orientation dispersion index (ODI) in WM from single-shell diffusion tensor imaging. However, these estimates are tensor-derived approximations rather than direct compartment-specific measures. We aimed to biologically contextualize NODDI-DTI estimates by examining their associations with plasma biomarkers and follow-up cognition and to assess their correspondence with multi-shell NODDI in an independent cohort. Single-shell diffusion MRI, clinical and plasma biomarker data from 42 older adults were obtained from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative 3 (ADNI3) database. We tested associations between diffusion metrics and plasma biomarkers by performing an exploratory voxel-wise analysis to characterize the spatial distribution and the percentage of statistically significant associations across the WM skeleton and tract-based analyses in a priori AD-vulnerable WM pathways. We additionally tested whether baseline NODDI-DTI metrics and plasma biomarkers were associated with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) performance at a mean 4.8-year follow-up in 25 participants. In a separate ADNI3 cohort ( n = 103), tract-wise NDI and ODI estimates obtained using NODDI-DTI and multi-shell NODDI were also compared using partial correlations and agreement analyses. pTau181 was the only biomarker showing widespread voxel-wise associations with diffusion metrics. Higher pTau181 was associated with lower NDI. In tract-based analyses, higher plasma pTau181 was associated with lower NDI in the fornix and inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus. Higher plasma NfL was associated with lower NDI and higher ODI in the fornix. Higher baseline ODI in the hippocampal cingulum and higher baseline pTau181 were both associated with worse follow-up cognitive performance. In the independent cohort, corresponding NDI and ODI estimates were correlated across all tracts, although agreement analyses showed negative, tract-dependent mean biases for NODDI-DTI. NODDI-DTI may provide an interpretable framework for summarizing single-shell diffusion variation in relation to AD-relevant biomarkers and cognition, particularly when multi-shell acquisitions are not available. However, its estimates remain closely constrained by the underlying tensor signal and should not be considered independent, compartment-specific or quantitatively interchangeable with multi-shell NODDI measures.

Article.Title: Enhanced leiomyoma organ culture: optimized tissue handling and ready-to-use scaffold
Article.Authors: Vázquez P.; Beltrán-Flores S.; Montes de Oca F.; Delgado A.; Almeida T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Uterine leiomyomas, or fibroids, are the most common benign tumors in women, yet their pathophysiology remains poorly understood because reliable culture models are lacking. Unlike 2D culture, fibroid organ culture preserves driver mutations in smooth muscle cells while maintaining the tumor’s structural integrity, cell interactions, and heterogeneity. This study introduces an enhanced fibroid organ culture that builds on our previous model. Fresh tumor tissues were manually sectioned, placed on commercial scaffolds, and cultured under controlled conditions. Replacing the vibratome with manual slicing made tissue preparation faster and feasible across all fibroid types. Highly porous commercial scaffolds may facilitate nutrient and oxygen exchange, supporting cell viability and reducing apoptosis. This improved model supports broader adoption of fibroid organ culture using commercially available scaffolds, offering a more accessible platform for mechanistic studies and the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.

Article.Title: Lead-free quaternary chalcogenide NaZrCuS3 for efficient thermoelectric energy conversion: insights from first-principles and Boltzmann transport
Article.Authors: Rabbi M.; Khatun M.
Article.Abstract: A comprehensive first-principles investigation is performed to evaluate the thermoelectric potential of the lead-free quaternary chalcogenide NaZrCuS 3 using density functional theory combined with semiclassical Boltzmann transport formalism. Structural and elastic analyses confirm that NaZrCuS 3 crystallizes in a stable orthorhombic phase with strong lattice rigidity and high thermal stability. Electronic structure calculations reveal a direct band-gap semiconductor with a moderate gap of ~ 0.92 eV, which is favorable for suppressing bipolar conduction at elevated temperatures. Orbital-resolved density of states indicates that hole transport is dominated by Cu–S hybridized states, while electron transport is mainly governed by Zr–S states, leading to pronounced anisotropic transport behavior. Thermoelectric transport analysis shows large Seebeck coefficients and high-power factors, particularly for n -type doping. Notably, within the constant relaxation time approximation and the semi-empirical Slack model for lattice thermal conductivity, a power factor of 17.17 \(\times \) 10 −3 Wm −1 K −2 and a maximum predicted figure of merit of ZT ≈ 0.78 are obtained at 1000 K along the a -axis, indicating promising high-temperature thermoelectric performance within the present theoretical framework. Although the lattice thermal conductivity is relatively high at room temperature, it decreases significantly at elevated temperatures, enhancing overall efficiency. These results suggest NaZrCuS 3 as a promising environmentally benign thermoelectric candidate for high-temperature waste-heat recovery and provide a theoretical foundation for future experimental validation and performance optimization.

Article.Title: Repeated intra-articular injections of human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells at 3-week intervals enhanced cartilage preservation in a rabbit model of knee osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Lei J.; Chen Z.; Xie H.; Chen X.; Xu D.; Xu L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mesenchymal stem cell-based therapies are a promising strategy for the regeneration of articular cartilage and management of knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Nevertheless, the comparative therapeutic efficacy of single versus repeated intra-articular injections of human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (haMSCs) for cartilage preservation in animal models of osteoarthritis, particularly in the lateral and medial femoral condyles and intercondylar fossa, remain unclear. This study compared a single‑dose regimen with a two‑dose regimen for knee articular cartilage preservation in a rabbit model of surgically induced KOA. haMSCs were isolated, expanded in culture, and characterized in vitro by flow cytometry and trilineage differentiation assays. KOA was surgically induced via anterior cruciate ligament transection followed by medial and lateral meniscectomy (ACLTM). After surgery, the left knee joints of rabbits received intra-articular injection as follows: the negative control and vehicle control groups respectively received sterile saline and vehicle at weeks 6 and 9; the single-dose group received haMSCs at weeks 6 followed by vehicle at weeks 9; and two-dose group received haMSCs at weeks 6 and 9. Rabbits were sacrificed 18 weeks after surgery, and samples (whole knee joints and femoral condyles) were collected, processed, and analyzed. Changes in knee articular cartilage were assessed by macroscopic examination, histology, and immunohistochemistry. ACLTM induced the degeneration of the femoral condyles and intercondylar fossa, confirming the successful establishment of KOA in rabbits. No abnormal clinical signs were observed following haMSC treatment during the study period. Compared with saline, vehicle, and single-injection treatments, two intra-articular injections of haMSCs produced better macroscopic improvements of femoral condyles, resulting in smoother articular surfaces and improved ICRS scores, along with significantly reduced Mankin scores, particularly in the medial femoral condyle and intercondylar fossa. Immunohistochemistry showed that two haMSC injections enhanced type II collagen expression in articular cartilage, as evidenced by higher H-scores and a larger type II collagen-positive area. In contrast, a single injection achieved only limited improvement. Compared with the single-dose regimen, two intra-articular injections of haMSCs provided superior cartilage matrix preservation in the medial femoral condyle and intercondylar fossa in a rabbit model of KOA, while no improvement was observed in the lateral femoral condyle. These findings suggest that the dosing regimen may influence the cartilage-protective effects of haMSCs.

Article.Title: MLCL: LVLM-guided multi-level contrastive learning for fake news detection
Article.Authors: Li J.; Yan L.; Liu Q.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The widespread dissemination of multi-modal disinformation on social media platforms poses a serious threat to public safety and social stability, elevating the need for automated detection of such content. Although existing studies have started to incorporate multimodal data, effectively modeling cross-modal interactions remains difficult, often leading to insufficient mining of information within individual modalities. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel LVLM-Guided multi-level contrastive learning network (MLCL). Within the textual modality, BERT and CLIP encoders extract features at varying granularities, while ResNet and CLIP encoders capture visual representations. Additionally, a Large Vision-Language Model is leveraged to derive text-based representations that reflect both local details and global contexts from images. We further introduce a multi-level alignment strategy: inside each modality, a normalized InfoNCE loss aligns features from the two encoders to reduce redundancy. Before cross-modal fusion, we jointly align the three modality-level features using both InfoNCE loss and batch-hard triplet loss, thereby explicitly modeling their consistency and relative distance. A modality-wise attention module is also incorporated to adaptively reweight and aggregate features. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that our approach outperforms existing methods, achieving overall accuracy improvements of 2.2% on Weibo and 1.5% on Gossipcop. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Ylh-s/MLCL .

Article.Title: Heat transfer enhancement via nanoparticle radius in non-Newtonian fluid flow around a rotating sphere
Article.Authors: Awan A.; Hussain M.; Ali B.; Ahammad N.; Gamaoun F.; Kafle J.; Nadeem S.
Article.Abstract: Efficient thermal regulation in magnetically actuated rotating systems motivates the examination of non-Newtonian nanofluids with adjustable nanoparticle radii. This study analyzes the time-dependent magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flow of a non-Newtonian nanofluid over a rotating sphere, focusing on the impact of nanoparticle radius variation on fluid flow and thermal transmission. This specific aspect has not previously been addressed for Casson fluid flow over the rotating geometries. The flow governing equations are non-dimensionalized using appropriate similarity transformations and solved numerically via the finite element method (FEM). This work targets three main performance goals: minimizing skin friction (drag), enhancing Nusselt number (heat transmission), and maintaining both thermal and flow stability. The results reveal that the Nusselt number can be enhanced by 40% and skin friction decreased by 25% by reducing the nanoparticle radius from 2.5 nm to 0.5 nm. Furthermore, raise in the Casson parameter from 1.0 to 2.0 leads to an approximate 30% reduction in axial velocity as compared with the Newtonian fluid case. These outcomes offer valuable insights for improving the efficiency of non-Newtonian nanofluid systems in magnetized rotating configurations, with possible uses in advanced material processing and thermal management.

Article.Title: Metamaterial assisted hybrid response from frequency selective surface roll off and leaky wave resonator integrated antenna for underground applications
Article.Authors: Yadav V.; Chakraborty S.; Annavarapu S.; Ghosh A.; Singh L.; Chattopadhyay S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In emerging era of wireless technologies such as cognitive radio, wireless sensor networks etc., designing effective low frequency antennas < 1000 MHz and specifically < 700 remains a significant challenge due to its poor (often negative) gain and severely limited bandwidth (≈ 1%), despite exhibiting fair radiation profile. Therefore, challenges to design antennas suitable for above said applications have been taken up in the present investigation. Unlike, other metamaterial antenna, here, a unique approach is adopted by exploring frequency selective surface (FSS) filtering characteristics by employing simultaneous transmissive and reflective feature to achieve hybrid resonance. Additionally, an integrated leaky wave Fabry Perot type resonator is employed to produce additional distinct resonance. The proposed antenna yields resonances (˂700 MHz) with appreciable bandwidths and positive gains at 462.4 MHz (2.5%), 579 MHz (5.9%) and 663.5 MHz (1.9%) with 1.22, 3.5 and 4 dBi, as is confirmed by both the simulations and measurements.

Article.Title: Peak ground acceleration underestimates narrow-band seismic amplification on mountain slopes
Article.Authors: Chen C.; Iida T.; Kawabe H.; Sato M.; Senna S.; Yamada R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Topographic amplification is widely invoked to explain strong shaking and slope failure in mountainous terrain, yet direct field observations remain limited. Here we analyze 24 regional earthquakes recorded by a four-station strong-motion array spanning a ridge crest, a valley bottom, and two contrasting slope facets on a single ridge in central Japan. Peak ground acceleration (PGA) and frequency-dependent measures reveal markedly different representations of local seismic response. PGA ratios vary among events and are positively associated with epicentral distance; however, earthquake magnitude also increases with distance, so source-size and propagation-distance effects cannot be separated in this catalog. In contrast, the NS slope exhibits a persistent narrow-band station-to-valley Fourier spectral-ratio peak at 3.5–4.0 Hz that remains stable across events and processing choices. Absolute spectra confirm enhanced energy at the slope in this band, while also showing that a relative spectral depression at the valley reference contributes to the large ratio magnitude. Most importantly, the geometric-mean 5%-damped response-spectral ratio reaches 6.67 at 0.277 s (3.61 Hz), compared with a corresponding full-record geometric-mean horizontal PGA ratio of 1.13. These observations show that PGA can substantially under-represent frequency-specific elastic response on mountain slopes, while the responsible mechanism cannot be uniquely attributed to topography or near-surface structure alone.

Article.Title: Elemental profiling of zebrafish (Danio rerio) across developmental stages using ion beam analytical techniques
Article.Authors: Caloni M.; Zaluski A.; Valente C.; Bonan C.; Papaléo R.; Dias J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread use of zebrafish as a biological model, comprehensive baseline elemental data across its developmental stages remain limited. In this work, ion beam analytical techniques were employed to establish the elemental composition of zebrafish larvae and adults under controlled vivarium conditions. The combined use of these techniques enables quantitative elemental analysis and spatially resolved elemental mapping of small biological samples within the same analytical framework, providing an integrated elemental baseline across zebrafish development. We show that most elements detected in zebrafish larvae were retained throughout development into adulthood, whereas Al, Si, Mn, Cu, and Sr were detected only in adults, suggesting progressive accumulation during the life cycle. No significant differences were observed in elemental composition or concentration between sexes. Elemental maps of larvae show a homogeneous spatial distribution for most elements, except for elevated S in the eye’s lenses and increased Ca in the otoliths and the head region, highlighting the early compartmentalisation of certain elements during organ development. The resulting dataset provides a developmental elemental baseline for future environmental, pharmacological, and toxicological studies using zebrafish.

Article.Title: Transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles analysis during human acclimatization to simulated high-altitude hypoxia
Article.Authors: Giannella A.; Mrakic-Sposta S.; Vezzoli A.; Magrini A.; Favero L.; Rigon L.; Khatoon N.; Strapazzon G.; Gatterer H.; Siebenmann C.; Schlittler M.; Ceolotto G.; Malacrida S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hypobaric hypoxia (HH) induces coordinated physiological and molecular responses supporting acclimatization to reduced oxygen availability. However, the temporal integration of blood mRNA and miRNA expression during early HH exposure remains incompletely understood. Eight healthy males were exposed for 72 h to simulated moderate HH (~ 3500 m) in the terraXcube facility. Blood transcriptomic and miRNA profiles were analyzed at baseline and after 12, 24, and 72 h, together with physiological variables, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and circulating inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers. Differential expression analysis revealed a progression from early stress and innate immune responses at 12 h, involving FOSB , CITED4 , and IDO1 , to remodeling of lymphocyte-specific programs at 24 h, including PAX5 , TCF7 , and TNFRSF13C . At 72 h, broader changes involved AP-1 components ( JUN , JUNB , and FOSB ), lymphocyte regulators ( PAX5 and FOXP3 ), and the antioxidant gene SOD2 . Integrated analysis identified predicted miRNA–mRNA pairs displaying inverse expression patterns within these pathways. Notably, miR-486-3p was consistently upregulated and miR-29c-5p downregulated across all time points. Plasma biomarkers remained largely stable, except for a transient increase in ICAM-1 and a marked decrease in TNF-α at 12 h, while ROS increased early and subsequently stabilized. Together, these findings identify distinct but overlapping phases of early HH acclimatization, progressing from stress and innate immune activation to lymphocyte-specific and redox remodeling. Article.Title: A wastewater balance reveals unexpectedly high TFA input from human water use
Article.Authors: Frenzel I.; Hilgert P.; Herbstritt B.; Nöltge D.; Müller M.; Lange J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Trifluoroacetate (TFA) is a member of the PFAS group and shares their persistence. Its very small molecular size and anionic character makes it, in contrast to many other PFAS, highly water-soluble and mobile in the aquatic environment. Wastewater shows elevated TFA concentrations. This TFA may stem from background sources such as drinking water, infiltrating groundwater, or rainwater. It may also come from human water use itself. To quantify a potential TFA surplus, we built a mass balance at three rural sewer sites in Freiburg, Germany. End-member mixing analysis yielded TFA loads from groundwater and drinking water. Flow comparisons between dry and rain-event conditions yielded the TFA load from rainwater. Groundwater and drinking water contributed the largest background TFA load at two sanitary sewers. During a storm event rainwater dominated the TFA load in the combined sewer despite diluting its concentration. At every site, human water use exceeded the sum of the three background sources and made up the largest share of the TFA load. TFA concentrations also peaked during the morning wastewater surge at every site. We attribute this surplus mainly to human excretion of ingested TFA from food and drink. However, a comparison with an approximate dietary TFA intake estimate shows that this source alone cannot explain the observed surplus. Other sources, such as cosmetic products, may contribute to the overall TFA load in the sewer. Our study highlights the need for more data on human TFA uptake and excretion, as well as on other potential sources of TFA in human water use.

Article.Title: Prediction of fast, slow, and average shear-wave velocities from well logs using artificial neural networks and statistical regression
Article.Authors: Teymouri H.; Nikrouz R.; Ciabeghodsi A.; Kadkhodaie A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of fast, slow, and average shear-wave velocities (Vs Fast , Vs Slow , and Vs Average ) is important for evaluating reservoir anisotropy, fracture networks, and stress regimes. In this study, multivariate statistical regression and artificial neural network (ANN) models were developed and compared to predict these velocity components in a well from the Sarvak Formation, Zagros Basin, Iran. The initial dataset comprised 3,234 depth points, of which 2,264 valid points were retained after data preprocessing and normalization. Compressional-wave velocity (Vp), neutron porosity (NPHI), and bulk density (RHOB) were used as input variables. For the statistical models, 70% of the data were used for calibration and 30% for testing, whereas the ANN employed a feedforward backpropagation architecture trained using the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm, with 70, 15, and 15% of the data allocated to training, validation, and testing, respectively. The statistical models achieved test-set R² values of 0.769129, 0.616225, and 0.725904 for Vs fast , Vs slow and Vs Average , respectively, while the corresponding ANN models achieved R² values of 0.786769, 0.641601, and 0.727609. The ANN therefore provided modest improvements over statistical regression, with the largest improvement observed for Vs Fast and Vs slow . Minor discrepancies at lower velocity ranges may reflect local geological complexities, including intense fracturing. Overall, the proposed approach, particularly the ANN models, provides a practical indirect method for estimating shear-wave velocity components from conventional well logs and may support reservoir characterization where direct dipole-shear measurements are unavailable.

Article.Title: Discovery and promotion of unknown sounds into operational detection targets for underwater passive acoustic monitoring under false alarm constraints
Article.Authors: Noda T.; Koizumi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Earth’s oceans cover 70% of the planet yet remain among the least observed regions. Underwater acoustics is a primary sensing modality, but recordings span biological, anthropogenic and natural sounds while labels remain sparse. We present an unknownness-aware monitoring framework for underwater acoustic sensing platforms: it adapts a pre-trained audio representation model to underwater soundscapes, defines an embedding-space unknownness score, and couples it with detector outputs in a Detect–Group–Promote–Union (DGPU) loop tuned under false positives per hour (FP/h) constraints: Detect surfaces candidate events from continuous audio; Group clusters unknown candidates in embedding space; Promote trains lightweight classifiers from sparse expert labels on selected clusters; and Union combines baseline and promoted detectors. Across a 56-class underwater Sound Event Detection (SED) benchmark and two cetacean field datasets, the framework attains a dataset-level bandwidth-matched out-of-distribution AUROC of 1.000 on Hawaiian survey data (HICEAS), raises right-whale upcall detection recall on continuous recordings (FRDR) from 0.027 to 0.390 at FP/h ≈ 10 with a supervised Promoter, with 300 labelled events (~ 32% of training-fold labels) reaching 0.37 (95% of the full-label recall), and classifies seven HICEAS cetacean species with the Promoter classifier alone (AUC 0.924–0.992 within-day and 0.51–0.97 cross-day with a fixed classifier), supporting stethoscope-like ocean monitoring.

Article.Title: Effectiveness of post-capture escape tactics in juvenile Japanese eels against various predatory fishes
Article.Authors: Hasegawa Y.; Yang W.; Kawabata Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although rare, it is possible for some prey species to actively escape from the digestive tract of predators after being captured. Because these tactics involve escaping after being swallowed by the predator, they are likely constrained by predator-specific factors. However, the limits of the effectiveness and the predator-specific factors that influence its success remain poorly understood. This study examined the effectiveness of a post-capture defensive tactic of juvenile Japanese eels, Anguilla japonica , in which they escape through the predator’s gills by navigating backward from the stomach. We evaluated the escape success of eels through predation experiments using six predator species that differ in habitat, swimming styles, and feeding styles (biting or suction feeding). The results indicated that eels escaped via the gills of all five suction-feeding predators examined (32%, 114/359), including Odontobutidae, Sebastidae, Lateolabracidae, Cyprinidae, and larger conspecific Japanese eels. In contrast, eels never escaped from the grass puffer Takifugu alboplumbeus (Tetraodontidae), the only biting-type predator, as the eels were torn into small pieces and consumed. Our results suggest that post-capture escape in eels is effective against diverse predator species encountered in nature. Meanwhile, predators that bite and kill prey before swallowing, such as tetraodontid fishes, may pose a greater threat to juvenile eels.

Article.Title: Comparative assessment of measurement uncertainty for ICP-MS determination of platinum and palladium in ore using tolerance intervals and ISO 11352
Article.Authors: Lambarki L.; El Hajji R.; El-Ghaly W.; El Kamli T.; Bourass M.; Ihssane B.; Bakkali F.; Saffaj T.; Jhilal F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate determination of platinum (Pt) and palladium (Pd) in ore matrices remains analytically challenging due to matrix complexity, spectral interferences, and the ultra-trace concentrations at which these elements naturally occur. This work presents the development and full validation of an inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) method for the simultaneous quantification of Pt and Pd in ore samples, using lead fire assay with cupellation as the preconcentration step. Validation was performed using a β-content, γ-confidence tolerance interval strategy, which integrates method validation and measurement uncertainty estimation into a single coherent framework, without requiring additional experimental data beyond routine validation work. A simple linear regression calibration model was selected based on systematic evaluation of uncertainty profiles across the working concentration range. Trueness, expressed as relative bias, did not exceed − 2.03% for either element at any concentration level, and recovery was within the predefined acceptance criteria of ± 15%. Measurement uncertainty was subsequently assessed using two complementary top-down approaches: the uncertainty profile method and the ISO 11352 framework. Statistical comparison by Fisher’s F-test demonstrated that the two approaches yield statistically equivalent uncertainty estimates when the proportion β is set to 90% or 95%, establishing this threshold as the minimum requirement for reliable prediction of routine analytical performance from validation data. These findings confirm that the uncertainty profile approach constitutes a practical and resource-efficient alternative to ISO 11352 for laboratories involved in platinum-group element analysis, enabling simultaneous method validation and uncertainty characterization from a single experimental dataset.

Article.Authors: Zendehdel E.; Loghman-Estarki M.; Li Z.; Davar F.; Jamali H.

Mechanical response was quantified through three-point bending tests and Vickers indentation, whereas polymerization shrinkage was determined in line with ISO 17304 guidelines. At the 5 wt.% level, however, observable particle agglomeration occurred, which was accompanied by a pronounced deterioration in overall properties. Meanwhile, a consistent drop in polymerization shrinkage was noted with increasing filler loading. A side-by-side comparison against commercially available resin‑based composites reveals that the newly developed ScYSZ-reinforced nanohybrid achieves an attractive trade-off between enhanced mechanical strength and lower volumetric shrinkage, underscoring its viability as a high-performance flowable material for restorative dentistry applications.

Article.Title: Ontogenetic shifts, trophic differentiation, and predator–prey size relationships in Oxyrhopus false coral snakes from Bahia, Brazil
Article.Authors: De la Quintana P.; Solé M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although snakes of the genus Oxyrhopus are generally regarded as opportunistic predators, the relative roles of interspecific dietary differentiation, ontogenetic variation, and predator morphology in their feeding ecology remain poorly understood. Juveniles consumed predominantly lizards, whereas adults incorporated proportionally more mammals and birds. Prey size increased with snake body size, whereas ontogenetic stage itself was not consistently associated with prey size. Head width was positively associated with prey width, indicating a relationship between predator cranial dimensions and prey dimensions. Because specimens were collected across different localities and were not necessarily syntopic, the observed differences should not be interpreted as direct evidence of local resource partitioning or competition. Overall, our results highlight interspecific and ontogenetic variation in prey use and provide a comparative assessment of dietary patterns and predator–prey size relationships in Oxyrhopus from Bahia.

Article.Title: A support vector machine classifier of PM₂.₅-based air quality index categories from co-pollutants and meteorological variables in Ahvaz, Iran
Article.Authors: Soltani F.; Soltani A.; Jaafarzadeh N.; Soltani N.; Talepour N.
Article.Abstract: Ahvaz, in southwestern Iran, experiences some of the most severe particulate air pollution in the world, driven by Middle Eastern Dust events, industrial emissions, and traffic. Continuous monitoring of fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is essential for public-health protection, yet PM₂.₅ monitors in the region frequently suffer outages and data gaps. This study evaluates whether the PM₂.₅-based Air Quality Index (AQI) category can be estimated from routinely measured co-pollutants (O₃, NO, NO₂, SO₂, CO, and PM₁₀) and meteorological variables (air temperature, dew point, relative humidity, wind speed, and wind direction), providing a surrogate risk label when direct PM₂.₅ measurements are unavailable. Hourly observations from the Naderi monitoring station in Ahvaz (October 2014 – July 2017) were aggregated into 3-hour intervals; each interval with at least two of three observed hourly PM₂.₅ values was labelled with one of six AQI categories using the U.S. EPA PM₂.₅ breakpoints in force during the study period, yielding 7,509 samples. A class-weighted radial-basis-function Support Vector Machine (SVM) was tuned by rolling-origin cross-validation within the training period (October 2014 – January 2017) and evaluated on a strictly held-out chronological test period (January – July 2017), alongside multinomial logistic regression, linear SVM, random forest, and gradient boosting baselines trained under identical protocols. On the unseen test period, the SVM achieved an exact-category accuracy of 0.633, macro-averaged F1 of 0.38, Cohen’s κ of 0.47, and quadratic-weighted κ of 0.61; 94.5% of predictions fell within one category of the truth, and misclassifications concentrated between adjacent categories. The random forest baseline performed best overall (accuracy 0.674; quadratic-weighted κ of 0.70; 97.7% within one category). Permutation importance and ablation experiments identified PM₁₀ as the dominant predictor: excluding it reduced SVM accuracy from 0.633 to 0.431, while PM₁₀ alone reached 0.523. Performance for the rare extreme categories (Very Unhealthy and Hazardous) remained limited and is reported transparently. At this station and over this period, co-pollutant and meteorological measurements—chiefly PM₁₀—can provide an operationally useful, near-real-time surrogate for the PM₂.₅ AQI category when the PM₂.₅ channel fails, while underscoring that such a surrogate cannot replace properly maintained PM₂.₅ instrumentation, particularly for extreme pollution episodes.

Article.Title: An explainable vision transformer approach for automated neurological disorder classification from brain MRI scans
Article.Authors: Alahmadi A.; Asim N.; Khan M.; Sirshar M.; Aljubayri I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diagnosing Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), Multiple Sclerosis (MS), and brain tumors early enough to matter still depends heavily on brain MRI, and brain MRI still depends on radiologists who are in short supply almost everywhere. Convolutional neural networks have made real progress on this problem, but a single convolution only sees a small patch of the image, which limits how well a purely convolutional model can tie together pathology that is spread across the brain. This study addresses that limitation from two directions at once: a controlled, same-protocol comparison of established CNN backbones, and a lightweight attention mechanism grafted onto one of them. We classify the full eight-class Multi-Class Neurological Disorder (MCND) dataset (AD MildDemented, AD ModerateDemented, AD VeryMildDemented, Multiple Sclerosis, Normal, and three brain-tumor subtypes: glioma, meningioma, and pituitary), comprising 9,564 MRI images split 80:20 into 7,651 training and 1,913 test images. Four established CNNs, VGG-16, ResNet-50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNet-B0, were fine-tuned under one shared protocol to serve as controlled baselines. We then built VGG-16 + CBAM: a VGG16 backbone fitted with a Convolutional Block Attention Module and a much smaller classification head in place of VGG-16’s original fully connected layers, trained for 15 epochs under the same optimizer and augmentation settings used for the baselines. It reached 98.90% accuracy, a weighted F1-score of 0.9890, a macro F1 of 0.9893, a macro AUC-ROC of 0.9997, and an MCC of 0.9874 on the held-out test set, beating all four baselines (98.12%–98.85% accuracy) while using just 14.88 million parameters, roughly 9% of VGG-16’s 134.29 million, for a 56.8 MB model. We also report parameter counts, model size, FLOPs, GPU inference latency, and training time for every baseline, so the accuracy gain can be weighed against actual computational cost rather than accuracy alone. Grad-CAM maps for all eight classes show the model focusing on plausible anatomical regions: periventricular and hippocampal areas for the AD stages, white matter for MS, and the tumor core for each tumor subtype. A t-SNE projection of the learned features shows the eight classes forming distinct, mostly non-overlapping clusters. Taken together, the results suggest a small, attention-augmented CNN can match or beat larger backbones on this task at a fraction of the cost, without losing the interpretability a clinician would need to trust it.

Article.Title: Climate change and the weather-energy Nexus in US energy demand
Article.Authors: Akadiri S.; Awosusi A.; Sendi A.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the long-run and short-run elasticities of U.S. residential and commercial final energy consumption with respect to historical variations in heating and cooling degree days and compares these weather sensitivities across sectors. We also use a Fourier-augmented Toda–Yamamoto procedure to examine directional predictive relationships. The results confirm long-run equilibrium relationships in both sectors. Heating degree days have positive, significant long-run effects on residential and commercial energy consumption. Cooling degree days become significant when we include the heating–cooling interaction term. The interaction coefficient is negative and significant, indicating that joint heating and cooling exposure has an attenuating, non-additive association with annual energy consumption. Because we include the interaction term, we interpret the estimated HDD and CDD coefficients as conditional effects rather than unconditional elasticities. Residential energy demand adjusts to disequilibrium approximately three times faster than commercial demand. The causality results indicate directional predictive relationships from HDD to commercial consumption and from CHDD to residential consumption. Overall, the findings provide evidence on historical weather–energy relationships and offer implications for demand forecasting, grid planning, and energy-efficiency policy, but do not constitute a formal counterfactual attribution of energy changes to climate change.

Article.Authors: Sadeghi Chemeh P.; Jam S.

The structure employs a 90°-rotated and y-mirrored bilayer arrangement, whose interlayer coupling induces effective magnetoelectric interactions and enables efficient cross-polarization conversion. For backward incidence, the polarizer provides y-to-x polarization conversion across the operating band, and the conversion direction reverses under forward incidence. The resulting asymmetric transmission reaches a peak value of 0.93. To provide a physics-oriented interpretation, the effective electric, magnetic, and magnetoelectric surface susceptibilities are retrieved using a complete reciprocity-constrained tangential GSTC model. The retrieved tensors provide a macroscopic description of the coupled anisotropic and bianisotropic response. Surface-current distributions complement this macroscopic description by indicating electric- and magnetic-type current excitations associated with polarization conversion. A fitted Foster equivalent-circuit model provides a compact circuit-level representation of the dispersive CST response. A fabricated prototype is experimentally characterized. The normal-incidence measurements show reasonable overall agreement with the simulated polarization-conversion and AT responses. Taken together, the combined performance characteristics and the physics-oriented interpretation of the conversion mechanism demonstrate its potential for broadband microwave polarization-control applications.

Article.Title: Sustainable production of critical components for the oil and gas industry
Article.Authors: Kusyi Y.; Ivanov V.; Horbal N.; Kostiuk O.; Klymash I.; Onysko O.; Zajac J.
Article.Abstract: This research addresses the need for sustainable manufacturing and quality assurance of high-load components in the oil and gas sector within the frameworks of Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0. A methodology was developed to analyze technological inheritability by evaluating the transfer and transformation of surface roughness parameters throughout the manufacturing route, from rough boring to final plastic deformation finishing (PDF). Volumetric vibratory equipment was adapted specifically to treat the hard-to-access internal surfaces of these critical components. The arithmetic mean deviation of the profile (Ra) decreased nearly tenfold, from 6.12 to 0.63 μm, while the ten-point height of irregularities (Rz) decreased by approximately 17-fold, reaching 1.38 μm. In addition, the load-bearing capacity of the surface was improved, as indicated by a 1.7-fold increase in the relative bearing length (tm). At the same time, the spacing parameters RS and RSm decreased by more than fourfold. The analysis of technological inheritability identified VCH as a critical technological barrier that effectively transforms the inherited surface characteristics and promotes the formation of a surface state with improved functional properties. The developed technology aligns with the principles of sustainable manufacturing. It supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 9, 12, and 13 by eliminating the use of potentially hazardous cutting fluids and abrasive materials, reducing energy demand, and minimizing material waste. The findings demonstrate the potential of integrating vibratory-centrifugal hardening into the manufacturing route of NB 32.02.102-04 cylinder liners as an environmentally responsible finishing strategy. At the same time, further research is required to establish its effects on wear resistance, fatigue strength, and the long-term reliability of critical industrial components.

Article.Authors: Citakoglu H.; Aslan S.; Herdem S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examined advanced machine learning models to predict key volumetric parameters of stone mastic asphalt (SMA) mixtures incorporating waste tire rubber. The input parameters were rubber aggregate and rubber modifier. The target outputs were air void, voids filled with asphalt, voids in mineral aggregate, and density. A total of 216 asphalt samples were prepared, representing 72 distinct mixture combinations, as three replicate samples were produced for each condition. Five machine learning techniques—Gaussian Process Regression, Support Vector Machine Regression (SVR), Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System, Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines, and Least Squares Support Vector Machines (LS-SVR) were implemented, and models were evaluated using the 5-fold cross-validation method. Model performance was assessed using mean absolute error, root mean square error, determination coefficient, Wilmott’s refined index, NSE (Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency coefficient), overall index, CA (Combined Accuracy), and RRMSE (relative root mean square error) indices. The LS-SVR model was found to achieve the best predictive performance across all four outputs, with an RRMSE value below 10%, an NSE value greater than 0.9, and a CA value closest to zero. Furthermore, the results show that LS-SVR provides the closest fit to the experimental data and the lowest error levels. In contrast, the standard SVR model produced the weakest predictions, with the widest error distributions and highest deviations. Transforming SVR into LS-SVR significantly improved accuracy. However, the use of only two input variables in this study represents a deliberate simplification that limits the generalizability of the model to broad applications. Consequently, this research is primarily positioned as a proof-of-concept investigation to demonstrate the applicability of ML to a controlled laboratory dataset. Furthermore, the lack of external (independent) validation prevents the developed models from being interpreted as universal predictive tools in practical asphalt mix design. Therefore, the results show that the models successfully capture the relationships between rubber content and volumetric properties within the narrow range of laboratory parameters examined in this study. For broader applications, the inclusion of additional inputs and testing with independent datasets are necessary; these steps will allow for stronger inferences about the actual generalization performance of the models.

Article.Title: Genome-wide CRISPR screening reveals a chromatin-to-mitochondrial dependency architecture underlying Galunisertib-induced OXPHOS vulnerability
Article.Authors: Akla N.; Boudah A.; Faye M.; Danalache B.; Annabi B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Galunisertib (LY2157299), a selective TGF‑βRI/ALK5 inhibitor with limited single‑agent Phase II efficacy, was used as a pharmacological probe to ask whether sustained Galunisertib exposure reorganizes cellular dependencies toward an OXPHOS-associated state. A genome‑wide CRISPR‑Cas9 loss‑of‑function chemogenomic screen was performed in Galunisertib‑treated NALM‑6 pre‑B leukemia cells and analyzed with CRANKS scoring, Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis, STRING network mapping, subcellular compartment annotation, and MitoCarta3.0/MitoPathways3.0 cross‑referencing. Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) was the only Hallmark gene set significantly enriched after correction for multiple testing, and mitochondrial compartments, mitochondrial gene expression and mitochondrial translation were enriched among genes whose loss improved fitness under treatment. Prioritized hits resolved into a layered architecture in which a chromatin-associated transcriptional module, anchored by the high-confidence sensitizer TCF4, is coupled to post-transcriptional regulation of mRNA metabolism and to genes maintaining membrane and ionic homeostasis, converging on mitochondrial gene expression and translation as the terminal layer. Resistance-associated genes defined two routes out of this state: altered chromatin remodeling, and loss of mitochondrial translation or iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis. These dependencies derive from a single high-dose chemogenomic screen and await confirmation by individual gene perturbation or by direct metabolic measurement. Within that limit, the screen defines a reorganization of cellular dependencies under sustained Galunisertib exposure and nominates chromatin, post-transcriptional and OXPHOS-directed combinations as priority candidates for validation.
