Article.Title: Retrospective modelling of space-time clusters of acute gastrointestinal syndromes in Lombardy, Italy
Article.Authors: Corrao G.; Crippa D.; Sguazzini E.; Conflitti C.; Bagarella G.; Maistrello M.; Covizzi A.; Colombo F.; Cereda D.; Gori A.; Franchi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gastrointestinal (GI) syndrome encompasses complex symptoms characterised by preventability, high morbidity, and relatively low mortality. We conducted this study to investigate the ability of syndromic surveillance for detecting space–time clusters of acute GI syndromes in Lombardy, Italy. The target population included the 10 million beneficiaries of the Regional Health Service during 2023. Individuals who experienced at least one Emergency Department (ED) admission for GI syndrome in 2023 were considered the main syndromic cases of interest, with retrospective data obtained from healthcare utilization databases. Two secondary case definitions, based on reports of GI infective disorders and drug dispensations for treating GI disorders, were also used. Daily data at the level of all 86 health districts composing Lombardy Region were monitored. By comparing observed and expected cases, space–time scan statistics were used to detect clusters within specific time frames and areas. Analyses were performed using SaTScan software. In 2023, 33.3 cases per 100,000 person-weeks were admitted to the ED for GI disorders. Based on the secondary definitions of cases, detection rates of 0.42 and 19.2 cases every 100,000 person-week were observed, respectively. Overall, 11 clusters were detected across 17 health districts, with durations ranging from 1 to 3 days. Clear positive linear trends were observed across the 86 health districts between ED-based rates and the corresponding reporting-based and drug-based rates. A syndromic surveillance system for acute GI syndromes is a promising tool for supporting policymakers in anticipating the emergence of new epidemics and evaluating the impact of actions aimed at reducing the risk of acute GI disturbances in endemic areas.

Article.Title: A hybrid machine learning framework integrating persian NLP for occupational risk classification in steel manufacturing
Article.Authors: Alamshah E.; Soleimani-Alyar M.; Hanifi S.; Jafari B.; Behravesh M.
Article.Abstract: Human error remains a leading cause of occupational accidents in high-risk industries, yet traditional risk assessment methods often overlook valuable information embedded in unstructured textual data. This study develops and validates a hybrid machine learning framework combining structured risk data with Natural Language Processing (NLP) to improve hazard classification accuracy in industrial settings. Data were collected from 258 work activities across 16 operational units in a steel manufacturing facility over five months, yielding 3,110 validated risk scenarios. Hazard identification employed Job Safety Analysis (JSA), while quantitative risk evaluation used the William Fine method. The dataset comprised structured variables (severity, exposure, probability) and unstructured Persian-language text (hazard descriptions, locations, activities). Text preprocessing included tokenization, stopword removal, stemming, and lemmatization. Features were extracted using TF-IDF vectorization for all models. Random Over-Sampling (ROS) addressed class imbalance. Four traditional machine learning algorithms were evaluated: Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM). On unbalanced data, SVM achieved the highest accuracy (93%), with F1-scores of 0.96, 0.83, and 0.92 for low, medium, and high-risk categories, respectively. After ROS balancing, performance showed practical improvements across most models, particularly for minority risk classes; however, the difference did not reach conventional statistical significance (p = 0.189), likely due to the small comparison sample (n = 3 models). SVM reached near-perfect classification, whereas KNN remained the weakest performer. The hybrid framework significantly outperforms traditional risk assessment methods by leveraging both structured data and unstructured textual information. The prevalence of low-risk scenarios (66.1%) suggests effective existing safety controls, while improved classification of medium and high-risk cases enables targeted interventions. This approach provides a foundation for real-time AI-driven safety monitoring systems in high-risk industrial sectors.

Article.Title: Nanoformulated silymarin enhances antifungal activity against resistant Candida albicans by reducing ergosterol and binding to cell envelope targets
Article.Authors: Ghodrati M.; Sharifzadeh A.; Fasaei B.; Malakootikhah J.; Koli A.; Khosravi A.
Article.Abstract: The increasing prevalence of antifungal resistance in Candida albicans poses significant challenges in managing candidiasis. Silymarin, a flavonolignan mixture derived from milk thistle ( Silybum marianum ), has shown promising antimicrobial properties in prior research. Here, we evaluated the in vitro antifungal activity of free silymarin and its nanoencapsulated form against ten C. albicans isolates, including nine fluconazole-resistant clinical isolates and one reference strain. Nanocapsules were prepared and characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and zeta potential measurements, yielding particles with mean diameters of 119.75 nm (SEM) and 157.5 nm (DLS), a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.407 and a highly negative zeta potential of − 77.9 mV. Susceptibility testing followed CLSI guidelines, revealing that nanoencapsulation improved efficacy: geometric mean minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) decreased from 7578.6 µg/mL (free silymarin) to 4061.3 µg/mL (nanosilymarin), while minimum fungicidal concentrations (MFCs) dropped from 15,157.2 to 7578.6 µg/mL. At sub-MIC levels, nanosilymarin reduced cellular ergosterol content to an extent similar to that observed with itraconazole, as measured by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Molecular docking simulations further indicated robust interactions of silymarin with key targets involved in cell wall integrity and ergosterol biosynthesis (namely Chs2, Erg11, and the transcription factor Upc2) with favorable binding energies of − 10.81, − 10.62, and − 12.84 kcal/mol, respectively. These results suggest that nanoformulation can enhance the antifungal action of silymarin against resistant C. albicans strains, likely through interference with ergosterol production and selective protein targeting.

Article.Title: Surface-modified magnetic polymeric–silver nanocomposites for broad-spectrum antibacterial applications
Article.Authors: Doan L.; Hoang L.; Nguyen K.; Dang Q.; Vo H.; Nguyen T.; Huynh K.
Article.Abstract: Magnetic antimicrobial nanocomposites have potential for applications in healthcare, food safety, and environmental settings. This study describes the synthesis of a multifunctional nanocomposite combining SPIONs with polylactic acid, an M8 polymer blend including PVA, PEG, PVP and chitosan, along with AgNPs to enhance antimicrobial activity while retaining potential for magnetic recovery. Strategies of surface modification, including carbon coating, SeNPs and chloramphenicol loading, were also systematically compared. Overall, SPION/PLA/M8Ag achieved > 92% OD-derived growth inhibition against Staphylococcus aureus , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Salmonella enterica , and Escherichia coli without antibiotic loading. This was supported by physicochemical characterization (FE-SEM, XRD, FTIR, EDS and VSM), which revealed particle sizes of 12–24 nm, retention of the magnetite-like crystalline phase after surface functionalization, and superparamagnetism indicating potential for magnetic separation and recovery. These findings suggest that SPION/PLA/M8Ag may serve as a promising research platform for antibiotic-free antimicrobial materials.

Article.Title: Impact of Leishmania RNA virus 2 on immune response and pathogenesis in Leishmania major-infected BALB/c mice
Article.Authors: Riazi-rad F.; Katebi A.; Pakzad S.; Ajdary S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Leishmania RNA virus (LRV)1 has been associated with altered disease outcomes in cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL), but the role of LRV2 in Leishmania major ( L. major ) infection remains poorly understood. This study investigated the impact of LRV2-positive L. major (Lm-LRV2 + ) on disease progression and host immune responses. J774A.1 macrophages were infected with Lm-LRV2 + or LRV2 - (Lm-LRV2 - ) parasites, and cytokine gene expression was measured by qPCR. BALB/c mice were inoculated subcutaneously with either strain; lesion development was monitored weekly, and parasite burden, cytokine responses (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-17 A), and humoral responses (IgG, IgG1, IgG2a) were assessed. Macrophages infected with Lm-LRV2 + showed significantly elevated IL-6 and IL-1β mRNA levels compared to Lm-LRV2 - ( p < 0.01). In vivo, Lm-LRV2 + infection resulted in larger lesions and higher parasite loads ( p < 0.01). Lymphocytes from Lm-LRV2 + mice produced significantly more IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-17 A at eight weeks ( p < 0.05), and antigen-specific IgG responses and IgG2a/IgG1 ratios were also increased. These findings demonstrate that LRV2 presence in L. major enhances pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and drives a more severe disease phenotype, with notable shifts in both cellular and humoral immunity. Our results underscore the critical role of LRV2 in CL pathogenesis and suggest that viral endosymbionts may serve as important modulators of disease outcomes in Leishmania infections.

Article.Title: Explainable deep learning for SEM-based classification of six Sclerodermataceae taxa
Article.Authors: Kumru E.; Aydoğan A.; Akarkamçi H.; Ekinci F.; Sevindik M.; Akata I.; Güzel M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate identification of closely related fungal species remains challenging because of substantial morphological similarities and overlapping diagnostic characters. This study evaluated explainable deep learning approaches for the image-level classification of six predefined Sclerodermataceae taxa using scanning electron microscope (SEM) images of fungal spores An original dataset consisting of 961 SEM micrographs representing Scleroderma areolatum , S. cepa , S. bovista , S. polyrhizum , S. verrucosum , and Pisolithus arhizus was constructed under specimen-preparation protocol. Image preprocessing included grayscale conversion, brightness normalization, histogram equalization, and annotation removal. The dataset was divided into training, validation, and test subsets, and data augmentation was applied to improve model generalization. Nine pretrained convolutional neural network architectures, including ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, RegNet-Y8GF, ConvNeXt-Small, SENet-154, VGG-16, Inception-V3, Xception, and EfficientNet-B3, were comparatively evaluated using identical training conditions. Performance assessment was conducted using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Matthews correlation coefficient, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, balanced accuracy, Cohen’s kappa, expected calibration error, and brier score. ResNet-50 achieved the highest classification performance with 99.48% accuracy, 99.49% precision, 99.48% recall, 99.48% F1-score, and 99.38% MCC, misclassifying only one test sample. Grad-CAM++ and occlusion sensitivity analyses suggested that model attention was predominantly associated with biologically relevant spore ornamentation regions. These findings support the applicability of SEM-based deep learning and qualitative XAI approaches for image-level classification among the six predefined Sclerodermataceae taxa examined under the present experimental conditions.

Article.Title: Effect of 1-min versus 3-min epinephrine dosing regimens on 48-h survival in a porcine cardiac arrest model
Article.Authors: Ahn G.; Lee J.; Roh Y.; Jung W.; Lee Y.; Im H.; Hwang S.; Cha K.
Article.Abstract: The optimal epinephrine redosing interval during advanced life support remains uncertain. We randomized 48 Yorkshire pigs with ventricular fibrillation (VF) cardiac arrest to intravenous epinephrine 0.02 mg/kg every 1 or 3 min, with first defibrillation at 20 or 24 min. Survival (70.8% vs 33.3%; P = 0.020) and sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) (75.0% vs 33.3%; P = 0.008) were higher with the 1-min regimen than with the 3-min regimen. After adjustment for first-defibrillation timing, the 1-min regimen was associated with a lower hazard of death within 48 h (hazard ratio, 0.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.13–0.78), higher odds of sustained ROSC (odds ratio [OR], 5.40; 95% CI, 1.68–19.29), and a more favorable composite 48-h neurological deficit score, with deaths assigned 400 (common OR, 4.66; 95% CI, 1.49–15.90). Pressure–time integrals for systolic, diastolic, and mean blood pressure differed in rank-based but not permutation analyses. In this porcine model, the 1-min epinephrine dosing regimen was associated with higher 48-h survival and a more favorable composite 48-h neurological deficit score. However, clinical translation requires further study because dosing interval was inseparable from cumulative exposure and defibrillation timing was protocol-defined.

Article.Title: A decentralized multi-agent-based optimization framework for intelligent traffic systems
Article.Authors: Basingab M.
Article.Abstract: The increasing complexity of urban transportation has increased the importance of intelligent traffic systems (ITS). Conventional approaches, such as fixed-time control (STS), rule-based adaptive control (RBAC), and centralized optimization (CTO), struggle with traffic demand, and network complexity. These limitations highlight the need for decentralized control strategies. To address this challenge, this study proposes a Decentralized Agent-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Traffic Optimization (DAB-MARLTO) framework for smart traffic networks. The framework modeled urban road as a directed graph where vehicles, traffic signals, and road segments operate as autonomous agents. Traffic demand is modeled using a Poisson arrival process, while vehicle behavior is simulated via car-following, lane-changing, and queue models. Each signalized intersection is modeled as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and optimized using decentralized tabular Q-learning (QL). The framework is implemented in Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) via Traffic Control Interface (TraCI) policy execution. Performance metrics include Average Travel Time (ATT), throughput, average queue length, Congestion Index (CI), fuel consumption, and emission intensity. Results show DAB-MARLTO outperforms STS, RBAC, and CTO by reducing network delay, queue length, and congestion while improving efficiency. The framework achieves a 26.9% reduction in travel time, 46.4% reduction in queue length, 33.3% improvement in congestion index, and 27.4% increase in network throughput.

Article.Title: Reactive power sharing between parallel VSI into islanded microgrid based on PSO algorithm
Article.Authors: Shamkhi A.; Jasim B.; Alhasnawi B.; Jasim A.; Homod R.; Dočekalová A.; Bureš V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract For islanded microgrids, the power sharing and frequency restoration significantly influence MG stability and reliability. This paper proposes a control strategy based on the PSO algorithm to modify a conventional droop control method. The active power sharing between parallel connected VSI can be ensured accurately by selecting a proper value of gain of p-f droop equation at each DG controller, but this produces a small steady-state frequency deviation. On the other hand, a proper selection of the gain of the Q-V droop equation cannot ensure accurate reactive power sharing. This paper proposed a centralized control strategy to compensate steady-state voltage and frequency error and ensure reactive power sharing between DGs into islanded MG. In this paper, a PSO algorithm is adopted to calculate the parameters of the PI controller of each DG unit, thus making system operation more stable and efficient for both transient response and a steady-state period. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy in terms of active and reactive power sharing and frequency restoration accuracy compared to a conventional droop method.

Article.Title: Clinical and histopathological patterns of American cutaneous leishmaniasis: diagnostic and therapeutic implications for targeted therapy
Article.Authors: Rosette V.; Drak Alsibai K.; Pierre-Demar M.; Lebret J.; Blaizot R.; Grotta G.
Article.Abstract: American cutaneous leishmaniasis (ACL) is a neglected tropical disease that is endemic in French Guiana. While the proportion of treatment failures is high, the risk factors are poorly understood. Although histological analysis of ACL has been described, few studies have investigated its correlation with severity or response to treatment in America. Our objectives were to provide a precise dermatological description of the clinical forms, investigate the association between histological and clinical characteristics, and determine their links with treatment failure to guide new therapeutics. Among the 1,577 patients with positive analysis for cutaneous leishmaniasis in French Guiana between 2016 and 2024, 268 patients with available histological examination were included, of whom 245 had a confirmed ACL diagnosis with 80 pictures available. A negative parasite load was associated with large lesions (> 3 cm), gold mining and immunosuppression. The presence of papular lesions, more than five lesions and lower limb involvement were significantly associated with a poorer response to treatment. When classified according to the picture-based classification, the papulo-nodular form tended to exhibit an anergic histological pattern and a poorer response to treatment. The bacterial-infection-like form tended to have a neutrophilic folliculitis pattern. For 21 patients with negative parasitological tests, histopathology allowed to correct the diagnosis. The sensitivity of histopathology was 82%. Therefore, this study shows that histopathology remains useful in atypical ACL, to confirm the diagnosis and determine the histological pattern. Targeted therapies (increased doses of antiparasitic drugs for papulo-nodular forms or neutrophils inhibitors for bacterial-like forms) could be guided by histopathology.

Article.Title: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
Article.Authors: Gomaa S.; Eissa M.; Abo Khashaba S.; Mostafa W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. The present study proposes an integrated spatial suitability framework employing Geographic Information Systems (GIS) coupled with Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) to delineate optimal sites for geothermal power plant development within the study area. In the context of escalating global energy demands, geothermal energy, defined as terrestrial heat extracted from the Earth’s crust through deep drilling and surface fluid transport, represents a viable pathway toward energy transition. The analytical framework was constructed from subsurface thermal data derived from 52 hydrocarbon wells, enabling the computation of geothermal gradients at varying depths and heat flow assessments. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was applied to nine (geothermal gradient, heat flow, fault density, geology, seismic activity, proximity to the electricity grid, proximity to roads, land use, and slope) spatially explicit criteria encompassing thermal, geological, topographic, environmental, and infrastructural parameters, each assigned relative weights commensurate with its significance. A robust correlation ( R = 0.975) was established between subsurface temperature and depth, yielding a mean geothermal gradient of 48.5 °C/km (R² = 0.9509) and affirming the reliability of the thermal model. The resulting suitability analysis demonstrates that the Gulf of Suez region possesses favorable conditions for the deployment of both Flash Steam and Binary Cycle power plant technologies. Along the eastern coastal corridor, localities including Hammam Faraun, Ras Sudr, and Abu Zenima were identified as suitable for Flash Steam systems at drilling depths of 3,000–4,000 m, corresponding to reservoir temperatures of 140–210 °C, while Binary Cycle systems are applicable at depths of 2,000–3,000 m with temperatures ranging from 100 to 160 °C. On the western coast, sites encompassing Ras Gharib, Ras Shukeir, Jabal al-Zeit, and Jabal Ataqa are technically viable for Flash Steam technology at depths of 3,000–4,000 m and temperatures of 140–210 °C, with supplementary Binary Cycle suitability observed at depths of 2,000–3,000 m and temperatures of 100–180 °C. Zones exclusively suited for Binary Cycle applications include Ayoun Moussa, Wadi Baaba, Wadi Feiran, and Wadi El-Tor to the east, and Zaafarana, Wadi Dara, and Wadi Araba to the west, at depths of 3,000–4,000 m with temperatures ranging between 100 and 160 °C and 100–155 °C, respectively. Northern portions of the study area, characterized by comparatively subdued geothermal gradients, are deemed appropriate for direct-use applications, including space heating, light industrial operations, and residential thermal supply.

Article.Title: Exploratory QSPR analysis of physicochemical properties of selected antifungal agents using topological indices
Article.Authors: Asim M.; Mufti Z.; Almehizia A.; Assiri A.; Ganati G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The structural-property relationships are key in the study of the physicochemical behavior of pharmaceuticals. The degree-based topological indices available through molecular graph theory are used to investigate the structure-property analysis of selected antimycotic agents in a quantitative way in this work. The molecular graphs of ten antimycotic agents were constructed, and several degree-based indices including $$M^o_1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$F^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$Y^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$S^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$G^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$P^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$HM^\alpha _1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$HM^\alpha _2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , and $$HF^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ were computed to describe their structural characteristics. To enhance descriptive reliability, this study introduces a novel integration of degree-based topological descriptors with comprehensive multivariate statistical techniques—combining linear regression, correlation profiling, and dimensionality reduction to evaluate structural-property dependencies. Statistical methods were applied to examine the connection between molecular structure and various physicochemical properties, including density, boiling point, enthalpy of vaporization, refractive index, molar refractivity, polarizability, molecular volume, surface tension, and atomic mass. The strength of the associations between topological descriptors and physicochemical parameters were analyzed using regression analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson analysis, and Spearman analysis of correlation. The accuracy of the fitted regression models was quantitatively evaluated for all parameters and showed to be property-dependent. The range of the standard model error metrics were: $$\textrm{MAE} = 0.0234$$ –161.7920 and $$\textrm{RMSE} = 0.0298$$ –262.6852 which scale directly with the magnitude of the target physicochemical properties. Furthermore, Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation yielded cross-validated performance metrics spanning $$Q^2_{\textrm{LOO}} = -2.1417$$ to 0.3514, with associated errors bounded by $$\mathrm {LOOCV\text {-}MAE} = 0.0320$$ to 191.2633 and $$\mathrm {LOOCV\text {-}RMSE} = 0.0371$$ to 304.5087. Moreover, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce data dimensionality and identify the most informative descriptors. These findings indicate that a number of topological indices have strong positive correlations with significant physicochemical characteristics, especially those of boiling point, molar refractivity, molecular volume, and atomic mass. Among descriptors that were examined, the most consistent correlations with physicochemical properties of antimycotic agents are observed in $$M^o_1(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , and $$HF^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$ , where $$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$ achieved strong descriptive performance for polarizability ( $$R^2 = 0.989$$ , $$\textrm{RMSE} = 22.8565$$ , $$\textrm{MAE} = 17.7267$$ ).. The analysis of the results of PCA indicates that the first two principal components cover about 82 percent of the total variance and, therefore, the cumulative structural and physicochemical descriptors are effective in distinguishing the targeted compounds. Overall, the results indicate that degree-based topological indices are reliable descriptor of the physicochemical behavior of antimycotic agents and serve as effective tools in computational drug development and structure-property prediction.

Article.Title: Establishing a reflective-formative higher-order measurement model for the Smartphone Addiction Inventory-Short Form (SPAI-SF)
Article.Authors: Wong B.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Given that model misspecification threatens the validity of constructs and distorts statistical findings, in the context of Smartphone Addiction Inventory-Short Form (SPAI-SF), this study investigates whether smartphone addiction construct should be modelled using reflective-reflective approach (Type I model) or reflective-formative approach (Type II model). Drawing on theoretical criteria such as (1) direction of causality, (2) interchangeability of the indicators, (3) correlation/covariation among the indicators, and (4) the relationship of indicators with other constructs, this study has specified smartphone addiction as a second-order reflective-formative construct. To verify this model specification, data was collected from undergraduate students at a Chinese university and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), confirmatory tetrad analysis (CTA-PLS), and several recently developed model fit indices (SRMR, d_ULS, d_G). The results have not only determined that reflective-formative approach (Type II model) is more appropriate than reflective-reflective approach (Type I model) for modelling smartphone addiction construct but also provided strong evidence for construct validity. This study makes a significant theoretical and methodological contribution to the smartphone addiction literature by emphasizing the importance of considering the formative nature of the smartphone addiction construct when designing research frameworks.

Article.Title: Analysis of building seismic damage characteristics and topographic amplification effects of the 2026 Diebu Ms5.5 earthquake
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang J.; Wang P.; Wang Q.; Su W.; Zhang X.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract On January 26, 2026, an Ms5.5 shallow-focus earthquake occurred in Diebu County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu Province. The affected area lies within the alpine gorge of the Bailong River on the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, a region characterized by rugged topography and complex geological conditions that are typically prone to topographic amplification of ground motion. To address how topographic and site conditions control ground-motion amplification and the resulting spatial distribution of seismic damage, this study selected Dianga Town in Diebu County—the area covered by the earthquake damage survey—as the study area. Field damage surveys, seismic station monitoring data, and FLAC3D three-dimensional numerical simulations were integrated to systematically reveal the relationships among ground-motion amplification, building damage, and slope deformation. Results indicate that the seismic intensity in the study area reached VI–VII on the Chinese seismic intensity scale. Ground-motion amplification was closely associated with the spatially non-uniform distribution of seismic damage: at steep cliffs, slope shoulders, and high-elevation sites, peak ground acceleration (PGA) amplification factors approached 2.0, and buildings at these locations experienced significantly more severe damage than those at other sites. Seismic loading also altered the shear strain distribution pattern of the slope, causing the zone of concentrated shear strain to redistribute and extend toward the residential area. Topographic relief, excavation-induced free faces, and elevation differences were identified as the primary factors contributing to topographic amplification in the studied alpine gorge; in particular, an elevation difference of only about 100 m produced pronounced differences in seismic damage. These findings qualitatively reveal the mechanism of ground-motion amplification and provide a scientific basis for seismic fortification and geological hazard mitigation in villages and towns within alpine gorge areas on the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau.

Article.Title: HSP90AA1 induces M2 macrophage polarization via stabilizing ITGB1 and promoting CCL2 secretion in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Article.Authors: Ding M.; Wang C.; Cao X.; Zong D.; Mao Y.; Wang W.; Ni X.; He X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) presents a major treatment challenge, largely due to immunotherapy resistance. The molecular mechanisms that drive the remodeling of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in NPC are still not well understood. This study explored how heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1 (HSP90AA1) regulated the NPC immune microenvironment. A total of 54 NPC patients receiving first-line immunotherapy were analyzed by immunohistochemistry (IHC). High HSP90AA1 expression predicted shorter progression-free survival (PFS). According to the TIMER database, HSP90AA1 expression positively correlated with M2 macrophage infiltration. Additionally, we established an indirect co-culture model containing NPC cells and THP-1-derived macrophages and found that HSP90AA1 facilitated macrophage M2 polarization. According to the results of co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and cycloheximide (CHX) chase assays, HSP90AA1 associated with integrin β1 (ITGB1) and stabilized its protein expression, subsequently increasing C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) secretion. HSP90AA1 knockdown suppressed CCL2 secretion and M2 polarization, and ITGB1 overexpression partially reversed this effect. Taken together, our in vitro models and retrospective clinical correlation suggest that the HSP90AA1-ITGB1-CCL2 axis may drive immunosuppressive TME remodeling in NPC, highlighting HSP90AA1 as a promising predictive biomarker and therapeutic target against immunotherapy resistance.

Article.Title: Feasibility and expert evaluation of a medical large language model in an interdisciplinary clinical board
Article.Authors: Ronicke M.; Sollfrank L.; Sagonas I.; Atreya R.; Grieshaber-Bouyer R.; Hoerning A.; Jefremow A.; Kowalski I.; Krickau T.; Lermer J.; Meidenbauer N.; Rech J.; Rothhammer V.; Schley G.; Sondermann W.; Sticherling M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Interdisciplinary clinical boards (ICB) on chronic inflammatory diseases discuss complicated and multidisciplinary cases with inflammatory conditions among experts in their discipline. Medically specialized large language models (LLMs) are finding increasingly widespread use among physicians to answer clinical questions. LLMs offer the potential to close the gap between rapidly expanding medical knowledge and limited time of physicians by providing evidence-based summaries to clinical questions and enable “real-time” literature search. However, it is unclear if LLMs can be implemented in clinical routine of ICB. In this prospective study, 100 consecutive real-world cases were discussed in our ICB. Each case was first discussed independently of the LLM and a preliminary recommendation was documented. The clinical question was then entered in the LLM “OpenEvidence”, the answer was reviewed by the board with the opportunity to add aspects not previously raised, and the recommendation was subsequently confirmed as final. Each participating expert evaluated the answer of the LLM using a questionnaire comprising eight Likert scale (1–5) items and one free-text item. Two physicians, blinded to each other, additionally evaluated outputs for their agreement with the board’s decision. The same cases were evaluated after prompt optimization at two different time points. The 100 discussed cases resulted in 759 rater-case evaluations. A mean of 2.3 specialties were directly involved in each case. The highest score was achieved by the item “OpenEvidence provided clinically relevant information for this case.” (4.06). Recommendation for future use achieved a mean score of 3.95. Complete agreement of the LLM answer with the final recommendation of the ICB was rated in 40.2% and 50.5% of all evaluable cases ( n = 97) by the two raters. When restricted to consensus cases, i.e. cases rated identically by both raters ( n = 62 of 97), complete agreement was 51.6%. Outputs after prompt optimization tended to be associated with higher agreement, but did not reach statistical significance. Outputs were not stable over time. The integration of OpenEvidence into an ICB was feasible and was perceived as useful by the participating specialists, with partial or complete concordance with the final board recommendation in the majority of evaluable cases. As the study did not assess patient outcomes, clinical harm or hallucinations, no conclusions on patient safety can be drawn. The LLM was naturally limited by the information provided in the prompt. Inadequate questions or missing information led to suboptimal answers, highlighting the importance of identifying and including relevant information beforehand. Expert oversight remains essential. Model drift of LLMs may outweigh prompt optimization.

Article.Title: Enhanced anti-ESKAPE pathogen and antibiofilm activities of Korean red ginseng-derived silver nanoparticles via membrane deformation: LC/HRMS profiling and dynamic correlations
Article.Authors: Aati S.; Bahr H.; Aati H.; Rajan S.; Shari F.; Sayed A.; Hassan H.; Basyony A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Red Ginseng is widely recognized for its diverse pharmacological activities, which are largely attributed to its ginsenoside content. A commercial processed Korean Red Ginseng extract product (HO3), hereafter referred to as “HO3 extract”, was used throughout this study. HO3 extract was analyzed using LC-HR-MS to evaluate and profile its ginsenoside content. LC-HR-MS analysis tentatively identified six major ginsenosides, namely Rh1, Rh2, Rg1, Rg2, Rg3, and Rb1. Subsequently, silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) incorporating HO3 extract were synthesized and analyzed using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR), spectroscopy ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta potential measurements, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. The synthesized AgNPs exhibited a characteristic absorption band at 420 nm, indicating nanoparticle formation, while FTIR analysis revealed the presence of functional groups involved in nanoparticle stabilization. The antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of HO3 extract and HO3-mediated AgNPs were subsequently evaluated. Antibacterial assessment demonstrated that AgNPs significantly outperformed HO3 extract, exhibiting higher inhibition percentages and lower minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens. Furthermore, biofilm inhibition assays revealed markedly greater suppression by AgNPs (55–75%) than by HO3 extract (7–16%), with the highest activity observed against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Time-kill assays further demonstrated that the antibacterial efficacy of AgNPs was both dose- and time-dependent. Moreover, the identified major ginsenosides were subjected to molecular dynamics (MD) simulations against microbial membrane models to predict their potential antimicrobial mechanisms. Notably, ginsenosides Rg1 and Rb1 exhibited the strongest membrane-disruptive effects, inducing substantial bilayer thinning and reducing local membrane thickness, thereby supporting their potential antimicrobial role.

Article.Title: Associations of cardiometabolic disease and depression with changes in instrumental activities of daily living disability among middle-aged and older adults
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Shin Y.
Article.Abstract: This study examined the independent and joint associations of cardiometabolic disease (CMD) and depression with changes in instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) disability among middle-aged and older adults. Longitudinal data were obtained from 16,780 individuals aged ≥ 45 years in the China Family Panel Studies from 2012 to 2020. Changes in IADL disability were assessed using transitions and trajectories. Mixed-effects models, Cox proportional hazards models, and multinomial logistic regression were applied, and joint associations were evaluated using multiplicative and additive interactions. CMD and depression were associated with higher IADL disability scores. Single CMD, cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), and depression were associated with increased risks of new-onset and persistent disability, a higher likelihood of severe disability trajectories, and a lower likelihood of recovery. The combination of CMM and depression showed evidence of multiplicative and additive interaction for IADL disability scores, with a broadly consistent adverse additive interaction pattern across new-onset disability, persistent disability, and severe disability trajectories. These findings suggest that CMD and depression are independently associated with adverse changes in IADL disability, with CMM and depression showing an additional adverse joint association. Integrated management of physical and mental health may help reduce disability in ageing populations.

Article.Title: Segmentation of brain tumors using a morphological Laplacian-enhanced active contour model on MRI
Article.Authors: Kazemi M.; Farsi H.; Ghaffari A.; Mohamadzadeh S.; Barati A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate segmentation of brain tumors in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is crucial for effective treatment planning and post-treatment monitoring. However, challenges such as intensity inhomogeneity, low-contrast boundaries, and highly irregular tumor morphology significantly complicate this task. In this work, we introduce a two-stage hybrid framework that integrates a convolutional U-Net for coarse tumor localization with a morphological Laplacian-enhanced active contour model for precise boundary refinement. While the U-Net is trained using bimodal input (FLAIR + T1ce) to generate reliable initial masks, all refinement steps and final performance evaluations are conducted exclusively on single-modality FLAIR images—ensuring clinical simplicity and robustness. The proposed active contour incorporates a novel local fitting term based on morphological Laplacian operators, which capture structural transitions and enhance edge sensitivity. An adaptive weighting function dynamically balances the influence of local and global intensity information during contour evolution, improving resilience to noise and intensity variations without compromising computational efficiency. When evaluated on the BraTS 2020 dataset, the proposed method achieves a Dice coefficient of 96.48% ± 1.57%, a Jaccard index of 93.43% ± 2.92%, and a sensitivity of 97.01% ± 1.69%. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms both classical active contour models and contemporary deep learning architectures in whole-tumor segmentation from FLAIR-only MRI. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

Article.Title: Characterization of plasma TNFRSF/TNFSF molecule profiles in HIV-associated disseminated Kaposi’s sarcoma over short- and long-term follow-up
Article.Authors: Ramón-Luing L.; Flores-Gonzalez J.; Espinosa E.; Islas-Muñoz B.; Briceño O.; Carpio-Guadarrama D.; García-Escutia D.; Volkow-Fernández P.; Chavez-Galan L.
Article.Abstract: The tumor necrosis factor superfamily (TNFSF) members regulate diverse cellular processes, yet their systemic profiles remain insufficiently characterized in persons living with HIV (PLHIV) with disseminated Kaposi sarcoma (DKS) caused by Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV). Plasma levels of fifteen TNFSF/TNFRSF molecules were quantified in twenty participants with DKS/HIV enrolled in a randomized clinical trial. Samples were obtained at diagnosis (week 0) and follow-up at weeks of treatment W 4 , W 12 , W 24 , W 48 , and W 365 . Three control groups were included: ten HIV-negative (HIV-), ten PLHIV without an AIDS defining event diagnosis (HIV+/AIDS-), and twenty-four HIV+ with an AIDS-defining event without KSHV- (HIV+/AIDS+). At baseline, DKS/HIV showed higher TNFR1 and TNFR2 levels than the control groups ( p < 0.0001). The APRIL level was lower compared to HIV+AIDS+ ( p < 0.0001) and HIV+AIDS- ( p = 0.0190). An exploratory multivariate ROC analysis identified TNFR1, TNFR2, and APRIL as the combination with the highest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.979) for distinguishing DKS/HIV patients from other groups, including HIV+/AIDS+ (significant predictive accuracy = 94.5%). Longitudinal analyses showed decreases in TNFR1 and BAFF at week 24 (W 24 ), ( p < 0.0001 and p = 0.0018, respectively) and decreases in TNFR2 beginning at week 12 ( p < 0.0001), with sustained reductions through week 48 ( p < 0.0001), and week 365 ( p < 0.0001). Mixed effects modeling indicated significant associations between follow-up time and changes in TNFR1, TNFR2, and BAFF. Multiple linear regression analysis demonstrated significant associations between follow-up time and changes in TNFR1, TNFR2, and BAFF. This study describes baseline differences and longitudinal patterns of TNFRSF/TNFSF molecules in DKS/HIV. TNFR1, TNFR2, and APRIL showed the strongest baseline differences, whereas TNFR1, TNFR2, and BAFF displayed consistent temporal variations throughout the follow-up period. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of TNFRSF/TNFSF members as candidate biomarkers indicative of disease dynamics in DKS over both short-term (48 weeks) and long-term (7 years) follow-up.

Article.Title: Distinct host responses to whole-cell and CFS effects of Clostridium perfringens in Caenorhabditis elegans
Article.Authors: Sundararajan B.; Baskarapandian T.; Eswaran G.; Marudhamuthu M.
Article.Abstract: Clostridium perfringens is an important toxin-producing pathogen associated with a range of infections in humans and animals. Although its toxins are recognized as major virulence determinants, the extent to which toxin-mediated effects account for host responses during infection remains unclear. In this study, we used Caenorhabditis elegans as an in vivo model to compare the physiological and molecular responses elicited by whole-cell C. perfringens and its cell-free supernatant (CFS). The C. perfringens isolate obtained from the gastrointestinal tract of patients diagnosed with IBD was characterized and evaluated for pathogenicity in C. elegans . The CFS was prepared and validated functionally through hemolytic activity, heat-inactivation and dose-dependent toxicity assays. Host responses were assessed using lifespan, pharyngeal pumping, egg laying and microscopic analyses. Transcriptional changes were analysed by quantitative RT-PCR, keeping pmp-3 as the reference gene. Exposure to both whole bacterial cells and the CFS significantly impaired the survival, feeding behaviour, and reproductive capacity of C. elegans . However, the magnitude of these effects was greater during whole-cell exposure. The molecular study assessed the expression of genes associated with host defence and stress responses, including sek-1 and pmk-1 associated with p38 MAPK signalling, and the antimicrobial response marker lys-7 . skn-1 and gst-4 are associated with stress and detoxification responses, together with the oxidative-stress marker sod-3. Whole-cell exposure showed greater relative expression of sek-1 , pmk-1 , and lys-7 , compared with CFS treatment. Similarly, skn-1 and gst-4 were more highly expressed following whole-cell exposure than CFS treatment, while the oxidative-stress marker sod-3 was strongly induced by whole-cell exposure but showed minimal change following CFS treatment. These results suggest that while the toxin-associated components present in the CFS may contribute to the observed host responses, they cannot recreate responses observed during whole-cell exposure. This study also showed that C. elegans proved to be a useful model to evaluate the potential contribution of bacterial toxins to the development of infection and disease.

Article.Title: Hour-scale response of low-Earth-orbit satellite altitude to extreme geomagnetic storms revealed by the NinjaSat CubeSat during the 2024 solar maximum
Article.Authors: Tanaka H.; Nakagawa T.; Nozawa S.; Tamagawa T.; Enoto T.; Kitaguchi T.; Iwakiri W.; Mihara T.; Takeda T.; Ota N.; Aoyama A.; Iwata S.; Takahashi T.; Yamasaki K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Extreme geomagnetic storms accelerate low-Earth-orbit satellite decay by inflating the thermosphere, yet the hour-scale pathway from solar-wind energy to atmospheric heating is poorly understood. Using the GNSS receiver of the NinjaSat CubeSat ( $$\sim 500$$ km, $$97^\circ $$ sun-synchronous), we tracked orbital altitude through solar-maximum 2024 and cross-correlated the storm-time altitude-change rate with geomagnetic indices during the two largest storms of the year. The EUV-corrected residual correlates with the polar-cap (PC) index at $$r\gtrsim 0.8$$ , PC leading or coincident with the response by up to $$\sim 3$$ h, as do the auroral electrojet indices AE and AL. It also correlates with the Dst index ( $$r\approx 0.82 - 0.84$$ ), but the altitude drop precedes the Dst minimum by $$\sim 3$$ h, attributing this to a common solar-wind driver rather than ring-current heating. XRISM ( $$31^\circ $$ , $$\sim 560$$ km) shows the storm-induced density enhancement reached low latitudes in May 2024 but not in October 2024, consistent with a shorter electrojet duration despite comparable peak intensity. Polar Joule heating, indexed by PC, is thus the dominant storm-time drag driver, providing a natural forecasting window of up to $$\sim 3$$ h.

Article.Title: Adsorption of hazardous Acid Violet 17 on Vachellia nilotica biochar: experimental and statistical physics modelling
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Al Shayeb A.; Naidu R.; Fegade U.; Jethave G.; Alluqmani A.; Martuza M.; Shatnawi Z.; Haque M.; Arifuzzaman M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inadequate management of chemical industrial effluents necessitates the development of high-capacity, sustainable wastewater treatment technologies. This study investigates the adsorptive removal of hazardous Acid Violet 17 (AV17) dye using a novel biochar derived from Vachellia nilotica stems (VNBB). Characterization via HRTEM and BET analysis revealed a mesoporous, sponge-like architecture with a surface area of 50.92 m 2 g − 1 and an average pore diameter of 8.02 nm. Batch experiments demonstrated that VNBB is highly effective, achieving a maximum removal efficiency of 97.94% at pH 6. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir isotherm, yielding a superior maximum adsorption capacity ( Q max ) of 333.33 mgg − 1 . Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second order model, (R² = 0.995), implying strong correlation with the experimental results. From thermodynamic and statistical physics study, it was found that the adsorption mechanism followed mainly physical interaction. To provide deeper mechanistic insights, advanced statistical physics modeling was applied. A double-layer model with five parameters successfully described the adsorption isotherms. The steric parameter n ranged from 0.39 to 0.42, indicating a multi-docking mechanism where AV17 molecules maintain a horizontal orientation on the VNBB surface. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed the process is endothermic and spontaneous, with adsorption energies ( E 1 ) between 22.16 and 24.48 kJmol − 1 , signifying a physical component to the binding. Furthermore, the biochar exhibited excellent stability, maintaining high performance across five regeneration cycles with less than a 2% loss in capacity. These findings position VNBB as a high-performance, cost-effective, and reusable adsorbent for the remediation of dye-contaminated industrial wastewater.

Article.Title: Prediction of Claudin18.2 expression in gastric adenocarcinoma by habitat radiomics based on spectral CT
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Pan X.; Ma H.; Tang C.; Lu L.; Yan X.; Huang J.; Tang X.; Qian T.; Liu K.
Article.Abstract: To explore the predictive value of habitat radiomics derived from Dual-layer spectral detector CT (DLSCT) for the preoperative evaluation of Claudin18.2 (CLDN18.2) expression in gastric adenocarcinoma. A retrospective cohort of 111 eligible patients with gastric adenocarcinoma who underwent preoperative dual-phase DLSCT examinations was randomly divided into training and test sets at a 7:3 ratio. On the basis of the DLSCT images, the habitat subregions were delineated by applying K-means clustering to the voxel intensity values. Habitat features were extracted and filtered from these subregions to construct a habitat radiomics model. A clinical model, a conventional radiomics model, and a combined habitat radiomics and clinical data nomogram model were subsequently constructed. Model performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curves. The AUC values for the nomogram model in the training and test sets were 0.802 and 0.757, respectively, which were superior to those of the clinical model (AUC: 0.643 and 0.604, respectively), conventional radiomics model (AUC: 0.713 and 0.716, respectively) and habitat radiomics model (AUC: 0.768 and 0.726, respectively). The calibration curves demonstrated good consistency between the predicted results and actual outcomes. The results of the decision curve analysis(DCA) indicated that the model has high clinical applicability. The habitat radiomics model based on DLSCT outperforms the traditional radiomics model. Furthermore, integrating habitat radiomics with clinical indicators yields promising non-invasive predictive performance for preoperative CLDN18.2 stratification in gastric adenocarcinoma; large-scale prospective multicenter validation is required prior to clinical application.

Article.Title: Molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus in chigger mites
Article.Authors: Lee H.; Kim S.; Kim H.; Lim H.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne viral disease with high case-fatality rates in East Asia. While hard ticks are recognized as the primary vectors of SFTS virus (SFTSV), the detection of SFTSV RNA in chigger mites suggests their involvement in viral maintenance in natural conditions. In this study, wild rodents were captured at 17 sites across the Republic of Korea in 2019, and spleen tissues and mites were collected and tested for SFTSV RNA using RT-PCR. To evaluate transovarial transmission, Leptotrombidium sp. collected from an endemic area were reared under laboratory conditions. Among 56 rodents and 3,402 mites, SFTSV RNA was detected in 3.6% of rodents and 2.3% of mite pools (minimum infection rate of 0.09%). Phylogenetic analysis revealed that all viral sequences clustered within genotype B. SFTSV RNA was detected in both parental mites and their F1 larvae, providing molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission. This study provides the first molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission of SFTSV in chigger mites under laboratory conditions and indicates that chigger mites may contribute to the natural maintenance of the virus. Further animal model-based studies are needed to clarify their vector competence.

Article.Title: Development of a prediction model for occupational satisfaction among cancer patients following counseling in German psychosocial cancer counseling centers
Article.Authors: Lange H.; Kurth T.; Roth R.; Sibert N.; Breidenbach C.; Schellack S.; Ernstmann N.; Heidkamp P.; Hiltrop K.; Rother J.; Heier L.; Kowalski C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A prognostic model was developed and internally validated to predict satisfaction with the occupational situation among cancer patients receiving psychosocial counseling regarding return to work (RTW). Data were collected from outpatient cancer counseling centers in Germany and included individuals who had sought counseling on work-related issues at different stages of their illness. Satisfaction with the occupational situation was measured using a single-item scale. LASSO regression with cross-validation and bootstrapping was applied for predictor selection. The final model ( n = 259) identified satisfaction with life, baseline satisfaction with the occupational situation, and higher household and personal income as positive predictors, while workplace conflicts and psychological distress were negative predictors. The model showed moderate predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.29, RMSE = 2.55) and good calibration-in-the-large (predicted: 5.45; observed: 5.45). The model may support the identification of cancer survivors likely to report low satisfaction with the occupational situation following psychosocial counseling. External validation is required to assess generalizability. A web-based tool was developed to support application in counseling settings.

Article.Title: A single-user feasibility study demonstrating real-time raycast-based stair and elevation-change detection on consumer smartphone LiDAR hardware
Article.Authors: Herdt N.; Braun T.; Bell T.; Russell S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract For individuals who are blind or visually impaired (BVI), undetected stairways, curbs, and sudden elevation changes represent a leading cause of fall-related injury. Herein we present a preliminary, single-operator feasibility evaluation of a computationally efficient geometric algorithm for detecting stair and elevation changes in real time, implemented entirely on an LiDAR-equipped consumer smartphone (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26.2). The algorithm uses a set of eight downward- and forward-facing raycasts projected into an ARKit (Artificial Reality developer Kit)-reconstructed mesh and performs line-segment angular analysis at 60 Hz within a 16.7 ms per-frame budget, without requiring cloud processing, GPU inference, or custom hardware. A single trained operator conducted 120 trials spanning eight real-world hazard locations, five step heights (4.5 to 7.5 in; 11.4 to 19.1 cm), four stair grades (22 to 33 degrees), varied lighting conditions (indoor artificial, outdoor daytime, and outdoor nighttime), and both ascending and descending approaches, yielding an overall detection rate of 92.5% (95% CI 86.4–96.0%) and a mean alert distance of 2.31 ft (0.70 m; SD = 0.91 ft). No false-positive alerts were observed during the hazard-approach or traversal segments of these trials, although dedicated hazard-free control trials were not conducted, so this should not be read as a validated false-positive rate across general non-hazard environments. Detection rate and alert distance both tended to increase with step height, with the smallest steps and one specific indoor location accounting for most missed detections; however, pairwise differences across step-height, lighting, and approach-direction categories did not reach statistical significance at the sample sizes tested (Fisher’s exact p > 0.05 in all cases), and step geometry covaried with test location in this design, so these patterns should be treated as preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than as an established reliability threshold. Descending approaches produced numerically lower detection rates and shorter warning distances than ascending approaches, consistent with a geometric limitation intrinsic to depth-based sensing of hazards that only become visible at close range. These results indicate that low-latency elevation-hazard detection is technically feasible on commodity mobile hardware under controlled, single-operator conditions; confirming this feasibility finding for real-world use by BVI individuals will require larger, multi-participant studies incorporating natural scanning behavior and dedicated negative-condition testing.
Article.Topic: Assistive Technology in Communication and Mobility

Article.Title: Translation, cultural adaptation, and psychometric validation of the Persian ObsQoR-10 in inpatient women 24 to 48 h after vaginal or elective cesarean delivery
Article.Authors: Maghalian M.; Rouhzendeh S.; Mirghafourvand M.
Article.Abstract: The quality of postpartum recovery is a complex process. In this study, we aimed to translate and culturally adapt the Persian version of the ObsQoR-10 instrument and evaluate its psychometric properties in inpatient women 24 to 48 h after vaginal or elective cesarean delivery. This cross-sectional study translated and validated the Persian version of the Obstetric Quality of Recovery-10 (ObsQoR-10) in accordance with COSMIN guidelines. A total of 408 postpartum women were recruited from Taleghani Hospital in Tabriz, Iran, between 2024 and 2025. The ObsQoR-10 underwent a rigorous translation process (forward and backward translation, followed by cognitive interviews) and comprehensive psychometric evaluation. Content validity was examined using expert panels through CVI and CVR indices, while face validity was assessed via patient feedback. Structural validity was evaluated using exploratory factor analysis (EFA, n = 150) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA, n = 258), and construct validity was assessed through hypotheses testing (convergent and known-groups validity). Reliability was assessed through Cronbach’s α, McDonald’s ω, and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) to determine test-retest stability. The ObsQoR-10 demonstrated excellent content validity (scale-CVI = 0.95, CVR = 0.89) and strong face validity (mean impact score = 4.37/5). EFA identified a single factor accounting for 73.4% of the variance. CFA supported acceptable model fit (scaled χ²/df = 1.53, CFI = 0.990, TLI = 0.986, robust RMSEA = 0.052, SRMR = 0.021). Internal consistency was high (α = 0.964, ω = 0.956), and test-retest reliability was good (ICC = 0.86). The total score was calculated as the sum of all 10 item scores (range: 0-100), with higher scores indicating better recovery. ObsQoR-10 scores correlated significantly with the Questionnaire About the Childbirth Experience (QACE) ( r = − .63, p < .001). No floor or ceiling effects were observed (0%). The Persian version of the Obstetric Quality of Recovery-10 is a valid, reliable, and clinically practical patient-reported outcome measure for evaluating inpatient postpartum recovery among Persian-speaking women 24 to 48 h after vaginal or elective cesarean delivery.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning and hybrid transformer-based proteochemometric modelling for breast cancer molecular subtyping and multi-target natural product discovery
Article.Authors: Jakkula B.; Perugu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Breast cancer comprises five intrinsic molecular subtypes with distinct transcriptomic programs, prognoses, and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Yet, accurate subtype discrimination remains limited by boundary-overlap and poor cross-cohort generalisability, while single-target agents often fail against pathway redundancy and acquired resistance. We developed an integrated computational framework linking transcriptomic-classification, explainable target prioritisation, and multi-target natural-product discovery. Three transcriptomic cohorts (METABRIC-BRCA-2016, TCGA-BRCA-2012, and TCGA-BRCA-2018; n = 2512 after quality-control and ComBat-correction) were integrated. Differential-expression analysis and PCA-based feature selection yielded a 50-gene signature that retained more than 90% of the subtype-associated variance. Among the six evaluated classifiers, XGBoost achieved the best performance and generalised to an independent cohort of 3,409 samples (accuracy: 85.70%; ROC-AUC: 0.95–0.99). SHAP-analysis identified 30-candidate genes associated with Basal-like and HER2-enriched subtypes, which were cross-referenced against ChEMBL to retain 11 targets for proteochemometric (PCM) modelling. A hybrid PCM multilayer-perceptron integrating ProtBERT and ChemBERTa embeddings with molecular fingerprints and chemical descriptors achieved a balanced-accuracy of 0.9140 and mean ROC-AUC of 0.9696. Screening of 30,898 NPASS natural products identified 292 pan-active compounds. Independent binding- and safety-prioritisation strategies converged on three leads: NPC139056, NPC196231, and NPC471997. This reproducible pipeline provides computationally prioritised leads for experimental validation in clinically challenging breast cancer subtypes.

Article.Title: Proteomics characterization of muscle-invasive bladder carcinoma identifies molecular subtypes and subtype-specific biological processes
Article.Authors: Pedregosa-Barbas J.; Trilla-Fuertes L.; García-Fernández E.; Becerril-Gómez F.; Lalanda-Delgado P.; Zambrana F.; Martínez-Salas I.; Gajate P.; Dittmann A.; López-Vacas R.; Kunz L.; Rubio G.; Nieto-Torrero S.; Pertejo A.; Vara J.; González-Peramato P.; Gámez-Pozo A.; Pinto-Marín Á.
Article.Abstract: Muscle-invasive bladder carcinoma (MIBC) has been classified into transcriptomic subtypes, but comprehensive proteomic characterization remains limited. In this study, we used data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) to characterize the proteomic landscape of MIBC and explore subtype-associated therapeutic opportunities. Proteins were extracted from 58 formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) MIBC transurethral resection (TURBT) samples and analyzed by data-independent acquisition mass-spectrometry (DIA-MS). Proteomics data were processed using Perseus and analyzed by hierarchical clustering and network analysis with TMEV, gRapHD, and DAVID. Findings were validated using the TCGA MIBC cohort. By the analysis of TURBT samples, three proteomic clusters that recapitulate MIBC transcriptomic subtypes were identified: Luminal-papillary (high KRT20 expression, mitochondrial and metabolic activity), Basal-squamous (basal biomarkers, DNA replication, and glycosylation activity), and Luminal-infiltrated + Luminal (immune and extracellular matrix activity). Network analysis revealed subtype-specific biological processes that were supported by analyses of the Dressler’s and TCGA MIBC cohorts. Subtype-specific proteomic profiles suggested candidate therapeutic approaches. DIA-MS profiling of routine, pre-treatment FFPE TURBT specimens (the diagnostic material on which treatment decisions are made) reproduces the established transcriptomic classification at the protein level. These findings provide a proteomic framework for molecular subtype characterization in MIBC and support the investigation of subtype-informed therapeutic strategies.

Article.Title: User-focused faceted aggregated exploratory multimedia search results framework
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Saadia A.; Rashid U.; Khan T.; Jan T.; Khalil R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Search engines have become a ubiquitous platform for finding information, yet web users still struggle to browse and filter retrieved results in exploratory search environments with ill-defined information needs. While search engines retrieve relevant results for keyword queries, users struggle to browse, filter, and comprehend disorganized, media-diverse, disjointed verticals. Existing research on vertical aggregation has mainly focused on aggregating heterogeneous verticals, thereby undermining crucial aspects such as organization, annotation, and personalization to support exploratory search. This research proposes an aggregated, personalized exploratory search framework that organizes search results into Named Entity Recognition (NER)-derived, domain-independent facet categories and ranks them using a modified Best Matching 25 Fielded (BM25F) ranking algorithm. The facets are linked to the user query as implicit pseudo-relevance feedback to personalize search results based on the user’s category-specific intent. We empirically validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm on standardized benchmarks (SciFact, TREC-COVID, NFCorpus, FiQA, SCIDOCS, ArguAna). The results show that the proposed ranking algorithm provides, on average, 12.59% superior data exploration performance while preserving lexical relevance. The algorithm’s efficacy in real-world exploratory search was further validated through a user study (N=23) that evaluated users’ exploratory search outcomes using system usability and behavioral metrics. An independent user study with 23 participants further indicates higher perceived usability and task satisfaction compared with a Google baseline, with a 17.72-point improvement in system usability and a 25.3% relative improvement in satisfaction with exploratory task completion. Behavioral analysis additionally shows shorter queries and substantially fewer query reformulations, indicating reduced query-formulation effort during exploratory search. These findings show that aggregating, annotating, organizing, and personalizing search results can substantially improve exploratory search effectiveness, reduce cognitive load, and enhance user satisfaction.

Article.Title: Spatial variability of TEC perturbations and ROTI during the 3 october 2024 X9.0 solar flare: a multi-station GNSS analysis
Article.Authors: Data E.; Setegn G.; Okoh D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the spatially heterogeneous low-latitude ionospheric response to the 3 October 2024 X9.0 solar flare using GNSS observations from seven equatorial and low-latitude stations. TEC, quiet-time differential TEC ( $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ ), and ROTI were analyzed under relatively quiet geomagnetic conditions ( $$K_p=1$$ –3). The flare peaked at 12:18 UT, and comparison with quiet-time conditions revealed $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ perturbations of approximately 6–14% at several stations, with pronounced spatial differences. YKRO showed the largest positive perturbation at the flare peak, reaching 12.75 TECU (14.21%), whereas MBAR and CUSV exhibited negative perturbations of $$-10.98$$ TECU ( $$-10.77\%$$ ) and $$-6.14$$ TECU ( $$-9.29\%$$ ), respectively. However, substantial and sometimes larger $$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$ variations occurred outside the flare interval, indicating that their magnitude alone cannot establish a flare-driven response. ROTI remained generally below 0.04 TECU min $$^{-1}$$ during the flare, with stronger irregularity activity occurring predominantly after sunset. The results indicate a measurable and spatially heterogeneous ionospheric response temporally associated with the X9.0 flare, while highlighting the substantial contribution of intrinsic low-latitude variability. These findings emphasize the importance of multi-station observations and quiet-time normalization for robustly assessing solar-flare-associated ionospheric disturbances.

Article.Title: Unravelling the roles of redox homeostasis and antioxidant system in facilitating adaptive responses during Pb induced hormesis in Brassica juncea
Article.Authors: Dhiman S.; Naresh R.; Bhardwaj R.; Singh R.; Kapoor N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This research explores the role of the antioxidant-prooxidant balance in eliciting the hormesis effect in Brassica juncea seedlings exposed to mild Lead (Pb). Excessive Pb doses in plants causes oxidative stress, which damages plant cells, stunts growth, and reduces agricultural yield. Conversely, mild Pb doses induce a hormetic effect inside plants system, leading to beneficial adaptive changes at cellular, molecular, and physio-biochemical levels. The plant's antioxidant defence network often relieves Pb metal stress. Antioxidants, both enzyme-based and non-enzyme-based, neutralize reactive oxygen species (ROS) created by Pb stress, protecting cellular structures and promoting plant resilience. Also, the idea of hormesis, which describes how modest doses of toxins like Pb metals cause plants to adapt, helps us understand how plants protect themselves and enhance stress tolerance to handle stress by raising antioxidant activity. In the present study, mild Pb exposed 10 days old B. juncea seedlings were tested for antioxidant activity and gene expression. Moderate Pb exposure increased B. juncea seedling protein content, antioxidant enzyme activity, and gene expression. The results suggest the possible role of antioxidants in inducing hormetic responses in B. juncea seedlings exposed to Pb, laying the foundation for understanding how these mechanisms cooperate to minimize Pb impact and improve seedling resilience.

Article.Title: Quantifying metal transferability in soil and its relationship to metal-related health risks in the strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa)-human food chain
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Yang H.; Liu H.; Wang Y.; Liu B.
Article.Abstract: Understanding metal transfer in soil-strawberry systems is indispensable for sustainable strawberry production. To date, much attention has been paid to metals in strawberries, while metal transferability in strawberry-growing soil has been ignored. In this study, the availability, mobility, and bioavailability indices established based on BCR-extracted metal fractions and previously used for metal bioavailability evaluation in sediments were utilized to estimate metal transferability in soil sampled from strawberry orchards in the Yangtze River Delta, China, and predict metal-related health risks in strawberries. Overall, soil Pb, Cr, Ni, and Cu had their average bioavailability index (BI) values lower than 0.1, indicating low bioavailability of these metals. In contrast, soil Cd and Zn generally exhibited very high and moderate bioavailability, as their mean BI values reached 1.46 and 0.241, respectively. Furthermore, the mean values of total mobility and availability indices were 0.427 and 0.566, respectively, suggesting high mobility and availability for soil metals. Notably, the significant increase of soil Cr bioavailability induced by the acidification of strawberry-growing soil exacerbated the cancer risk caused by gastrointestinal bioaccessible Cr in strawberries. Overall, these indices, particularly the bioavailability index, can effectively reflect soil metal bioavailability and predict metal-related health risks in strawberries.

Article.Title: A physics guided hybrid modeling framework for rainfall runoff forecasting in data scarce regions
Article.Authors: Molajou A.; Tajbakhsh A.; Shokatian-Beiragh M.; Variani H.; Aram S.; Brysiewicz A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rainfall-runoff (R-R) forecasting in data-scarce regions remains challenging due to limited hydrometeorological observations, uncertainties in satellite-based precipitation products (SPPs), and the inability of individual modeling approaches to fully represent complex watershed dynamics. To address these challenges, this study develops a physics guided hybrid modeling framework that integrates bias-corrected satellite precipitation products, signal decomposition techniques, process-based hydrological modeling, and deep learning (DL) for improved runoff simulation and forecasting. In the proposed framework, physical knowledge is incorporated through the soil and water assessment tool (SWAT), which provides physically meaningful representations of watershed processes, while a long short-term memory (LSTM) network learns residual nonlinear relationships between physically simulated and observed runoff responses. Three widely used SPPs, including CHIRPS, IMERG, and PERSIANN-CDR, were evaluated against available rainfall observations, and a PDF-based additive bias correction approach was applied to improve precipitation estimates. Wavelet transform (WT) and variational mode decomposition (VMD) were further investigated within a time consistent feature construction framework to extract hydrologically relevant temporal patterns from corrected precipitation inputs and SWAT-simulated runoff outputs. The framework was evaluated in two hydroclimatically contrasting watersheds in Iran, namely the semi-arid Tabriz Basin and the humid Ghaem Shahr Basin. Results indicated that CHIRPS provided the most reliable precipitation estimates among the tested SPPs, while VMD outperformed WT in extracting temporal characteristics relevant to runoff generation. The proposed VMD-SWAT-LSTM framework generally achieved superior or comparable performance compared with standalone SWAT, LSTM, and conventional SWAT-LSTM models during training, validation, and testing periods under a temporally consistent evaluation framework. During the training phase, the proposed framework achieved CC = 0.99, NSE = 0.96, and RMSE = 2.61 m 3 . s − 1 in Tabriz Basin, and CC = 0.98, NSE = 0.97, and RMSE = 0.58 m 3 . s − 1 in the Ghaem Shahr Basin. The proposed approach also demonstrated improved robustness in multi-step-ahead forecasting (up to 7 days), although predictive performance decreased with increasing lead time, and maintained robust performance under uncertainty according to Monte Carlo (MC) analysis. The findings demonstrate that combining physically based watershed representation with decomposition assisted data-driven (DD) error learning within a physics-guided framework can improve R-R forecasting accuracy and robustness in data-scarce regions. The proposed methodology showed robust performance in the two investigated hydroclimatically contrasting basins, suggesting its potential for hydrological prediction in data-scarce regions. However, its transferability to other basins and broader hydrological and climatic conditions requires further evaluation.

Article.Title: An international multilocation trial reveals genotype-by-environment interactions in Arabica coffee across climate gradients
Article.Authors: Gautron R.; Berny Mier y Teran J.; Delgado Muñoz L.; Lemus S.; Rahn E.; Castro Llanos F.; Bunn C.; Gezan S.; Pruvot-Woehl S.; Maina C.; Cheserek J.; Alonso Castillo J.; López Morgado R.; Alpízar E.; Alvarado J.; Arevalo J.; Banda B.; Baudry D.; Bordeaux M.; Castro E.; Devasia J.; Gichuru E.; Gimase J.; Alunga C.; Kachiguma N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Climate change makes the future of Arabica coffee ( Coffea arabica L.) uncertain, a crop supporting Coffee is produced on approximately 12.5 million farms worldwide, predominantly family-run smallholdings. Identifying varieties that combine high productivity with disease resistance across diverse environments is critical for climate adaptation, yet global empirical evidence remains limited. We leveraged a dataset from an international multi-environment trial evaluating 32 varieties for yield and coffee leaf rust severity across a total of 30 sites in 17 countries. Genotype-by-environment interactions were analyzed using factor analytic mixed-effects models, and latent environmental factors were linked to climatic gradients through partial least squares regression. Yield stability was associated with thermal gradients, distinguishing varietal adaptation between cooler environments with high diurnal temperature variation and warmer, thermally stable conditions. In contrast, rust severity and its interactions were associated with joint gradients of temperature, precipitation, humidity, and thermal variability. Among the evaluated genotypes, the F1 hybrids H1 Centroamericano and EC16, followed by the introgressed line Parainema, showed the strongest combined performance for yield and rust resistance, although with distinct climatic preferences and trade-offs in yield stability. Overall, introgressed varieties consistently outperformed pure Arabica varieties, which exhibited lower yields and greater rust susceptibility. These findings provide a robust empirical basis for climate-informed variety deployment and breeding strategies in Arabica coffee.

Article.Title: Latent profiles of mental health literacy and associated factors among older adults with cataracts
Article.Authors: Tang X.; Li X.; Li J.; Long L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mental health literacy may shape how older adults with cataracts recognize psychological distress and seek support, but variation within this population remains poorly understood. This cross-sectional study surveyed 209 hospitalized adults aged 60 years or older with cataracts using validated measures of mental health literacy, anxiety, perceived social support and sleep quality. Latent profile analysis identified three mental health literacy profiles: low-MHL/negative-attitude (16.7%), limited-recognition/moderate-attitude (33.5%) and high-MHL (49.8%). Multinomial logistic regression showed that diagnosis duration, anxiety level, living arrangement and primary caregiver were associated with profile membership. These findings highlight different patterns of recognition and attitudes within this hospitalized sample. They support examining these dimensions separately in nursing assessment research. Independent validation is required before using the profiles to guide nursing assessment or select educational support.
