Article.Title: Tracing of 13C-labeled fatty acids indicate the lack of linoleic acid synthesis in mammalian cells
Article.Authors: Mika A.; Hliwa-Slazyk A.; Koszalka P.; Andrieu A.; Kokotkiewicz A.; Krol A.; Luczkiewicz M.; Sledzinski T.
Article.Abstract: The belief that n-3 and n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) cannot be synthetized de novo in mammalian cells is based on evidence from very early experiments. In recent literature misinterpretations can be found suggesting de novo synthesis of n-3 and n-6 PUFA from monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA), which in turn originate from saturated fatty acids (SFA), in human and other mammalian cells. Thus, to draw attention to this problem, we performed experiments with 13 C-labeled stearic acid using a modern analytical technique to verify the possibility of de novo PUFA synthesis in mammalian cells. We have supplemented the cultures of human hepatoma-derived cells (HepG2), mouse primary fibroblasts, and Salvia apiana cells (as a positive control) with 13 C stearic acid. 13 C-labeled fatty acids originating from 13 C stearic acid were detected in cultured cells with gas chromatography – mass spectrometry with selective ion monitoring. In human and murine cells, we did not detect any n-3 or n-6 PUFA containing 13 C, whereas in Salvia apiana cells we have found linoleic acid (a representative of n-6 PUFA), which contained 13 C in its structure. Interestingly, both in human and murine cells, we have found 13 C18:2n-9. Our results agree with the early evidence that n-3 and n-6 PUFA are not synthetized de novo in mammalian cells using a modern mass spectrometry-based technique. This study should prevent the continued repetition of the erroneous notion that human or other mammalian cells can de novo synthesize n-6 or n-3 PUFAs in the lipid-related literature. Furthermore, our results show the possibility of synthesis of other, much less studied group of PUFA – n-9 PUFA from MUFA in mammalian cells.

Article.Title: Coupled interactions between particulate microplastics and leached plastic-derived additives during magnetite-assisted water treatment
Article.Authors: Kida M.; Dytłow S.; Pochwat K.; Strojny W.; Ziembowicz S.; Gruca-Rokosz R.; Koszelnik P.; Radoń M.; Bester K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The coupled interactions between particulate microplastics and dissolved plastic-derived additives were investigated using magnetite (Fe₃O₄). The investigated materials included tire wear particles (TWP), poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) pipe particles, and reference polymers. Magnetite rapidly induced heteroaggregation and enabled efficient magnetic separation of the investigated MPs. Simultaneously, dissolved plastic-associated organic compounds were scavenged from model solutions, with removal depending on their physicochemical properties. SEM, FTIR, and magnetic analyses confirmed attachment of Fe₃O₄ particles to microplastic surfaces, the formation of Fe₃O₄–MP aggregates, and the absence of detectable chemical modification of the investigated polymers. Magnetic measurements further demonstrated that the magnetic response of the heteroaggregates depended on polymer type, pH, and aggregate organization. Statistical analysis and exploratory Random Forest modelling were used to examine relationships among the investigated variables and to identify their relative contributions within the experimental dataset. Phthalate release from TWP continued after rapid magnetite-induced aggregation and separation of the microplastic particles, indicating that removal of the particulate fraction did not immediately terminate additive release from the polymer matrix. The simultaneous presence of MPs and magnetite therefore involved coupled processes associated with particulate aggregation, additive release, and scavenging of dissolved compounds. These findings demonstrate that physical removal of microplastic particles alone does not necessarily eliminate the dissolved fraction of plastic-derived contamination. The study provides an experimental assessment of these coupled processes under controlled conditions and highlights the importance of considering both particulate and dissolved plastic-related contaminants when evaluating magnetite-assisted treatment strategies.

Article.Title: Deep reinforcement learning-based adaptive FOPID tuning for power system stability enhancement: A twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient approach
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Singh M.; Singh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)-based adaptive fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative (FOPID) controller for joint load-frequency and voltage regulation in a renewable-rich power system. The proposed controller adaptively tunes five FOPID parameters, namely $${K_p}$$ , $${K_i}$$ , $${K_d}$$ ,λ, and µ, through a multi-objective reward formulation that simultaneously minimizes frequency integral time-weighted absolute error (ITAE), terminal-voltage ITAE, maximum frequency deviation, and tie-line power error. A curriculum-based training strategy is employed to progressively expose the TD3 agent to increasing disturbance severity. The proposed framework is evaluated on a modified IEEE 14-bus system incorporating 46% renewable penetration, comprising DFIG-based wind generation and photovoltaic generation under low-inertia operating conditions. Under the standard 0.10 p.u. step-load disturbance, the proposed TD3-FOPID controller achieves an ITAE of 0.0612, a settling time of 1.48 s, and an overshoot of 1.82%. Across four nominal disturbance scenarios, the obtained damping ratios range from 0.74 to 0.78, while the broader tested operating-envelope analysis gives a minimum damping ratio of 0.72. The maximum system-level ROCOF observed at disturbance inception across the evaluated scenarios is 0.82 Hz/s, below the 2 Hz/s reference threshold adopted in this study. Statistical evaluation over ten independent training/evaluation runs with different random seeds further demonstrates consistent performance of the proposed approach. Numerical Lyapunov verification using the linearized closed-loop model provides numerical evidence of stable closed-loop behaviour within the tested operating envelope. The results demonstrate the potential of TD3-based five-parameter FOPID adaptation for robust frequency and voltage regulation in renewable-rich power systems.

Article.Title: Gut microbiome composition and oxalate-related metabolic functions in staghorn calcium oxalate stone formers: a shotgun metagenomic analysis
Article.Authors: Lu Y.; Toh T.; Lim L.; Toh K.; Tan C.; Chong T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Introduction: To characterize gut microbiome composition and oxalate-related metabolic functions in patients with staghorn calcium oxalate (CaOx) stones using shotgun metagenomic sequencing, and to determine whether specific bacterial taxa and pathways differ from stone-free controls. Methods: We conducted a prospective study of adults aged 21–75 years with partial or complete staghorn stones composed of >80% CaOx who underwent percutaneous nephrolithotomy between January 2023 and April 2024. Age-matched stone-free individuals served as controls. Stool samples were collected before intervention, preserved in stabilizing buffer, and analyzed using metagenomic shotgun sequencing. Microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and metabolic pathway abundances were assessed using standard bioinformatic pipelines. Dietary intake and clinical covariates were incorporated into multivariable models. Oxalobacter formigenes prevalence was determined from metagenomic reads. Results: Fifty-six participants were included (28 stone formers, 28 controls). Stone formers demonstrated significantly reduced alpha diversity (Shannon and Chao1 indices, p<0.05) and distinct beta diversity profiles (PERMANOVA R²=0.030, p=0.009), independent of diabetes, hypertension, urolithiasis history, and respiratory conditions. Differential abundance analysis showed increased Erysipelatoclostridium ramosum SGB6744 and reduced levels of several commensals, including Bifidobacterium adolescentis , Faecalibacterium spp ., and Eubacterium rectale . Functional profiling revealed reduced abundance of bacterial pathways related to glycine, serine, and tryptophan metabolism. Oxalobacter formigenes was detected less frequently in stone formers than controls (3.6% vs 21.4%). Conclusions: Staghorn CaOx stone formers exhibit gut microbiome dysbiosis and reduced representation of metabolic pathways linked to endogenous oxalate handling. These findings support a potential mechanistic role of the gut microbiome in CaOx stone biology and justify future interventional studies targeting microbial metabolic functions.

Article.Title: The relationships among achievement motivation health related physical fitness and academic procrastination in adolescents from a multitheoretical perspective
Article.Authors: Ying J.; Feng L.; Qiu W.; Xiao H.; Yang X.; Wang Y.; Luo L.; Liu C.; Feng L.
Article.Abstract: Academic procrastination among adolescents is a complex phenomenon associated with multiple factors. This study aimed to examine the associations among achievement motivation, health-related physical fitness, and academic procrastination in adolescents. A cross-sectional study design was employed. Using a stratified cluster random sampling method, 700 adolescents aged 12–14 years were recruited from two secondary schools in Yunnan Province, China. Data were collected through an online self-report questionnaire assessing academic procrastination and achievement motivation, along with. objective field-based physical fitness tests administered by certified physical education teachers to evaluate health-related physical fitness. After excluding invalid responses, 625 valid questionnaires were retained, yielding a valid response rate of 89.28%. Statistical analyses, including correlation, regression, and mediation analyses, were conducted using SPSS version 29.0. Correlation analyses indicated significant pairwise statistical associations among achievement motivation, academic procrastination, and health-related physical fitness in adolescents. Further analysis showed that health-related physical fitness exhibited a significant indirect statistical association between achievement motivation and academic procrastination, with an indirect association estimate of − 0.014 (95% confidence interval [CI]: −0.0350 to − 0.0012). However, this indirect association was small in magnitude, accounting for only 8.33% of the total statistical association between achievement motivation and academic procrastination. Achievement motivation was significantly associated with academic procrastination among adolescents, while health-related physical fitness exhibited a significant indirect statistical association with the relationship between achievement motivation and academic procrastination. Future research should further examine the interconnected relationships among achievement motivation, health-related physical fitness, and academic procrastination to provide a more comprehensive understanding of adolescents’ academic behaviors and healthy development.

Article.Title: Initiation mechanism of irrigation-induced retrogressive loess landslides on the South Jingyang Tableland, China
Article.Authors: Ma P.; Chen L.; Xue Y.; Wang J.; Mu Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Repeated sliding disturbs the slope structure and degrades soil mechanical properties, promoting the progressive development of retrogressive loess landslides on the South Jingyang Plateau, China. These landslides progressively encroach upon the plateau surface and have caused substantial casualties and property losses. Field investigations revealed that two subsequent retrogressive failures caused the landslide crown to retreat by approximately 8 and 7 m, respectively, suggesting that the near-crown zone formed after the initial failure underwent sustained disturbance and structural readjustment. Accordingly, undisturbed loess samples were collected from a sliding-disturbed zone approximately 5 m from the current crown (No.1) and a relatively undisturbed zone approximately 50 m from the crown (No.2). Consolidated undrained triaxial tests, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) infiltration tests, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analyses were conducted to systematically compare the strength, water-migration characteristics, and microstructural damage of the soils from the two zones, thereby elucidating the triggering mechanism of retrogressive landslides. The results indicate that: (1) The soil in the sliding-disturbed zone exhibited pronounced mechanical weakening. Under natural conditions, the average shear strength of No. 1 was approximately 20% lower than that of No. 2; under saturated conditions, its shear strength was only 71.9–90.0% of that in the relatively undisturbed zone. The disturbed soil was characterized by a higher proportion of large pores, weaker interparticle bonding, and more irregular pore geometries, making its mechanical behavior more sensitive to variations in water content. (2) The sliding-disturbed zone exhibited more pronounced water migration. The average signal intensity of the second peak in the NMR T₂ spectrum was approximately 1.97 times that of the relatively undisturbed zone, indicating a stronger water-filling response within the larger-pore domain. During water infiltration, pore-structure readjustment and changes in pore morphology occurred in the disturbed zone, further promoting structural weakening of the soil. (3) The subsequent evolution of retrogressive landslides can be summarized as follows: the initial failure disturbs the slope and alters its stress state and pore structure; sustained water infiltration subsequently promotes further structural readjustment and degradation of the soil’s mechanical properties, thereby reducing slope stability and increasing the likelihood of renewed failure. This process ultimately produces a cascading “sliding–disturbance–re-sliding” evolution pattern.

Article.Title: Optical mediation of chlorophyll-a trends and radiative heating in coastal waters
Article.Authors: Adhikari A.; Cahill B.; Menon H.
Article.Abstract: Long-term trends in satellite-derived chlorophyll- a (Chl- a ) in optically complex coastal waters may reflect changes in multiple constituents rather than phytoplankton biomass alone. Using satellite Chl- a observations from 1998-2023 and 10 years of in situ hyperspectral remote-sensing reflectance data, \(R_{rs}(\lambda )\) (sr \(^{-1}\) ), together with derived constituent-specific absorption coefficients from the eastern Arabian Sea, we identified coherent positive and negative trends and classified eight optical water types. Positive-trend types generally exhibited greater particulate absorption, whereas negative-trend types showed greater fractional coloured dissolved organic matter (CDOM) absorption at shorter wavelengths. Three-stream radiative-transfer modelling revealed corresponding differences in dimensionless subsurface spectral irradiance reflectance, \(R(z,\lambda )=E_u(z,\lambda )/[E_d(z,\lambda )+E_s(z,\lambda )]\) , euphotic depth, and radiative heating rate. Positive-trend types exhibited mean euphotic depths of 4.0-5.3 m, whereas negative-trend types portrayed shallower values of 3.1-3.6 m and more surface-intensified heating. CDOM-enhanced types exhibited approximately 1.18-fold greater depth-integrated radiative heating within their respective euphotic zones, despite reduced water-leaving reflectance at strongly absorbed wavelengths. These results demonstrated that constituent composition and spectral absorption mediated both the expression of long-term variability in satellite ocean colour and the vertical distribution and transmission of solar irradiance.

Article.Title: Metagenomic insights into viral community restructuring and microbial interactions in waste stabilization ponds
Article.Authors: Rizk N.; Marouf M.; Ahmed N.; El-Gayar M.; Kamel M.; El-Khateeb M.; Sedhom R.; Elfeky E.; El-Liethy M.; Gad M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Waste stabilization ponds (WSPs) operate as sequential ecological compartments in which physicochemical gradients, microbial succession, and trophic interactions increase toward the final polishing stage. Among these units, the maturation pond represents the terminal control point for pathogen attenuation and effluent quality; however, its role in shaping viral community structure remains insufficiently resolved. Here, we applied shotgun metagenomics to characterize DNA viral communities across the full treatment train of a full-scale WSP system in Giza, Egypt, with particular emphasis on maturation-stage restructuring. Viral community composition was strongly structured by treatment stage (PERMANOVA R² = 0.53, p < 0.05), with the most pronounced compositional turnover occurring between upstream ponds and the maturation pond. Relative abundance changes were highly taxon dependent. Human-associated viral families, including Adenoviridae and Poxviridae , were detected in the inlet but fell below detection in the maturation pond, whereas other groups such as Microviridae showed partial persistence. In contrast, several bacteriophage-associated signals increased in relative abundance in the maturation pond, suggesting stage-associated restructuring of viral DNA profiles that may be linked to host community shifts, environmental filtering, or particle-associated DNA dynamics. Notably, the maturation pond virome displayed differentiation from upstream stages, including the emergence of eukaryote-associated viral signals, consistent with potential co-variation with locally established microeukaryotic communities. Cross-domain network analysis further revealed that the maturation pond was characterized by tightly connected virus–bacteria–microeukaryote modules dominated by positive associations, indicative of coordinated responses to shared environmental filtering. Together, these findings position the maturation pond as a distinct ecological compartment associated with downstream virome restructuring under combined environmental filtering, treatment-stage conditions, and host-community-associated processes.

Article.Title: Prioritizing usability attributes in bottled food packaging for older consumers using the Kano model
Article.Authors: Jian X.; Mustafa M.
Article.Abstract: Bottled food packaging may pose operational challenges for older adults due to age-related declines in physical strength, joint mobility, and sensory perception. However, limited research has systematically examined how different packaging usability attributes influence user satisfaction and dissatisfaction. This study investigates operability-related design attributes of bottled food packaging for older consumers using a mixed-methods approach. Semi-structured interviews were first conducted to identify common operational difficulties and generate candidate attributes. A two-round Delphi consultation with experts was then used to refine and validate the attribute system. Finally, a Kano-model questionnaire survey involving 385 older adults was conducted to evaluate how the presence or absence of specific attributes affects user satisfaction. The results identified 27 usability-related attributes across five dimensions: functionality, reliability, usability, proficiency, and creativity. Basic operational and safety-related attributes were mainly classified as Must-be or One-dimensional attributes, indicating that their absence strongly increases dissatisfaction. In contrast, innovation-related attributes were primarily categorized as Attractive attributes, contributing to satisfaction when present but not causing dissatisfaction when absent. These findings reveal an asymmetric satisfaction–dissatisfaction mechanism in older adults’ evaluation of packaging usability and provide design implications for developing ageing-friendly bottled food packaging.

Article.Title: Effect of Bacillus sp. N188 application on turf quality and functional value
Article.Authors: Radkowski A.; Szpytma M.; Radkowska I.; Bujak H.; Dobrzyński J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Maintaining high-quality functional and recreational turfgrass requires effective management practices that support turf performance under field conditions. One promising strategy involves the use of plant growth-promoting microorganisms. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of Bacillus sp. N188 on turf quality and functional performance. A field experiment was conducted in 2024–2025 under the conditions of southern Poland on Haplic Phaeozem soil. The study included two lawn mixtures differing in species composition and intended use: “Uniwersalna U-1” and “Super Trawnik”. The experimental design comprised control treatments and variants with annual application of a preparation containing Bacillus sp. N188. Turf quality was assessed according to the COBORU methodology, including visual traits (overall appearance, turf density, leaf colour and structure, and disease susceptibility), as well as physiological indices (NDVI, LAI, SPAD) and selected indicators of functional value. The application of Bacillus sp. N188 significantly improved turf quality compared to the control treatments. An increase in sward density and uniformity, more intense leaf coloration, improved structural characteristics, and reduced incidence of fungal diseases were observed. The physiological indices confirmed improved plant condition in plots treated with the bacterial preparation. The positive effects of Bacillus sp. N188 were observed in both lawn mixtures, although the magnitude of the response varied depending on species composition. The results indicate that Bacillus sp. N188 has potential as a plant biostimulant for improving the aesthetic and functional properties of turfgrass under temperate climatic conditions.

Article.Title: A new evolutive clustering algorithm (eSIMBA) for active module identification in p-value attributed temporal biological networks
Article.Authors: Singlan N.; Abou Choucha F.; Pasquier C.
Article.Abstract: Biological processes are inherently dynamic: gene expression and molecular interactions fluctuate as cellular mechanisms evolve over time. Active Module Identification Methods (AMIMs) capture these functional behaviours by identifying sets of molecular entities exhibiting coordinated activity. Yet, understanding biological systems requires more than a static picture and calls for the temporal contextualization of such modular dynamics. To address this need, the proposed algorithm combines static and sliding-time-window community detection using a greedy matching procedure that maintains continuity across time. This method detects active modules at each time point and consistently tracks their evolution. Extensive experiments performed on both synthetic and real-world biological networks confirm its effectiveness. By explicitly embracing temporal variability, the proposed approach reveals how active modules emerge, split, merge, or disappear, providing new insights into the dynamic organization of node-attributed biological networks.

Article.Title: Design, implementation, and evaluation of a comprehensive educational program for microbiology laboratory personnel and graduate students in teaching hospitals
Article.Authors: Baseri Z.; Irajian G.; Dehghan A.
Article.Abstract: Patient care and clinical diagnosis are significantly dependent on laboratory results. Repeated shortages of skills and evolving technologies, however, highlight the need for continuous professional development in graduate students and laboratory personnel. The purpose of this study was to design, implement, and evaluate a comprehensive educational program for the microbiology personnel in the teaching hospitals of Tehran University of Medical Sciences as well as for postgraduate students. This single-group, uncontrolled pre-test/post-test evaluation included a nine-month pre-and-post audit of laboratory quality. Baseline assessments in 14 teaching hospitals identified training needs. Ten focused workshops on a set of priority topics, including quality control, antimicrobial resistance, and specimen processing were formulated. Personnel were required to attend, whereas students were invited to attend. Pre- and post-tests, follow-up laboratory audits, and participant satisfaction surveys were used to assess the program’s effectiveness. In total, 282 personnel and 200 student workshop attendances were analyzed; all participants who began a session completed both the pre- and post-tests. Post-test knowledge scores increased significantly for personnel (4.32 ± 1.66 to 7.52 ± 1.70; p < 0.001; Cohen’s d z = 1.68) and students (3.64 ± 1.08 to 7.35 ± 1.47; p < 0.001; Cohen’s d z = 2.33). At nine months, the mean audit score across 14 centers improved from 15.86 ± 2.99 to 17.93 ± 2.75 out of 20 (mean improvement 2.07, 95% CI 1.16–2.98; paired t (13) = 4.93, p < 0.001; Wilcoxon p = 0.001). Satisfaction was high: 85% rated the program as “very good,” and 15% rated it as “good.” The implementation of an organized program led to substantial improvements in knowledge and laboratory audit scores. Due to the lack of a control group and improvements in other areas apart from the training, one cannot conclude that these improvements can be directly attributed to the effect of the training alone. Control groups, individual attendance data, and validated assessment instruments need to be included in future evaluations.

Article.Title: Antioxidant treatments combined with refrigerated storage, modified atmosphere packaging, and precooling improve postharvest quality of red cabbage
Article.Authors: Abo Elmakarem A.; Mostafa N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postharvest deterioration of red cabbage involves water loss, oxidative imbalance, membrane damage, and loss of structural and sensory quality. This study evaluated the effects of four food-grade antioxidants—ascorbic acid, citric acid, glutathione, and α-tocopherol—together with an untreated control under three refrigerated storage strategies: conventional refrigeration, modified atmosphere packaging (MAP), and pre-cooling followed by MAP. A 5 × 3 factorial experiment was conducted to assess treatment effects and interactions on physiological, biochemical, oxidative, structural, and quality-related attributes after 12 weeks of storage. Antioxidant treatment, storage condition, and their interaction significantly affected several measured attributes, indicating that treatment responses varied with the storage environment. The combination of citric acid and pre-cooling followed by MAP resulted in the lowest weight loss (8.96%), representing a 69.6% reduction compared with the untreated control under the same storage condition (29.46%). Under this combination, SOD activity reached 49.08 units mg⁻¹ protein compared with 25.69 units mg⁻¹ protein in the corresponding control. Antioxidant treatments also influenced phytochemical retention, membrane stability, firmness, texture, and oxidative-stress-related responses, although the magnitude and direction of effects varied among antioxidant–storage combinations. Multivariate analyses supported associations among oxidative status, antioxidant defense, structural attributes, and postharvest quality. The results indicate that antioxidant application can complement refrigerated MAP-based storage, with citric acid combined with pre-cooling and MAP providing the lowest weight loss among the tested combinations. These findings support the potential of integrating food-grade antioxidant treatments with established refrigerated handling practices, while further studies are needed to evaluate their performance under commercial-scale conditions.

Article.Title: SGA-based volleyball teaching with explicit life skills instruction is associated with technical-tactical, psychosocial, and motivational improvements in school students
Article.Authors: Gonçalves C.; de Sá Filho A.; Arantes D.; Clemente F.; Silva R.; Gonçalves C.; Trybulski R.; Rodrigues M.; Noll M.; de Lira C.; Laporta L.; De Conti Teixeira Costa G.
Article.Abstract: This quasi-experimental study examined whether a school volleyball unit based on the Step-Game-Approach model combined with explicit life skills teaching (SGA + LS) was associated with changes in technical-tactical performance, life skills, motivation, and perception of success. The intervention comprised 18 Physical Education classes. Outcomes were assessed before and/or after the intervention using IAD-VB, Life Skills Scale for Sport, Behavioral Regulation in Sport Questionnaire, and Perception of Success Questionnaire. Significant group × time interactions that remained significant after false discovery rate correction were observed for goal setting, Wald χ²(2) = 11.875, pFDR=0.009, time management, Wald χ²(2) = 10.203, pFDR=0.014, and communication, Wald χ²(2) = 7.538, pFDR=0.044. All technical-tactical outcomes showed significant adjusted interactions, Wald χ²(2) = 10.764–60.676, pFDR≤0.012, with both volleyball-specific conditions showing improvements across several outcomes. At post-test, SGA + LS showed higher decision-making than control, whereas SGA + LS and direct instruction did not differ significantly after Holm adjustment. Article.Title: Prevalence of ocular allergy among children in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Ismail M.; Khalafalla I.; Dirie A.; Alemayehu C.; Zalwango C.; Isse S.; Farah F.; Sheck Z.; Mire A.; Herow A.; Ahmed A.; Abdi F.; Mohamed I.; Jayte M.; Mumin B.; Hakizimana T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ocular allergy ranges from seasonal and perennial allergic conjunctivitis to chronic, potentially sight-threatening vernal keratoconjunctivitis (VKC). African prevalence studies use heterogeneous terminology and case-ascertainment methods, and their estimates have not previously been synthesized. To synthesise published prevalence estimates of ocular allergy among African children, quantify uncertainty around summary estimates, and describe between-study variation. PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, African Journals Online and African Index Medicus were searched for observational studies published from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2025. Disease-specific terms were supplemented with broader ocular-morbidity terminology, reference-list screening and citation verification to identify studies reporting ocular allergy as a secondary outcome. Eligible studies enrolled African children and provided an extractable numerator and denominator. Logit-transformed proportions were pooled using a random-effects restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) model in Stata 17. Heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals, diagnostic and setting subgroups, and sensitivity analyses were reported. Fourteen studies from five countries included 18,681 children, of whom 1,911 had ocular allergy, allergic conjunctivitis or VKC/vernal disease. The pooled prevalence was 9.4% (95% confidence interval [CI] 5.4%–15.6%), with extreme heterogeneity (τ2 = 1.23; I2 = 99.19%; Q(13) = 1844.38, p < 0.001) and a 95% prediction interval of 0.8%–55.9%. The pooled estimate was 14.5% (95% CI 5.5%–33.0%; k = 6) for allergic conjunctivitis and 6.6% (95% CI 3.8%–11.2%; k = 8) for VKC/vernal disease; the subgroup difference was not statistically significant (Q β (1) = 1.99, p = 0.158). School/community studies yielded 8.9% (95% CI 5.0%–15.4%; k = 13), whereas the single clinic study reported 17.6% (95% CI 15.8%–19.6%). Substituting a narrower VKC case definition gave 8.4% (95% CI 4.9%–14.2%), and leave-one-out estimates ranged from 8.0% to 10.2%. Published studies consistently report ocular allergy among African children, although the available evidence is too heterogeneous to support a reliable continental prevalence estimate. Variation in case definition and ascertainment is a plausible and likely substantial contributor, but could not be quantified formally. The findings support consideration of ocular allergy within school eye-health and primary eye-care programmes while underscoring the need for standardised diagnostic and reporting methods.

Article.Authors: Abdo M.; Elnaggar M.; Elissawy A.; Gad H.; El-Ahmady S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lepidium sativum L. (garden cress) seeds are a valuable source of oil rich in unsaturated fatty acids. This study examined the effect of extraction temperature on the yield, fatty acid composition, metabolic profile, and functional properties of L. sativum seed oil. Chemical characterization by GC–MS revealed marked differences between the two oils. α-Linolenic acid was the major fatty acid in CSO (36.04%), whereas oleic acid predominated in HSO (24.73%). The influence of these compositional changes on functional properties was assessed using DPPH radical-scavenging and α-amylase inhibition assays. CSO showed higher antioxidant activity (IC 50 = 138.47 ± 2.87 µg mL −1 ) and stronger α-amylase inhibitory activity (IC 50 = 123.46 ± 2.48 µg mL −1 ) than HSO. The results demonstrate that extraction temperature significantly affects the lipid composition of L. sativum seed oil and is associated with changes in its functional properties.

Article.Title: Deep reinforcement learning based optimal control for wave energy converters: practical implementation and experimental validation
Article.Authors: Subramanian A.; Zou S.; Bosma B.; Lou J.; Beringer C.; Robertson B.; Lomonaco P.
Article.Abstract: Ocean wave energy resources are immense and, if harnessed, can serve as a reliable source to support a significant portion of electricity needs. However, the technology to convert wave power into useful electrical power is still cost-intensive. One significant challenge is inefficient Power Take-Off (PTO) control technologies. To address this challenge, the research team has previously developed a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based optimal control for Wave Energy Converters (WECs) and has shown promising performance in terms of power production and quality (in contrast to state-of-the-art advanced PTO controls). However, the study remains on paper, and the practical performance of the control is unknown. Therefore, in this study, we present the practical implementation and experimental validation of the DRL-based optimal control through wave tank testing, aiming to provide meaningful insights into (1) the challenges and limitations associated with implementing the DRL control in practice; and (2) the real-world power production performance (in contrast to numerical predictions), which is vital knowledge for the practical viability of DRL control (and, more broadly, other advanced controls). More specifically, the control is demonstrated using the Laboratory Upgrade Point Absorber (LUPA) WEC at Oregon State University and tested under a variety of regular and irregular wave conditions. Important takeaways from the testing results are: (1) The real-time implementation of the DRL control is straightforward with a low computational cost; (2) the robustness of the control under uncertainties and nonlinearities in real-world applications can be improved by introducing significant randomness during training; (3) The power produced in the real world is significantly less than that predicted by the numerical simulations due to various types of losses in the system (e.g., mechanical friction, electromagnetic damping, etc.), and (4) The DRL control is able to achieve good power production compared to practical control.

Article.Title: Knowledge attitudes and practices regarding toothbrush hygiene and disinfection among dental students in a multicenter cross sectional study
Article.Authors: Demircan B.; Çamgöz A.; Çalışkan A.; Selen M.; Aydogdu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate dental students’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding toothbrush contamination and disinfection, and to assess differences according to clinical training level and gender. A total of 1206 dental students (years 1–5) from three dental faculties in Turkey were included. Data were collected through an online questionnaire covering demographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Chi-square test, independent samples t-test, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) were used for statistical analysis. Of the participants, 767 were preclinical and 439 were clinical students. Mean knowledge, practice, attitude, and total scores were 3.87 ± 0.76, 3.45 ± 1.32, 2.83 ± 0.61, and 10.14 ± 1.86, respectively. Disinfection knowledge was higher in the clinical group ( p = 0.010), whereas disinfection practice was lower ( p = 0.001). The practice rate was significantly higher among students with disinfection knowledge (70.8% vs. 46.2%; p < 0.001) and among those who considered disinfection necessary (57.1% vs. 14.7%; p < 0.001). The most common source of information was social media, and the most frequently reported disinfection method was tap water. Knowledge and positive attitudes do not consistently translate into evidence-based practice among dental students. Although clinical training improves knowledge, it does not independently enhance disinfection behavior. Toothbrush hygiene should therefore be addressed through practice-oriented learning outcomes from the preclinical years.

Article.Title: A comprehensive study on multi-dimensional predictive safety analysis of machine learning models in diabetes detection
Article.Authors: Mumenin N.; Pranto M.; Yousuf M.; Monowar M.; Hamid M.; Alotaibi F.; Alassafi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High discrimination performance is often interpreted as evidence of model reliability in clinical machine learning (ML). However, strong predictive accuracy does not guarantee safe decision behavior. In safety-critical domains such as healthcare, miscalibrated probabilities, ineffective uncertainty estimation, and overconfident errors can lead to harmful decisions despite high area-under-curve metrics. This study presents a comprehensive multi-dimensional predictive safety analysis demonstrating that models with comparable discrimination performance can exhibit substantially different reliability and risk characteristics. We conduct a rigorous benchmarking evaluation across two heterogeneous diabetes risk datasets, a large population-scale BRFSS cohort and a small-sample early-stage clinical dataset. A diverse set of classical, ensemble, and deep tabular models are evaluated under a strict leakage-free cross-validation protocol with dedicated calibration splits. Beyond conventional discrimination metrics (PR-AUC, ROC-AUC), we assess probabilistic calibration (ECE, Brier score, NLL), epistemic uncertainty using a unified bootstrap-based framework, uncertainty–error correlation, selective prediction safety, high-confidence error rates, subgroup fairness across age and sex, and conformal prediction with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees under the standard exchangeability assumption. Our results reveal a consistent accuracy–safety gap that models achieving near-identical PR-AUC display markedly different calibration quality, uncertainty effectiveness, subgroup reliability, and overconfidence behavior. On the early-stage clinical dataset, near-ceiling discrimination performance is observed across models, but due to the limited sample size, these results should be interpreted cautiously, as variability across folds may affect the stability of comparative performance across models. The findings demonstrate that discrimination metrics alone are insufficient to characterize reliable clinical decision-making. A comprehensive evaluation incorporating calibration, uncertainty quality, subgroup fairness, and formal coverage guarantees is essential for the trustworthy pre-deployment assessment of machine learning in healthcare. Rather than introducing a new predictive algorithm, this work contributes a unified empirical audit of safety-relevant model behavior, addressing reliability dimensions that are commonly evaluated separately or omitted in conventional diabetes prediction benchmarks.

Article.Title: Using sensor and self-reported data to understand fatigue within the massage therapy profession
Article.Authors: Resnick P.
Article.Abstract: This exploratory study examined the relationship between the massage modalities used, the length of the massage treatment, and the areas of the body massaged on the perceived self-reported effort level and muscular fatigue as well as the ergonomic sensor data for average composite risk score and average fatigue risk score. Participants completed their normal routine of massages while wearing sensors: watch placed on the upper arm to collect physiological data; GoX ® sensor placed on the dominant upper arm and back of the shirt to collect ergonomic data. Participants performed massages in their regular clinic, following their normal treatment plan. Following each session, a survey was completed about the massage treatment, including areas massaged, techniques used and self-reported effort and muscle fatigue. Mean self-reported effort level was 10.71± 2.40, light level on the Borg Scale. Mean self-reported muscular fatigue level was 2.69 ± 0.75, light activity on the RPE scale. Length of time of the massage session was not a strong indicator of subjective or objective measures. No one technique provided an increased risk of fatigue. This exploratory study gave a snapshot into fatigue and risks for work-related musculoskeletal disorders in massage therapists while practicing in their normal clinical setting.

Article.Title: HIFN-Mamba: hybrid information flow networks with selective state-space sequence modeling for intrusion detection in the Internet of Medical Things
Article.Authors: Tawfik M.; Almekhlafi M.; Shakah G.; Al-walidi N.; Fathi I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The exponential growth of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) — a multi-billion-device infrastructure of clinically critical sensors, monitors, and connected medical equipment — has dramatically expanded the attack surface for ransomware, lateral-movement, and protocol-specific exploits against healthcare networks. Existing deep-learning intrusion detection systems (IDSs) for this domain suffer from three coupled limitations: fixed information-bottleneck hyperparameters that cannot adapt to heterogeneous protocol distributions, dependence on costly post-hoc explainability methods (SHAP, LIME) that violate sub-millisecond clinical latency budgets, and quadratic-cost attention mechanisms that are infeasible for edge deployment. This paper proposes HIFN-Mamba, a hybrid architecture that couples a two-layer Hybrid Information Flow Network (HIFN) trunk with a stack of selective state-space (Mamba/S6) sequence blocks. Each HIFN layer learns four information-theoretic regulators end-to-end: a static gate vector providing intrinsic sample-invariant feature interpretability, a magnitude scaling factor preventing latent collapse, an information retention coefficient replacing the fixed beta of the Variational Information Bottleneck, and an entropy budget enforcing a hinge constraint on latent differential entropy. We prove that HIFN strictly generalises VIB and that all four regulators remain bounded for any finite training dynamics. Empirical evaluation across the IoMT-focused CICIoMT2024 dataset and two cross-domain benchmarks (UNSW-NB15, CICIDS-2017) in six experimental settings yields 99.999% accuracy with zero false alarms on CICIoMT2024 binary, 99.995% accuracy and 0.9999 macro-F1 on CICIoMT2024 19-class, and sub-millisecond inference latency (0.0129–0.0170 ms/sample) on all six experiments. The static gates provide global feature rankings at zero inference cost, eliminating the exponential complexity of post-hoc SHAP. To our knowledge, HIFN-Mamba is the first IoMT IDS to combine learned information-theoretic regularisation with linear-time selective state-space modelling and to report verifiable sub-millisecond throughput on a nineteen-class IoMT benchmark.

Article.Title: Trajectories of body roundness index and risk of incident hyperuricemia in middle-aged and older Chinese adults: evidence from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study
Article.Authors: Zou C.; Huang L.; He L.
Article.Abstract: The body roundness index (BRI) is an emerging anthropometric indicator of abdominal obesity. However, the longitudinal association between BRI trajectories and the risk of hyperuricemia remains unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between long-term BRI trajectories and incident hyperuricemia among middle-aged and older Chinese adults. This prospective cohort study included 4565 participants aged ≥ 45 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) who were free of hyperuricemia at baseline. Group-based trajectory modeling was used to identify distinct BRI trajectories across the 2011, 2013, and 2015 waves. Multivariable logistic regression models were applied to estimate odds ratios for hyperuricemia assessed at the 2015 follow-up, with Model 2 (adjusting for demographic and lifestyle factors) designated as the primary model. Four distinct BRI trajectories were identified: low (19.2%), moderate-low (35.9%), moderate-high (28.8%), and high (16.1%). At the 2015 assessment, 458 participants (10.03%) were identified with hyperuricemia. In the primary model, participants in the moderate-low, moderate-high, and high trajectory groups had significantly higher odds of hyperuricemia compared with the low group, with odds ratios (ORs) of 1.92 (95% CI 1.35–2.73), 3.04 (95% CI 2.13–4.35), and 4.80 (95% CI 3.26–7.05), respectively (P for trend < 0.001). These associations persisted for the moderate-high and high groups after additional adjustment for baseline BRI and serum uric acid (ORs 1.79 and 2.35, respectively). Extended adjustment models incorporating additional clinical and laboratory covariates yielded consistent results. Higher long-term BRI trajectories were associated with greater odds of hyperuricemia among middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and this association persisted after additional adjustment for baseline BRI and serum uric acid. These findings support the relevance of longitudinal adiposity patterns to hyperuricemia risk, while the exposure–outcome overlap limits causal and prospective interpretation.

Article.Title: m6A-modified mRNA–LNP system enables in vivo CAR expression and is associated with antitumor immune responses
Article.Authors: Meng S.; Hara T.; Sato T.; Tatekawa S.; Yanagida K.; Nikaido K.; Saito Y.; Arao Y.; Motooka D.; Ofusa K.; Ogawa K.; Nishiyama N.; Mori M.; Eguchi H.; Satoh T.; Miura Y.; Ishii H.
Article.Abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have emerged as a versatile modality for transient gene delivery, but strategies to incorporate epitranscriptomic regulation into synthetic mRNA design remain limited. Among RNA modifications, N6-methyladenosine (m 6 A) is a major regulator of mRNA stability, translation, and cellular signaling through coordinated actions of methyltransferases, binding proteins, and demethylases. However, the use of engineered m 6 A-modified mRNAs to modulate immune responses in vivo has been relatively unexplored. Here, we developed a tunable lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery system using m 6 A-modified mRNAs encoding chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP). Administration of these mRNA–LNPs was associated with altered RNA methylation states in immune cells and elicited antitumor immune responses. Transcriptomic analyses indicated activation of immune-related pathways and signatures consistent with immune memory. The formulation design was modular, allowing modification of LNP composition. Substitution with pH-responsive polybetaines maintained therapeutic activity without substantial loss of efficacy. In addition, replacing the FAP-targeting sequence with cancer stem cell (CSC) markers, including EpCAM, LGR5, and CD133, preserved antitumor responses. Targeting CSC-associated antigens was also accompanied by suppression of tumor-intrinsic SPP1 signaling pathways. Together, these results suggest that mRNA–LNPs provide a flexible and programmable system for CAR targeting and immunotherapy, influencing epitranscriptomic states while enabling modulation of nanoparticle composition and antigen specificity. This work establishes a framework for the development of programmable mRNA-based cancer immunotherapies through synthetic RNA engineering and controlled m 6 A modification of exogenous mRNA.

Article.Title: A sliding mode control approach to suppress power quality challenges in single-phase variable frequency drives within the constant power region
Article.Authors: Maleki M.; Tafti M.; Motamedi M.; Vahidi B.; Montazeri S.; Hosseinian S.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes a variable frequency drive (VFD) for single-phase induction motors that features power factor correction (PFC) and addresses power quality issues, including current and voltage harmonic distortion on the grid and load sides. The proposed VFD topology employs a two-stage architecture: a front-end totem-pole PFC stage for controlling the DC-link voltage and a subsequent neutral point clamped (NPC) inverter to supply the induction motor with the commanded output voltage waveform. To ensure robust performance, the front-end converter employs an adaptive gain super-twisting sliding mode control (SSMC). This approach concurrently achieves the unity power factor and minimizes the total harmonic distortion (THD) in the grid current and voltage. The NPC stage switches are governed/driven by a controller based on the unipolar selective harmonic elimination (SHE) technique to satisfy the load-side voltage quality specifications. Simulation results confirm that the designed VFD complies with relevant power quality standards across the entire constant power operating region of a typical single-phase induction motor. Furthermore, a comprehensive report covers the designed VFD performance across various frequencies of the output voltage. Results verify the superiority of the SSMC hysteresis current control over the PI peak current control within the power quality characteristics.

Article.Abstract: This study investigated the structural behaviour of Concrete Filled Steel Tubular (CFST) columns under axial compression using two infill materials: Lightweight Concrete (LWC) and Hybrid Fibre-Reinforced Concrete (HFRC). In Phase I, the LWC mix was developed by partially replacing the fine aggregate with perlite and the coarse aggregate with pumice stone, and incorporating PVA fibres. In Phase II, the HFRC mix was developed by partial replacement of cement by flyash with the addition of Polypropylene (PP) and Coconut Fibre (CF). In Phase III, CFST column specimens filled with both LWC(CFSTLWC) and HFRC(CFSTHFRC) were experimentally tested to examine load deformation response, ductility, energy absorption, and failure characteristics. CFST columns filled with LWC demonstrated reduced self-weight while maintaining satisfactory load-carrying capacity and deformation behaviour, and CFSTHFRC columns exhibited a significant improvement in structural performance, achieving approximately 39% higher axial load capacity compared to a CFST column filled with Control Concrete (CFSTCC). A parametric study was conducted by varying diameter-to-thickness (D/t) and length-to-diameter (L/D) ratios to assess their influence on axial performance using finite element analysis. The findings highlight that an increase in (D/t) reduces the confinement and thereby reduces the load-carrying capacity, and increasing (L/D) results in an increase in buckling behaviour, which reduces the load-carrying capacity. Axial load carrying capacity of CFST columns compared with existing codal provisions. A mathematical model was also developed with L/D and (D/t), which predicted the ultimate strength ratio of CFST columns filled with LWC and HFRC, having a coefficient of correlation of 0.934 and 0.948 and validated with the experimental results existing in the literature.

Article.Title: Linking environmental variability to diatom assemblages in seasonal wetlands
Article.Authors: Madonsela N.; Mangadze T.; Mpopetsi P.; Munyai L.; Dondofema F.; Dalu T.
Article.Abstract: Seasonal wetlands undergo recurrent inundation and contraction, creating strong hydrochemical variability and non–independent observations within pans. We tested whether this variability translated into diatom differentiation in five pans within each of two South African Ramsar wetland systems, Makuleke and Nylsvley, during cool–dry and hot–wet seasons. Two field replicates per pan–season yielded 40 diatom samples and 40 environmental records. Environmental replicates were averaged within pan–season; diatom relative abundances were calculated within each replicate and averaged with equal weight. Fifty–three taxa were detected. Makuleke had higher temperature, pH, total dissolved solids, conductivity and several major ions than Nylsvley, whereas temperature, total dissolved solids, conductivity, nitrate and sodium differed between seasons. Hierarchical permutation tests detected no community difference between systems or system by season interaction, and the seasonal pattern approached but did not reach the 0.05 threshold. Rarefied diversity and the six variable canonical correspondence model were also non–significant. Thus, hydrochemical separation did not yield supported assemblage separation at the sampled scale. These results caution against inferring ecological status from nested samples and identify repeated, substrate consistent monitoring as necessary for diatom–based assessment of seasonal wetlands.

Article.Title: TMEM174 deficiency reduces longevity by promoting phosphate-driven vascular calcification
Article.Authors: Miranda J.; Blaine J.; Miyazaki M.
Article.Abstract: Dysregulation of phosphate homeostasis contributes to reduced longevity and vascular complications in chronic kidney disease and aging. This study investigates the role of TMEM174, a proximal tubule-specific protein, in regulating the phosphate co-transporter NPT2A and its subsequent impact on lifespan and vascular health. TMEM174 knockout (KO) mice (C57BL6/J and DBA/2 J) were fed diets with varying phosphate concentrations (0.6% vs. 1.2%). In OKP cells, TIRF and FRET microscopy, alongside immunoprecipitation, were used to identify the TMEM174 protein regions essential for NPT2A binding and endocytosis. TMEM174 KO mice exhibited significantly shorter lifespans than wild-type controls. High phosphate diets exacerbated vascular calcification, stiffness, and mortality, while low phosphate diets rescued these phenotypes. In vitro, TMEM174 siRNA blocked PTH-induced NPT2A endocytosis, increasing its apical membrane retention. FRET and biochemical assays revealed that the C-terminal region of TMEM174 is essential for its association with NPT2A. While intact TMEM174 and N-terminal mutants (TMEM174ΔN) facilitated NPT2A degradation, C-terminal deletions (TMEM174ΔC) failed to associate with or degrade NPT2A. TMEM174 is a critical regulator of phosphate homeostasis and longevity. The C-terminal region of TMEM174 is specifically required for NPT2A endocytosis and degradation, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target for managing phosphate-related vascular complications.

Article.Title: Coordinated integration of renewables, STATCOMs, and V2G for hosting capacity improvement under uncertainty
Article.Authors: Ali Z.; Aleem S.; Aldawsari F.; Zenhom Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although incorporating renewable energy sources (RESs) into electric distribution networks (EDNs) offers significant sustainability and environmental benefits, improper management of RESs may threaten the technical performance of the network. To assess the safe integration of distributed generation (DG), the hosting capacity (HC) concept is employed. Plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), through coordinated charging and discharging, can further support RES integration. Moreover, reactive power compensation using devices such as static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) remains a key strategy for mitigating voltage violations under high RES penetration. This article proposes a novel stochastic multi-objective optimization framework, from the distribution system operator’s (DSO) perspective, to optimally coordinate the dispatch of PEV aggregators, wind-based DGs, PV-based DGs, and STATCOMs. The model accounts for uncertainties in load demand, solar radiation, wind speed, and PEV demand using stochastic programming. The objectives are to maximize HC while minimizing voltage deviation and power losses. The feasibility of employing a recent optimization technique, Tianji’s Horse Racing Optimization (THRO), to solve the proposed multi-objective problem is demonstrated and benchmarked against three other optimization algorithms on both the IEEE 33-bus system and a real 59-bus network in Cairo, Egypt. Results of IEEE 33-bus EDN show that optimal coordination of V2G-enabled PEVs and reactive power support via STATCOMs can enhance HC by 37%, reduce voltage deviation by 74%, and decrease power losses by 15%. In addition, the Cairo 59-bus EDN system exhibited similar trends, achieving an approximately 83% increase in hosting capacity, accompanied by nearly a 39% reduction in voltage deviation.

Article.Title: A train-once, evaluate-twice protocol for cross-lingual depression detection with large language models
Article.Authors: Abdalla A.; Parvez M.; Alam T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depression affects more than 280 million people worldwide, and social media text provides a large-scale resource for automated mental health assessment. Large language model (LLM)-based approaches have shown promising performance for social media-based depression detection; however, their cross-lingual robustness for underrepresented languages such as Arabic remains insufficiently explored. We proposed the “train once, evaluate twice” protocol to evaluate the cross-lingual robustness of eight LLMs for detecting depression in both English and Arabic. For six open-source LLMs, we used QLoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) to adapt them; for two closed-source GPT models, we fine-tuned them with the OpenAI supervised fine-tuning (SFT) API. To provide context for understanding transfer performance, we also evaluated a translation-based pipeline (MarianMT + XLM-R) and a bilingual fine-tuning ablation using data-mixing techniques. The models performed nearly at ceiling in their monolingual evaluation (English), with the best Macro-F1 score of 0.990 in GPT-4.1 Mini, and moderately well in Arabic (best Macro-F1 of 0.800 in Qwen2). Cross-lingual evaluation revealed significant directional asymmetry. The strongest transfer performance was observed in AR → EN (Macro-F1 = 0.793 for GPT-4.1 mini), whereas EN → AR remained considerably more challenging (best Macro-F1 = 0.638 for GPT-3.5 Turbo). The MarianMT + XLM-R translate-then-classify baseline achieved consistently lower cross-lingual performance than the fine-tuned generative LLMs evaluated in this study. The results of a bilingual fine-tuning ablation experiment conducted using Qwen2-7B-Instruct suggested that bilingual data mixing is sufficient to preserve English performance at near-ceiling levels. However, bilingual data mixing did not improve Arabic performance relative to monolingual Arabic fine-tuning. Thus, for this family of models, simple bilingual exposure appears insufficient to address the cross-lingual performance gap. Error analysis showed that EN→AR transfer predominantly increased false negatives, whereas AR → EN transfer exhibited more balanced precision–recall degradation profiles. Notably, the two Arabic-specialized models evaluated did not consistently outperform the strongest general-purpose multilingual models under cross-lingual transfer settings. PEFT produced compact adapters with low local inference latency, whereas API-based GPT inference exhibited substantially higher end-to-end latency. These findings support the notion that standard single-language fine-tuning does not afford much robustness when models are deployed across languages, especially in the EN → AR direction; thus, providing impetus for further research into new methods for adapting LLMs across multiple languages. Article.Title: Assessment of the appropriateness of the selection for radiotherapy intensity from a quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30) perspective in older patients with cancer
Article.Authors: Murofushi K.; Kuribayashi S.; Ohnishi K.; Hayakawa S.; Tsuchida K.; Inoue Y.; Ohkawa A.; Ishida T.; Machitori Y.; Murakami M.; Takizawa D.; Saito M.
Article.Abstract: We previously evaluated the predictive factors for reduced radiotherapy intensity based on radiation oncologist experience. In this study, we evaluated the appropriateness of the treatment intensity selection based on radiation and medical oncologists’ experience from a patient-reported outcome (PRO) perspective. We prospectively enrolled patients with non-metastatic cancer (≥ 70 years) between November 2020 and February 2022. Reduced treatment intensity implied changes to the irradiation field, radiotherapy schedule, and/or concurrent chemotherapy from the standard based on primary tumor guidelines. PRO was assessed using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Core Quality of Life Questionnaire scores before radiotherapy and at 3–5 and 8–16 weeks post-radiotherapy. A clinically relevant change was defined as a difference of ≥ 10 points. Overall, 294 of 317 enrolled patients were eligible for analysis. Treatment policies were modified in 72 patients (24%), and 43 patients (15%) experienced grade ≥ 3 acute adverse events. None of the observed differences between before and after radiotherapy were ≥ 10 points in the standard and reduced-intensity treatment groups. Significant differences were observed in physical and role functioning, and dyspnea (p = 0.015, 0.003, and 0.010, respectively) in patients with grade ≥ 3 adverse events, which deteriorated by ≥ 10 points. Our results indicate that the treatment intensity was appropriately selected from a PRO perspective. Nevertheless, it is necessary to pay attention to the deterioration of quality of life after radiotherapy for older patients with grade ≥ 3 adverse events. This study was registered in the University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN) under the number UMIN 000042473. We assessed the appropriateness of treatment intensity selection in cancer patients aged ≥ 70 years using PRO. Of 294 patients, 24% received reduced-intensity treatment and 15% experienced grade ≥ 3 adverse events. Quality of life changes were minimal, indicating appropriate treatment selection; however, a significant decline occurred in severe adverse events.

Article.Title: Testosterone exposure shifts female baseline phenotypes toward a male-associated tear-nerve-epithelial state in mice
Article.Authors: Feret N.; Megido A.; Pernot S.; Girard M.; Decoudu M.; Kindermans J.; Fichter L.; Llorens S.; Attina A.; Vialaret J.; David A.; Daien V.; Loulier K.; Hirtz C.; Michon F.

We compared vehicle-treated female mice with testosterone-treated females and used intact males as a physiological reference rather than as a procedure-matched control. Modified-nucleoside profiling, tear proteomics, corneal and trigeminal ganglion RNA sequencing, corneal flat-mount nerve volumetry, von Frey aesthesiometry, phospho-histone H3 labelling and single-endpoint Krt14-CreERT; CAG-Cytbow lineage tracing were combined to examine the tear-nerve-epithelial system at baseline. Tear collection rate was unchanged, whereas total tear protein concentration and proteomic composition differed between vehicle-treated and testosterone-treated females and shifted toward the intact male reference; 1,052 of 3,125 identified tear proteins were modulated in at least one pairwise comparison. Testosterone-treated females also showed lower central βIII-tubulin-positive nerve-fibre volume and mechanical sensitivity and fewer mitotic epithelial cells than vehicle-treated females, while lineage-labelled epithelial foci showed a qualitatively concordant distribution. Corneal transcriptional responses were substantially broader than those in the trigeminal ganglion. These findings show that adult testosterone exposure is associated with coordinated plasticity across several baseline ocular-surface phenotypes. They establish endocrine status as an important biological variable for experimental design while leaving its consequences for injury and disease to future functional studies.

Article.Authors: Rahman A.; Bhuiyan A.; Hossain M.; Uddin M.; Islam M.; Aziz I.; Alkubaisi N.; Giesy J.; Aboul-Soud M.; Haque S.
Article.Abstract: The growing burden of infectious and chronic diseases associated with bacterial infections and oxidative stress highlights the need for novel antibacterial and antioxidant agents. Fungal endophytes are promising sources of bioactive metabolites with pharmaceutical potential. This study focused on the isolation, characterization, and biological evaluation of endophytic fungus extract obtained from the leaves of Centella asiatica (L.) Urban. The isolated fungus was identified as Aspergillus fumigatus through ITS-rDNA sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. GC–MS profiling of its ethyl acetate extract (CAL 3) revealed 37 volatile compounds, including Pyrrolo[1,2-a]pyrazine-1,4-dione, hexahydro-3-(2-methylpropyl)-, 9-Octadecenamide, and 1-Nonadecene. The extract showed moderate antibacterial activity at 500 µg/disc, with inhibition zones of 15.75 ± 0.14 and 16.61 ± 0.19 mm against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli , respectively. MIC values were 5 mg/mL against E. coli and P. aeruginosa and 10 mg/mL against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis . The extract exhibited DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities, with IC₅₀ values of 44.56 ± 0.50 and 48.77 ± 0.22 µg/mL, respectively. Molecular docking indicated favorable binding of selected metabolites to DHFR and MPO. These findings support further investigation of C. asiatica -associated endophytic fungi as potential sources of bioactive metabolites for future drug discovery.

Article.Title: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention introduction is associated with sustained reductions in childhood malaria burden in northern Ghana
Article.Authors: Anafo A.; Gmayinaam V.; Aheto J.; Afrane Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five in northern Ghana. Transmission in this setting is intense and highly seasonal, with most cases occurring during the rainy season from June to September. Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC), the monthly administration of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine to children aged 3–59 months during peak transmission, was introduced across the Northern Region in June 2019. However, its population-level association with childhood malaria outcomes, after accounting for background trends and climatic variability, had not been comprehensively assessed. Here we combined 10 years of monthly health facility data from 2015 to 2024 with four rounds of nationally representative household survey data from 2014 to 2022. We assessed the association between SMC implementation and childhood malaria outcomes using seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average models with exogenous covariates, incorporating monthly rainfall and temperature, alongside a Bayesian structural time-series counterfactual framework. Compared with the projected counterfactual trajectory, malaria death rates, admission rates, and incidence rates in the post-SMC period were estimated to be 80.3%, 23.0%, and 16.1% lower, respectively. However, because of uncertainty around the counterfactual estimates, these results should be interpreted as suggestive of a possible programme-level contribution rather than definitive evidence of statistically confirmed effects. At the individual level, children surveyed in the post-SMC period had significantly lower odds of malaria infection after adjustment for survey month (adjusted odds ratio = 0.595; 95% confidence interval: 0.470–0.751), with consistently lower predicted malaria probabilities observed across all child age groups. Although insecticide-treated net coverage declined during the post-SMC period, malaria burden continued to decrease across both routine facility and household survey data sources. These findings are consistent with an association between SMC implementation and reduced malaria burden among children under five in a high-transmission Sahelian setting and highlight the importance of maintaining high SMC coverage as part of an integrated malaria control strategy.

Article.Title: Seasonal and annual variation in Borrelia garinii infectiousness in a wild bird
Article.Authors: Zarka J.; Heylen D.; Fonville M.; Matthysen E.; Sprong H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Successful reproduction of zoonotic diseases depends, among others, on the reservoir host’s ability to maintain and transmit the infection. Temporal variation in host infectiousness, i.e. the capacity of the host to infect susceptible individuals, and contact rates with naïve hosts strongly influence transmission dynamics. The vector-borne Borrelia garinii , causative agent of Lyme neuroborreliosis, is maintained in the environment through transmission between birds and Ixodes ricinus ticks. Although temporal variation in avian infectiousness affects B. garinii spread, it remains poorly understood in wild populations. Here, we assessed year-round variation in infectiousness of wild great tits ( Parus major ) using xenodiagnosis. Over seven consecutive seasons (from the 2022 until the 2024 breeding season), we conducted 420 xenodiagnoses. Our results showed a higher prevalence of infectious individuals during breeding seasons, particularly in 2023 (49% of birds were infectious). This peak was followed by a sharp decline in autumn and winter, which could suggest transient infectiousness. Few birds were repeatedly infectious, and most birds transmitted a single B. garinii haplotype, further indicating that most infections were transient. Our findings highlight the importance of accounting for species-specific temporal variation in host infectiousness, in addition to spatiotemporal host-vector overlap, when estimating avian contributions to Lyme neuroborreliosis transmission.

Article.Title: Mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles attenuate inflammation-associated cognitive impairment and hippocampal microglial-synaptic remodeling
Article.Authors: Ayyubova G.; Gasimov E.; Rzayev F.; Mehraliyeva G.; Sadigi I.; Guliyeva N.; Ismayilova S.; Ayyubova N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Microglia are central regulators of synaptic structure and cognitive function, yet under chronic inflammatory conditions, they can adopt stress-associated states associated with neuronal and synaptic vulnerability. Although inflammation-driven cognitive decline is often attributed to synapse loss, increasing evidence suggests that synaptic remodeling may precede or occur independently of overt synapse elimination. In this study, we combined behavioral testing, immunofluorescence, microglial morphometric analysis, and quantitative transmission electron microscopy to define structural correlates of inflammation-induced cognitive dysfunction and to evaluate the therapeutic potential of mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs). Chronic systemic inflammation was induced in mice by repeated lipopolysaccharide (LPS) administration, followed by intravenous MSC-EV treatment during the inflammatory phase. LPS exposure impaired working memory, object recognition, and spatial recognition memory without affecting locomotor activity. Immunofluorescence revealed increased CD68 immunoreactivity detected with the ED1 antibody clone within IBA1-positive cells, together with increased microglial soma area, reduced arborization area, and an elevated morphological index, consistent with microglial inflammatory remodeling and enhanced endolysosomal/phagolysosomal engagement. Ultrastructural analysis further demonstrated increased phagolysosomal inclusion burden, increased blood vessel-associated microglial profiles, elevated dark microglia-like profiles, reduced neuronal soma profile area, decreased SYN- and PSD95-positive structures, and coordinated pre- and postsynaptic alterations. Total excitatory synapse density showed only a non-significant numerical reduction, indicating synaptic vulnerability characterized primarily by structural remodeling rather than definitive synapse loss. MSC-EV treatment was associated with attenuated microglial inflammatory and morphometric alterations, reduced phagolysosomal and dark microglia-like ultrastructural features, partially restored synaptic marker-positive structures and synaptic ultrastructure, and improved hippocampus-dependent cognition, particularly spatial recognition memory. Together, these findings suggest that MSC-EVs are associated with partial normalization of inflammation-induced microglial, neuronal, and synaptic alterations.

Article.Title: Quantum-compatible error correction using a Bayesian Dual-Gated ProbSparse transformer in discrete-variable quantum key distribution
Article.Authors: Raoof S.; Tejasree G.; Satheesha T.; Chhetri Y.; Eduru S.; M. P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation with information-theoretic security guaranteed by the principles of quantum mechanics. However, achieving high reconciliation efficiency, high throughput, and low frame error rates under noisy channel conditions remains a significant challenge for practical and cost-effective Discrete-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (DV-QKD) systems. To address this issue, this research proposes a Quantum-based Bayesian Dual-Gated ProbSparse Transformer (Q-BDPT) framework for quantum-compatible error correction during the reconciliation stage of DV-QKD. Initially, a system model for DV-QKD is presented. Subsequently, an adaptive error-correction framework comprising Deep-Q-Encoder and Deep-Q-Decoder modules is developed. Unlike physical quantum error-correction codes that operate directly on qubits, the proposed framework processes measurement-derived error features, syndrome information, and channel-dependent error characteristics obtained after quantum-state transmission and measurement. The Deep-Q-Encoder and Deep-Q-Decoder are constructed using Q-BDPT with Binary Cross Entropy (BCE) loss. The proposed Q-BDPT integrates Bayesian Adversarial ProbSparse Transformer (BAPT) and Dual-Gated Spatiotemporal Attention Network (DSANet), while harmonic analysis is employed to enhance feature integration and adaptive error modelling. The framework learns probabilistic, spatial, and temporal error dependencies associated with quantum-channel behavior and generates adaptive reconciliation decisions to improve key recovery performance. Experimental results demonstrate that Q-BDPT achieves a minimum Bit Error Rate (BER) of 0.01760, a minimum Logical Error Rate (LER) of 0.00776, and a maximum Secure Key Rate (SKR) of 0.65805, thereby improving reconciliation effectiveness and secure key generation performance in DV-QKD environments.

Article.Title: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection is associated with a shift in the human secondary sex ratio at birth
Article.Authors: Ammar O.; Rimmer M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human sex ratios at birth are remarkably stable, yet may be sensitive to events during fertilisation and early embryo development. Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) bypasses sperm-zona interaction by injecting a selected sperm directly into the oocyte and is increasingly used beyond severe male-factor infertility. We analysed anonymised UK Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority registry data for 2005–2018 to test whether fertilisation method is associated with the secondary sex ratio among singleton live births. The cohort included 164,684 singleton live births after conventional IVF or ICSI with recorded infant sex. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for maternal age, treatment year, number of embryos transferred, and fresh or frozen embryo transfer. The adjusted proportion of male live births was 52.6% after IVF and 49.2% after ICSI, an absolute difference of 3.4 percentage points (95% CI 2.8–3.9); the adjusted odds ratio for male live birth after ICSI versus IVF was 0.88 (95% CI 0.86–0.89). The association was consistent across single-embryo transfers, fresh and frozen cycles, cycles without recorded male-factor infertility, and analyses excluding preimplantation genetic testing and donor-gamete cycles. These data identify a small association between fertilisation method and the proportion of male singleton live births within this ART cohort. They do not establish that ICSI causes a shift in the secondary sex ratio in the wider population and should not alter individual counselling, but support deeper study of sex-specific selection across fertilisation, embryo culture, transfer, and early survival.
