Article.Title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) in relation to metabolic profile and dietary antioxidant quality in adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
Article.Authors: El-Sehrawy A.; Salah A.; Kandil I.; Yusuf S.; Abohassan M.; Alanazi M.; Kurbaniyazova F.; Almansouri T.; Basunduwah T.; labib S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a common metabolic condition characterized by hepatic steatosis and chronic low-grade inflammation, with oxidative stress playing a pivotal role in its progression. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) has been proposed as an accessible marker reflecting systemic inflammatory status. This study aimed to examine the relationship between NLR, metabolic risk factors, body composition indices, and dietary antioxidant quality in adults with NAFLD. In this cross-sectional study, 257 adults with ultrasound-confirmed NAFLD were enrolled. Anthropometric parameters and body composition were measured using standardized procedures and bioelectrical impedance analysis. Fasting biochemical markers were assessed via enzymatic colorimetric methods. NLR was calculated from complete blood count data. Dietary intake was evaluated using a validated semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire, and the Dietary Antioxidant Quality Score (DAQS) was derived based on the adequacy of vitamins A, C, and E, selenium, and zinc intake. Comparisons across NLR tertiles were performed using one-way analysis of variance, followed by Tukey’s post hoc test, and multivariable multinomial logistic regression was used to assess associations. Participants in the highest NLR tertile had significantly higher FBS (93.33 ± 11.03 vs. 88.40 ± 9.65 mg/dL), TC (191.81 ± 38.78 vs. 169.58 ± 32.62 mg/dL), and LDL-cholesterol levels (115.26 ± 33.63 vs. 99.11 ± 28.57 mg/dL) compared with those in the lowest tertile (all P < 0.05). Higher NLR levels were significantly associated with lower DAQS values and reduced intake of antioxidant vitamins A and C (p < 0.05). In stratified multinomial logistic regression analyses by physical activity, higher NLR was associated with increased FBS in the low activity group (Third tertile: OR: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.03–1.13, P = 0.003) and with higher TC in the high activity group (second tertile: OR: 1.02, 95% CI: 1.00–1.04, P = 0.05; third tertile: OR:1.02, 95% CI: 1.005–1.04, P = 0.016). Elevated NLR is associated with an unfavorable metabolic profile and poorer dietary antioxidant quality among individuals with NAFLD. These findings support the potential role of NLR as a practical inflammatory marker linked to metabolic risk and highlight the relevance of antioxidant-rich dietary patterns in mitigating inflammation in NAFLD.

Article.Title: A cautionary tale on the cost-effectiveness of collaborative AI in real-world medical applications
Article.Authors: Cremonesi F.; Innocenti L.; Goh V.; Ourselin S.; Antonelli M.; Lorenzi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Federated learning (FL) has gained wide popularity as a collaborative learning paradigm allowing collaborative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in sensitive healthcare applications. Nevertheless, the practical implementation of FL presents technical and organizational challenges, as it generally requires complex communication infrastructures. In this context, consensus-based learning (CBL) may represent a promising alternative for collaborative learning, allowing the combination of local knowledge into a federated decision system, while potentially reducing deployment overhead. Nevertheless, a comprehensive assessment of the viability of consensus-based learning as a cost-effective and sustainable alternative to federated learning has not yet been conducted. In this work we propose an extensive benchmark of the accuracy, cost-effectiveness, and sustainability of a panel of FL and CBL methods in a wide range of collaborative medical data analysis scenarios. The benchmark includes 7 different medical datasets, encompassing 3 machine learning tasks, 8 different data modalities, and multi-centric settings involving 3 to 23 clients. Our results reveal that CBL is a cost-effective and more sustainable alternative to FL. When compared across the panel of medical datasets in the considered benchmark, CBL methods provide equivalent accuracy to the one achieved by FL. Nonetheless, CBL significantly reduces training time and communication cost (resp. 15 fold and 131 fold decrease) ( p -value< 0.05). This study opens a novel perspective on the deployment of collaborative AI in real-world applications, whereas the adoption of cost-effective methods is instrumental to achieve sustainability and democratization of AI by alleviating the need for extensive computational resources.

Article.Title: Text–relation joint modeling improves the robustness of Chinese social bot detection against paraphrasing attacks
Article.Authors: Guo S.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: Generative language models have made paraphrasing a low-cost and practical evasion strategy against social bot detectors, especially on Chinese platforms where textual content is a major detection signal. We introduce TRJD-AT, a text-relation joint framework that combines a Chinese MacBERT encoder, a two-layer heterogeneous graph attention network over user-post publication and user-user follow relations, a lightweight gated fusion module, and Fast Gradient Method (FGM) training on input embeddings. We further define a three-tier paraphrasing protocol - lexical substitution, sentence-level rewriting, and benign-token insertion - with explicit attack budgets and automatic semantic-preservation constraints, while separating post-level attack construction from account-level evaluation. On the Chinese Weibo Social Bot dataset, TRJD-AT obtains a clean macro-F1 of 0.891. Under the default Tier 2 condition (semantic-similarity threshold 0.80), it obtains a macro-F1 of 0.835, corresponding to a 5.6-percentage-point reduction, whereas the MacBERT + MLP text-only baseline obtains 0.733, corresponding to a 13.4-point reduction. Clean performance and adversarial degradation are reported as distinct quantities. Ablation results indicate that the observed robustness is mainly associated with relational modeling; FGM improves clean performance in this setting but does not provide an independent gain in attacked macro-F1. A density-based analysis further identifies reduced relational benefit for accounts with sparse interaction histories.

Article.Title: Ga-induced defect engineering and charge transport mechanisms in ZnO ceramic materials
Article.Authors: Chouiref L.; Benamara M.; Hammami I.; Moussa S.; Alzahrani A.; Valente M.; El Mir L.; Graça M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ga-doped ZnO (G3ZO) ceramics were successfully synthesized and their structural, electrical, dielectric, impedance, and relaxation properties were investigated to understand the effect of Ga incorporation on charge transport. X-ray diffraction confirmed the hexagonal wurtzite structure without detectable secondary phases. Williamson–Hall analysis showed a decrease in crystallite size from 51.7 nm for pure ZnO to 29.4 nm for G3ZO, while FE-SEM revealed agglomerated nanoparticles with an average particle size of about 38 nm. Electrical conductivity increased with frequency and temperature and followed Jonscher’s universal power law. The activation energy was 0.132 ± 0.007 eV, indicating thermally activated, defect-assisted charge transport. Impedance analysis showed a decrease in resistance with increasing temperature, while dielectric measurements revealed strong low-frequency dispersion associated with interfacial polarization. Electric modulus analysis indicated non-Debye relaxation behavior. Compared with pure ZnO, G3ZO exhibited improved electrical conductivity, dielectric response, and polarization, which can be related to Ga-related donor defects and increased charge-carrier concentration. These results demonstrate that Ga incorporation can effectively modify the structural and electrical properties of ZnO ceramics and may be useful for electronic and dielectric applications.

Article.Title: In silico design and immunogenic assessment of a strain-specific peptide in Brucella melitensis 16 M for DIVA diagnosis
Article.Authors: Procopio A.; Soggiu A.; Hussein H.; Bonizzi L.; Zecconi A.; Guzzi P.; Urbani A.; Roncada P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Brucella melitensis is a facultative intracellular pathogen that causes brucellosis in small ruminants and humans. Strain-specific molecular targets are needed to improve vaccination monitoring and epidemiological surveillance, particularly for DIVA strategies aimed at distinguishing naturally infected animals from Rev.1-vaccinated animals. Here, we performed a computational, hypothesis-generating characterization of the RD3-associated genomic interval 824,171 − 824,131 on chromosome II of the virulent reference strain Brucella melitensis 16 M. Comparative sequence analyses were conducted across a selected DIVA-oriented panel of 56 publicly available bacterial chromosomal/genomic sequence records, including Brucella melitensis biovar 3 strain Ether chromosome II (NZ_CP007761.1), and the 16 M/Rev.1 locus was further inspected using the NC_003318.1 and CP024716.1 chromosome II FASTA sequences. The 16 M interval contains a 39-nt ATG-initiated coding segment on the negative strand that translates into the 13-amino-acid peptide MDHRSSGRGYDEK, whereas the homologous Rev.1 locus lacks the corresponding 40-bp ATG-containing segment. IEDB Next-Generation tools prioritized three MHC class I candidates, HRSSGRGY, MDHRSSGRGY, and DHRSSGRGY, while cross-species mapping using bovine MHC alleles as exploratory proxies identified Ovar-N*14:01 as the closest ovine sequence comparator. VaxiJen and BepiPred analyses provided complementary antigenicity and linear-epitope support, and host-proteome similarity screening against Ovis aries and Capra hircus did not identify full-length host matches or exact 8-13-mer host-protein matches. These findings support MDHRSSGRGYDEK as a panel-level, 16 M/RD3-positive-context computational candidate for DIVA-oriented assay development, but not as a validated diagnostic marker. No experimental evidence is currently available for peptide expression, antigen processing, MHC presentation, antibody reactivity, ELISA performance, PCR/qPCR/ddPCR diagnostic accuracy, or biological absence of cross-reactivity; therefore, no diagnostic performance or broad field applicability is claimed here.

Article.Title: Effects of speed and lane on lateral offset of vehicles in desert expressway
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Zheng C.; Xu J.; Zhu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Desert expressways feature straight alignments, monotonous roadside environments and limited external disturbances, which lead to distinctive speed selection and lateral control behaviors of drivers. This study aims to explore the coupling mechanism between vehicle speed and lateral trajectory on desert expressways. Taking passenger cars on straight segments of desert expressways as the research objects, this study obtained high-precision vehicle trajectory data through unmanned aerial vehicle field measurement. The speed distribution and lateral offset rules under different speed intervals and lane positions were analyzed. Correlation analysis and regression analysis were adopted to quantify the independent influence of vehicle speed on lateral trajectory characteristics. A multi-dimensional evaluation system was further constructed to determine the optimal safe driving speed ranges for inner and outer lanes.Lane position presents a significant stratified constraint effect on vehicle speed, and obvious heterogeneity exists in trajectory offset features and driving risk levels, between inner and outer lanes. Vehicle speed shows an extremely weak positive correlation with lateral offset, indicating that speed is not the core factor affecting vehicle trajectory behavior on desert expressways.The comprehensive evaluation results demonstrate that the optimal safe speed range for the inner lane is 125–130 km/h, while that for the outer lane is 95–100 km/h. Significant lane-based differences in vehicle lateral trajectory and speed adaptation behavior exist on desert straight expressways. Speed variation has limited influence on trajectory stability, whereas lane location dominate driving safety performance. The defined sectional safe speed intervals can effectively support speed limit calibration, dynamic traffic safety control, and safety facility layout optimization for desert expressways in arid regions.

Article.Authors: Pellegrini F.; Casalino G.; Lombardi R.; Lanave G.; Diakoudi G.; Bugarim T.; Banyai K.; Camero M.; Di Martino B.; Camarda A.; Circella E.; Martella V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We identified hepadnaviruses in passerine birds. The virus was detected in four eggs from Gouldian finches ( Chloebia gouldiae ), in three feather quills, and in a liver sample from other ornamental birds. The full-length circular genome (~3 kb in length) of hepadnavirus strains detected in a Gouldian finch, a Society finch ( Lonchura striata domestica ) and a Long-tailed finch ( Poephila acuticauda ) was reconstructed. Hepadnavirus replicative circular DNA was detected in the egg and quill samples, suggesting the presence of cccDNA in these sites. The viruses were genetically distantly related to other avian hepadnaviruses and endogenous hepadnavirus elements, suggesting geographical or host-species restriction in passerine birds.

Article.Title: Time to death and predictors of in-hospital mortality among adults underwent emergency abdominal surgery at a tertiary hospital in Ethiopia: a retrospective follow-up study
Article.Authors: Bayleyegn N.; Kune G.; Birhanu A.; Sisay A.; Merga H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emergency abdominal surgery is burdened by significant mortality and morbidity rates. There is a short window between the time of presentation and the time of surgical intervention which causes an inherent risk of increased perioperative and postoperative morbidity and mortality. This study is aimed at determining the time to in-hospital mortality as well as its predictors in patient who underwent emergency abdominal surgery. Retrospective cohort study was conducted among adult patients who underwent surgery for emergency abdominal conditions from January 1, 2019 to December 30, 2023 at JUMC (Jimma University Medical Center). Three hundred records were selected by systematic random sampling technique. Data were collected using a structured data extraction checklist with Kobo Toolbox by trained data collectors at JUMC. The collected data were exported into STATA Version 17 for analysis. Bivariate Cox regression analysis was conducted to identify candidate variables at p-value < 0.25 for multivariable Cox regression model. Finally, in multivariable Cox-Regression analysis, the p-value < 0.05 and Adjusted Hazard Ratio (AHR) with 95% CI were used to judge statistical significance. 300 medical records of surgical patients with emergency abdominal surgical conditions who underwent surgery during the five-year study period at JUMC were reviewed. Out of the 300 patients, 37 had died in the hospital and the median time of death was 40 days. The overall incidence rate of death was 1.35 (95% CI: 0.98–1.86) per 100 person-days. Being male (AHR = 4.1, 95% CI 1.25–15.42), and older adults (AHR = 7.77, 95% CI 2.57–33.5) had an increased hazard of death. Patients’ American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (AHR = 2.81, 95% CI: 1.2–6.6), shock (AHR = 9.7, 95% CI: 1.8–39.9), surgical site infection (AHR = 0.43, 95% CI 0.23–0.79) and re-laparotomy (AHR = 2.18, 95% CI 1.35–13.6) were significant predictors of time to death. In-hospital mortality among adults undergoing emergency abdominal surgery remained high in our study. The condition of the patient at presentation and postoperative complications were significant predictors of in-hospital mortality. Devising special integrated efforts and guidelines for perioperative management of patients can improve survival outcome and decrease postoperative complications.

Article.Title: Seasonal variation in water quality and evaluation of optimal iron removal conditions in acid mine drainage at A mine, Japan
Article.Authors: Fuchida S.; Nakamura A.; Kato S.; Ito H.; Ohara Y.; Kawahara R.; Otake T.; Makita H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acid mine drainage (AMD) often contains high concentration of iron (Fe), which can exceed 100 mg/L, while speciation and precipitation are key factors controlling the removal efficiency of Fe and other elements. This study monitored seasonal variations in AMD quality at A mine, Japan (pH: 2.6–3.2, Total-Fe: 128–162 mg/L), and found the dominant dissolved Fe species shifted from ferrous ion (Fe(II) aq ) in summer to ferric ion (Fe(III) aq ) in winter. Neutralization experiments using simulated AMD containing either Fe(II) aq or Fe(III) aq revealed that initial Fe speciation had little effect on arsenic and copper removal efficiency at this site. Furthermore, the reaction experiments using natural AMD in the presence or absence of Fe precipitates (5 v/v%) revealed the Fe(II) aq oxidation rate was 3 × 10 5 and 8 × 10 5 times higher in the presence of Fe precipitates at pH 3.0 and 3.5, respectively. Fe(II) aq oxidation was reduced substantially when using autoclaved Fe precipitates, suggesting that Fe(II) aq oxidation might be enhanced by processes associated with Fe precipitates, including microbial activity, rather than by homogeneous chemical oxidation alone. Therefore, promoting interaction between AMD and Fe precipitates, together with slight pH adjustment, could be effective for Fe removal from AMD at A mine.

Article.Title: Potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in marine fish caught from the mediterranean sea at Damietta city, Egypt: perspective on cooking effects and health hazard assessment
Article.Authors: Yusuf S.; Mahros M.; Zaher H.; Sallam K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the concentrations of mercury (Hg), arsenic (As), lead (Pb), and cadmium (Cd) in 270 fish muscle samples comprising 90 each of flathead grey mullet ( Mugil cephalus ), gilthead bream ( Sparus aurata ), and brushtooth lizardfish ( Saurida undosquamis ) collected from the Mediterranean Sea at Damietta, Egypt. The impact of common household cooking methods (grilling and frying) on toxic metal levels and the associated human health risks was assessed in 90 fish samples comprising 30 from each fish species. Fish samples were subjected to wet digestion using a nitric-perchloric acid mixture and analyzed with the atomic absorption spectrophotometer for heavy metal determination. Mean ± SE concentrations (mg/kg wet weight) of Hg, As, Pb, and Cd were 0.05 ± 0.004, 11.69 ± 0.72, 0.895 ± 0.14, and 0.046 ± 0.005 in raw flathead grey mullet; 0.069 ± 0.005, 12.38 ± 0.45, 0.865 ± 0.13, and 0.062 ± 0.004 in raw gilthead bream; and 0.145 ± 0.011, 8.215 ± 0.50, 1.012 ± 0.13, and 0.087 ± 0.006 in raw brushtooth lizardfish, respectively. Arsenic concentrations exceeded permissible limits in all examined samples, while Pb and Cd surpassed regulatory limits in substantial proportions of the tested fish. In contrast, Hg levels remained below the recommended limit in all samples. Grilling and frying generally reduced toxic metal concentrations in the three fish species tested; however, grilling increased As levels in brushtooth lizardfish by 8.2%. Dietary exposure was evaluated by comparing estimated daily intake (EDI) with available health-based guidance values, whereas potential non-carcinogenic risk for Hg, Pb, and Cd was evaluated separately using USEPA reference-dose-based target hazard quotients (THQs). Health risk assessment revealed that estimated daily intakes of all analyzed metals were below their provisional tolerable daily intake values. Total arsenic concentrations exceeded the applicable maximum permissible level in all examined fish samples. However, arsenic-specific non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risk estimates were not derived because total arsenic was measured without determination of its inorganic fraction. The present findings demonstrate considerable contamination of fish from the study area, particularly with As, Pb, and Cd, and highlight the need for continuous monitoring, stricter environmental controls, and effective regulatory strategies to protect public health and ensure seafood safety.

Article.Title: Sustainable production of pure nanocrystalline cellulose (NCCs) as a binder for enhanced aspirin tablets: Valorization of palm kernel waste
Article.Authors: Alminderej F.; El-Sayed W.; Ragab T.
Article.Abstract: The search for new efficient drug-excipient from natural resources will be of interest in drug delivery research. The current study demonstrates the optimal valorization of palm kernel (PK) residue to create value-added materials for biomedical applications. Valorization of palm kernel (PK) residue by producing nanocrystalline cellulose (NCCs) as a binder in aspirin tablets was studied. Applying the factorial design (2 2 ) and investigating the effect of two independent variables with two levels involving binder type (Avicel and NCCs), and binder concentration (40% and 50% w/w). Powder blends containing NCCs (F1 and F2) exhibited superior flow properties compared to Avicel blends (F3 and F4). The physiochemical analysis of PK residues was studied and Characterization was investigated by FT-IR spectroscopic analysis, phase analysis by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscope (SEM) and TEM analysis. The Formulated tablets were evaluated via studying weight variation, hardness, friability, wetting test, dispersion times and water solubility. The powder blend was evaluated and the In-vitro dissolution was studied. Post-compression evaluation showed all tablets met USP standards for weight variation (< 2%) and demonstrated acceptable hardness and friability (< 0.75%), with NCCs tablets showing faster wetting, shorter dispersion times (21–48 s), and improved aspirin solubility due to the high surface area of nanocellulose. NCCs were non-cytotoxic to normal human epithelial cells (1-BJ1) and exhibited broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against Bacillus cereus , Bacillus subtilis , and Clostridium perfringens . Additionally, NCCs tablets showed prebiotic activity, particularly with L. casei . These findings highlight NCCs as a biocompatible, effective excipient for enhanced tablet performance and potential biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Temperature susceptibility and structural performance of CORMBB: A bio-based asphalt binder for the paving application
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Suman S.; Dwivedi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing demand for sustainable pavement materials has increased interest in bio-based alternatives to petroleum bitumen. This study develops castor oil- and rice husk ash-modified bio-bitumen (CORMBB) by partially replacing VG-30 and evaluates its physical, chemical, temperature-dependent, and rheological properties. Temperature susceptibility was assessed using penetration index (PI), penetration viscosity-number (PVN), viscosity-temperature susceptibility (VTS), and Arrhenius activation energy, while rutting performance was evaluated using the 2.2 kPa failure-temperature criterion. The colloidal index decreased from 0.33 for the base binder to 0.26 for CORMBB-2, suggesting a more stable colloidal composition. FTIR indices showed increased aliphatic and methylene contents and reduced carbonyl and sulfoxide indices after modification. PI decreased from − 1.26 for the base binder to − 1.64 and − 2.37 for CORMBB-1 and CORMBB-2, respectively, while PVN decreased from − 10.77 to − 12.30. Activation energy decreased markedly from 57.81 kJ/mol for the base binder to 43.77 and 42.67 kJ/mol for CORMBB-1 and CORMBB-2, indicating lower viscosity sensitivity to temperature. However, the RTFOT-aged rutting failure temperature declined from 94.7 °C for the base binder to 76.7 °C and 74.1 °C for CORMBB-1 and CORMBB-2, respectively. Overall, CORMBB showed improved thermo-viscous response but reduced high-temperature rutting resistance, highlighting a trade-off between temperature sensitivity and stiffness.

Article.Title: Intelligent hierarchical control for SI-SIDO buck converters
Article.Authors: Averneni V.; Gangula S.; Nizami T.; Chakravarty A.; Teli N.; Momin M.; Ahmad F.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This article describes a nonlinear control strategy for a single-inductor single-input dual-output (SI-SIDO) DC–DC buck converter. To competently regulate the multiple outputs while sharing a common inductor, a hierarchical control architecture is proposed, enabling coordinated control of the dual-output system. The proposed adaptive control framework ensures accurate voltage regulation at both output terminals while explicitly addressing the challenges of cross-regulation and cross-coupling effects inherent in SI-SIDO converters. By decoupling the control objectives across different hierarchical levels, the proposed approach enhances dynamic performance and improves steady-state voltage tracking under load and reference variations. Comprehensive simulation studies are carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed nonlinear hierarchical controller under various operating points. Furthermore, the simulation results are validated through extensive experimental implementation using the dSPACE DS1104 platform, demonstrating fast output tracking, superior regulation, robustness and practical feasibility of the proposed control scheme.

Article.Title: A conditional generative adversarial network with dual-context aggregation and color enhancement for digital mural creation
Article.Authors: Xiao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes an improved model based on generative adversarial networks to address the problems of unreasonable structural layout, color gradient distortion, and limited style controllability in digital mural generation. This model integrates the Dual Aggregation Context Module, Fast Fourier Convolutional Global Encode, Color Enhancement Polarized Self Attention Mechanism, and Pre trained Style Encoder, aiming to enhance the structural integrity, color authenticity, and style diversity of mural generation through multi-scale feature fusion, frequency-domain spatial domain joint modeling, and color space optimization. Experiments on Dunhuang murals and MetCollection datasets have shown that this method significantly outperforms mainstream generative models in objective evaluation metrics. The introduced evaluation of interaction efficiency and style consistency shows that this method can achieve higher consistency with the target style (CLIP similarity 0.891) with fewer interaction rounds (average 2.3 rounds) and faster response time (153 ms). In subjective evaluation, the average scores of generated images in terms of aesthetics, style consistency, and other dimensions are all higher than 4.3 points. The results indicate that the proposed method can effectively enhance the quality control of the structure, color, and style of digital murals, providing a reliable technical path for the digital restoration and creative generation of cultural heritage.
Article.Topic: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

Article.Title: Breaking the $$\:{\varvec{T}}_{\varvec{g}}$$ barrier in 4D printing: ultra-high temperature GF/TPI shape memory composite
Article.Authors: Kumar K.; Kumar S.; Doddamani M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Integrating 4D printing with high-performance thermoplastic polyimide (TPI) offers significant potential for developing adaptive/self-deployable structures for extreme environments. However, processing TPI through fused filament fabrication (FFF) remains challenging due to its elevated melt viscosity and high melting temperature. In this work, glass fiber (GF) reinforced TPI (GF/TPI) composites are developed for ultra-high-temperature 4D printing applications. Firstly, the GF/TPI composite is developed through melt-mixing, followed by filament preparation and 3D printing. Printed specimens are subsequently post-processed and systematically characterized for microstructural and shape-memory properties to evaluate their suitability for high-temperature 4D printing. Microstructural analysis confirmed uniform material deposition, strong fiber-matrix interfacial bonding, and good printing integrity, validating selected processing parameters. The 4D printed GF/TPI composite showed excellent shape-memory behavior, exhibiting a shape fixity ( $$\:{R}_{f}$$ ) of 93.33% and shape recovery ( $$\:{R}_{r}$$ ) of 98.70% in the first cycle, which further decreased to 91.62% and 90.19% in the tenth cycle. A reduction of 8% in the $$\:{R}_{r}$$ across the successive ten cycles is observed, indicating good cyclic stability of the shape memory effect (SME). The comparative study demonstrated superior shape-memory performance of the developed GF/TPI composite compared with existing high-temperature polymer systems under repeated cycles. The 4D-printed GF/TPI soft robotic gripper demonstrated excellent dimensional accuracy, surface finish, and stable actuation, confirming its suitability for deployable structures in space.

Article.Title: Design, modeling, and characterization of a low-pressure dual-mode pneumatic soft actuator-gripper
Article.Authors: Xu S.; Xiong Y.; Qu X.; Zhang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soft pneumatic grippers show immense promise in grasping fragile, irregular, and unknown objects; however, simultaneously achieving high payload capacity and grasping flexibility under low actuation pressure remains a critical challenge. In this paper, we propose a low-pressure dual-mode pneumatic soft gripper, which is constructed by rigidly coupling a cylindrical enveloping module and a three-finger soft pneumatic network (PneuNet) bending module. The cylindrical module achieves an active enveloping grasp for heavy loads through inward radial expansion, whereas the three-finger module flexibly accommodates objects of various shapes and sizes via bending deformation. To characterize the actuation behavior of the cylindrical module, its deforming architecture is modeled as a thin-walled curved chamber, and the deformation process is conceptualized into two sequential stages: inversion and bulging. By combining analytical formulations and finite element analysis (FEA), a two-stage inflation mechanics model is established, augmented by a semi-empirical correction to account for non-ideal boundary constraints and material softening effects. Furthermore, FEA is utilized to predict the bending deformation of the PneuNet fingers, exhibiting excellent agreement with experimental measurements. Experimental results demonstrate that under a low actuation pressure of merely 20 kPa, the dual-mode gripper can achieve an exceptional vertical payload of up to 6.5 kg when grasping a 36-mm-diameter sphere. Moreover, the two grasping modules can synergistically interact to manipulate and reorient a single complex target, or independently grasp two distinct objects simultaneously. Ultimately, the proposed low-pressure, dual-mode soft gripper demonstrates substantial potential for versatile, safe, and highly efficient robotic manipulation.

Article.Title: Magnetically supported Cobalt (II) Schiff base complex as a recoverable catalyst for the synthesis of Betti base compounds
Article.Authors: Moosavi-Zare A.; Darvishi Z.; Balali M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cobalt (II) Schiff base complex supported on cobalt ferrite magnetite nanoparticles was used as a heterogeneous and reusable catalyst for the preparation of 1 Betti base compounds by the reaction of 2-naphthol with different aldehydes and morpholine. Cobalt (II) complex by the rearrangement from tetrahedral to square planar structure, and then increasing the coordination number of cobalt can be accelerated and catalyze the synthesis of Betti base compounds.

Article.Title: Fault identification and localization in transmission lines using an IVY-optimized generalized additive model
Article.Authors: Qiao R.; Zhou W.; Dai W.; Wu T.; Liu F.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate fault-type identification and fault-distance estimation are essential for the reliable operation of transmission lines, yet their simultaneous realization remains challenging under nonlinear transient responses and limited labeled data. This study proposes an IVY-optimized generalized additive model (IVY-GAM) framework that combines physically guided feature construction, interpretable nonlinear modeling, and adaptive hyperparameter optimization. A 200 km two-terminal transmission-line model is established in MATLAB/Simulink to generate 385 fault samples covering 11 fault categories. Twelve features are constructed from phase-mode transformation, db4 wavelet decomposition, transient modulus maxima, three-phase voltage statistics, and double-ended wavefront-arrival indices. IVY is then used to optimize the key GAM parameters for fault identification and localization. Under a fixed train–validation–test partition, IVY-GAM achieves an identification accuracy of 99.987% and a localization $$R^2$$ of 0.99674, with an MAE of 3.16 km, an RMSE of 3.91 km, and a maximum error of 11.84 km. Stratified five-fold out-of-fold evaluation further yields an identification accuracy of 99.22% and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.992, while the localization task obtains a mean MAE of 7.08 km and a mean $$R^2$$ of 0.9520. Feature-group ablation, permutation importance, and GAM main-effect analyses show that three-phase voltage means primarily support fault-type discrimination, whereas double-ended arrival indices dominate distance estimation and modal maxima provide complementary information. The proposed framework therefore offers a balanced solution for accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient transmission-line fault diagnosis.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: fault location; generalized additive models; phase-mode transformation; model interpretability

Article.Title: SentiGraphRec: sentiment perception entity graph for personalized news recommendation
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Wang J.; Zhang Y.; Hang H.; Cao S.; Yang X.; Ibrahim N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the digital era, accurate news recommendation is essential for improving user engagement and supporting effective information delivery. Most existing methods mainly focus on semantic or structural signals, while largely overlooking users’ sentiment preferences toward entities in their reading histories. As a result, these approaches struggle to model dynamic sentiment patterns and fail to provide sufficiently personalized recommendations. To address this issue, we propose SentiGraphRec, a sentiment-aware entity graph model for personalized news recommendation. SentiGraphRec constructs a global entity graph that jointly encodes semantic relations, structural connections, and entity-level sentiment information. By explicitly modeling the interactions among users, news articles, and entities with sentiment orientations, the proposed framework captures both semantic relevance and affective preferences in a unified manner. Extensive experiments on public benchmark datasets demonstrate that SentiGraphRec consistently outperforms strong state-of-the-art baselines across multiple evaluation metrics. In particular, the model achieves notable improvements in recommendation accuracy and diversity. These results validate the effectiveness of sentiment-aware entity modeling and highlight the general applicability of SentiGraphRec for personalized news recommendation.

Article.Title: Research on multi-objective scheduling optimization of emergency resources based on simulated annealing algorithm
Article.Authors: Song Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Emergency departments face persistent challenges including prolonged patient wait times, unbalanced resource utilization, and high staff overtime. To address these issues, this study proposes a multi‑objective resource scheduling model based on real hospital data and optimizes it using a simulated annealing (SA) algorithm. The model discretizes time slots and integrates multiple resources (doctors, consultation rooms, beds), with objectives of minimizing weighted waiting time and labor cost under triage‑priority and maximum‑wait constraints. A neighborhood operation set (patient exchange, cross‑doctor reallocation, shift fine‑tuning) was designed to fit clinical workflows. Simulation on annual 2023 data from a tertiary hospital showed that, compared to the current system, the SA‑optimized schedules reduced average waiting time by 20–35%, lowered the overall threshold-violation rate by 46.8% (26.7 to 14.2%), and balanced resource utilization across weekday, peak‑day, and night‑shift scenarios. These gains were not cost-neutral: total daily labour cost rose by 11.4% (CNY 31,680 to 35,280) and cost per patient visit by 10.6% (CNY 102.3 to 113.1), while overtime hours fell by 29.7% and overtime cost by 30.2%. The SA-based framework converged reliably and retained its ordering across scenarios, and is best described as a candidate decision-support component that buys substantial improvements in timeliness, resource equity and staff workload at a quantified increase in labour expenditure. Although the framework was validated only in a simulation environment calibrated with one year of real ED data and has not yet undergone prospective real-world deployment, the results suggest that it constitutes a potentially deployable decision-support component for intelligent ED scheduling. All results derive from a single-centre in-silico evaluation calibrated on one tertiary emergency department; prospective and multi-centre validation is required before any claim of generalisability or operational readiness can be supported.

Article.Title: Multimodal customer intent recognition and profile dynamic update network based on temporal attention and gated fusion
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Lei G.; Guan J.; Pan Y.; Zheng W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate recognition of customer intent, together with the timely maintenance of user profiles, underpins a range of downstream applications including personalized recommendation, customer segmentation, targeted promotion, customer relationship management (CRM) and customer service quality assurance. Three practical limitations continue to constrain existing systems: multimodal fusion strategies remain insufficiently adaptive to per-sample modality reliability, temporal behavior models tend to collapse short-term intent shifts and long-term preference drift into a single flat sequence, and intent recognition pipelines are typically decoupled from downstream profile update mechanisms, so newly detected signals only propagate to profiles after a batch cycle. To address these gaps in a unified way, this paper proposes the Multimodal Customer Intent Recognition and Profile Dynamic Update Network (MCIP-DUN). The framework combines a pre-trained language backbone with a cross-modal gated fusion unit that reweights textual, behavioral and interaction-attribute streams per sample, a time-decay-aware temporal attention module that separates short-term tactical shifts from long-term preference evolution, and a gated recurrent profile update module in which the forget gate and update gate are decoupled so that stable dimensions and volatile dimensions can be governed independently. A joint training objective with homoscedastic uncertainty weighting balances the intent classification loss against a bounded-target profile reconstruction loss. On the Alibaba User Behavior Dataset (AUBD) and the Customer Service Dialog Intent Dataset (CSDID), MCIP-DUN reaches 89.46% accuracy and 87.77% macro-F1, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.59 and 3.25% points; the profile update pipeline achieves 88.39% tag accuracy with an end-to-end persistence lag of roughly 18 min — measured from event ingestion to database refresh, and clearly distinguished from the 14.1 ms model forward latency reported separately. Ablation studies isolate the individual contribution of each component. It should be noted that the evaluation is restricted to e-commerce and customer-service data; generalization to other verticals such as power-utility customer service is discussed as future work.

Article.Title: Gestational age and antenatal growth discordance are principal predictors of composite neonatal outcomes in very preterm twins
Article.Authors: Hašlík L.; Korček P.; Hanulíková P.; Krofta L.; Širc J.; Straňák Z.; Hanáček J.; Halaj M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Very preterm twin pregnancies show heterogeneous neonatal trajectories that are incompletely captured by infant-level survival alone. Pregnancy-level neonatal outcomes and their antenatal and perinatal determinants were evaluated in 434 dichorionic and monochorionic twin pregnancies managed at a national tertiary referral center between 2013 and 2024. The primary outcome was composite survival without major neonatal morbidity (C-SNM). Secondary outcomes were composite morbidity burden (CoMB; neither twin, one twin, or both twins affected), cumulative morbidity burden (CMB; the unweighted number of affected clinical domains across both infants), and dominant organ-system morbidity (DSM; organ system contributing most to morbidity). C-SNM was achieved in 222/434 pregnancies (51.2%). In multivariable analyses, gestational age at delivery and antenatal estimated fetal weight discordance ≥ 25% were the principal predictors of C-SNM. A significant interaction was observed ( P = .003): the odds of C-SNM increased by approximately 80% per additional week among pregnancies with discordance < 25% and by approximately 30% among pregnancies with discordance ≥ 25%. Lower gestational age and greater discordance were also associated with worse CoMB and higher CMB, whereas dichorionicity was associated with lower morbidity burden. For DSM, discordance was most strongly associated with respiratory morbidity. Pregnancy-level composite assessment may refine risk stratification and strengthen prenatal counseling.
Article.Topic: Assisted Reproductive Technology and Twin Pregnancy

Article.Title: Canagliflozin reduces the recovery of intracellular uropathogenic Escherichia coli from uroepithelial cells and affects α-hemolysin function
Article.Authors: Hilger A.; Adick A.; Putze J.; von Vietinghoff S.; Dobrindt U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract SGLT2 inhibitors, used for diabetes treatment, have been discussed with an increased urinary tract infection (UTI) risk due to increased glucose excretion in urine. Beyond their primary function, these drugs exhibit diverse off-target effects. We investigated whether canagliflozin and other SGLT2 inhibitors impact the interaction between the host and uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), as well as UPEC pathogenicity. In vitro cultures of uroepithelial cell lines were infected with UPEC strains CI5 and CFT073. Effects of different SGLT2 inhibitors were assessed by measuring the intracellular bacterial burden, glucose uptake and ATP levels of host cells, and the hemolytic activity of the toxin α-hemolysin. Canagliflozin showed the most pronounced and consistent reduction in intracellular UPEC recovery, while ipragliflozin showed a weaker effect. We observed the same effect of canagliflozin for the intracellular recovery of Salmonella Typhimurium strain LT2 from uroepithelial cells, an invasive pathogen that employs different invasion mechanisms than UPEC. The effect of canagliflozin on the recovery of intracellular UPEC and Salmonella was cell type-dependent and was observed in uroepithelial cell lines and macrophage-like THP-1 cells, but not in human colorectal adenocarcinoma-derived Caco-2 cells. Additionally, several SGLT2 inhibitors interfered with hemolysis. Taken together, canagliflozin demonstrated activity against UPEC regarding intracellular bacterial numbers and hemolytic activity in vitro, suggesting novel avenues for UTI treatment. Targeting the pore-forming toxin α-hemolysin and reducing the number of intracellular UPEC may offer a potential complementary strategy to antibiosis in combating recurrent UTI.

Article.Title: Somatic symptoms in cisgender men, transgender men, and gender-diverse individuals assigned male at birth: a Swiss Nationwide Study
Article.Authors: Lieb M.; Jedamzik J.; Laskowski N.; Müller R.; Paslakis G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Somatic symptoms are highly prevalent and constitute a major public health concern. Sociodemographic factors associated with these symptoms, particularly among cisgender men, transgender men, and gender-diverse individuals, remain insufficiently explored in Switzerland. We analyzed data from the Swiss Health Survey 2022, a nationally representative cross-sectional study. The sample included cisgender men, transgender men (i.e., assigned female at birth and identifying as men), and gender-diverse assigned male at birth (AMAB) individuals (i.e., assigned male at birth and currently identifying as nonbinary or another gender). Somatic symptom load was assessed by combining common somatic complaints including gastrointestinal issues, pain, palpitations, and weakness and subsequently dichotomized into lower vs. severe symptom burden. Sleep problems were measured by difficulties falling asleep, restless sleep, repeated awakenings, and early-morning awakening and categorized into no/few vs. moderate/severe sleep problems for subsequent analyses. Energy and vitality were assessed using the Short Form 36 Health Survey (SF-36) Vitality (VT) subscale, capturing fatigue, tiredness, and overall vitality over the past four weeks and were analyzed as a continuous outcome. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics©. Two binary logistic regression analyses were conducted for symptom load and sleep problems, respectively, and one linear regression analysis was performed for vitality as a continuous outcome. To account for the complex survey design, all analyses incorporated survey weights and canton as the stratification variable using design-based (complex samples) procedures. The analytical sample comprised 8,699 individuals (unweighted), representing an estimated population of 3,505,801 after applying survey weights. Compared with cisgender men, gender-diverse AMAB individuals showed higher odds of severe somatic symptom load (OR = 7.82, 95% CI [2.50; 24.45]), whereas transgender men did not differ significantly on this outcome (OR = 1.22, 95% CI [0.39; 3.76]). Both groups showed higher odds of sleep problems (transgender men: OR = 4.66, 95% CI [1.64; 13.25]; gender-diverse AMAB individuals: OR = 3.87, 95% CI [1.21; 12.30]) and lower vitality scores (B=-13.70, 95% CI [-20.04; -7.35]; B=-14.70, 95% CI [-25.93; -3.47], respectively). These estimates rest on small unweighted subgroups (35 transgender men, 16 gender-diverse AMAB individuals), are correspondingly imprecise, and should be read as exploratory. Additional factors associated with poorer outcomes included non-heterosexual orientation, nonemployable status, migration background, and residence in French- or Italian-speaking regions. Older age (65 + years) was associated with lower odds of severe somatic symptom load (OR = 0.71, 95% CI [0.53; 0.96]) but higher odds of sleep problems (OR = 1.35, 95% CI [1.08; 1.70]) and higher vitality scores (B = 8.89, 95% CI [6.83; 10.95]). Factors associated with somatic symptom load, sleep problems, and vitality showed both shared and outcome-specific patterns. Gender identity was associated with poorer sleep and lower vitality in transgender men and gender-diverse AMAB individuals compared with cisgender men, whereas higher somatic symptom load was found only in gender-diverse AMAB individuals. Given the small unweighted subgroup sizes and the resulting imprecision of the estimates, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. These preliminary findings highlight the importance of differentiating gender identities and adopting a gender-sensitive perspective in research and healthcare to better identify vulnerable groups and inform targeted interventions.

Article.Title: Multi-trait selection using the MGIDI for simultaneously improving rapeseed performance and energy-eco efficiency in dryland farming
Article.Authors: Khoshhal-Zolpirani F.; Majidian M.; Banaeian N.; Sabouri A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Attaining sustainability in agroecosystems requires balancing trade-offs between maximizing yield, optimizing energy efficiency, and minimizing environmental footprints. Yet, determining the optimal configuration of tillage and fertilisation regimes to satisfy these multifaceted goals under dryland farming conditions remains a complex agronomic challenge. This two-year field experiment aimed to identify the most efficient integrated management strategy for winter rapeseed ( Brassica napus L.) using a split-plot design comprising three tillage intensities and ten integrated fertilisation protocols. For the first time in rapeseed agronomic assessment, the Multi-trait Genotype-Ideotype Distance Index (MGIDI) was deployed to rank treatments based on 23 morphological, yield-related, quality, and environmental traits. Factor analysis reduced data dimensionality into two principal factors (agronomic and yield components: 63.19% and sustainability and energy indices: 28.25%) which collectively accounted for over 91% of the total variance. The MGIDI analysis identified conventional tillage combined with farmyard manure as the treatment closest to the ideotype. Analysis of Selection Differentials (SD) revealed that this strategy yielded substantial gains over the grand mean, including increases in oil performance (+ 26.09%), net energy (+ 31.13%), seed yield (+ 16.76%), and energy use efficiency (+ 71.62%). Concurrently, marked reductions were observed in specific energy (-51.73%) and, most notably, total CO 2 equivalent emissions (-98.94%). These findings demonstrate the robustness of the MGIDI as a multi-criteria decision-making tool in cropping systems, highlighting conventional tillage supplemented with farmyard manure as the superior strategy for maximizing productivity and eco-efficiency in dryland farming rapeseed.

Article.Title: Fabrication of three-dimensional MXene-MWCNT composite for the swift removal of cationic BB3 Dye from aqueous solution
Article.Authors: Goswami M.; Srivastava A.; Kumar B.; Sar P.; Jangde D.; Tiwari K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The contamination of aquatic ecosystems with synthetic dyes is a considerable environmental concern due to their detrimental properties and persistence. Basic blue 3 (BB3), an aromatic dye, poses significant hazards owing to its cancer-causing properties, hence requiring efficient removal techniques. Investigating versatile materials that effectively remove contaminants from wastewater is of paramount significance for ecological restoration. This study developed an MXene-Multi-walled carbon nanotube (MXene-MWCNT) composite adsorbent for the removal of BB3 dye from aqueous solutions. Multi-layered MXene was produced via the etching of the Ti 3 SiC 2 MAX phase employing HF–H 2 O 2 , followed by the preparation of the MXene-MWCNT composite via a solvothermal approach. The synthesized composite was analyzed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET), Raman, and infrared (IR) spectroscopic techniques, suggesting the effective incorporation of MWCNT with MXene nanosheets. BET studies revealed that MXene-MWCNT maintained a mesoporous structure (39.46 Å) with a specific surface area (SSA) of 15.37 m 2 g − 1 . The adsorbent exhibited swift and effective BB3 elimination, attaining 99% removal within 27 min and showcasing an adsorption capacity of 217 mg g − 1 . Adsorption kinetics adhered to a pseudo-second-order model. Adsorption isotherm analysis demonstrated a strong correlation with the Langmuir model (R 2 = 0.9996), implying the occurrence of monolayer adsorption. Thermodynamic analysis indicates that the adsorption process is spontaneous and endothermic in nature. Electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, and π–π stacking govern the mechanisms of adsorption between BB3 molecules and the functional groups of MXene-MWCNT. The composite demonstrated a removal efficacy over 90% after five rejuvenation cycles, affirming its notable reusability. These findings indicate that the MXene-MWCNT nanocomposite shows potential for BB3 removal from aqueous solutions.

Article.Title: An uncertainty and interaction-aware framework for sustainable additive manufacturing decisions in electric vehicle applications
Article.Authors: Momena A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Expert-based sustainability assessment of additive manufacturing (AM) for electric-vehicle (EV) components frequently relies on crisp ratings due to elicitation simplicity and auditability. However, crisp evaluations conceal three critical uncertainty sources: inter-expert disagreement, heterogeneous assessor reliability, and criterion-dependent ambiguity. This paper proposes an aggregation-centered decision framework that (i) adaptively transfers crisp evaluations into trapezoidal fuzzy numbers using a Takagi–Sugeno (TS) uncertainty inference mechanism driven by dispersion, reliability, and criterion volatility; (ii) performs interaction-aware robust aggregation through a consensus-based capacity, Shapley-effective weights, and power-support adjustment to mitigate unsupported or weakly aligned opinions; and (iii) completes the decision using value–ambiguity ranking with an explicit ambiguity-aversion parameter. A full EV bracket manufacturing-route case study demonstrates deterministic matrix construction, uncertainty propagation, interaction-aware aggregation, comparative prioritized (TrIFPWA) and Einstein-induced baselines, module-ablation analysis, controlled expert-conflict stress testing, and extensive sensitivity and uncertainty analyses. Results show that the ranking favors the polymer-composite route, and the preferred alternative remains stable across the tested ranges of ambiguity aversion, interaction strength, robustness parameters, uncertainty scaling, reliability perturbation, module-ablation variants, and progressively stronger expert conflict. Under maximum controlled conflict, the full model attenuates the conflicting expert more strongly and preserves a larger top-second score gap than additive aggregation. The proposed workflow enhances interpretability, robustness, and traceability in sustainability-driven manufacturing decision making.

Article.Title: Droplet-scale combustion memory analysis of hydrogen-enriched date palm pollen biodiesel using a novel ant colony optimization algorithm with Lévy flight
Article.Authors: Khan O.; Alnamasi K.; Yahya Z.; Yadav A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The implementation of biodiesel in diesel engines is limited by high viscosity, lower heating value, poor atomization, incomplete combustion, and increased fuel consumption. Hydrogen enrichment ca. overcome these limitations by improving flame propagation, premixed combustion intensity, and burning stability; however, the simultaneous variation of hydrogen supply and injection timing creates nonlinear ignition-delay, heat-release, pressure-rise, and emission interactions that are difficult to optimize using conventional methods. This study novelly investigates date palm pollen biodiesel under hydrogen-enriched diesel engine operation, integrating droplet-scale combustion memory with engine-level performance, combustion, emission, and acoustic analysis. A 64-run full-factorial design was developed using engine load, injection timing, and hydrogen flow rate as input factors. Pearson correlation was used to establish combustion-memory relationships among outcomes, while entropy priority weighting assigned the highest importance to BTE (22%), BSFC (18%), and NOx (18%), followed by peak pressure (12%), CO (10%), HRR (10%), vibration (6%), and sound pressure level (4%). Conventional ACO converged within 20 iterations, stabilizing near a fitness value of 0.80 in 12.8 s. Incorporating Lévy flight improved global exploration and avoided local pheromone stagnation, achieving a higher fitness value of 0.94 within 9 iterations in 6.3 s with only two inflection points. The optimum condition is dataset 59/Path-1, corresponding to 100% load, 4 LPM hydrogen flow, and 23° bTDC injection timing, producing BTE 38.7%, BSFC 0.21 kg/kWh, peak pressure 98 bar, HRR 82 J/deg, vibration 3.6 mm/s, and sound 93 dB. The results establish date palm pollen biodiesel as a feasible hydrogen-assisted biodiesel candidate and demonstrate that ACO–Lévy optimization effectively resolves coupled hydrogen–injection timing combustion complexity.

Article.Title: Noise scheduling and out-of-distribution generalisation in deep reinforcement learning for 6-DOF robotic grasping
Article.Authors: Mizhimakoski I.; Zlatinov S.; Gjoreski H.; Nadzinski G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exploration strategy is a fundamental but underexplored design choice in deep reinforcement learning for robotic manipulation. This paper presents a controlled empirical comparison of three off-policy configurations on a 6-DOF robotic grasping task using a Universal Robots UR5e in the RoboSuite simulation environment: Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) with automatic entropy tuning, Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) with piecewise linear noise decay, and TD3 with constant Gaussian noise. All configurations share identical network architectures, reward functions, and training budgets. The two TD3 variants differ only in the action-noise schedule and form the controlled comparison of the study, while SAC serves as a widely used entropy-regularised reference. Each configuration is trained over 10,000 episodes across five independent runs and evaluated over 1,000 deterministic episodes both within and beyond the training distribution. SAC achieves the highest in-distribution success rate (89.6%) and training efficiency, with a large effect size over both TD3 variants ( $$d = 1.32$$ and $$d = 1.47$$ ) and complete rank separation in area under the learning curve. Within the training distribution, the two TD3 variants are statistically indistinguishable ( $$d = 0.04$$ ). Under out-of-distribution evaluation, however, this contrast changes sharply: the noise-decay variant reaches a mean success rate of 43.1% against 32.3% for constant noise — an effect size of $$d = 1.08$$ , where the same comparison within the training distribution is negligible — together with the lowest cross-run variance of the three configurations and a more uniform distribution of success across the workspace. No pairwise difference reaches significance at five runs per configuration, and the comparisons are interpreted through effect sizes and confidence intervals. These results indicate that noise schedule design has a measurably different effect on in-distribution performance and spatial out-of-distribution generalisation, and that standard single-metric evaluation protocols may fail to capture meaningful differences between exploration strategies.

Article.Title: Association of a structured nutrition-centred multidisciplinary supportive-care program with treatment tolerance and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing precision radiotherapy for head and neck cancer: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Su N.; Huo Z.; Zhang Z.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Malnutrition, systemic inflammation, and treatment-related toxicity may compromise radiotherapy tolerance in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated a structured nutrition-centred multidisciplinary supportive-care program during precision radiotherapy. This prospective cohort included 258 patients with HNSCC receiving intensity-modulated or volumetric-modulated arc radiotherapy. Patients entered the comprehensive nutritional management (CNM) group ( n = 129) or usual care (UC) group ( n = 129) according to program availability. Outcomes included radiotherapy interruption, Grade ≥ 3 oral mucositis, treatment delay, longitudinal nutritional and inflammatory markers, quality of life, and exploratory survival outcomes. Linear mixed-effects, parsimonious logistic, and Cox regression models were used. Radiotherapy completion without major interruption was 95.3% in the CNM group and 89.1% in the UC group ( P = 0.063). Grade ≥ 3 oral mucositis was less frequent with CNM (14.0% vs. 26.4%; P = 0.013), as was Grade ≥ 2 dysphagia (17.1% vs. 28.7%; P = 0.026). Treatment delay was shorter with CNM [2 (IQR 1–3) vs. 5 (IQR 3–7) days; P = 0.018]. CNM was associated with more favorable longitudinal trajectories of PNI, SII, global health status, and swallowing symptoms (all interaction P ≤ 0.020). Adjusted analyses showed lower odds of severe mucositis (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.27–0.92), while the association with major interruption was not statistically significant (OR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.17–1.05). A structured nutrition-centred multidisciplinary supportive-care program was associated with lower treatment-related toxicity, shorter delays, and more favorable nutritional, inflammatory, and quality-of-life trajectories during radiotherapy.

Article.Title: Heavy metal bioaccumulation potential of indigenous rhizospheric soil fungi with comparative assessment of lead and cadmium resistance
Article.Authors: Amin I.; Nazir R.; Rather M.; Hamid B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fungi are highly suitable for use in bioremediation processes because of their high degree of metal tolerance. The present investigation focused on comparing the tolerance levels of the two most toxic metals, such as lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd), and the bioaccumulation capacities of certain unexplored fungi isolated from rhizospheric agricultural soils. Twenty-one (21) fungal strains were isolated, observed for their morphological features and then identified via molecular approach using ITS rDNA regions for Sanger sequencing (ITS1 and ITS4). The tolerance of the fungal isolates to Cd and Pb was assessed by examining their growth response to increasing concentrations of Cd and Pb in the form of cadmium chloride (CdCl₂·H₂O) and lead nitrate [Pb (NO₃)₂], respectively. The majority of the isolates showed tolerance to both Pb and Cd, as indicated by visual observation of growth on solid media. Species-specific differences in metallic tolerance were determined by minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and tolerance index (TI) assays, with Penicillium atramentosum (IA47) having the highest resistance to Cd, with MIC of 500 ppm. Against Pb, both Aspergillus calidoustus (IA40) and Penicillium atramentosum (IA47) , showed highest MIC of 400 ppm. The isolates demonstrating the best resistance and growth rates were further investigated for their ability to uptake metals. For that purpose, the fungal biomass was asceptically spiked with 50 and 100 ppm cadmium chloride (CdCl₂·H₂O) and lead nitrate [Pb (NO₃)₂]. The concentration of accumulated metals in the digested biomass was quantified through atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS). It was found that Phoma herbarum (IA52) had the greatest ability to bioaccumulate Cd (3.693 mg/g) at a 100 ppm concentration. The isolates showed a greater ability to uptake Cd than Pb because Pb tends to be less soluble than Cd and is therefore less readily available for fungal cells. These findings provide valuable insights into the selection of native fungal strains for eco-friendly and sustainable bioremediation of heavy metal contaminated environments and support their potential application in future environmental remediation strategies.

Article.Title: Moored observations of the deep western boundary current east of the Gagua Ridge in the Northwestern Pacific
Article.Authors: Xun H.; Zhou C.; Xiao X.; Zou T.; Qu T.; Zhang Z.; Guan S.; Huang X.; Zhao W.; Tian J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The deep western boundary current (DWBC) of the Pacific serves as a lower limb of the meridional overturning circulation that has been identified as a key component of the global climate system. Here, we report the results of observations from a set of full-depth subsurface moorings deployed in the Northwestern Pacific from August 2017 to May 2020. The observations reveal a southward, bottom-intensified DWBC east of the Gagua Ridge, featuring a core velocity of 4.5 cm/s and a mean southward volume transport of 1.79 ± 0.75 Sv (1 Sv = 10 6 m 3 /s). Seasonally, this DWBC shows a tendency to move southward with relatively cold water in summer and northward with warm water in winter. On intraseasonal time scales, its variability is closely related to surface-detectable mesoscale eddies, suggesting that some of these eddies are deep ocean reaching and can directly modulate the bottom current as deep as ~ 5500 m east of the Gagua Ridge. These results enhance our understanding of the deep circulation and pathway of deep water in the Pacific.

Article.Title: Emotionally intelligent preference optimization for conversational behavior change support
Article.Authors: Chen B.; Dethlefs N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Procrastination negatively affects productivity and well-being, yet current large language models (LLMs) often lack the nuanced emotional understanding necessary for effective behavior-change support. This study proposes emotionally intelligent preference optimization (EIPO), a unified framework integrating emotional chain-of-thought reasoning, teacher-guided self-correction, and direct preference optimization to enhance emotional intelligence in conversational user interfaces. Through ablation experiments evaluated using the emotional generation score (EGS), we demonstrate that EIPO significantly improves empathetic and constructive responses in procrastination-related interactions. Crucially, cross-model validation on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Gemma-2-2B confirms EIPO’s model-agnostic design, with consistent EGS gains ( $$\Delta = +0.13$$ to $$+0.27$$ ) and robust independent evaluation using Claude-3.5-Sonnet. These findings establish EIPO as a principled, transferable framework for embedding emotionally intelligent behavior-change support into diverse LLM-driven CUIs.

Article.Title: Bone-adapted oral squamous cell carcinoma cells show adaptive responses to the osseous microenvironment in a murine tumor transplantation model
Article.Authors: Vohl N.; Herrmann A.; Ooms M.; Müller-Diesing F.; Heitzer M.; Schaffrath K.; Apel C.; Hölzle F.; Modabber A.; Winnand P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bone invasion is a decisive step in the progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and is associated with increased tumor aggressiveness, worsening the prognosis. Under the selection pressure of the bone microenvironment, a fundamental biological divergence arises. Bone-adapted cells represent not only a variant but also a distinct subpopulation with stable pro-invasive properties. To model tumor biological selection through the bone microenvironment, the murine OSCC cell line SCC-7 was injected under the periosteum of immunocompetent C3H mice and cultured in situ for a period of 25 days. A cell population was then isolated from the induced bone-invasive tumor and established in vitro. The selected cells were systematically characterized. Migration and invasion behavior, cellular morphology, size, and metabolism were examined using standardized functional and metabolic analysis methods. Compared with the parental tumor cell line, bone-selected SCC-7 cells showed significantly increased migration and invasion activity as well as clear morphological differences. A constant change in the metabolic profile was detected. Phenotypic alterations indicated adaptive reprogramming as a result of exposure to the bone microenvironment, which selects for a distinct, stably altered tumor cell population. Thus, bone-infiltrating OSCC cells fundamentally differ phenotypically and metabolically from non-bone-invasive tumor cells.

Article.Title: Staphylococcus aureus in bovine mastitis in northwestern Iran: patterns of antimicrobial and multidrug resistance, biofilm formation, and virulence/resistance gene carriage
Article.Authors: Hosseini R.; Aram M.; Nofouzi K.; Asadpour R.; Ghorani M.; Ateba C.; Enferadi A.; Sadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ), a major cause of bovine mastitis, represents a significant challenge for the dairy industry due to its economic and zoonotic importance. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of major virulence-associated genes (lukE, seA, sei), the methicillin-resistance gene (mecA), antimicrobial susceptibility, and biofilm formation in S. aureus isolates obtained from cases of bovine clinical mastitis in dairy farms of East and West Azerbaijan provinces, Iran. A total of 138 milk samples were collected from East Azerbaijan (67; 48.6%) and West Azerbaijan (71; 51.4%) provinces. S. aureus isolates were identified by culture, biochemical tests, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the nuc gene for confirmation. Target genes were detected using conventional PCR. Antimicrobial susceptibility was evaluated by the disk diffusion method, and biofilm formation was assessed using the crystal violet microtiter plate assay. Of the 138 samples, 42.0% were positive for S. aureus . The prevalence of lukE, seA, sei, and mecA genes was 39.7%, 36.2%, 17.2%, and 6.9%, respectively. Resistance was highest to penicillin (94.8%) and lowest to gentamicin (22.4%). Overall, 39 isolates (67.2%) were classified as multidrug-resistant (MDR), of which 25.8% were resistant to four or five of the six antimicrobial classes tested and 10.3% were resistant to all six tested antimicrobial classes, with a mean multiple antibiotic resistance (MAR) index of 0.53 ± 0.23. Resistance profiles did not differ significantly between provinces, whereas biofilm formation showed a significant interprovincial difference ( P = 0.002), with a moderate degree of herd-level clustering (ICC = 0.158). These results indicate a high isolation proportion of S. aureus with substantial multidrug resistance and regional variation in biofilm-forming capacity, emphasizing the necessity of targeted antimicrobial stewardship and improved surveillance.

Article.Title: Thymol as a potential botanical insecticide against Tuta absoluta: life history parameters, toxicity and enzymatic responses
Article.Authors: Rostami E.; Afrazeh Z.; Nemati A.; Jalali Sendi J.; Zhao Q.; Zhang Y.; Li L.; Lin K.; Gao S.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the insecticidal potential of thymol against the pest Tuta absoluta (Meyrick) (Lepidoptera: Gelechiidae), its effects on key physiological enzyme activities, and investigated the duration of the insect's developmental stages. Initially, the study's complete objectives and conducted experiments were detailed, including toxicity assessment via topical bioassays and the estimation of lethal doses (LD 50 ) using probit analysis. Thymol exhibited high toxicity, with a 24-h LD 50 calculated at 6.866 µg/larva. The larval development period and adult longevity were significantly reduced at LD 30 and LD 50 compared to the control, and the oviposition rate also decreased. Biochemical assays revealed substantial alterations in the activities of detoxification and antioxidant enzymes. Antioxidant enzyme activities were elevated. In contrast, detoxification enzymes, including glutathione S-transferase, α- and β-esterases, and cytochrome P450 monooxygenases, were significantly and dose-dependently decreased, as was acetylcholinesterase. Thymol was also observed to reduce sodium–potassium adenosine triphosphatase (Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase) activity. The results indicate that thymol induces toxicity through multiple physiological pathways, including disruption of detoxification systems and ionic homeostasis. These findings introduce thymol as a promising candidate for a botanical insecticide in managing the T. absoluta .

Article.Title: Differences in competitive adsorption mechanisms of CH4 and CO2 in mylonitic and primary structure coal
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Chen X.; Li J.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tectonically deformed coal exhibits significantly different gas adsorption-desorption characteristics from primary structure coal due to intense coal mass deformation, making it a research hotspot in coalbed methane development and gas disaster prevention and control. To explore the differences in the competitive adsorption mechanisms of CH 4 and CO 2 between mylonitic coal and primary structure coal, this study took No. 8 coal from the Zhuxianzhuang Mining Area as the research object. Based on experimental results, molecular models of mylonitic coal (C 214 H 159 N 3 O 20 ) and primary structure coal (C 208 H 152 N 2 O 18) were constructed respectively. Isothermal adsorption simulations of single-component and mixed gases of CH 4 andCO 2 at different ratios were carried out using molecular dynamics methods. The results show that the adsorption of CH 4 and CO 2 in both types of coal belongs to physical adsorption, with stronger adsorption capacity under low temperature and high pressure. Under the same conditions, the adsorption capacity and adsorption heat of CO 2 are higher than those of CH 4 , and the adsorption advantage of CO 2 in mylonitic coal is more prominent. This is closely related to the more complete aromatic ring conjugated π-electron system, abundant oxygen-containing functional groups and a higher proportion of ultramicropores in mylonitic coal. With strong polarity and small kinetic diameter, CO 2 molecules are more prone to interact with π-electrons and produce the “pore-filling effect”. In mixed gas adsorption, the total adsorption capacity and interaction energy of both coal types increase with the rise of CO 2 molar fraction. Although the adsorption selectivity coefficient of CO 2 to CH 4 decreases, it is always greater than 1, and the selectivity coefficient of mylonitic coal is higher. The energy distribution curve of CO 2 shifts to adsorption sites with low interaction energy, while that of CH 4 shows the opposite trend, and the shift amplitude of gas molecular curves in mylonitic coal is larger. In addition, the interaction energy of mylonitic coal is dominated by van der Waals force, accounting for a higher proportion than that of primary structure coal. Its CH 4 adsorption heat also has a larger fluctuation range, reflecting a stronger competitive adsorption capacity for CO 2 . The research findings provide a theoretical basis for mine gas prevention and control and efficient coalbed methane development.

Article.Title: Differentiating acute from chronic pulmonary thromboembolism: a preliminary study using dual-layer CT
Article.Authors: Bae K.; Cho M.; Jeon K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to evaluate the actual values and ranges of conventional and spectral parameters in pulmonary thromboembolism (PE) and assess their potential for distinguishing acute PE (APE) from chronic PE (CPE) using dual-layer CT (DLCT). This retrospective study included 52 patients with central PE diagnosed with CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) using DLCT. Patients were categorized into APE and CPE groups. Conventional and spectral parameters including Hounsfield unit (HU) and electron density (ED) values were measured at the thrombus and pulmonary trunk on both pre- and post-contrast images. Additionally, in vitro experiments were conducted to generate clots of varying compositions. Apart from D-dimer levels, no significant clinical differences were found between APE and CPE groups. APE showed significantly higher mean HU and ED values than CPE on both unenhanced and enhanced images (both p < 0.001). Thrombus enhancement, using true non-contrast (TNC) values as a reference, was similar between groups. APE showed greater variability in HU and ED values, whereas CPE consistently demonstrated lower values across all imaging phases. Unenhanced HU and ED values provided better discrimination than post-contrast values, with high AUCs ( p < 0.05). The in vitro findings were consistent with these observations and may provide a plausible explanation for the compositional differences between APE and CPE. APE showed higher HU and ED values than CPE. Conventional and spectral CT parameters could help differentiate APE from CPE, reflecting distinct thrombus compositions.

Article.Abstract: Abstract While the potential of Virtual Reality (VR) in destination marketing is recognized, tourists’ motivations to adopt it remain underexplored. Integrating the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology with Anticipated Emotion, an online survey was conducted on 626 respondents. Structural Equation Modelling-Partial Least Squares was employed to test the effects of cognitive and emotional predictors. For practitioners, the study offers strategies to promote VR in heritage sites by addressing both rational and emotional motivations, fostering pre-visit engagement and enriching on-site experiences. Article.Title: DuSR-Net: a statistical- and optimization-prior-guided deep-unrolled network with cross-scale manifold alignment for hyperspectral image classification
Article.Authors: Zhang R.; Chang Y.; Li Q.; Wang X.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the issues of missing interpretability in existing deep learning models, weak spatial-spectral structure preservation,and poor generalization in small-sample-size scenarios, this paper proposes a Deep Unfolding Tensor Low-Rank Network(DuTLR-Net) that deeply integrates physical priors. First, a Cross-Scale Manifold Alignment (CSMA) module is designed,which uses a global PCA manifold as guidance to dynamically select high-variance spectral bands, achieving alignment ofmulti-scale features. Subsequently, the constructed ADMM-based deep unfolding backbone network explicitly models thespectral low-rankness and noise sparsity constraints as a differentiable iterative optimization process, enabling end-to-endlearning through parameterized dictionaries and adaptive soft-thresholding. Experiments demonstrate that DuTLR-Net, withfewer parameters and faster convergence speed, exhibits superior classification accuracy and spatial consistency underextremely low labeling rates.code:https://github.com/yongqichang202-beep/DuTLR-Net
