Article.Title: Effect of a Greenberg-based emotion-focused intervention on marital stress in patients with burn injuries
Article.Authors: Mansouri A.; Mousavi M.; Mohammadi Z.; Moghimian M.
Article.Abstract: Burn injuries can result in persistent changes in appearance, body image, physical functioning, and emotional well-being that may interfere with intimate relationships. Emotional difficulties associated with altered self-perception and concerns about acceptance may contribute to marital stress. This study aimed to determine the effect of a Greenberg-based emotion-focused intervention (EFI) on marital stress among patients with burn injuries. This randomized controlled trial included 40 married patients with burn injuries who were recruited using convenience sampling and randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention (n = 20) or control (n = 20) group using a computer-generated randomization sequence. Marital stress was assessed using the Stockholm Marital Stress Scale at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and 1 month after completion of the intervention. Participants in the intervention group received 10 weekly emotion-focused sessions, each lasting approximately 60 min, based on Greenberg’s emotion-focused framework. The control group received routine care. Data were analyzed using a 2 × 3 mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance. All 40 participants completed the three assessment points, resulting in a 100% retention rate. The groups did not differ significantly in baseline demographic and clinical characteristics. Baseline marital stress scores did not differ significantly between the intervention and control groups (43.41 ± 8.08 vs. 46.00 ± 6.16, respectively; p = .26). A significant Group × Time interaction was observed for marital stress F = 62.92, p < .001, ηp 2 = .624. In the intervention group, marital stress decreased significantly from baseline to post-intervention (mean difference = 6.36, p < .001) and from post-intervention to the 1-month follow-up (mean difference = 2.10, p < .001), whereas no significant changes were observed in the control group. A Greenberg-based EFI significantly reduced marital stress among patients with burn injuries, with the reduction maintained at the 1-month follow-up. EFI may therefore be considered a complementary psychosocial component of comprehensive burn rehabilitation for patients experiencing marital difficulties.

Article.Title: Virtual self-excited induction generator based grid-forming control with inherent current limiting through virtual demagnetization and GWO-DE optimized adaptive capacitance
Article.Authors: Rajak M.; Pawar M.; Meitei I.; Pudur R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents the Virtual Self-Excited Induction Generator (V-SEIG), a grid-forming control concept for power electronic converters that, to the best of the authors’ knowledge, constitutes the first reported implementation of the complete self-excited induction generator dynamic model as the generative core of a grid-forming converter control algorithm in the low-inertia grid context. The fourth-order d – q axis model of a squirrel-cage induction machine, including the nonlinear magnetizing characteristic, slip-dependent electromagnetic torque, self-excitation dynamics from a virtual residual flux, and an adaptive virtual capacitor bank, is solved within the converter control loop at 10 kHz. Three structural features distinguish the V-SEIG from synchronous-machine-based virtual generators: inherent current limiting through saturation-driven virtual demagnetization without external protection logic; natural voltage bounding through magnetic saturation; and a software-implemented adaptive virtual capacitance bounded between 30 and 80 $$\mu$$ F, with PID adaptation gains and underlying virtual machine parameters jointly tuned by a Grey Wolf Optimizer–Differential Evolution (GWO-DE) hybrid metaheuristic. The present study is a simulation-based proof of concept: the concept is evaluated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations across eight operating scenarios, anchored to a 5.5 kW, 4-pole, 415 V, 50 Hz reference machine and incorporating a switching-level converter model together with a representative measurement, noise, and quantization pipeline. Voltage builds up from a 0.01 Wb virtual residual flux to rated value within 0.65 s. Within this simulation scope, comparative benchmarking against a current-limited grid-forming VSG equipped with a threshold virtual impedance scheme indicates a 48.4% reduction in peak fault current ( $$1.47 \pm 0.02$$ pu vs. $$2.85 \pm 0.04$$ pu), driven by a collapse of the virtual magnetizing inductance from 254 mH to 92 mH within 20 ms of fault inception; 35.6% faster voltage recovery (85 ms vs. 132 ms); an 89.2% improvement in islanded voltage regulation under nonlinear loading ( $$4.45\% \rightarrow 0.48\%$$ ); a voltage THD of $$1.83\% \pm 0.05\%$$ against $$3.95\% \pm 0.07\%$$ (a 53.7% reduction); a 50% load-step voltage dip of 18.0 V vs. 27.5 V with recovery in 120 ms vs. 248 ms; and slip-based parallel power sharing with $$1.8 \pm 0.3\%$$ error and a 70.8% lower circulating current (0.35 A vs. 1.20 A rms). Voltage regulation is retained below $$1.2\%$$ and the dominant-mode damping ratio above 0.18 across short-circuit ratios from 1.5 to 10. The GWO-DE optimizer converges to an objective value of $$0.110 \pm 0.004$$ within $$122 \pm 6$$ iterations over 30 independent runs, and robustness to $$\pm 20\%$$ parameter uncertainty is confirmed across 200 Monte Carlo realizations with a worst-case peak fault current of 1.68 pu, below the 2.0 pu device limit. The control law executes within $$1.52\%$$ of the 10 kHz control period on a representative digital signal processor.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: metaheuristic parameter tuning; fault current limitation; squirrel cage induction motor; grid-forming inverters; islanded operation; low-inertia power systems; voltage total harmonic distortion

Article.Title: SemioKAT-FL: explainable, background-invariant, and privacy-preserving video seizure detection with a Kolmogorov–Arnold Transformer and federated learning
Article.Authors: Alharbi A.; Dhopeshwarkar M.; Tawfik M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automatic detection of epileptic seizures from video promises non-invasive, continuous patient monitoring, yet web-sourced seizure corpora are dominated by background confounds : recording-specific cues (studio, home, clinic) that are spuriously correlated with the seizure label. Models that appear highly accurate under conventional random splits may therefore be recognizing studios rather than seizures , and they remain opaque and dependent on centralizing sensitive patient video. We present SemioKAT-FL, a framework that addresses all three issues jointly. Spatial features from an ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 encoder are temporally modeled by a Kolmogorov–Arnold Transformer (KAT) that couples multi-head self-attention with learnable B-spline (KAN) feed-forward layers; a temporal-attention pooling layer yields per-second saliency; and an adversarial background-invariance head, driven by a gradient-reversal layer, penalizes any ability to recover the source recording. Training uses Federated Averaging so that raw video never leaves a site. On a corpus of 1,148 clips from 275 source recordings evaluated under leakage-controlled subject-wise (GroupKFold) cross-validation, we first show that a faithful re-implementation of the reference method drops from 99.5% under random splits to 94.9% subject-wise, and that a background-only model still reaches 90.4%—direct evidence of confounding. The adversarial head substantially reduces a source-recovery probe from 70% to 50% (chance $$\approx 1.3\%$$ ); the representation retains reduced but non-negligible source information, which we characterize as partial rather than complete invariance. The full calibrated ensemble attains $$96.6\%\pm 1.8\%$$ accuracy (F1 $$=96.8\%$$ , AUC $$=0.93$$ , expected calibration error 0.02–0.03) under source-level GroupKFold, and the federated model—trained on simulated site partitions without formal differential privacy—matches its centralized counterpart within 0.4%. To our knowledge, SemioKAT-FL is the first video seizure detector that jointly addresses background confounding through adversarial invariance, provides intrinsic explainability, and avoids centralization of raw video through federated training.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: federated learning; epilepsy; privacy-preserving machine learning; explainable AI; gradient reversal layer

Article.Title: Designing and simulating a real-time SCADA-based monitoring system for the Tis-Abay II hydroelectric power plant
Article.Authors: Ayalew G.; Kebede G.; Nagarajan S.; Paramasivam V.
Article.Abstract: Automation is a method for monitoring and regulating systems, enhancing work quality by utilizing control systems, intelligent electronic devices, instrumentation, and new communication technologies. In the Tis-Abay II hydropower plant, the previous SCADA (H9000) has an outdated operating system and is currently not functional. Nowadays, due to the failure of the SCADA in the plant, all tasks are executed manually, which decreases the willingness of the operators to work day-to-day. The study allows real-time data acquisition, control, and monitoring through the Simatic WinCC Runtime Advanced SCADA within the TIA Portal software for the Tis-Abay II hydroelectric power station. In the operational control segment, the control programs were developed, and a human-machine interface (HMI) was designed for configuration changes, parameter settings, and status indications. The new SCADA system was simulated and validated. The simulation results enable users to get historical data points across various time intervals, alarm operators for predefined events as per the identified real-time, and allow for insightful analysis and trend view identification when the generator runs at an output power of 36 MW, with a terminal voltage of 10.5 KV, a current of 2083.8 A, and reactive power of 13.4 MVAR.=

Article.Title: Combined effects of a novel reduced graphene oxide-enriched diesel-hazelnut biodiesel-tetrahydrofuran blend on combustion and emission characteristics of a compression ignition engine
Article.Authors: Kocakulak T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The gradual exhaustion of fossil fuel reserves and the enforcement of stricter emission regulations have driven the search for sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative fuels for compression-ignition engines. In this study, the effects of the combined use of hazelnut biodiesel, tetrahydrofuran (THF), and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) nanoparticles on combustion characteristics, engine performance, and exhaust emissions were experimentally investigated in a diesel engine. Pure diesel, biodiesel–diesel blends, THF-containing blends, and nanofuel blends enriched with 50, 100, and 150 ppm rGO nanoparticles were tested under three engine loads (11, 16.5, and 22 Nm). Combustion analysis was performed using in-cylinder pressure data. The indicated mean effective pressure (IMEP), thermal efficiency (TE), specific fuel consumption (SFC), ringing intensity, combustion duration, maximum pressure rise rate, cyclic variations, and CO, CO₂, HC, and NOx emissions were evaluated. The experimental results showed differences in combustion characteristics, engine performance, and exhaust emissions among the tested fuel blends. Among the tested nanofuels, the highest IMEP increase reached 21.79% at low engine load, and cyclic variations were reduced through improving combustion stability. In addition, CO and NOx emissions decreased by up to 29.41% and 13.09%, respectively. The rGO-containing fuel blends reduced HC emissions by up to 14.9% at high engine load and increased thermal efficiency by up to 3.92%. These findings indicate that fuel blends containing hazelnut biodiesel, THF, and rGO nanoparticles can contribute to improved engine performance and reduced harmful exhaust emissions under the investigated operating conditions.

Article.Title: Species-specific variation in thermal tolerance in Montipora capitata and Porites compressa corals across two Hawaiian bay habitats
Article.Authors: Klein A.; Voss J.; Drury C.; Hancock J.; Lewis C.; Hughes K.; Toonen R.; Levy J.; N/A N/A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding variation in coral thermal tolerance is critical for predicting coral responses and reef persistence under future ocean conditions. This study investigated thermal performance of two dominant Hawaiian reef-builders, Montipora capitata and Porites compressa , collected from three sites in Kāneʻohe Bay and one site in nearby Kailua Bay (Ulupaʻu). Corals were subjected to a controlled heat-stress assay, and photosynthetic efficiency was measured using Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM) fluorometry. Thermal tolerance was quantified as effective dose 30 (ED30), the experimental degree heating week (eDHW) exposure at which corals lost 30% of photosynthetic efficiency. Both species exhibited high thermal tolerance, with ED30 values ranging from 5.93 to 7.21 eDHW and mean values of 6.44 eDHW for M. capitata and 6.70 eDHW for P. compressa . Within Kāneʻohe Bay, thermal performance was similar for both species. In contrast, P. compressa from Ulupaʻu displayed significantly greater tolerance than Kāneʻohe conspecifics and all M. capitata populations. Together, these findings demonstrate that coral thermal tolerance is shaped by environmental history in a species-specific manner. This highlights the importance of selecting both appropriate species and source populations when identifying thermally resilience corals for restoration and conservation strategies in Hawaiʻi.

Article.Title: Functional maturation of the infant gut microbiome during dietary transition in the first year of life
Article.Authors: Joos R.; Das A.; Ahern G.; Dempsey E.; Lavelle A.; Murray D.; Ross R.; Kiely M.; Stanton C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract During the first months of life, breastfeeding and/or formula provide an infant’s sole nutrition. The introduction of solid foods marks the complementary feeding period – a major dietary and gut microbial transition. While taxonomic development of the early-life gut microbiome is well described, functional changes and the influence of different milk types remain less understood. This study used metagenomic data from a subset of 125 Irish infants of the COMBINE cohort to examine taxonomic and functional microbiome shifts during early feeding transitions. Consistent with nutritional guidelines, over 80% of mothers introduced solid foods between four and six months. Alongside, 16.8% of infants were still breastfed, 12.8% were mixed-fed, and 69.6% were formula-fed. Microbial diversity increased over time, alongside a shift in community structure toward a more anaerobic gut environment. Functionally, carbohydrate metabolism transitioned from simple sugar degradation to complex polysaccharide degradation and SCFA fermentation. Clear differences emerged between milk types, with a pacing effect of breastfeeding and distinct metabolic adaptations to varying nutritional substrates. The study reveals consistent, early functional shifts in the gut microbiome with the onset of complementary feeding, highlighting the strong influence of feeding mode on microbial metabolism and underscoring the need to consider function alongside taxonomy in early-life microbiome research.

Article.Title: Enhancing student performance prediction using an optimized RNN-LSTM model: a step towards personalized education
Article.Authors: Joann J.; Balasubramanian M.; Nisha A.; Kokila P.
Article.Abstract: Learning Analytics is an emerging field that strives to analyze and predict trends in student performances over time. With the increased usage of Learning Management Systems (LMS), which are equipped with learning content, interaction, and assessment aligned with educational objectives, advanced machine learning techniques such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are being used to analyze sequential data. This research aims to assess the efficiency of LSTM in student performance prediction by comparing its accuracy with other baseline models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs). The proposed optimized recurrent LSTM model outperforms CNN and GRU baseline models in prediction accuracy and efficiently captures temporal dependencies in sequential student academic data. To enhance training stability and predictive performance, the model was trained using Binary Cross-Entropy loss and validation-based parameter selection. The research indicates that such a model has the ability to be used in personalized learning by adjusting learning paths dynamically to improve student performances.Experiments were conducted using a synthetic dataset designed to simulate realistic academic progress patterns, demonstrating the model’s predictive capability.

Article.Title: Association between pain intensity and perceived cognitive impairment in non-central nervous system cancer survivors: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Qiu Z.; Xu Y.; Huang Q.; Chen Q.; Zhang Y.; Weng G.; Ke X.
Article.Abstract: While pain is known to pose a significant risk for cognitive outcomes in non-central nervous system cancer survivors, the impact of pain intensity remains unclear. This study aims to explore the association between pain intensity and perceived cognitive impairment and to examine the moderating role of sleep quality between them among non-central nervous system cancer survivors. Data collection was conducted in 14 wards across grade-A tertiary hospitals in China between 2024 and 2025. The data of demographics, disease-related, and treatment-related factors, pain intensity, perceived cognitive impairment were included in the analyses. Pain intensity included least, worst and average pain, as measured by the Brief Pain Inventory-Short Form. Least, worst and average pain are defined as the lowest, highest and average levels of pain intensity experienced in the past 24 h, respectively. Perceived cognitive impairment was assessed using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire cognitive functioning subscale. Data were analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models to account for ward-level clustering while testing the main effects of pain intensity and Johnson-Neyman method to test the moderating role of sleep quality on cognitive outcomes. A total of 692 non-central nervous system cancer survivors were included (mean age: 58.09 ± 11.45 years; 78.90% male; 57.08% primary education or below, 61.42% digestive system cancer participants. According to the results of the fixed-slope model, after controlling for demographic, disease-related, and treatment-related factors, the least, worst, and average pain were positively associated with attention complaints (β = 0.288–0.395, all P < 0.01). Worst pain was associated with memory complaints in this exploratory analysis (β = 0.279, P = 0.034). Sleep quality significantly moderated the association between all pain intensities and perceived cognitive impairment, particularly for memory complaints across all pain intensities (interaction β = 0.187–0.262, P = 0.047 − 0.013). Johnson-Neyman analyses revealed that pain intensity became significantly associated with cognitive complaints only when the sleep quality scores exceeded certain thresholds. The impact of pain intensity on perceived cognitive impairment in cancer survivors appears domain-specific, with attention complaints associated with all three pain intensities. In exploratory analyses, worst pain was associated with memory complaints, though this finding requires confirmation using more comprehensive cognitive assessments. Sleep quality moderated the association between pain intensity and memory complaints. Clinically, the association between pain intensity and cognitive complaints should be assessed multidimensionally. The potential role of worst pain as an indicator of cognitive risk is preliminary and warrants further investigation. Sleep management should be integrated into symptom protocols for cognitive complaints.

Article.Title: Pulp oxygen saturation and clinical outcomes after direct pulp capping with MTA or 45S5 bioactive glass in mature permanent teeth: a pragmatic randomized clinical trial
Article.Authors: Gonçalves B.; Grazziotin-Soares R.; Nogueira A.; Costa C.; Gavini G.; Filho E.; dos Santos T.; Ferreira M.; Carvalho C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To evaluate pulp oxygen saturation and clinical outcomes after direct pulp capping with mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA) or 45S5 bioactive glass in mature permanent teeth with carious pulp exposure. This pragmatic randomized clinical trial included 44 mature permanent teeth from patients aged 15–40 years presenting deep carious lesions with a clinical diagnosis compatible with reversible pulpitis or early pulpal inflammation. Teeth were randomly allocated (1:1) to direct pulp capping with MTA (n = 22) or 45S5 bioactive glass (n = 22). Pulp oxygen saturation, cold sensitivity, and radiographic findings were assessed at baseline and after 1, 3, 6, 12, and 18 months. Pulp oxygen saturation values were measured using pulse oximetry and analyzed over time using the Friedman test. Clinical survival was estimated using Kaplan–Meier analysis and compared between groups using the log-rank, Breslow, and Tarone–Ware tests. No significant changes in pulp oxygen saturation were observed over time in either group (MTA, p = 0.665; 45S5, p = 0.723). Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated a significantly higher clinical survival probability for teeth treated with MTA than for those treated with 45S5 bioactive glass (log-rank, p = 0.002). Cox regression analysis showed that the pulp-capping material was the only variable significantly associated with treatment failure (HR = 9.51; p = 0.012). Pulp oxygen saturation remained stable after treatment but did not discriminate between successful and failed cases. MTA demonstrated more favorable clinical outcomes than 45S5 bioactive glass for direct pulp capping in mature permanent teeth.

Article.Title: The enhanced importance of CD4+ T cell based monitoring of microbial flora in patients with HIV
Article.Authors: Yang S.; Liu J.; Yu F.; Tang Y.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Individuals infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) frequently display diminished CD4 + T Cell levels, heightening susceptibility to diverse infections and imposing substantial burdens alongside life-threatening risks. This study aimed to compare lung microbial communities between general infections and HIV-associated cases. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples from 221 patients with lung diseases or infection underwent 16S and ITS sequencing analysis. The cohort comprised with 18 HIV-negative, GM-negative individuals; 29 HIV-negative, GM-positive individuals; 104 HIV-positive, GM-negative individuals; and 70 HIV-positive, GM-positive individuals. Through comparative analysis of microbial disparities across groups, we observed that GM test-positive individuals displayed pronounced fungal infections, which significantly amplified the detectable diversity of fungal species while exhibiting heterogeneous compositional profiles. Conversely, bacterial diversity demonstrated negligible overall variation. Notably, viral load exhibited an inverse correlation with CD4 + T Cell counts, and these immune cells further revealed a discernible association with both viral load dynamics and microbial community shifts. These insights underscore the critical necessity for real-time monitoring of CD4 + T Cell fluctuations and microbial equilibrium in HIV-infected patients.

Article.Title: Hybrid graph-temporal modeling with uncertainty-aware Transformers for elderly fall detection
Article.Authors: Khalili N.; Rastgoo R.
Article.Abstract: The accurate detection of falls, particularly among elderly populations, remains a critical challenge in smart health monitoring due to the severe physical and psychological consequences of delayed intervention. In this work, a novel hybrid fall detection framework is proposed, which simultaneously captures spatial and temporal dynamics of human motion through the integration of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), Graph Attention Networks (GATs), Inverse Graph Fourier Transform (IGFT), and uncertainty-aware Transformer (UATransformer) architectures. Spatial dependencies are modeled via GCNs to extract local joint interactions, while GATs adaptively prioritize critical joints, enhancing robustness to occlusions, misaligned camera angles, and visually similar motions. Motion features are further refined in the spectral domain using IGFT and multi-scale spectral filtering, allowing the separation of global posture drifts, coordinated joint movements, and high-frequency fall accelerations. Temporal modeling is performed using an uncertainty-aware Transformer, which assigns higher attention to ambiguous or fall-onset frames, enabling early detection of imminent falls. To address class imbalance and improve sensitivity to rare events, a multi-component loss function combining weighted cross-entropy, focal loss, and fall-onset prediction loss is employed. The framework is evaluated on the NTU RGB + D and University of Rzeszow Fall Detection datasets, comprising 114,480 samples across 120 classes of daily activities and 40 daily living activities, as well as 30 fall sequences, achieving accuracies of 99.00% and 99.80%, respectively. Collectively, these contributions yield a model that robustly distinguishes falls from similar actions, anticipates fall onset, and demonstrates strong potential for deployment in clinical and elderly care environments.

Article.Title: Engineered pediatric human muscle models the interferon-driven transcriptome of juvenile dermatomyositis
Article.Authors: Swain Lenz D.; Dvergsten J.; Turnier J.; Neely J.; Madubata C.; Goudsmit C.; Banerjee S.; Ardalan K.; Kandil S.; Truskey G.; Covert L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) is a rare pediatric autoimmune disease characterized by a strong type I interferon (IFN) signature in muscle. Mechanistic and therapeutic discovery has been limited by the lack of a clinically relevant disease model. To address this, we tested whether IFN treatment of a human muscle-derived microphysiological system (myobundles) recapitulates the transcriptional profile of JDM muscle. Principal component analysis of RNA sequencing from healthy and JDM muscle along with IFN-treated and untreated myobundles revealed separation of healthy and untreated samples from JDM and IFN-treated samples. JDM muscle exhibited 4,121 differentially expressed genes (DEGs, p adj <0.05) compared to healthy muscle, of which 56.2% showed concordant differential expression in IFNβ-treated and 30.0% in IFNα-treated myobundles. Hallmark pathway analysis demonstrated concordant directional changes between JDM muscle and IFN-treated myobundles. IFN and inflammatory pathways were most upregulated; oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid metabolism, and adipogenesis were downregulated, though not reproducible across sites. Normalized enrichment score correlations between JDM muscle and IFN-treated myobundles were strongly positive ( r = 0.63, p =1 × 10 − 6 for IFNα; r = 0.67, p = 1.3 × 10 − 7 for IFNβ). These findings indicate that IFN-treated myobundles, particularly with IFNβ, mirror key transcriptional features of JDM muscle and provide a needed muscle-centric platform to study IFN-driven mechanisms and therapeutic targets.

Article.Title: Location and manifold based dual prediction method for dynamic multiobjective optimization with stochastic changes
Article.Authors: Li G.; Deng X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Most methods for solving dynamic multiobjective optimization problems (DMOPs) are suitable primarily for addressing problems with deterministic changes. However, in practical scenarios, environmental changes in DMOPs are often characterized by stochasticity. Therefore, a location- and manifold-based dual prediction method (LMDP) is proposed for DMOPs with stochastic changes. In this method, one or two historical PSs closest to the PS in the new environment are identified to predict the location of the new PS. Based on the predicted location, submanifolds of the historical PSs similar to the manifold of the PS in the new environment are subsequently identified to predict the manifold of the new PS. This approach improves the ability of the prediction model to capture the location and manifold of the PS in the new environment, thereby increasing its adaptability to stochastic changes. The proposed method is tested on DMOPs designed with stochastic changes. The results demonstrate that our method outperforms several comparative methods, thus validating its effectiveness in solving DMOPs with stochastic changes.

Article.Title: Experimental study on the evolution of mesoscopic structure and macroscopic mechanical properties of typical karst fillings soil under dry-wet cycles
Article.Authors: Nie Z.; Luo X.; Shao G.; Li X.; Yao C.; Liu Z.; Yang G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The limestone formation in the Jinan area belongs to a typical karst development zone in northern China. Initially, basic physical tests were conducted on karst fillings from typical sites in the Jinan area. The data indicated that the fillings exhibit moderate expansion potential, with high montmorillonite content being the cause of their expansibility. Further tests were carried out on the expansive karst fillings, including free swelling ratio tests under dry-wet cycles, mercury intrusion porosimetry tests, and triaxial tests. The specimens were subjected to 1, 3, 7, and 11 dry-wet cycles. The findings are as follows: (1) Multiple dry-wet cycles significantly reduce the expansibility of karst fillings. (2) After 11 dry-wet cycles, the total pore volume increased by 83%, with the proportion of large pores rising from 6% to 49%, indicating a significant deterioration in the microstructure of the karst fillings. (3) With an increase in the number of dry-wet cycles, the shear strength decreased noticeably, and the elastic modulus declined exponentially, stabilizing after a reduction of approximately 38% following 3 cycles. The rate of shear strength decline was relatively uniform, with an eventual deterioration of about 40%. Quantitative relationships between elastic modulus, shear strength, and the number of dry-wet cycles were established based on experimental data. Stress paths and effective stress ratio curves revealed a strain-softening effect in the karst fillings after dry-wet cycles, gradually exhibiting ductile failure. As the number of cycles increased, repeated expansion and contraction weakened the cementation between particles, making them more prone to rearrangement and compaction. This led to a 1.3-fold increase in the maximum static pore water pressure during the tests. Based on the results of mercury intrusion porosimetry and triaxial tests, a progressive macro-micro damage evolution pattern was established, revealing the intrinsic correlation between microscopic damage evolution and macroscopic mechanical deterioration of karst fillings under dry-wet cycles. This study provides valuable references for engineering construction in karst areas.

Article.Title: Elastic-band post-activation performance enhancement alters lower-limb coordination during stable and unstable single-leg landings
Article.Authors: Sahraei I.; Mohammadipour F.; Amiri-Khorasani M.; Bui F.
Article.Abstract: Warm-up may change how soccer players organise lower-limb motion during landing, but the separate contributions of elastic-band post-activation performance enhancement (PAPE) and surface instability remain unclear. Twenty male collegiate soccer players completed four conditions in counterbalanced order on four non-consecutive days: general warm-up or elastic-band PAPE, each followed by single-leg landings from a 30-cm platform onto a stable or an unstable surface. Hip-knee and knee-ankle coordination and coordination variability were quantified from continuous relative phase and averaged over five accepted trials per condition. Within-participant contrasts tested warm-up, surface and interaction effects. Elastic-band PAPE increased hip-knee coordination (mean difference 3.50°, 95% CI 1.01 to 5.98, Cohen’s dz = 0.66, false-discovery-rate-adjusted p = 0.025) and knee-ankle coordination (5.42°, 95% CI 3.08 to 7.76, dz = 1.08, adjusted p = 0.001); both effects were confirmed by Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Neither surface nor the warm-up-by-surface interaction reached significance for any outcome, and coordination variability was unchanged. Individual surface responses were, however, large and bidirectional, so the null surface result reflects cancellation of opposing individual responses rather than absence of response. Elastic-band PAPE acutely alters landing coordination; this is not evidence of reduced injury risk.

Article.Title: Multimodal deep learning framework for LoRaWAN based crop health monitoring
Article.Authors: Theerthagiri P.; Usha Ruby A.; George Chellin Chandran J.; Sekhar Roy K.; Sardar T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cucumber is a widely cultivated vegetable crop worldwide. However, environmental stress, pest infestations, and diseases can significantly reduce crop quality and yield. Early disease detection and continuous crop monitoring are essential for improving productivity and minimising agricultural losses. This study proposes A gri P redict– L oRaWAN Net work (APLNet), an Internet of Things (IoT)-based agricultural monitoring and disease classification framework designed for cucumber farming. The system integrates LoRaWAN (Long Range Wide Area Network) enabled sensors to continuously collect critical soil parameters, including moisture, temperature, pH, and electrical conductivity. In addition, leaf image analysis is employed to identify healthy and diseased cucumber plants. The collected soil and leaf data are processed and analysed using the proposed APLNet model, and the model’s performance is evaluated using standard classification metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Experimental results demonstrate that APLNet achieves superior classification performance compared with established deep learning models, including EfficientNet-B0 to B7, ResNet50, and InceptionV3. The proposed model achieves 98% classification accuracy in distinguishing healthy from unhealthy cucumber leaves. Furthermore, the proposed system is deployed as a web-based decision-support AgriPredict platform that enables farmers with real-time crop monitoring and management. It supports timely decision-making, improves productivity, reduces crop losses, and promotes sustainable cucumber cultivation.

Article.Title: Multi-task deep learning with fisheye cameras for patient fall detection: development and real-world hospital deployment
Article.Authors: Lee S.; Kim J.; Lee S.; Park C.; Park J.; Jeong I.
Article.Abstract: Falls in hospital wards remain a significant safety concern, and conventional monitoring relying on intermittent observations may delay escalation. We developed a ceiling-mounted, top-view fisheye framework integrating a Panoptic-DeepLab-inspired, multi-task model within real-time ward operations. The network employs an EfficientNetV2-S encoder and bidirectional feature pyramid network decoders with parallel heads for patient detection, eight-class posture recognition, and seven-class human–object interaction classification, supported by auxiliary depth and normal supervision during training. We analyzed a de-identified, non-public actor-staged dataset collected at hospital and hospital-like sites (nine participants, 40 scripted actions) with fine-grained annotations, including skeletons, postures, interactions, and object polygons. Evaluation used leave-one-site-out cross-validation across the recording sites. The proposed system achieved a mean fall-positive precision of 0.9829 ± 0.0297, recall of 0.9219 ± 0.2040, and F1-score of 0.9343 ± 0.1766. During real-world deployment across seven wards over 1,450 monitoring days, the system recorded 325 true falls and 695 false alarms, corresponding to an average false-alarm frequency of 0.48 per monitoring day. Seated falls occurred as frequently as recumbent falls, and over 20,000 non-alarming “fall cautions” reflected the prevalence of bed-edge dynamics in routine care. These findings support the feasibility of context-aware, ceiling-mounted fisheye monitoring for room-scale fall surveillance; however, broader prospective validation remains necessary to establish generalizability across routine clinical environments.

Article.Title: Dual-branch cross-modal architecture with global-to-local feedback for radiographic image–text retrieval in chest X-rays
Article.Authors: Abedin R.; Laridi S.; Tam K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Radiology reports are vital for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning, yet their manual generation is time-consuming and dependent on radiologist expertise, leading to delays and inconsistent clinical decisions. Medical image–text retrieval offers a scalable solution by enabling the retrieval of relevant prior cases and reports. However, existing models often rely on static embeddings, which limits their ability to capture fine-grained, clinically meaningful cross-modal relationships. This limitation is particularly critical in chest X-ray interpretation, where nuanced textual descriptions must align with subtle visual cues. We introduce a novel dual-branch retrieval framework that distinguishes between shared semantics and complementary features through a Synergy branch and a Difference branch , respectively. These branches are stabilized through orthogonal regularization, ensuring minimal redundancy while keeping complementary diagnostic cues. A Global-to-Local Feedback mechanism guides fine-grained local attention using global context, enhancing interpretability and clinical relevance. Evaluated on two benchmark datasets, our model achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance across both image $$\rightarrow$$ text and text $$\rightarrow$$ image tasks. Through hierarchical gated co-attention, our approach dynamically aligns image and text representations, addressing the limitations of static fusion and providing a foundation for interpretable, real-time retrieval systems that can accelerate and improve clinical decision support.

Article.Title: Machine learning enhanced coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of graphene incorporated aluminium based metal matrix composite
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; De A.; Darvekar A.; Pradhan S.; Pandey T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Graphene-reinforced aluminum metal matrix composites (Al–Gr MMCs) have attracted significant attention for high-temperature structural applications due to their potential to combine low density with improved dimensional stability. While aluminum exhibits favorable mechanical properties and processability, it undergoes considerable thermal expansion at elevated temperatures. In contrast, graphene possesses low or negative thermal expansion characteristics and can act as a thermal constraint within the matrix, making Al–Gr composites promising for applications requiring thermal stability. However, experimental characterization particularly at high temperatures and higher graphene concentrations is limited due to challenges such as dispersion difficulties, agglomeration beyond 1 wt% graphene, and restricted availability of comprehensive datasets. To address these limitations, this research work highlights a physics-guided hybrid machine learning framework to predict the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) and overall length change of Al–Gr composites. The approach integrates physics-aware feature engineering with synthetic data augmentation to construct an extended dataset spanning a wider range of temperatures and compositions. For accurate interpolation within the experimentally observed domain, a multi-model stacking ensemble is employed, combining the best-performing models from five algorithmic groups using a Ridge Regressor meta-learner. To improve reliability in extrapolation, the ensemble is dynamically fused with a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) and a Bayesian Neural Network (BNN). The PINN introduces physics-guided behavior through a gradient-based monotonic regularization term, encouraging predictions that follow physically consistent trends with increasing graphene content. The BNN, implemented using Monte Carlo dropout, provides approximate estimates of predictive uncertainty through stochastic forward passes. A composition-dependent weighting strategy is used to combine these components, allowing the framework to balance data-driven accuracy, physical consistency, and uncertainty awareness across different regimes. The proposed framework demonstrates very high predictive performance within the observed data range (R 2 ≈ 0.999176 with low prediction error) and is further used to explore thermal behavior up to 2.4 wt% graphene and temperatures up to 500 °C. The results capture key trends, including the gradual stabilization of thermal expansion at elevated temperatures and the overall reduction in effective CTE with increasing graphene content. While these predictions extend beyond currently available experimental data, they provide useful insights into material behavior and highlight the potential of physics-guided hybrid machine learning approaches for supporting composite design in high-temperature environments.

Article.Title: Conventional light microscopy or digital slides: a study to evaluate the effectiveness and acceptance of digitized histological sections in teaching
Article.Authors: Gerdinand K.; Tolks D.; Joost S.; Kipp M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Digital learning formats are increasingly used in medical education. In histology, virtual microscopy offers a flexible alternative to conventional light microscopy, but its impact on learning outcomes and student acceptance remains debated. This study compared digital and conventional microscopy in terms of learning performance, usability, and student preferences. First-year medical students participated in a practical histology course using either digital slides or light microscopy in a crossover design. Cohort A studied muscle tissue digitally and bone tissue conventionally, while Cohort B followed the reverse arrangement. Learning outcomes were assessed using 14 image-based examination questions. Student perceptions and preferences were evaluated through a questionnaire addressing navigation, efficiency, collaboration, enjoyment, and perceived importance of technical basics. Students rated digital microscopy significantly higher (all p < 0.0001). Overall, 79.9% preferred digital slides for future courses. Higher technological affinity was associated with preference for digital microscopy, with male students reporting significantly higher affinity than female students ( p = 0.0063). Examination performance did not differ significantly between learning modalities. Digital microscopy was preferred by students and perceived as more efficient, collaborative, and enjoyable than conventional microscopy. As learning outcomes were equivalent, digital microscopy represents an effective alternative and supports its broader integration into undergraduate histology education.

Article.Title: Language adaptive state space learning with text guided pseudo supervision enables weakly supervised skin lesion segmentation
Article.Authors: Jiang Y.; Shao Z.; Tian X.; Chen P.; Wang X.; Zhou K.
Article.Abstract: Accurate lesion segmentation in dermoscopy images is critical for high-throughput clinical screening, yet deploying automated diagnostic systems is severely hindered by the prohibitive computational cost of massive foundation models and the manual bottleneck of acquiring dense annotations. While recent vision-language pipelines alleviate the labeling burden by generating pseudo-masks from textual prompts, their staggering memory footprints and extreme inference latency render them unviable for real-time clinical edge deployment. Furthermore, contemporary State Space Models (SSMs) employed in such tasks typically process spatial features in fixed raster-scan orders, failing to efficiently capture semantic coherence between spatially disparate lesion regions. To overcome these computational and algorithmic bottlenecks, we propose a novel pseudo-supervision framework driven by a computational offloading paradigm. By isolating the massive multi-modal workloads to a highly parallelized offline pipeline, we strictly preserve real-time efficiency during online inference. The cornerstone of our method is an Adaptive Selective State-Space Module (ASSM) that employs a differentiable semantic routing mechanism to dynamically group related pixels into coherent sequences, ensuring robust long-range dependency modeling with minimal computational overhead. To harness textual priors without inflating inference latency, we introduce a Language-Fusion Squeeze-and-Excitation (LFSE) module to integrate domain-specific lesion descriptions via multi-scale cross-modal attention during the distributed training phase. The resulting semantic attention maps drive a Text-Guided Patch Augmentation (TPA) strategy to explicitly target uncertain boundary regions. By aligning a pure-vision student with a multimodal student and an exponential moving average teacher, our framework achieves robust segmentation relying solely on raw images during inference. Crucially, by entirely discarding the text-branch overhead, the deployed pure-vision model operates with exceptional computational efficiency. Specifically, it requires only 8.40M parameters and 0.37GB of peak memory, alongside a competitive computation cost of 18.06G FLOPs, perfectly satisfying the stringent real-time processing demands of modern clinical edge environments. Extensive experiments on five dermoscopic and endoscopic segmentation benchmarks demonstrate the strong cross-domain generalizability of the proposed approach. By utilizing bounding-box priors exclusively from a single source domain (ISIC 2017) to warm up the text-grounded detector, our pipeline operates in a strictly target-annotation-free regime for all other evaluated datasets. Compared to the most competitive text-supervised baseline, our method yields consistent absolute Dice Similarity Coefficient improvements of 1.41%, 1.65%, 1.38%, 1.64%, and 0.45% across the respective datasets, substantially narrowing the performance gap with fully supervised models while guaranteeing high-speed clinical applicability.

Article.Title: Mechanical and microstructural performance of residual sandy soil treated with different polymers
Article.Authors: Raheel M.; Jaffar S.; Jalal F.; Alqahtani F.; Abubakar S.; Khan H.
Article.Abstract: Sustainable management of environmentally vulnerable, moisture-sensitive soils is a critical challenge because they are susceptible to moisture-induced degradation. Biopolymer (BP) stabilisation offers an environmentally sustainable approach to transforming residual sandy soils into green geomaterials with reduced environmental impact. Consequently, engineering properties of these residual sandy soils vary spatially, and moisture conditions strongly influence their shear strength. This study investigates the efficacy of four categories of soil additives, i.e., (i) biodegradable polyester-based BPs (BPBs), (ii) natural polysaccharide BPs, (iii) synthetic polymers, and (iv) amino-polysaccharide BPs to enhance the mechanical performance of residual sandy soils. Specifically, the BPBs, namely polybutylene succinate (PBS) and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) are evaluated and compared with natural polysaccharides; xanthan gum (XG), guar gum (GG), gellan gum (GLG) and sodium alginate (SA); a synthetic polymer, i.e., polyacrylamide (PAM); and cationic amino-polysaccharide biopolymer, i.e., chitosan (CS). To this end, varying proportions of BPBs were incorporated into the residual sandy soil to optimize stabilization performance and evaluate its effectiveness against conventional BP-based stabilizers at 28-days under isothermal curing at 16 °C using unconfined compressive strength test and advanced material characterization techniques i.e., Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA). It was observed that the highest single improvement in UCS 28−d was obtained with a natural polysaccharide (2.0% GG, ≈ 8.8× the untreated strength), although performance within the polysaccharide group varied by an order of magnitude (334–1936 kPa) and overlapped with the amine-based and synthetic polymers. Despite BPBs showing comparatively lower UCS 28−d yet offering dosage efficiency; TGA confirmed that 0.4% PBS specimens demonstrated higher thermal stability among all treated samples while consolidated undrained triaxial test confirmed that PBS proves to be very effective in enhancing shear strength of residual sandy soil thus making it suitable for performance-specific applications.

Article.Title: Pilot-scale two-stage biohythane production from molasses under trace metal supplementation and organic shock loading
Article.Authors: Sittijunda S.; Promnuan K.; Chu C.; Imai T.; Reungsang A.
Article.Abstract: Biohythane production from molasses was studied in a pilot-scale two-stage anaerobic digester (0.4 m³/day) for 325 days. Hydraulic retention times were 18 h (H₂) and 9 d (CH₄) at an organic loading rate of 5.56 kg-COD/m³·day. Production rose from 0.48 m³/m³-reactor·day during start-up to 1.23 m³/m³-reactor·day in Phase 2. Trace metal supplementation (Ni 40, Co 40, Fe 200 mg/L) in Phase 3 (days 121–180) coincided with 1.62 m³/m³-reactor·day (9.24% H₂, 53.73% CH₄). Yields were 0.20 m³-H₂/kg-COD and 1.14 m³-CH₄/kg-COD. Between days 181 and 194, at unchanged feed, first-stage alkalinity fell from 2,661 to 496 mg/L. This decline preceded the loss of gas production by about ten days, marking alkalinity as an early warning indicator. Organic overloading at 50.56 kg-COD/m³·day (Phase 4) then caused system failure. Production dropped to 0.49 m³/m³-reactor·day and volatile fatty acids reached 8,972 mg/L. Bicarbonate addition (6,720 mg/L NaHCO₃) and trace metal re-supplementation (Phase 5) restored performance. Hydrogen recovered in 19 days, but methane required 55 days. The stable period (days 267–325) reached 1.97 m³/m³-reactor·day (0.24 m³-H₂/kg-COD, 1.42 m³-CH₄/kg-COD). Hydrogen production was associated with Firmicutes- (84%) or Proteobacteria-dominated (80%) consortia, methane with acetoclastic Methanosaeta. PICRUSt2 predicted higher formate dehydrogenase and methyl-coenzyme M reductase abundance in Phases 3 and 2, representing genetic potential only. Energy ratios were 2.97–10.17 in the stable periods and 1.93 under overload, equivalent to 85 MWh/year at best. These observations come from a single unreplicated pilot unit. They nonetheless identify first-stage alkalinity monitoring and stage-specific recovery allowances as practical controls for scale-up.

Article.Title: Mechanical characterization and deformation behaviour of polymer-based lattice structures fabricated via fused deposition modelling
Article.Authors: Rukmangad P.; Sen S.; Thomas B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lattice structures fabricated using additive manufacturing have gained significant attention due to their ability to achieve lightweight designs with enhanced mechanical performance. In this study, a comparative investigation was carried out on two different lattice geometries, namely Structure A (Re-entrant Hexagon structure) and Structure B (star triangular re-entrant structure), fabricated using Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) with PLA and ABS filament. The design was validated through FEA using ABAQUS from the reference study. The obtained deformation patterns and stress distributions showed good agreement with those reported in the reference study. Although auxetic deformation is governed by geometry, its mechanical performance is significantly influenced by material properties and manufacturing parameters. Compression tests were conducted using a Universal Testing Machine to evaluate their deformation characteristics and compressive performance. Among the tested specimens, PLA exhibited a maximum compressive stress of approximately 3.2 MPa compared to 2.3 MPa for ABS, while Structure A and Structure B achieved peak compressive stresses of approximately 28 MPa and 32 MPa, respectively. This study systematically investigates the influence of auxetic geometry and material selection on the compressive behaviour of FDM-fabricated lattice structures through multi-specimen experimental testing and finite element simulations, with quantitative comparison between experimental and numerical responses.The findings provide valuable insights for designing optimized PLA lattice structures A for Lightweight structural panels (aerospace/automotive), drone frame components, Robotic arms & fixtures, and ABS for Automotive interior components & Protective housings (electronics casing), and structure B of PLA and ABS for Packaging structures (fragile items protection), Automotive crash absorbers (crumple zones), Helmet liners & protective gear.

Article.Title: Microphone directionality improves speech perception in Mandarin-speaking cochlear implant users
Article.Authors: Qi B.; Dong R.; Gu X.; Zhuang B.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Speech understanding in noise remains challenging for cochlear implant (CI) users. To address this, microphone directionality has been integrated into speech processors to improve the signal-to-noise ratio. Despite demonstrated benefits for users of non-tonal language, studies investigating its efficacy for users of tonal languages are limited. In this study, we evaluated the benefit of microphone directionality in 24 Mandarin-speaking adult CI users with uni- or bilateral post-lingual deafness (≥ 6 months of experience) using the Mandarin Speech Test Materials in quiet and noise. Speech and noise were presented simultaneously (S0N180). Results of the MSTM are presented as speech recognition score (SRS) as percentage correct. Performance with an omnidirectional speech processor (OPUS 2) was compared to one (SONNET) with three directional modes (omni, natural, adaptive). A visual analogue scale (VAS) questionnaire was used to assess preferences for each speech processor setting. Directional modes significantly improved speech perception in noise: SONNET/natural outperformed both OPUS 2 by 10.4% (95% CI: 3.4% to 17.5%; p = 0.006) and SONNET/omni by 12.4% (95% CI: 6.0% to 18.7%; p = 0.001), while SONNET/adaptive outperformed both OPUS 2 (by 13.6%; 95% CI: 7.9% to 19.3%; p < 0.001) and SONNET/omni (by 15.6%; 95% CI: 8.4% to 22.7%; p < 0.001). The difference between SONNET/adaptive and SONNET/natural was 3.17% points (95% CI: -2.2% to 8.5%; p = 0.231). No significant difference was observed in quiet. 63% of participants favored SONNET/adaptive in noise. Under the S0N180 conditions tested, directional microphone settings were associated with better speech perception in noise than omnidirectional settings in Mandarin-speaking CI users, whereas no statistically significant difference was observed between the SONNET/adaptive and SONNET/natural settings. Upgrading from an omnidirectional speech processor to one equipped with directional technology may provide substantial and clinically meaningful benefit.

Article.Title: Cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of the persian version of the needling patient-reported experience measure in older adults undergoing hemodialysis
Article.Authors: Mahmoudian A.; Jamshidiavval N.; Shamsalinia A.; Abad Y.; Mousavi T.; Ghaffari F.
Article.Abstract: The Needling Patient-Reported Experience Measure (NPREM) is the first disease-specific instrument developed to assess this experience, but no culturally adapted, psychometrically validated Persian version exists for use with Iranian patients. The present study aimed to translate, cross-culturally adapt, and psychometrically validate the Persian version of the NPREM for older adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis in Iran. This methodological cross-sectional psychometric validation study was conducted in 2026 across eight hemodialysis centers in Mazandaran Province, Iran. The NPREM was translated and cross-culturally adapted according to Beaton’s guidelines, with two clinically inapplicable buttonhole cannulation items removed. Of the 655 eligible older adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis, 600 completed the survey (response rate: 91.6%). The final sample was selected using stratified random sampling and randomly divided into two independent subsamples for exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 300) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 300). Content and construct validity, measurement invariance, reliability, measurement error, and floor and ceiling effects were evaluated. Exploratory factor analysis supported a five-factor structure, explaining 59.90% of total variance, consistent with the original NPREM domains: Communicating with the Team, My Fistula/Graft and Needling, Steps in Needling, Working Together, and My Personal Experience. This structure was corroborated by exploratory graph analysis and confirmed by confirmatory factor analysis, which showed acceptable-to-good fit for both first- and second-order models (CFI = 0.980, TLI = 0.978, RMSEA = 0.035, SRMR = 0.036). Measurement invariance was supported at the configural and metric levels. All subscales demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency (α = 0.808–0.904; ω = 0.816–0.905), composite reliability (0.840–0.916), convergent validity (AVE = 0.584–0.687), and discriminant validity (HTMT = 0.435–0.589). Test–retest reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.906–0.972). Random forest analysis identified Working Together as the domain with the greatest predictive importance for overall needling experience. No meaningful floor or ceiling effects were observed. The Persian NPREM appears to provide a valid and reliable measure of needling experiences among older adults undergoing hemodialysis. It appears suitable for routine patient-reported experience assessment, quality improvement initiatives, and intervention research, pending further validation in broader and more diverse populations.

Article.Title: Substantial genomic and methylation variability between MCF-7 sublines
Article.Authors: Atanda H.; Ewing A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cancer cell lines have long been used as in vitro models for molecular assays in diagnostic and therapeutic development due to their accessibility as a well-controlled system. MCF-7 cell lines are the most widely studied cell lines in human breast cancer research, and its sublines have been reported to exhibit clonal, cytogenetic, and transcriptomic variability. However, allele-specific methylation alterations in cancer genomes remain inadequately explored, largely due to limitations in sequencing methods. Here, we characterise the genomic and epigenomic landscapes of two MCF-7 sublines using previously published Oxford Nanopore Technology sequencing data. We identified global and local DNA methylation differences as well as ~ 5000 structural variants and ~ 26,000 single-nucleotide variants between and within the sublines. Our analysis revealed substantial divergence in methylation patterns between the sublines, with ~ 5.1% of 1909 differentially methylated regions (DMRs) overlapping known cancer driver genes. These DMRs overlap breast cancer-associated genes, including ERBB2, CDH1, SALL4, GATA2, GATA3, HMGA2, and FBLN2. We find that 31 out of 63 manually assessed DMRs are explained by differential allelic methylation, and that allele-specific DMRs often overlap points where antisense non-coding RNAs overlap protein-coding genes. Transposable elements in both sublines also showed distinct methylation profiles, with one subline having hypomethylated L1 elements compared to the other, which coincided with the amount of apparent insertional mutagenesis attributable to L1 between the sublines. Our study demonstrates the utility of nanopore sequencing in providing novel insights into genomic and methylomic differences within MCF-7 sublines, in addition to insight into the nature of differential allelic methylation.

Article.Title: Prison health is public health: incarceration, equity, and an urgent global agenda
Article.Authors: Welter Wendt G.; da Costa F.; Zeki R.; Brömdal A.
Article.Abstract: Prison health is not a subsidiary of public health; it is integral to it. The health of incarcerated populations is inseparable from community health, equity, and sustainable social development. Yet despite longstanding commitment to equivalence of care, healthcare remains subordinate to custodial priorities in many prison systems. Nearly one-third of the global prison population is held in pretrial detention, often in overcrowded and under-resourced environments. Prisons are not isolated from society: communicable diseases affect incarcerated people, staff, and visitors, while the health consequences of imprisonment extend well beyond release. Formerly incarcerated individuals face reduced life expectancy, disrupted healthcare continuity, unstable housing, and substantial barriers to reintegration. Mental health conditions, already highly prevalent in custody, frequently worsen after release, contributing to cycles of disadvantage and recidivism. Contributors to this Collection show how imprisonment compound pre-existing vulnerabilities among women, older adults, people living with chronic illness, and those with unrecognised/inadequately treated injury. Simultaneously, incarceration may represent a critical opportunity for healthcare engagement, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. Excluding incarcerated populations from the reach of national health systems undermine progress towards health, equity, justice, and sustainable development. The challenge is no longer identifying solutions, but generating the political and institutional will to implement them.

Article.Title: Engineering functional halloysite nanotubes via dual-biopolymer interfacial assembly for pH-responsive antibiotic delivery
Article.Authors: Heydarifar F.; Zamiri B.; Mohebali A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Localized, pH-responsive drug delivery systems offer an effective strategy to enhance antibiotic efficacy and overcome the limitations of conventional systematic therapies for chronic infected wounds. In this study, functional halloysite–chitosan–xanthan gum (HNT–CS–XG) nanocomposites were engineered for the controlled release of minocycline (MC). The dual-biopolymer modification produced a hybrid interface on HNTs, not previously explored. The interfacial interactions established between chitosan, xanthan gum and the HNT surface generated a unique cohesive interfacial network that resulted in mechanical integrity and pH-responsive behavior, central to the design of advanced functional materials. Comprehensive physiochemical characterization (FTIR, XRD, zeta potential, TGA, DLS, SEM, and TEM) confirmed successful surface modification, strong polymer–polymer interactions, higher dispersion stability and preservation of the tubular structure of the halloysites. Among the formulations with different ratios, 2:1:2 ratio of HNT:CS:XG,HNT–CS–600XG exhibited optimal particle size (442 nm), excellent dispersion stability (PDI = 0.071) and high drug encapsulation (EE = 33%), offering a favourable balance between colloidal stability and bio-interface compatibility. In-vitro release studies for the nanocomposites, compared to halloysites alone, demonstrated a sustained and pH-responsive behavior, with significantly higher release at alkaline pH (43%) relative to acidic conditions (19%) proven advantageous for chronic infection. Kinetic modeling for MC release followed first-order and Korsmeyer–Peppas models, suggesting a diffusion-controlled mechanism. This observation arises from the hierarchical transport barriers created by the polymer-nanotube interface. The results highlight the potential of HNT–CS–XG as a biopolymer-based framework for prolonged and targeted antibiotic delivery.

Article.Title: Adaptive entropy and robust aggregation for client selection in federated credit risk modeling
Article.Authors: Zhou M.; An Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Federated learning enables collaborative modeling for financial risk prediction including credit default and transaction fraud without exposing raw local data. However, client heterogeneity, Non-IID data distribution, and dynamic participant involvement inevitably degrade model performance and incur excessive communication overhead. Existing client selection methods, either heuristic strategies or deep reinforcement learning solutions, suffer from inadequate exploration–exploitation tradeoff and overlook the inherent instability of local model updates. This paper proposes ERPPO-VA, an entropy-regularized proximal policy optimization framework for federated client selection. We formulate the client‑selection procedure using a heuristic‑augmented Markov‑decision‑process‑style framework, introduce an adaptive entropy coefficient together with prioritized experience replay to dynamically balance exploration and exploitation, and further design an exponential moving average based confidence-weighted aggregation mechanism to suppress the negative impact of unstable clients. Extensive experiments are conducted on three real-world financial datasets, namely CCFD, HCDR and IEEE-CIS, with over one million samples in total. The proposed approach is compared with Random selection, Greedy selection, DDQN, standard PPO, FedProx, MAPPO, and a faithful reimplementation of ERPPO. Under typical Non-IID settings, ERPPO-VA elevates the AUC metric by 4.5–8.7%, cuts total cumulative communication energy consumption by 52% over 200 federated rounds compared to ERPPO, accelerates the convergence speed by approximately 30%, and also achieves superior client fairness. Extensive empirical convergence analysis confirms the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Article.Title: Predicting mortality risk among non-cardiac surgical patients in the surgical intensive care unit: a retrospective study based on the MIMIC-IV database
Article.Authors: Ma M.; Liu J.; Li C.; Chen Y.; Jia H.; Hou A.; Xu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Timely and accurate mortality risk stratification for patients admitted to surgical intensive care units (SICUs) following non-cardiac surgery facilitates rapid risk triage and rational allocation of medical resources. In this retrospective analysis, multiple machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models were constructed to quantify 30-day postoperative mortality risk in this patient population. Clinical laboratory indicators and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals were extracted from non-cardiac surgical patients recorded in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. Five classical ML models were developed to predict 30-day mortality: logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and support vector machine (SVM). Two additional DL architectures, backpropagation neural network (BPNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN), were established for comparative performance testing. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis was applied to the optimal predictive model to identify dominant mortality-associated risk factors from both global and local interpretability perspectives. A total of 4 843 eligible patients were included, among whom 526 (10.9%) died within 30 days after non-cardiac surgery. The LGBM model outperformed all alternative machine learning and deep learning architectures, achieving the highest F1 score (0.934, 95% CI 0.913–0.942), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC, 0.977, 95% CI 0.972–0.982). Compared with the traditional Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI), the LGBM framework delivered substantially improved classification performance. Global SHAP analysis identified preoperative international normalized ratio (INR), serum bicarbonate, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and creatinine as the four most predictive variables for postoperative 30-day mortality. The LGBM model offers a novel and convenient method for preliminary prognostic risk stratification among non-cardiac surgical patients. This model can assist clinicians with early risk evaluation, though it cannot independently guide targeted clinical treatment decisions.

Article.Title: Prediction of pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in locally advanced lung adenocarcinoma: a multimodal machine learning approach
Article.Authors: Liu B.; Fu Y.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Predicting pathological complete response (pCR) following neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in locally advanced lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains clinically challenging. We aimed to develop an explainable machine learning framework to predict pCR and stratify patient prognosis. This retrospective study included 627 driver-negative LUAD patients (2020–2025). Fifteen baseline clinicopathological, metabolic, and inflammatory features were integrated to evaluate four algorithms. The optimal model was interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and validated for progression-free survival (PFS). The Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model exhibited superior discriminative performance (AUC = 0.872), significantly outperforming traditional logistic regression ( P < 0.001). SHAP analysis identified PET-CT SUVmax, CEA, and PD-L1 expression as the primary predictors, unveiling their non-linear thresholds and synergistic interactions. Decision curve analysis confirmed its clinical net benefit. Furthermore, patients stratified into the high-probability group by the AI model demonstrated significantly prolonged PFS, even within highly malignant sub-cohorts ( P < 0.001). This SHAP-enhanced XGBoost framework shows significant potential as a proof-of-concept model for predicting pCR and stratifying long-term survival in LUAD. However, given the artificially enriched cohort, prospective multicenter external validation is required before it can be considered a definitive clinical tool for optimizing individualized neoadjuvant therapeutic strategies.

Article.Title: Evaluation of mandibular molar mesialization by various methods with finite element analysis
Article.Authors: Uzun B.; Uslu F.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the biomechanical behavior of sliding mechanics of mandibular molar mesialization with different force application models using finite element analysis. Four models were created to simulate different force applications: force applied from the miniscrew to the second molar hook (Model 1), force applied from the miniscrew to an extended lever arm reaching the center of resistance of the second molar (Model 2), force applied to the second molar hook with indirect anchorage (Model 3), and force applied to the second molar hook with dental anchorage (Model 4). Maximum and minimum principal stresses in the tooth, alveolar bone, and around the miniscrew; Von Mises stress distribution; and tooth displacement patterns were analyzed separately for each model. In Model 1, mesial tipping of the molar was observed with concentrated stresses around the molar and miniscrew. Model 2 demonstrated a near-parallel displacement tendency of the second molar with more evenly distributed stresses. Models 3 and 4 showed similar tipping and mesialization of the molar but differed in stress and strain patterns. Applying force via an extended lever arm directed toward the tooth’s center of resistance produced a more parallel initial displacement of the second molar together with a more balanced stress distribution. Within the limits of an initial, linear-static analysis, miniscrew anchorage reduced the stress and strain transmitted to the adjacent teeth compared with dental anchorage.

Article.Title: Carotid artery disease diagnosis comprehensive review and two stage artificial intelligence framework
Article.Authors: Salama G.; Safy M.; Hassanin D.; Kamil C.; Khalaf A.; Abd-Ellah M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carotid artery occlusion is a major risk factor for stroke and cerebrovascular disease, often developing silently without warning. Early and accurate diagnosis of carotid artery plaque is crucial for improving treatment outcomes and reducing potential complications. Thus, there is a great demand for computer-aided diagnostic techniques for the early diagnosis of carotid artery disease with improved accuracy. However, existing literature remains fragmented, typically decoupling initial classification from detailed lesion tracing. This research is organized under three primary axes to bridge this clinical and technical gap. The first axis includes a structured review-of-reviews study that evaluates previously published review papers, while the second axis presents a complete methodological overview of authenticated techniques utilized in carotid diagnosis, such as carotid lumen segmentation, plaque segmentation, carotid classification, and IMT measurement. By mapping the limitations within these domains, the third axis presents a practical two-stage framework, including classification of the carotid artery into normal and plaque-containing, and then segmentation of its plaque to mirror a radiologist's natural decision-making hierarchy. Five lightweight transfer learning networks with multiple preprocessing filters were tested for carotid classification on an independent external clinical dataset. It is followed by a YOLOv11n-based segmentation head used to delineate plaques using expert-generated annotations. Methodologically, ShuffleNet combined with local laplacian filtering produced the best classification results, achieving 98.25% accuracy, 96.17% sensitivity, 100.00% specificity, 100.00% precision, and 98.05% F1-score. Crucially, this screening gate protects the subsequent segmentation stage from processing normal scans and eliminates false positives. The YOLOv11n-seg pipeline achieves a Dice Similarity Coefficient of 90.84%, a mask recall of 77.73%, and a mAP50 of 83.21% on unseen clinical scans. By filtering out healthy frames early, this dual-stage pipeline reduces computational overhead to processing times of 6.37 ms for screening and 6 ms for segmentation per frame.

Article.Title: Flexible PVA/SA–ZnO/Zn₆Al₂O₉ nanocomposite films with tunable optical band gap and enhanced dielectric performance for optoelectronic devices
Article.Authors: Mohamed H.; Wissa D.; Ismail A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aims to develop novel poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/sodium alginate (SA) nanocomposites reinforced with mixed-phase ZnO/Zn₆Al₂O₉ (ZnAl) nanoparticles to enhance their structural, optical, and electrical properties for advanced electrical and optoelectronic applications. The novelty of this work lies in the incorporation of mixed-phase ZnO/Zn₆Al₂O₉ nanoparticles at different loadings (2–8 wt%) into the PVA/SA matrix to achieve tunable multifunctional properties through optimized nanoparticle dispersion and interfacial interactions. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of mixed-phase ZnO/Zn₆Al₂O₉ nanoparticles with an average crystallite size of 43.3 nm, while the crystallinity of the nanocomposites varied with ZnAl concentration. Attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy indicated hydrogen bonding between the polymer chains and ZnAl nanoparticles. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) revealed a morphological transition from smooth PVA/SA surfaces to granular structures upon ZnAl incorporation. The optical band gap exhibited a non-monotonic decrease from 3.30 eV for PVA/SA blend, reaching a minimum of 1.45 eV at 6 wt% ZnAl, and then rising to 1.73 eV at 8 wt%. This effect is ascribed to defect-induced localized states at low and moderate loadings, as well as to nanoparticle agglomeration and microstructural heterogeneity at elevated loadings. Dielectric analysis demonstrated enhanced electrical conductivity and dielectric constants with increasing ZnAl content, with the optimum performance achieved at 4 wt% owing to the formation of interconnected conductive pathways. Complex modulus analysis further confirmed the ionic conduction mechanism. These multifunctional nanocomposites exhibit tunable optical and electrical properties, highlighting their potential for flexible electronics, UV-shielding, and optoelectronic applications.

Article.Title: Multiwavelength fluorescence imaging using a CEA-targeted fluorescent agent and indocyanine green to increase surgical precision in patients with colorectal liver metastases
Article.Authors: Warmerdam M.; Dijkhuis T.; Bijlstra O.; van Ravens T.; van Dam M.; Hartgrink H.; Burggraaf J.; Crobach A.; Cailler F.; Vahrmeijer A.; Mieog J.
Article.Abstract: Complete (R0) resection is essential for curative treatment of colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). Fluorescence-guided surgery with indocyanine green (ICG; emission wavelength ~ 800 nm) is increasingly being adopted as standard care because it enhances lesion detection and improves R0 resection rates. However, unintended R1 resections still occur, while the limited tumor specificity of ICG may lead to false-positive resections. Multiwavelength fluorescence imaging, combining ICG with a tumor-specific tracer, may overcome these limitations. SGM-101, a carcinoembryonic antigen-targeting fluorescent antibody (emission wavelength ~ 680 nm), enables tumor-specific visualization of colorectal cancer cells. This prospective feasibility study therefore evaluated the feasibility of simultaneous multiwavelength fluorescence imaging using SGM-101 in addition to standard ICG-guided CRLM surgery. Ten patients with high-risk features for R1 resection received ICG (0.5 mg/kg) 7 ± 1 days and SGM-101 (10 mg) 4 ± 1 days before surgery. Feasibility was predefined by four criteria: surgical usability and patient experience assessed through surveys, absence of spectral interference, and SGM-101 sensitivity > 80% for CRLM detection, considered necessary for potential intraoperative R1-margin identification. Three of the four predefined feasibility criteria were met. (1) Surgeons reported excellent usability; (2) patients experienced no burden from additional tracer administration, and (3) no spectral interference was observed. The prespecified sensitivity criterion (4) was not met, with an overall SGM-101 sensitivity of 50% on a lesion-level and 70% on a patient-level. However, in an exploratory subgroup analysis, sensitivity increased to 90% in lesions with higher tumor cell density (tumor regression grade 3–5). SGM-101’s specificity for lesion and margin discrimination was 100%. Importantly, all R1 margins were identified intraoperatively by at least one of the two tracers. These findings support further evaluation of multiwavelength fluorescence imaging in larger clinical trials. Refining preoperative patient selection may be key to improving sensitivity in future studies.
